WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC TAG: with every edge event tagged "dev" you cannot (a) attribute a production error to a build, (b) tell whether a deployed fix actually shipped, (c) see a regression appear at a release boundary, or (d) make a rollback decision on evidence — and ROLLBACK.md assumes you can identify the bad build. Note errorTracking reports "enabled" and /health/ready features.observability reports "ok", so the health surface actively says observability is fine while the release dimension of it is inert; that is why AC4 asks for a guard rather than just a config fix. The fix itself is small (one build arg); the reason it survived this long is that nothing measured it. | 2026-07-19 AC1/AC4/AC5 DONE; AC2/AC3 need a deploy to confirm. THE ROOT CAUSE WAS A MISSING BUILD ARG, and the fix is DECLARATIVE rather than another instruction: docker-compose.coolify.yml now carries build.args GIT_SHA: dev. That placement is the whole point — the Dockerfile has carried a comment telling the builder to pass GIT_SHA since it was written, and per this story's own evidence that comment did not survive contact with the actual deploy. A build arg in compose is APPLIED BY THE PLATFORM instead of remembered by a person, so documenting it harder would have reproduced the same failure. The :-dev fallback keeps a plain local docker compose build working. AC4 DONE and it is the anti-regression half: the observability feature group now requires SENTRY_DSN *and* a real RELEASE_SHA, so /health/ready reports observability DEGRADED while the release is a placeholder — previously it reported 'ok' in the exact prod state this story measured (errorTracking enabled, release 'dev'), which is the false confidence that let it sit unnoticed. isRealReleaseSha is deliberately permissive on FORM: it rejects the placeholder set (dev/unknown/local/none/latest/empty) but accepts short SHAs and tags, because the measured failure was the literal ARG default surviving the build, not a malformed SHA — requiring 40 hex chars would break tag-based deploys for no benefit. 4 tests, including the exact prod state as a case. AC5 DONE in COOLIFY.md with a MEASURE-DO-NOT-READ verification step (curl /health | jq .release), plus the warning that deploying from docker-compose.yml rather than the .coolify.yml variant needs the same args block. ⚠ REMAINING AND GENUINELY UNVERIFIABLE FROM HERE: AC2 (measure /health after a deploy) and AC3 (confirm a real Sentry event carries the release). Both require the deploy to actually happen. What HAS changed is that a regression now announces itself on /health/ready instead of waiting for someone to think to curl. [2026-07-19 AC4+AC5 DONE, AC1-AC3 NEED THE COOLIFY BUILD + A PROD MEASUREMENT] AC4: /health/ready now carries features.release, degraded whenever the release is unattributable (dev / unknown / empty / whitespace, case-insensitive). Deliberately a SEPARATE key from features.observability: that group reports ok whenever a Sentry DSN is present, which stays true and stays misleading while every event it ships is tagged dev. Also deliberately does NOT flip the service to not_ready — the AC allowed either, and refusing readiness on an untagged build would pull grading, payments and webhooks out of rotation to protect observability. health.ts already argues this exact principle for the schema probe (a probe that can fail a container over a diagnostic is a worse bug than the blind spot it fixes). A test asserts ready stays true. releaseReadiness() is pure; 5 new tests. AC5 FINDING: COOLIFY.md already had a US-2001 build-args section from an earlier pass, and it CLAIMED /health/ready reports features.observability as degraded on a placeholder release. That was FALSE — nothing implemented it. The documentation described a guard that did not exist, which is a plausible reason nobody built one; same defect class as US-2035 (comment asserting a property the code lacks) and US-2123 (copy advertising an ungranted entitlement). Doc now names the real key, shows the curl, and records the correction rather than quietly overwriting it. STILL OPEN (all need the deploy, not code): AC1 the Coolify build must actually pass GIT_SHA=$SOURCE_COMMIT — docker-compose.coolify.yml declares it but prod measured release=dev on 2026-07-18, so either the deploy uses docker-compose.yml or the Build Args field is unset. AC2 verify by curling /health after a deploy. AC3 confirm a real Sentry event carries the SHA. The new features.release entry makes AC2 checkable without remembering the curl. | 2026-08-02 AC2 MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION, and it FAILS. The AC insisted on measuring the endpoint rather than reading the config, and that instruction earned its keep: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns features.release = 'unattributable: release="dev" — the image was built without a GIT_SHA build arg, so errors cannot be tied to a commit'. So AC1 is declared but NOT IN EFFECT. docker-compose.coolify.yml carries build.args.GIT_SHA: ${SOURCE_COMMIT:-dev}, and the running image was still built without it. Three candidate causes, in the order worth checking: (1) Coolify is deploying from docker-compose.yml rather than the .coolify.yml variant — the previous pass explicitly warned that the plain file needs the same args block, and that warning is now the leading hypothesis rather than a footnote; (2) the running image predates the compose change and no rebuild has happened since; (3) SOURCE_COMMIT is not populated in this Coolify version, so the :-dev fallback wins silently — which is exactly what the fallback is designed to do and exactly why it is indistinguishable from cause (2) without a rebuild. AC3 (a real Sentry event carrying the release) is moot until this is fixed: every event currently ships tagged 'dev', which is the state the story exists to end. WHAT THIS CONFIRMS ABOUT AC4, and it is the useful part: the guard works. /health/ready reported the problem in plain language, unprompted, to a caller who did nothing but curl a public endpoint. That is the difference between a config that is wrong and a config that ANNOUNCES it is wrong — before this, the only way to learn it was to notice that every Sentry release said dev. The AC4 decision not to flip the service to not_ready also holds up: the service is genuinely serving, and pulling grading and payments out of rotation to protect observability would have been the wrong trade. STILL OPEN: AC1 in practice (the build arg must actually reach the image), AC2 re-measured after that deploy, AC3 confirmed on a real event. All three need one Coolify rebuild, and the first thing to check is which compose file the service is deploying from. ALSO OBSERVED IN THE SAME RESPONSE, recorded here because it is the same curl: schema reports {expected:00512, applied:00512, status:match}. See the note on the held-migration gate. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-03: any "HELD"/"apply-BEFORE-push" wording earlier in this note describes the state AT THE TIME OF WRITING and is STALE. Prod was measured at applied=00514 on 2026-08-03 via /health/ready (the database's own answer, not a recollection), and every migration up to 00514 is on origin/main. The only migration currently held is 00515 (US-2168), which is unrelated to this story. Do not read this note as evidence that the branch is frozen. | 2026-08-08 CAUSE (1) CONFIRMED AND FIXED. The 2026-08-02 pass listed three candidate causes and said the first thing to check is which compose file the service deploys from. Checked it, and the answer is in this repo's own doc: COOLIFY.md line 11 says the one-time setup makes Coolify 'auto-pick docker-compose.yml'. That file's first line calls itself 'Production compose used by Coolify' — and it had NO build.args block. So the arg was declared only in docker-compose.coolify.yml, which is not the file the documented setup deploys. docker-compose.staging.yml was missing it too.

FIX: both now declare args.GIT_SHA: ${SOURCE_COMMIT:-dev}, identical to the .coolify.yml one. Deliberately declared in ALL of them rather than picking the 'right' one — the question 'which compose file is it actually using?' is precisely what nobody could answer for three weeks, and making the answer irrelevant is cheaper than making it knowable.

NEW STATIC GUARD (AC4's missing half): services/edge-functions/src/tests/compose-release-arg_test.ts walks every docker-compose*.yml, and any file with a build: section that lacks GIT_SHA fails CI with the reason. It also asserts the Dockerfile still wires ARG GIT_SHA -> ENV RELEASE_SHA, so the guard cannot stay green over a dead mechanism. Override files with no build: section (docker-compose.dev.yml) are exempt — they inherit the base build. Sabotage-verified: deleted the arg line from docker-compose.yml, test failed naming the file; restored, 2 passed. deno lint + deno check clean.

WHY A STATIC GUARD ON TOP OF THE RUNTIME ONE: the /health/ready guard worked exactly as designed and still cost three weeks, because it can only speak after a bad image is already serving. A per-file declaration that only one file carries is a per-file bug, and nothing was looking ACROSS the files. This test looks across the files.

COOLIFY.md rewritten: the old text carried a warning telling the operator to add the block by hand or fill in Coolify's Build Args field — asking a person to remember something, which is the failure mode this story is about, and the Dockerfile had been asking in a comment since it was written. It now states all three files declare it, records why, and keeps ONE residual manual step for the only cause the code cannot rule out (a Coolify version that does not populate SOURCE_COMMIT, where :-dev wins silently).

STILL passes:false, and only on the deploy: AC2 (curl /health/ready after a Coolify rebuild and see a real SHA) and AC3 (confirm a Sentry event carries it). Both need a rebuild, which ADE Hub is disarmed for. Nothing further is doable from a checkout — the code side of AC1 is now complete on all three files and guarded. | 2026-08-09 A SECOND, INDEPENDENT FAULT FOUND — the build arg was never the whole story, and every prior pass (incl. mine) chased it alone. MEASURED FIRST: GET /health returned release:"dev" on an image whose SAME response reported schema.expected=00585, i.e. an image built AFTER the 2026-08-08 commit that put build.args.GIT_SHA in all three compose files. That eliminates the 2026-08-02 note's cause (2) 'the running image predates the compose change'. THE CODE BUG: observability.ts releaseSha() read RELEASE_SHA ?? COMMIT_SHA ?? SOURCE_COMMIT ?? GIT_SHA, and its comment claimed it 'accepts any of the common env names so the same code works on Coolify / CI / local'. It does not. Dockerfile sets ENV RELEASE_SHA=${GIT_SHA} with ARG GIT_SHA=dev, so RELEASE_SHA is ALWAYS SET in the image — to the literal 'dev'. ?? falls through on undefined, never on a placeholder VALUE, so the first key always won and the other three were DEAD CODE on the only platform they were written for. Consequence that matters most: setting SOURCE_COMMIT by hand in Coolify — the obvious workaround, and the one COOLIFY.md was steering toward — would have been SILENTLY IGNORED. FIXED: new services/edge-functions/src/lib/release-identity.ts (resolveRelease/isPlaceholderRelease/RELEASE_ENV_KEYS) falls through placeholder VALUES; observability.ts, env-validation.ts isRealReleaseSha and routes/health.ts all consolidated onto it — health.ts had its OWN narrower set ['dev','unknown',''] so /health/ready could have called a release of 'local' ok while env-validation called it a placeholder. Two more instances of the same defect class fixed: (a) agent-tools.ts:654 releaseSha() fed US-1610's release-verify agent, which detects a deploy by watching that value CHANGE — a constant 'dev' is not an error, it is a value that never changes, so that agent has reported 'no deploy' on every run since it shipped; it now returns null on a placeholder so no-identity stays distinguishable from an identity. So setting SOURCE_COMMIT in Coolify now fixes prod WITHOUT a rebuild, which is the fastest thing to try. STILL passes:false on AC2/AC3, unchanged: both need a deploy or an env-var change on the Coolify side, then re-measure /health. What changed is that the fix no longer requires a rebuild. | 2026-08-12 AC2 MEASURED AGAINST PROD, AND IT STILL FAILS. GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health returns {"env":"production","release":"unknown","errorTracking":"enabled"}. So the declarative fix from 2026-07-19 - build.args GIT_SHA in docker-compose.coolify.yml - has NOT taken effect across every deploy since, and the value moved from the literal "dev" to "unknown", which is the same problem wearing a different word. AC1 is therefore NOT done: something in the Coolify build is not substituting the arg, and the next step is to look at how Coolify expands build.args rather than to add another instruction somewhere. AC4 IS CONFIRMED WORKING, and this is the part worth keeping: /health/ready now reports features.release as "unattributable: release="unknown" - none of RELEASE_SHA, COMMIT_SHA, SOURCE_COMMIT, GIT_SHA held a real commit, so errors cannot be tied to a build. That is the guard doing exactly its job - it names the defect, names the candidates, and points at the doc - and it is why this was measurable in one GET instead of another deep dive. AC3 (a real Sentry event carrying the release) is moot until AC1 lands, since the release it would carry is the broken one. ALSO MEASURED IN THE SAME CALL, recorded so the sweep is not lost: features.observability reports "set but not satisfied - every var is present; see the observability check", and features.hostWatchdog reports "unconfigured: no host watchdog has ever checked in" (US-2447 working as designed - the absence is visible). Schema is {expected:00589, applied:00589, status:match}. | 2026-08-16 THE OPERATOR STEP IS ONE ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE, not a build-arg investigation, and the last note sends the next reader down the harder path. That note said 'the next step is to look at how Coolify expands build.args'. That was correct on 2026-08-12 and is not correct now.  PROVEN BY RUNNING IT, not by reading: the edge was started with SOURCE_COMMIT set as a plain environment variable and nothing else changed, and GET /health returned {"release":"abc1234deadbeef"}. So a RUNTIME override takes effect and no build arg is needed.  WHY THIS CHANGED, and it is worth understanding before trusting it: releaseSha() used to read RELEASE_SHA ?? COMMIT_SHA ?? SOURCE_COMMIT ?? GIT_SHA, and the Dockerfile sets ENV RELEASE_SHA=${GIT_SHA} with ARG GIT_SHA=dev - so RELEASE_SHA was ALWAYS SET, to the literal 'dev', and ?? only falls through on null. The first key always won and every fallback was dead code on the one platform they existed for. That is why setting SOURCE_COMMIT by hand would have been silently ignored, and why three passes went hunting for the build arg. lib/ release-identity.ts now falls through on a placeholder VALUE rather than on an unset key, which is what makes the env var work at all. The module's own header records this; the story's operator instruction never caught up.  WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVEN: that Coolify passes the variable through (it should - it is an ordinary env var on the resource), that prod then reports it (AC2, one curl after the redeploy), and that Sentry tags an event with it (AC3). The build arg may still be broken and it no longer matters.  SEPARATELY, AND NOT A FINDING: /health/ready on the local run answered 503 not_ready with env:"missing", because a local test-mode edge has no ANTHROPIC/STRIPE keys. The features block - including features.release, the US-2001 AC4 guard, and features.pages_origin_bypass that US-2612 waits on - is not populated in that state, so neither could be read here. Both need a READY edge, which locally means supplying the full env set. | 2026-08-17 ROOT CAUSE FOUND, AND IT WAS NEVER A CONFIGURATION MISTAKE. The commit was being sent and thrown away.  Coolify passes the commit as a build argument named SOURCE_COMMIT. DOCKER ONLY EXPOSES A BUILD ARG THE DOCKERFILE HAS DECLARED WITH ARG - an undeclared one is dropped with a build warning nobody reads. services/edge-functions/Dockerfile declared only GIT_SHA. So Coolify supplied the value, Docker discarded it, RELEASE_SHA kept the literal ARG default, and /health/ready reported an unattributable release while the operator had correctly set nothing.  THE COMPOSE FIX NEVER APPLIED, which is why this survived two rounds of work. All three compose files have passed GIT_SHA: dev since 2026-08-02 and it changed nothing, because US-2665 established the compose file is NOT what deploys this service. The fallback had to live in the Dockerfile to be reached at all.  THE FIX: ARG SOURCE_COMMIT="" declared FIRST, then ARG GIT_SHA=. An ARG may use a previously-declared ARG as its default, so an explicit GIT_SHA still wins and Coolify's value flows on its own otherwise. The old ARG GIT_SHA=dev default is gone: a literal default surviving the build is the failure this story recorded in the first place. Empty is the correct no-op, because "" is in RELEASE_PLACEHOLDERS and resolveRelease falls through to the next key.  VERIFIED AGAINST A REAL docker build, four cases, not reasoned about:   SOURCE_COMMIT=abc1234 only            -> RELEASE_SHA=abc1234   (the Coolify case)   SOURCE_COMMIT=abc1234 GIT_SHA=deadbee -> RELEASE_SHA=deadbee   (explicit still wins)   neither passed                        -> RELEASE_SHA=          (falls through safely)   SOURCE_COMMIT= (blank)                -> RELEASE_SHA=          (the case that was live)  ⚠ THE LAST ONE IS PROBABLY WHAT THE OPERATOR HIT. A hand-created Coolify variable named SOURCE_COMMIT SHADOWS the built-in, and a blank value resolves the chain to empty no matter what else is set. The instruction is now DELETE that variable rather than fill it in - recorded in COOLIFY.md and vault/10-ops/env-reference.md.  TWO NEW GUARDS in compose-release-arg_test.ts: SOURCE_COMMIT must be DECLARED (and declared BEFORE GIT_SHA, since a default can only reference an arg already in scope), and GIT_SHA must default to  rather than to any literal. Sabotage-verified: restoring ARG GIT_SHA=dev reddens the second one naming the value found.  STILL OPEN until the next rebuild: this is a BUILD-time fix, so /health/ready keeps reporting unknown until the edge is rebuilt. That rebuild is the one deploy window US-2003, US-2010 and US-2011 are all also waiting on - and after it, curl /health/ready and features.release should name a commit. | CORRECTION 2026-08-17, same session: the segment above was mangled by the SHELL, not by the author, and one of the mangled phrases is the actual fix. Written with `node -e` through bash, which expanded the dollar-brace syntax inside the string before node ever saw it.  IT SAYS  : ARG GIT_SHA=. IT MEANT : ARG GIT_SHA=${SOURCE_COMMIT}  IT SAYS  : the compose files have passed GIT_SHA: dev IT MEANT : the compose files have passed GIT_SHA: ${SOURCE_COMMIT:-dev}  The second one is the more misleading of the two - read literally it says the compose files hardcode the placeholder, when they interpolate Coolify's commit and only fall back to it. The point of that paragraph is that the interpolation was correct all along and simply never ran, because the compose file is not what deploys this service.  THE CODE AND THE DOCS ARE NOT AFFECTED. services/edge-functions/Dockerfile, COOLIFY.md and vault/10-ops/env-reference.md were written with the Edit tool and read correctly; only this note and the commit message for 015d99d2 carry the damage. The commit is already pushed and a second agent is active on this branch, so it is left alone rather than force-amended - the authoritative statement of the fix is the Dockerfile comment.  THE PROCESS LESSON, which is the reason this is recorded at all: prose containing ${...}, backticks or backslashes must go through a scratchpad .mjs file invoked with execFileSync, never through `node -e` inside a shell command. This is the same trap logged in memory as backticks-in-shell-args and it has now bitten on a note ABOUT shell-variable handling. | 2026-08-22: THE DIAGNOSTIC NOW POINTS AT THE ANSWER INSTEAD OF ONLY REPORTING THE PROBLEM. AC1-AC3 stay operator; AC4 and AC5 were already done. Re-measured first: scripts/probe-prod-readonly.mjs reports 'unattributable: release="unknown" - none of RELEASE_SHA, COMMIT_SHA, SOURCE_COMMIT or GIT_SHA held a real commit', so this is still live.  WHY ANYTHING WAS ADDED AT ALL, given the fix is one Coolify variable. This story has been re-diagnosed THREE times (build arg, then ARG declaration, then runtime override) and the reason is in the shape of the signal: 'release: unknown' says something is wrong and nothing about what to do. The operator cannot tell an unset variable from one already set under a name this code does not read, so every pass restarts the guessing. resolveRelease answers 'which build is this'; nothing answered 'which variable SHOULD I be reading'.  NEW unreadReleaseCandidates() in lib/release-identity.ts, logged once at boot from main.ts as edge.boot.release_unknown, and ONLY when the release is a placeholder - a healthy deploy logs nothing extra. It names env keys that look like they carry a build identity and are not in RELEASE_ENV_KEYS, so the next deploy log says either 'COOLIFY_GIT_COMMIT looks like a build id and nothing reads it - copy it into SOURCE_COMMIT or add the key' or 'nothing here looks like one - set SOURCE_COMMIT'. Either sentence ends the guessing.  NAMES ONLY, NEVER VALUES, and that is the load-bearing property rather than a nicety: this line lands in a deploy log, so a value would put whatever the key holds somewhere it was never meant to be. A SECRET DENY LIST WINS OVER THE CANDIDATE PATTERN - COMMIT_SIGNING_KEY matches /COMMIT/ and is a secret, so /SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|CREDENTIAL|PRIVATE|_KEY$|APIKEY/ is checked first. A missed diagnostic costs one more question; a leaked secret NAME in a deploy log costs a rotation. Capped at 8, because a list of forty is a list nobody reads, which is the same as not having it. A key holding 'dev' is not a candidate - pointing the operator at it sends them to the placeholder they already have.  SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 6 OF 6, and the first run caught a REAL HOLE in my own guard - the most important one. Five behavioural sabotages reddened immediately (deny list removed, placeholder offered, already-read keys re-suggested, cap removed, name pattern widened to match everything). THE SIXTH STAYED GREEN: rewriting the boot log to emit [key, value] pairs instead of names. Every behavioural case passed, because unreadReleaseCandidates still returned names only - the leak was at the CALL SITE, not in the function.  THAT IS THE ONE PLACE A SOURCE SCAN IS THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT, which is worth stating because I have spent this session replacing scans with calls. What has to hold here is a property of main.ts's log payload, not of a function: no Deno.env.get and no toObject() inside the edge.boot.release_unknown block. A behavioural test cannot see that. Scans are right for wiring and wrong for logic; this is wiring. The scan strips block comments as blocks before matching, because the block it reads is heavily commented and the comment names the very tokens it looks for.  AC4 WAS ALREADY DONE and the probe proves it end to end: /health/ready names which of the four keys held a real commit, which is exactly what AC4 asked for. AC5 IS ALSO ALREADY DONE - COOLIFY.md carries the SOURCE_COMMIT block including the warning that a hand-created Coolify variable of that name SHADOWS the built-in one and must be deleted.  VERIFIED: deno check clean on lib and main, deno lint clean on all three files, release-identity_test.ts 15 passed / 0 failed (7 new).  STILL OPEN, unchanged and unchanged in kind: AC1/AC2/AC3 are the Coolify UI. Set SOURCE_COMMIT on the edge resource (or delete a blank hand-made one and let Coolify supply it), redeploy, re-read /health, and confirm a Sentry edge event carries the release. WHAT IS DIFFERENT NOW is that the redeploy itself will say in the log whether a usable value was already sitting on the container - so if the obvious fix does not take, the next line is data rather than a fourth theory. | 2026-08-22 STILL UNATTRIBUTABLE, measured rather than assumed.  features.release reads: 'unattributable: release="unknown" - none of RELEASE_SHA, COMMIT_SHA, SOURCE_COMMIT, GIT_SHA held a real commit, so errors cannot be tied to a build. Either the image was built without a GIT_SHA build arg or none of those vars is set at runtime.'  So the value has moved from 'dev' to 'unknown' - which is US-2001's own AC1 working, since 'unknown' at least refuses to lie - but the underlying condition is unchanged and every production edge error is still unattributable to a commit.  WHY THIS ONE FIRST: prd-operator ranks it at the top of the queue with EIGHT other open stories naming it (US-1968, US-2003, US-2010, US-2011, US-2347, US-2447, US-2597, US-2665). It is a Coolify build-arg question rather than a repo change, and until it is answered, every incident investigation on the other eight starts by not knowing which build produced the error.  MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION 2026-08-22, read-only and repeatable by anyone: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready. No credentials needed. It also reported schema {expected 00647, applied 00648, ahead} and NO features.connector field, which together date the running build: it predates both the 00648 commit and this morning's US-2687 work, so the deployed edge is behind local main by more than a few commits. | 2026-08-22 SECOND SYMPTOM, SAME CAUSE, and it makes this the highest-leverage item in the operator queue rather than merely the most-named one.  The same /health/ready read shows features.observability as 'set but not satisfied - every var is present; see the observability check'. That is not a separate misconfiguration. env-validation.ts's own comment names this exact case: the observability group fails its satisfiedWhen with EVERY variable present, because isRealReleaseSha() rejects the placeholder. SENTRY_DSN is set; the group is unsatisfied purely because the release is unknown.  SO ONE COOLIFY BUILD ARG FIXES TWO THINGS: errors become attributable to a commit, and the observability group goes green rather than reporting a gap it cannot explain. Everything else in the features block is already ok or is an honest two-sided caveat (smtp, alerting and auth_email_hook each say plainly that being CONFIGURED is not proof anything ARRIVES - that is US-2003's delivery drill, not a config error).  WORTH KNOWING THAT THIS USED TO BE WORSE: production once reported the literal string 'missing: ' with nothing after the colon - telling an operator something was missing and refusing to say which. The current wording exists because of that.  ALSO CONFIRMED IN THE SAME READ, and it closes a question two other stories were sequenced behind: features.pages_origin_bypass reports 'PROVEN FROM THE OTHER SIDE: 154 request(s) carrying a matching x-pages-origin have reached this service since it started, the most recent 24s ago'. US-2612 is archived and this is direct positive evidence rather than inference - so the US-2113 sequencing that blamed an unset CF_PAGES_ORIGIN_SECRET is dead twice over. | 2026-08-22 THE 2026-08-17 FIX IS IN THE RUNNING IMAGE AND THE RELEASE IS STILL UNKNOWN. Measured, not inferred, and it changes what the remaining work is.  COOLIFY.md carries a callout dated 2026-08-17 headed "you should not have to set anything for this any more": the Dockerfile now declares ARG SOURCE_COMMIT and defaults ARG GIT_SHA=${SOURCE_COMMIT}, so Coolify's own commit was expected to flow into the image with no configuration. Production today says otherwise.  THE MEASUREMENT, and the part that makes it conclusive is dating the image:   GET /health        -> release: "unknown"   GET /health/ready  -> schema: { expected: "00649", applied: "00650" } The commit that set EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = "00649" is 008a7fc71, made today at 08:16 and the tip of origin/main. The Dockerfile fix is 015d99d28, made 2026-08-17 and an ancestor of it. So the deployed image WAS built with ARG SOURCE_COMMIT declared. This is not a stale deploy, which was the obvious alternative explanation and is now ruled out.  (The schema line is also a clean secondary read: expected 00649 against applied 00650 is the edge running one migration behind the database, which is the safe direction and exactly what a held migration looks like.)  TWO CANDIDATES REMAIN AND THIS STORY ALREADY NAMED ONE. Either a hand-made Coolify variable called SOURCE_COMMIT is shadowing Coolify's built-in and resolving the chain to empty - COOLIFY.md's own ⚠, whose symptom is precisely "unknown no matter what else you set" - or this deploy never receives Coolify's build arg. Nothing readable from outside the host separates them, so the operator step is now ONE GLANCE rather than an investigation: look for a variable named SOURCE_COMMIT and delete it if it is there.  AND THERE IS A ONE-FIELD FALLBACK THAT NEEDS NO BUILD AT ALL, which this story did not have before because the whole section was written about build args. Setting a RUNTIME variable COMMIT_SHA works on the image already running, and the reason is the fallthrough fix from 2026-08-09: RELEASE_SHA is baked into the image as the empty string, "" is in RELEASE_PLACEHOLDERS, and resolveRelease() falls through a placeholder VALUE rather than only an unset key - so the next key in RELEASE_ENV_KEYS wins.  COMMIT_SHA, NOT SOURCE_COMMIT, and the distinction is the whole reason to write it down: SOURCE_COMMIT is the name Coolify uses for its built-in, so a hand-made one is the failure above. COMMIT_SHA is used by nothing else here and sits second in the precedence order behind the placeholder RELEASE_SHA.  It is manual and has to be updated per deploy, which is the exact thing this story exists to remove - so it is the stopgap that makes eight blocked stories measurable again, not the fix. Both are now in COOLIFY.md with the measurement under them.  STILL OPERATOR-ONLY. Nothing in this repo can read the Coolify variable list. | 2026-08-22 THE 'HELD' LANGUAGE IN THIS STORY IS STALE. RESOLVED. prd-lint has been warning about it on every run: a held migration is by definition unpushed, so the word tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not. Checked rather than assumed, and it is stale on BOTH counts. PUSHED: every migration this story names is on origin/main — verified with git cat-file against the remote ref, not inferred from a local log. APPLIED: PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md opens with 'HELD: none' and records everything through 00644 as applied, 00646 and 00647 applied and verified 2026-08-21, and 00650 applied and VERIFIED 2026-08-22 against the database itself — items_full reporting 63 columns in PostgREST's OpenAPI document with garment_category and material both present. THE TWO ARE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS AND THIS NOTE ANSWERS BOTH ON PURPOSE. 'Pushed is not applied' is the trap the migration process warns about, and a note that cleared only the first half would swap one wrong impression for another. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md remains the file that tracks applied state; this note is not a substitute for reading it. Nothing in this story is blocked on a push or an apply. | 2026-08-22 STATUS CORRECTION: every migration named in this story is on origin/main and applied to production. Nothing here is frozen. PUSHED: verified with git cat-file against the remote ref rather than inferred from a local log. APPLIED: PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md opens with a 'none outstanding' banner and records everything through 00644 as done, 00646 and 00647 verified 2026-08-21, and 00650 verified 2026-08-22 against the database itself — items_full reporting 63 columns in PostgREST's OpenAPI document with garment_category and material both present. BOTH QUESTIONS ANSWERED ON PURPOSE. Pushed is not applied, and a correction clearing only the first half would swap one wrong impression for another. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md stays the file that tracks applied state; this is not a substitute for reading it. ⚠ THE SEGMENT I APPENDED JUST BEFORE THIS ONE MADE THE WARNING WORSE, and the reason is worth more than the fix. It said the same thing in my own words, so it matched none of prd-lint's three correction phrases while itself containing the trigger word beside a list of migration numbers — the guard read it as a fresh claim and the warning grew. A correction has to speak the detector's vocabulary, and reading the detector first would have cost thirty seconds. | 2026-08-23 MEASURED IN PRODUCTION, which is what AC2 asks for. No code changed.

GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health
  {"status":"ok","env":"production","release":"unknown","errorTracking":"enabled"}

So the defect is UNCHANGED since the 2026-08-16 note: release is still the
placeholder, and every prod edge error remains unattributable to a commit.
AC1, AC2 and AC7 are all still open, and AC7 is still the shortest path.

AC4 IS DONE AND IS NOW PROVEN IN PRODUCTION, not merely present in the source.
GET /health/ready reports it as a degraded FEATURE while keeping status=ready:

  release: unattributable: release="unknown" — none of RELEASE_SHA, COMMIT_SHA,
  SOURCE_COMMIT, GIT_SHA held a real commit, so errors cannot be tied to a
  build. Either the image was built without a GIT_SHA build arg or none of
  those vars is set at runtime (see COOLIFY.md, US-2001)

That is the AC4 design working exactly as its comment describes: it SURFACES
rather than failing readiness, because a probe that can fail a liveness check
over a build-identity problem would take the service down for a labelling bug.
It also names all four variables it looked at, so AC7 does not require guessing
which one Coolify wants.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE READER: AC4 no longer needs verifying. Anyone picking
this up should go straight to AC7 - set SOURCE_COMMIT as an ordinary
environment variable on the Coolify service - and then RE-MEASURE /health, not
the config. The endpoint already tells you whether it worked, in one line, and
it will keep telling you until it does.

Eight open stories name this one (US-1968, US-2003, US-2010, US-2011, US-2347,
US-2447, US-2597, US-2665), so it is the single highest-leverage operator item
in the queue and it is one environment variable. | 2026-08-29 STILL BROKEN, MEASURED. AC2 asks for the endpoint rather than the
config, so here is the endpoint:

  GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health
  {"env":"production","release":"unknown","errorTracking":"enabled"}

So Sentry IS enabled - the DSN is set - and every event it receives from the
prod edge is tagged release "unknown". The defect is exactly as AC6 restated
it: the value moved from "dev" to "unknown", the same defect wearing a
different word.

HOW I GOT HERE, because it is a cheaper route than the one the story implies:
/health/ready reports features.observability as "set but not satisfied - every
var is present". That phrasing is the tell. The group requires SENTRY_DSN AND
isRealReleaseSha(), so "every var present but not satisfied" can only mean the
SHA is not real. /health then names the value outright. Both are unauthenticated
reads and neither needs a deploy to answer.

WHY IT IS WORTH MORE THAN ITS RANK (1977, effectively last). It silently
degrades every other observability story:
  - US-2662 AC6 wants a Sentry search for a specific error to decide whether a
    defect was ever live. Events that exist but carry no release cannot answer
    "was this before or after the fix", which is half of what that search is
    for.
  - Sentry regression detection and "resolved in next release" do not work at
    all without a release, so a fixed error can reappear unremarked.
  - Today I shipped a database crash fix and a UI fix. Neither is attributable
    to a deploy in Sentry when they land.

AC7 is still the way: SOURCE_COMMIT as an ordinary env var on the edge resource
in the Coolify UI. One field, and it is not a repo change - nothing in this
commit or any other can set it.

userStories.title: Category grading criteria cover 8 of 20 garment categories — 12 categories grade with no category guidance at all
userStories.description: As a seller of a shirt, a coat or a skirt, I want the grader to know what matters on my category, because the ones that do get it are measurably better guided. Verified: ai-grading.ts:320 GARMENT_CATEGORY_CRITERIA has exactly 8 keys (jeans, pants, shorts, jacket, sweater, hoodie, t-shirt, dress) while src/lib/constants.ts GARMENT_CATEGORIES has 20 values. The 12 with no entry — shirt, blouse, coat, skirt, sneakers, boots, sandals, hat, bag, belt, scarf, other — fall through to the generic prompt with only DESIGN_VS_DEFECT_PRINCIPLE. Each of the missing ones has real category-specific signal the model is currently not told to look for: collar and cuff fray and yellowing on shirts, seam slippage and pulls on blouses, lining and shell separation and pilling on wool coats, zipper and hem and lining on skirts, and for footwear the outsole and midsole entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: Every value in GARMENT_CATEGORIES has a criteria entry, or the fallback is made explicit and deliberate for the ones that genuinely have none.
Each new entry follows the existing voice: what is INTENTIONAL design on this category vs what is genuine wear, since that distinction is the whole point of the block.
The prompt change ships as a new prompt version through shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary, not a silent edit — this changes the per-image prompt for 12 categories at once.
Golden-set cases exist for the newly-covered categories before activation, tagged so the eval report can slice per category.
Categories already covered produce byte-identical prompts, test-guarded, so the eval measures only the new coverage.

OPERATOR: bootstrap a golden set for the twelve uncovered garment categories, then decide the shadow spend (AC3, AC4). They are all waiting on the SAME missing input, which is worth seeing together: a prompt only ships through shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary, and a gate with no cases for the new category cannot pass or fail it - it would report on the eight categories already covered and say nothing about the ones the story is about. Golden cases grow from REAL human-corrected grades, so the bootstrap is: grade some of these items behind the flag, collect expert corrections, THEN gate. AND IT IS A SPEND DECISION, not just a flag flip: the per-image shadow path is OFF by default and costs a vision call per photo plus a composite per sampled submission (PER_IMAGE_SHADOW_DAILY_VISION_CAP). GRADING_CATEGORY_CRITERIA_V2 stays OFF until both are settled.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Grading/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). 8 of 20 categories covered. Cheapest coverage win in the epic (prompt data, no schema), but it changes the per-image prompt for 12 categories at once so it needs a real eval cycle and per-category golden cases first. | 2026-08-08 AC1/AC2/AC5 DONE. AC3 IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE AS WRITTEN, and that is the finding. AC4 unchanged and still blocking.

AC1: all 11 remaining categories written (shirt, blouse, coat, skirt, sneakers, boots, sandals, hat, bag, belt, scarf). "other" is DELIBERATELY left uncovered and the absence is now pinned by a test: it is the value assigned when the category is UNKNOWN (garment-mapping.ts maps five of six garment types to it), so an "other" item may be any of the twenty and there is no honest guidance to give. Generic filler there would restate DESIGN_VS_DEFECT_PRINCIPLE and make coverage look complete while the real gap is upstream classification.

AC2: each entry draws the design-vs-defect line, and a test fails any entry that names only defects. The calls worth having are the ones a generic prompt gets backwards: midsole yellowing on sneakers is OXIDATION not soil (and some releases ship pre-yellowed), vachetta patina on a bag is supposed to darken, leather patina on boots is desirable aging, the molded footbed impression on sandals is permanent use that affects resale, and the fold crease at the worn hole is the defining signal on a belt.

AC3 CANNOT BE SATISFIED — verified, not assumed. The AC says ship through shadow -> golden-set eval -> canary. That lifecycle covers the SYSTEM prompt ONLY. GARMENT_CATEGORY_CRITERIA is interpolated into the per-image USER message by buildUserPrompt, and: an ai_prompt_versions row carries one prompt_text which becomes the system block, so no override can reach it; canary picks between two system texts; runEval overrides system text only, so the criteria are ambient on BOTH legs of its comparison; grading-shadow.ts is composite-stage only AND reuses per-image results verbatim, so there is no per-image shadow path at all. Worse, PerImageAnalysis carries no version field, so PER_IMAGE_PROMPT_VERSION never reaches a grade record — bumping it would have looked like compliance and changed nothing.

So the change ships ENV-FLAG GATED (GRADING_CATEGORY_CRITERIA_V2, default OFF), which is the only gate the architecture offers and is the same pattern GRADING_BASELINES / GRADING_TAG_OCR already use. The eleven entries live in a SEPARATE map from the shipped eight, so byte-identity is a property of the file rather than a claim a reviewer has to diff. Composite grades attributed with a +cat2 suffix, appended last per the stated ordering rule.

AC5 DONE and strengthened: byte-identical for the eight with the gate ON, AND a no-op for all twenty with it OFF, so deploying this commit changes no grade. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED four ways — dropped a category entry (AC1 + coverage + disjoint reddened), flipped the gate to default-on (the no-op test reddened), duplicated a key into both maps (only the source-scan caught it, which is exactly why that test is a source scan and not behavioural), and moved +cat2 out of last position (ordering test reddened).

STILL passes:false: AC4 (golden-set cases for the newly-covered categories, tagged for per-category slicing) needs real human-corrected grades on those categories, which do not exist yet — the same bootstrap problem US-1997 Phase 2 has. Until then the flag stays off, and the flag being off is why that is safe rather than merely convenient. The structural fix for AC3 is US-2432.

Also corrected in the same commit: vault/20-domain/grading-prompt-channels.md claimed each block appends a suffix "so accuracy-tracking can attribute an era per block". The suffix records a block PRESENCE, not its CONTENT — editing FABRIC_CRITERIA still reports +fabric — and the per-image stage is not attributed at all. The note now carries the versioned-vs-not split as a third axis alongside trusted/untrusted. | 2026-08-08 AC3 IS NO LONGER IMPOSSIBLE. The note above says the shadow/eval/canary lifecycle CANNOT reach GARMENT_CATEGORY_CRITERIA because it is interpolated into the per-image USER message, and names US-2432 as the structural fix. That fix shipped as US-2438: category_criteria is now one of two blocks in a versioned registry (ai_prompt_block_versions, migration 00563), and runEval takes a blockCandidate that pins exactly that block while the system prompt stays active. So the eval-gate leg of AC3 is available today. TWO CAVEATS, both real: the SHADOW leg is still missing — grading-shadow.ts is composite-stage only and reuses per-image results verbatim, so there is no per-image shadow path to run a category-criteria candidate through, and that is US-2438 AC2 rather than a wiring task here. And AC4 is unchanged and still blocking on its own: a per-category golden set has to come from real human-corrected grades on those categories, which do not exist yet. So GRADING_CATEGORY_CRITERIA_V2 stays OFF and this story stays passes:false — what changed is that the gate is now buildable rather than architecturally unreachable. | 2026-08-09 CORRECTION: THE SHADOW BLOCKER NAMED IN THE NOTE ABOVE IS GONE. That note said 'the SHADOW leg is still missing — grading-shadow.ts is composite-stage only and reuses per-image results verbatim, so there is no per-image shadow path to run a category-criteria candidate through, and that is US-2438 AC2 rather than a wiring task here.' US-2443 shipped that path today: services/edge-functions/src/lib/grading-shadow-per-image.ts re-analyzes every photo under a challenger per-image artifact and re-composites, and ai_prompt_block_versions gained is_shadow / shadow_sample_rate / shadow_daily_cap (migration 00566, HELD) specifically so a BLOCK candidate — which category_criteria is — can be sampled. So all three legs of AC3's lifecycle now exist: shadow (US-2443), eval gate (US-2438), canary (US-896). Recording this because a stale blocker is the specific failure this repo keeps paying for — someone picking this story up would have read the note above, concluded the lifecycle was architecturally unreachable, and stopped. WHAT STILL BLOCKS, unchanged and genuinely: AC4. A per-category golden set has to come from real human-corrected grades on those twelve categories, and they do not exist. Shadow can now MEASURE a category-criteria candidate on live traffic, but AC3 also requires the golden-set eval gate, and a gate with no cases for the new categories cannot pass or fail them — it would report on the eight already covered and say nothing about the twelve this story is about. Also note the per-image shadow path is OFF by default and costs a vision call per photo plus a composite per sampled submission (PER_IMAGE_SHADOW_DAILY_VISION_CAP), so running it is a spend decision, not just a flag flip. GRADING_CATEGORY_CRITERIA_V2 stays OFF and this story stays passes:false on AC4. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-09 (second half of the day): the HELD-migration claim in this story's notes is now STALE. Migrations 00563 and 00566 are on origin/main - verified with git ls-tree against a freshly fetched origin/main, not inferred - and the branch has zero unpushed commits. A held migration is by definition unpushed, so the word is no longer merely out of date, it is an active instruction to stop on a branch that is not frozen. Nothing in this story is blocked on a push. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: pushed is not applied. Whether the SQL has been run against prod is an operator fact this checkout cannot observe, and PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md is the file that tracks it. Read that, not this prose. Recorded because prd-lint caught it the same hour the branch moved, which is the guard working as intended - it went unactioned for weeks before, and a stale freeze cost real sessions. | 2026-08-22 AC4's BOOTSTRAP HAS A WAY OUT, filed as US-2810. The notes above establish that all three lifecycle legs now exist and that AC4 alone blocks: the eval gate needs human-corrected grades on the twelve newly-covered categories and none exist. Correct, and it reads as a dead end because the gate is described as the thing that must happen FIRST. It does not have to. SHADOW runs before the gate, not after. It changes no published grade, so it is available today with no golden set at all — and the divergences it records ARE the raw material AC4 wants. A reviewer correcting a shadow divergence on a real pair of boots produces exactly the human-corrected grade that does not exist. The gate cannot bootstrap itself; shadow can feed it. US-2810 is the runbook for doing that on the three FOOTWEAR categories, which is where the owner's attention is. It is scoped to sneakers, boots and sandals rather than all twelve on purpose: a narrower sample spends less per day and produces cases for the categories being posted now. TWO TRAPS IT NAMES, both of which fail SILENTLY. block_key is a closed vocabulary and a row naming an unknown key is INERT rather than an error, so a typo does nothing quietly. And PER_IMAGE_SHADOW_DAILY_VISION_CAP is unset by default, which reads as 0, which means no shadow runs — so creating the rows without setting that env var also does nothing quietly. Two different causes of 'nothing happened', which is why US-2810 has an AC for proving the rows are actually live. THIS STORY STAYS passes:false and GRADING_CATEGORY_CRITERIA_V2 STAYS OFF. Nothing here changes that, and US-2810 does not flip it either. What changed is that AC4 now has a path rather than a wait.

userStories.title: Backups: mechanism verified, prod backup cron never installed — real RPO is total loss
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want prod data to be recoverable. The scripts are all real and executable (scripts/ops/backup-postgres.sh, backup-storage.sh, restore-postgres.sh, restore-drill.sh) and a restore drill genuinely passed 2026-06-12 (BACKUPS.md:129, 270 RLS policies matched) — but that drill ran against a LOCAL stack at migration 00151. The prod side is unchecked: LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:236-243 has all five boxes unticked, including 'Backup cron installed on the DB host' and 'first nightly dump confirmed in the offsite bucket'; the drill table at :231-234 is empty. PITR is explicitly aspirational (BACKUPS.md:90-92, 'MANUAL: wal-g setup happens on the prod host'). So the documented RPO<=24h / RTO<=2h is only true if a cron nobody confirmed is running. Prod is a SINGLE-NODE self-hosted Postgres (SCALING.md:47) holding grades, billing and the credit ledger.
acceptanceCriteria: Install the backup cron on the prod DB host (BACKUPS.md:42-43) and CONFIRM a dump plus its .sha256 lands in the offsite bucket — verified by listing the bucket, not by reading the runbook.

Run restore-postgres.sh against a REAL offsite dump on a scratch host and record the measured timing in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:231. The 11-second figure at BACKUPS.md:129 came from a near-empty schema-only DB and will not predict prod RTO.
Either stand up wal-g PITR or amend the stated RPO to the honest nightly-dump figure — do not leave a documented RPO the infrastructure cannot deliver.
Tick the five LAUNCH_CHECKLIST boxes only once each is independently verified.

OPERATOR: on the prod DB host, install the backup cron and confirm a dump plus its .sha256 lands in the offsite bucket, then run restore-postgres.sh against a REAL offsite dump on a scratch host and record the measured timing (AC1, AC2, AC4). Until the cron is proven to run, the real RPO is not 24 hours, it is total loss.
userStories.notes: [P1][Ops/DR][LAUNCH BLOCKER] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. This is the single highest-value hour of work in the repo: the ONLY finding in the entire audit whose failure mode is unrecoverable data loss. Everything else degrades; this one ends the company. Note the shape — NOT a missing-mechanism finding. The scripts exist, they work, someone drilled them. It is an ACTIVATION gap: a runbook step marked MANUAL that was never performed, and a checklist that honestly records it was never performed. The danger is that the presence of good tooling reads as protection. | 2026-08-02 AC3's DOCUMENTATION HALF DONE — the runbook no longer states an RPO the infrastructure may not deliver. AC3 says "either stand up wal-g PITR or amend the stated RPO to the honest figure — do not leave a documented RPO the infrastructure cannot deliver." The note was already honest about ONE gap (nightly-dump 24h vs PITR 5min, with a callout saying the 24h figure stands until wal-g is configured) and blind to the bigger one: EVERY number in that Targets section is a property of the backup MECHANISM, and the mechanism running is what was never verified. If the cron is not installed on the prod host, the real RPO is not 24 hours, it is TOTAL LOSS — and the table would have told an operator otherwise at exactly the moment being wrong costs the most. Added a danger callout under Targets stating that, marked LAUNCH BLOCKER, with the two checks that settle it (crontab -l on the DB host should list the backup line from the Setup section; the offsite bucket should hold a dump from the last 24h WITH its .sha256 beside it — a dump with no checksum is a backup nobody has proven readable) and an instruction to replace the callout with the date once both are true. I did NOT assert the cron is missing. I cannot see the prod host, and a runbook that states an unverified fact as fact is the same defect one level down. It says UNVERIFIED and how to verify. WHY THIS WAS WORTH DOING WHILE THE REST IS BLOCKED: AC1, AC2 and AC4 all need someone on the prod host and are genuinely operator work. AC3 is the only half that is a claim rather than an action, and a runbook is read during an incident by someone who will not re-derive it — which is precisely when an overstated recovery point does its damage. The shape is worth remembering and is written into the callout: this is not a missing mechanism. The scripts exist, they work, the restore was drilled on 2026-06-12. It is a runbook step marked MANUAL that nobody performed. STILL OPEN, all operator: install the cron and confirm a dump plus checksum lands offsite (AC1), run restore-postgres.sh against a REAL offsite dump on a scratch host and record the measured timing (AC2), tick the five launch-checklist boxes only once each is independently verified (AC4).

userStories.title: Every alert channel is optional and silently no-ops — nothing proves anyone gets paged
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want a SEV1 to reach a human. Today every channel degrades to silence when unconfigured. .github/workflows/uptime.yml:46 marks UPTIME_ALERT_WEBHOOK 'Optional' and scripts/ops/uptime-check.mjs:188 logs 'not set — skipping webhook channel' then continues. Edge-side, ops-events.ts:104-108 falls back to MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK, which ENV_REFERENCE.md:168 marks as not set. ops-events.ts:242-244 records an ops_event.alert_undelivered metric when neither channel exists — a metric that itself has no alert. INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md:42-46 asserts all three sources 'must point at the same on-call channel before launch', which is an instruction, not a verified state; LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:264-268 leaves it unchecked. The only channel that works with zero config is the GitHub uptime issue fallback, which pages only if repo-watch mobile notifications happen to be on.
acceptanceCriteria: Set UPTIME_ALERT_WEBHOOK and MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK, then RUN THE DRILL: break a target, confirm the message arrives on a phone, record the date in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md. Configuration is not evidence.

Make alert_undelivered loud rather than a silent metric — fail at boot (or emit at critical) when production has no alert channel configured. A monitoring system that cannot page is worse than none, because it produces false confidence.
Confirm Sentry alert routing actually delivers (LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:264) — see also the webhook dead-letter story, which routes ONLY to Sentry.
Measure detection latency against the 15-minute ack target in INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md:33 — a 10-minute GitHub cron plus jitter can consume most of it before a human is notified.

OPERATOR: run the delivery drill (AC1). /health/ready already reports features.alerting = ok, so at least one channel is CONFIGURED - what is unproven is whether a message ARRIVES. A configured webhook pointing at a dead endpoint reports ok here forever, so configuration is not the question. Fire a test alert and confirm it reaches a human.
userStories.notes: [P1][Ops/Alerting][LAUNCH BLOCKER] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. Pairs with the backup story: that one is about surviving a disaster, this one is about LEARNING there is one. Every other alerting improvement is worthless until these two secrets are set and drilled, because they are the last mile for all of them. | 2026-07-19 AC2 DONE (partially — see below); AC1/AC3/AC4 still need you. AC2 asked to make alert_undelivered loud rather than a silent metric, because 'a monitoring system that cannot page is worse than none, because it produces false confidence'. Added an 'alerting' feature group to env-validation: in PRODUCTION ONLY, a deploy with none of MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK / MONITOR_ALERT_EMAIL / SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL set now reports DEGRADED on /health/ready and warns at boot, instead of the current state where every channel silently no-ops and nothing says so. Non-production is exempt via enabledWhen — a dev box has no business paging anyone, and warning there would train people to ignore the warning. ANY channel satisfies it, deliberately: the failure being caught is 'none of them', not 'not the one I expected'. I did NOT make it fatal at boot, which AC2 offered as an option. Refusing to start the edge because no webhook is configured would convert a monitoring gap into a total outage — strictly worse than the problem, and the opposite of the fail-open reasoning applied in US-2013. Degraded-and-loud is the right severity for 'we cannot tell you when things break'. STILL BLOCKED ON YOU and this is the launch-blocker part: AC1 (set the two secrets, break a target, confirm the message reaches a phone, record the date in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md), AC3 (confirm Sentry routing delivers) and AC4 (measure detection latency against the 15-minute ack target). Configuration is not evidence and neither is a degraded-flag — this story stays open until a human has watched an alert arrive. Note US-2004's cron stall detector is now proven to detect, so it is queued up behind exactly this last mile. | 2026-08-02 MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION, and fixed a reporting bug the measurement exposed. AC2's health surface WORKS: GET /health/ready reports features.alerting = "ok", so at least one channel (MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK / MONITOR_ALERT_EMAIL / SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL) IS configured in prod. That is worth recording plainly, because AC1's framing assumed none were set. What is still unproven is whether a message actually ARRIVES — AC1's drill is about delivery, not configuration, and a configured webhook pointing at a dead endpoint reports "ok" here forever. THE BUG THE SAME CURL FOUND: features.observability returned the literal string "missing: " — nothing after the colon. The cause is a group whose satisfiedWhen fails while every var it LISTS is present. observability requires SENTRY_DSN plus a real RELEASE_SHA; the DSN is set, so the `miss` array is empty, and the message named nothing. An operator reading that at 3am is told something is missing and refused the name of it, which is worse than no line at all because it costs them the time to go looking. FIXED in computeFeatureReadiness and warnMissingFeatureGroups: when nothing is literally absent, the message now says the vars are all present and the check still rejected one, instead of an empty list. Two tests pin both paths — the all-present case, and the regression that a genuinely absent var must still be NAMED, which is the whole value of the line for every other group. WORTH BEING PRECISE ABOUT WHAT observability's DEGRADED MEANS, since "missing" read alarmingly and I nearly reported it that way: Sentry IS configured and IS receiving events. The group is degraded solely because RELEASE_SHA is "dev" — US-2001's problem, reported here as a second symptom. So the dead-letter path in US-2011 does reach Sentry; its events are simply untagged and unattributable to a commit. One Coolify rebuild with the GIT_SHA build arg clears BOTH this line and US-2001. STILL OPEN AND ALL OPERATOR WORK: AC1's drill (break a target, confirm the page lands on a phone, date it in the launch checklist), AC3 (confirm Sentry routing delivers — see US-2011, which routes ONLY to Sentry), AC4 (measure detection latency against the 15-minute ack target; a 10-minute cron plus jitter can consume most of it before a human is notified). None is a code change and none can be done from a checkout. VERIFIED: edge suite 5092 passed / 0 failed, deno lint clean across 1291 files. | 2026-08-15 THE HEALTH LINE NOW AGREES WITH THIS STORY. /health/ready reported alerting: ok, which is a claim about CONFIGURATION and was reading as a claim about monitoring. This story exists because the two are different, and its criterion already said so: a configured webhook pointing at a dead endpoint reports ok here forever. TWO WAYS ok CAN BE TRUE AND USELESS, both now named on the line itself: a webhook URL that resolves nowhere, and SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL alone satisfying the group while depending on the same mail path whose DELIVERY is unproven (see the smtp group, corrected in the same pass). So alerting: ok could be satisfied entirely by an email address, sent through a mailer that drops everything, and nothing said so. THE GROUP ARGUED FOR THIS ITSELF: its own comment says a production deploy with no channel should say so rather than reporting a healthy monitoring posture it does not have. That was written about the UNSET case; the bare ok was doing the same thing from the other side. AC1 IS UNCHANGED AND IS STILL THE ONLY REAL PROOF: fire one test alert and confirm a human receives it. | 2026-08-22 AC2 IS BUILT. AC1/AC3/AC5 stay operator (the drill), AC4 is a cadence question nobody has measured.  AC2 asked to make alert_undelivered loud rather than a silent metric. Done in two places, and the second one is a gap this story never named.  AT BOOT: main.ts logs edge.boot.no_alert_channel at error when isProduction() and no env channel is set, checking MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK, MONITOR_ALERT_EMAIL and SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL. LOGGED, NOT FATAL, and that is the decision rather than an omission - AC2 offers 'fail at boot (or emit at critical)', and refusing to start would trade a blind monitor for a dead service. The edge handles grading, payments and eBay writes; none of them get safer by being off. A deploy that cannot page is a serious problem and is not a reason to stop taking money. A test fails if Deno.exit or a throw ever appears in that block.  NEW hasEnvAlertChannel() reads the ENVIRONMENT only and deliberately not system_settings: this is a boot-time question and a monitoring check that can hang the start-up of the thing it monitors is its own outage. A settings-only configuration therefore reads as 'none' and still works at dispatch - a false alarm in the safe direction for an alarm whose text is 'go and check your alert channels'. A BLANK variable is not a channel, which matters because a dashboard variable set to '' is SET as far as the shell is concerned and pages nobody.  AT DISPATCH, AND THIS IS THE GAP THE STORY DID NOT NAME. dispatchOpsAlert recorded alert_undelivered when `!email && !webhook` - when nothing was CONFIGURED. It recorded NOTHING when channels were configured and every one of them FAILED. That is the worse of the two: a webhook failure at least dead-letters, but an email-only deployment whose send fails left a warn-level exception and an outcome object nobody reads, while /health/ready reported alerting: ok throughout. The condition is now `!emailOk && !webhookOk` - 'did this land anywhere', not 'was anything set up' - and it raises through captureException so it arrives via Sentry, the one channel that does not depend on the configuration that just failed.  THE OLD METRIC IS KEPT AND NOW MEANS THE NARROWER THING IT ALWAYS SAID: nothing was configured at all. That distinction is the actionable half - it tells an operator whether to set a variable or to go and look at a broken endpoint - and a test fails if it is dropped.  SEVERITY IS THE EVENT'S OWN, not a blanket critical. A lost `info` event is not worth waking anyone, and treating it as critical is how a page becomes something people mute.  SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 8 OF 8, and the first run left ONE BLIND, which was mine rather than the code's: 'the boot check becomes fatal' passed green. My guard sliced forward from the edge.boot.no_alert_channel string, so a Deno.exit(1) inserted one line ABOVE the logEvent call sat outside the window. Read the whole `if` body or the check covers half of it. Re-sliced from the guard condition to the first column-0 brace; all eight now redden. The other seven caught on the first run: a blank variable counting as a channel, SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL dropped from the list, dispatch keying on configuration again, the capture removed, the narrower metric dropped, the boot check firing outside production, and the boot check removed entirely.  VERIFIED: deno check clean on lib and main, deno lint clean on all three files, ops-events_test.ts 14 passed / 0 failed (6 new), env-validation + release-identity 46 passed / 0 failed.  STILL OPEN. AC1/AC3/AC5 are the DRILL and nothing in this repo can stand in for it: break a target, confirm the message arrives on a phone, record the date. /health/ready reporting alerting: ok is a claim about configuration, and the line now says so itself. AC4 is unmeasured - the Uptime workflow's 10-minute cron plus GitHub's best-effort jitter plus its own 2-consecutive-failure threshold can consume most of the 15-minute ack target before a human is notified, and nobody has put numbers on that. It is arithmetic over the workflow's own schedule rather than an operator task, so it could be closed from here by someone who decides what the target should be. | 2026-08-22 AC4 IS ANSWERED, MEASURED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. That leaves AC1/AC3/AC5 (the drill) as the only open items.  AC4 asked to measure detection latency against the 15-minute SEV1 ack target, noting that 'a 10-minute GitHub cron plus jitter CAN consume most of it'. It does not consume most of it. It exceeds it, at the median.  MEASURED over 99 consecutive scheduled Uptime runs, 2026-08-21T00:13Z to 2026-08-22T06:06Z, from `gh run list --workflow=Uptime --json startedAt,event` filtered to event=schedule (workflow_dispatch runs are manual and say nothing about the schedule):   scheduled cadence  10.0 min   min                 9.8 min   median             17.2 min   p90                24.4 min   max                43.0 min   mean               18.1 min   ran on schedule (<= 10 min):  1 of 99 ONE interval out of ninety-nine hit the cadence the cron declares.  DETECTION LATENCY is a full interval of blindness (the outage starts just after a passing check) plus the 30s CONFIRM_DELAY_MS re-check plus the run itself:   median          18.0 min  EXCEEDS the 15-minute target   p90             25.2 min  EXCEEDS   worst observed  43.8 min  EXCEEDS So the alert typically arrives AFTER the deadline it is supposed to feed. Not in the tail - at the median.  THE FRAMING WAS THE PROBLEM, not the cron. Both the workflow and vault/10-ops/uptime-monitoring.md said GitHub cron is 'best-effort (a run can start a few minutes late)'. A few minutes late is a rounding error against a 15-minute target and reads as acceptable; 1.7x the schedule at the median and 4.3x at the worst is a different decision. Both now carry the measurement instead of the reassurance, and both say plainly that the 10-minute cadence stays as the launch baseline while the claim that it MEETS the ack target does not.  NEW scripts/ops/uptime-cadence.mjs makes it repeatable rather than a number in a note. Read-only (one `gh run list`, nothing writes), exits NON-ZERO while the target is unmet, and has a --json mode. A number in a note is true on the day it is written and GitHub's scheduler load moves; the honest form of this finding is something anyone can re-run before deciding whether the vendor-check upgrade is still needed. It resolves the gh binary itself, because gh is not on PATH on the Windows box.  WHAT IT DOES NOT DECIDE. Whether to move the target or add the 1-minute vendor check (vault/10-ops/uptime-monitoring.md section 5) is an owner call about what a SEV1 ack is worth, not something a measurement settles. What the measurement removes is the option of leaving both claims standing - a 15-minute target and a detector that cannot serve it.  ONE THING THIS DOES NOT MEASURE, and it cuts the other way: the GitHub issue and webhook are not the only paths. An edge that is up-but-degraded emits its own ops alerts through dispatchOpsAlert immediately, and Sentry fires on its own schedule. This latency is specifically for the case the Uptime workflow exists to catch - the edge or SPA being unreachable from outside - which is the case where nothing inside can report anything.  VERIFIED: eslint clean on the new script, vault:lint clean at 197 notes, the script re-run at two sample sizes (99 intervals and 29) with consistent shape - median 17.2/16.3, onSchedule 1 in both. | [2026-09-02][PROD READ] MEASURED, not inferred: no alert has anywhere to go. Source: scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql run read-only against prod over SSH on 2026-09-02 (container supabase-db-kcksoks4kk0kswk0ccs40os8, 29 sections, 0 SQL errors). Raw output kept out of the repo; it contains customer data. system_settings holds both ops_alert_email and ops_alert_webhook_url as rows with value_length 0, unchanged since 2026-06-14. So the "silently no-ops" in this story's title is the live production state, and nothing proves anyone gets an alert because nobody does. Setting either value is a Coolify/settings action and stays operator; the code half of this story is unaffected.

userStories.title: eBay Media API: video upload for listings
userStories.description: As a clothing seller, I want to add video to my listings to lift conversion. Today images are passed as external URLs only (InventoryItemPayload.imageUrls) and there is no video support. Integrate the eBay Media API (/commerce/media) to upload video and attach it to listings.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge can createVideo -> uploadVideo -> poll getVideo to a terminal status, and attach the resulting id via product.videoIds on createOrReplaceInventoryItem

TRANSCODE DECISION MADE AND WRITTEN DOWN: eBay accepts .mp4 H.264/AVC only, and iPhones record HEVC by default. Either the client transcodes before upload, or the edge does, or HEVC is rejected with a message that tells the seller how to fix it. Silently failing on the most common input is not an option

PUBLISH-ORDERING DECISION MADE: processing is async and terminal status is not immediate, so either publish waits for LIVE, or publish proceeds without video and a later revise attaches it. Whichever is chosen, a seller never ends up with a listing that permanently lacks the video they added
BLOCKED is handled as a moderation outcome, not an error: it is terminal and expected, and the seller is told their video was rejected rather than shown a retry that cannot succeed
Video upload gets its own validation path. The US-276 hardening (validateImageUpload / stripImageMetadata) is image-only and does NOT cover video, which also carries GPS/EXIF-equivalent metadata
iOS/web can add a video during compose and see it reflected on the published listing
Respects the Media API POST rate limit (50 requests / 5 seconds, per user)

OPERATOR: two facts need a human with a browser on eBay's docs, and nothing is built yet. Max video duration (believed 1 minute) and videos-per-listing (believed 1) remain unconfirmed from a primary source. Confirmed already: max file size 150 MB / 157,286,400 bytes, classification should be ITEM, eBay accepts .mp4 H.264/AVC only, and playlists are generated only once a video reaches LIVE - so a poll that stops before LIVE has no playable URL to attach. ⚠ DO NOT SPEND MORE AGENT ATTEMPTS ON THE DOCS. Five fetches failed across two sessions on four distinct URLs plus the edp.ebay.com mirror, each exceeding 60s. That is a recorded conclusion, not a run of bad luck: every eBay doc fact in this repo now comes from search summaries, the generated SDKs or the community forum until someone opens a page by hand. The two open decisions are also yours and they gate the build: AC2, whether the client transcodes HEVC before upload or the server does (iPhones record HEVC by default and eBay takes H.264 only), and AC3, whether publish waits for LIVE or proceeds without the video and attaches it later.
userStories.notes:
[P3][Edge/Media] iOS listing-lifecycle audit 2026-07-14. No Media API; images external-URL only (InventoryItemPayload.imageUrls). Nice-to-have; video is a real apparel conversion lever. 

INVESTIGATED 2026-07-18. Confirmed greenfield: no videoId / commerce-media / uploadVideo reference anywhere in services/edge-functions/src or src. Two findings change the shape of this story.

FINDING 1 — NOT SCOPE-BLOCKED, contrary to the obvious assumption. The Media API's createVideo requires sell.inventory, which is ALREADY in our production grant (ebay-client.ts:233). This story therefore does NOT depend on US-1421 (restricted-scope acquisition) and does not need a new seller consent round. Attachment is also on the path we already use: product.videoIds on createOrReplaceInventoryItem — a sibling of the product.imageUrls we already send at ebay-client.ts:2163 — NOT a Trading-API-only feature as the AddItem/VideoDetails docs might suggest. So the integration surface is much smaller than the P3 implies: the eBay side is three new calls plus one extra field on a payload we already build.

FINDING 2 — THE REAL COST IS TRANSCODING, AND IT LANDS ON AC2. eBay accepts .mp4 MPEG-4 Part 10 / AVC (H.264) only. iPhones have defaulted to HEVC / H.265 since iOS 11 unless the user changed Camera > Formats to 'Most Compatible'. AC2 specifically promises iOS compose. So the single most likely real-world input is a format eBay will not accept, and the failure would surface late — after upload, as PROCESSING_FAILED — which is the worst place to discover it. Whoever picks this up should size the transcode decision FIRST, because it dominates the estimate: client-side transcode, server-side transcode (ffmpeg in the Deno container, which is a real image-size and CPU change on Coolify), or explicit rejection. The eBay calls are the easy part.

FLOW: createVideo returns 201 with the video id in the Location header -> uploadVideo sends the bytes -> poll getVideo. Statuses PENDING_UPLOAD -> PROCESSING -> LIVE, with BLOCKED and PROCESSING_FAILED as the other terminal states. BLOCKED is a moderation verdict rather than a fault, so it needs its own message; a generic retry there loops forever. Rate limit is 50 POSTs / 5s per user.

ALSO: AC3's original wording ('routes through the hardened fetch path') is misleading and has been rewritten. Our upload hardening is image-specific — validateImageUpload magic-byte-sniffs for images and stripImageMetadata drops EXIF/GPS from images. Neither does anything for an .mp4, which carries its own location metadata. Video needs a parallel validator, not a reuse of the image one.

NOT CONFIRMED, flagged rather than guessed: max file size, max duration, and how many videos a single listing accepts. eBay's docs point at Seller Center for those numbers and I could not retrieve them (developer.ebay.com WebFetch timed out twice; the above is from eBay doc search summaries, not the doc pages read directly). Confirm those three numbers against the live docs before implementing, since max-duration in particular shapes the compose UX. | 2026-08-12 THE THREE UNCONFIRMED NUMBERS ARE CONFIRMED, AND AC2 IS DECIDED. SOURCING CAVEAT FIRST, because it matters for how much weight to put on these: developer.ebay.com WebFetch timed out a THIRD time (createVideo, managing-video-media, uploadVideo, and the edp.ebay.com mirror all exceeded 60s), so these come from search-result summaries of those same doc pages plus eBay seller help, not from the pages read directly. Multiple independent results agreed on every number below, but re-check them against the live docs when you have a browser. MAX FILE SIZE: 150 MB, stated as exactly 157,286,400 bytes. MAX DURATION: 1 minute. VIDEOS PER LISTING: exactly 1 - so the compose UX is add-or-replace, never a gallery, which simplifies AC6 considerably. FORMAT: .mp4, H.264 video with AAC audio (eBay seller help also names .mov, but that is the web UI which transcodes for you; the API path is the mp4/H.264 one this story already assumed). A FOURTH FACT NOBODY HAD, and it is load-bearing: createVideo takes the byte size as metadata and the uploaded stream must match it EXACTLY, or the video does not upload and eBay may block the seller from uploading. PROCESSING_FAILED is documented as covering all three of corrupted / too large / size does not match the metadata - so a size mismatch surfaces as the SAME terminal status as a genuinely broken file, which means the edge has to know its own byte count precisely rather than trusting a client-declared length, and cannot distinguish the two after the fact. Status flow confirmed as PENDING_UPLOAD -> PROCESSING -> one of LIVE / PROCESSING_FAILED / BLOCKED, with BLOCKED documented as malware or the video moderation feature - i.e. a verdict, which is exactly what AC4 assumed. AC2 DECISION: TRANSCODE ON THE CLIENT THAT CAUSES THE PROBLEM, REJECT EVERYWHERE ELSE WITH A MESSAGE. Not server-side ffmpeg, and the reason is concrete rather than aesthetic: it would add ~70-100 MB to the Deno image and put a CPU-heavy transcode of a file up to 150 MB on a single-replica edge that per US-2010 still has no second replica and strands in-flight work for 6-15 minutes on every deploy. Buying a transcoder with that is the wrong trade. iOS has AVAssetExportSession natively and is the platform whose HEVC default creates the problem in the first place, so iOS transcodes before upload; Android has androidx.media3.transformer if it ever composes. Web and every other input gets sniffed and, if it is not H.264 mp4, REFUSED with a message naming the fix (Camera > Formats > Most Compatible on iOS, or export as H.264). That satisfies AC2 third branch honestly rather than silently failing on the most common input, which is the one thing the AC rules out. WHAT IS LEFT is the build itself and it spans three trees: the edge three-call flow plus product.videoIds (AC1), a video-specific validator since US-276 hardening is image-only and an .mp4 carries its own location metadata (AC5), the publish-ordering decision (AC3), and iOS/web compose (AC6), plus the 50-POST/5s per-user limiter (AC7). The estimate is no longer blocked on unknowns. | 2026-08-12 AC5 SUBSTANTIALLY DONE, AND I STOPPED DELIBERATELY BEFORE AC1 - the reason is the useful part. WHAT SHIPPED (0d0997c0 + follow-up): the codec gate. My own brief called AC5 greenfield and that was WRONG - validateVideoUpload has existed since US-1763 and already sniffs magic bytes, enforces a format allowlist, and caps bytes and duration, and grade.ts:543 already uses it. What it did NOT do is read the CODEC, which is the case AC2 is actually about: eBay takes H.264 only and an .mp4 container says nothing about what is inside it. isoBmffVideoCodec walks moov > trak > mdia > minf > stbl > stsd and checks each trak hdlr for "vide", skipping audio tracks - reading trak[0] blindly returns mp4a and calls a good H.264 file non-H.264. Fail-open on an unreadable header, matching the duration parser, because a faststart-less file hides moov behind mdat and refusing on unknown would block valid uploads. Exposed as an opt-in allowCodecs option so the existing US-1763 grading path does NOT start rejecting HEVC; the refusal message names Camera > Formats > Most Compatible, because catching this before a 150 MB upload is pointless if the seller is not told how to fix it. Nine cases, five sabotages each watched failing (hdlr check dropped, HEVC folded into the H.264 set, sample entry read four bytes early, the allowlist made inert, the allowlist inverted). WHY I STOPPED AT AC1 RATHER THAN CONTINUING: it needs somewhere to record the eBay video id and its status per listing, and listings.platform_fields is explicitly NOT that - 00113 own header says "The eBay draft keeps its dedicated columns" and the blob is keyed by NON-eBay platform.
