So AC1 needs a migration, and there is already ONE held migration (00590) blocking the push. Adding a second, for code that nothing can call until AC6 ships client compose, would be shipped-but-unwired with a prod-apply attached - the exact combination vault/70-agent/shipped-but-unwired.md exists to warn about. WHAT IS LEFT, in the order it should be built: AC1 (createVideo -> uploadVideo -> getVideo plus product.videoIds, and the storage decision - a new listings column or a small table), AC3 (publish proceeds WITHOUT the video and a DURABLE job attaches it on LIVE; the AC requirement that a seller never permanently lacks the video they added is exactly why it must be a locked job with retries and a terminal state, not a fire-and-forget promise), AC4 (BLOCKED is a moderation verdict, terminal, and needs its own message - PROCESSING_FAILED is a different one because the docs also use it for a size mismatch), AC7 (50 POSTs / 5s per user), AC6 (iOS/web compose). THE LOAD-BEARING DETAIL FOR WHOEVER BUILDS AC1: createVideo takes the byte size as metadata and the uploaded stream must match EXACTLY, and a mismatch surfaces as the same PROCESSING_FAILED as a corrupt file - so the edge must compute its own byte count and never trust a client-declared length. VERIFIED: deno lint 1505 files, deno check, full edge suite 6566 passed / 0 failed. | 2026-08-15 THE HELD-MIGRATION WORDING ABOVE IS HISTORICAL, RESOLVED. The owner applied every outstanding migration and pushed main; origin/main and local are the same commit, PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md lists no HELD section, and the session-context hook reports none. So nothing in this story is waiting on a prod apply and the branch is not frozen on its account. Recorded as an appended correction rather than by editing the sentence, because these notes are append-only and prd-lint resolves by segment order. WHY THIS GETS ITS OWN NOTE INSTEAD OF BEING LEFT TO ROT: HELD is not a status, it is an instruction to stop, and a stale one tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not. That has cost real sessions in this repo (US-2286's 2026-08-09 note says so explicitly). VERIFY IT RATHER THAN TRUST THIS: curl -fsS https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready | jq .schema — US-2603 added a missing[] listing versions this build ships that the database never recorded, which is the check a bare status:match cannot do. | 2026-08-15 STATUS CORRECTION, formal: no migration named in this story is held. Every outstanding migration is applied to prod and main is pushed (origin/main == local). The previous segment said this in words prd-lint does not recognise, so the guard kept warning; this one uses the token it reads. | 2026-08-17 A CONSTRAINT NOBODY HAD, AND IT CHANGES THE DESIGN: eBay DELETES an API-uploaded video when its retention expires, and the window was cut from 365 days to 30.  SOURCING, STATED FIRST because it decides how much weight to put on this. The generated SDK model (github luongtran/sdk-ebay-rest-media, docs/Model/Video.md) documents an expirationDate field, verbatim: "automatically set to 365 days (one year) after the video initial upload". Chasing what that field MEANS led to an eBay Developers Program community thread answered by eBay staff (developer_support@ebay): "Videos uploaded through the Media API are retained by eBay for 365 days", videos are DELETED after the retention period, and - the load-bearing part - "Starting April 8th, 2024, this retention window was reduced to 30 days for newly uploaded videos", with existing videos keeping their original 365. A listing still referencing an expired video no longer displays it.  SO A 30-DAY CLOCK STARTS AT UPLOAD. FlipDesk listings routinely outlive a month - that is the ordinary case, not the tail. As specified, this feature would put a video on a listing and let it silently vanish four weeks later, on a listing that is still live and still selling. Nothing in ACs 1-7 accounts for that; AC3 reasons only about the gap between upload and LIVE, which is minutes, and the real gap is the one between LIVE and deletion.  WHAT THAT ADDS TO THE STORY, and it should be decided before any code: either re-upload on a schedule (getVideo before expiry, createVideo again, revise the listing to the new videoId - which multiplies the rate-limit and bandwidth cost by however long a listing lives), or set the expectation with the seller at compose time (this video expires in 30 days), or attach video only to listings expected to be short-lived. All three are worse than the story assumed, and picking one is a product decision rather than an implementation detail.  RE-VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING: the 30-day figure is from a community thread, not from a doc page read directly. It is specific, dated and staff-attributed, which is why it is recorded rather than ignored - but a number this load-bearing should be confirmed against the live Media API docs by someone with a real browser.  ⚠ AND THAT IS NOW A KNOWN LIMIT RATHER THAN BAD LUCK: developer.ebay.com CANNOT BE FETCHED BY THIS TOOLING. The 2026-08-12 note recorded three timeouts and said "re-check them against the live docs when you have a browser". Two more attempts today - createVideo and the Media API overview - each exceeded 60s. That is five failures across two sessions on four distinct URLs plus the edp.ebay.com mirror. Stop spending attempts on it: "when you have a browser" means a HUMAN browser, and every eBay doc fact in this repo is going to come from search summaries, the generated SDKs, or the community forum until someone opens one by hand.  CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY THIS PASS: max file size 150 MB / 157,286,400 bytes (search results agree with the earlier note). Also new and small: classification should be set to ITEM, and playlists are only generated once a video reaches LIVE - so a poll that stops before LIVE has no playable URL to attach. STILL UNCONFIRMED FROM A PRIMARY SOURCE: max duration (1 minute) and videos-per-listing (1). Both remain as the earlier note left them. | 2026-08-22 THE 'STOP TRYING' CONCLUSION HOLDS, and now has a control. MEASURED 2026-08-22: developer.ebay.com timed out again at 60s (the sixth failure across three sessions and five distinct URLs plus the edp.ebay.com mirror). What is NEW is the control: pe.usps.com was fetched successfully FOUR times in the same session, including a dense multi-service rate table. So this is not a slow network or a blocked environment - it is eBay's developer documentation specifically. That narrows the conclusion from 'docs are unreliable here' to 'eBay's are unreachable and other carriers' are not', which is worth knowing before anyone spends another attempt. The recorded instruction stands: eBay doc facts come from search summaries, the generated SDKs or the community forum until someone opens a page by hand.

userStories.title: Authenticity tell coverage follows brand-pack order, not counterfeit prevalence
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want tell coverage driven by what actually gets faked, because an add-on a seller can buy for any brand currently has real depth for three (CANONICAL_TELLS: louisvuitton, coach, gucci) and legacy free-text {tell, detail} rows for the rest, which brand-authenticity.ts coerces to category 'other' with no redFlag and which therefore contribute almost nothing to the verdict. The 37 migrations that mention authentication_tells were written in brand-pack order — luxury first because that pack came first — not from any ranking of counterfeit exposure. Nike, adidas, Supreme, BAPE, Moncler, Canada Goose, The North Face and Patagonia are among the most-counterfeited apparel brands in the world and sit in packs whose tells were never structured. US-2139 fixes the SHAPE and the depth of what we have; this story fixes WHICH BRANDS we invest in next and why.
acceptanceCriteria: A written, sourced prioritization of brands by counterfeit exposure crossed with our own submission volume, recorded in the vault as a decision note rather than in a commit message.
The top-ranked brands get structured, sourced, verified tells with redFlags — not free-text rows.

The add-on's purchasability is reconciled with coverage: a brand with no verified tells either cannot be purchased for, or is sold with an explicit stated limitation. Silent degradation to generic reasoning is not acceptable for a paid add-on.
Coverage is measurable: a query or admin view reports verified-tell count per brand so the gap is visible instead of anecdotal.
No claim about detection accuracy is published anywhere until the authenticity golden set (US-2131) can support it.

OPERATOR: AC1 needs SOURCED counterfeit-exposure figures from outside this repo, and AC2 is the seeding that follows. Half of AC1 is already available - submission volume is in our own database and scripts/brand-style-coverage.mjs --db shows the query shape - but the exposure half needs external sources, and a ranking assembled from recollection is the exact failure this corpus documents as its worst (the RN 17257 / Longchamp trap: a real record, the right brand string, completely the wrong company). WHERE THE CORPUS ITSELF POINTS, needing no external source: the packs headers repeatedly note Nike, adidas, Supreme, BAPE, Moncler, Canada Goose, The North Face and Patagonia as heavily counterfeited, and every one sits in a pack whose tells were written in the legacy shape. THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE RANKING, already done: all 179 seeded tell payloads use the legacy {tell, detail} shape and ZERO use the structured one, so they are prose the prompt reads and the verdict cannot use.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Authenticity/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Coverage today follows brand-pack authoring order, which put luxury first. Nike/adidas/Supreme/BAPE/Moncler/Canada Goose/TNF/Patagonia sit in packs whose tells were never structured. Pairs with US-2139 (shape) — this one is about which brands get invested in next. | 2026-07-28 SHIPPED except AC1's sourced ranking and AC2's seeding (both deferred with reasons). Commit 2c95f59, no migration.
THE PREMISE WAS UNDERSTATED, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS THE MAIN RESULT. The story says coverage follows brand-pack authoring order. The real state is worse and more precise: ALL 179 seeded authentication_tells payloads across the packs use the LEGACY {tell, detail} shape, and ZERO use the structured one. coerceTell maps a legacy entry to category "other" with no redFlag, so those 179 payloads are PROSE THE PROMPT READS AND THE VERDICT CANNOT USE. On top of that CANONICAL_TELLS holds 7 structured tells across 3 brands, every one sourced to "seed:... (unverified — review in admin)". So the distinction that actually matters is between HAVING TELLS and HAVING USABLE TELLS, and almost the entire corpus is on the wrong side of it. A test pins the 179/0 split and instructs the next reader to UPDATE its floor rather than delete it when US-2139 re-shapes the rows.
THAT REFRAMED THE STORY. The useful question was not "which brands to prioritize" but "what does a PAID add-on owe a buyer when it has almost nothing to check against" — because before this, a brand with no usable tells still produced a confident-looking assessment from generic reasoning and NOTHING in the output said so. That is the part a buyer would object to, and it needed no new data to fix. AC3 DONE and it is the substance of this commit. AC4 DONE: classifyTellCoverage reports level/total/actionable/categories, which is the per-brand measurement the AC asked for.
DECISION TAKEN AND RECORDED (vault/20-domain/authenticity-coverage-priority.md, type: decision, revisit_by 2026-10-31): DISCLOSE AND CAP RATHER THAN BLOCK THE SALE. Two answers were defensible — refuse the purchase when coverage is thin, or sell with a mandatory disclosure plus a confidence cap. Took the second: a general construction-and-finishing assessment has real value to some buyers even without brand tells, and what is NOT defensible is charging for it while IMPLYING brand-specific authentication. purchaseDisclosure() returns a non-null string the offer surface cannot render without. Blocking remains available and is a PRODUCT call, not an engineering one — revisit if buyers report the disclosure is insufficient.
CAPS: 0.6 with no tells, 0.75 with inert ones, composing by MIN with US-2218's reference cap. Two coarse bands again rather than a gradient, same reasoning: we know an assessment with nothing to check against rested on generic reasoning and we do NOT know how much that costs; the golden set (US-2131) is what should set real numbers. Never raises. The limitation text is written in terms of what WE hold, never the garment — a test asserts it contains no counterfeit/fake/suspect/inauthentic/replica.
ONE TRAP AVOIDED, worth knowing: the new `tells` parameter on normalizeAuthenticityAssessment is OPTIONAL and absent means "NOT MEASURED", not "none". Defaulting it to [] would have classified every existing caller as having zero coverage and silently capped them all — the exact silent-degradation failure this story exists to end, reintroduced from the other direction. A test pins that an existing caller passing no tells is byte-identical.
AC1 DEFERRED, WITH THE REASON WRITTEN DOWN. The AC asks for a SOURCED ranking by counterfeit exposure crossed with our submission volume. Half is available — volume is in our own database and scripts/brand-style-coverage.mjs --db already shows that query's shape. The other half is not: counterfeit-exposure figures need external sources I could not obtain from this sandbox, and a ranking assembled from recollection would be precisely the failure this corpus documents as its most dangerous (the RN 17257 / Longchamp trap — a real record, the right brand string, completely the wrong company). So the RANKING is deliberately NOT recorded; the METHOD is, plus one observation needing no external source: the packs' own headers repeatedly note that Nike, adidas, Supreme, BAPE, Moncler, Canada Goose, The North Face and Patagonia are heavily counterfeited, and every one of them sits in a pack whose tells were written in the legacy shape. That is where the corpus itself points for the first pass.
AC2 DEFERRED (seeding verified tells is the same sourcing project). AC5 HOLDS: nothing in this commit publishes an accuracy number, and the caps are explicitly documented as placeholders until the golden set can measure them.
VERIFICATION: 4703 edge tests pass, 15 new in authenticity-coverage_test.ts; the 8 failures are the same pre-existing imagescript-FFI / network-timeout sandbox artifacts confirmed against a clean tree in US-2210. deno lint clean; zero new type errors. | ⚠ 2026-08-22 CORRECTION, and it is a safety one rather than a tidy-up. This story's notes say the edge suite has 8 pre-existing failures that are imagescript-FFI and network-timeout artifacts of substituted deps, because deno.land and esm.sh were blocked in the sandbox. THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE ON THIS HOST.  MEASURED TODAY: the full edge suite ran 8311 passed / 0 failed / 261 ignored, exit code 0, with both registries reachable. There is no red baseline.  WHY THIS IS WORTH A NOTE INSTEAD OF LEAVING IT. A sentence telling the next reader to expect 8 failures teaches them to look at a red suite and move on. That is the one direction a stale note costs something real: a genuine regression arrives looking exactly like the noise they were told about, and it gets waved through. The same correction has been applied to US-2210, US-2218 and US-2219, which all carry the identical sentence.  The rule now: a deno failure IS your regression. If the suite is red here, something in the working tree did it.

userStories.title: Authentication tells are text-only — there is no known-genuine reference imagery to check a font, stitch or stamp against
userStories.description: As a reviewer or a grading model, I want a picture of what genuine looks like, because half our tell taxonomy is VISUAL and cannot be verified from prose. Verified: brand-authenticity.ts defines 11 tell categories including stitching, font, stamp, hardware and construction, and CANONICAL_TELLS's own text admits the gap — the Louis Vuitton stamp tell says to 'compare letter spacing/shape to a KNOWN-GENUINE REFERENCE' and no such reference exists anywhere in the system. A tell whose check instruction depends on an artifact we do not have is not a checkable rule. This is distinct from US-2139 (tell DEPTH and counterfeit-side modelling) and US-2138 (decoder cross-checks): this is the missing evidence layer both of those assume.
acceptanceCriteria: A reference-image store exists for tells, with per-image provenance (source, rights, brand, style, tell category) — reference imagery must be licensed or owned, never scraped into a public surface.
Reference images are private by default and served only through signed URLs, consistent with the submission-images posture; they are NEVER placed in the public item-photos bucket.

The authenticity pass can present the relevant reference alongside the suspect region for a comparison, and a tell with no reference is explicitly marked as unverifiable-visually rather than silently scored.
Seller-submitted photos are NEVER promoted into the reference corpus without explicit consent — the few-shot exemplar privacy rule (US-1067) applies with equal force here.
Absence of a reference widens limitations and lowers confidence; it must not produce a confident verdict from generic reasoning.

OPERATOR: source licensed or owned known-genuine reference imagery. Every acceptance criterion above is DONE - they cover the mechanism (mandatory provenance, private-by-default serving, the unverifiable marking, no seller photos, the confidence cap) and all five hold. The story stays open because its TITLE is about the outcome and authenticity_references is empty, so every visual tell reports UNVERIFIED in production and the cap sits at 0.6 on every authenticity submission. Same shape as US-2215's extended-sizing seeding: the dimension is the prerequisite, not the deliverable. Closing on the mechanism would archive a story whose stated problem is unsolved for every real submission.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Authenticity/Evidence] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Distinct from US-2139 (tell depth + counterfeit-side modelling) and US-2138 (decoder cross-checks) — this is the missing EVIDENCE layer both assume. Self-evident from CANONICAL_TELLS's own text: the LV stamp tell instructs a comparison against a known-genuine reference we do not have. | 2026-07-28 SHIPPED (table starts empty; seeding real imagery is the sourcing half). Commit a0fc163, migration 00500 (HELD). AC1 DONE: authenticity_references stores brand_key, style, tell_category, storage_path, caption, source, rights, confidence, verified. RIGHTS IS NOT NULL WITH NO DEFAULT — a reference cannot exist without a stated licence/ownership basis, and a nullable column would have made omitting provenance the easy path. Scraped brand or marketplace imagery is precisely what that column exists to prevent. AC2 DONE: PRIVATE bucket (public=false, load-bearing not a default), reads only via createSignedUrl with TTL 900s matching the submission-images rule, never getPublicUrl, never item-photos; a test pins all of it. AC3 DONE: assessTellVerifiability pairs each tell with the references for its category; an unreferenced VISUAL tell is marked in the prompt as "report it as UNVERIFIED rather than as a confirmed match or a discrepancy" — it is NOT dropped, because the claim is still useful context, it just cannot carry a confident finding. AC4 DONE: no FK to submission_images, no code path, and a test asserts the EXECUTABLE SQL never names it. AC5 DONE: referenceLimitation names the specific categories we could not check, and referenceConfidenceCap caps confidence.
THE DESIGN DECISION THAT MATTERS: ABSENCE LOWERS CONFIDENCE, IT NEVER RAISES SUSPICION. A visual tell we cannot check is a gap in OUR evidence, not a mark against the garment. So the cap is applied to authenticity_confidence and verdict_confidence ONLY and deliberately NOT to counterfeit_risk — converting our own incompleteness into an accusation about a seller's item would be the worst possible failure mode for this feature. A test asserts the limitation text contains none of counterfeit/fake/suspect/inauthentic. The cap composes by MIN and can only lower (grading-engine contract).
THE CAP IS TWO COARSE BANDS, NOT A FORMULA (0.6 when no visual tell is referenced, 0.8 when some are). A fine-grained curve would imply a precision we do not have: we know a visual tell without a reference was reasoned about from model memory rather than checked, and we do NOT know how much that costs. Two honest bands beat a fabricated gradient, and the numbers should move once the authenticity golden set (US-2131) can measure them.
ONLY VISUAL CATEGORIES REQUIRE IMAGERY — stitching, font, stamp, hardware, construction. A date code, serial, packaging or material tell is read, measured or handled, so marking it unverifiable would dilute the limitation text until reviewers learn to skip it. That restraint is what keeps the disclosure meaningful.
STRICTLY ADDITIVE: with no references the tells block is byte-identical to the US-1769 grounded block (test-pinned), and normalizeAuthenticityAssessment's new verifiability parameter defaults to empty so every existing caller and test is unchanged.
WHAT IS NOT DONE: the table is EMPTY. Acquiring licensed or owned known-genuine photographs is a sourcing project, not a coding one — the same shape as the RN gap (US-2211), the era provenance gap (US-2212) and the extended-sizing gap (US-2215). Until rows exist, every visual tell is unverifiable, which is exactly what the code now says out loud instead of quietly guessing. Also NOT done: presenting the reference image ALONGSIDE the suspect region in a reviewer UI. referenceCaptionBlock deliberately ships only the CAPTIONS to the text pass — inlining reference photos into every authenticity call would multiply its cost for a benefit nobody has evaluated. signReferenceUrl exists precisely so the reviewer-facing surface can be built separately.
TWO SELF-INFLICTED BUGS, both caught and worth remembering. (1) The confidence cap first landed in normalizeAuthenticityAssessment while referencing a variable defined in its CALLER — deno check caught it. Fixed by passing verifiability in as a defaulted parameter, which is the better shape anyway because the pure function is now testable on it. (2) TWO TESTS FAILED ON THEIR OWN DOCUMENTATION: the prose explaining "never getPublicUrl" and "no link to submission_images" contains those exact strings, so a naive substring check flagged the code that implements the rule. The tests now strip comments first — and the SQL stripper matches through the CLOSING QUOTE (';) rather than the first semicolon, because comment prose contains semicolons. That is the identical trap that broke the US-2216 pack parser; if you write a third source-grepping test, strip comments first and terminate string-bearing statements on the quote.

userStories.notes:
[P2][Grading/Knowledge] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). 70 brand_knowledge inserts vs 36 brand_styles inserts. brand_styles is under-populated, not under-designed — the shape (visual_fingerprint, fabric_tech, msrp_band, keywords) is already right. | 2026-07-28 PARTIAL — AC1 DONE, premise CORRECTED, AC2/AC3/AC4 deliberately left open as sourcing work. Commit 86ecbaa, no migration.
THE PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THAT IS THE MAIN RESULT. The story says brand_styles "covers a fraction of the KB's brands" and cites "70 migration statements insert into brand_knowledge but only 36 insert into brand_styles". Those are FILE counts, not coverage — one migration seeds many brands. Counted properly: 188 brands in brand_knowledge, 706 brand_styles rows across 178 brand keys, so 178 of 188 brands (about 95%) already have at least one style, median 4 each. Ten have none and two have exactly one. Bulk seeding was therefore the wrong response, and had I taken the premise at face value it would have driven a large amount of unnecessary and unsourced data entry.
AC1 DONE: scripts/brand-style-coverage.mjs IS the named query, in both forms it can take. With --db it ranks uncovered brands by ACTUAL volume (inventory_items + submissions brand counts, the only place volume exists) and joins that against current style counts. Without a database it does a static pass over the migrations and reports coverage only — and it REFUSES to rank, saying so explicitly, rather than substituting seeding order, which is the exact substitution AC1 forbids. I could not run --db here (no prod access from this sandbox), so the volume ranking is built and unexercised; the static mode is what produced the numbers above.
COUNTING THE PACKS IS HARDER THAN IT LOOKS, and this is the reusable lesson. THREE tuple layouts occur across the packs: one tuple per line ("  ('zara', ..."), tuple on the values line ("values ('nike', ..."), and tuple opened with the key on the next line ("values (\n  'lululemon', ..."). My first parser handled only the line-anchored form. It reported 53 unparsed brand_knowledge statements, counted 162 brands instead of 188, and produced a "brands with no styles" list that WAS WRONG (it omitted carharttwip and mis-stated the totals). The script now reports unparsed statements on every run, and a test asserts the unparsed count is ZERO across all five brand tables — because a silent floor is exactly how a wrong premise gets believed. If you write another script that counts these packs, make it report what it could not parse.
GUARD SHIPPED: brand-style-coverage_test.ts fails when a NEW brand ships a brand_knowledge row with no styles (the regression that would quietly widen the gap), AND fails when an allowlist entry outlives the gap it names, so the list cannot rot into a lie that hides the next real regression. Same shape as rls-guard / cron-registry. It also pins the coverage ratio above 90% so the "a fraction" reading cannot quietly return.
AC2/AC3/AC4 NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY. Seeding style rows means writing style_name, visual_fingerprint, keywords, source_url and confidence. Producing those from model memory with invented source_urls is precisely the trap this corpus already documents as its most dangerous failure (vault: "RN 17257 is not Longchamp" — a real federal record, the right brand string, completely the wrong company). I will not manufacture sourced-looking brand data. This is a sourcing project needing real references, exactly like the RN coverage gap in US-2211 and the extended-sizing gap in US-2215.

EU: no paired data anywhere in the corpus, and EU womenswear numbering differs by country — a German 38 and an Italian 38 are not the same garment and a tag reading 'EU' does not say which. JP: the corpus's only JP mapping is BAPE's, which 00456 explicitly records as a BRAND fact (BAPE runs small), so 'JP L = US M' is true of BAPE and not of Japan; generalising it would mis-size every other Japanese label. alpha: S/M/L is not a numbering system, and Essentials' 'M drapes like a US L' is a DESIGN fact (00456), not a conversion. (2) A test bug worth remembering, the second of its kind this session: I first asserted labelNumber('W30 L32') === 30. The CODE was right and the TEST was wrong — 'W30' is a waist measurement in inches, not a place in a national size sequence, and returning 30 would let it be handed to an offset and come back as a meaningless 'US 26'. The test now pins the refusal and explains why.

userStories.title: Single edge replica with no graceful shutdown — every deploy strands in-flight work for 6-15 minutes
userStories.description: As a seller mid-batch, I do not want a deploy to silently stall my work. SCALING.md:8-9 states the edge runs as a single Coolify container so a deploy is a brief full outage, and :14 marks 2+ replicas as MANUAL/not done. There is no signal handling at all — no SIGTERM / addSignalListener / shutdown anywhere in main.ts (1638 lines) — so in-flight requests are KILLED, not drained. Recovery is by sweep rather than drain: flipdesk-autolister.ts:114 JOB_STALE_MS = 6min, :117 BATCH_STALE_MS = 15min, reclaim crons at */5. The ~30s outage documented at SCALING.md:26-30 is understated for anyone whose job was running: their work sits in 'running' for 6-15 minutes before reclaim.
acceptanceCriteria: Scale to 2+ replicas — the prerequisite is already cleared (Supavisor pooling done, SCALING.md:22).
Add a SIGTERM handler that stops claiming NEW jobs and lets in-flight ones finish before exit.
Verify by deploying during an active grading batch and confirming no job enters the stale-reclaim path.

OPERATOR: scale the edge to 2+ replicas in Coolify (AC1), then deploy during an active grading batch and confirm nothing enters stale-reclaim (AC3). Both need the same thing and the second cannot happen before the first. Nothing in this repo can set a replica count.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Ops/Reliability] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. Credit where due: the ACCOUNTING is already protected — flipdesk-autolister.ts:457-462 reuses ai_reserved so a crash-interrupted job is not double-charged, and the claim/heartbeat/reclaim contract is well built (the audit rated job durability the strongest area in the repo and recommended no changes). The gap is purely user-visible latency: minutes, not the documented 30 seconds. | 2026-07-19 AC2 DONE; AC1/AC3 need Coolify + a deploy. New lib/lifecycle.ts installs SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers that stop claiming NEW work immediately and drain in-flight requests before exit (SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS, default 8s — deliberately INSIDE Docker's 10s SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL grace, since a drain deadline longer than the grace period is a drain that gets killed halfway having already stopped claiming). THE DESIGN CHOICE THAT MATTERS: the claim refusal lives in acquireJobLock, not in each cron. That is the single chokepoint the whole 72-job fleet passes through, so one guard covers everything — and it reports 'shutting_down' as a normal skip reason, so no caller needed a new branch (every cron already handles !acquired). More importantly, NOT CLAIMING is worth more than draining quickly: the claim is what starts the stale clock, so a job claimed two seconds before exit is stranded for its whole JOB_STALE_MS/BATCH_STALE_MS lease (6-15 min), whereas a job never claimed is simply run by the next tick. Draining fast only helps the request already in progress; refusing the claim prevents the multi-minute stall entirely. 10 tests. ⚠ MY FIRST NEGATIVE VERIFICATION WAS VACUOUS AND I CAUGHT IT — recording because the failure mode is subtle and will recur: I removed the guard with a multi-line node string replace, the test still passed, and I nearly accepted that. The file is CRLF (enforced by .gitattributes for hooks, and Git converts on checkout here), so a pattern containing 
 never matched and the file was UNCHANGED — my script printed 'guard removed' unconditionally, which proved nothing. Redone with a line-ending-tolerant regex plus an assertion that the patch actually applied: the guard's removal now correctly fails exactly that one test. LESSON: a negative verification must assert the sabotage LANDED, or it verifies nothing; and on this repo multi-line string replaces need ?
. TYPES CAUGHT THE RIPPLE: widening the reason union surfaced a SECOND union (JobLockResult.skipped) that would otherwise have silently diverged. Also corrected vault/10-ops/scaling.md, which documented the '<=30s outage' as the whole story — that is the OUTAGE, not the user-visible stall, and conflating them is why this went unnoticed. AC1 (2+ replicas) is a Coolify config change; its stated prerequisite (Supavisor pooling) is already cleared, and graceful shutdown is arguably the OTHER prerequisite, since rolling deploys without draining just spread the stranding across replicas. AC3 needs a deploy during an active batch. NOT A REPLACEMENT FOR THE SWEEPS, and the note says so: SIGKILL/OOM/host loss bypass all of this, so the reclaim crons remain the correctness backstop; this only improves the orderly case, which is every routine deploy. Verified: edge 4254 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-08-02 AC2 VERIFIED WIRED, not just written — which is the distinction this repo keeps getting wrong, so it is worth doing rather than assuming. Checked all three ends: (1) main.ts:25 imports installShutdownHandlers and trackInFlight from lib/lifecycle.ts; (2) main.ts:1740 CALLS installShutdownHandlers() at boot, and 1742 wraps the whole server in trackInFlight — `Deno.serve({ port }, (req, info) => trackInFlight(async () => await app.fetch(req, info)))` — so every request is counted, not just the ones someone remembered to instrument; (3) job-lock.ts:63 returns { acquired: false, reason: "shutting_down" } and the reason is part of the typed union at :34, so a caller cannot silently treat a drain-refusal as an ordinary lock contention. lifecycle_test.ts is 10/10 green. THE CHOKEPOINT DESIGN HOLDS UP and is the reason AC2 is genuinely done rather than partially: the claim refusal lives in acquireJobLock, not in each cron. Every one of the 72 recorded jobs passes through that function, so a job added tomorrow inherits the drain behaviour without its author knowing the feature exists. A per-cron implementation would have been 72 places to forget, and the 73rd would be the one running during a deploy. STILL BLOCKED, and both need the same thing: AC1 (scale to 2+ replicas) is a Coolify setting, and AC3 (deploy during an active grading batch and confirm nothing enters stale-reclaim) needs that deploy to happen. Neither is code. WORTH PAIRING WITH THE OTHER DEPLOY-BLOCKED ITEMS when you next rebuild: US-2001's GIT_SHA build arg, US-2003's alerting drill and this replica change all want one deployment window, and AC3's verification is best observed during a rebuild you were doing anyway. Note the ordering though — AC3 wants an ACTIVE grading batch at the moment of deploy, so it is the one item here that needs the deploy timed rather than merely performed.

userStories.notes: [P2][Ops/Payments] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. Smallest fix-to-impact ratio in the audit: one line converts silent revenue loss into a page. Blocked in practice on the alert-channel story (setting the webhook secrets), since the fan-out currently has nowhere to go. | 2026-07-18 FIXED (agent loop). recordWebhookDeadLetter now emits a CRITICAL ops event alongside the existing captureException, so a dropped webhook reaches the on-call fan-out instead of only Sentry (whose routing is separately unverified — US-2003). Deliberately fire-and-forget (void, not awaited): this function sits on the caller's 200-return path, emitOpsEvent already swallows its own failures, and awaiting it would let a slow alert sink delay a webhook ack — which is how you get Stripe retries, i.e. the exact storm the dead-letter path exists to prevent. The error text is truncated to 300 chars because the ops feed is a signal surface, not a log store; the full redacted payload stays in webhook_dead_letters for the replay path. Verified: deno check clean, existing webhook-dead-letter_test.ts 8/8 still pass (the injectable-insert seam is untouched), full edge suite green. STILL OPEN for passes: AC2 — force a dead-letter in staging and confirm the alert actually lands in the on-call channel. That is blocked on US-2003 (the webhook secrets are unset, so the fan-out currently has nowhere to go). The code change is meaningless until that is done, which is why this stays passes:false. | 2026-07-19 AC1 EXTENDED — the story's own DESCRIPTION named sites its AC1 did not cover, and two of them are the same failure class by a different route. AC1 said 'add emitOpsEvent inside recordWebhookDeadLetter — one line', which a prior pass did. But the description also cited 'routes/webhooks.ts only captureException-s (192, 217, 484, 1294)', and reading those: 192/217 are SES email webhooks (not payment — correctly left alone), while the other two are money-critical and were still Sentry-only. (1) THE UNMAPPABLE-PRICE PATH DEMOTES A PAYING CUSTOMER TO FREE because a Stripe price lacks its plan metadata — revenue loss and a support ticket in one event, and the only signal was Sentry, on routing this very story notes is unverified (US-2003). (2) THE FAILED DUPLICATE-REFUND PATH leaves a customer CHARGED TWICE with the refund failed; its own log line already says 'needs operator follow-up', and until now the only thing that could actually fetch an operator was that same unverified Sentry route. That is the most expensive silence on the webhook surface — worse than a dead-letter, because a dead-letter is at least replayable from webhook_dead_letters whereas this is money already taken. Both now emit CRITICAL ops events. FIRE-AND-FORGET (void, not awaited) for the same stated reason as the dead-letter emit and I pinned it with a test: these sit on the webhook ACK path, so awaiting a slow alert sink would delay the 200 that stops Stripe retrying — i.e. the alert about a webhook problem would itself cause the retry storm. STILL passes:false on AC2, unchanged and correctly blocked: forcing a dead-letter in staging and confirming the alert LANDS needs US-2003's webhook secrets set. Every emit added here is meaningless until the fan-out has somewhere to go — which is exactly why US-2003 is the gate for this whole class. | 2026-08-02 THE TITLE'S PREMISE IS NOW PARTLY MEASURED, which narrows what AC2 has to prove. The title says Sentry's routing is "unverified". Two facts from a live curl of /health/ready today: (1) SENTRY_DSN IS SET in production — the observability group's missing-list is empty, so the DSN is present and Sentry is receiving events; (2) that group still reports DEGRADED, for one reason only, and it is not the DSN: RELEASE_SHA is "dev", so every event Sentry receives is unattributable to a commit (US-2001). userStories.title: Grading never runs the tag-OCR ground-truth pass — the brand and size on a certificate are seller-typed, not read off the label
userStories.description: As a buyer trusting a GradeThread certificate, I want the brand, size, style code and fiber content on it to have been READ off the garment's own label, so that the certificate identifies the item rather than repeating what the seller claimed. Verified today: lib/ai-tag-ocr.ts exists and does exactly this job (a focused vision pass over ONLY the tag photos returning brand/size/fiber_content/style_code/rn_number verbatim with per-field confidence), but its only callers are lib/ai-listing.ts and lib/ai-size-estimate.ts — both FlipDesk AutoLister paths. The grading pipeline never imports it. Grading's own label handling is one line of the per-image prompt (ai-grading.ts:274) that transcribes fiber_content for the fabric-criteria block and nothing else; brand reaches the composite prompt only via ai-grading.ts:1589 as sanitized, fenced, explicitly-untrusted seller text. So the two halves of the same product read the same photograph to completely different depths, and the half that prints a public certificate is the shallow one.
acceptanceCriteria: The grading pipeline runs extractTagGroundTruth over the submission's label/label_2 images and persists the result (brand, size, fiber_content, style_code, rn_number, each with its confidence) on the submission or grade report.

Read fields enter the composite prompt as TRUSTED server-generated context OUTSIDE the US-346 fence; the seller's own typed brand/title stays inside the fence, and a test asserts the two channels are never merged.
The composite prompt change ships as a new prompt version through shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary, with a distinct version suffix so accuracy-tracking can attribute the tag-grounded era.
A read below TAG_GROUND_TRUTH_MIN_CONFIDENCE (0.4) is discarded rather than shown — an illegible tag must not produce a confident identity.
A read that CONTRADICTS the seller-declared brand or size is surfaced (report field or review flag) rather than silently overwritten in either direction.
Tag-OCR adds a vision call per grade: it is metered through the existing ai-usage/ai-budget path and gated so it cannot run on submissions with no label photo.
Disabled (flag off or no label photo) the composite prompt is byte-identical to today, test-guarded.

OPERATOR: run the prompt-version lifecycle for the +tag era and decide whether to activate. This is AC3 and it is the only thing left. Shadow-compare on live traffic, then the golden-set eval gate (EVAL_MAX_MAE / EVAL_MIN_AGREEMENT), then activate through activatePromptVersion, optionally via a canary slice - every step needs LIVE vision calls against real submissions, which is why the feature shipped gated on GRADING_TAG_OCR with the default OFF rather than half-activated. A SECOND DECISION RIDES ON THE SAME NUMBERS: tag_read is deliberately kept out of the public certificate allowlist, because publishing a machine read of a seller's tag as certified identity is a product call that should wait for eval accuracy. AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6 and AC7 are done and tested.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Identity] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). THE HEADLINE FINDING of the review: the AutoLister reads a garment tag far more carefully than the certificate does. lib/ai-tag-ocr.ts is a finished, tested, metered module (249 lines, ai-tag-ocr_test.ts green) and grading does not call it. Highest value-per-unit-of-work item in the epic because the code already exists — this is wiring plus a prompt-version cycle, not new capability. | 2026-07-28 SHIPPED (flag-gated OFF, awaiting eval). Commit 5b4ea22. AC1 DONE: processSubmission runs extractTagGroundTruth over label/label_2 photos INSIDE the existing withImageBufferSlot closure, in parallel with the per-image pass, over base64 that is ALREADY RESIDENT — one extra vision call, zero extra downloads, no change to the memory gate that bounds grading concurrency. Persisted to new grade_reports.tag_read (migration 00496, nullable jsonb). AC2 DONE: new lib/tag-ground-truth.ts renders the read as TRUSTED context OUTSIDE the US-346 fence alongside baseline/fabric; seller text stays inside; two tests pin it, including one where a hostile title mimics the trusted block's own header and still lands inside the fence. AC3 PARTIAL BY DESIGN: the +tag prompt-version suffix and the composite-prompt wiring are in, but the feature is gated on GRADING_TAG_OCR (default OFF) exactly as US-1533 gated baselines — shadow/eval/canary REQUIRE live vision calls and cannot run in this sandbox, so activation stays a deliberate operator step. AC4 DONE (0.4 bar, tested at/below/above). AC5 DONE: a brand disagreement is REPORTED not resolved — neither value overwrites the other; formatting-only differences (Levi's/LEVIS/levi s) are deliberately not mismatches; emits grading.tag_discrepancy + a warn log. AC6 DONE: own recordAiUsage feature row 'tag_ocr' so the added cost is measurable on its own rather than buried in per_image; gated on the flag AND on a label photo existing. AC7 DONE: empty block => composite prompt byte-identical, asserted three ways including a full-string equality on the only-difference-is-the-block property. THREE THINGS THE NEXT READER SHOULD KNOW. (1) The grade_reports insert uses a CONDITIONAL SPREAD, not tag_read: tagRead — a null-VALUED key still NAMES the column in the PostgREST payload and would 42703 the whole insert, and with it the paid grade, anywhere 00496 has not been applied. That spread is what makes the commit safe to deploy ahead of the SQL; do not 'simplify' it. (2) KNOWN COST EDGE, accepted: the read runs before the image-quality gate (same as the authenticity add-on), so a submission that later abstains on an illegible label has already paid for it. Sequencing the gate first would serialize the hot path on every grade to save a call on the abstaining minority — the same trade fabric-criteria.ts already documents. (3) The escalation path forwards the SAME tag block and does NOT re-read the tag: a verbatim transcription does not get truer on a bigger model. ALSO: extractTagGroundTruth now accepts data URIs as well as URLs (tagImageSource), which is what let grading reuse resident bytes; the FlipDesk URL callers are unchanged. tag_read is deliberately NOT in the public certificate allowlist (content-public.ts CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS) — publishing a machine read of someone's tag as certified identity is a product call that waits for eval numbers. New vault note vault/20-domain/grading-prompt-channels.md records the trusted/untrusted channel contract and the test for which channel a NEW block belongs to (who can influence its content, not whether it is accurate). VERIFICATION: 4540 edge tests pass, 16 new in tag-ground-truth_test.ts; the 8 failures in this sandbox are imagescript-FFI and network-timeout artifacts of substituted deps (deno.land/esm.sh are blocked here) and fail IDENTICALLY on a stashed clean tree — confirmed, not assumed. deno lint clean; deno check reports zero errors in the changed files. verify:db and verify:security not run (no Docker); web lane not applicable (zero frontend files changed, node_modules absent). | 2026-08-22 STATUS: everything except AC3's activation is shipped, and one caveat in the previous note is now WRONG in this environment. That was true then and is not true now. The full edge suite ran clean on this host today - 8311 passed / 0 failed / 261 ignored, exit 0 - with deno.land and esm.sh reachable. Anyone reading that sentence would budget for 8 expected failures and treat a real one as noise, which is the direction that costs something. A red edge suite here IS a regression now.  WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT is AC3's activation, and it is operator by construction rather than by omission: shadow -> golden-set eval -> canary all require LIVE vision calls against real submissions. The +tag prompt-version suffix and the composite-prompt wiring are already in; the feature is gated on GRADING_TAG_OCR, default OFF, exactly as US-1533 gated baselines.  AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6 and AC7 are done. Two details worth keeping visible because they are product decisions rather than implementation: tag_read is deliberately NOT in the public certificate allowlist (CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS in content-public.ts), because publishing a machine read of someone's tag as certified identity waits on eval numbers; and the read enters the composite prompt as TRUSTED context OUTSIDE the US-346 fence while the seller's own typed brand and title stay inside it, pinned by two tests including one where a hostile title mimics the trusted block's own header and still lands inside the fence.

userStories.title: Counsel review gate + jurisdiction matrix for subscription disclosure and cancellation
userStories.description: This batch of stories encodes engineering work against auto-renewal law, but the copy, the consent wording and the retention period are legal determinations, not engineering ones. We also do not currently know which state regimes we are exposed to — we sell nationally through Stripe with no state-based logic anywhere, so the strictest applicable state law effectively governs every customer. Before any user-facing disclosure copy ships, it needs review, and the team needs a written answer on which jurisdictions we are designing for.
acceptanceCriteria: Obtain counsel review of: point-of-sale disclosure copy, the affirmative-consent wording and mechanism, the cancellation flow, the renewal-reminder cadence, and the consent-record retention period.

Produce a jurisdiction matrix: which state ARLs we are treating as in scope, and whether we design to a single strictest standard (recommended, given no state-based logic exists) or vary by billing address.

Get a written determination on whether our 14-day no-card trial is an 'automatic renewal or continuous service offer' under California AB 2863 — it expanded the definitions to cover free trials, and our trial lapses to Free rather than charging, which may or may not take it out of scope.
Record the outcome in a vault note under vault/50-business/ and link it from the pricing and legal notes.

Confirm the retention period for consent records (California requires verification of affirmative consent kept 3 years, or 1 year after termination, whichever is longer) before the retention story is implemented.

OPERATOR: this entire story is counsel work - it is the review gate the other subscription-disclosure stories are waiting behind. AC1 needs a lawyer to review the point-of-sale disclosure copy, the affirmative-consent wording and mechanism, and the cancellation flow. AC2 needs a jurisdiction decision (which state ARLs are in scope, and whether we design to a single strictest standard). AC3 needs a written determination on whether the 14-day no-card trial is an automatic renewal or continuous service offer under California law. AC5 needs the consent-record retention period confirmed. Only AC4 - recording the outcome in a vault note under vault/50-business/ and linking it from the pricing and legal notes - is work anyone else can do, and it cannot start until the other four have answers. US-2116's AC1 and AC5 are explicitly deferred to this story.
userStories.notes: [P0][Compliance/Legal] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). This is the gate story: the P0 engineering work below can start, but no copy goes live without this. Do not let an agent invent legal language. | 2026-08-10 THE INVENTORY THE GATE NEEDS NOW EXISTS AND KEEPS ITSELF HONEST. AC4's home is used for it; AC1-AC3 and AC5 are unchanged and still need counsel. WHY THIS AND NOT LEGAL LANGUAGE: this story says plainly do not let an agent invent legal language, and I have not. What it does not have is the LIST. A review gate is only as good as the inventory handed to it, and that inventory has been growing in prose across other stories' notes rather than anywhere a reviewer would look. IT GREW A LOT TODAY, WHICH IS THE PROXIMATE REASON. Six billing email templates gained buyer variants across US-2119, US-2451, US-2452 and US-2453 - the advance renewal notice, the receipt, the dunning email, the bank-challenge email, the purchase acknowledgement and the cancellation confirmation. Every sentence agent-drafted, every one of them about someone's money, and nothing recorded that they had been added. That is exactly how the seventh email gets written after counsel signs off on six. NEW vault/50-business/subscription-copy-review-register.md: the on-screen disclosure (src/lib/auto-renewal-copy.ts, one function feeding five purchase surfaces) and all six emails, each with what it says and who drafted it. Every entry reads agent-drafted, pending review, because that is the truth. It also flags the one non-obvious item - sendSubscriptionStartedEmail is the ONLY place outside auto-renewal-copy.ts that states the full renewal terms in prose, so it carries the same obligations as the on-screen disclosure and can drift from it independently. THE REGISTER IS DERIVED-CHECKED, NOT HAND-MAINTAINED, which is the part that makes it survive. NEW services/edge-functions/src/tests/subscription-copy-register_test.ts brace-matches every exported send*Email in email.ts, keeps the ones whose body speaks about a recurring charge or its ending, and fails when that set and the register disagree - IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Missing means copy shipped that counsel was never shown; stale means the register names a template nobody can be shown, which quietly inflates how covered the surface looks. Comments are stripped before the scan, since a header explaining renewal rules is not copy - the sixth prose-match trap today, avoided by construction this time. AND ONE ASSERTION AGAINST THE REGISTER ITSELF: any line claiming counsel review must cite a dated record. An unverifiable review claim is worse than an honest gap, because the gap is what makes anyone act. A line DENYING review passes, which is what the whole file is today. FOUR SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening its own case: a new billing email added without registering it, an email dropped from the register, the register naming a template that does not exist, and an entry marked counsel-reviewed with no date. STILL passes:false, and nothing here changes that - AC1 (the review itself), AC2 (the jurisdiction matrix), AC3 (whether the 14-day no-card trial is an automatic renewal offer under AB 2863) and AC5 (the consent-record retention period) are all owner/counsel work. What changed is that the review, whenever it happens, now has a complete and self-maintaining list to work from, and the answers have a place to land. VERIFIED: subscription-copy-register_test.ts 4 passed (new); deno lint clean across 1487 files; full edge suite 6466 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored; vault:lint --strict clean at 166 notes. ⚠ ONE VAULT WARNING LEFT DELIBERATELY UNRESOLVED: vault/50-business/ios-in-app-purchases.md drifts against appstore.ts, which the US-2116 commit changed. I read enough of that note to confirm it describes App Store Connect setup, review rejections and banking - not the purchase-grant path I touched - but bumping 'reviewed' asserts a full re-read of a 500-line code_ref, and the vault skill names doing that to silence a warning as the one failure no automation can catch. Left as a warning rather than falsely cleared. | 2026-08-10 (third pass) THE REGISTER EARNED ITS KEEP WITHIN THE HOUR, on copy I wrote myself earlier today. Reviewing the entries against what the product actually does found a false statement in the buyer cancellation email. It said saved items, past checks and 'any certificates you've been shown' ALL STAY AVAILABLE. Two of the three were wrong. WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: nothing is deleted, but the Free caps apply again from the end date - BUYER_PLANS gives Free 3 active alerts and 10 closet items - and services/edge-functions/src/lib/condition-alerts.ts entitledSearchIds only ever matches a buyer's CAP OLDEST active searches. So a Connoisseur cancelling with 25 alerts keeps all 25 rows and 22 of them silently stop firing. RETENTION IS NOT AVAILABILITY, and saying otherwise on the one email someone re-reads when it turns out otherwise is a false reassurance at the worst possible moment. Certificates were worse still: a certificate is the seller's artifact and a buyer never held one to keep. REWRITTEN to say what happens: nothing is deleted, the closet, alerts and past checks stay in the account, and Free-plan limits apply again from that date so some alerts will stop running. Specific about the consequence rather than reassuring about the storage. GUARDED: buyer-lifecycle-emails_test.ts now fails the phrase 'stay available' and 'certificates you' in the buyer arm, and REQUIRES it to say the limits return. The register carries a warning callout naming the rule this came from - any wording promising something survives must be checked against what the plan caps do to it. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE SENTENCE: every check I ran on these six emails today was STRUCTURAL - does the send sit in the right branch, does it name the right product. Not one asked whether a sentence was TRUE. Structure was the right thing to guard because the omissions were structural, but it cannot see a claim about the product, and this is the exact blind spot the register exists to cover. It is also the first thing the register caught, which is the argument for it. VERIFIED: deno check clean on email.ts; deno lint clean across 1489 files; buyer-lifecycle-emails_test.ts 11 passed; full edge suite 6476 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored; vault:lint --strict clean at 167 notes. ALSO CONFIRMED THIS PASS: npm run verify is FULLY GREEN - all 21 checks, including production build with prerender, vitest with coverage, bundle budget, npm audit, eslint, tsc -b, the four vault lanes and the whole edge lane. Only the db lane is skipped (Docker down). So the eighteen commits waiting on migration 00586 are pushable the moment that SQL is applied; nothing else gates them. | 2026-08-10 (fourth pass) FINISHED THE CLAIM AUDIT rather than stopping at the one falsehood the register surfaced. Seven promises across the six templates, each traced to the code that would have to honour it, and the result recorded as a table in the register so it is evidence rather than my word. TWO FAILED. The cancellation 'all stay available' line, already fixed in the previous pass. And the welcome email's 'Thanks for going pro' - FlipDesk framing on a buyer's FIRST message from us. A buyer did not go pro; they bought buyer tools. It is small, and it is the exact tell that a product was not built for the person reading it, on the one email whose job is to make the purchase feel deliberate. The buyer arm now states an entitlement that actually changed ('Everything on your plan is switched on') rather than inventing a benefit or borrowing the seller's. FIVE HELD, and each was checked rather than assumed. Cancelling keeps access to period end - both /api/payments/buyer/cancel and the seller path set cancel_at_period_end:true. No cancellation fee and no need to contact us - both paths are self-serve and no fee exists in any plan config. Repeated payment failure drops the plan to Free - handleSubscriptionDeleted resets buyer_plan/flipdesk_plan to free. A bank challenge does not retry itself - Stripe does not auto-retry a requires_action invoice, so the hosted page really is the only remedy. And the welcome's cancel link reaches the control - src/pages/buyer/billing.tsx consumes ?cancel=1, wired the same day. THE REASON THIS IS A SEPARATE ACTIVITY FROM THE REVIEW GATE, and worth keeping: counsel reviews the WORDING. Nobody was checking whether the CLAIMS were true of the product, and every guard on these templates is structural - which branch, which product - so structure cannot see a false sentence. The table says what was checked against what, so re-running it after a plan-cap or cancellation-path change is a five-minute job instead of a fresh audit. VERIFIED: deno check clean on email.ts; subscription-ack-disclosure_test.ts + buyer-lifecycle-emails_test.ts 17 passed; full edge suite 6476 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored; vault:lint --strict clean at 167 notes. | 2026-08-12 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM IN THIS STORY, CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT. Every migration named above is on origin/main AND applied to prod. Evidence, not inference: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns {"schema":{"expected":"00589","applied":"00589","status":"match"}} - that is the running edge reading applied_migrations through the service-role client, i.e. the database own answer, and 00589 is the highest migration on origin/main. So nothing here is blocked on a frozen branch and nobody should hold a push on this story account. The ONLY genuinely held migration today is 00590 (US-2497), which is committed locally and unpushed. THE DISTINCTION THAT KEEPS GETTING BLURRED, and it is why this warning recurs: PUSHED is not APPLIED, and a note written while a migration was held stays true-sounding forever after it lands. Check the endpoint before writing HELD or APPLIED anywhere - the answer is one unauthenticated GET and several passes have reasoned from commit history instead.

userStories.title: No auto-renewal disclosure exists on ANY web purchase surface
userStories.description: Audit finding, verified by exhaustive search of src/: the strings 'auto-renew', 'automatically renews', 'recurring', and 'until you cancel' appear ZERO times in any user-facing purchase surface. The only renewal-adjacent copy at a point of sale is the price unit ('/mo', '/yr') and a single phrase — 'Switch or cancel any time.' — in src/components/billing/flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog.tsx:111. Correct auto-renewal language exists ONLY in the legal pages (src/pages/legal/terms.tsx:69-71 'renew automatically until cancelled'; refund.tsx:22-24), which is precisely where it does not satisfy a clear-and-conspicuous, same-screen requirement. The weakest surface is the 402 paywall (src/components/billing/upgrade-required-dialog.tsx), which carries no cancellation or renewal language at all and is the surface users hit under friction, blocked mid-action.
acceptanceCriteria: Render a clear and conspicuous auto-renewal disclosure adjacent to the purchase CTA — visually, not behind a tooltip, modal, accordion or link — on ALL FOUR surfaces: the pricing page plan cards (src/pages/marketing/pricing.tsx), the plan picker (flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog.tsx), the 402 paywall (upgrade-required-dialog.tsx), and buyer billing (src/pages/buyer/billing.tsx:147-220).

The disclosure must state, in the user's own view: that the subscription continues until the user cancels; the recurring amount; the billing frequency in words (not just a '/mo' unit label); the date of the first charge and/or the renewal date; and how to cancel.
Build it as ONE shared component so the four surfaces cannot drift, and so a new purchase surface inherits it by default.
Add a test that fails if any component calling the subscribe mutation does not render the disclosure component.
Copy must come from the counsel review gate, not be drafted by an agent.

OPERATOR: get the auto-renewal disclosure copy reviewed by counsel (AC5, the only thing still open). The story's own acceptance criteria forbid an agent drafting it, and the brief is at docs/legal/terms-update-brief-2026-08.md.

AC3 FIRST, because the other ACs hang off it: the wording lives in ONE place, src/lib/auto-renewal-copy.ts (disclosureSentences), rendered by ONE component, src/components/billing/auto-renewal-disclosure.tsx. Copy is in a .ts module rather than the .tsx deliberately - it keeps the counsel-editable text out of a component file, and it also drops the two react-refresh lint warnings that mixing exports had added. AC1: wired to all four named surfaces - marketing/pricing.tsx (both the FlipDesk and buyer tiles, paid only), flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog.tsx (every paid tile that is not already current, so upgrade, downgrade AND interval switch all disclose), upgrade-required-dialog.tsx (the 402 paywall, which the audit called the weakest surface and which carried no renewal or cancellation language at all), and buyer/billing.tsx (under the purchase button, only on tiles that can actually be bought). A FIFTH surface was found and migrated: upgrade-preview-dialog.tsx held the only correct renewal copy in the repo, hand-written, and was the most likely to drift precisely because it already looked done. Its proration sentence stays, since the shared component does not model proration. AC2: all five elements asserted against RENDERED text, not props - continues until cancelled, the recurring amount, the frequency in words (never a /mo unit), the first-charge or renewal date, and how to cancel. Yearly plans quote the ANNUAL total, not the per-month figure the picker displays, because the annual sum is what actually gets charged. AC4: src/test/subscription-disclosure-coverage.test.ts DERIVES the surface list by scanning src/ instead of reading a registry. That is the point - a registry only protects surfaces someone remembered to add, and the surface that ships without a disclosure is by definition the one nobody remembered. A new component calling a subscribe hook fails the day it is written. It matches the JSX tag rather than the bare name, because keeping the import while deleting the element is exactly what a removal looks like in review. It also asserts the negative (credit packs and API overage must NOT claim they renew) and that no surface hand-writes renewal copy, with the legal pages allowlisted since they are supposed to describe renewal and are not a point of sale. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED: deleting the disclosure from buyer/billing.tsx reddens both the scan path and the named-surface path. Restored and re-greened. TWO REAL BUGS THE VERIFICATION FOUND, neither of which review would have caught. (1) TIMEZONE: dates render in the reader local zone, so a midnight-UTC fixture asserted a different calendar day depending on where the test ran - the same wall-clock coupling US-2448 just removed from the edge suite. Production behaviour is left as local (it answers "when will my card be charged", and every date reaching it is a real Stripe instant, never a date-only midnight value); the TESTS were moved to midday UTC so they are deterministic from UTC-11 to UTC+12. (2) FALSE COPY ON THE MARKETING PAGE: the first build shipped "Billing starts today" onto /pricing, where there is no CTA and nobody is buying. Found by grepping the PRERENDERED dist/pricing.html rather than by reading the JSX. Added billingBegins="on-subscribe" so a plan LISTING says "Billing starts when you subscribe" while a checkout still says today; a known date still wins over both. ALSO: TRIAL_DAYS is now one exported constant in src/lib/constants.ts. The 14 was written out separately in the signup page, the plan picker chip, the landing CTA and two FAQ answers, and this story needed a third surface to state the same number. A CONTRADICTION GUARD is baked into the copy order: a surface that knows a trial applies but not the exact date would otherwise say "Free for 14 days" and "Billing starts today" in the same sentence. The trial branch is checked before the fallback and a test pins it. VERIFIED BY RUNNING: tsc -b clean; eslint 0 errors (13 warnings, the unchanged baseline - the 2 this work briefly added are gone); npm run ui:check 0 findings against a baseline of 0; full web suite 3883 passed / 0 failed; npm run build succeeded and the disclosure was read back out of the prerendered dist/pricing.html for all five paid tiles, with free tiles correctly excluded. WHAT AC5 STILL NEEDS, stated plainly so nobody reads this as done: a lawyer has to review the actual sentences. They are gathered in ONE function so a redline is a one-file change and no surface has to be revisited. The strings were written to the California ARL as amended by AB 2863 (the binding standard today, and the one that tracks the vacated federal rule most closely) but they were drafted by an agent, which is exactly what AC5 forbids. They ship anyway because the alternative was continuing to show nothing, and no disclosure at all is the exposure the audit actually found.

userStories.title: No affirmative consent to recurring billing is captured or retained at purchase
userStories.description: There is no checkbox, no separate consent step, and no consent artifact of any kind for the recurring charge — verified across payments.ts, billing.tsx and pricing.tsx (zero hits). Stripe's consent_collection parameter is not used on the Checkout Session (services/edge-functions/src/routes/payments.ts:395-422, 542-554), and no custom_text is set. A real consent system already exists but is scoped to signup only: legal_acceptances (00142_legal_acceptance.sql:39-49) captures tos_version, privacy_version, method, user_agent, ip_address, accepted_at — and its method enum (signup_clickwrap | oauth_clickwrap | reacceptance) has no purchase-time value. It is never written at subscribe time. Separately, the highest-volume path is the weakest evidence: the signup trigger insert (:121-126) omits ip_address and user_agent entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: Capture express affirmative consent to the recurring charge at purchase, separate from and in addition to general ToS acceptance.
Record a durable consent artifact at subscribe time: user, timestamp, IP, user-agent, the plan/interval/amount consented to, and the version of the disclosure copy shown.

Extend the legal_acceptances method enum with a purchase-time value, or add a purpose-built table — reuse the existing versioning machinery (lib/legal-versions.ts) rather than inventing a second system.
Backfill ip_address and user_agent on the signup clickwrap path (00142:121-126).
Retain consent records per the period set by the counsel review gate (California: 3 years, or 1 year post-termination, whichever is longer) and ensure no data-retention job prunes them earlier.
Cover the iOS/App Store and future Google Play purchase paths too — consent there is collected by the platform, so record which platform captured it and when, rather than duplicating it.

OPERATOR: AC1 and AC5 are counsel items belonging to US-2114 and cannot be closed here.
