userStories.notes: [P0][Compliance/Web] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). Express informed consent plus retained proof is the core of both ROSCA and the California ARL. Today we could not demonstrate what any subscriber agreed to. Depends on the terms-snapshot story for the 'what was shown' half. | 2026-07-19 INVESTIGATED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — and the scoping matters, so here is what the next pass needs. THIS STORY IS GENUINELY MORE COUNSEL-GATED THAN ITS NEIGHBOURS. US-2117, US-2119, US-2120 and US-2125 all turned out to be mechanism (I was wrong to call them gated, four times). This one is not the same: US-2114's AC1 explicitly puts 'the affirmative-consent WORDING AND MECHANISM' under review, so AC1 here is squarely gated, and AC5's retention period is gated by US-2114 AC5 by name. AC4 IS NOT GATED, and I traced it to a precise conclusion. THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS: POST /api/legal/accept (routes/legal.ts:109) records ip_address via clientIp(c) and user_agent from the request header, SERVER-SIDE, and it already accepts method='signup_clickwrap' in its allowlist. So nothing needs building — the strong-evidence path is there and is used today by the legal GATE (oauth_clickwrap / reacceptance). The gap is only that the EMAIL-signup path never calls it: handle_new_user's trigger (00142:121-126) writes the signup_clickwrap row itself, inside Postgres, where it has no request context — hence no IP, no user-agent. That is exactly why the highest-volume path carries the weakest evidence. ⚠ THE TRAP, and the reason I did not just 'fix' it: the obvious shortcut is to pass ip/user_agent through signUp()'s options.data so the trigger can read them. DO NOT. Those would be CLIENT-SUPPLIED and trivially forged, and a forged IP in a consent record is worse than an absent one — it looks authoritative in exactly the setting where the record's only value is that it can be trusted. Same reasoning as US-2117's refusal to write a partial agreement and US-2119's refusal to send a dateless notice. THE ACTUAL SEAM, for whoever picks this up: email signup defers the session until confirmation (emailRedirectTo), so /api/legal/accept — which requires auth — cannot be called at signUp() time. The right hook is the FIRST AUTHENTICATED SESSION, in use-auth.ts's onAuthStateChange SIGNED_IN branch, which already runs exactly this shape of one-shot post-signup work (redeemStoredAffiliateRef, sendWelcomeEmailOnce gated on a user_metadata flag). Call /api/legal/accept with method='signup_clickwrap' there. ONE DESIGN QUESTION TO SETTLE FIRST: legal_acceptances is an append-only audit table, so this produces TWO rows for one signup — the trigger's (guaranteed, weak) and the endpoint's (best-effort, strong). I think that is the RIGHT outcome rather than a defect: you always have a record, and usually a provable one. But it should be a decision, and the endpoint needs an idempotency guard so a repeated SIGNED_IN does not append a third. AC6 is also unblocked and unstarted: recording WHICH PLATFORM captured consent for IAP/Play purchases (where the platform collects it) rather than duplicating it — subscription_agreements.source (US-2117, migration 00486) already has the appstore/google_play values for exactly this. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) AC6 DONE. Both platform purchase paths now record WHICH PLATFORM captured the consent — appstore verify and the Play RTDN reverify each write a subscription_agreements row via recordPlatformAgreement. This became cheap only because two other pieces landed first: US-2117's table (with the appstore/google_play values already in its source CHECK) and US-2124's platform-event work that made me read these routes. THE HONESTY CONSTRAINT IS THE DESIGN, and it is what AC6 actually asks for: Apple and Google COLLECT AND STORE the affirmative agreement natively, so duplicating it would be dishonest — we did not take that consent and cannot attest to its wording. The row therefore records THAT the platform took it, not a claim that we did. Concretely: amount_cents is 0 with an in-place comment saying it is NOT a real price, because the platform owns and localises the amount and inventing a figure would be the same error US-2117 refuses on the Stripe path — a partial record that reads as fact. A test asserts BOTH the zero and its explanation, because an unexplained 0 will eventually be read as 'this user agreed to pay nothing'. stripe_subscription_id is namespaced as <source>:<external_id> so an Apple transaction id cannot collide with a Stripe subscription id in the uniqueness index, and a 23505 is swallowed — a replayed IAP verify or a repeated RTDN must not report a failure, since the index firing IS the idempotency working. A test pins that both paths call it, so the gap cannot reopen on one platform while looking closed on the other. WHAT THIS CHANGES IN PRACTICE: before, 'what did this user agree to?' was answerable for a Stripe subscriber and unanswerable for an IAP or Play one — the two populations had different evidentiary standing for the same product. STILL OPEN and correctly gated: AC1 (express affirmative consent at web purchase) and AC5 (retention period) are US-2114 counsel items; AC4 (server-side IP/UA on the signup clickwrap) is scoped above with its trap named — the mechanism already exists in /api/legal/accept, the seam is the first authenticated session, and passing a CLIENT-SUPPLIED ip through signUp() would be worse than the current absence. Verified: edge 4319 passed, deno check + lint clean. | AC4 DONE 2026-08-09; story stays OPEN on AC1 and AC5, which are US-2114 counsel items. NEW POST /api/legal/confirm-signup (services/edge-functions/src/routes/legal.ts) plus the pure rules in NEW services/edge-functions/src/lib/signup-consent-evidence.ts, called once per user per page session from the SIGNED_IN branch of src/hooks/use-auth.ts via NEW src/lib/signup-consent.ts. THE PREVIOUS PASS SCOPED THIS AS "call /api/legal/accept from the first authenticated session" AND THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG, which is the finding worth carrying. /accept stamps the CURRENT published versions AND the users.tos_accepted_version / privacy_accepted_version columns. Email signup defers the session until the confirmation link is clicked, which can be days later, so a version bump in between would have recorded the user as accepting a document they never saw - and cleared a re-acceptance prompt nobody answered. Worse, that row would have looked like the STRONGER evidence of the two, because it carries a real IP. So the endpoint is separate and it COPIES the versions off the trigger row rather than resolving them. WHAT THE ROW HONESTLY CLAIMS. It is a CORROBORATION, not a backfill of the signup request: at this time, from this address, the holder of this account was authenticated, and the clickwrap being corroborated named these documents. accepted_at is when the SERVER OBSERVED THE SESSION, not when consent was given - the clickwrap row holds that - and conflating the two is the one way this could overstate what we know. That is why the method is a DIFFERENT string, signup_clickwrap_confirmed, rather than one value distinguished by a null IP. A signup now ends with a pair: guaranteed-and-weak beside best-effort-and-strong. The trap the previous note named is still refused for its original reason: passing ip/user_agent through signUp() options.data would make them client-supplied and forgeable, and a forged IP in a consent record is worse than an absent one. TWO REFUSALS IN THE CODE. No clickwrap row means an OAuth signup or a pre-00142 user; the endpoint refuses rather than asserting an acceptance that never happened, because a fabricated record will be believed. A clickwrap row naming no document is refused too - a confirmation that says somebody agreed to something reads as evidence and carries none. IDEMPOTENCY IS SERVER-SIDE, deliberately: legal_acceptances is append-only, so a lost race is not a retry, it is a duplicate audit row forever, and a client flag can be stale, cleared or raced by two tabs. The client dedup is only to keep a request off every token refresh. A SEPARATE TRAP FOUND AND MARKED: /accept has accepted method=signup_clickwrap in its allowlist since US-377 and NOTHING sends it - checked across src, ios, android and extension-unified. It is now commented as a hazard pointing at the new endpoint, because reaching for it is exactly the wrong fix described above. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS: versions resolved fresh instead of copied, idempotency guard removed, a row fabricated when there is no clickwrap, and the LATEST clickwrap taken instead of the earliest. Each reddened its own cases and only its own; module restored and re-run green. NOT EXPLORED, AND NAMED SO IT IS NOT LOST: GoTrue writes its own auth.audit_log_entries row on signup carrying the REAL signup IP. If that row is reachable and its write ordering against handle_new_user is provable, it would satisfy AC4 literally rather than by corroboration. Neither fact can be established without a running GoTrue, and the db verify lane starts Postgres alone. HELD, NOT SHIPPED: migration 00573_legal_acceptances_signup_confirmed.sql updates the legal_acceptances.method column comment, which 00142:44 leaves naming three values while the code now writes four. It is comment-only, changes nothing functional, and is deliberately NOT committed - see the note about the branch state. VERIFIED: 10 deno cases in NEW signup-consent-evidence_test.ts, 7 vitest cases in NEW src/lib/__tests__/signup-consent.test.ts, deno check and deno lint clean across 1453 files, full edge suite 6242 passed / 0 failed, tsc -b clean, eslint clean, ui:check 0 findings. Commit cf08b2da. | CORRECTION 2026-08-09, same session: the AC4 segment above was appended with the done command, which flipped passes to true. That was wrong and is reverted here - AC1 (express affirmative consent at web purchase) and AC5 (retention period) are US-2114 counsel items and are untouched. Recording it rather than silently fixing it, because a story that reads as closed is exactly the failure mode this backlog keeps paying for. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-09, later the same day: the sentence above reading "HELD, NOT SHIPPED: migration 00573_legal_acceptances_signup_confirmed.sql ... deliberately NOT committed" is STALE and must not be acted on. 00573 was committed, applied to prod and pushed the same day - prod was measured at applied=00573 via /health/ready at 14:27 UTC, the database's own answer, and PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md now records all of 00564-00573 as APPLIED with that measurement. Nothing in this story is blocked on a branch freeze. WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE OF HOW IT WAS FOUND: prd-lint did not catch this when the note was written, and the reason was a bug in the guard rather than an exemption - MIGRATION_ID used a right-hand \b, and underscore is a word character, so a migration named by its FILENAME never matched. This story's note names 00573 exactly that way. The guard therefore saw only the pushed ids it cites for context, concluded nothing was left to hold, and warned on a CORRECT freeze; the same blindness would have kept it silent on a genuinely stale one. Fixed in commit 9ec66743 and negative-verified both edges. AC1 and AC5 remain US-2114 counsel items and are untouched. | 2026-08-10 ⚠ CORRECTION TO THIS STORY'S OWN NOTES, AND IT IS MATERIAL: AC4's strengthened-evidence path HAS NEVER RECORDED A SINGLE ROW. The notes here describe /api/legal/confirm-signup as working - two rows per email signup, one guaranteed and weak, one best-effort and strong. In fact decideSignupConsentEvidence has returned refuse/no_signup_clickwrap for EVERY caller since it shipped, because there is no signup_clickwrap row to corroborate. handle_new_user lost its clickwrap write at migration 00303, which replaced the function to add use_case and did not carry 00142's block forward; 00379 and 00401 rebased on the truncated body. Traced across all seven definitions and fixed in 00586 under US-2017 (HELD - see PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md). AC4's mechanism becomes live the moment that SQL is applied, and not before. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY CORRECT HERE: the client wiring (src/lib/signup-consent.ts, called from use-auth.ts, gated to provider === 'email'), the refusal itself, and the decision to corroborate rather than backfill. Nothing in the design was wrong. The endpoint was answering exactly as specified about a row that no longer existed. THE REAL DEFECT WAS THE SILENCE, and that is what this commit fixes. Both non-insert outcomes returned 200 with no metric, no warn and no distinguishable shape - deliberately, so ordinary traffic would not become alert noise. But the two reasons are NOT alike: already_confirmed is a returning user, while no_signup_clickwrap means an email signup produced no consent record at all. Collapsing them is what let a compliance path record nothing for months while three separate comments described it working. FIXED: the no_signup_clickwrap branch now emits recordMetric('legal.signup_clickwrap_missing') and a warn naming the trigger and the migration. already_confirmed stays silent, and a test asserts it stays silent - counting it would fire on every returning user and the metric would stop meaning anything within a day. WHY A METRIC RATHER THAN A 4xx: the endpoint's existing reasoning still holds - answering an error would turn ordinary sign-ins into noise, and the client deliberately ignores the status. A counter is the right instrument for 'this should be rare and is not'. THREE SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening the new case: the branch removed (back to a silent 200), the metric dropped while the warn stayed, and the two reasons collapsed into one condition. AC4 STATUS UNCHANGED as a deliverable - it was and remains implemented-by-corroboration rather than by backfilling ip/user_agent onto the trigger row, which the module explains and refuses. What changed is that the claim in these notes is now true only after 00586 applies, and there is now an instrument that says so if it stops being true again. VERIFIED: deno check clean on routes/legal.ts; deno lint clean across 1486 files; signup-consent-evidence_test.ts 11 passed (1 new); full edge suite 6462 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored. | 2026-08-10 (second pass) AC6 WAS DONE FOR ONE OF THE TWO PRODUCTS APPSTORE.TS SELLS, and the guard could not see the difference. POST /api/payments/appstore/verify handles both a seller subscription and a BUYER subscription. The buyer branch (mapping.kind === 'buyer_subscription') applied the entitlement and RETURNED before BOTH recordAppstoreEvent and recordPlatformAgreement. So an App Store BUYER purchase left no audit row and no agreed-terms row, while an App Store SELLER purchase got both and a Stripe buyer purchase got the agreement via applyBuyerSubscriptionChange. Three populations, two answers to 'what did this user agree to?'. THE GUARD PASSED THROUGHOUT, and that is the reusable part. US-2116's wiring test asserted /recordPlatformAgreement\(/.test(appstore) - whether the FILE calls it, not whether each PRODUCT PATH does. A file-level check over a file that sells two things is a check over neither. It is now per-branch: each product's grant must be followed, inside its own brace-matched branch, by both the audit row and the agreement, with the agreement naming ITS OWN plan. FIXED: the buyer branch now writes both. from_plan/to_plan are NULL rather than the user's FlipDesk tier - those columns are typed public.flipdesk_plan (00037) and this event changed no FlipDesk plan, so null is the true statement while repeating their seller tier would imply a transition that did not happen. The buyer tiers ride in raw_payload. subscription_agreements.plan is free text and guard/connoisseur cannot collide with starter/pro/business, so the agreement names the real buyer plan. Skipped when the mapped plan is 'free', matching the Play path. GOOGLE PLAY IS NOT AFFECTED, checked rather than assumed: google-play-rtdn.ts and google-play.ts contain no buyer_plan references at all - Play sells only the seller product today, so there is no second branch to miss. TWO GUARD FAULTS FOUND WHILE WRITING IT, both the same family as the rest of today. (1) My first slice ran from the branch start to the first `return c.json(`, which cut before the grant because the buyer branch returns a 409 early when a Stripe subscription is already active - the assertion failed against CORRECT code, and the tempting response would have been to weaken it back to the file-wide check that hid the bug. Brace-matched instead. (2) The plan assertion read the whole branch, which also contains `plan: update.buyer_plan` in its JSON response - so switching the AGREEMENT to the seller plan stayed green. Scoped to the recordPlatformAgreement call's arguments. FOUR SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening the case: the buyer agreement dropped (the original bug), the buyer audit row dropped, the buyer agreement recording the seller plan, and the seller agreement dropped instead. AC6 IS NOW GENUINELY DONE for every platform purchase path that exists. AC1 and AC5 remain US-2114 counsel items and are untouched. VERIFIED: deno check clean on routes/appstore.ts; deno lint clean across 1486 files; agreed-terms_test.ts 19 passed; full edge suite 6462 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored. | 2026-08-12 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM IN THIS STORY, CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT. Every migration named above is on origin/main AND applied to prod. Evidence, not inference: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns {"schema":{"expected":"00589","applied":"00589","status":"match"}} - that is the running edge reading applied_migrations through the service-role client, i.e. the database own answer, and 00589 is the highest migration on origin/main. So nothing here is blocked on a frozen branch and nobody should hold a push on this story account. The ONLY genuinely held migration today is 00590 (US-2497), which is committed locally and unpushed. THE DISTINCTION THAT KEEPS GETTING BLURRED, and it is why this warning recurs: PUSHED is not APPLIED, and a note written while a migration was held stays true-sounding forever after it lands. Check the endpoint before writing HELD or APPLIED anywhere - the answer is one unauthenticated GET and several passes have reasoned from commit history instead. | 2026-08-17 AC4's BLOCKER IS GONE, AND THE NOTE ABOVE IS NOW THE STALE ONE. That segment ends 'AC4's mechanism becomes live the moment that SQL is applied, and not before'. That moment has passed. The SQL is 00586_handle_new_user_restore_legal_acceptance.sql, which restores the clickwrap INSERT that 00303 dropped, and it is APPLIED IN PRODUCTION: it appears in the shipped migration manifest, and /health/ready returns expected 00612, applied 00612, status match WITH NO missing KEY - and the absence of that key is what proves the applied SET is complete rather than merely its maximum, which is the distinction this story's own last segment insists on. So decideSignupConsentEvidence should now find a signup_clickwrap row to corroborate, and an email signup should be writing TWO legal_acceptances rows again: signup_clickwrap from the trigger (guaranteed, weak, no IP) and signup_clickwrap_confirmed from POST /api/legal/confirm-signup (best-effort, strong, server-observed IP and user-agent). ⚠ ONE CORRECTION WHILE I WAS IN HERE, because a reader chasing this would lose a session to it: the blocking migration is 00586, NOT 00573. 00573_legal_acceptances_signup_confirmed.sql is COMMENT ONLY - its own header says so in the first line, 'No table, column, constraint, index, policy or function changes', because method has always been plain text with no CHECK and the fourth value wrote fine without it. Nothing was ever gated on 00573. WHAT TO CHECK NOW, and it is cheap because the last pass built the instrument: the recordMetric('legal.signup_clickwrap_missing') counter should have STOPPED incrementing at the moment 00586 applied. A flat counter since then is the fix working; continued increments mean the trigger is still not writing and the diagnosis needs reopening. One query settles the other half: SELECT method, count(*) FROM public.legal_acceptances WHERE accepted_at > <apply time> GROUP BY method - expect both signup_clickwrap and signup_clickwrap_confirmed present, in roughly equal numbers. Added to the operator queue. AC1 and AC5 are unchanged and remain US-2114 counsel items.

userStories.title: No record of what price or terms any user actually agreed to — pricing_plans is mutated in place
userStories.description: The users table stores flipdesk_plan and flipdesk_interval but NO amount column; price is resolved live on every read via getFlipdeskPriceIds() against pricing_plans. pricing_plans (00166:69-80) is mutated in place with only an updated_at trigger — no history table, no versioning. flipdesk_subscription_events records from_plan/to_plan and the raw payload but, per the note already in 00215_revenue_dashboard.sql:20, not even the billing interval. Combined, there is no way to reconstruct what price any user was shown or agreed to on any past date. If a price changes, the historical record changes with it.
acceptanceCriteria: Snapshot the agreed terms onto the subscription record at purchase: amount, currency, interval, plan, trial terms, and the disclosure-copy version — immutable once written.
Version pricing_plans (history table or append-only revisions) so a past price is reconstructable.
Record the billing interval on flipdesk_subscription_events.
Make cancellation_reason append-only per-event rather than a single mutable text column overwritten on each cancel.
Follow the migrations skill: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bump in the same commit, self-record footer.

Also unblocks honest revenue reporting. | 2026-07-19 ALL FOUR SCHEMA ACs DONE (migration 00486) + the write path. ⚠ I FIRST ASSERTED THIS WHOLE COMPLIANCE BATCH WAS GATED ON US-2114 (counsel) AND THAT WAS WRONG — recording it because the error was mine and would have left a P0 sitting untouched. US-2114 gates what the disclosure copy SAYS; this story is about whether we can still PROVE what it said. Those are different questions, and only the first needs a lawyer. Testing the assertion instead of repeating it is what surfaced the work. AC1 subscription_agreements — immutable snapshot at purchase (plan, interval, amount, currency, trial terms, disclosure_version pointer). IMMUTABILITY IS TRIGGER-ENFORCED, not merely intended: UPDATE and DELETE both RAISE. A comment asking people not to edit a compliance record is not a control, and this table's entire value is that its contents cannot drift. disclosure_version is nullable because the copy versioning (US-2114/US-2115) has not landed — recording the POINTER now means no second migration later. AC2 pricing_plan_revisions — append-only history written BY TRIGGER on pricing_plans, deliberately not by the application: a history table that depends on the writer remembering is a history table with gaps. Stores a full jsonb row snapshot too, so a column added to pricing_plans later is captured historically without another migration here. Seeded with current rows as revision zero so the history has a floor rather than implying prices did not exist before today. AC3 flipdesk_subscription_events.billing_interval — the gap 00215's OWN comment recorded; from_plan/to_plan alone cannot distinguish a monthly→yearly switch from a no-op. AC4 subscription_cancellations — append-only; users.cancellation_reason was a single mutable column each cancel overwrote, so a repeat canceller left one reason and no trace it happened twice. Backfilled from that column (timestamped updated_at, the best available approximation — the true cancel time was never recorded, which IS the defect) and the old column is KEPT since readers still use it. WRITE PATH: lib/agreed-terms.ts, pure extraction + a thin IO half, wired into handleSubscriptionChange — chosen over checkout.session because the subscription object carries what Stripe ACTUALLY applied (amount, interval, trial) whereas checkout carries what was requested. THE DESIGN POINT WORTH REVIEWING: it DECLINES TO WRITE rather than writing a partial row when the subscription cannot support a truthful record (no price, no unit_amount, or an interval we do not sell — Stripe also emits day/week). A compliance record containing a plausible guess is worse than a visible gap, because it will be read as fact. The refusal is reported, so the gap is not silent. Best-effort throughout: a compliance record must never be why a paying customer fails to get entitlement. Idempotent via a unique index, so a webhook redelivery cannot mint a second agreement for one purchase. 9 tests. The one that matters most: a MISSING amount must yield NO record while a REAL zero is kept — 0 is a legitimate agreed price (comped/fully-discounted), so defaulting absence to 0 would be indistinguishable from a genuine free agreement on the record. Negative-verified by making absence default to 0; that test goes red. ⚠ THE RLS GUARD CAUGHT MY OWN TABLES, which is the system working: three new tables with owner columns, RLS enabled and no policies is exactly the case US-2008's widened guard exists to catch, and the full suite went red until I classified them. All three are now in SERVICE_ROLE_ONLY with the reasoning — they are evidentiary, read only by admin/support tooling, and the failure mode of a permissive policy (a user reading, or influencing, the record of what they agreed to) is precisely what they exist to rule out. STILL OPEN: nothing schema-side. What remains is US-2114's counsel review before any disclosure COPY ships, and wiring disclosure_version once that copy is versioned. Migration 00486 is HELD (7th) — see PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md for the two backfills and the deploy-order note. | 2026-07-19 ⚠ STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — do not act on it. The migration(s) this note calls HELD (00215, 00486) are all on origin/main, verified individually with git log origin/main against each file rather than inferred from the linter's summary. The standing rule makes this decisive: a commit containing a migration is NOT pushed until the operator has applied the SQL, so a migration present on origin/main was pushed, which means its hold was already released. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md agrees — every entry through 00490 (the highest migration in the tree) is marked APPLIED and confirmed by the user, so nothing is genuinely pending. WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO CORRECT: a stale hold tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not, which either invites a pointless prod session or — worse — makes them hold back an unrelated push that was always safe. Correction APPENDED rather than edited into the original sentence, because these notes are append-only and the history of what was believed when is itself worth keeping. | 2026-08-09 THE LAST OPEN ITEM IS BUILT: disclosure_version is wired end to end, so there is NO CODE LEFT TO WRITE on this story. The July note ended 'what remains is wiring disclosure_version once that copy is versioned' - US-2115 shipped the copy on 2026-08-09 and this closes the loop. THE COPY IS NOW VERSIONED, AND THE VERSION IS NOT A HAND-MAINTAINED NUMBER, which was the whole risk. DISCLOSURE_VERSION plus an append-only DISCLOSURE_ARCHIVE live in src/lib/auto-renewal-copy.ts; NEW src/lib/__tests__/disclosure-version.test.ts re-derives the sentence templates FROM THE SOURCE of disclosureSentences and fails unless they equal the current version's archive entry exactly. A version constant nobody bumps drifts away from the copy while looking authoritative, and a pointer aimed at the wrong words is a FALSE record, not a missing one - strictly worse than the null column it replaced. The archive stores TEMPLATES rather than rendered sentences on purpose: a rendering bakes in an amount and a date, and dateLabel formats in the reader's local timezone, so a rendered archive would differ by machine and could not be compared at all. THE PATH: both subscribe hooks in src/hooks/use-billing-summary.ts report the constant, payments.ts bounds it and puts it on subscription_data.metadata (and on both in-place upgrade metadata writes), and agreed-terms.ts resolves it at the write site. SENT FROM THE HOOKS, NOT FROM EACH SURFACE - every subscribe surface renders AutoRenewalDisclosure out of the same module the constant comes from, so the hook's answer is the one the screen gave, and a new surface cannot forget. AN UNKNOWN VERSION IS REFUSED, NOT STORED, and that is the same rule extractAgreedTerms already applies to a guessed amount: an id we cannot resolve is a pointer to nothing on an immutable compliance row, reading as provenance while carrying none. It is reported instead, because the realistic cause is the web copy being versioned without the edge, which would silently strip the pointer off a whole cohort. THE HONESTY CONSTRAINT, WRITTEN INTO services/edge-functions/src/lib/disclosure-versions.ts BECAUSE IT LIMITS WHAT THE FIELD PROVES: disclosure_version is CLIENT-REPORTED. Only the browser knows which build rendered the disclosure, and the edge deploys separately, so an edge-derived version would be a guess during any skew window. A determined user could report an older known version. What the server independently vouches for is the material terms - amount, interval, trial - which come from the Stripe subscription object. The version points at wording; it is not evidence against an adversarial client and must not be described as such. THE MIRROR IS DELIBERATELY THIN - version ids only, no sentences - and there are guards in BOTH directions, because US-1995 is the standing example of two copies with two green suites silently disagreeing. SECOND GAP FOUND AND FIXED, NOT IN ANY AC's WORDS BUT SQUARELY IN AC1's: applyBuyerSubscriptionChange RETURNS before the seller path's recordAgreedTerms call, so a Guard/Connoisseur subscriber had NO agreement row at all while a FlipDesk subscriber did - two paying populations with different evidentiary standing for the same question, the exact asymmetry US-2116 AC6 closed for App Store and Play. Now recorded, SKIPPING plan 'free' because that value is the unmappable-price fallback and subscription_agreements.plan is free text with no product column, so a buyer free and a seller free are indistinguishable on the record. guard/connoisseur cannot collide with starter/pro/business, so the named plans are safe as they are. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SIX WAYS, each reddening its own case and only its own, module restored: a word changed in the copy without a version bump, the edge mirror losing the current version, the insert losing the disclosure_version column, normalizeDisclosureVersion accepting unknown ids, the buyer recordAgreedTerms call removed, and one of the four payments.ts metadata sites removed. STAYS passes:false ON ONE NARROW ITEM, and only one: nobody has OBSERVED an agreement row carrying a disclosure_version. Every test here is a unit or source-structural test; none of them touch Stripe or Postgres. The mechanism is not speculative - subscription_data.metadata is the same channel that already carries user_id, which handleSubscriptionChange reads in production today - but this is an evidentiary field whose only job is to be trusted later, and 'we are confident it writes' is the wrong standard for that. One production SELECT against subscription_agreements after the next subscription settles it; it belongs with US-2347's queries. VERIFIED: full edge suite 6404 passed / 0 failed, full web suite 3892 passed / 0 failed across 319 files, deno check + deno lint clean across 1476 files, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors / 13 warnings (unchanged baseline), ui:check 0 findings. New tests: 9 web (disclosure-version.test.ts), 8 edge (disclosure-versions_test.ts), 6 added to agreed-terms_test.ts. | 2026-08-15 THE ONE OPEN ITEM IS NOW A QUERY RATHER THAN AN INTENTION. This story's last note kept it open on a single narrow thing: every disclosure_version test is a unit or source-structural test, and nobody had OBSERVED a subscription_agreements row carrying one. scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql §21 asks it directly - total agreements, how many carry a disclosure_version, the first versioned row's timestamp, and a breakdown by version/plan/interval so an unrecognised string is visible rather than averaged away. The reading note names the two distinct zero answers, because they mean opposite things: agreements_total at zero means nobody has subscribed since the table shipped and the question is still unanswered, while a non-zero total with with_disclosure_version at zero is the bad answer - rows are being written and the Stripe metadata is not arriving. Still passes:false, unchanged, and it closes on running §21 rather than on more code. | [2026-09-02][PROD READ] ANSWERED, and it is the BAD answer the section warned about. Source: scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql run read-only against prod over SSH on 2026-09-02 (container supabase-db-kcksoks4kk0kswk0ccs40os8, 29 sections, 0 SQL errors). Raw output kept out of the repo; it contains customer data. agreements_total is 2 and with_disclosure_version is ZERO; both rows are starter/monthly, newest 2026-07-28. The section states the reading rule explicitly: zero rows would mean nobody has subscribed and the question stays open, but a NON-ZERO total with zero disclosure versions means rows ARE being written and the metadata is NOT arriving. That is what prod shows. So the Stripe subscription_data.metadata channel is not delivering disclosure_version, and the column that exists to be trusted years later in a dispute is empty for every agreement that exists.

userStories.title: Build the authenticity golden set — the gate is worthless without ground truth
userStories.description: authenticity_eval_cases (00405_authenticity_eval.sql) exists but has NO seed rows anywhere in the repo — by design, the golden set is operator-curated. runAuthenticityEval would throw on first call (authenticity-eval.ts:183). This is the expensive, slow, expert-dependent asset that everything else in the epic depends on, and it cannot be generated by an agent: it requires labeled authentic-vs-counterfeit items with real photos and defensible provenance for each label.
acceptanceCriteria: Define what a case requires: photos at the resolution the pipeline actually receives, the ground-truth label, the provenance of that label (who determined it and how), brand, garment type, and the tells that justify the label.
Build the operator curation surface for adding, reviewing and retiring cases.
Set the passing bar with counsel/product input — including the false-positive bar, which matters far more than overall accuracy: calling a genuine item fake is the more damaging error.
Seed an initial set covering the brands we actually see most, not the brands that are most interesting.
Track per-brand coverage so the gate cannot pass on a brand it has never seen.
Follow the grading-engine skill's golden-set rules and exemplar-privacy constraints.

OPERATOR: the authenticity golden set needs LABELS, and labelling is the story. The gate is worthless without ground truth, and ground truth here means a person deciding genuine or not on real items. Nothing in this repo can produce it, and US-2134's AC5 (narrowing the prompt) is gated on it.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Data][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. USER/EXPERT ACTION REQUIRED — an agent can build the surface and the schema, but not the labels. This is the true critical path for the whole epic; sequence accordingly. Sourcing options to evaluate: partner with an authentication service, buy a labeled corpus, or curate from our own human-review history where provenance is defensible. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: the CURATION SURFACE is built — GET/POST/PATCH /api/admin/grading/authenticity/cases, needing NO migration because 00405 already carries every column including source_url for label provenance. Deliberately NO delete route: per the grading-engine contract a shrinking golden set is a red flag, and deleting the cases a prompt fails is the easiest way to fake a pass — cases are RETIRED (is_active=false) and every ground-truth change is audited. validateAuthenticityCase rejects empty images at write time rather than letting runAuthenticityEval throw mid-run after spending vision calls on earlier cases. summarizeCaseCoverage marks a brand usable ONLY with at least one authentic AND one counterfeit case: a perfect score over authentic-only cases cannot demonstrate the one error the gate exists to catch. 4357 edge tests pass. STILL BLOCKED: the labels themselves. An expert must now add real cases through this surface; nothing downstream (the gate passing, US-2134 prompt narrowing, US-2143 positioning) can move until they exist. ITER 2026-07-19: bulk import shipped — lib/golden-set-import.ts + POST /api/admin/grading/authenticity/cases/import, plus docs/authenticity-golden-set-template.json. Partial success is REPORTED per row (index + reason) and does not fail the batch: re-uploading 50 rows over one typo is how people start bypassing validation. Returns 207 when any row was rejected, 201 when clean, and a rejected count is always present so a caller can tell a partial from a full success without parsing counts. brand_key is alias-resolved via brandKeyForRaw, so an import written "Levi Strauss" lands on the same key as the KB row and as a review-promoted case. coverageWarnings flags a brand imported with only ONE polarity — 40 genuine cases and no fakes scores perfectly and proves nothing, since the dangerous miss cannot occur; the mirror case (counterfeit-only) yields no false-positive rate, the error that harms sellers. Warnings do NOT reject, since a corpus may legitimately arrive in halves. Capped at 500 rows/batch. 4426 edge tests pass (+9). STILL THE BLOCKER: the labels themselves. UI 2026-07-19: /admin/authenticity console shipped (src/pages/admin/authenticity.tsx), route + nav registered. Gate status is the FIRST thing on the page rather than three clicks deep, because an ungated prompt is currently serving real users including a public endpoint. Accuracy NEVER renders a single number — the two error directions sit side by side and are labelled by WHO they harm (buyer got a fake we vouched for / seller had a genuine item flagged, which nobody reimburses), because a combined figure stays flat while a version trades one for the other.

userStories.title: A seller whose GENUINE item is flagged has no way to contest it
userStories.description:
Every control in the authenticity module protects the buyer. There is nothing for a seller whose genuine item receives a red_flags verdict: the dispute system is grade/condition-shaped and carries no authenticity path (verified — zero authenticity references in the dispute routes/lib), there is no appeal, no re-assessment, and no way to have a wrong verdict withdrawn.

This got WORSE on 2026-07-19, by our own hand. US-2141 sealed the verdict into certificate integrity v4, and US-2142 wrote it to the garment passport — an append-only ledger with no update or delete policy. So a wrong verdict is now durable, tamper-evident, and by design cannot be erased. We made the record permanent before building the correction path.

Three things compound it: the pass has never cleared an accuracy gate (US-2130/2131), so we cannot state an error rate; confidence is capped but not zero when no macro evidence exists (US-2134), so thin-evidence verdicts still publish; and this is the error direction a financial guarantee would NOT cover (Entrupy-style guarantees pay out on fakes sold as real, not on genuine items called fake), so the seller bears it entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: A seller can contest an authenticity verdict from the surfaces where they see it, with a defined SLA and a human decision — not a form that goes nowhere.

Define what the certificate and passport show WHILE an appeal is open. The passport is append-only, so a withdrawal is a superseding event, never a deletion — decide and document what the public view renders for a superseded verdict.

Wire the outcome through the existing authenticity review path (US-2140) so an upheld appeal produces a reviewer verdict, and a wrongly-flagged genuine item becomes an 'authentic' golden-set case — the most valuable label we can get.
Reseal the certificate on withdrawal (integrity v4 covers the verdict, so a change without a reseal breaks verification).
Notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is published, not only when they happen to look. They cannot contest what they never saw.
Counsel sign-off on the notice and appeal wording — fold into US-2133 rather than running a separate review.
OPERATOR: AC6 needs counsel on the contest/appeal terms. AC1 through AC5 shipped, including the contest button that was the only missing piece of the flow.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Fairness][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 reviewing the authenticity module for gaps after the epic's backend landed. Publicly attaching 'red flags' to a real person's item, from a model with no measured error rate, has a defamation-adjacent shape that belongs in the counsel review. Sharpest open exposure in the module. Sequence with US-2133; do not let an agent draft the notice language. PARTIAL 2026-07-19 (mechanics only): migration 00489 adds disputes.kind (grade|authenticity, default grade) — EXTENDING the existing disputes table rather than building an appeals table, since disputes is already generic at the schema level (grade_report_id, user_id, free-text reason, status, resolution_notes) and only its RESOLUTION path is grade-shaped. One lifecycle, one admin queue, one place a user looks. HELD; packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md. lib/authenticity-appeal.ts encodes three decisions worth review: (1) an upheld appeal CLEARS the verdict rather than flipping it to likely_authentic — the assessment should never have been published, which is not the same as positively vouching for the item, and asserting that would be the same overreach reversed; (2) the reseal carries the SCORES through untouched, because an authenticity appeal says nothing about condition and silently re-deriving a grade would change a number nobody contested; (3) a REJECTED appeal produces NO golden-set case — upholding the original verdict is not a human independently confirming counterfeit (the reviewer may just have found the appeal unpersuasive), and treating it as ground truth would seed the golden set with unverified labels. An upheld appeal DOES yield an authentic case, which is a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE — the most valuable label available, and the error direction US-2146 exists to measure. 4408 edge tests pass (+7). DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED, still needs you + counsel (US-2133): what the certificate and passport RENDER while an appeal is open, the SLA, the seller notification wording, and whether a published red_flags verdict should notify the seller proactively. No routes shipped yet — the lib is pure logic + tests, so nothing is user-reachable until those decisions land. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (in my own iteration-4 work): withdrawAssessment cleared only verdict/verdict_confidence, but the PUBLIC certificate view (00172, carried through 00307) does NOT read verdict — it derives what a buyer sees from authenticity_confidence (-> confidence band), counterfeit_risk (-> risk label) and summary (rendered verbatim). So an upheld appeal would have cleared the internal verdict while the certificate kept publicly showing an elevated counterfeit risk and the original red-flag summary: the seller wins and stays flagged, which is exactly the failure this story exists to fix. Now clears every projected field, moves the original under withdrawn_original (operator-side; no view projects it) so the record of what was said survives, and exports PUBLICLY_PROJECTED_ASSESSMENT_FIELDS with a test that iterates it — if the view ever learns a new field, that test fails rather than a seller silently staying flagged. Also confirmed: the edge-SSR cert page renders no authenticity at all (SPA-only), and authenticity_checked in the public view derives from image_authenticity (PHOTO-EDIT, 00061), which is a different signal from the brand add-on and must not be conflated. 4412 edge tests pass. SELLER ROUTE 2026-07-19: POST /api/grade/authenticity-appeal shipped, implementing the approved §1a/§1b decisions. Files as disputes.kind=authenticity (00489) rather than a parallel table. Ownership verified through the submission (grade_reports has no user_id) and a miss reports 404 so an id probe cannot distinguish does-not-exist from not-yours; viewers are blocked, matching the grade-dispute route. Hiding the verdict while an appeal is open is REVERSIBLE — hideAssessmentForAppeal clears the publicly-projected fields and stashes the originals under appeal_hidden_original, so a rejected appeal restores exactly what was there and hiding is not a quiet way to lose a verdict; hiding twice does not bury the original (tested). Rate limited to 5 open appeals per seller, which exists BECAUSE hiding is free otherwise: unlimited appeals would suppress every verdict indefinitely at no cost. CAUGHT DURING IMPLEMENTATION: the first version called the reseal before the update landed, so it would have hashed the OLD verdict and written a signature verifying against nothing — resealAfterAuthenticityChange now takes the NEXT assessment explicitly, which makes that mistake impossible rather than merely fixed. If hiding fails the appeal is still recorded (better a visible verdict with a filed appeal than a silent appeal nobody actions). 4431 edge tests pass. STILL OPEN: the admin resolve route, seller notification on a published red_flags verdict, and the notice wording (needs the SLA number + counsel). ADMIN RESOLVE 2026-07-19: GET /authenticity/appeals (open queue, OLDEST FIRST — while an appeal is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade, so waiting time is itself a penalty) + POST /authenticity/appeals/:id/resolve. Step-up gated: upholding withdraws a published verdict and reseals a certificate, rejecting republishes one. Upheld -> withdrawAssessment (permanent, clears every publicly-projected field); rejected -> restoreAssessmentAfterAppeal (exactly what was hidden, since the reviewer finding the appeal unpersuasive is not a new finding about the item). Both reseal with the NEXT assessment. An upheld appeal also records an authentic reviewer verdict through the US-2140 path, because a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE is the most valuable label available and the error direction nothing else measures — the model_verdict snapshot reads from appeal_hidden_original, since the live field was nulled when the appeal was filed. Already-resolved appeals 409 rather than double-applying. 4431 edge tests pass. REMAINING on this story: seller notification on a published red_flags verdict, and the notice wording (SLA number + counsel). | 2026-07-19 ⚠ STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — do not act on it. The migration(s) this note calls HELD (00061, 00172, 00307, 00489) are all on origin/main, verified individually with git log origin/main against each file rather than inferred from the linter's summary. The standing rule makes this decisive: a commit containing a migration is NOT pushed until the operator has applied the SQL, so a migration present on origin/main was pushed, which means its hold was already released. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md agrees — every entry through 00490 (the highest migration in the tree) is marked APPLIED and confirmed by the user, so nothing is genuinely pending. WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO CORRECT: a stale hold tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not, which either invites a pointless prod session or — worse — makes them hold back an unrelated push that was always safe. Correction APPENDED rather than edited into the original sentence, because these notes are append-only and the history of what was believed when is itself worth keeping. NOTIFICATION 2026-07-19: lib/authenticity-notify.ts, fired from the pipeline at finalize. Implements the approved §1a decision — red_flags ONLY, never on inconclusive (not a finding; telling a seller invites appeals against nothing) and never on likely_authentic. SLA of 5 business days is stated in the notice, per the decision: an appeal with no stated turnaround cannot be planned around, and while it is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade. COPY IS DELIBERATELY NON-ACCUSATORY and tested to stay that way — it says the check flagged details it COULD NOT CONFIRM, calls itself an automated photo estimate and not a determination, and a test asserts the words counterfeit/fake never appear, because the pass has no measured error rate and must not assert what it cannot support. Rides the existing dispute_update channel rather than inventing a type the users notification preferences do not know about, which would have made it unsuppressable. Best-effort so a notification problem never breaks a paid grade. ⚠ COPY STILL NEEDS COUNSEL REVIEW under US-2133 — flagged in the module header; it should be reviewed alongside the certificate copy, not separately. 4453 edge tests pass (+22). | 2026-08-02 THE APPEAL PIPELINE IS BUILT AT BOTH ENDS AND HAS NO SELLER-FACING BUTTON. Verified by grep, not inferred. The SELLER endpoint exists and is complete: POST /authenticity-appeal at routes/grade.ts:1301 — it verifies the caller owns the submission, 422s when the grade has no authenticity assessment to contest, and rate-limits deliberately (the comment says why: hiding the verdict while an appeal is open means an unlimited appeal is a free way to suppress every verdict indefinitely — that is a well-reasoned control, not boilerplate). The ADMIN side exists too: GET /authenticity/appeals is the open queue oldest-first and POST /authenticity/appeals/:id/resolve closes them, and the queue's ordering carries its own reasoning (while an appeal is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade, so waiting time is itself a penalty). AND NOTHING IN src/ CALLS THE SELLER ENDPOINT. A grep for "authenticity-appeal" across every .ts and .tsx under src returns ZERO hits. So an operator opening the appeals queue sees a list that can only ever be empty, and a seller whose genuine item was flagged still has exactly what the story title says: no way to contest it. THE SHAPE IS THE ONE THIS SESSION KEPT FINDING, and it is the third instance today — the waitlist backend with no public capture form, the grade-card switch writing columns nothing read, and now this. Each time the expensive half was built and the cheap half was not, and each time the missing half is the one a USER touches. Worth naming explicitly on a story about a seller being unable to defend a genuine item: the backend being done makes this look further along than it is, and anyone reading the route file would conclude the feature ships. WHAT REMAINS FOR AC1 is therefore smaller than the AC implies but not trivial: the surfaces where a seller SEES the verdict (the certificate view and the submission detail) need a contest action that POSTs to the existing endpoint, plus the open-appeal state AC2 asks about — and AC2 is a real design question, not wiring, because the passport is append-only so a withdrawal is a superseding entry rather than an edit. AC5 (notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is published) is also still open and is arguably prior to AC1: they cannot contest what they were never told about. AC6 needs counsel. I did not build the UI — the certificate and passport display rules in AC2 have to be settled first, and shipping a contest button before deciding what the certificate shows while an appeal is open would put a seller in a state nobody has defined. | 2026-08-02 AC1 AND AC2 DONE — the seller can now contest a verdict. MY EARLIER BLOCKER DISSOLVED ON INSPECTION, and that is worth recording because I nearly left this unbuilt on it: I said AC2 (what the certificate shows while an appeal is open) had to be settled first. It already was, server-side, and I had not read far enough. hideAssessmentForAppeal (lib/authenticity-appeal.ts:106) NULLS verdict, verdict_confidence, authenticity_confidence, counterfeit_risk and summary, sets under_appeal + appeal_opened_at, and stashes the original in appeal_hidden_original — guarded against stashing a stash on a second appeal, which would make the original unrecoverable. The endpoint then RESEALS (AC4) because integrity v4 covers the verdict, and its own comment explains why the reseal passes the HIDDEN assessment rather than the stored one. So AC2 and AC4 were shipped; only the button was missing. SHIPPED: NEW src/components/grade/authenticity-appeal-dialog.tsx and a "This is genuine — contest this result" action on submission-detail.tsx, the surface where the seller actually sees the verdict. THREE DETAILS THAT ARE NOT DECORATION. (1) The page now renders an UNDER-REVIEW card when under_appeal is set, instead of the normal card. Without it the seller sees a row of blanks where the verdict was — which reads as a bug, and is worse than not shipping the button at all, because it makes them think their appeal broke something. (2) The dialog is mounted at the PAGE root, not inside the authenticity card, so it is not unmounted the instant the card swaps to its under-review state on a successful file. (3) MIN_REASON = 20 mirrors the server's validateAppeal floor deliberately, and the client copy spends it telling the seller what a reviewer needs before they type: being rejected after writing is how someone abandons an appeal they were entitled to. The 429 path surfaces the SERVER's message rather than a generic retry, because that cap is a deliberate control (an unlimited appeal is a free way to suppress every verdict) and a retry prompt would send the seller round the same loop. GUARD: NEW src/test/authenticity-appeal-wired.test.ts — something must POST to the endpoint, the dialog must be RENDERED somewhere rather than merely defined, the seller surface must handle under_appeal, and the client minimum must match the server's. A route with no caller is invisible to tsc, to lint, and to every test that exercises the route directly, so only a scan catches it. STILL OPEN: AC3 (wire an upheld appeal through the US-2140 reviewer path), AC5 (notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is PUBLISHED — arguably prior to all of this, since they cannot contest what they were never told), AC6 (counsel, folded into US-2133). VERIFIED: full web suite 248 files / 3154 tests 0 failed, build clean through the 216-route prerender, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors. | 2026-08-02 CORRECTION TO MY OWN NOTE ABOVE, and a better outcome than expected. I wrote that AC5 was "still open" and "arguably prior to all of this, since they cannot contest what they were never told". THAT IS WRONG. AC5 IS DONE. notifyAuthenticityFlagged (lib/authenticity-notify.ts:71) is called from grading-pipeline.ts:2785, fires only on a red_flags verdict, and is best-effort so a notification problem never breaks a paid grade. It had reached the same design conclusion I was about to: it rides the existing dispute_update channel rather than inventing a notification type the user's preferences do not know about — an appeal IS a dispute. Its copy is careful in a way worth preserving: "our authenticity check flagged details it could not confirm ... an automated estimate from photos, not a determination", because saying the item IS counterfeit would assert something an ungated photo-only estimate cannot support. THE FLOW IS NOW END-TO-END, which is the actual news: the notice links to /dashboard/submissions/{id}, and that is exactly the page where the contest button I added this session lives. So the loop closes — red_flags verdict fires a notification, the seller clicks through, and the button is there. Before today the notification landed on a page with nothing to do. That is the same defect one level up from the one I fixed: the notice was built, the endpoint was built, and the two were never joined. HOW I GOT IT WRONG: I asserted AC5 was open from the AC text plus the absence of any UI, without grepping the pipeline for a notify call. The lesson is the one this session kept re-learning in the other direction — I checked whether the ENDPOINT had a caller and correctly found none, then failed to run the same check on the NOTIFICATION and assumed. Absence of a caller is a thing you verify, not infer, in both directions. REMAINING ON THIS STORY: AC3 (wire an upheld appeal through the US-2140 reviewer path so a withdrawal produces a reviewer verdict) and AC6 (counsel sign-off on the notice and appeal wording, folded into US-2133). AC1, AC2, AC4 and AC5 all stand. | 2026-08-02 AC3 IS ALSO ALREADY DONE — checked rather than assumed this time, having just been wrong about AC5. POST /authenticity/appeals/:id/resolve takes an outcome of upheld or rejected, refuses to re-resolve an already-closed appeal, and splits correctly: UPHELD withdraws the verdict permanently, REJECTED restores exactly what was hidden — with the reasoning stated inline that a reviewer finding an appeal unpersuasive is not a new finding about the item, so the original stands rather than being re-derived. It reseals, updates the dispute status, and when plan.reviewerVerdict is set it feeds the outcome through the same review path so it counts toward accuracy and can be promoted, which is precisely what AC3 asked for. SO US-2145 STANDS AT: AC1 done (the contest button, this session — the only piece that was actually missing), AC2 done, AC3 done, AC4 done, AC5 done, AC6 outstanding and needing counsel on the notice and appeal wording, folded into US-2133 per the AC itself. THE SHAPE OF THIS STORY IS WORTH KEEPING, because it is the clearest example of the pattern this whole session kept hitting: FIVE of six criteria were fully implemented — endpoint, hiding, reseal, reviewer path, notification — and the story read as untouched because the one missing piece was a button. Every file a reader would open to check suggested the feature shipped, and the seller still could not contest anything. The expensive halves were all built; the cheap half, the one a user touches, was not. A route with no caller is invisible to tsc, to lint, and to any test that exercises the route directly, which is why it survived. RECOMMENDATION: close on AC1-AC5 and let AC6 travel with US-2133, or leave open pointing there — an owner call, and specifically not one I should make by writing a note that sounds like agreement on a story with a legal-review criterion.

userStories.title: EPIC: Grading depth — identity, sizing, brand knowledge and product coverage
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the grading pipeline to identify WHAT it is grading as rigorously as it grades CONDITION, and to cover the product categories sellers actually list, because today the two halves of the product are lopsided: the condition engine is deep (5 weighted factors, defect taxonomy with mm tolerances, fabric-aware criteria, confidence caps, shadow/eval/canary lifecycle) while identity is thin (brand and size on a certificate are whatever the seller typed) and coverage is clothing-only (a hat, a tie, a belt and a handbag all have a garment_category and no way to be graded).
acceptanceCriteria: Every child story in this epic names the exact module, table or enum it changes — no story in this epic may be closed on prose alone.
Identity work does not weaken US-346: label-read fields are server-derived and TRUSTED; seller-typed brand/size stay fenced and untrusted, and neither channel may move a factor score.
Any change to a grading prompt in this epic goes through the mandated lifecycle (new version name -> shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary), never a silent edit.

Any new rubric added by this epic keeps the three weighted-overall rounding sites in lockstep (ai-grading.ts roundToTenth, human-review.ts computeWeightedOverall, admin/reviews.tsx computeWeightedScore) in the same commit.
Epic closes only when its children close; it carries no implementation of its own.

Three of the six ids this epic names are still open and all three are declared. userStories.title: In-place plan upgrade charges a prorated amount on a single click with no confirmation
userStories.description: services/edge-functions/src/routes/payments.ts:326-380: if a user already has a subscription, clicking a higher tier calls stripe.subscriptions.update with proration_behavior: 'create_prorations' — charging immediately with NO Stripe Checkout page, no price confirmation, no interstitial and no disclosure. The click IS the purchase. Every other purchase path at least passes through Stripe's hosted checkout, which renders the recurring price; this one renders nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: Show an explicit confirmation step before an in-place upgrade that states the prorated amount charged today, the new recurring amount, the new billing frequency, and the next renewal date.
Capture the same affirmative consent artifact as a new subscription.
Apply the same treatment to downgrades and interval switches if they charge or change terms.
Test asserting the upgrade mutation cannot fire without the confirmation step.

OPERATOR: run one real paid-to-higher upgrade against Stripe TEST MODE, on both products, and confirm the prorated figure the dialog discloses is the figure Stripe actually charges. Everything else is built and guarded on both FlipDesk and buyer: the 409 gate sits before the mutation, the preview endpoint simulates the item swap, the consent artifact is written, and seven sabotage mutations plus a control each reddened their own test. WHY THIS CANNOT BE WAVED THROUGH: a dialog stating a WRONG prorated amount is worse than today's no-dialog state, because it converts an omission into an affirmative misstatement about a charge. The structural tests prove the gate is wired; they cannot prove the arithmetic. Also confirm the webhook writes an agreement row for an in-place change (AC2 - US-2117 landed the plumbing).
userStories.notes:
[P1][Compliance/Web] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). A charge with no disclosure and no confirmation is the clearest Section 5 / ROSCA exposure in the codebase after the missing disclosures themselves. | 2026-07-19 SCOPED, DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT — and the reason is the story's own logic, not capacity. AC1 needs a confirmation stating the PRORATED AMOUNT CHARGED TODAY, the new recurring amount, the new frequency and the next renewal date. Those numbers do not exist anywhere yet: payments.ts has fetchUpcomingInvoice (US-400) but that returns the CURRENT subscription's upcoming invoice, not a simulation of what a CHANGE would cost. Getting the real figure needs Stripe's proration preview — invoices.retrieveUpcoming with the PROPOSED subscription_items plus a subscription_proration_date — which is a new endpoint, and one whose output I cannot verify from this sandbox (the Stripe MCP connector is unauthorized; see US-2033, blocked the same way). WHY THAT BLOCKS RATHER THAN MERELY SLOWS: a confirmation dialog that states a WRONG prorated amount is worse than the current no-dialog state. Today the defect is an OMISSION — the click is the purchase and nothing is stated. A dialog showing an unverified number converts that into an AFFIRMATIVE MISSTATEMENT about a charge, on the exact surface this compliance batch exists to fix. That is the same reasoning applied in US-2117 (refuse to write a partial agreement), US-2119 (refuse to send a notice with no date) and US-2116 (refuse to record a client-supplied IP): on an evidentiary or money surface, a plausible-looking wrong value is worse than an acknowledged gap. WHAT THE NEXT PASS NEEDS, so it is short: (1) a preview endpoint wrapping invoices.retrieveUpcoming with the target plan's price id, returning prorated-now / new-recurring / interval / next-renewal; (2) a confirmation dialog — DowngradePreviewDialog is the established pattern to mirror, and AC3's 'apply the same treatment to downgrades' is already satisfied by it, which is why upgrades being bare is the anomaly rather than the norm; (3) route the upgrade mutation through it; (4) AC4's test that the mutation cannot fire without confirmation. AC2 (capture the same consent artifact as a new subscription) is now CHEAP because US-2117 landed: subscription_agreements + recordAgreedTerms already exist, and an in-place upgrade produces a customer.subscription.updated event that already flows through handleSubscriptionChange — which now calls recordAgreedTerms. So an upgrade ALREADY writes an agreement row with the new plan/interval/amount. Worth verifying rather than assuming, but the plumbing is in place. The FIGURES are the blocker, and they need a Stripe session — not more code reading. | 2026-07-23 CODE COMPLETE (branch claude/session-planning-jokq5h); edge unvalidated in-sandbox (no deno), CI + a real Stripe test env confirm. The in-place upgrade (payments.ts /flipdesk/subscribe, existing paid sub → higher tier) called stripe.subscriptions.update with create_prorations on a single click — no disclosure, no consent. AC1: new POST /flipdesk/upgrade-preview computes the real proration via stripe.invoices.retrieveUpcoming (simulating the item swap with subscription_items + subscription_proration_behavior) and returns amount_due_today_cents, currency, new_recurring_cents, interval, next_renewal_at (current_period_end). AC4 (server-enforced, the strong guarantee): the in-place path now refuses unless the body carries confirmUpgrade:true — returns 409 { code:'UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED', requiresConfirmation:true } and does NOT mutate; the gate sits BEFORE subscriptions.update. AC2: on a confirmed change it writes a consent artifact to flipdesk_subscription_events (event_type 'in_place_change_confirmed', from/to plan, raw_payload with prices+interval+source) — the equivalent of Checkout's disclosure. Web: new UpgradePreviewDialog (mirrors the existing DowngradePreviewDialog) fetches the preview and discloses amount today / new recurring rate+frequency / next renewal before confirming; the plan picker's upgrade CTA opens it for a paid→higher change and calls subscribe with confirmUpgrade:true on confirm. A free→paid upgrade still goes straight to Stripe Checkout (which discloses on its own hosted page), so it skips the dialog. AC3: downgrades already route through DowngradePreviewDialog and interval switches through the Stripe billing portal (both disclose/confirm) — the upgrade path was the only gap, now closed. TESTS: edge upgrade-confirmation-gate_test.ts asserts (source-structural, this repo's idiom for Stripe-heavy routes — cf. subscription-ack-disclosure_test.ts) that the confirmUpgrade gate precedes the mutation, the preview endpoint + retrieveUpcoming exist, and the consent artifact is written; all 10 assertions verified green by replicating them in node against payments.ts. Verified in-sandbox: web tsc -b + eslint clean; billing+hooks vitest 36/36 green; only flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog uses useFlipdeskSubscribe and only use-billing-summary calls the endpoint, so no other caller now 409s. KEPT passes:false: the edge route + the Stripe preview call are not runnable here (no deno, no Stripe test key); run the deno lane + exercise a real paid→higher upgrade against Stripe test mode to confirm the prorated amount + consent row, then flip. | 2026-08-09 THE EDGE HALF IS NOW VALIDATED BY RUNNING IT, and doing that found a hole in the guard itself.

The 2026-07-23 note recorded the edge tests as "unvalidated in-sandbox (no deno)" and said the assertions had been verified by REPLICATING them in node against payments.ts. Deno is on this host, so I ran the real thing: services/edge-functions/src/tests/upgrade-confirmation-gate_test.ts, 4 passed / 0 failed. Replicating assertions in another runtime proves the assertions, not the test file — and the difference showed up immediately when the file was attacked properly.

⚠ THE HOLE, FOUND BY MUTATION AND NOW CLOSED. Three sabotages were run against payments.ts. Two reddened (deleting the UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED gate, deleting the /flipdesk/upgrade-preview endpoint). THE THIRD DID NOT: replacing the definition with a constant — `const confirmUpgrade = true` — left the whole file GREEN while every unconfirmed click charged a prorated amount again, which is precisely the defect this story exists to fix.

WHY IT SLIPPED, and it generalises: the test asserted `if (!confirmUpgrade)` appears inside inPlaceBlock(), so it proved the gate READS a variable and said nothing about where that variable's value comes from. The definition sits ABOVE the block slice's start marker, so the slice never saw the change. A guard that checks the USE but not the DERIVATION passes over a gate that no longer gates — the worst shape a compliance guard can take, because its greenness is what stops anyone looking.

FIXED: the test now pins the derivation to the request body (const confirmUpgrade = (body...).confirmUpgrade === true) and separately refuses a literal. Re-run of the same three mutations: 3/3 caught, revert green.

STILL passes:false, and the remaining blocker is UNCHANGED and genuinely not doable here: a real paid->higher upgrade against Stripe test mode, to confirm the prorated figure the dialog discloses is the figure Stripe actually charges. The 2026-07-19 note's reasoning still governs and is worth restating because it is why this cannot be waved through — a dialog stating a WRONG prorated amount is worse than today's no-dialog state, because it converts an omission into an affirmative misstatement about a charge. The structural tests prove the gate is wired and now prove it is genuinely wired; they cannot prove the arithmetic.

VERIFIED: upgrade-confirmation-gate_test.ts 4 passed (now with 2 added assertions), full edge suite 6375 passed / 0 failed, deno lint clean. | 2026-08-09 SCOPE CORRECTION FOUND WHILE WIRING US-2117, and it widens this story rather than advancing it: THE CONFIRMATION GATE IS ON THE FLIPDESK PATH ONLY. services/edge-functions/src/routes/payments.ts POST /buyer/subscribe has its own in-place upgrade branch - retrieve, release schedule, subscriptions.update with proration_behavior 'create_prorations' - and it has NO confirmUpgrade check and no equivalent of the FlipDesk 409 UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED. So a Guard subscriber clicking Connoisseur is charged a prorated amount on a single click with no interstitial and no disclosure: precisely the defect in this story's title, still live, on the buyer product. THAT IS AC1 AND AC3 UNMET FOR ONE OF THE TWO SUBSCRIPTION PRODUCTS, and AC4's test does not catch it because upgrade-confirmation-gate_test.ts pins the FlipDesk route by name. A guard scoped to one of two identical code paths reads as covering both. NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately, because it is not a one-line gate: it needs the buyer equivalent of the proration-preview endpoint and a buyer confirmation dialog, and shipping the 409 without them would break buyer upgrades outright. Recorded so the next pass on this story starts with the correct scope rather than re-finding it. The story's existing blocker (a real paid-to-higher upgrade against Stripe test mode, to confirm the disclosed prorated figure matches what Stripe charges) is unchanged and now applies to both products. | 2026-08-10 THE BUYER HALF IS BUILT. The 2026-08-09 scope correction found that the confirmation gate was on the FlipDesk path ONLY, and that POST /buyer/subscribe had the same in-place branch - retrieve, release schedule, subscriptions.update with create_prorations - with no gate and no disclosure. So a Guard subscriber clicking Connoisseur was charged a prorated amount on one click. That is now closed to parity with FlipDesk. EDGE: /buyer/subscribe refuses without confirmUpgrade (409 UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, gate BEFORE the mutation), and a NEW POST /buyer/upgrade-preview returns amount_due_today_cents / currency / new_recurring_cents / interval / next_renewal_at from stripe.invoices.retrieveUpcoming simulating the item swap. Kept as its OWN route rather than a product parameter on the FlipDesk one: the two read different subscription ids, different price tables and different plan enums, and a single route branching on a product string is one wrong branch away from previewing a FlipDesk charge for a buyer click. ⚠ THE ENUM TRAP, avoided by reading the schema rather than copying the FlipDesk insert. The consent artifact goes to flipdesk_subscription_events (the generic subscription audit log - App Store, Google Play and admin all reuse it). Its from_plan/to_plan columns are typed public.flipdesk_plan = free|starter|pro|business (00037). Buyer tiers are guard|connoisseur (public.buyer_plan, 00402). Writing to_plan:'guard' raises 22P02 - and because this insert is best-effort BY DESIGN (the plan change already succeeded, so a logging failure must not fail the request), the row would simply never appear while the charge went through. A consent artifact that silently does not exist is worse than none, because the code reads as if it does. The buyer plans go in raw_payload, which is jsonb and has no enum to violate. WEB: useBuyerSubscribe takes confirmUpgrade; NEW useBuyerUpgradePreview; UpgradePreviewDialog generalized to a discriminated product union ('flipdesk' | 'buyer') so a buyer tier cannot be passed as a FlipDesk one - one dialog rather than two near-identical ones that drift. The buyer billing page now diverts an already-paying click to the dialog instead of the mutation; a buyer with NO live subscription still goes straight to Stripe Checkout, which discloses on its own hosted page. THE GUARD THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THIS, and it is the part worth keeping. upgrade-confirmation-gate_test.ts named one route, which is exactly how the second one stayed bare for months. It is now driven off a PRODUCTS table, and a new final case DISCOVERS prorating mutations from the source instead: every `await stripe.subscriptions.update(` whose options contain proration_behavior 'create_prorations' must have UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED between the start of its handler and the call. A third subscription product cannot repeat this. The derivation check also became a COUNT (one body-derived confirmUpgrade per product) rather than a presence check, so adding an ungated product fails it. WEB GUARD, derived by scanning src/ rather than from a list, same reasoning: NEW src/test/in-place-upgrade-confirmation.test.ts finds every caller of a subscribe hook, and requires each to render the dialog, to mount it with ITS OWN product string, and - the one that matters - to be able to open the dialog from the very handler that can fire the subscribe mutation. Rendering the dialog is NOT the same as routing to it, and that difference IS this defect: the buyer page could have mounted the dialog and still charged on the click. Handler bodies are brace-matched rather than sliced to the mutation, because the FlipDesk picker puts the mutation in one if/else arm and the dialog in the other. MY FIRST TWO WEB ASSERTIONS WERE TOO WEAK AND SABOTAGE FOUND BOTH. Deleting the buyer page's diversion left the file green (it still RENDERED the dialog), and replacing the disclosed amount with money(null) left it green (the field name still appeared elsewhere). Both are now bound: the handler check above, and the figures asserted as BINDINGS to the preview response (value={money(data.amount_due_today_cents, currency)} etc.) rather than as strings present in the file. ALSO FIXED A HARNESS BUG WORTH RECORDING: my sabotage runner stripped ANSI as /\[[0-9;]*m/ without the ESC character, so deno's coloured 'name ... FAILED' lines never matched and EVERY mutation reported NOTHING FAILED. I nearly read that as the tests being weak. A negative verification whose PARSER is broken is indistinguishable from one that found nothing - the runner needs a control mutation that is expected to change nothing, which this one now has (moving a no-op line inside the gate; it correctly stays green). STILL passes:false, blocker UNCHANGED and now covering both products: a real paid-to-higher upgrade against Stripe test mode, to confirm the prorated figure the dialog discloses is the figure Stripe actually charges. The 2026-07-19 reasoning still governs - a dialog stating a WRONG prorated amount is worse than no dialog, because it converts an omission into an affirmative misstatement about a charge. The structural tests prove the gate is wired; they cannot prove the arithmetic. AC2 also still wants confirming that the webhook's recordAgreedTerms writes a buyer agreement row for an in-place change (US-2117 landed the plumbing). VERIFIED: npx tsc -b clean; eslint 0 errors / 13 warnings (baseline held); npm run ui:check 0 blocking / 0 noise; full edge suite 6431 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored (up 7); upgrade-confirmation-gate_test.ts 11 passed; in-place-upgrade-confirmation.test.ts 10 passed; deno lint clean across 1481 files.
