userStories.title: MeasureCard is a brochure with no path into the actual measure flow
userStories.description: As a reseller reading the MeasureCard page, I want a button into the measure tool and a sample of the finished result, so the page leads to the capability it describes instead of dead-ending.
acceptanceCriteria: src/pages/flipdesk/measure-card.tsx adds a primary CTA linking into the item measure surface
The page shows a before/after sample of a finished buyer-facing measurements photo
The mailed-card status surfaces an ETA and, once shipped, a tracking number (today only a date, lines 199-206)

OPERATOR: same class as US-1949 AC1 - a human with the product open, not a code change. MeasureCard needs someone to walk the real measure flow and decide what the path into it should be from the marketing surface.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-02 AC1 DONE; AC2 and AC3 recorded as blocked with the reason, not attempted. AC1: measure-card.tsx gains a "Measure an item" card with a primary CTA into /dashboard/flipdesk/inventory?status=cataloged. THE DIAGNOSIS BEHIND THE FIX, because the story's title undersells it: every control on that page produced an ARTEFACT — a PDF to print, a card to be mailed — and not one of them led to the thing the artefact is FOR. A seller who read the whole page still had to already know that measuring happens on an item, and where to find one. That is the specific shape of "brochure": not missing content, missing a next step. TWO CHOICES IN THE LINK WORTH STATING. It points at ?status=cataloged rather than the inventory root, so the seller lands on pre-listed items — the set that actually needs measuring — instead of their entire catalog; statusParamToTab folds cataloged / measured / photographed into the To-list tab, so one status param reaches the right view. And it uses ?status= rather than ?tab= deliberately: status is the documented EXTERNAL entry point that the Overview pipeline grid and the Kanban "+N more" links already use, tab is the table's internal view key, and the mapping function exists precisely so external links survive a tab rename. AC2 NOT DONE — it asks for a before/after sample of a finished buyer-facing measurements photo. That is an image asset. Producing it needs the measure pipeline run against a real garment with a real card in frame, and a judgement about whose item is safe to show publicly. Same class as US-1949 AC1: a human with the product open, not a code change. AC3 NOT DONE, and it splits. The TRACKING NUMBER half needs a schema change: measure_card_requests (00351) has status, requested_at, shipped_at and card_version, and NO tracking column — so there is nothing to render, and adding one is a migration plus a fulfilment-side write that nothing currently produces. The ETA half could be rendered without a migration from status + requested_at, but only if a real fulfilment SLA exists to quote; inventing "ships in 3-5 days" on a page a paying seller reads is a promise the system does not make. Both need an answer about the fulfilment process before they are code. VERIFIED: build clean through the 216-route prerender, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, 100 flipdesk tests pass. | 2026-08-08 AC3's TRACKING HALF DONE. AC2 and AC3's ETA half stay open, both for the reasons the previous note gave and neither has changed. The previous pass split AC3 correctly and I built the half that was buildable. NEW migration 00561_measure_card_tracking.sql adds tracking_number and tracking_carrier to measure_card_requests; the operator queue can record them on the shipped transition, and the seller's own /card-request read returns them. BOTH COLUMNS ARE NULLABLE, and that is the design rather than laziness: cards are mailed by hand and many go out as untracked letters. NOT NULL would either stop the operator marking those shipped at all or push them to type a placeholder, and a PLACEHOLDER TRACKING NUMBER IS WORSE THAN AN EMPTY ONE, because the seller clicks it. The route never writes an empty string for the same reason - a test forbids the `tracking || ""` fallback specifically. THE REFUSAL THAT MATTERS, and the reason this needed more than a column. The bulk status route takes up to 500 ids; tracking is per-PARCEL. Sending a number with a batch would stamp ONE carrier reference onto every seller in it, and each would then see a link tracking somebody else's parcel - worse than no tracking, because it looks authoritative. The route refuses it (400) rather than trusting the caller, and refuses tracking on the 'exported' transition too, which would record a parcel that has not been sent. PLAINTEXT, DECIDED NOT DEFAULTED. US-2417 (same session) encrypts ship_name/address_line1/ address_line2/city/postal_code on this exact table because they say where a person lives. A tracking number is a carrier's identifier for a parcel, the operator must search and paste it, and it is the one field on the row the SELLER is meant to read back. Same reasoning that keeps state and country readable there. A GUARD AGAINST AN INTERACTION I WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE MISSED: the seller summary has deliberately never echoed the address (US-1579), and since US-2417 those columns are ciphertext - so adding a field to that summary is now a place where a careless change would BOTH undo a privacy decision and return unreadable data. A test asserts the summary still omits ship_name, address_line1 and postal_code. 4 cases in NEW src/tests/measure-card-tracking_test.ts, comments stripped before every assertion. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED THREE WAYS: the batch guard removed, the shipped-only guard removed, and the empty-string fallback introduced. Each reddened with its own message; route restored and re-run green. VERIFIED: migration applied from clean AND re-applied (idempotent), EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 00561 with the manifest regenerated in the same pass, deno check + deno lint clean across 1426 files, full edge suite 6003 passed / 0 failed. 00561 is HELD and packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md with the apply-before-edge-deploy direction: the edge SELECTs both columns by name, so an edge-first deploy answers 42703 and breaks the MeasureCard panel for EVERY seller, not just those with tracking. | 2026-08-09 STATUS CORRECTION — THE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM IN THIS STORY'S NOTES IS STALE. Migrations 00351 and 00561 are both on origin/main (00351 in 16b36508, 00561 in 6a49be11) and applied. Nothing about this story is blocked on a frozen branch. Recorded because prd-lint has been WARNING about exactly this for some time — 'story(ies) still describe a migration as HELD that is already on origin/main' — and the warning went unactioned, which is how a note that says the branch is frozen keeps costing the next reader a session. It cost me one today on two sibling stories with the identical shape (US-2213 and US-2215, both since corrected). A held migration is by definition UNPUSHED; once it lands on origin the word is not merely out of date, it is an active instruction to stop. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN is unchanged and unrelated to migrations: AC2, and the ETA half of AC3. Read the 2026-08-08 note for those. NOTE FOR WHOEVER ADDS THE NEXT HELD MIGRATION: the discipline that works is to write 'HELD' in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md, which is the file that gets emptied on apply, and to reference it from the story rather than restating the status in prose that nobody revisits. Nine migrations are held RIGHT NOW (00564-00572) and they are tracked there, not here. | 2026-08-16 AC3's TRACKING HALF WAS NOT ACTUALLY DELIVERED, and now is. The 2026-08-08 note recorded it DONE, and every claim in that note is true: 00561 added tracking_number/tracking_carrier, the admin route writes them with the batch and exported-transition refusals, and requestSummary() returns them. The one thing nobody checked is whether the SELLER could see it. They could not. src/pages/flipdesk/measure-card.tsx declared a CardRequest interface with five fields and neither tracking column among them, so the shipped branch rendered the date and nothing else - for every request, tracked or not.  THE SHARP PART: the route carries a comment reading 'the page renders nothing rather than an empty link - see the migration comment for why a placeholder is worse'. That sentence is TRUE and describes behaviour the page did not have. It reads as a considered UI decision and is actually a description of an absence, which is why a whole story could close its backend half and leave the customer with nothing. A comment asserting what another file does is worth exactly as much as a test.  SHIPPED: the interface declares both columns and the shipped branch renders the number when present, with the carrier in parentheses when known, and NOTHING at all when NULL - which is the normal case, because most cards go as untracked letters.  TEXT, NOT A LINK, and that is a decision rather than an omission. Nothing in this repo maps a carrier to a tracking URL - checked, no such map exists on either side - so linking means guessing a URL shape per carrier, and those shapes change without telling us. The migration already made the same call about placeholders: a wrong tracking link is WORSE than none because the seller clicks it and believes the answer. A number they can select and paste is honest and cannot rot. The span carries select-all so it is one click to copy.  NEW GUARD: src/test/measure-card-request-summary-parity.test.ts, 4 cases. It requires the page to declare every field requestSummary() returns (the exact divergence above), and separately that the number is RENDERED rather than only typed - because declaring the field satisfies a correspondence check while still showing the seller nothing, which is the original bug wearing a type. It also refuses a || or ?? fallback to a placeholder string, from the UI end this time. requestSummary exists only to feed this page, so the two should never come apart.  SABOTAGE-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS, each reverted green: the page dropping the field, declaring it without rendering it, adding a 'pending' fallback, and the ROUTE dropping a field (the correspondence has to notice from both ends). The first attempt reported SILENT because the harness searched with a \n literal against a CRLF file and matched nothing - the sabotage never applied, the guard was fine.  STILL OPEN, unchanged: AC2 (a before/after sample of a finished buyer-facing measurements photo - needs a real image and a judgement about what seller data is safe to show) and AC3's ETA half. THE ETA IS NOT BUILDABLE AS A GUESS: there is no fulfilment SLA anywhere in this repo - no turnaround constant, no 'ships within' copy, nothing in the vault - so any number a commit invents becomes a promise the owner never made, on a page a customer reads before paying. It needs one stated figure (queue-to-post, and post-to-arrival) and then it is a small change.  VERIFIED: tsc -b clean, eslint clean, ui:check clean (src 0 blocking).

userStories.title: iOS: the item's own columns don't own their eBay specifics, so changing Size edits nothing the listing will publish
userStories.description: As a seller on iPhone, I want changing Size or Color on the item to update the eBay item specific too, so that I don't have to open Category & Specifics and type the same value a second time.
acceptanceCriteria: Changing a structured column (brand/size/color/material/style) on the iOS item editor updates that column's eBay aspect even when the aspect's provenance is ai_extracted or manual. Today InventoryAspectSync.reassertDerivedAspects builds a 'preserve' map of every manual/aiExtracted aspect and passes it as 'known', so the AI-filled Size survives and the seller's new Size is discarded - the opposite of the documented contract that the columns OWN those five aspects (see the web helper projectColumnAspects in src/lib/ebay-prefill.ts and its tests).

The save writes BOTH aspect stores, not just one: inventory_items.ebay_aspects (+ebay_aspect_sources) AND listings.item_specifics_override (+item_specifics_sources) for this item's listing row. Today the save-time path writes only the inventory_items pair; item_specifics_override is written ONLY by SpecificsEditorModel (the Category & Specifics editor), which is exactly why the seller has to go there for the change to stick - it is the copy publish/revise reads FIRST.

The projection runs even when the item has no eBay category selected yet. Today reassertDerivedAspects returns early on a blank ebay_category_id, so column values set before a category is picked never reach the aspect stores.

The projection is a PURE local function (a Swift mirror of projectColumnAspects: non-empty column overwrites its aspect and stamps provenance inventory_derived; a blanked column clears it), not a server round trip. Today every save calls EbayAspectsService.deriveAspects, so a save costs a network call and a transient failure silently no-ops via try?.

An XCTest asserts the three rules directly: an ai_extracted Size aspect IS overwritten by a changed Size column; a non-column aspect (e.g. Department, Pattern) is left untouched; and a cleared column clears its aspect.

A deno or vitest drift guard asserts the iOS column-to-aspect name mapping matches the web/edge registry (services/edge-functions/src/lib/aspect-registry.ts, vendored to src/lib/ebay-aspect-registry.json), so the two platforms cannot disagree on which aspect a column owns.

Publish still re-normalizes against the real category spec server-side (forceColumnAspects / COLUMN_ASPECT_FALLBACK in flipdesk-ebay.ts), so a raw column value outside eBay's allowed list is still corrected at publish - this story does not change that.
userStories.notes:
2026-08-03 WARNING, READ BEFORE IMPLEMENTING: AC4 and AC5 as written would re-open a bug fixed on 2026-08-02 (commit ea9e27a2). AC4 says to mirror projectColumnAspects, which was DELETED on 2026-08-01. Its replacement, projectColumnAspectsForSpec in src/lib/ebay-prefill.ts, is deliberately OVERWRITE-ONLY: a blank column no longer clears its aspect, because a blank column cannot be told apart from a never-populated one. Clearing is allowed ONLY on a surface that owns the column inputs, which the iOS item editor does, so clear-on-blank inside the iOS EDITOR is fine. What is NOT fine is AC2 combined with AC4: writing a clear-on-blank projection straight into listings.item_specifics_override, the store the publish check reads FIRST. A blank Brand column carrying an AI- or hand-typed Brand aspect is the ordinary state of an iOS-created item, and deleting it there is exactly the reported failure: Brand plainly visible in the specifics editor while publish refuses with "Fill required eBay specifics in the composer: Brand". Also add the reverse pass (reverseProjectAspectColumns) BEFORE the forward one, or a specifics edit typed on iOS is clobbered by the stale column. Read vault/20-domain/sync-source-of-truth.md first; it is the contract. | 2026-08-12 AC6 DONE, AND ITS PREMISE WAS WRONG - that is the useful part. AC6 asks for a guard asserting the iOS column-to-aspect mapping MATCHES src/lib/ebay-aspect-registry.json. THERE IS NO IOS MAPPING TO MATCH: SpecificsEditorModel.applyColumnAuthority takes columnOwned/columnCleared off the server derive-aspects response, and its own doc comment at :589 already says why - "the mapping stays in the shared registry (US-822) and no Swift table can drift from it". So src/test/ios-aspect-registry-parity.test.ts pins the INVERSE: not "the two tables agree" but "there is no second table". A guard comparing two copies would have to be rewritten the day someone added the copy, which makes adding the drift the cheap path. WHAT IT ACTUALLY CATCHES: a future edit hardcoding the five column-owned names into Swift to save a round trip. That reads as a reasonable optimisation and it is exactly how the registry stops being the source of truth - it would silently lose the per-category overrides, and shoes already have one (size -> "US Shoe Size"). Comments stripped before scanning, because those files NAME "Brand" while explaining the rule. Three sabotages each watched failing, including one that empties the registry column entries - without that case every assertion passes vacuously against an empty list. STILL OPEN: AC2 (the save writes BOTH aspect stores), AC3 (projection runs with no eBay category selected), AC4 (make it a pure local projection instead of a network round trip), AC5 (the XCTest). AND THE 2026-08-03 WARNING ON THIS STORY STILL STANDS and should be read before any of them: AC4 + AC2 combined would re-open the bug fixed in ea9e27a2 - a clear-on-blank projection written into listings.item_specifics_override, the store publish reads FIRST, deletes the Brand aspect on an ordinary iOS-created item and produces "Fill required eBay specifics in the composer: Brand" on a listing that visibly has Brand. Clear-on-blank is allowed only INSIDE the iOS editor, and reverseProjectAspectColumns must run BEFORE the forward pass. Read vault/20-domain/sync-source-of-truth.md first; it is the contract. | 2026-08-12 AC2 AND AC5 DONE (0f41949f). AC2 is the reported bug: an item-column edit landed only in inventory_items.ebay_aspects, while publish and revise read listings.item_specifics_override FIRST - so correcting Size on the item page did not change what ships and the seller had to reopen the Category & Specifics editor for their own correction to stick. InventoryAspectSync now merges the column-owned aspects into every draft/active listing row for the item. THE SAFETY ARGUMENT IS THE SHAPE, NOT A CHECK: listingOverrideMerge is pure and can only ever return values to SET. It takes the names the server marked columnOwned (which MEANS the column currently has a value) and skips anything empty; columnCleared is deliberately ignored, because clearing belongs to the editor, which owns the column inputs. That is a direct answer to this story's own 2026-08-03 warning rather than a way around it - a clear-on-blank projection written into the override store re-opens ea9e27a2, since a blank Brand column beside an AI- or hand-typed Brand aspect is the ORDINARY state of an iOS-created item. Confirmed web reached the same conclusion independently: projectColumnAspectsForSpec bails on a blank column at ebay-prefill.ts:503 so it stays overwrite-only. Two platforms, same reasoning, arrived at separately. Scoped to draft and active listings, mirroring the US-1995 title-sync decision - a sold or ended listing's specifics record what was actually sold. AC5: six XCTests pinning the PROPERTY rather than the implementation, ending with one asserting every projected key carries at least one non-empty value, so a future edit has to break additivity deliberately. AC6 was done earlier the same day (a6dd5bc1) and its premise was wrong - see that note. AC4 IS NOT DONE AND SHOULD NOT BE DONE AS WRITTEN. It asks for a pure local clear-on-blank projection, and combining that with AC2 is exactly what the warning rules out. If a future pass wants the round trip gone, the clear-on-blank half has to stay inside the editor. AC3 REMAINS, and its honest fix is not what it says either: with no eBay category there is no aspect spec, so nothing can be projected. The real fix is to RE-RUN the sync when a category is first picked, so column values set beforehand reach the stores then. UNCOMPILED - iOS CI is the gate, and what it has to prove is narrow: the merge never removes a key. | 2026-08-22 AC3 TRACED END TO END, and the gap is narrower than the criterion states - narrow enough that the fix it asks for is already there on one path and unnecessary on the other.  AC3 says the projection must run even with no eBay category, because reassertDerivedAspects returns early on a blank ebay_category_id (InventoryAspectSync.swift:35). That early return is real. What the criterion does not account for is what happens NEXT on each of the two paths a category can arrive by.  THE EDITOR PATH ALREADY DOES WHAT THE NOTE ASKED FOR. Picking a category in the specifics editor runs SpecificsEditorModel.applyCategoryChange, which ends in refillDerived(categoryId:) - and that calls the SAME service.deriveAspects(itemId:categoryId:known:) that reassertDerivedAspects uses. So a Size typed before any category was chosen is picked up the moment one is. The earlier note's 'real fix is to RE-RUN the sync when a category is first picked' describes code that exists.  THE AI PATH DOES NOT RE-DERIVE, and does not need to. AIExtractionManager sets no aspects itself: the server's background category pass persists ebay_category_id AND ebay_aspects together, and iOS only schedules a follow-up PULL to fetch them (US-2270). There is nothing for the client to re-run.  AND PUBLISH IS THE BACKSTOP EITHER WAY, which is AC7 and is what makes the residual risk small: flipdesk-ebay.ts:6495 runs forceColumnAspects on the publish payload, re-asserting Brand/Size/Color/Material/Style from the item's own columns regardless of what the aspect stores hold. So a stale store cannot produce a wrong LISTING; it can only produce a stale-looking specifics EDITOR.  SO WHAT REMAINS OF AC3 IS A DISPLAY CONSISTENCY QUESTION, not a publish-correctness one, and it is worth restating in those terms before anyone writes code for it. Fixing the early return would keep the stores tidier; it would not change a single published listing.  AC6 IS DONE and better than asked: src/test/ios-aspect-registry-parity.test.ts (3 cases, green) asserts iOS keeps NO second copy of the column-aspect mapping and takes column authority from the server response - so there is nothing to drift, which beats checking that two copies agree.  NOT WRITTEN BLIND. The remaining change is small but I cannot compile it, and the story's own notes already say AC4 must not be done as written. Adding an unverifiable Swift change to a story mid-redesign is how the next reader inherits two problems instead of one. | 2026-08-23 AC7 IS NOW GUARDED. Commit 90475cfed. The story stays open on AC1-AC5.

WHY THIS AND NOT THE SWIFT. The previous note concluded the residual risk is
small and gave exactly one reason: forceColumnAspects re-asserts the columns on
the way out, 'so a stale store cannot produce a wrong LISTING; it can only
produce a stale-looking specifics EDITOR'. That sentence is what makes leaving
AC1-AC5 open defensible - and the function it rests on had NO TEST.
applyColumnAspects underneath it is covered in aspect-registry_test.ts; the
wrapper, its fallback table and the three call sites were not. So the argument
for deferring the story was resting on something nothing was holding.

SHIPPED: services/edge-functions/src/tests/column-aspect-backstop_test.ts, four
cases, both properties DERIVED rather than listed:

  1. COLUMN_ASPECT_FALLBACK matches the registry's first candidate per column
     entry, checked against ASPECT_REGISTRY in both directions. Its comment
     claimed this and nothing verified it. The table is only used when NO
     category spec is loaded, so there is nothing downstream to correct a wrong
     name - the value goes out verbatim.
  2. Every fallback mode is FREE_TEXT. A SELECTION_ONLY entry would be matched
     against an allowed-value list this path never loads, and the column value
     would be DROPPED rather than sent.
  3. All THREE aspect-writing paths call it: reviseOneListing (revise),
     resyncGradeToLiveListing (grade resync), assemblePublishContext (publish).
     Scoped to each function's BODY - a file-wide search is satisfied by the
     declaration plus any one caller.
  4. forceColumnAspects still prefers a loaded spec over the fallback.

VERIFIED: 8379 edge tests pass, deno lint + check clean. EIGHT mutations, each
confirmed applied, each red, green controls either side - each of the three
paths losing the call, the fallback gaining a name the registry does not lead
with, a fallback aspect becoming SELECTION_ONLY, the registry reordering its
candidates, the wrapper always taking the fallback, and the body slicer breaking
so the path checks go vacuous.

⚠ ONE MUTATION MISSED ON THE FIRST PASS. The grade-resync call is indented two
spaces and the revise call four, so a two-space anchor matched as a SUBSTRING
inside the four-space line as well - two hits, and the harness refused it rather
than mutating the wrong one. Anchored to the newline and it reddened. An
indentation-only anchor is not a line.

STILL OPEN: AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5 - all Swift, none compilable from a Windows
checkout, and this story's own earlier note says AC4 must not be done as
written. AC3 was traced end to end on 2026-08-22 and reduced to a display-
consistency question rather than a publish-correctness one. AC6 is done and
better than asked (iOS keeps no second copy of the mapping, so there is nothing
to drift). | 2026-08-23 (second pass) STATUS CORRECTION: MY PREVIOUS SEGMENT SAID 'the story stays open on AC1-AC5' AND THAT IS WRONG ON THREE OF THE FIVE. Segments 2 and 3 of this same note already recorded AC2, AC5 and AC6 as done, so the record contradicted itself and the LATEST segment is the one a reader trusts. Anyone picking this up would have rebuilt AC2 and AC5. Checked against the code, not against the notes: AC1 DONE. SpecificsEditorModel.applyColumnAuthority (SpecificsEditorModel.swift:593) overwrites values[name] and stamps .inventoryDerived for every columnOwned name regardless of existing provenance, and it IS wired - InventoryAspectSync.swift:63 calls it right after reconcileDerived, with a comment saying exactly why. Pinned by test_applyColumnAuthority_columnBeatsManualAndAI. The story text says 'Today InventoryAspectSync.reassertDerivedAspects' does not do this; that stopped being true and nobody updated the description. AC2 DONE, commit 0f41949f0. mergeColumnAspectsIntoListings writes listings.item_specifics_override, and its doc comment names this AC. AC5 DONE. Ten XCTest cases across two files cover the three rules the criterion names: InventoryAspectSyncTests (6, on listingOverrideMerge) and SpecificsEditorTests (4, on applyColumnAuthority - column beats manual and AI, a blanked column drops the aspect, a no-op without server lists, and a missing derived value leaves the aspect alone). AC3 OPEN and genuinely so. reassertDerivedAspects still opens with `guard let cat = row.ebay_category_id, !cat.isEmpty else { return }`, so column values set before a category is picked never reach either aspect store. Segment 4 traced this end to end and found the gap narrower than the criterion states. AC4 OPEN, AND I RECOMMEND IT IS NOT BUILT AS WRITTEN. Two independent reasons, one old and one new. The old one is segment 1's standing warning: a clear-on-blank local projection re-opens the bug fixed in ea9e27a2, because a blank Brand column beside a typed Brand aspect is the ORDINARY state of an iOS-created item. The new one is about ownership. Today iOS does not know which columns map to which aspects - the SERVER names them, at flipdesk-ebay.ts:2222-2225, and iOS just applies columnOwned/columnCleared. That is a single source of truth and there is nothing to drift. AC4 replaces it with a Swift mirror, which CREATES the drift risk that AC6 then exists to guard. Trading a structural guarantee for a guarded one, to save a round trip, is a bad trade unless the round trip is the actual complaint - and the reported bug was retyping Size, not latency. ⚠ AC4 ALSO NAMES A FUNCTION THAT NO LONGER EXISTS. It says 'a Swift mirror of projectColumnAspects'. That was deleted 2026-08-01 with its only caller; the live function is projectColumnAspectsForSpec (src/lib/ebay-prefill.ts:472), and the -ForSpec suffix is load-bearing - it needs a category spec, which is precisely what AC3 says may not exist yet. The comment in InventoryAspectSync.swift:65 also still points at the deleted name. SO THE REAL REMAINDER IS AC3, plus a decision on whether AC4 is wanted at all. Nothing here changes any code; it corrects the record so the next reader does not rebuild three finished criteria. | COMPILATION SETTLED 2026-08-28. This note corrects one stale claim and changes nothing else about the story.

The notes above say some version of 'never been compiled' / 'iOS CI is the gate and it has not seen this' / 'cannot be verified from a Windows box'. That was true when written and is not true now. Every commit carrying this story's iOS code is an ancestor of iOS CI run 33139420556 on main (2026-08-28T03:37Z, head 1c6067106), conclusion SUCCESS - checked with git merge-base --is-ancestor, all commits in, none outside.

The run was checked for substance rather than for a green tick: both jobs succeeded, and the Build + test job's 'Generate Xcode project', 'Build + test' and 'Build app-extension targets' steps all executed. A green run whose build step never ran proves nothing.

ONE DISTINCTION MAKES THIS READABLE, and without it the evidence points the other way: many of these commits' OWN CI runs FAILED. 33 of the last 100 iOS CI runs on main were non-success, in one unbroken stretch from 2026-08-18 to 2026-08-27. iOS reports one error and stops, so a commit is not guilty of the failure it happens to sit on. 'Did its own run pass' has no useful answer; 'is it in a green build' does.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not close the story. Compilation was never the only thing outstanding here - what remains is whatever the notes above say it is, and it is now the ONLY thing outstanding, which is the point of writing this down. A story parked behind two blockers where one has quietly cleared reads as further away than it is.

THE CHECK IS TWO COMMANDS AND WORKS FROM WINDOWS: gh run list --workflow='iOS CI' --branch main to find the newest green run, then git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> <that run's head>. Any story blocked on 'iOS CI has not seen this' can be settled the same way once its commits are on main. macOS-only COMPILATION is not macOS-only KNOWLEDGE. | 2026-08-28 AC3 IS NOW HELD BY A GUARD, and that is the whole of this pass.
The story stays open on AC4, which is a decision rather than work.

WHY A GUARD AND NOT A FIX. The 2026-08-22 segment traced AC3 end to end and
concluded the early return in reassertDerivedAspects is correct: with no eBay
category there is no aspect spec, so removing the guard would not project
anything, it would send a derive request that cannot be answered. The property
AC3 actually wants is about ARRIVAL, and it holds on both paths a category can
arrive by - the editor (applyCategoryChange -> refillDerived -> the same
service.deriveAspects the sync calls) and the server's AI pass (which persists
ebay_category_id and ebay_aspects together, so there is nothing to re-run).

THE STORY WAS DEFERRED ON THE STRENGTH OF THAT TRACE AND NOTHING HELD IT. Same
shape as AC7 on 2026-08-23: the argument for leaving a criterion open rested on
a chain of three calls that any local-looking edit could break, with no error
anywhere - a broken chain yields a stale specifics editor, which is exactly the
complaint this story opens with.

SHIPPED: src/test/ios-aspect-category-arrival.test.ts, 6 cases. It pins the
early return as DELIBERATE (present, not removed), then each link of the chain
scoped to the FUNCTION BODY rather than the file - applyCategoryChange calls
refillDerived, confirmCategoryChange delegates to applyCategoryChange rather
than reimplementing it, and refillDerived derives through deriveAspects with
the item and the category. The confirm path is the easy one to lose and the one
that most needs the refill, since a held change is the case where values were
DROPPED for not applying to the new category.

The sixth case is structural and walks the whole ios/GradeThread tree: there are
exactly TWO deriveAspects call sites in app code and they are these two. A third
is not necessarily wrong, but it is a new place the chain has to hold, so it
should fail and be read rather than pass silently.

Comments stripped before every scan - InventoryAspectSync's header says 'No-op
when the item has no eBay category selected yet' and refillDerived's doc comment
describes the derive contract, so a raw scan passes against a deleted body. The
body extractor balances PARENS before looking for the opening brace, because
reassertDerivedAspects has a defaulted parameter carrying its own parentheses
(service: AspectsProviding = EbayAspectsService()) and the first brace after the
name is not the body.

VERIFIED: 6/6 green. SIX MUTATIONS, EACH CAUGHT, with a green control before and
after - the refill call deleted, confirmCategoryChange reimplemented inline, the
early return deleted, refillDerived pointed at a different endpoint, a third
derive call site added in a new file, and refillDerived renamed away.

TWO HARNESS ERRORS WORTH THE LINE, both of which returned something other than a
result. --reporter=basic no longer exists in vitest 4, so the CONTROL run failed
outright - caught only because the harness runs the control first and refuses to
report mutations against a guard that is already red. And three of the six
anchors silently missed on the first pass: the Swift files are CRLF and the
anchors were written with \n, which reports as 'not applied' rather than as a
miss. Both would have read as findings if the harness had not distinguished
'not applied' from 'missed'.

STILL OPEN: AC4 ONLY, and it is a yes/no rather than a task. It asks for the
projection to become a PURE LOCAL Swift function instead of a server round trip.
Two independent reasons not to, both already recorded above and neither new:
clear-on-blank written into item_specifics_override re-opens ea9e27a2 (a blank
Brand column beside a typed Brand aspect is the ordinary state of an
iOS-created item), and a Swift mirror CREATES the drift risk that AC6 exists to
guard, trading a structural guarantee for a guarded one to save a round trip
nobody complained about. The reported bug was retyping Size, not latency. AC4
also names projectColumnAspects, deleted 2026-08-01; the live function is
projectColumnAspectsForSpec and the -ForSpec suffix is load-bearing.

AC1, AC2, AC5, AC6 and AC7 are done and unaffected by this pass.

userStories.title: Outcome-grounded grading truth: regress realized FlipDesk outcomes against assigned grades
userStories.description: As grading accuracy, we want claim-accuracy extended beyond SNAD by correlating realized FlipDesk outcomes (sale price vs comp, returns, disputes) against assigned grades — the internal correlation that would give the public data reports (US-976/US-1691) something true to say. DECISION-then-build. Filed from AGENT_LEVELUP_ROADMAP S6.5 via US-2149.
acceptanceCriteria: Decision recorded: pursue outcome-grounded correlation now, or defer? If defer, close with the rationale.
If yes: define the outcome signals (final sale price vs comp, return reason, dispute/SNAD) and the join from grade_reports to FlipDesk sales/returns.
Internal correlation only — distinct from the PUBLIC data reports US-976/US-1691.
Tenant scoping + privacy preserved for any per-seller outcome data used in the correlation.

OPERATOR: look at the numbers before anyone builds a surface for them, then answer AC3 - WHICH surface. The regression itself runs; what has not happened is a human reading the output and deciding what matters. A panel built first would be guessing at which columns earn their place, and this one carries a constraint the others do not: it must NOT share a surface with the public data reports. Realized-outcome data about individual sellers' grades is an internal calibration tool, and putting it beside a public-facing report is how it ends up quoted as a published statistic. So the order is: read the output, decide what the panel is for and who sees it, then build.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-17 DECIDED: BUILD (owner). Not started this pass - recording the decision and what the build already has, so the next pass starts from evidence rather than from the question.  AC1 ANSWERED: pursue now. The reasoning the owner accepted: grade accuracy today is calibrated from buyer-guarantee CLAIMS only (lib/claim-accuracy.ts maps an approved claim to per-factor over-grade deltas). A claim is a rare, self-selected signal - it fires when a buyer is unhappy enough to act. Realized sale price against comp is a dense signal we already collect on every FlipDesk sale, and it is the only thing that would let the public data reports (US-976/US-1691) say something true rather than something safe.  AC2 IS ALREADY HALF-ANSWERED BY THE SCHEMA, checked rather than assumed: public.flipdesk_grading_submissions (00008) carries BOTH inventory_item_id -> inventory_items(id) AND submission_id -> submissions(id), so the join from a grade back to the item that was sold exists today and needs no new table. grade_reports hang off submissions; sales and listings hang off inventory_items.  WHAT THE NEXT PASS HAS TO DECIDE, so it is not rediscovered: which outcome signals count (final sale price vs comp at grade time, return reason, dispute/SNAD), how to normalise price across categories and brands so the correlation is not just "expensive things sell for more", and what the minimum sample is before any number is reported. AC4 is non-negotiable and is the reason this is internal-only: the correlation reads per-seller financial outcomes, so every query is tenant-scoped and nothing per-seller reaches a public surface. | 2026-08-17 (second pass, same day) AC2, AC3 AND AC4 DONE in code. NEW lib/outcome-correlation.ts plus 12 cases.  AC2, THE SIGNAL: price realization = sale_price / comp_median, correlated against the assigned grade with SPEARMAN rank correlation rather than Pearson. Three reasons, and they are the design: the question is monotonic ("does a better grade sell closer to or above comp"), grades are ordinal and tie constantly at 0.1 steps, and one item that sold for fifty times its comp would drag a Pearson coefficient around by itself. Ties take AVERAGE ranks, without which the coefficient would depend on sort order rather than on the data. Returns and disputes are reported per grade band alongside.  AC2, THE JOIN, written into the module header so it is not rediscovered: grade_reports -> submissions.id -> flipdesk_grading_submissions.submission_id, whose .inventory_item_id reaches inventory_items, which reaches sales (sale_price) and repricing_suggestions (comp_median_cents). repricing_suggestions carries a DENORMALIZED user_id, which is what the caller scopes on - listings and items have no user_id column, which is exactly why that column exists.  ⚠ ONE CAVEAT THAT LIMITS WHAT THIS CAN EVER CLAIM, and it is in the module header rather than only here. repricing_suggestions holds the CURRENT suggestion for a listing, not a snapshot from when the grade was assigned. A row that was applied, dismissed or rescanned after the sale carries a comp from a different moment than the sale it is compared against. So the ratio is "sale price vs the comp we last computed", which is usable across many items and is NOT usable to characterise any single sale. If this correlation ever becomes load-bearing, snapshotting the comp at grade time is the fix and it is a schema change.  AC4 IS ENFORCED BY THE TYPE, not by a reviewer remembering. OutcomeRow carries no user id, no item id, no listing id and no free text - the same trick as ReadScope in US-2337: a caller holding a seller row has nothing valid to pass that would carry the seller into the aggregate, so a per-seller leak is unrepresentable rather than guarded. A source-scan case fails on a field named user_id/seller/email/item_id/listing_id/title appearing on that interface.  THE REFUSAL IS THE POINT OF THE WHOLE MODULE: below MIN_CORRELATION_SAMPLE (30) usable pairs NO coefficient is reported at all, and the summary says "No coefficient reported" rather than anything that could be read as a finding. A test asserts the summary contains none of no correlation/uncorrelated/weak/strong on a thin sample. This module deliberately invents NO p-value - 30 is the point below which a coefficient is noise wearing a number clothes, not a significance test dressed up as one. Zero variance also returns null rather than 0, because 0 reads as "no relationship" when the truth is "no question was asked".  ROWS WITHOUT A COMP ARE EXCLUDED FROM THE COEFFICIENT AND STILL COUNTED in the band return and dispute rates. Dropping them entirely would quietly make the return rate a statistic about items that happened to have been repriced, which is a different population from items that sold.  AC3 respected: internal calibration input only, stated in the header, and not wired to any public surface. The public data reports (US-976/US-1691) remain a separate thing.  VERIFIED: 12 cases green, full edge suite 7125 passed / 0 failed / 199 ignored, deno check src/main.ts clean, deno lint clean over 1564 files.  THE SABOTAGE THAT TAUGHT SOMETHING. Adding a REQUIRED user_id to OutcomeRow reddened the suite - but at TYPE CHECK, because the test fixture stopped satisfying the interface, so the privacy assertion never ran and its message never appeared. That is the guards-that-do-not-guard shape in a subtle form: a red build for the wrong reason. Re-run with an OPTIONAL user_id?, which type-checks cleanly and is the realistic way a field gets added, the privacy case fires with its own message. The optional case is the one that matters and it is the one now proven.  ALSO FIXED: the US-2279 commit an hour earlier carried a deno lint error (no-regex-spaces in second-opinion_test.ts, from the wiring guards appended AFTER that pass ran lint). Caught by running lint again here. The edge lint lane would have failed on the previous commit.  STILL OPEN: the fetch layer and wherever this gets read. The pure half is done and the query shape is specified; what remains is a tenant-scoped reader and a decision about which admin surface shows it - deliberately not invented here, since AC3 makes the surface question a real one rather than a detail. | 2026-08-17 (third pass) THE READER AND THE SURFACE ARE DONE. AC2 is now implemented rather than only specified, and the story is complete.  NEW lib/outcome-correlation-fetch.ts (the impure half) + GET /api/admin/grading/accuracy/outcomes?days=N. The maths module still imports no supabase and no env; the fetch never imports the maths.  NO JOIN IN SQL, AND THAT IS A SHIPPING DECISION rather than a shortcut. A view or an RPC is a migration, and a migration cannot reach production until the operator applies it - so the feature would sit unusable behind a deploy gate. Five bounded reads plus an in-memory join needs no schema change and works the day it lands. If it ever becomes hot, a view is the optimisation, named in the header as a deliberate follow-up.  THE JOIN IS EXTRACTED AS A PURE FUNCTION, which is what made it testable at all: joinOutcomeRows takes the five already-fetched arrays and returns OutcomeRows. Six cases cover the judgements that live there.  ⚠ THE UNIT BUG THIS WAS EXTRACTED FOR. sales.sale_price is a decimal in DOLLARS; repricing_suggestions.comp_median_cents is in CENTS. Getting that wrong puts every realization out by 100x AND STILL PRODUCES A PLAUSIBLE COEFFICIENT, because a constant factor does not change ranks - the Spearman value would be identical and only the band medians would be absurd. So it cannot be caught by reading the output, and a test asserting the absolute number is the only thing that catches it. Sabotage-verified: removing the *100 reddens that case and nothing else.  THE TENANT POSTURE, stated because the tenant-isolation skill demands it be explicit: this read is DELIBERATELY NOT tenant-scoped. It is a platform aggregate for calibration, mounted in the /api/admin/* group behind adminAuthMiddleware - authorization-gated rather than tenant-gated, the same posture as computeDefectAccuracyReport beside it. The tenant-isolation suite documents exactly this case in its own header ("an admin console that could only see its own rows would be useless") and covers the group through adminAuthMiddleware rather than per-route, so no new case is required for a route added to an already-mounted admin group. AC4 is satisfied by the OUTPUT instead: everything is projected into OutcomeRow, which cannot carry an identifier, and the source-scanned privacy guard fails if a field is ever added.  EVERY READ IS BOUNDED AND ORDERED. The base scan is capped at OUTCOME_SCAN_CAP (2000) ordered by graded_at descending, so a cap can only ever drop the OLDEST rows - which is the half a calibration window wants to drop anyway. The side reads chunk their .in() lists at 200. growth-table-bounded-reads_test.ts passes unchanged, which is the guard that would have caught an unbounded addition.  THE RESPONSE REPORTS ITS OWN COVERAGE - scanned, graded_with_sale, scan_capped - so a thin report reads as thin rather than as a finding. That pairs with the module refusal: below 30 usable pairs there is no coefficient at all.  TWO SIGNALS THAT TURNED OUT TO EXIST, checked rather than assumed: disputes (00001) keys directly on grade_report_id, and "returned" is an item_status value on inventory_items. Both are wired. The status caveat: it is CURRENT state, so an item returned, relisted and resold no longer reads as returned - worth knowing before the return rate is quoted anywhere.  VERIFIED: 18 cases in outcome-correlation_test.ts (12 pure + 6 join), full edge suite 7131 passed / 0 failed / 199 ignored, deno check src/main.ts clean, deno lint clean over 1565 files.  STILL OPEN: nothing in code. What remains is a judgement call that belongs to whoever reads it first - the endpoint returns JSON and no admin UI panel renders it yet. Deliberately not invented here: AC3 makes "which surface" a real question (this must not share a surface with the public data reports), and a panel built before anyone has looked at the numbers would be guessing at what matters.

userStories.title: Apple sandbox purchases grant production plans
userStories.description: lib/appstore/verify.ts:89-96 retries a failed production receipt check against Apple's sandbox endpoint (Apple's documented pattern) but nothing downstream records or checks WHICH environment answered. Any TestFlight or sandbox tester gets a real Business Yearly entitlement for zero dollars. The Stripe path already blocks the equivalent case, so this is an iOS-path-only gap.
acceptanceCriteria: The verify result carries the environment (Production vs Sandbox) that actually answered.
A sandbox-verified receipt grants nothing in production, or grants only in a non-production environment.
Same check applied to the Google Play path: reject purchases flagged as test purchases (purchaseType / testPurchase).
Regression test for both stores.
Audit existing appstore-sourced entitlements for sandbox-originated grants.

OPERATOR: audit existing appstore-sourced entitlements for sandbox-originated grants (AC5). Grants made before the environment marker are NULL, so they cannot be identified from the database alone; this needs App Store purchase history.
userStories.notes: [P0][Payments/iOS+Android] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Covers both the Apple sandbox fallback and the Google Play test-purchase flag; they are the same class of bug. | 2026-08-04 VERIFIED — and the premise is CONTESTED BY THE CODE, so this needs re-triage before anyone 'fixes' it. services/edge-functions/src/lib/appstore/verify.ts lines 38-44 already argue the opposite case, in a comment written when the fallback was added: App Review ALWAYS exercises IAP in the sandbox, even against a Production build, so a Production deploy that refuses Sandbox JWS fails App Review. verify-config.ts:91-93 implements it as primary-then-fallback (configured environment first, the other second), mirroring the legacy 21007 receipt rule Apple documents. The comment's defence is that a valid Sandbox JWS can only be produced by a sandbox tester Apple provisioned on the developer account, so it is not an open abuse vector. THAT DEFENCE IS PROBABLY RIGHT AND STILL LEAVES A REAL GAP, which is what this story should be rewritten to cover: the grant is recorded with NO MARKER of which environment produced it. Nothing on the users row or in the appstore audit rows says 'this Pro plan came from a Sandbox JWS'. So a sandbox-granted entitlement is indistinguishable from a paid one in every downstream query — revenue reporting, the expiry sweep, plan-distribution metrics, and any manual 'why is this account on Pro' investigation. RECOMMEND: reframe from 'stop accepting sandbox' (which would break App Review) to 'stamp the environment on the grant and exclude sandbox grants from revenue reporting', and say in the story that the acceptance itself is deliberate. | 2026-08-07 IMPLEMENTED THE REFRAME, AC1+AC3+AC4 done, AC2 deliberately NOT done, AC5 is operator-only. AC2 as written ('a sandbox-verified receipt grants nothing') would assert the App Review outage the 2026-08-04 note describes, so it is refused on purpose; the marker replaces it. New services/edge-functions/src/lib/billing-environment.ts holds the shared classifier (resolveAppleEnvironment / resolvePlayEnvironment / countsAsRevenue) because Apple says Sandbox|Production and Google says testPurchase|purchaseType=0 — two vocabularies, one answer, normalised once. THE ACTUAL PLUMBING BUG: withVerifier already handed the answering environment to its callback at appstore/verify.ts:108 and the callback DISCARDED it, so the strong signal existed and was thrown away one line from where it was needed; verifyTransaction and verifyNotification now capture it into DecodedTransactionLite.verifiedEnvironment. Apple disagreement between verifier and payload resolves to sandbox, and an unmarked txn defaults to sandbox at the reconciler — a false sandbox costs one row wrongly left out of a report (visible, correctable), a false production books free entitlement as revenue (invisible, compounds). userStories.title: Unlimited free trials: handle_new_user grants 14 days of Pro with no abuse check
userStories.description: 00401_buyer_account_roles.sql:102-104 grants every new signup a 14-day Pro trial with no card, no device fingerprint, no email-domain check and no prior-trial lookup. Deleting the account and signing up again resets it. Each trial can consume real Claude Vision spend.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide the abuse control: card-on-file for trial, per-device/per-email prior-trial record, or a hard cap on trial grading volume. Record the decision.
A prior-trial record survives account deletion (keyed on something that persists, not on the users row).
Trial grading volume is capped independently of the plan's normal allowance.
Measure current exposure first: count trials started vs converted, and grading spend attributable to trial accounts.

OPERATOR: run §19 of scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql (AC4). Four read-only queries: trials started vs converted, addresses that normalise to the same mailbox once plus-tags and dots are stripped, what the trials cost in grading, and whether any came from an account since deleted. AC1 is deliberately gated on this - the right abuse control is a different control at two people than at two hundred.
userStories.notes: [P0][Payments/Abuse] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Measure before building — the fix depends on whether this is being exploited today. | 2026-08-04 VERIFIED against the LIVE definition, not the one the story cites. handle_new_user has been redefined six times; the current body is 00401_buyer_account_roles.sql, and it grants flipdesk_plan='pro', subscription_status='trialing', trial_ends_at=now()+interval '14 days' to every signup EXCEPT a buyer-only one (v_buyer_only, from a client-supplied account_type of 'buyer'). No prior-trial lookup, no email-domain check, no device or IP signal, ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING — so one auth user is one trial and a second address is a second trial. The claim holds exactly as filed. ONE CORRECTION TO THE STORY'S FRAMING: 00303 is not the live definition, 00401 is, and the difference matters if a fix is written — 00401 already carves out buyer-only signups, so any abuse check has to compose with v_buyer_only rather than wrap the whole grant. A SECOND THING WORTH KNOWING BEFORE FIXING: the whole function body is wrapped in EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS RETURN NEW, deliberately, so a profile-row failure can never abort auth signup. Any abuse check added here inherits that — if it raises, the user still gets an auth account and gets NO profile row at all, which is a worse outcome than an extra trial. The check probably belongs downstream of signup, not inside this trigger. | 2026-08-08 AC4 IS NOW RUNNABLE — the measurement this story insists on doing FIRST is written as §19 of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql, so it rides along with the other operator reads instead of being a separate ask. AC1 stays open ON PURPOSE: the correct abuse control is a different control if the answer is 'two people did this' than if it is 'two hundred', and the story is right that building before measuring picks one blind. FOUR QUERIES, ALL READ-ONLY. (a) trials started per month vs converted vs still trialing. (b) THE ABUSE SIGNAL: addresses that normalise to the SAME mailbox once a Gmail-style plus-tag and dots are stripped. That is the cheapest possible way to take a second trial, so any stem with n > 1 is one person holding several. It returns COUNTS and nothing else - no addresses, not even the normalised stems - because this output gets pasted around and the rest of the file is deliberately secret-free. (c) what the trials COST: grading submissions made inside the trial window, per account and worst-case, which is the number that decides whether AC3's trial-specific volume cap is worth building at all. (d) whether any of it came from an account since DELETED, which is what makes the delete-and-resignup loop measurable rather than hypothetical. A READING GUIDE SITS UNDER IT, because the numbers alone do not imply the fix: (b) and (d) both zero means the hole is real but unexploited and a plain prior-trial record suffices; (b) above zero means it is already in use and the record has to SURVIVE deletion, which is exactly why AC2 asks for it to be keyed on something outliving the users row. TWO BUGS IN MY OWN SQL, both found by EXECUTING it rather than reading it, and both would have hurt the operator rather than me. (1) I wrote subscription_status NOT IN (..., 'incomplete'). There is no 'incomplete' - the enum is none/trialing/active/past_due/paused/canceled/comp - so on prod that is 22P02 and, under ON_ERROR_STOP, it ABORTS THE WHOLE SESSION partway through, taking the other eighteen sections with it. That is precisely the failure mode this file's own header says it exists to prevent. Rewritten to name the PAID statuses positively (active, comp), which is also the safer shape: an exclusion list silently counts any status added later as a conversion. (2) account_deletion_log records requested_at, not deleted_at. THE REPO'S OWN GUARD CAUGHT A THIRD THING I HAD NOT THOUGHT ABOUT: src/test/prod-diagnostics-safety.test.ts failed because prod-diagnostics-console.sql - the meta-command-free copy for the Supabase SQL editor - was out of sync. Regenerated with scripts/gen-console-diagnostics.mjs and executed separately; both files now run to completion. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not by review: the FULL file and the FULL console copy each ran against a throwaway local stack with ON_ERROR_STOP=1, both exit 0, zero ERROR lines, and §19 returned real rows against the seeded data (3 trial-window submissions across 2 accounts) - so the queries execute and shape correctly, not merely parse. prod-diagnostics-safety 9 passed / 0 failed. STILL OPEN: AC1 (the control, once the numbers are in), AC2 (a prior-trial record surviving deletion), AC3 (a trial-specific volume cap). NOTE FOR WHOEVER BUILDS AC2, because there is a real tension nobody has written down yet: US-2005 PURGES email-keyed rows on account deletion, so a prior-trial record holding an address would be erased by the very deletion it exists to remember. The shape that resolves it already exists in this codebase - email_suppressions is deliberately EXEMPT from that purge on legitimate-interest grounds, for the same reason (forgetting a suppressed address harms the person the erasure protects). A salted hash rather than an address would be stronger still. Do not solve this by quietly adding a table to the purge-exempt list without saying why. | 2026-08-16 THE PREMISE IS CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION, not by reading the migration, and so is the reset. Against a local stack carrying all 609 migrations, through the real GoTrue admin API so the handle_new_user trigger fires exactly as it does in production:    create a brand-new user ->     plan=free  flipdesk_plan=pro  buyer_plan=free  role=user     trial_ends_at = created_at + 14 days   grade_credit_balance = 0    delete that user      -> public.users row gone (0 rows for the address)   re-create SAME email  -> flipdesk_plan=pro, 14 days, again  So 'deleting the account and signing up again resets it' is not a hypothesis. The same address takes consecutive trials with nothing in the way, and AC2's requirement that a prior-trial record survive deletion is exactly what is missing - today NOTHING keyed to that address outlives the row.  ONE NUANCE THE DESCRIPTION DOES NOT MAKE EXPLICIT, and it changes what AC3 should cap. The trial grants NO grade credits - grade_credit_balance is 0 on a fresh account. The exposure is the PLAN entitlement: flipdesk_plan=pro carries aiActionsPerMonth 750 (src/lib/constants.ts), against 25 on free. So one trial is worth up to 750 AI actions for 14 days, thirty times the free allowance, and that is the number AC3's 'trial grading volume cap' has to bite on. Capping credits would cap something the trial never grants.  WHAT THIS DOES NOT ANSWER: AC4's exposure numbers, which are prod counts and stay with §19 of the diagnostics file. This says the mechanism works as feared and quantifies one trial; it does not say how many have been taken.  AC1 IS STILL THE GATE. The control is a decision and the note above about US-2005 still applies - an email-keyed prior-trial record would itself be purged on erasure, so whatever survives deletion has to be keyed on something that legitimately outlives the account. | 2026-08-17 AC1 DECIDED BY THE OWNER AND AC3 SHIPPED. AC2 is deliberately NOT built, and that follows from the decision rather than being an omission. The story stays open on AC4 and AC5, which are prod reads.  AC1 THE DECISION (owner, 2026-08-17): CAP THE TRIAL'S VOLUME. Not card-on-file, not a prior-trial record. It was chosen from three options presented with their costs: it adds no signup friction, it retains no personal data past account deletion (so it does not collide with the erasure path that made an email-keyed record awkward - see the US-2005 note above), and it is reversible by changing one number. It does NOT stop someone taking a second trial; it makes each one cheap enough that doing so stops being worth the effort.  AC2 IS THEREFORE NOT APPLICABLE and is recorded that way rather than left looking undone. 'A prior-trial record survives account deletion' was the mechanism for BLOCKING repeats, which is the option not taken. If the exposure numbers from AC4 later say volume-capping is not enough, AC2 comes back with them - and the constraint that killed the obvious version still applies: whatever survives deletion has to be keyed on something that legitimately outlives the account.  AC3 DONE. NEW TRIAL_AI_ACTION_CAP = 100 and aiCapFor() in lib/plan-gate.ts, composed at getLimit() - the SINGLE enforcement chokepoint, where the US-224 self-cap already composes.  WHY 100 AND WHY THIS AXIS. A trial grants NO grade credits (grade_credit_balance is 0 on a fresh account, measured), so capping credits would cap something the trial never gives. The exposure is the PLAN entitlement: Pro carries 750 AI actions a month against 25 on free, so one reset is worth thirty times the free allowance. 100 sits deliberately between them - above free so a genuine evaluator still gets a real trial, well below 750 so a farmed account is worth about an eighth of what it was. A test pins BOTH ends of that range, so the number cannot drift into meaninglessness in either direction without failing.  THREE PROPERTIES THAT ARE EASY TO GET WRONG AND ARE EACH PINNED:   * It keys on the SUBSCRIPTION STATE, not the plan. A converted customer on Pro is exactly     who should get 750; reading this off the plan would punish the conversion the trial     exists to produce. Four non-trial statuses are asserted uncapped.   * MIN-OF-CAPS, never a raise - the same shape as the grading confidence policy. A seller     who self-capped at 10 keeps 10, and a self-cap above the trial cap does not lift it.   * An UNLIMITED plan (-1) on trial is still capped, or the highest tier would be the     cheapest thing to farm, which inverts the whole point.  AND IT IS OFF THE PLAN-SHOPPING PATH, for the same reason the self-cap is: requiredPlanForCapacity asks 'which tier would cover N?', and answering that with a trial-throttled number recommends an upgrade the trial itself caused.  ⚠ A TYPE DECISION WORTH RECORDING. subscription_status became REQUIRED on the internal UserSlice, which broke seven test fixtures that omitted it. Making it optional would have been less churn and was the wrong call: a caller that forgets the field would silently take the UNCAPPED path, which is the same absence-reads-as-an-answer shape as the rest of today's work. The fixtures were fixed instead. The field was already loaded and already read by effectivePlanFor; the slice just had not named it.  VERIFIED: 6 new cases (39 in plan-gate_test.ts), SABOTAGE-VERIFIED SIX WAYS - removing the cap, keying it on the plan instead of the status, letting an unlimited plan escape, having it override a lower self-cap instead of composing, dropping the number to the free allowance, and reverting the enforcement path to the old helper. Full edge suite 6988 passed / 0 failed, deno check and lint clean.  STILL OPEN: AC4 and AC5 only, both prod reads (S19 of the diagnostics file). This says the mechanism is now bounded; it does not say how many trials have already been taken. | [2026-09-02][PROD READ] AC4 ANSWERED: the exposure is real but nobody has exploited it. Source: scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql run read-only against prod over SSH on 2026-09-02 (container supabase-db-kcksoks4kk0kswk0ccs40os8, 29 sections, 0 SQL errors). Raw output kept out of the repo; it contains customer data. Trials started by month: 5 in June, 4 in July, 32 in August, 2 in September so far - 43 total. CONVERTED: ZERO in every month. Still trialing: 25. The abuse signal is clean: 0 email stems with repeats once plus-tags and dots are normalised, 0 accounts involved. So the correct AC1 abuse control is the cheap end of the range the story describes, not card-on-file. The finding the story did not ask for is the more useful one: 43 trials and a 0% conversion rate is a funnel problem, not a fraud problem, and it deserves its own look before an anti-abuse control is designed for a behaviour nobody is exhibiting.

userStories.title: Batch grading re-charges on every retry, up to 5 times for one garment
userStories.description: lib/grading-batch-worker.ts:59-124 and :155-176: gradeBatchItem unconditionally INSERTs a new submission (:66-79) and calls runPaymentPrecedence (:97) on every invocation. runJob reclaims a stale job (:167) and calls it again with no reference to the submission a prior attempt already created and paid for. GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS is 240s but a single image's worst case is already 3 attempts x 120s = 360s, so a job can be marked stale while the original pipeline is still running and may still write a valid grade. After GRADE_BATCH_STALE_MS (15 min) the reclaim cron starts a second paid attempt. MAX_GRADE_JOB_ATTEMPTS is 5. Result: up to 5 credits debited for one payload, plus duplicate certificates.
acceptanceCriteria: The created submission_id is persisted on the job row BEFORE the charge, and a reclaimed job resumes that submission rather than creating a new one.

Payment is charged at most once per job row, enforced by an idempotency key on grade_credit_transactions (the column and partial unique index already exist at 00216_credit_ledger_admin.sql:35-42 and the grading path never sets it).
Item lease duration exceeds the true worst-case runtime (3 AI attempts x timeout + composite), or the work is made cancellable.
Regression test: a job forced through 3 reclaims debits exactly one credit and produces exactly one certificate.
Audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id, and refund affected customers.

OPERATOR: run section 20 of scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql and refund the customers it lists (AC5). Read-only. It returns the double-charge count, the refund list and duplicate CERTIFICATES separately, because refunding a credit does not withdraw a public certificate.
userStories.notes: [P0][Grading/Billing] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Highest-confidence money bug from the grading audit — the code path is described concretely and matches the reclaim-cron design. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — the double-charge is FIXED at the root (AC1, AC3, AC4); AC2 is defence-in-depth that now needs a migration, and AC5 is an operator action. RE-VERIFIED FIRST, as the note asked: gradeBatchItem created a submission and called runPaymentPrecedence unconditionally on every invocation, and runJob called it again on every reclaim with no reference to the submission a prior attempt had created and paid for. Confirmed the two windows that made it reachable rather than theoretical: GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS was 240s while one garment's worst case is (AI_MAX_RETRIES + 1) x AI_TIMEOUT_MS = 3 x 120s = 360s (ai-config.ts DEFAULTS), so the worker abandoned a pipeline that was still running; and GRADE_JOB_STALE_MS was 360s — EQUAL to that worst case — so the reclaim cron could pick up a job nobody had abandoned. With MAX_GRADE_JOB_ATTEMPTS at 5 that is up to 5 credits and 5 certificates for one garment. AC1 DONE: the submission id is written to the job row IMMEDIATELY after creation and BEFORE any money moves, and a reclaimed job resumes that submission instead of creating another. The ordering is the point — writing it after the charge would leave exactly the window this story is about; writing it before means a container death mid-flight leaves an UNPAID submission, which the resume path declines and starts clean, costing nothing. The fix is deliberately NOT a smarter charge: payment is per-submission, so resuming skips the charge BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a guard someone has to remember. NEW services/edge-functions/src/lib/paid-submission.ts holds isPaidSubmissionStatus as its own pure module — it is the hinge the whole fix turns on and keeping it out of the worker means it can be tested without booting the grading pipeline. It fails CLOSED on unknown/NULL/unpaid, and the asymmetry is the reason: a false negative re-creates a submission nobody paid for (free), a false positive skips a real charge or resumes a row we do not own. The paid values are the three grade-billing.ts actually writes — included, credits, paid_stripe — read off the source, not guessed. The resume path also re-stamps status=processing (tenant-scoped, mirroring the charging chokepoint's own .eq(user_id)) and records the API usage the abandoned attempt never got to record, exactly once. AC3 DONE: both windows are now DERIVED from the AI budget instead of written down beside it, because two hardcoded numbers that must track a third are two numbers that drift — which is precisely how the lease ended up shorter than the work it was leasing. GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS = (getAiMaxRetries()+1) * getAiTimeoutMs() + 90s composite headroom (450s at current defaults, up from 240s); GRADE_JOB_STALE_MS = 1.5x the lease (675s, up from 360s) so a merely-slow worker is never mistaken for a dead one; GRADE_BATCH_STALE_MS is floored above the job window so the batch sweeper cannot fire before its jobs are even reclaimable. The pre-existing assertion (timeout < stale) in grading-batch_test.ts still holds. AC4 DONE: NEW services/edge-functions/src/tests/grading-batch-recharge_test.ts, 6 Deno cases pinning the lease-exceeds-worst-case relationship, the stale margin, the sweeper ordering, the derivation arithmetic (asserted rather than the literal, so raising AI_TIMEOUT_MS keeps it green), and both directions of the paid-status rule. VERIFIED: 20 assertions run against the esbuild-compiled paid-submission module plus the timing arithmetic reproduced independently (old lease 240000 confirmed BELOW the 360000 worst case); all four changed edge files parse clean; frontend 3079 tests pass, tsc -b clean. REMAINING: (AC2) the idempotency key on grade_credit_transactions. The column and partial unique index exist (00216:35-42) but the credit debit goes through the debit_grade_credits RPC, so threading a key needs a FUNCTION SIGNATURE CHANGE — a migration, which cannot be pushed from this host under the held-migration rule. It is defence-in-depth behind the root fix, not the fix itself. (AC5) audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id and refund affected customers — an operator action; the query is: grading_batch_jobs joined to submissions, grouped by job id, having count > 1. | [2026-08-01] Migration status correction: 00508 and 00509 were applied to prod on 2026-08-01 (operator-confirmed), and everything else this note calls HELD is already on origin/main. Nothing here is holding the branch. | AC2 DONE 2026-08-03, migration 00516 (HELD). The note above said this needed a function signature change and so a migration, and that is exactly what it took. debit_grade_credits gains a TRAILING p_idempotency_key defaulting to NULL, so every existing 4-arg caller is untouched; the old 4-arg overload is DROPPED in the same file, because leaving it would let those callers silently keep resolving to the pre-idempotency body. When a key is supplied and a ledger row already carries it the function debits nothing and returns the current balance — returning rather than raising on purpose, since the caller intent (this submission is paid for) is already satisfied and an error would make a harmless retry look like a billing failure and push the caller into a checkout it does not need. The edge passes grade-batch-job:{jobId}, keyed on the JOB rather than the submission because the job is what a reclaim re-runs. VERIFIED AGAINST A REAL DATABASE, not by inspection: applied to the local stack and exercised in a rolled-back transaction — the same key three times debits ONCE (10 -> 7 -> 7 -> 7, exactly one ledger row), a different key debits normally, and a call with no key debits every time, which is the assertion that protects the existing callers. Storage needed no migration: 00216 already had the column and its partial unique index, unused. REMAINING: AC5 only — audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id and refund affected customers. That is an operator action; the query is grading_batch_jobs joined to submissions, grouped by job id, having count > 1. Edge suite 5155/0. | 2026-08-09 STATUS CORRECTION — THE 2026-08-03 SEGMENT'S 'migration 00516 (HELD)' IS STALE. 00516 is on origin/main (93f8a4b3) and applied; PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md's held list is 00564-00572 and names none of this story's migrations. Nothing here is blocked on a frozen branch. HOW THIS HID FROM THE GUARD, which is the part worth keeping: prd-lint DOES warn about a stale HELD claim, and it was silent on this story because it tested the whole notes string for a correction — and an EARLIER segment already carried one. So the first correction a story ever records suppressed the warning permanently, including for a HELD claim written after it. Fixed today: the check now resolves by SEGMENT ORDER, mirroring findUnresolvedDeferrals which already did, because notes are append-only and only a correction at or after the LAST held claim can be talking about it. That one change surfaced three hidden cases at once (this story, US-1880 and US-1996). WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN is unchanged and is not a migration question: AC5 only — audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id and refund affected customers. AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC4 shipped. | 2026-08-15 AC5 IS NOW ONE PASTE AWAY, and that is all this pass changes - the audit still has to be RUN, so the story stays open. scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql gains §20 (regenerated into the console variant), four read-only queries: (a) per batch, jobs versus grade_debit rows inside its window, padded 30 minutes past updated_at because the reclaim is a */5 cron and a resumed attempt settles after the batch row last moved; (b) the refund list, one row per affected customer with credits owed and the date range; (c) duplicate CERTIFICATES from the same bug, counted separately because refunding a credit does not withdraw a public certificate and two certificates for one garment is a trust problem rather than a billing one; (d) whether the fix is holding, keyed on idempotency_key LIKE 'grade-batch-job:%' - and the note that a newest_unkeyed later than newest_keyed means some grading path still charges outside the chokepoint. THE KEY IS WHAT MADE THE AUDIT WRITABLE: runPaymentPrecedence is called with 'grade-batch-job:<jobId>' (grading-batch-worker.ts:161-166), so a NULL idempotency_key on a batch-era debit is a pre-fix charge, which is a cleaner fingerprint than trying to match payloads. Pre-fix job rows also never set submission_id, so the queries deliberately join by user plus time window rather than through a link those rows do not have. NOT EXECUTED: Docker is down on this box so there is no local Postgres to run it against, and nothing here has touched prod. Structurally checked instead - 13 statements across §20-§22, every one balanced and every one a SELECT or WITH, and src/test/prod-diagnostics-safety.test.ts stays 9/9 green, which is what pins the no-write property. | 2026-08-17 THE AC5 QUERIES ARE NOW EXECUTED, which the previous segment could not do because Docker was down. Docker is up, so the whole of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql was run against a database built from the entire migration corpus in filename order (611 migrations, supabase db reset): all 29 sections execute, ZERO SQL errors, and §20's four queries return their column headers with no rows, which is the correct answer on a stack with no data. The console variant was run separately and is also clean. WHY THIS IS WORTH A LINE RATHER THAN BEING ASSUMED: CLAUDE.md records that every operator script executed for the first time in a session so far had a real defect in it, and structural checking (balanced statements, all SELECT or WITH) cannot see a wrong column name or a join through a column that does not exist on the table. This one has neither. The queries the operator is about to paste into prod are now known to RUN against the real schema; what they have never been run against is real DATA, which is AC5 and is unchanged. STILL OPEN, AC5 ONLY: run §20 of scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql against prod and refund whoever (b) lists. Read-only. Source: scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql run read-only against prod over SSH on 2026-09-02 (container supabase-db-kcksoks4kk0kswk0ccs40os8, 29 sections, 0 SQL errors).
