userStories.title: The golden-set eval gate never runs in CI and the live prompt versions have no DB row
userStories.description: Two compounding problems. (1) The grading eval appears in none of the 16 files in .github/workflows/, no package.json script, not scripts/verify.mjs, not services/edge-functions/deno.json. The only eval task there is the agent eval, and CI does not call that either. No build, deploy or PR is blocked by golden-set accuracy. runScheduledEval raises alerts and blocks nothing. (2) The code defaults are per_image_v5 and composite_v4 (ai-grading.ts:62-63) but the only grading seed migration (00050_grading_self_improvement.sql:121-127) inserts per_image_v2 and composite_v2, and no migration sets is_active. So the live prompts have no row and were never evaluated. (3) The repo contains no golden-set data at all: zero INSERTs into grading_eval_cases, no seed, no fixture. A fresh database has an empty golden set; runEval throws on empty but grading-monitor.ts:287-294 treats zero cases as a clean skip, so an empty set is silent. Net effect: editing prompt text in ai-grading.ts ships straight to customers without ever touching an eval.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm first, against prod, whether grading_eval_cases has any rows and which ai_prompt_versions rows are active. Record the answer in the story before building.
The golden-set eval runs in CI and fails the build on regression, or the reason it cannot is written down.
Every prompt version the code can use has a DB row with eval results and qualified_model, including the code defaults.
An empty golden set is treated as a hard failure, not a clean skip.
Prompt text in ai-grading.ts cannot ship without a corresponding evaluated version — enforced by a test, not by convention.
EVAL_MAX_MAE default of 1.0 (grading-eval.ts:26-29) is reconsidered: on a 1.0-10.0 scale a prompt can be a full grade point off on average and pass.

OPERATOR: two reads settle AC1 and size AC3. §15 of scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql returns golden-set size and which ai_prompt_versions rows are active with what qualified_model. An EMPTY set is the finding, not a null result: it means the accuracy gate has never run and cannot.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Lifecycle] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. The prompt-lifecycle doc reads as if a pipeline gate exists. It does not. Either add one or correct the doc. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — ALL FOUR factual claims independently RE-VERIFIED and TRUE; AC4 and AC5 shipped, the doc corrected; AC1/AC2/AC3/AC6 need prod access or a migration and are recorded with why. VERIFICATION (mechanical, not by reading the cited lines): (1) NO CI GATE — the golden-set eval appears in no file under .github/workflows/, no package.json script, not scripts/verify.mjs, not services/edge-functions/deno.json; the only match anywhere in those trees is a mention in scripts/ralph/progress.txt. Nothing blocks a build, PR or deploy on grading accuracy. (2) THE LIVE PROMPTS HAVE NO ROW — code defaults are per_image_v5 / composite_v4 (ai-grading.ts:62-63); the sole seed migration (00050:121-127) inserts per_image_v2 / composite_v2 with is_active false. Scanned EVERY migration touching ai_prompt_versions: neither v5 nor v4 appears. (3) ZERO GOLDEN-SET DATA — no INSERT into grading_eval_cases in any migration. A fresh database starts with an empty set. (4) EMPTY WAS SILENT — grading-monitor.ts runScheduledEval returned skipped_reason "no active eval cases" and moved on. AC4 DONE, and the reasoning matters: an empty set is the accuracy gate being SWITCHED OFF, not "nothing to check". With no cases the eval never runs, so eval_passed is null rather than false and NO other rule in evaluateAlerts fires — the state where no prompt has ever been evaluated, and none can be, produced complete silence from the only component whose job is to notice. evaluateAlerts now raises golden_set_empty at CRITICAL. Deliberately an ALERT rather than a thrown error: throwing would break the monitor cron on a fresh deploy, trading a silent gap for a noisy one and teaching operators to ignore the job. The message names the remedy AND the anti-remedy ("never synthetic") because an operator reading "the set is empty" under pressure will reach for fabricated cases, which makes every future eval meaningless while reading green. Kept DISTINCT from golden_set_shrank: a 40→0 set is both, and collapsing them loses the deliberate-abuse signal US-2037 exists for. AC5 DONE as a PIN rather than a fix, since seeding rows is a migration this host cannot push: a new case reads both prompt-version constants, scans every migration that touches ai_prompt_versions, and asserts the unseeded set equals KNOWN_UNSEEDED_PROMPT_VERSIONS exactly — both ways. So a FURTHER version bump fails until its author seeds a row or amends the declaration, and seeding one without amending also fails. That converts "nobody noticed for four versions" into "you cannot bump a version without deciding". DOC CORRECTED (the story's own closing note asked for exactly this): .claude/skills/grading-engine/references/prompt-lifecycle.md read as if a pipeline gate existed. It now opens with what the gate does NOT cover — no CI gate, code defaults with no DB row — while stating clearly that the part which IS real (activation and canary refusing an un-evaled version, via checkPromptServingEligibility, US-2300) applies only to versions that go through a DB row. VERIFIED: 4 alert assertions plus the seeding scan run against the real tree in Node (no deno on this host) — the scan reports exactly composite_v4 and per_image_v5 as unseeded, matching the declaration; grading-monitor.ts and the test parse clean; frontend 3079 tests pass, tsc -b clean. REMAINING: AC1 (confirm against prod what grading_eval_cases holds and which ai_prompt_versions are active) — operator only, and it should be done BEFORE the rest, as the AC says. AC3 (seed rows for the code defaults) — a migration, push-blocked here. AC2 (eval in CI) — depends on AC1/AC3: a CI eval against an empty golden set would be theatre, and the golden set must grow from REAL human-corrected grades, never fabricated ones, so it cannot be seeded from this host either. AC6 (EVAL_MAX_MAE default of 1.0 lets a prompt be a full grade point off on a 1-10 scale and still pass) — a product judgement about acceptable error, with a real cost either way, and it belongs to the owner rather than to a sandbox. | 2026-08-15 AC2 AND AC6 CLOSED; AC1/AC3 remain and are operator/migration work. AC6 DECIDED (owner): EVAL_MAX_MAE default drops from 1.0 to 0.5. On a 1.0-10.0 scale rounded to 0.1, a mean absolute error of a full point is an entire grade - the gap between Excellent and Good - so a candidate prompt could be that wrong on average and still be promoted, on the one number the product sells. 0.5 is one tier rather than two and is still generous. 0.3 was offered and refused FOR NOW with a reason: it is close to the disagreement between two human experts, and the golden set is not yet large enough to tell a real regression from an unrepresentative sample. THIS CHANGES NO GRADE - it decides only what may be ACTIVATED - and the env override means a deliberate exception is one variable while the silent default is the strict one. NOTE THE NUMBER IS PUBLISHED: evalThresholds() feeds accuracy-tracking.ts and src/pages/marketing/transparency.tsx renders it as a promise to buyers, so this tightens a public claim as well as the gate. The page reads it from the code, so nothing was hardcoded and nothing else needed editing - checked rather than assumed. AC2 CLOSED VIA ITS SECOND BRANCH ('or the reason it cannot is written down'), in NEW vault/20-domain/grading-eval-gate.md, and the reason is not 'nobody got to it': every run spends real vision calls on a set that must GROW to stay meaningful, so a per-PR gate scales its bill with the thing that makes it worth having; grading is not temperature-pinned on the default model (US-2035) so the same prompt against the same case moves between runs, and a build gate that fails on noise gets bypassed - a lesson this repo has already written down twice (db-denied-rpc-crash-check.mjs is advisory for exactly this, and US-1927 records a permanently-red guard being switched off); and the golden set cannot be faked to make CI green, because a synthetic set turns the gate into a test of the fixture. WHAT GATES INSTEAD IS STRONGER: activation. A version cannot go active without a passing eval recorded against it, so the check sits where the change would reach a CUSTOMER rather than where it reaches main. VERIFIED: 4 new cases in src/tests/grading-eval-gate_test.ts including junk/zero/negative overrides falling back to the strict default, and one asserting the agreement floor did NOT move so a later edit cannot take the other half of the gate with it. Sabotage-verified by restoring 1.0, which reddened two cases. deno check + lint clean, tsc -b clean, vault:lint strict clean at 179 notes.

userStories.title: FlipDesk grading drops the label photo the pipeline still blocks on
userStories.description: flipdesk-grading.ts:83 sets REQUIRED_GRADING_PHOTO_TYPES to front and back only, with a comment claiming the tag shot is covered by the sub-0.75 review path. That premise is false: lib/image-quality.ts:68 still lists label as required with severity 'block' and there is no carve-out at its only call site (grading-pipeline.ts:1859). A FlipDesk item with no tag photo is charged (flipdesk-grading.ts:591), runs one Claude Vision call per image, then abstains to needs_photos and refunds. Money returns, AI spend burns every time, seller round-trips. iOS and Android both use this path with no local check.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide: either FlipDesk requires the label photo, or image-quality gets an explicit FlipDesk carve-out. Record which and why.
The two requirement lists cannot disagree — one source, or a test that asserts they match.
The client validates before upload so the seller is told up front, not after a round trip.
Measure how often this fires today (submissions ending needs_photos with a refund) to size the wasted AI spend.

OPERATOR: run §26 of scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql (AC4). It counts FlipDesk grading rows that ended in needs_photos per month and the refunds that followed. Read the two together: rows with no matching refunds is a WORSE finding than the one this AC asked about, because the seller then paid for a grade they never got.
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Grading] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. | 2026-08-03 AC1, AC2, AC3 DONE. AC4 is a prod query and stays open as the operator half. VERIFIED THE AUDIT FIRST, as its note asked, and every claim held. AC1 DECISION (owner, via AskUserQuestion): FLIPDESK REQUIRES THE TAG PHOTO. THE OLD COMMENT'S PREMISE WAS FALSE, which is what made this worth asking about rather than assuming: flipdesk-grading said front+back were enough because 'the <0.75 → human-review path already covers the weaker-signal case'. image-quality.ts lists `label` in REQUIRED_IMAGE_TYPES at severity `block`, and grading-pipeline.ts applies it at Step 4b — BEFORE any confidence scoring. The review path it named never executed. So a FlipDesk item with no tag was charged (flipdesk-grading.ts runPaymentPrecedence), ran ONE CLAUDE VISION CALL PER IMAGE, abstained to needs_photos, and was refunded. The money came back and the AI spend did not, every time, and the seller round-tripped to be told something we could have said up front. Requiring it is therefore strictly better for the SAME seller the old comment was written to protect. THE OTHER OPTIONS AND WHY NOT: loosening image-quality would have changed grading for every WEB submission too (more human review, a global product change for a FlipDesk bug); a FlipDesk-only carve-out would have frozen two deliberately-different paths forever. Both were offered to the owner with their costs. ⚠ LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY: the old comment's concern is real — some garments (Lululemon cut size labels, tagless resale) genuinely have no readable tag. That is a product question about what those sellers photograph, and it is recorded at the call site rather than settled by loosening a grading gate. AC2 DONE BY DERIVATION, not by matching two literals: REQUIRED_GRADING_PHOTO_TYPES is now REQUIRED_IMAGE_TYPES.map(gradingImageTypeToPhotoType), so the lists cannot drift apart again. Two tests pin the derivation and the round trip — a wrong entry in the inverse map would make them agree on paper while asking the seller for a photo type the UI cannot produce. A REAL BUG THE TEST CAUGHT, and it would have been a prod outage rather than a wrong answer: REQUIRED_GRADING_PHOTO_TYPES is built at MODULE LOAD, and I first placed the GRADING_TO_PHOTO_TYPE map below it. A function declaration hoists; the `const` it reads does not, so the module threw ReferenceError at import and the edge would not have booted. The map is now above its use with that reason written next to it. AC3 DONE: the client already had a readiness mirror (src/lib/grading-readiness.ts) driving the Submit card live, so the seller is told before paying. THE TRAP IN THE CLIENT HALF: REQUIRED_PHOTO_TYPES was doing DOUBLE DUTY — it gates 'may this item advance to photographed and be listed?' AND fed the grading readiness preview. Adding `tag` to it would have blocked the LISTING pipeline for every tagless garment, which nobody asked for and is a different product decision. Added a SEPARATE REQUIRED_GRADING_PHOTO_TYPES (front, back, tag); the listing list is unchanged, and a test asserts the two stay different. THE SHARED FIXTURE (src/test/fixtures/grading-readiness-cases.json, asserted by BOTH suites) was regenerated from the rules rather than hand-edited — 13 cases each needing a blocker string and a missingPhotos list is where a typo becomes a cross-project contract both sides then agree on. But a straight recompute BROKE WHAT THE CASES WERE FOR: 'fully ready' had no tag, so it stopped being ready and every case collapsed onto the same missing-tag blocker, testing nothing. Inputs were patched to preserve each case's intent, the case named 'tag photo does not satisfy anything' was renamed (it is no longer true), and a 'missing tag only' case was added for the new rule — 14 total. Also fixed a latent wrong-name in the edge parity test: it passed the GRADING type `label` where the FlipDesk readiness function takes `tag`. It passed either way while neither was required. AC4 REMAINS (operator): count submissions ending needs_photos with a refund, to size the wasted AI spend. It belongs with the other prod diagnostics. VERIFIED: full edge suite 5358 passed / 0 failed, deno check + lint clean across 1339 files, tsc -b clean, web readiness + hooks suites 112 passed. | 2026-08-15 AC4 IS NOW PART OF THE ONE-PASTE FILE. §26 of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql asks it in two halves: (a) flipdesk_grading_submissions rows that ended in needs_photos, by month, and (b) the refunds that followed, joined through submission_id - the only link between the FlipDesk bridge row and the credit ledger. Counts and dates only, no ids. THE READING GUIDE MATTERS MORE THAN THE QUERY: (a) non-empty with (b) empty is a WORSE finding than the one this AC asked about, because it means the abstention happened and the refund did not, so the seller paid for a grade they never received. Both empty closes AC4 at zero. And the AI spend itself is NOT recoverable from either number - images-per-submission is the multiplier and these rows do not store it, so the honest answer is a count of occurrences, not a dollar figure. COLUMN NAMES VERIFIED AGAINST THE MIGRATION CORPUS, not assumed: the safety test's required-columns list now covers flipdesk_grading_submissions (status, submission_id, created_at) and grade_credit_transactions (reason, submission_id, delta, created_at), so a rename on either side of that join fails in CI rather than on the operator's prod session. Sabotage-verified by typoing created_at, which reddened it naming the pair. The reason value is 'refund', from 00037's CHECK constraint, read rather than guessed. | [2026-09-02][PROD READ] AC4 ANSWERED. Source: scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql run read-only against prod over SSH on 2026-09-02 (container supabase-db-kcksoks4kk0kswk0ccs40os8, 29 sections, 0 SQL errors). Raw output kept out of the repo; it contains customer data. Refunds attributable to the missing-tag-photo path: 2 in June 2026 and 6 in July 2026, with credits_returned 0 in both months. So it happened 8 times and no credit was actually returned to those customers, which is the part worth acting on.

userStories.title: Nothing in version control creates or verifies the 73 production cron schedules
userStories.description: There is no scheduling mechanism in the repo. docker-compose.coolify.yml has no cron, sidecar or command (only the healthcheck at lines 70-79); same for the other compose files. .github/workflows has zero /api/jobs references and its only three schedule blocks are lighthouse, staging-smoke and an uptime probe. pg_cron is unused (zero cron.schedule across all 506 migrations). NO CI scheduling: zero references to api/jobs anywhere in .github/workflows. So the sole mechanism really is hand-typed Coolify UI tasks, and the repo has no way to create, apply or verify them. CORRECTION 1: the story says the workflows have three schedule blocks (lighthouse, staging-smoke, uptime). There are FOUR — secret-scan-history.yml also runs on a schedule. Immaterial to the conclusion, but the story should not be quoted as an inventory. CORRECTION 2: the count 73 is stale. CRON_REGISTRY now holds 74 entries — 67 recorded:true and 7 recorded:false — of which 2 are marked oneOff. The number moves whenever a job is added, which is itself an argument for AC2's manifest-and-compare over any figure written into prose. CONFIRMED AND WORTH THE EMPHASIS THE STORY GIVES IT: cron-fleet-health is itself entry number N of the same hand-entered list, so if the operator never created that one Coolify task, nothing in the system alerts about anything — the watcher and the watched share a single point of failure. AC4 CONFIRMED AT THE CODE LEVEL: ops-events.ts reads ops_alert_webhook_url and ops_alert_email via getSetting with an empty-string default for both, so an unconfigured prod terminates the entire alert path in an admin screen. WHAT I CANNOT DO FROM HERE, and it is the half the story says to start with: AC3 and AC4 both require PROD state — whether the cron-fleet-health task exists in the Coolify UI, and whether those two system_settings rows are non-empty in production. This host has no prod access. Those two are operator checks, not agent work, and should be split out so the buildable half (AC1/AC2, schedules-as-code or a verified manifest) is not blocked behind them. RELATED, same day: US-2312 made every recorded cron run report body-level failures and populate rows_processed, and US-2318's notes measured that the admin dashboard's 2000-row window covers only ~14.2 hours at the current fleet cadence — so the ledger this story would compare a manifest against is more trustworthy than it was, but the screen reading it still hides daily jobs. | 2026-08-03 AC1 DECIDED and AC2 CLOSED. AC3 and AC4 are prod checks this host cannot make and stay open as the operator half — which is what the 2026-08-02 pass asked for. AC2 WAS MOSTLY ALREADY BUILT, and saying so is the honest half of this. The story asks for 'an artifact in the repo listing every expected schedule, and a job that compares it to what actually ran and alerts on absence'. CRON_REGISTRY is that artifact (74 entries, each with a schedule and an endpoint), lib/cron-fleet-governance.ts is that comparison — its own header calls itself 'the diff between the SCHEDULE (CRON_REGISTRY) and REALITY (cron_runs)' — and US-2004's routes/jobs-cron-fleet.ts is the alert. All three predate this story. SO THE REAL HOLE IS THE ONE THE STORY EMPHASISED and nothing had addressed: cron-fleet-health is itself entry N of the same hand-typed Coolify list. If the operator never created that one task, or deleted it, or typo'd its secret, then nothing in the system alerts about anything — and the silence is indistinguishable from health. The watcher and the watched share one point of failure, which means the alerting is not merely unverified, it is unverifiABLE from inside. AC1 DECIDED, and scoped rather than sweeping: THE SCHEDULES STAY IN COOLIFY, EXCEPT ONE. Moving 74 tasks into a compose sidecar or pg_cron is a migration with its own failure modes, and the diff-against-reality job already covers a missing task ONCE SOMEONE IS WATCHING. What moves to schedules-as-code is exactly the job whose absence is silent by construction. NEW .github/workflows/cron-fleet-watchdog.yml invokes /api/jobs/cron-fleet-health every 6 hours from GitHub-hosted runners — infrastructure that cannot fail the way Coolify does. If the Coolify task exists these ticks are near-no-ops (the job takes a lock); if it does not, the alarm stays connected. TWO DELIBERATE DESIGN CHOICES. It SKIPS, exit 0, when EDGE_JOB_SECRET is unset — a watchdog that cries wolf every six hours because nobody configured it gets muted, and a muted watchdog is worse than none. And it checks the BODY as well as the status, because this endpoint can answer 200 with an error payload and this is the one job where a green-looking check that proves nothing is exactly the failure being fixed. NEW src/tests/cron-fleet-watchdog_test.ts, 6 cases, pinning the two halves agreeing: the workflow is SCHEDULED (a workflow_dispatch-only file would look like coverage and provide none), it calls the endpoint the REGISTRY declares, it sends the header requireJobSecret reads, the unset-secret branch exits 0, the body is inspected, and every registry entry still carries a schedule and an endpoint. TWO WEAKNESSES IN MY OWN GUARD, both found by MUTATION rather than by reading, and both the same family. (1) The endpoint assertion searched the whole file — but the workflow names that endpoint in its header comment and its step name too, so it would have been satisfied by PROSE while the actual request drifted. It matches the curl line now. That is the eighth time a guard here has been confused by a comment. (2) Worse, the fixed version used `includes`, and '/api/jobs/cron-fleet-healthz' CONTAINS '/api/jobs/cron-fleet-health' — so a renamed route still passed. It matches with the closing quote now, so the path has to end where the registry says it ends. A substring check on a path is a prefix check, and prefix checks wave through exactly the rename they exist to catch. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SIX WAYS: the schedule removed, the endpoint drifted, the auth header changed, the unset-secret branch made to fail, the body check deleted, and a registry entry stripped of its endpoint. Each reddened on its own case — two of them only after the guard itself was fixed. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE STORY carried forward from 2026-08-02 and still true: there are FOUR scheduled workflows, not three, and the fleet is 74 entries, not 73 — which is itself the argument for a manifest over a number in prose. REMAINING (operator, both need prod): AC3 — confirm the cron-fleet-health task actually exists in the Coolify UI and that its alerts reach a human. The new watchdog reduces the cost of getting this wrong but does not answer it. AC4 — confirm ops_alert_webhook_url and ops_alert_email are non-empty in prod system_settings; both default to empty string, in which case the entire alert path terminates in an admin screen nobody is watching, and every alert this story is about would be raised into a void. VERIFIED: deno lint clean across 1334 files, full edge suite 5300 passed / 0 failed. | 2026-08-03: this story's last open AC is now answerable by scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql, which the operator runs in ONE psql session alongside the other blocked stories. Read-only, verified by executing against a real database with ON_ERROR_STOP=1 — so it cannot fail the operator's session on a wrong column name, which is the failure mode that makes someone distrust the whole file. §11 reports whether ops_alert_webhook_url and ops_alert_email are configured — PRESENCE and length only, never the value, since a webhook URL is a capability rather than a setting. A MISSING ROW is reported separately from an empty one, because ops-events.ts falls back to "" for both and the two look identical from the code's side. If they are unset, every alert this story is about is raised into a void, including the cron-fleet-stalled one. | PROD ANSWER 2026-08-03 (owner ran scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql). §11's second query returned webhook_row_present 1 and email_row_present 1, so both ops_alert settings rows EXIST. STILL MISSING: the first query of §11, which reports whether each row's value is actually non-empty. A present row with an empty value behaves identically to a missing one — ops-events.ts falls back to '' either way — so row presence alone does not answer AC4. That is the one number left on this story. | 2026-08-15 AC1 and AC2 CLOSED; AC3 and AC4 are operator confirmations and are now declared as one. AC1 asked for a DECISION recorded, and it had been made implicitly and never written down: NEW vault/10-ops/cron-schedule-governance.md records a verified manifest rather than schedules-as-code, with the three reasons the alternatives were refused — pg_cron would make the database hold a credential for the API in front of it; a sidecar is a second thing that can be down with no way to alert about its own absence, which is this story's failure moved one layer along; and Coolify tasks already survive a redeploy because they live on the service rather than in the image. It also states the COST plainly: creating a schedule stays a manual step, so a new cron can be merged and never installed, and that is exactly why the drift check is not optional. AC2 was already satisfied and is now written down as such: CRON_REGISTRY is the artifact, scripts/render-cron-docs.ts generates the tables in COOLIFY.md and the launch checklist with a drift test that fails when they diverge, and jobs-cron-fleet.ts compares expected ticks to the cron_runs ledger hourly. THE PROPERTY THAT MAKES A MANIFEST SUFFICIENT, and it is worth stating because it is not obvious: detectMissedTicks computes expected slots from the SCHEDULE rather than from prior runs, so a task that was never created in Coolify reads as stalled from its first elapsed slot. Without that, a never-installed job would be indistinguishable from a job with nothing to do. The note also carries the honest limits: the check cannot see an EXTRA Coolify task hitting an endpoint the registry does not know about, and five registry entries sit outside the ledger (US-2616/US-2617) and are named in the fleet report rather than silently excluded. | [2026-09-02][PROD READ] AC4 ANSWERED, and it is the bad answer. Source: scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql run read-only against prod over SSH on 2026-09-02 (container supabase-db-kcksoks4kk0kswk0ccs40os8, 29 sections, 0 SQL errors). Raw output kept out of the repo; it contains customer data. Both system_settings rows EXIST and both are EMPTY: ops_alert_email and ops_alert_webhook_url have value_length 0, last touched 2026-06-14. A missing row and an empty value both fall back to "", so every ops alert this system raises currently goes nowhere. This is the same finding US-2003 is open for; note it there rather than treating them as two problems.

userStories.title: Concurrent token refresh disconnects sellers on providers that rotate refresh tokens
userStories.description: No advisory lock, mutex or single-flight guard exists in any token path (no pg_advisory, no FOR UPDATE, no in-flight promise map). The read-modify-write is check expiry, refresh, persist. Four connectors do this and all four persist a rotated refresh token when the provider sends one, which proves rotation is expected: etsy-client.ts:392-396, whatnot-client.ts:347-350, depop-client.ts, flipdesk-google.ts:353-355. Scenario (Etsy, 1-hour tokens): a user opens the Marketplaces page while the sync cron fires; both see expiresAt - now < 60s (etsy-client.ts:368) and POST the same refresh token; Etsy rotates and invalidates the old one on first use; the second call gets 400 invalid_grant; isPermanentEtsyAuthFailure classifies 400 as PERMANENT (:243) so the handler sets is_active:false and stores a reconnect message (:410-416). The user is force-disconnected by a race, not a revocation. eBay is not exposed (its refresh token is not rotated).
acceptanceCriteria: A per-connection advisory lock (keyed on connection id) around refresh, so concurrent callers wait rather than racing.
invalid_grant immediately after a successful sibling refresh is treated as transient (re-read the row and retry once) rather than permanent.

refreshExpiringEtsyConnections (etsy-client.ts:467) scans on a 24-hour horizon but delegates to getEtsyAccessToken which only refreshes inside a 60-second window, so the cron decrypts every active connection every run and proactively refreshes nothing. Fix or delete it.
Confirm whether Etsy/Depop/Google actually invalidate the old token on rotation — that sets the real severity.
Audit prod for connections deactivated with an invalid_grant refresh_error and offer affected sellers a reconnect.

OPERATOR: ask Etsy, Depop and Whatnot whether they invalidate the OLD refresh token on rotation (AC4). This sets SEVERITY, not correctness - siblingRefreshWon already makes the race survivable either way. AC5 is answered: prod section 13 returned no rows, so the race never disconnected a seller.
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Auth] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. | PARTIAL 2026-08-03 — AC1, AC2 and AC3 DONE for all three affected connectors. AC4 needs a partner answer and AC5 needs prod; both are named below with what to ask. THE AUDIT WAS RIGHT ON THE MECHANISM AND WRONG ON ONE CONNECTOR. Etsy, Whatnot and Depop all do read-expiry → refresh → persist with no coordination, all three persist a rotated refresh token when the provider sends one, and all three classify the loser's failure as PERMANENT — is_active false plus a reconnect message. eBay is genuinely not exposed (no rotation). But there is no flipdesk-google.ts in the repo and nothing under src/lib/google* stores refresh_token_encrypted, so the fourth connector the story names does not exist. Three, not four. AC2 IS THE LOAD-BEARING FIX AND IT WENT IN FIRST, because it makes the race SURVIVABLE rather than rarer. NEW lib/token-refresh-race.ts exports the pure siblingRefreshWon(before, after, now): before deactivating, each connector re-reads its own row, and if a sibling has stored a DIFFERENT and still-valid token then we lost a race rather than the grant — use their token, leave the connection active. It compares ciphertext, which is the right test even though a fresh IV means identical plaintext encrypts differently: the question is 'did this row change', and an unchanged row is byte-identical because nobody rewrote it. AC1 DONE as in-replica single-flight, and the cross-replica advisory lock the AC names was CONSIDERED AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT. try_acquire_job_lock (00094) would give one with no migration, but job_locks is the cron fleet's table — cron-fleet-governance reads it — and keying it per CONNECTION would put a row per seller per marketplace into a table that exists to describe scheduled jobs. A lock also only makes the race rarer, while AC2 makes it harmless. If duplicate refresh calls later show up as a quota problem, that is what the lock fixes, and it belongs on its own table. Recorded in the module header so the next reader sees a decision rather than an omission. The single-flight entry is deleted in a finally, so a REJECTED refresh is not cached — on these paths a shared rejection would turn one transient provider 503 into a deactivation for everyone waiting behind it. AC3 DONE, FIXED NOT DELETED, and it was worse than 'refreshes nothing': all THREE sweeps (not just Etsy's) select connections expiring within 24 HOURS and then called a getter that only refreshes inside 60 SECONDS. So every run decrypted every active connection and renewed none of them — a cron wearing the costume of a safety net. The getters now take refreshWithinMs (default 60s) and the sweeps pass their own horizon. The single-flight key deliberately IGNORES the threshold: a page load arriving mid-sweep inherits the freshly renewed token, and a sweep landing on a page load's still-valid token simply renews on the next tick. A NEGATIVE TEST THAT PROVED NOTHING, caught and fixed. The 'an unchanged row is not a sibling refresh' case used a 30-second expiry on both sides and stayed GREEN with the unchanged-row guard deleted — the freshness floor rejected it for an unrelated reason. The times are the test: the token now has HOURS left, which is the sweep's world, where refreshWithinMs is the 24-hour horizon and a proactive refresh can fail on a row nowhere near expiry. There the unchanged ciphertext is the ONLY thing between a dead grant and being called a race. NEW src/tests/token-refresh-race_test.ts, 10 cases: six behavioural on the pure helper and the single-flight (including different connections not collapsing, and a rejection not being cached), and four on the wiring — all three connectors wired with eBay's absence ENUMERATED as a decision, the race check running BEFORE the deactivating update by index, and the sweep passing its horizon AND the getter honouring it. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SIX WAYS, each reddening on its own case: the unchanged-row guard removed, the freshness floor removed, the in-flight entry left behind, a connector losing single-flight, a sweep reverting to the 60s window, and the race check physically moved below the deactivating update. REMAINING. AC4: confirm Etsy/Depop/Whatnot actually invalidate the old refresh token on rotation. That sets severity, not correctness — the fix is right either way — so it is a documentation question, not a blocker. AC5: audit prod for connections with is_active=false and a refresh_error matching the reconnect message, and offer those sellers a reconnect. That needs the prod session and is a candidate for scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql on the next pass. VERIFIED: deno check clean, deno lint clean across 1328 files, full edge suite 5267 passed / 0 failed. | 2026-08-03: this story's last open AC is now answerable by scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql, which the operator runs in ONE psql session alongside the other blocked stories. Read-only, verified by executing against a real database with ON_ERROR_STOP=1 — so it cannot fail the operator's session on a wrong column name, which is the failure mode that makes someone distrust the whole file. §13 lists connections already deactivated with a refresh_error, split by marketplace and by the distinct error text — the split matters because a genuine revocation must not be mistaken for a lost race and offered a pointless reconnect. No token material is selected; refresh_error is our own message, not the provider's payload. | PROD ANSWER 2026-08-03 (owner ran scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql). §13 returned NO ROWS: not one marketplace connection is deactivated with a refresh_error. AC5 ANSWERED — the refresh race never disconnected a seller in production, so there is nobody to offer a reconnect to. The fix shipped before it cost anyone their connection, which is the good version of this outcome. AC4 (do Etsy/Depop/Whatnot actually invalidate the old token on rotation?) still needs a partner answer and is a severity question rather than a correctness one. | 2026-08-17 AC4 ANSWERED AS FAR AS THE PUBLIC RECORD GOES, and answering it found that three of our own files were asserting the unverified half as fact.  ONE OF THREE IS CONFIRMED, FROM THE VENDOR. Whatnot documents it outright at developers.whatnot.com -> Getting Started -> Authentication: "The used refresh token will be invalidated, and you should store the newly returned Refresh Token." Refresh tokens expire in 1 year. So on Whatnot the race is exactly as this story described and siblingRefreshWon is load-bearing.  THE OTHER TWO ARE NOT DOCUMENTED EITHER WAY, which is a different answer from "no". Etsy: the authentication page describes a 90-day refresh token and a new one on each refresh, and says nothing about the previous one. The nearest thing to a statement is Etsy staff in open-api discussion #1351 - "Each time you use your access_token, the API provides a new refresh token" and "You should not have issues with your refresh_token after 24 hours of non-use" - neither of which says whether the old token is revoked. Community reports of invalid_grant / "refresh_token is revoked" exist but do not separate rotation from expiry or from a genuine revocation, so they cannot carry the claim. Depop: the partner API authentication page names a "long-lived Refresh Token" and has no rotation, reuse or single-use section at all.  WHAT THAT ACTUALLY CHANGED, and it is the useful part. token-refresh-race.ts:5, its test header, and vault/30-platform/marketplace-connector-contract.md all stated that Etsy, Whatnot AND Depop "rotate the refresh token and invalidate the old one on first use". The rotation half is true of all three and verifiable here - every connector persists a returned refresh token. The invalidation half was true of one and assumed of two, written in the register voice, and it is the specific sentence AC4 was opened to check. All three now say what is documented and what is not, and name the source.  IT SETS SEVERITY, NOT CORRECTNESS - which is what the AC said and is now demonstrated rather than predicted. siblingRefreshWon survives the race whichever way the two unknowns fall, which is exactly why the fix did not wait on a partner. The operational instruction added alongside: do NOT drop either defence for Etsy or Depop on the strength of a silent document. Silence is not a guarantee, and a provider can tighten rotation without announcing it.  WHAT WOULD SETTLE THE REMAINING TWO: a partner answer, or a deliberate two-refresh experiment against a real connection (refresh, then present the OLD token again and read the response). The second needs live seller credentials and is not available from the repo, but it is a five-minute answer for anyone who has them.  ALSO FIXED IN PASSING, because it blocked the vault CI lane for every commit: vault/50-business/subscription-copy-review-register.md was in ERROR under vault:lint --strict, drifting on email.ts. The drift was a false positive of file-level watching - the change was the US-2667 crisis-escalation template, which is support copy and not subscription copy. Verified before bumping: all six registered subscription templates plus the deliberately-excluded sendCancellationRequestedEmail are present and unchanged since the last review (git log -L on the region returns nothing since 2026-08-14), and the other three code_refs last changed 2026-08-09/08-10. Reviewed bumped to 2026-08-17; the vault lane is green again.  VERIFIED: token-refresh-race_test 10 passed, deno check src/main.ts clean, deno lint clean, vault:lint 187 notes with 0 errors.  STILL OPEN: nothing here is blocking. AC4 is answered for Whatnot and is answerable for Etsy/Depop only by a partner or a live experiment; AC5 was answered 2026-08-03 (prod §13 returned no rows). If the owner wants this story closed, AC4 as written asks to "confirm whether" - and the confirmed answer is one yes and two undocumenteds, recorded where the code that depends on it can be read. | 2026-08-17 (second pass) ⚠ MY OWN AC4 ANSWER WAS WRONG ABOUT DEPOP, and the way it was wrong is the part worth keeping.  The earlier note recorded "Depop - UNDOCUMENTED. The partner API authentication page names a long-lived Refresh Token and has no rotation, reuse or single-use section at all." The first sentence was a conclusion; the second was the whole evidence for it. I opened the page whose TITLE matched the question and stopped.  DEPOP DOCUMENTS IT PLAINLY, in How to Guides -> Using OAuth Refresh Tokens: "You receive a new Refresh Token with every successful refresh request. The previous Access Token and Refresh Token are immediately invalidated and cannot be used again." The new token inherits the grant original expiry, 1 year from consent. So Depop rotates strictly and single-use, the race is real there, and siblingRefreshWon is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces.  HOW IT SURFACED: while reading the same site for US-2326 webhook headers, the docs overview listed its How-To sections - Restocking, Validate webhooks, Processing an Order, Managing Offers, Managing Shipping, Using OAuth Refresh Tokens. The last one had been sitting there the whole time.  THE LESSON, now written into the vault note rather than only here: enumerate a vendor doc SECTIONS before concluding silence. An absence recorded in a contract note is read as evidence by everyone after you, and "undocumented" is a much stronger claim than "not on the page I opened".  ETSY RE-CHECKED RATHER THAN LEFT ON THE FIRST READING, since the Depop miss made the first reading untrustworthy. Its refresh section describes only how to USE the new token and still says nothing about the previous one fate. Etsy remains the one genuine unknown.  CORRECTED IN ALL FOUR PLACES the original claim was written: vault/30-platform/marketplace-connector-contract.md (the callout, retitled "Two of three document that the OLD token dies"), the token-refresh-race.ts header, its test header, and here. The vault note also carries the enumerate-the-sections lesson.  VERIFIED: 63 cases green across token-refresh-race / size-systems / grading-size, deno lint clean, vault:lint --strict clean at 187 notes.  STILL OPEN: Etsy only, and it is a severity question rather than a correctness one. It needs a partner answer or a deliberate two-refresh experiment against a real connection. | [2026-09-02][PROD READ] AC5 ANSWERED: clean. Source: scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql run read-only against prod over SSH on 2026-09-02 (container supabase-db-kcksoks4kk0kswk0ccs40os8, 29 sections, 0 SQL errors). Raw output kept out of the repo; it contains customer data. Zero marketplace connections have been deactivated by a refresh failure - the per-marketplace deactivation census returned 0 rows, and the distinct refresh_error_prefix census also returned 0 rows. So the concurrent-refresh race has not disconnected a seller in production. The race is still real in code; what this settles is that there is no customer damage to repair.

userStories.title: Marketplace webhooks have no freshness window and one debug flag disables all four
userStories.description: Verification itself is correct everywhere — all four receivers read the raw body, verify before any DB write, fail closed when the secret is missing, and use constant-time comparison (or asymmetric verify for eBay). Three residual gaps. (A) isDebugAllowed('WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG') is checked at flipdesk-webhooks.ts:123, :201, :493, :1229 and skips the whole verify block when true; lib/env.ts:82-85 returns false in production and edgeEnv() defaults to 'production' when unset, so a bare container fails closed — but any staging or preview with EDGE_ENV non-production and the flag on accepts unsigned requests on the account-deletion path (mass seller disconnect) and logs headers plus 2KB of body verbatim. (B) No replay or freshness check anywhere. All four rely on event-id dedupe which is skipped when the provider's id header is absent (:756, :389, :512) and FAILS OPEN on a DB error (:770, :400, :595, :1290). eBay's notification.publishDate is declared in the type at :744-745 and never read; Shopify's X-Shopify-Triggered-At is never read. (C) fetchPublicKeyMaterial (ebay-notification-verify.ts:135-154) does getAppAccessToken plus a call to eBay's public_key/{kid} for any attacker-supplied kid, with no timeout and no negative cache (keyCache at :92 stores only successes), bounded only by the 600/60s limiter at main.ts:1025 — so an attacker can drive 600 unauthenticated outbound eBay calls per minute per replica and burn the app's API quota.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm EDGE_ENV and WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG in staging, and whether staging shares marketplace_connections with prod. If it does, this is live.
A timestamp freshness window (+/- 5 min) on the eBay and Shopify receivers using the headers already sent.
Dedupe fails CLOSED on a DB error rather than open.
Negative cache plus a timeout on the eBay public-key fetch.

Depop's header names (x-depop-signature / x-depop-hmac-sha256 at :495-496, x-depop-webhook-id / x-depop-delivery-id at :512) are unconfirmed guesses. The signature failure mode is safe (401) but the dedupe failure mode is SILENT — if Depop uses neither header, every delivery is reprocessed with no error. Confirm and narrow, including the hex-or-base64 hedge at depop-api.ts:488-491.

OPERATOR: two confirmations that cannot be made from here (AC1, AC5). (a) In staging, check EDGE_ENV and WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG, and whether staging shares marketplace_connections with prod - if it does, the unsigned-request path is live against real seller connections. (b) Get Depop's actual webhook documentation: the header names in the receiver (x-depop-signature / x-depop-hmac-sha256, x-depop-webhook-id / x-depop-delivery-id) are GUESSES, and the dedupe failure mode on a wrong guess is SILENT.
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Webhooks] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Secrets at rest are CLEAN: crypto-aes.ts uses a fresh 96-bit IV per encryption, key from env never logged, and v2 binds user_id as GCM additionalData so a ciphertext copied to another tenant fails to decrypt. No plaintext tokens in any log path. | PARTIAL 2026-08-03 — AC2 and AC4 DONE. AC3 is PUSHED BACK ON with a reason (see below). AC1 and AC5 need an operator and a partner respectively. AC4 DONE, and it was the real one. fetchPublicKeyMaterial did getAppAccessToken plus a bare `fetch` — no deadline — to eBay's public_key/{kid} endpoint, with `kid` taken from the REQUEST'S OWN signature header, so an unauthenticated caller chose it. Only SUCCESSES were cached, so every request bearing a non-resolving kid produced a fresh token + a fresh outbound call, bounded only by the 600/60s limiter: 600 unauthenticated outbound eBay calls per minute per replica, burning the app's own quota, on requests that were going to be rejected anyway. Added a NEGATIVE cache (5-min TTL — short, because a kid can legitimately start resolving when eBay publishes a key, and a long negative cache would then reject genuine notifications until the process restarted) and a 5s timeout via fetchWithTimeout. The no-bare-fetch guard's declaration for that file went 1 -> 0, which is how I knew the change actually landed. AC2 DONE: NEW lib/webhook-freshness.ts, applied to the eBay and Shopify receivers using the timestamps both providers ALREADY SEND and neither receiver read — eBay's notification.publishDate (declared in the payload type and never touched) and Shopify's X-Shopify-Triggered-At. A signature proves the provider signed a payload; it does not prove the payload is recent, and a captured delivery stays validly signed forever. TWO ASYMMETRIES, deliberate and both tested. ABSENT timestamp -> ACCEPT: a provider renaming a header or shipping a topic without the field must not become an outage on a path we do not control, and freshness is a SECOND line after the signature. PRESENT but unparseable -> REJECT: that is not an omission, it is a value that does not mean what it claims, which is the shape a forged replay has. The window is symmetric because provider clock skew runs both ways and a one-sided window rejects every delivery from a clock running fast — indistinguishable from an outage. The eBay check sits in the ROUTE, not in processEbayWebhookEvent: that function runs detached from the response, so a rejection there could not produce a status and would be indistinguishable from success to the caller. Both checks run AFTER signature verification so an unsigned request is still reported as unsigned rather than as stale. A TEST OF MINE WAS WRONG BEFORE THE CODE WAS: I asserted '0000' is unparseable. Date.parse accepts it as year zero, so it is a valid-but-ancient timestamp and is caught by the staleness branch instead. Rejected either way, but via the honest reason — the test now asserts that explicitly rather than being loosened. AC3 — I AM NOT IMPLEMENTING THIS AS WRITTEN, and the reason should be decided rather than inherited. The AC says dedupe should fail CLOSED on a DB error. The current fail-open is not an oversight: US-509 chose it, documented it inline, and made it observable (a webhook.fail_open metric plus a captured exception), on the grounds that the downstream payout/sale ingest is idempotent. Failing closed would DROP a real webhook on a transient database blip — losing a genuine sale — to prevent a double-process that the idempotent ingest already prevents. That trade looks worse, not better. If the owner still wants fail-closed, it needs a durable retry/parking path first, otherwise it converts a benign duplicate into permanent data loss. REMAINING: AC1 (confirm EDGE_ENV and WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG in staging, and whether staging shares marketplace_connections with prod — if it does, the unsigned-request path is live) is an operator check. AC5 (Depop's header names are unconfirmed guesses, and the dedupe failure mode is SILENT) needs Depop's actual documentation. VERIFIED: edge suite 5155/0, deno lint clean across 1308 files. | 2026-08-15 AC3 DECIDED by the owner: keep failing open, do NOT implement the AC as written. AND THE RULE TURNED OUT TO BE SHARPER THAN THE STORY'S NOTE CLAIMED. The earlier note argued 'fail-open is fine because the ingest is idempotent'. True, but incomplete — routes/webhooks.ts:125 already fails CLOSED on the Stripe path (US-509) and returns a 500 on purpose. So the codebase is not inconsistent; it applies one rule to two providers: FAIL CLOSED WHERE THE PROVIDER REDELIVERS, OPEN WHERE IT DOES NOT. Stripe retries on a 500 and its events move money, so asking for a redelivery costs nothing. A marketplace does not reliably redeliver, so failing closed there drops a real sale on a transient blip to prevent a double-process the idempotent ingest already prevents — trading a benign duplicate for permanent loss. RECORDED IN THE CODE, not just here, because the AC's wording is exactly the kind a future reader implements without asking: the fail-open branch in flipdesk-webhooks.ts now cites US-2326 AC3, states the redelivery rule so the Stripe difference does not read as an inconsistency, and names the precondition for ever revisiting it (a durable retry or parking path has to come FIRST — fail-closed without one is strictly worse than what is there). NEW src/tests/webhook-failure-policy_test.ts, 3 cases: Stripe records fail_closed and says the 500 is a retry request; the marketplace path records fail_open AND captures an exception (a SILENT fail-open is the version that is actually wrong); and the decision, the rule and the precondition all survive in the source. Sabotage-verified by removing the US-2326 citation, which reddened the third case. AC1 and AC5 are now declared as one OPERATOR criterion. AC5 is worth flagging on its own: the Depop header names in the receiver are GUESSES, and a wrong guess fails SILENTLY — the dedupe simply never matches, so every Depop delivery would be processed as new. deno check + lint clean. | 2026-08-17 AC5 ANSWERED FROM DEPOP OWN DOCS, and the answer was a live bug rather than a confirmation.  THE AC SAID: "Depop header names are unconfirmed guesses, and the dedupe failure mode is SILENT - needs Depop actual documentation." The documentation exists and is public: partnerapi.depop.com -> How to Guides -> Validate webhooks. Nobody had read it.  WHAT IT SAYS, quoted rather than paraphrased: the signature header is X-Depop-Signature, the timestamp header is X-Depop-Timestamp, the algorithm is HMAC-SHA256, and the signature covers "the timestamp and body of the request, separated by a dot: <timestamp>.<body>" using "the raw request body ... the exact bytes we send".  ⚠ SO THE VERIFIER WAS WRONG. verifyDepopWebhook HMAC-ed the RAW BODY ALONE. Every genuine Depop delivery would have failed the comparison and been refused with a 401 - orders never arriving, and the log line saying "signature mismatch", which reads like an attack rather than like our own bug. It has never fired in anger for one reason only: the connector is gated off behind DEPOP_ENABLED (US-2473). The bug was queued, not live, and go-live would have hit it on the first order.  FIXED: the signed string is now `${timestamp}.${rawBody}`, the route reads X-Depop-Timestamp and refuses when it is absent - not a missing nicety, since nothing can be verified without it - and the hex/base64 tolerance stays, because the guide does not say which encoding the header carries and a wrong guess there is another silent rejection.  AND AC1 GOT ITS FRESHNESS WINDOW OUT OF THE SAME PAGE. The guide says to "verify the timestamp is within an acceptable timeframe to prevent replay attacks" and names no number, so DEPOP_WEBHOOK_MAX_SKEW_MS is ours: five minutes, SYMMETRIC. A future timestamp is as much a sign of a forged or skewed sender as an old one, and a one-sided window leaves the door open from the other side - which is its own test case. Checked BEFORE the HMAC, so a replay is refused on a cheap comparison rather than after a key import. Seconds and milliseconds are told apart by magnitude, so a sender that switches units does not silently fall outside every window.  THE DEDUPE HALF IS ANSWERED AS A NEGATIVE: the guide documents NO delivery-id or event-id header at all. So x-depop-webhook-id / x-depop-delivery-id in the receiver are guesses at something that does not exist, and dedupe cannot key on a header. It has to key on the payload. Recorded rather than changed - picking the payload field is a decision about Depop event shape and belongs with the go-live work in US-2473, not in a signature fix.  VERIFIED: 10 cases in depop-api_test.ts (the old ones signed the body and are rewritten - one new case asserts a body-only signature is REFUSED, which is exactly the regression this file used to miss), full edge suite 7140 passed / 0 failed / 199 ignored, deno check src/main.ts clean, deno lint clean over 1565 files. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED TWO WAYS: reverting to a body-only signature, and making the window one-sided. Each reddened its own case.  STILL OPEN: AC1 operator half (confirm EDGE_ENV and WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG in staging, and whether staging shares marketplace_connections with prod) and the dedupe key decision above.

userStories.title: Add Shopify fulfillment: tracking numbers never reach Shopify
userStories.description: The platform coverage matrix shows Shopify as REAL for connect, list, sync, delist and price revise, but SHELL for ship. There is no fulfillmentCreate call anywhere in the repo. A seller who ships a Shopify order through FlipDesk leaves the Shopify order unfulfilled and the buyer never gets tracking.
acceptanceCriteria: Shipping an order marked as sourced from Shopify calls fulfillmentCreate with the tracking number and carrier.
Failure to fulfil is surfaced to the seller, not swallowed.
Test against the Shopify sandbox.
OPERATOR: exercise the fulfillment call against a Shopify sandbox store (AC3). AC1 and AC2 are written; nothing here can be proven without sandbox credentials.
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Shopify] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. | 2026-08-03 AC1 and AC2 DONE. AC3 (sandbox) is operator work and stays open. No migration. VERIFIED THE AUDIT FIRST, as its note asked: there is no fulfillmentCreate anywhere in the repo, and eBay + Depop both have ship routes while Shopify has none. The claim held exactly. A PRECONDITION THE STORY DOES NOT MENTION, and it had to be fixed first or AC1 was impossible: sales.platform_order_id was NEVER POPULATED FOR SHOPIFY. ingestShopifyOrder recorded the money and dropped the only handle back to Shopify, so the ship route would have had nothing to fulfil against. The column has existed since 00032 and eBay has always used it. Now stored. ⚠ Sales ingested BEFORE this change have it null and cannot be fulfilled — the route 409s with `missing_platform_order_id` and tells the seller to re-sync, rather than writing tracking locally and returning ok. Recording it silently would tell the seller their buyer was notified when no Shopify call was ever made, which is the exact failure this story exists to remove, reintroduced for older rows. WHY THIS IS TWO API CALLS: Shopify does not fulfil an ORDER. Since the 2022 fulfillment-orders migration the unit is the FULFILLMENT ORDER — an order split by location and by who is responsible — and fulfillmentCreate takes fulfillment-order ids, never an order id. NEW lib/shopify-fulfillment.ts reads the order's fulfillment orders, then submits EVERY fulfillable one. Submitting only the first would mark a multi-location order part-shipped and silently leave the rest, which reads as complete success on both sides. TWO REFUSALS THAT ARE NOT ERRORS, and one that is: a fulfillment order already CLOSED returns alreadyFulfilled rather than throwing (re-shipping is the common case — a retry, or a seller correcting tracking — and throwing turns a no-op into a red banner). A fulfillment order assigned to a THIRD-PARTY fulfilment service is skipped even though its status is OPEN: submitting for it claims someone else's work is done. But a NULL order throws, because that means the id is wrong or belongs to another shop, and reading it as 'already fulfilled' would swallow a real misconfiguration. AC2 IS THE SUBTLE ONE: fulfillmentCreate answers HTTP 200 with a populated `userErrors` array when it refuses. A handler checking only the transport status tells the seller their buyer has tracking when Shopify said no. assertNoUserErrors throws and carries Shopify's own words plus the field, because the seller is the only one who can fix a bad tracking number. The route returns 502 with that detail. A refusal on the SECOND fulfillment order still fails the whole call — reporting success because something worked would leave half the order unshipped with the seller told otherwise. notifyCustomer defaults TRUE: Shopify emailing the buyer is the entire point. TESTS: 10 cases in NEW shopify-fulfillment_test.ts driving the real function through an injected graphql fake (the codebase's existing deps pattern) — selection, third-party skip, userErrors, every-order submission with the tracking payload asserted, the no-op, a partial refusal, a missing order, an unparseable response, plus two source guards on the order-id storage and the 409. A tenant-isolation case was added for the new route (US-268 rule): it is scoped through inventory_items.user_id like the eBay one, and it gets its own case because a leak here would not merely read A's row — it would FULFIL A's Shopify order under B's request. A REAL WEAKNESS IN MY OWN TEST, found by negative verification: the ordering assertion used indexOf on both markers, and indexOf returns -1 when a marker is GONE — so -1 < anything is true and deleting the refusal code entirely left the case GREEN. Both indices are now checked for presence first, with that reason written next to them. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SEVEN WAYS: only the first fulfillment order submitted, userErrors swallowed, a third-party-held order claimed, a missing order read as fulfilled, the sale losing its order id, the 409 refusal removed, and notifyCustomer defaulting off. Each reddened on its own case. AC3 REMAINS (operator): exercise it against the Shopify sandbox with a real order. Everything decided before and after the network call is pinned here; what cannot be pinned without a shop is that Shopify accepts this exact mutation shape. VERIFIED: full edge suite 5368 passed / 0 failed, tenant-isolation 17/0, deno check clean, deno lint clean across 1341 files. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-08: the word held above is not a hold. This story has NO migration of its own — the note names 00032 only to say the platform_order_id column has existed since then, and 00032 is long since on origin/main. Nothing here is waiting on a prod apply and the branch is not frozen on this account. Recorded as an appended correction rather than by editing the sentence, because these notes are append-only and prd-lint keys its silence on an explicit correction so a fixed story stops being reported.

userStories.title: iOS: SyncEngine can prune the entire local database when the session lookup fails
userStories.description: ios/GradeThread/Persistence/SyncEngine.swift:367 does `let selfId = try? await ...auth.session.user.id`, swallowing the failure. At :430 that means the .eq('user_id', ...) filter is dropped, :438 treats the resulting zero rows as a complete result, and SyncMergeActor.reconcileDeletes:564 then prunes the entire local mirror. A transient session read failure wipes the user's offline data.
acceptanceCriteria: A failed session lookup aborts the sync rather than proceeding unfiltered.
reconcileDeletes refuses to prune when the fetch was not provably complete and scoped.
Test: a session-lookup failure leaves local data intact.
Check crash/analytics for users whose local item count dropped to zero.

OPERATOR: check Sentry and PostHog for users whose local item count dropped to zero (AC4). Correlate against the new breadcrumbs 'Sync reconcile aborted: tenant scope unresolved' and 'Sync reconcile refused: prune requested under an unresolved tenant scope'.
userStories.notes:
[P0][iOS/Sync] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Data loss on the customer's device. Highest-severity mobile finding. | 2026-08-04 VERIFIED against the code, and the failure path is real — with one narrowing that changes who it hits. THE CHAIN HOLDS EXACTLY AS FILED: SyncEngine.swift:367 is 'let selfId = try? await SupabaseShared.client.auth.session.user.id.uuidString', which swallows a throw into nil; :368 is 'let ownerId = WorkspaceScope.activeOwnerId ?? selfId'; :386-388 pass that ownerId into fetchServerIds for inventory_items, sales and flipdesk_expenses; and fetchServerIds:430 applies the tenant filter only under 'if let scopeUserId'. Nil scope means the query runs UNFILTERED. If it then returns zero rows, :438's short-page rule ('a short page means we've read every surviving id') treats an EMPTY set as a COMPLETE set, and reconcileDeletes prunes the local mirror against it. THE NARROWING, and it is the reason this has not been reported by users at scale: BOTH sources have to be nil. A user inside a workspace has WorkspaceScope.activeOwnerId set, so the filter still applies and the bug cannot fire. It fires for a solo seller on their personal scope whose session read transiently fails — which is the ordinary configuration, so this is not exotic. WHAT IS ALREADY DEFENDED, worth knowing so the fix is not duplicated: fetchServerIds returns nil (skip pruning) on any thrown error and on hitting maxRowsPerPass with rows remaining; :398 bails when ALL five fetches failed; :404 re-checks the scope epoch so a workspace switch mid-scan cannot prune the new tenant; protectedIds and protectedItemIds shield queued creates and pending edits. Every one of those guards handles a DIFFERENT failure. None of them covers 'authenticated as nobody, legitimately got zero rows' — an empty non-nil set passes the :398 guard cleanly. SMALLEST CORRECT FIX is AC1: make an unresolvable owner id abort the reconcile, since an unscoped id-scan is never something this function wants. AC2 is the belt-and-braces version and is also worth having. | PARTIAL 2026-08-06 — AC1, AC2 and AC3 are DONE in code; AC4 is an operator read of crash/analytics and cannot be done from here. THE ROOT FIX (AC1), at ios/GradeThread/Persistence/SyncEngine.swift: reconcileDeletesIfDue() and pullRemote() both used to do 'let ownerId = WorkspaceScope.activeOwnerId ?? selfId' and carry on when BOTH were nil. Both now go through a new pure static SyncEngine.resolveScopeOwnerId(workspaceOwnerId:sessionUserId:) and ABORT when it returns nil — the reconcile returns before any id-scan (and before lastReconcileAt is stamped, so the throttle is not burned and the very next pass retries), the pull returns .failure(SyncScopeError.unresolvedTenantScope) so it surfaces on the existing banner / lastPullError path instead of looking like an empty account. THE RESOLVER'S CONTRACT IS THE INTERESTING PART and is why it is a named function rather than an inline '??': a nil sessionUserId abandons the pass EVEN WHEN A WORKSPACE IS SELECTED. The story's narrowing said the bug needs both sources nil, which is true of the crash chain, but the underlying condition is that the session read failing means the requests go out UNAUTHENTICATED — so a workspace id would scope a query that returns nothing anyway. Scoping an unauthenticated read is not safer than not scoping it. A BLANK id is also treated as absent, because .eq('user_id','') matches nothing and produces the same empty set by a different route. AC2 IS DONE TWICE, DELIBERATELY, at two different altitudes. (a) Type level: fetchServerIds(table:scopeUserId:String?) became fetchServerIds(table:scope:ReadScope) with cases .owner(String) and .parentRLS. One nil used to mean two unrelated things — 'listings/item_photos have no user_id column' and 'the owner id did not resolve' — and only one of those is safe. Now a caller holding no id has nothing valid to pass; the dangerous state is unrepresentable rather than merely guarded. (b) Destructive site: SyncMergeActor.reconcileDeletes gains a NON-OPTIONAL leading scopeOwnerId: String and refuses to prune (breadcrumb, no deletes) when it is blank. That repeats the check where the deletes actually happen, so any future caller inherits the floor. AC3: 4 new XCTest cases in ios/GradeThreadTests/SyncTests.swift. The load-bearing one is test_reconcileDeletes_unresolvedScopeLeavesEveryTableIntact — every id set EMPTY (i.e. 'the server has nothing') plus a blank scope must leave items, sales and listings all intact; its control test_reconcileDeletes_resolvedScopeStillPrunesOnEmptySets asserts the SAME empty sets DO prune under a resolved scope, so the guard is proven to reject the unscoped case specifically rather than to have disabled reconciliation. Plus two on the resolver: failed-session-with-workspace returns nil, and workspace-then-self precedence with blank-falls-through. The five pre-existing reconcileDeletes call sites in that file were updated for the new parameter. VERIFICATION LIMITS, stated plainly: Swift cannot be built or tested on this Linux host (no toolchain), so these changes are NOT compile-verified here — iOS CI on macOS runners is the gate. What WAS run locally: python3 ios/Scripts/no-ungated-print.py passes, and a grep for name collisions on ReadScope / SyncScopeError / nonBlank / resolveScopeOwnerId across all of ios/ found none. NOT CHANGED, and worth knowing: paginatedFetch keeps its scopeUserId: String? because the disputes fetch legitimately passes selfId and the pull path is not the destructive one; the pull guard above means ownerId is non-nil everywhere it is used. REMAINING: AC4 only — check crash/analytics for users whose local item count dropped to zero. That is an operator read of Sentry/PostHog, not a code change; the new breadcrumbs ('Sync reconcile aborted: tenant scope unresolved' and 'Sync reconcile refused: prune requested under an unresolved tenant scope') give it something to correlate against going forward. | 2026-08-17 THE VERIFICATION LIMIT RECORDED ABOVE IS NARROWER THAN IT SAYS. That segment states only no-ungated-print.py was run, because the work was done on a Linux host. On this Windows box ALL SIX iOS source guards now run in about four seconds (node scripts/verify.mjs --ios): no ungated print, no default URLSession.shared, no raw JPEG encode, no new bare UI strings, no force unwrap, ATS not relaxed. 6/6 pass against the current tree, so the SyncEngine and SyncMergeActor changes clear every source-level gate this repo has. Swift still cannot be COMPILED here (macOS-only toolchain), so iOS CI remains the gate for anything that has to build; what changed is that five guards which were being deferred to CI no longer are. AND THE FIX WAS RE-READ RATHER THAN TRUSTED, since the note describing it was written by a session that could not run it: SyncEngine.swift:481 has the pure static resolveScopeOwnerId, both call sites go through it and abort (:379 the reconcile, :867 the pull returning SyncScopeError.unresolvedTenantScope), the ReadScope enum at :447 makes the dangerous nil unrepresentable with .owner(String) and .parentRLS, and SyncMergeActor.swift:576 carries the second check at the destructive site - a blank scopeOwnerId leaves a breadcrumb and returns before any delete. Both load-bearing tests exist by name (test_reconcileDeletes_unresolvedScopeLeavesEveryTableIntact and its control test_reconcileDeletes_resolvedScopeStillPrunesOnEmptySets) in a file carrying 82 test functions. STILL OPEN: AC4 only, and it is unchanged - an operator read of Sentry and PostHog for users whose local item count dropped to zero, correlated against the two new breadcrumbs. | COMPILATION SETTLED 2026-08-28. This note corrects one stale claim and changes nothing else about the story.

The notes above say some version of 'never been compiled' / 'iOS CI is the gate and it has not seen this' / 'cannot be verified from a Windows box'. That was true when written and is not true now. Every commit carrying this story's iOS code is an ancestor of iOS CI run 33139420556 on main (2026-08-28T03:37Z, head 1c6067106), conclusion SUCCESS - checked with git merge-base --is-ancestor, all commits in, none outside.

The run was checked for substance rather than for a green tick: both jobs succeeded, and the Build + test job's 'Generate Xcode project', 'Build + test' and 'Build app-extension targets' steps all executed. A green run whose build step never ran proves nothing.

ONE DISTINCTION MAKES THIS READABLE, and without it the evidence points the other way: many of these commits' OWN CI runs FAILED. 33 of the last 100 iOS CI runs on main were non-success, in one unbroken stretch from 2026-08-18 to 2026-08-27. iOS reports one error and stops, so a commit is not guilty of the failure it happens to sit on. 'Did its own run pass' has no useful answer; 'is it in a green build' does.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not close the story. Compilation was never the only thing outstanding here - what remains is whatever the notes above say it is, and it is now the ONLY thing outstanding, which is the point of writing this down. A story parked behind two blockers where one has quietly cleared reads as further away than it is.

THE CHECK IS TWO COMMANDS AND WORKS FROM WINDOWS: gh run list --workflow='iOS CI' --branch main to find the newest green run, then git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> <that run's head>. Any story blocked on 'iOS CI has not seen this' can be settled the same way once its commits are on main. macOS-only COMPILATION is not macOS-only KNOWLEDGE. | 2026-08-29 AC4/AC5 ATTEMPTED AGAINST REAL SENTRY, and the blocker is not the
one the criterion assumes. No code changed.

MEASURED 2026-08-29. This session has a connected Sentry account, so AC4/AC5
was worth ATTEMPTING rather than assuming an agent cannot read Sentry. It can
reach Sentry; it cannot reach THIS app's project, and the difference is a
permissions grant rather than a capability gap.

WHAT THE CONNECTED ACCOUNT SEES: one organization, `pearson-media-llc`
(regionUrl https://us.sentry.io), containing exactly ONE project, `react-native`,
with ZERO error events and zero issues over 90 days.

WHAT THE APP ACTUALLY REPORTS TO, read from the shipped bundle rather than from
a dashboard - the DSN is public and ships to every browser, so this is a plain
GET. Fetched https://gradethread.com/, followed its entry chunk, and found:

  https://<key>@o4510398791352320.ingest.us.sentry.io/4511508903362560

So the web client IS wired: a real DSN, a real org id, a real project id, in the
us region. That is the half people usually doubt, and it is fine.

AND QUERYING THAT PROJECT RETURNS 403. search_issues against project
4511508903362560 under pearson-media-llc answers 'HTTP 403: You do not have
permission to perform this action.' Not 404 and not empty - denied.

SO THE ZERO ABOVE PROVES NOTHING ABOUT GRADETHREAD. `react-native` is a
different project in a different product, and reading its emptiness as 'Sentry
receives nothing' would be exactly the kind of confident wrong answer this
backlog keeps recording. What is established is narrower and more useful: the
account this session holds cannot see the data.

⚠ THIS IS A CROSS-CUTTING UNBLOCK, not a note about one story. Every AC in the
backlog phrased 'OPERATOR: check Sentry' has the same shape, including US-2011
(Stripe webhook dead-letters alert only to Sentry, routing unverified) and
US-2003 (every alert channel is optional and silently no-ops). Granting this

'a human must go and look' into something an agent can answer and record.

ONE MORE THING WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ANYONE TRUSTS WHAT THEY FIND THERE:
production /health/ready currently reports `observability: set but not
satisfied` and `release: unattributable: release="unknown"`. That is US-2001,
still live - so even events that DO arrive cannot be tied to a commit.

WHAT THIS STORY STILL NEEDS is unchanged in substance: someone with access has
