userStories.title: Android: expense dates walk back one day on every edit-sync cycle
userStories.description: android/app/src/main/java/com/gradethread/app/money/ExpenseRepository.kt:128 sends ExpenseDraft.isoDate(entity.spentOn), which re-derives YYYY-MM-DD from a UTC-midnight epoch using ZoneId.systemDefault() (ExpenseDraft.kt:72). It is used for updates as well as inserts, so for any user west of UTC the date moves back one day each time the expense is edited and synced. iOS fixed exactly this as US-1494 at ios/GradeThread/Money/ExpenseStore.swift:34-43.
acceptanceCriteria: The stored calendar date is round-tripped as a date, never re-derived through the local timezone.
Port the iOS US-1494 approach.
Test with a device timezone west of UTC across several edit cycles.
Audit prod expense rows for dates that have drifted.

OPERATOR: audit prod expense rows for dates that already drifted (AC4). Note the drift is directional and COMPOUNDING - an affected row is off by one day per edit-sync cycle it went through, so it cannot be corrected by a single fixed offset. Only rows edited by a user in a negative-UTC-offset zone are affected.
userStories.notes: [P1][Android/Money] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Already solved on iOS — port, do not redesign. | 2026-08-04 VERIFIED, including the part that makes it embarrassing: the bug is DESCRIBED IN ITS OWN DOC COMMENT and was still shipped. ExpenseDraft.kt:69-71 says outright that re-deriving 'moves an evening expense to the next day east of Greenwich and to the previous day west of it', and :72-73 is exactly that — 'fun isoDate(epochMs: Long, zone: ZoneId = ZoneId.systemDefault()) = Instant.ofEpochMilli(epochMs).atZone(zone).toLocalDate().toString()'. ExpenseRepository.kt:129 calls it inside wireBody. CONFIRMED IT COVERS EDITS, which is the whole premise: wireBody has ONE caller, line 61, on a path that computes 'val id = draft.id ?: UUID.randomUUID()...' with the comment 'An edit keeps its id so the upsert replaces rather than duplicates' and then does client.from(TABLE).upsert(body). One code path for insert and edit, so every re-save re-derives, and the drift compounds per edit rather than settling. So AC3's 'across several edit cycles' is the right test shape. NOTE FOR AC2: iOS solved this at ExpenseStore.swift:34-43 — port that, and check whether the Android ExpenseEntity should carry the calendar date as a string rather than an epoch at all, since as long as the local column is epoch-millis the conversion has to happen somewhere and can be got wrong again. | 2026-08-12 AC1/AC2/AC3 DONE (d660095e). THE MECHANISM: spent_on is a date-only column and spentOn is a Long carrying a CALENDAR DATE, not a moment. The round trip was split across two zones - RealtimeService.parseTimestamp parses the server's bare date at UTC midnight, and isoDate formatted it back in the DEVICE zone. Chicago is UTC-5, so UTC midnight on the 12th is 19:00 on the 11th: the edit wrote the 11th, the next pull parsed the 11th, the next edit wrote the 10th. wireBody serves insert and edit from one path, which is why it compounded per save rather than being a one-off. THE FIX IS ONE NAMED CONSTANT, ExpenseDraft.EXPENSE_ZONE = UTC, and every reader moved onto it: entry (ExpenseFormSheet), display (MoneyScreen.formatDate), the wire format (isoDate), and month bucketing in BOTH MoneyViewModel and MoneyAnalyticsRollup.cashFlow. A device-zone read of any one of them re-opens the drift, which is why it is a constant rather than a default argument. AC2 SATISFIED AS A PORT, exactly as it asks: iOS settled this in US-1494 with ExpenseStore.bucketingCalendar, a UTC calendar whose comment says parsing and bucketing must happen in the same zone. Same bug, same answer, reached independently on the two platforms. cashFlow needed expenses given their OWN month boundaries - a sale date is a real moment and belongs in the device zone, an expense date does not. One zone for both was the bug in miniature. NO ROOM MIGRATION: the column still stores epoch ms; only the zone convention changed. That is why this did not need the ISO-string column the story offered as an option. ONE OF MY OWN ASSERTIONS WAS WRONG BEFORE THE CODE WAS. I asserted the wire value must DIFFER from the device reading - true in Chicago, FALSE in Berlin, which is east of Greenwich where UTC midnight is still the same date. Only a negative-offset zone shifts it. It failed against correct code, which is how I caught it. The note in the test now names which case is runner-independent: a round trip leaning on the DEFAULT zone passes on a UTC CI machine while the bug is live for every seller who is not on UTC. Sabotage reverting EXPENSE_ZONE to systemDefault() reddens all four cases. VERIFIED: testDebugUnitTest 1866 pass, lintDebug, no-bare-strings, no-ungated-log, check-string-formats. AC4 REMAINS and is not agent work: a prod audit for rows that already drifted. Note the drift is directional and compounding, so an affected row's error equals the number of edit-sync cycles it has been through - it cannot be corrected by a single fixed offset. | 2026-08-17 AC4 IS NOW ONE COMMAND, and the reason it sat open is that nobody had worked out what could actually be detected. scripts/audit-expense-date-drift.mjs; set RETENTION_DB_URL to point it at production, and it refuses to print anything without a database rather than showing an unchecked list as a checked one.  THERE IS AN EXACT SIGNAL AND IT IS THE RECURRING CHILDREN. monthlyDueDates() puts a child on min(template day, days in that month) and NEVER on the previous occurrence - the anti-drift rule lives in the generator. So a child sitting on any other day is a date the generator could not have produced. That is arithmetic, not a threshold, and it is the only certain detection available here.  AND A BOUND THAT MAKES THE REST USABLE: a row whose updated_at still matches its created_at has been saved once and CANNOT have drifted, however far back its date looks - drift only happens on re-save, because wireBody serves insert and edit from one path. The script leads with that split, so the operator sees the size of the at-risk population before any list.  WHAT IT REFUSES TO DO, stated in the tool itself. Standalone expenses have no ground truth: a seller entering last month's receipts backdates legitimately and nothing distinguishes that from three drift cycles. It prints the distribution, labels it NOT A FINDING, and does not invent a cutoff. It also does not repair anything - the error compounds, so there is no single offset, and a guessing repair would swap a wrong date for a differently wrong one while making it look reviewed.  PROVEN AGAINST SEEDED DATA, five cases, including the two that matter most:   - a clean child on its generated day was NOT flagged   - a child three days back WAS flagged, delta -3d, marked re-saved   - an off-day child that was NEVER re-saved was flagged AND labelled 'not this bug'   - a 31st-anchored template's February child on the 28th was NOT flagged. That is the case a     naive check gets wrong, and getting it wrong would put every end-of-month recurring     expense on a remediation list.   - the standalone distribution printed with its caveat Fixture removed afterwards and the table confirmed back to 0 rows.  8 unit tests on the arithmetic (scripts/audit-expense-date-drift.test.mjs, in npm run test:scripts - 513 passing across 35 suites). Sabotage-verified: removing the end-of-month clamp reddens three of them.  ⚠ THE FIX IS CLIENT-SIDE so it lands per seller as they update the app. A device on an older build KEEPS DRIFTING. Run the audit after the release has had time to roll out, and run it more than once. That is now written in the tool's header and in the vault note.  vault/20-domain/expense-date-is-a-calendar-date.md owns the convention - EXPENSE_ZONE on Android, bucketingCalendar on iOS, one rule - so the third platform does not rediscover it.  AC4 STILL NEEDS A HUMAN because nothing here holds prod credentials. It is a single command now instead of an open question. | 2026-08-22 AC1-AC3 CONFIRMED DONE BY RUNNING THEM, not by reading the diff. AC4/AC5 remain operator and genuinely so.  AC1/AC2 THE FIX IS IN. ExpenseDraft declares EXPENSE_ZONE and its comment states the rule as 'UTC, everywhere, always'; isoDate(epochMs, zone = EXPENSE_ZONE) defaults to it instead of ZoneId.systemDefault(), and ExpenseRepository.kt:128 goes through it for the wire value. That is the iOS US-1494 approach (anchor the date-only column in one fixed zone rather than re-deriving it through whatever zone the device is in), ported.  AC3 IS SATISFIED AND IS BETTER THAN THE AC ASKED FOR. It asked for a test with a device timezone west of UTC across several edit cycles. ExpenseDraftTest runs three edit cycles across THREE device zones on both sides of Greenwich - America/Chicago (west, the failing case), Pacific/Auckland and Europe/Berlin - with the stated reason that a test leaning on the DEFAULT zone would pass on a UTC CI machine while the bug was live for every seller not on UTC, which is exactly where it would never be caught.  ONE THING IN THAT TEST IS WORTH KEEPING as a general note: it records an assertion that was DROPPED for being wrong rather than weak. 'the wire date differs from the device reading' looks like the stronger claim and fails against correct code on the Berlin case, because Berlin is EAST of Greenwich and UTC midnight on the 12th is still the 12th there. Only a negative-offset zone shifts the date at all. The runner-independent guarantee is the explicit EXPENSE_ZONE == ZoneOffset.UTC case instead.  EXECUTED, NOT CACHED, and the distinction matters after US-2776: a first gradle run there reported BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1s with every task UP-TO-DATE, which is not a test result. This was forced with cleanTestDebugUnitTest, and the XML proves it: TEST-com.gradethread.app.money.ExpenseDraftTest.xml, timestamp 2026-08-22T06:23:39Z, tests=11 failures=0 errors=0 skipped=0.  AC4/AC5 STAY OPERATOR, and I tried to shorten them before saying so. scripts/audit-expense-date-drift.mjs takes RETENTION_DB_URL for the prod audit and otherwise falls back to `docker exec supabase_db_gradethread`, which is a DRY RUN against the throwaway stack and proves nothing about production rows. The drift signal it uses is per-user expense data behind RLS, so the anon PostgREST read that answered the pricing and schema questions elsewhere in this backlog cannot reach it - this one really is a database session. The script already refuses to print anything without a database rather than showing an unchecked list as a checked one.  WHAT IS STILL UNTESTED HERE, said plainly: nobody has edited a real expense on a real device west of UTC and watched the date hold. The maths is asserted across three zones and eleven cases; the device is not.

userStories.title: Run the production verification queries this audit could not run
userStories.description: Several audit findings cannot be scored without reading production state, and this session had no prod access (the Supabase MCP connector is unauthorized). Doing these first prevents building the wrong fix.
acceptanceCriteria: SELECT proname, proacl FROM pg_proc WHERE pronamespace='public'::regnamespace AND prosecdef; — how many SECURITY DEFINER functions are world-callable.
Actual applied schema version, to settle the 00504-00506 held-migration question.
Does grading_eval_cases have any rows, and which ai_prompt_versions rows are active with what qualified_model.
Does users_billing_source_chk still exclude 'googleplay', and has any Play purchase ever succeeded.
Do the three dead cron schedules exist in Coolify, and what do their run histories show.
Are ops_alert_webhook_url and ops_alert_email set in system_settings, and is PGRST_DB_MAX_ROWS set on the stack.
Are EBAY_TOKEN_REVOKE_URL and EBAY_CATEGORY_TREE_ID set; what is EDGE_ENV in staging and is WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG on.
Record every answer in this story so the dependent stories can be scored.

OPERATOR: this whole story is prod reads (AC1-AC8). Most of it is already written up as scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql, which is read-only and was executed against a real database with ON_ERROR_STOP=1 so it cannot fail your session on a wrong column name. Run it and paste the output back into this story.
userStories.notes: [P0][Ops/Verification] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Blocks accurate sizing of at least eight other stories in this batch. Human-run, not code. | 2026-08-03 SCOPED AND HALF-ANSWERED. The owner ran the diagnostics and it settled AC2 outright: highest applied version is 00523, an unbroken run with no gap, so the 00504-00506 held-migration question is closed. THREE MORE ACs ARE NOW IN THE SCRIPT rather than waiting on a separate ask — NEW sections 14, 15 and 16 cover AC1 (SECURITY DEFINER functions callable by PUBLIC, reading proacl IS NULL, since a NULL acl on a function IS execute-to-PUBLIC and therefore the dangerous case rather than the safe one), AC3 (golden-set size plus which prompt versions are live and whether they were eval-gated) and AC4 (the users_billing_source_chk definition, plus whether any non-default billing source has ever been written). Verified end to end against a real database with ON_ERROR_STOP. AC5 and AC7 CANNOT go in this script and are named as operator checks rather than left implied: Coolify scheduled tasks and edge env vars are not database state. AC6 is half in (section 11, ops_alert rows) and half not (PGRST_DB_MAX_ROWS is a stack setting, though US-2169 already measured no row cap at or below 1055 by probing). AC8 is what the story notes now are. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-08: every migration this story names — 00504, 00506, 00523 — is on origin/main, so none of them is held. The held-migration wording above is the QUESTION the story was asked to settle, and the 2026-08-03 segment already records that the owner settled it (applied version 00523, unbroken run, no gap). Both texts coexist because the notes are append-only; this segment exists so prd-lint stops reporting a story whose hold question is closed, and so the next reader does not read the older wording as a live freeze. | 2026-08-16 THE FILE HAS NOW BEEN EXECUTED END TO END, and it did not survive the first run. Docker came up on this box, so scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql was run against a throwaway local stack (supabase db reset, built from the migration corpus, all 609 applied) under ON_ERROR_STOP=1. It ABORTED at line 985 with ERROR: array_agg is an aggregate function.  THE DEFECT, and it fails on EVERY Postgres rather than on some data shape. S22(e) asked which functions mention storefront and was written as FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ... WHERE n.nspname='public' AND (proname ILIKE ... OR pg_get_functiondef(p.oid) ILIKE ...). pg_get_functiondef RAISES on an aggregate, and a namespace filter expressed as a JOIN narrows nothing the planner is obliged to apply first - so the call landed on pg_catalog's aggregates. Under ON_ERROR_STOP=1 that abandons every remaining section: the operator gets a dead prod session instead of an answer. Same failure this file's own header promises it cannot cause, and the same class as the SHOW supautils.hint_roles bug caught on 2026-08-15 - which is the point: two for two, both invisible to review, both trivial to catch by running it once.  THE FIX is a MATERIALIZED CTE narrowing to prokind='f' before the call. MATERIALIZED is an optimization fence (PG12+), so it is a guarantee rather than a hope about qual ordering; pronamespace='public'::regnamespace replaces the join so the restriction sits on the same relation as the call.  AFTER THE FIX: exit 0, all 27 sections ran, 1021 lines of output. Console variant regenerated from source, still in sync.  TWO NEW GUARD CASES in src/test/prod-diagnostics-safety.test.ts (12 passing): pg_get_functiondef must have a MATERIALIZED prokind='f' narrowing ABOVE it and must not sit downstream of a JOIN pg_namespace; and the section count is pinned at 27 so adding one is a visible prompt to re-run the file by hand. The header claim that neither property 'is checkable by running it' is CORRECTED in place: true of prod, and it had quietly become an argument for never executing the file anywhere.  THE FIRST WRITING OF THE NEW GUARD FAILED ON CORRECT SQL - it searched the raw text and matched the comment paragraph that names pg_get_functiondef while explaining the trap, finding it before the real call site. Comments are stripped first now. Same shape as the bug being guarded: a filter that looks like it applies and does not.  SABOTAGE-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS, each reverted green: dropping MATERIALIZED, dropping the prokind filter, reverting to the JOIN form, and adding a 28th section.  STILL OPEN: unchanged. AC1-AC8 are prod READS and this story is operator work - nothing here touched prod. What changed is that the paste is now known to run to completion instead of assumed to. | 2026-08-17 THE PREMISE IS OUT OF DATE AND THAT IS THE USEFUL PART. This story opens 'this session had no prod access', and several of its questions turn out to be answerable from UNAUTHENTICATED, READ-ONLY endpoints. Nothing below required a credential or wrote anything.  AC2 SETTLED. Applied schema version: GET functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns schema {expected 00609, applied 00609, status match} with NO missing key - and the absence of that key is the evidence, because it is emitted only when the applied SET is incomplete. So the 00504-00506 held-migration question this AC was filed to settle is closed: nothing is missing beneath the maximum. (That distinction is not theoretical - it is exactly how 00594 hid, per US-2606.)  AC1 HALF SETTLED, and the half that is settled is the one that matters. The full pg_proc/proacl census still needs prod. But the MECHANISM is now proven and the answer is worse than the question assumed: REVOKE ... FROM anon is a NO-OP (US-2666, proven three ways in a rolled-back transaction), so counting revokes in migrations tells you nothing about what is world-callable. Confirmed against PRODUCTION by a single anon POST: flipdesk_overview_metrics answers HTTP 200 to the public anon key while its migration has revoked it from anon since the day it was written. On the local stack built from all 609 migrations, 146 of 175 public functions are anon-executable.  AC6 HALF SETTLED. features.alerting reads 'ok - at least one channel is CONFIGURED', so the ops_alert_* settings are present. The line says outright that it does not prove a message ARRIVES, and that half still needs a human. PGRST_DB_MAX_ROWS is NOT answerable this way - see the failed attempt below.  AC7 PARTLY SETTLED. features.ebay reads 'ok', so the eBay vars are set. EDGE_ENV was set to the literal 'production' by the owner on 2026-08-16 (US-2660). The staging EDGE_ENV and WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG are NOT established - I can see no endpoint that reports either, and the boot-time [SECURITY] warning for a debug flag under production goes to logs rather than to /health/ready.  ⚠ AC3 AND AC6's ROW CAP ARE NOT ANSWERABLE AS ANON, and I nearly recorded that they were. GET /rest/v1/grading_eval_cases returned [] and help_articles returned content-range */0. Both are HTTP 200 and both look like an answer. They are not: RLS filters anon to zero rows on a protected table, so [] means 'you may not see any' rather than 'there are none'. And the row-cap probe is worthless against a table that is genuinely empty - it needs a table with more rows than the cap. This is the same shape as everything else tonight: an empty result that reads as a finding.  WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT FOR AC9's OPERATOR RUN, narrowed from seven questions to four: the proacl census (AC1's other half), grading_eval_cases + active ai_prompt_versions (AC3), users_billing_source_chk against PROD's catalog rather than a fresh local build (AC4 - the local stack proves the migrations CONVERGE, not that prod matches, and 00104's IF NOT EXISTS probe is precisely why those differ), and the Coolify cron histories (AC5).  THE TRANSFERABLE BIT: /health/ready is a much richer prod read than this story assumed, and PostgREST's OpenAPI document (Accept: application/openapi+json, anon key) answers RPC signature questions without calling anything. Before marking a prod question operator-only, check whether one of those two already answers it. | 2026-08-17 THE OPERATOR QUEUE NOW CLASSIFIES 74 OF 83 ITEMS, up from 57. Recorded here because this story is the one that exists to get operator work actually DONE, and an unreadable queue is the thing standing in the way.  prd-operator.mjs --sessions grouped 83 items into six sittings and dropped 26 into "unclassified". Reading those 26 by hand - which is what the loop kept having to do - showed they were not unclassifiable, they were three kinds the tool had no name for, plus four near-misses.  THREE NEW SITTINGS, each anchored to phrasing read out of the live backlog rather than invented: (7) COUNSEL REVIEW - legal wording, where every one of the five stories says in its own criteria that an agent must not draft the language, so no amount of code closes them; (8) SOURCING - reference imagery, brand data, screenshots, golden-set labels, where the mechanism is built and the content is missing; (9) ROOT ON THE HOST - disk encryption, installing the backup cron, moving a key off the machine it protects, which need shell access rather than a dashboard and so are not the config pass.  FOUR NEAR-MISSES WIDENED: "after deploy" without "the next"; Stripe TEST MODE; "a real browser and a person" and "with the product open"; and the four [OPERATOR]-titled stories whose evidence text is empty.  RESULT: unclassified 26 -> 9. The nine that remain are genuinely mixed cases, which is what that bucket should mean.  ⚠ AND THE WAY I BROKE IT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING, because this repo already documents the trap and I walked into it anyway. The new patterns were written through an inline shell heredoc, which ATE a backslash: every \b was written to the file as U+0008, a real backspace control character. Everything looked fine - the source reads correctly in an editor and in grep, node -c passes, the module imports - and a regex whose source prints as /(counsel|...)/i returned FALSE for the string "counsel". Three sittings silently matched nothing.  CLAUDE.md forbids invisible characters in source for exactly this reason, and the memory note "Escapes in a Bash argument are EATEN" prescribes the fix: a scratchpad .mjs, not an inline heredoc. Every edit after that point went through one.  TWO GUARDS SO IT CANNOT RECUR: no session pattern may contain a character below U+0020, and every pattern must match a probe phrase it is supposed to match - because a pattern matching nothing is indistinguishable from a missing one, which is the exact state the bug produced. A third pins that the sitting numbers run in array order, since the array order IS the running order. Sabotage-verified by reintroducing the control character: both fire.  VERIFIED: 15 cases in prd-operator.test.mjs (3 new), all green. | 2026-08-17 (second pass) THE QUEUE NOW CLASSIFIES 80 OF 83. Unclassified went 26 -> 9 -> 3, and every placement was checked by hand against the phrase that matched it rather than trusted from the count.  TWO MORE FIXES. (1) THE TITLE IS MATCHED TOO. Four [OPERATOR]-prefixed stories carry their whole instruction in the title and have NO evidence text, so the matcher had literally nothing to read - they were unclassifiable because nobody had given them anything to classify. (2) "restricted scopes" plural: US-1421 title says scopes, the pattern said scope, and the word boundary refused it.  THIRD-PARTY NOW RUNS FIRST, and that is a scheduling decision rather than a tidy-up. The title fallback initially put Depop and Etsy go-live into the CONFIG pass, because both titles say "set DEPOP_ENABLED" - technically true and practically a lie, since what blocks them is partner approval and no amount of config reaches it. A queue that misfiles is worse than one that admits it does not know, which is this file own principle. Every other sitting is work the operator finishes in one go; this one is a REQUEST to somebody else with days of lead time, so it is started first and the wait is spent on the other eight. The header sentence that named SQL as "first because cheapest" was rewritten rather than left to contradict the array.  ⚠ AND PROMOTING IT EXPOSED A SECOND-ORDER BUG, which is the part worth keeping: running first means winning every tie, and a bare vendor NAME is not an action. US-2001 got pulled into "third-party consoles" on the word Sentry - but its operator work is a Coolify build variable, and Sentry appears only as the thing that BENEFITS from a real release tag. Sending the operator to the wrong system is worse than leaving the item unclassified. The vendor names now have to appear as a place you GO ("check Sentry", "Sentry dashboard", "Apple support"), and all fourteen third-party items were re-read one by one to confirm each matched on a real action.  THE THREE THAT REMAIN are genuinely three different one-off kinds - reading EXIF off storage objects, an alert-delivery drill, and picking an experiment to run - and inventing a sitting for each would be worse than admitting it.  ONE MORE SELF-INFLICTED LESSON, recorded because it is the same class as the backspace bug an hour earlier: my first probe phrase for "a vendor named in passing" was "unattributable in Sentry", which contains the literal string "in Sentry" - the exact place-you-go form the rule is built on. The test failed and it was RIGHT to. A probe has to be checked against the rule as carefully as the rule is checked against the corpus.  VERIFIED: 18 cases in prd-operator.test.mjs (3 new), all green. | 2026-08-18 CI HAS BEEN RED ON main AND THE THIRD CAUSE IS NOW FIXED. Recorded here because this story is about getting blocked work actually done, and a red lane that nobody reads is the same failure at the CI layer.  CHECKED AFTER PUSHING TODAY WORK, and the run before this session (be221430, "feat(photo-manager)") had THREE distinct failures in the frontend job:   1. "deno: not found" - the scripts test lane shells out to deno run scripts/*.ts   2. .or() applied to a mutation - one guard failing another guard on its documentation   3. prd-archive-integrity - completed stories left in the active file  TWO OF THE THREE WERE FIXED EARLIER TODAY, before I had any idea they were CI failures: the guard-on-guard false positive and the archive. Both were found locally by running the full lane rather than a directory, which is the same lesson twice.  THE THIRD IS FIXED HERE and it predates everything: the frontend job runs npm run test:scripts, several of those tests invoke deno run scripts/*.ts because the operator scripts are Deno, and the job never installed Deno. Every such test failed with "/bin/sh: 1: deno: not found" and took the lane down.  INSTALLED RATHER THAN SKIPPED. Making the tests skip when Deno is absent would turn a guard that checks operator scripts print a usage line into one that only ever runs on a developer laptop - the exact shape this repo keeps naming. denoland/setup-deno@v2 pinned to 2.8.0, matching security.yml and money-cert-integration.yml, so one Deno behaviour change cannot pass one lane and fail another.  ⚠ WORTH SAYING PLAINLY: my local `node scripts/verify.mjs --web` passed all 14 checks while CI failed, and the difference is not a flaw in verify.mjs - it is that this box HAS Deno on PATH and the runner did not. A local lane can only ever prove the code, never the runner. That is the second time today a green local run has meant less than it looked (the first was running a directory instead of the lane).  VERIFIED: ci.yml parses (24 steps in the build job, setup-deno at index 4, immediately after npm ci and before anything that shells out); npm run test:scripts 550 passed. | 2026-08-18 CONFIRMED GREEN. Every workflow on 1acfde67 passed: CI (frontend lane AND E2E), iOS CI (build + test and the UI critical-flow job), Security, Static analysis, Tenant Isolation, Money & Certificate Integration, Secret scan, IndexNow.  THAT CLOSES THE LOOP ON A CLAIM RATHER THAN REPEATING IT. The three frontend failures recorded earlier - deno not found, the guard failing another guard on its documentation, and completed stories left in the active file - are all confirmed fixed by a run that actually finished, not by local lanes agreeing with themselves.  ⚠ AND THE REASON IT TOOK SO LONG TO SEE IS WORTH KEEPING: I was cancelling my own evidence. Every push cancels the run in flight, and I had been pushing faster than CI completes - four consecutive CI runs show "cancelled", including the one that would first have proven the Deno fix. The fix was correct at 02:13 and unverified until 02:38, entirely because of my cadence. On a repo where the answer takes seven minutes, pushing again before reading is the same mistake as not looking.  ALSO CONFIRMED BY THE SAME RUN: the two tenant-isolation cases added for the unread-count route pass, and the E2E lane - which has not been run locally this session at all - is green. | 2026-08-23 THE READ-ONLY PROMISE THIS STORY RESTS ON WAS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKED, AND IS NOW TIGHTER. Commit 1d1b44b21. Nothing in prod-diagnostics-console.sql was ever unsafe - the finding is about the CHECK, not the file - but AC9 sends the operator to paste that file into a production SQL editor on the strength of it, so it is worth recording here rather than only in the test.  THE TWO COPIES WERE CHECKED AGAINST TWO DIFFERENT STANDARDS. src/test/prod-diagnostics-safety.test.ts checked the psql file against twelve write verbs and the CONSOLE file against six. TRUNCATE, GRANT, REVOKE, COPY, VACUUM and REINDEX were forbidden in the file that runs through a client and permitted in the file a person pastes by hand - the weaker check guarding the more dangerous path. Appending `truncate public.users;` to the console copy left the whole suite green.  AND SELECT INTO WALKED PAST BOTH. `select * into public.scratch from public.users` creates a table and names none of the banned verbs. The table is the smaller half: the copy it leaves behind carries user rows and has no RLS, because nothing declared any. Both files now also refuse DO blocks, since a procedural block can assemble a write verb from string pieces no keyword scan will see - the sabotage that used one was caught only because it happened to spell TRUNCATE in a literal.  ONE LIST NOW, used by both. Ten mutations, each applied and each RED with a green control either side: a plain UPDATE, a lowercase delete, a write inside a CTE, SELECT INTO on each copy, a DO block, and TRUNCATE / GRANT / UPDATE against the console file.  WHY IT MATTERS TO THIS STORY SPECIFICALLY: AC9 is the instruction to paste, and the file's own header already argues that the review establishing read-only 'happens once while the file changes many times'. That argument applies to the test too, which is what this pass found. The console copy the operator will paste is unchanged and verified read-only under the stricter list.  UNCHANGED: every AC here is still a prod read and still needs you. Nothing was answered by this pass. | [2026-09-02][PROD READ] The whole story ran. Source: scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql run read-only against prod over SSH on 2026-09-02 (container supabase-db-kcksoks4kk0kswk0ccs40os8, 29 sections, 0 SQL errors). Raw output kept out of the repo; it contains customer data. AC1: 120 SECURITY DEFINER functions in public; the default-ACL PUBLIC census returns 0, but has_function_privilege says anon can EXECUTE 100 of the 120 and authenticated the same 100 - see the US-2282 note and the new story filed for the eight credit functions. AC2: recorded schema version is 00721 and the footer era runs 00254..00721 across 464 rows, but the sequence is NOT contiguous: gaps at 00527 (parked .BLOCKED by owner decision, expected), 00636-00637 and 00689. The 00504-00506 held-migration question is settled - they are recorded. AC3: grading_eval_cases is EMPTY (0 rows, 0 active, 0 not-deleted), so the golden set does not exist in prod; ai_prompt_versions holds 4 rows (listing_gen_v2, listing_gen_v1, per_image_v2, composite_v2) and every one is is_active false, is_shadow false, is_canary false, rollout 0, with eval_passed and qualified_model both blank - nothing is serving from the DB, so the code default is the live prompt. AC4: users_billing_source_chk now reads stripe/appstore/googleplay, so it no longer excludes Play; billing_source is NULL for all 44 users, so no purchase of any source has ever been written. AC5-AC7 are Coolify/env reads, not database reads, and stay operator.

userStories.title: Impersonation is unbounded, unmarked, non-revocable, and allows account deletion as the user
userStories.description: admin-impersonation.ts:43-132 gets the entry right: super_admin only (:44), users:role scope (:38), fresh step-up (:49), self and privileged targets refused (:54, :68-73), start audited (:116). Everything after the token is minted is open. No time limit — generateLink type magiclink (:90) yields a normal Supabase session for the target, access token plus long-lived refresh token, in the admin's browser, with no cap anywhere. No revocation on stop — src/lib/impersonation.ts:126-129 only redeems the resume token and never calls auth.admin.signOut(targetId), so a copied refresh token outlives the session. No marker — there is no impersonated_by claim and no server-side active-impersonation row, so every request made while impersonating is indistinguishable from the real user's. And destructive actions are fully available: POST /api/account/delete's only server-side control is the confirm string (account.ts:390); the password re-auth at :625-631 is client-side only. A super_admin can impersonate a disputing customer, cancel their subscription and delete their account, and every downstream record shows the customer did it.
acceptanceCriteria: A hard maximum impersonation duration, enforced server-side.
Stopping impersonation revokes the target's sessions.

The impersonated session carries a server-visible marker, and destructive routes (account delete, subscription cancel, marketplace disconnect, grading spend) refuse or require additional authorization while it is set.
The account-delete password re-auth moves server-side.
PRIVILEGED_ROLES (:40) is {admin, super_admin} so a reviewer can be impersonated — decide whether that is intended.
admin-impersonation.ts:137 writes target_id straight from the request body with no check against the start record, so the stop audit row is client-controlled. Fix.
Confirm the GoTrue OTP TTL in prod — it sets the real lifetime of the impersonation and resume tokens.

userStories.notes: [P0][Admin/Security] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. A target's own MFA does not protect them: a magiclink redemption yields an aal1 session. | PARTIAL 2026-08-03 — AC1-AC6 DONE. AC7 is an operator check on prod and stays open. EVERY CLAIM VERIFIED. The entry really is well guarded and the story says so; everything after the token was minted really was open. Confirmed line by line: no cap anywhere, /stop only redeemed the admin's resume token, no marker of any kind, and the stop audit row read target_id straight from the request body. AC1 DONE. NEW admin_impersonation_sessions (00521) plus lib/impersonation-session.ts. Cap is 30 minutes, ENFORCED ON READ rather than by a scheduled sweep — the window between a cap passing and a job noticing is exactly when a forgotten session is most dangerous. And a start that cannot be RECORDED does not happen: a failed insert returns 500 and mints nothing, because a session with no row is precisely the unbounded, unmarked, unrevocable one this story removes. AC2 DONE. /stop revokes the target's sessions through GoTrue's admin logout with scope global. supabase-js cannot do this — auth.admin.signOut wants a JWT, which is the one thing the server does not have — and 'global' is the only scope that reaches a refresh token already copied out of the browser. The result is RETURNED rather than swallowed: an un-revoked stop means the target's tokens are still live and the operator needs to know now. AC3 DONE. The marker is a database row, not a token claim, deliberately: a claim is equally invisible to any route that does not parse it and cannot be revoked once minted. isImpersonated FAILS CLOSED — a lookup error returns true, so a database blip refuses the destructive action. Being wrong that way costs a real user one retry; being wrong the other way is unrecoverable. Guarded by ENUMERATION at eight sites (account delete, buyer + flipdesk subscription cancel, billing portal, and all five marketplace disconnects) rather than by a blanket middleware, which would have to enumerate what is destructive anyway and would silently permit anything it did not know about — the same failure shape US-2354 removed from the scope guard. AC4 DONE. The delete password re-auth moves into the edge, against GoTrue's password grant, and fails CLOSED: an unreachable auth service means the password cannot be proved, and 'cannot prove' must not read as 'proved' on the one endpoint that permanently destroys an account. It deliberately does NOT use the service-role client, which would mint a session — a successful check must prove the password and produce nothing reusable. The browser's local check is REMOVED rather than kept alongside: two places deciding the same thing is how one drifts, and the browser's answer was never the one that mattered. OAuth accounts are exempt on both sides; demanding a password that does not exist is not a control. AC5 DECIDED: reviewer joins PRIVILEGED_ROLES. The set means 'roles whose account carries authority a super_admin should not be able to borrow', not 'roles above a line in the ladder'. A reviewer holds grading:review — they adjust issued grades, which are the product, and RLS grants them human_reviews through is_reviewer_or_admin(). Impersonating one produces a grade adjustment audited to the reviewer rather than to the admin who made it: the same non-repudiation loss the admin exclusion exists to prevent. AC6 DONE: the stop record comes from the START row. The old shape let an admin impersonate one person and log having stopped impersonating another, which is worse than no row because it reads as evidence. A stop with no live session is still audited, with no_active_session set — a double-click and a probe both look like that, and both are worth seeing. PROVEN ON A REAL DATABASE: corpus applied to a throwaway stack, then the target cannot SELECT the row, cannot UPDATE it to end their own impersonation record (0 rows), and the record survives deleting BOTH parties with the emails intact. That last one matters — the record of an impersonation is not the impersonator's to erase. TWO GUARDS CAUGHT MY NEW CODE, both correctly. rls-guard demanded the new table be classified in SERVICE_ROLE_ONLY (deny-all in both directions: a readable table leaks operator activity to the person being impersonated, a writable one lets them end the RECORD while the session continues). no-bare-fetch caught both new outbound calls having no deadline — the GoTrue logout runs while an admin waits on /stop, and the password check is the last thing between a request and a permanent deletion. Both go through fetchWithTimeout now. COLUMN NAMING, worth recording: actor_id / target_id rather than actor_user_id / target_user_id, because rls-guard discovers tenant tables by the literal string user_id and this is an operator table that must have no policy at all. Added to the service-role-tables note as a worked example — the existing rule covers ONE owner column and says to call it owner_user_id, which does not help when there are two. A MISTAKE THAT KEEPS RECURRING, so it is written down: my first AC4 assertion searched for the word signInWithPassword and fired on my own comment explaining what the old local check used to do. Second time this session a guard has accused its own prose. It matches a CALL now. NEW services/edge-functions/src/tests/impersonation-bounds_test.ts, 10 cases. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED THREE WAYS (stop reading the body again, isImpersonated failing open, the guard dropped from one marketplace route), each restored. Vault: NEW vault/20-domain/impersonation.md carries the contract. REMAINING: AC7 — confirm the GoTrue OTP TTL in prod. It sets the real lifetime of the minted impersonation and resume tokens, so it is a SECOND clock running alongside the 30-minute cap: the cap bounds what the server honours, the TTL bounds how long the link stays redeemable. Both should be known. VERIFIED: deno check clean, deno lint clean across 1317 files, edge suite 5206 passed / 0 failed, web 3225 passed / 0 failed, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, build green through the 216-route prerender, vault-lint 135 notes clean. | 2026-08-03 FOLLOW-UP on AC5. The decision landed but its REFUSAL MESSAGE did not: adding reviewer to PRIVILEGED_ROLES left the 403 saying "Impersonating an admin or super-admin is not allowed", so a refused reviewer was told about a rule that was not the one applied. That is not cosmetic — the next operator reads a message that disagrees with the code, concludes the check is broken, and goes hunting a bug that is not there. The message now names all three roles and says WHY (their actions audit to them, not to you), and the new test asserts it against PRIVILEGED_ROLES itself rather than a fixed string, so the two cannot drift apart again. AND THE GUARD WAS SATISFIED BY ITS OWN PROSE — a new variant of the recurring trap. My first version checked the raw source slice, which includes the explanatory comment above the message, and that comment names every role: reverting to the stale message left the case GREEN, passing on prose about the very bug it was written to catch. Only the negative verification found it; the assertion read as correct. It strips comments now. Previous instances of this family accused their own prose; this one was SATISFIED by it, which is the more dangerous direction because nothing fails. AC7 remains and is an OPERATOR/CONFIG check, not a database one: the GoTrue OTP TTL is an env var on the self-hosted auth container (GOTRUE_MAILER_OTP_EXP), so it cannot be added to prod-diagnostics.sql. It matters because it is a SECOND clock — the 30-minute cap bounds what the server honours, the TTL bounds how long the minted link stays redeemable, and the longer of the two is the real exposure. VERIFIED: deno check clean, deno lint clean across 1338 files, full edge suite 5332 passed / 0 failed. | 2026-08-16 AC7 IS NARROWED TO ONE READ, and two properties behind it are now measured rather than assumed. Everything below comes from a running GoTrue and Postgres (the local Supabase stack), not from documentation.  (1) THE VARIABLE NAME IS CONFIRMED FROM A RUNNING CONTAINER, not from docs: GOTRUE_MAILER_OTP_EXP is present in the auth container's environment (locally 3600, set from config.toml's otp_expiry). GOTRUE_SMS_OTP_EXP exists alongside it and is a different clock; the impersonation path is email magiclink, so MAILER is the one that matters.  (2) READING IT IS SUFFICIENT - there is nowhere else a longer lifetime could hide. auth.users stores recovery_token and recovery_sent_at and NO expiry column at all (the full set of token/sent_at columns was enumerated). So the redeemable window is computed as sent_at + the env var, there is no per-token override, and no link can outlive the setting. That is what makes AC7 a single read rather than an investigation. Confirmed that generateLink type magiclink writes recovery_sent_at: it moved to 7 seconds ago immediately after the call.  (3) A MITIGATING PROPERTY THE STORY DID NOT KNOW, and it bears on the 'copied refresh token outlives the session' worry: recovery_token is a SINGLE column per user, so minting a second link OVERWRITES the first. Measured - token c37ec41d... became 8a53df54... on the second generateLink for the same user, so only ONE impersonation link per target is redeemable at a time and starting a new impersonation invalidates any earlier un-redeemed link.  WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE. The exposure the story describes is the REDEEMED session - once the magiclink is exchanged, the target's access and refresh tokens exist in the admin's browser, and nothing above touches that. Stopping impersonation still does not call auth.admin.signOut(targetId). So (3) bounds the un-redeemed link, not the session it produces.  STILL OPEN: read GOTRUE_MAILER_OTP_EXP on the PROD auth container. If it is 3600 like the local default, the minted link stays redeemable for an hour while the server honours a 30-minute cap - and the story's own framing applies: the LONGER of the two clocks is the real exposure. | ⚠ 2026-08-16 CORRECTION TO MY OWN NOTE ABOVE, and it turned into a finding. That note's last paragraph said 'stopping impersonation still does not call auth.admin.signOut(targetId)'. I carried that from this story's ORIGINAL description instead of reading the current code, which is the exact mistake this backlog keeps recording. The code DOES revoke: /stop calls revokeUserSessions() (routes/admin-impersonation.ts:216), which POSTs to {SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/admin/users/{id}/logout with scope 'global'. AC2 was implemented, and my sentence was wrong.  THEN I CHECKED WHETHER IT WORKS, and it does not on the version to hand. Against a running GoTrue v2.195.0:    GET    /auth/v1/admin/users/{id}          -> 200   (the control)   POST   /auth/v1/admin/users/{id}/logout   -> 404   DELETE /auth/v1/admin/users/{id}/sessions -> 404  and auth.sessions for that user stayed at 2 rows. The GET is what makes the 404s mean something - auth, gateway routing and the user id are all fine, the route simply is not there. Same 404 calling the container directly on :9999 with a service-role bearer, so it is not Kong. POST /logout answers 403 rather than 404, which distinguishes 'absent' from 'unauthorised'.  So on this version every /stop returns sessions_revoked: false and the admin's copy of the target's refresh token stays live. Filed as its own story rather than buried here, because it is a security control that reads as done.  WHAT THIS DOES TO THE EARLIER PARAGRAPH: the conclusion it reached happens to be right - the redeemed session is not revoked - but for the wrong reason, and 'the code does not call it' would have sent the next reader to write a call that already exists. The real defect is one layer down.  PROD IS NOT ASSUMED. The local container is v2.195.0; prod's version is unknown from here. Two unauthenticated-ish checks settle it and neither requires impersonating anyone: GET /auth/v1/health returns the version, and Sentry will already hold 'GoTrue logout returned 404' events under route impersonation.revoke if this is live there. | 2026-08-17 AC2 IS NOW ACTUALLY TRUE, which it was not when this story was first marked done on it. The gap was one layer below the code: /stop did call revokeUserSessions, and revokeUserSessions did POST to GoTrue's admin logout with scope global, and that route answers 404 on v2.195.0, so every stop revoked nothing while reporting a clean call. Fixed under US-2662: 00612 adds a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that deletes the target's auth.sessions and auth.refresh_tokens rows, revokeUserSessions falls back to it when GoTrue does not answer, and src/tests/impersonation-revoke_test.ts asserts the OUTCOME rather than the call, which is the property the old test lacked. The old test is kept and annotated, because a case that stayed green through a dead security control is worth leaving where the next reader will see it. Applies to this story's own AC8 line 'AC1-AC6 are done': AC2 was done in source and not in effect until now. | 2026-08-17 AC2 RE-CHECKED AND IT WAS NOT TRUE WHEN THIS CLOSED (US-2662 AC5). 'Stopping impersonation revokes the target's sessions' passed on the strength of code that called GoTrue's admin/users/{id}/logout, and that route does not exist on the version this project runs - 404 on v2.195.0 with GET admin/users/{id} returning 200 beside it, and production is v2.174.0, older still. Every stop returned sessions_revoked:false and the target's refresh token stayed live.  IT IS TRUE NOW, by a mechanism we own: 00614's revoke_user_sessions deletes the user's auth.sessions rows and the refresh tokens cascade, proven by seeding rows and looking at what is left rather than by reading the source. AC2 is therefore RESOLVED rather than reopened - the rest of this story's controls were unaffected.  THE PART OF AC2 THAT WAS NEVER ACHIEVABLE, now stated instead of implied: an access token already issued survives any revocation, GoTrue's included, because it is a JWT verified by signature. Up to an hour on jwt_expiry. AC1's 30-minute cap and the server-side marker are what bound that window, which is a good reason they are enforced by every reader.

userStories.title: Buyer plan gating: all 13 gate flags are now accounted for — only the free-tier usage count (AC4) is left
userStories.description: lib/buyer-entitlements.ts:221 defines requireBuyerFeature, the 402 upgrade-required guard, and nothing calls it. Its helper buyerFeatureEnabled is used only by it and by tests. So no buyer route enforces plan gating except buyer-authenticity.ts:24, which does its own inline check. buyer-wants.ts — the demand board, a Connoisseur-tier feature — has no gate at all. Every buyer paid feature is available on the free tier.
acceptanceCriteria: Inventory which buyer routes are supposed to be tier-gated, and against which tier.
requireBuyerFeature is applied to each of them.
A test asserts every tier-gated buyer route returns 402 for a free-tier user.
Measure how many free-tier buyers have been using paid features before deciding whether to grandfather them.

OPERATOR: run the ALL-TIME half of section 12 of scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql (AC4) - the demand_board and guarantee_claim rows of its first query. The 30-day slice came back 0 twice, so nobody ACTIVE loses anything; what is unanswered is whether an account that used either feature months ago should be grandfathered before the gates deploy.
userStories.notes:
[P1][Buyer/Billing] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. The dead-code sweep called this its top finding. Revenue leak, not just dead code. | 2026-08-02 VERIFIED, and quantified. requireBuyerFeature is defined at lib/buyer-entitlements.ts and grep across the whole edge service (excluding _test files) returns ONE hit — its own definition. Zero callers, exactly as reported. buyerFeatureEnabled has two hits: its definition and the single use inside requireBuyerFeature, so the entire gating helper pair is dead. THE SIZE OF THE GAP: BuyerGateFlags in lib/buyer-plans.ts declares THIRTEEN gated features — extensionSecondOpinion, discrepancyScoring, priceFairness, conditionAlerts, fitPrediction, authenticityAddon, videoGrading, rewards, trustScore, purchaseGuarantee, wardrobePortfolio, demandBoard, prioritySupport. Across the seven buyer route files, exactly ONE reads a gate flag: buyer-authenticity.ts checks ent.gateFlags.authenticityAddon inline. buyer-closet.ts, buyer-purchases.ts, buyer-rewards.ts, buyer-trust.ts and buyer-wants.ts contain no gate reference at all (buyer-profile.ts's only hit is the word "entitlements" in a comment). So one of thirteen flags is enforced anywhere, and the story's specific example holds — buyer-wants.ts, the demand board, has no gate. A DETAIL THAT CHANGES AC2 AND IS NOT IN THE STORY: the one gate that does exist returns 403 with code "not_entitled", while requireBuyerFeature is the 402 upgrade-required guard. They are not interchangeable. Applying requireBuyerFeature to buyer-authenticity as part of AC2 would change its status code from 403 to 402, which is a client-visible change — the buyer web/iOS clients may branch on one or the other. Either check the clients first, or leave authenticity on 403 and say why. Do not assume the helper is a drop-in for the inline check just because both deny. SEQUENCING NOTE on AC4: it asks how many free-tier buyers have been using paid features before deciding whether to grandfather. That is a PROD query this host cannot run, and it should gate AC2 rather than follow it — switching thirteen features on at once for users who have had them free is a support event, not just a fix. Split AC4 out as an operator task so AC1 (the inventory) can proceed without it. AC1 is the cheap half and is mostly done by this note: the thirteen flags above are the candidate list, and what remains is deciding the TIER each belongs to, which is a product call rather than a code reading. | PARTIAL 2026-08-03 — AC1, AC2 and AC3 DONE. AC4 is a prod query this host cannot run and stays open as the operator half. AC1, the inventory, is now a FILE rather than a paragraph: services/edge-functions/src/tests/buyer-plan-gates_test.ts lists all 21 buyer routes across the seven route files, each with either the feature that gates it or a stated reason it is open. AC2: TWO ROUTES WERE GENUINELY UNPROTECTED and are now gated. The demand board (POST /wants, PATCH /wants/:id) is Connoisseur-only and had no gate on any of its four routes. The purchase-guarantee claim (POST /purchases/:id/claim) is Guard and up and had none either. Both now call requireBuyerFeature and RETURN its refusal. The claim gate goes BEFORE the ownership read on purpose: a free-tier buyer should be told to upgrade, not told whether some other buyer's purchase id exists. A RULE I HAD TO INVENT, because the story does not state one and the naive reading causes harm: GATE THE PATHS THAT CREATE OR CONSUME A PAID FEATURE, NEVER THE ONES THAT READ OR REMOVE WHAT THE BUYER ALREADY HAS. Gating GET /wants and DELETE /wants/:id would mean a buyer who downgrades cannot see or clean up wants they created while paying — the gate would convert a billing state into data loss. Both are left open with that reason recorded at the call site and in the registry. WHAT I DID NOT GATE, and why each: eleven routes read a flag that is TRUE ON EVERY TIER (wardrobePortfolio, extensionSecondOpinion, rewards, trustScore), so a gate there denies nobody and costs a database round trip — a test case now FAILS if anyone claims a gate on a feature no tier withholds, because a gate that cannot deny reads as protection and is not. POST /authenticity keeps its inline 403 not_entitled rather than being converted: requireBuyerFeature returns 402, and the buyer web and iOS clients may branch on the status. That is a client contract change and belongs in its own story rather than in a sweep — the previous pass flagged this and it was right. AC3: the story asks for a live 402 assertion for a free-tier user. That needs an authenticated request against a seeded buyer, i.e. the database, so I did NOT claim it and built the strongest thing that works without one — six cases asserting the guard is CALLED on the right route with the right feature name, that its refusal is RETURNED rather than discarded, that the declared route set IS the route set, that every ungated route carries a real reason, and that the free tier genuinely lacks demandBoard and purchaseGuarantee (otherwise the two new gates would silently stop denying anyone while every other case still passed). WHY ENUMERATION: dead security code is the worst kind, because the helper's EXISTENCE is what makes a reviewer believe the gating is handled. Nothing about reading buyer-wants.ts said "this is ungated" — the absence was the bug, and absence is what a diff never shows. A new buyer route now fails until its author answers the question nobody asked for thirteen features. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS: removed the demand-board gate (reddened naming the route and flag), kept the call but discarded its Response (reddened on the return), added an undeclared /probe route (reddened as an unlisted route), and re-declared the claim gate against the rewards flag (reddened as a gate that denies nobody). Each restored. A MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING: my first route regex was a bare .get( / .post(, which also matched c.get("userId") in every handler and reported a phantom route per file. Over-matching is not harmless here — it would have left the guard permanently red, and a permanently red guard gets deleted. It is anchored to the Routes receiver now and says so. AND A SELF-INFLICTED ONE: I reverted my own uncommitted gate edits with a git checkout while restoring a negative-verification probe, then caught it by grepping for the guard before moving on. VERIFIED: deno check clean, deno lint clean across 1310 files, full edge suite 5166 passed / 0 failed, tenant-isolation 17/0. REMAINING: AC4 (how many free-tier buyers have been using the demand board and the guarantee claim, to decide grandfathering) is a prod query — it belongs with the other operator diagnostics in scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql. Worth doing BEFORE this deploys, since switching a feature off for users who have had it free is a support event, not just a fix. | 2026-08-03: this story's last open AC is now answerable by scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql, which the operator runs in ONE psql session alongside the other blocked stories. Read-only, verified by executing against a real database with ON_ERROR_STOP=1 — so it cannot fail the operator's session on a wrong column name, which is the failure mode that makes someone distrust the whole file. §12 counts free-tier accounts that used the two features that were genuinely ungated — the demand board and the guarantee claim — BY ACCOUNT rather than by row, because '3,000 wants' and '4 buyers' call for very different decisions about grandfathering. A 30-day slice is reported separately: an account that used it once a year ago is not the same support problem as one using it this week. | AC4 FIRST DATA POINT, 2026-08-03 (owner ran the diagnostics): free_tier_accounts_last_30d = 0. No free-tier buyer has used the demand board in the last 30 days, so switching its gate on is NOT a support event for anyone currently active. That is the half of AC4 that decides urgency. What is still needed to close it is the ALL-TIME half from the same section — the demand_board and guarantee_claim rows of the first query in §12 — because an account that used the feature months ago still loses access on the next deploy, and whether that matters is a grandfathering call rather than a code one. | PROD ANSWER 2026-08-03 (owner ran scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql). §12's 30-day slice returned 0. Combined with the earlier reading, no free-tier buyer has used the demand board recently. STILL MISSING: the ALL-TIME half of §12 — the demand_board and guarantee_claim rows of that section's first query — which is what decides grandfathering for someone who used the feature months ago and would lose it on the next deploy. | 2026-08-04 RE-CHECKED — the title is now FALSE and should not be quoted. grep for requireBuyerFeature across services/edge-functions/src excluding tests returns four hits: its definition in lib/buyer-entitlements.ts plus three real call sites — buyer-purchases.ts:301 gating purchaseGuarantee, and buyer-wants.ts:40 and :91 gating demandBoard. Commit 6e3915f7 closed the zero-caller claim, and the story's own worked example (the demand board) is one of the routes now gated. WHAT REMAINS is the count, not the mechanism: the earlier note recorded THIRTEEN flags in BuyerGateFlags, and two of them are now enforced through this helper (a third, authenticityAddon, is enforced inline in buyer-authenticity.ts). So AC1 (the inventory of which routes gate against which tier) and AC2 (applying it to each) are still open for the remaining ten, and AC4 (measuring free-tier usage before deciding whether to grandfather) is untouched. Keep the story, retitle it to something like 'Ten of thirteen buyer gate flags are still unenforced' — the current title will read as stale to the next person and invites closing it by mistake.

| 2026-08-08 RETITLED, as the previous note asked, and the number in the old title was wrong in BOTH directions.

The 2026-08-04 note said to retitle this to "Ten of thirteen buyer gate flags are still unenforced". I checked that number instead of adopting it, and it does not survive. THE REAL ACCOUNTING, measured by grepping every flag name across the whole edge service:

FIVE FLAGS ARE TRUE ON EVERY TIER — extensionSecondOpinion, conditionAlerts, rewards, trustScore, wardrobePortfolio. Nothing withholds them from anyone, so there is no revenue to leak and a gate on them would be decoration plus a database round trip. They were being counted as unenforced. They are not enforceable.

THE OTHER EIGHT ARE DENIABLE, AND ALL EIGHT ARE ENFORCED — just not all in the buyer route files, which is the whole reason the count kept reading wrong. A route-shaped audit of seven buyer files cannot see five of them:
  demandBoard, purchaseGuarantee -> requireBuyerFeature 402 (buyer-wants.ts x2, buyer-purchases.ts)
  authenticityAddon -> inline 403 not_entitled (buyer-authenticity.ts), deliberately not converted
  discrepancyScoring, priceFairness, fitPrediction -> FIELD SUPPRESSION via resolveExtensionGates in routes/public-grading.ts:1107-1122 and :1818 — the extension scan returns, with the paid fields nulled
  videoGrading -> 402 UPGRADE_REQUIRED at routes/grade.ts:617, after the seller plan is checked and the buyer plan is the second way in
  prioritySupport -> NO runtime path by design; lib/plan-gate.ts:52 states it is an SLA/routing attribute

THE SHAPES DIFFER AND ALL OF THEM ARE RIGHT. A 402 on the extension scan would refuse the free feature in order to withhold the paid one; suppressing three fields is the correct answer there. Writing a test that demanded one uniform shape would have pushed three of these toward the wrong one — worth saying, because that is the obvious next move and it would be a regression.

NEW GUARD, the flag side of the question this story was actually filed on: buyer-plan-gates_test.ts already enumerated all 21 ROUTES, which answers "is this route gated?" and cannot answer "is this paid feature enforced anywhere?". FLAG_ENFORCEMENT now maps every BuyerGateFlags key to null / "GATES" / a file path. A null entry must be true on every tier (so "we do not gate it" stays earned, not assumed); a "GATES" entry must appear in the route registry; a file entry is READ and must still mention the flag, so deleting an enforcement reddens here instead of leaving the table describing code that used to exist. The Record type forces exhaustiveness one way; a key-set assertion catches the other.

NEGATIVE-VERIFIED TWICE: flipped rewards to false on the free tier (reddened, naming rewards and free — a paid feature nothing withholds); repointed videoGrading at lib/plan-gate.ts (reddened, naming the file that no longer mentions it). Both restored, 7 passed. deno lint + deno check clean.

STILL passes:false ON AC4 ALONE, unchanged: the ALL-TIME half of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql section 12 — how many free-tier accounts EVER used the demand board or the guarantee claim, which decides grandfathering. The 30-day slice already came back 0 twice. Operator query; this host cannot run it. | [2026-09-02][PROD READ] AC4 ANSWERED: clean. Source: scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql run read-only against prod over SSH on 2026-09-02 (container supabase-db-kcksoks4kk0kswk0ccs40os8, 29 sections, 0 SQL errors). Raw output kept out of the repo; it contains customer data. Free-tier accounts that used a paid buyer feature: demand_board 0 accounts / 0 rows, guarantee_claim 0 accounts / 0 rows, and 0 free-tier accounts in the last 30 days. So the free-tier gate has never been exercised in production and there is no support backlog to reconcile behind it.

userStories.title: Variation listings cannot be revised: resubmit needs an offer id a group listing never has
userStories.description: As a seller with a multi-variation eBay listing, I want Save and resubmit to push my edits to eBay, so that a listing with size or color variants is not frozen the moment it goes live.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/:id/revise on a listing whose listings.variations is non-null and whose platform_offer_id is null no longer returns the 409 "This listing has no eBay offer id" (flipdesk-ebay.ts, the guard above the offerId const) and instead revises through the eBay inventory item group.

The revise resolves its strategy group-FIRST, the same way the end path does via resolveEndStrategy (flipdesk-ebay.ts:8836), and keys the group on the PINNED listings.inventory_sku rather than the current inventory_items.sku, so a SKU rename cannot orphan the live group.

The group branch updates every variant inventory item and then calls createOrReplaceInventoryItemGroup and publishOfferByInventoryItemGroup (both already exported from services/edge-functions/src/lib/ebay-client.ts), so title, description, price, photos and specifics changes reach the live listing.

A single-offer listing keeps the existing offer branch byte-for-byte; a deno test in services/edge-functions/src/tests/listing-variations_test.ts asserts both branches are chosen correctly from a listings row (variations present versus platform_offer_id present).

The composer treats a published variation listing as live: isLiveListing in src/pages/flipdesk/composer.tsx stops requiring platform_offer_id when listings.variations is present and platform_listing_id is set, so the footer shows Save and resubmit to eBay instead of offering to publish an already-live listing. A vitest guard pins that gate.

Tenant scoping is unchanged: the revise route still reaches the listing through an owner-verified parent row (US-268), and services/edge-functions/src/tests/tenant-isolation_test.ts gains a case covering the group-revise branch.

Verified after deploy against a real multi-variation listing, not by reading code: the publish path never writes platform_offer_id for a group (the variation listingPayload in flipdesk-ebay.ts omits it), so unit tests alone cannot prove the round trip.

OPERATOR: this story's AC7 is the only thing still open and it cannot be done from a checkout — after the next edge deploy, open a real multi-variation eBay listing, change ONLY the price, and Save and resubmit. That is the case the second pass introduced and then fixed (a price-only revise used to fall through to the offer path with an empty offer id), so it is the one worth exercising by hand.
userStories.notes: PARTIAL 2026-08-03 — AC2, AC4 and AC5 DONE, plus a truthful refusal in place of misleading advice. AC1, AC3, AC6 and AC7 remain, and the reason is scoped rather than vague. VERIFIED THE WHOLE CHAIN FIRST. The revise route really does begin with `if (!row.listing.platform_offer_id) return 409`, eBay really never mints an offer id for a listing published through publish_by_inventory_item_group, and loadListingOwned already selects both `variations` and the pinned `inventory_sku`. The END path already solved the same problem correctly under US-1999 (resolveEndStrategy, group-first, keyed on the pinned SKU) — two resolvers in one file giving different answers to the same question is the shape that made this findable. AC2 DONE: NEW resolveReviseStrategy, deliberately the same shape and the same ORDER as resolveEndStrategy. Group first, because an offer-first resolver reads a group listing as having no mechanism at all — which is precisely the bug. Keyed on the PINNED listings.inventory_sku, since the inventory_item_group was created under the base SKU at publish and a later rename would aim the revise at a group that does not exist. One deliberate difference from the end resolver: no-mechanism is `none`, not `local`. Ending locally is a real outcome — the listing is closed in FlipDesk — whereas a revise with no mechanism has done nothing and must not report otherwise. A test pins both the agreement and that single divergence. AC5 DONE, AND IT WAS THE WORSE HALF OF THE BUG. isLiveListing required a platform_offer_id, so every LIVE variation listing was classified as a DRAFT and the footer offered to "Publish to eBay" something already live. The 409 at least refused; this invited the seller to publish a duplicate of their own listing. The gate now also accepts variations + platform_listing_id — the eBay item id publish-by-group returns — and a test requires BOTH halves, since a matrix alone would call an unpublished draft live. SHIPPED AHEAD OF THE FEATURE, on purpose: the 409 for a variation listing no longer says "Sync from eBay or republish to enable edits". That is advice that CANNOT WORK — republishing does not create an offer id for a group, and republishing a live listing is worse than doing nothing. It now says the truth: group revise is not supported yet, edit on eBay for now. A wrong instruction is worse than a plain refusal, and this one was pointing sellers at an action that could duplicate their listing. AC4 DONE: seven cases appended to listing-variations_test.ts covering both branches from a listings row, the ordering (group wins even when a stale offer id is present), the pinned-SKU key, the two no-mechanism shapes, the revise/end agreement, and the refusal text. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED: the resolver flipped to offer-first (reddened on the ordering case) and the composer's variation branch reduced to the matrix alone (reddened on the both-halves case). WHAT REMAINS AND WHY I DID NOT DO IT. AC1/AC3 are the group-revise branch itself: update every variant inventory item, then createOrReplaceInventoryItemGroup and publishOfferByInventoryItemGroup. The machinery exists — publishVariationListing does exactly this — but reusing it means reconstructing a PublishContextOk, PublishItem, policies and photos inside the revise handler, and that function also performs publish-shaped PERSISTENCE which a revise must not repeat. It is a substantial change to the most sensitive file in the service, on the path every seller's Save-and-resubmit uses, and AC7 states plainly that unit tests cannot prove the round trip because the publish path never writes platform_offer_id for a group. Half-implementing it risks breaking the COMMON single-offer revise to fix the rare one. The resolver, the composer gate and the honest refusal are the parts that are safe and testable now; the branch wants one deliberate pass with a real multi-variation listing to verify against, which is what AC7 asks for anyway. AC6 (the tenant-isolation case) belongs with that branch — there is no new query to scope yet. VERIFIED: deno check clean, deno lint clean across 1323 files, edge suite 5245 passed / 0 failed, web 260 files / 3236 tests 0 failed, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, build green through the 216-route prerender. | 2026-08-09 AC1/AC3 SCOPED, NOT IMPLEMENTED, and there is a SEMANTIC DECISION nobody has taken that the ACs do not mention. Recorded so the next session finds it before writing the branch rather than after. AC3 reads as plumbing: update every variant inventory item, then call createOrReplaceInventoryItemGroup and publishOfferByInventoryItemGroup, both already exported. Traced the publish path (flipdesk-ebay.ts:7650-7740) to mirror it, and the plumbing IS that shape. THE PROBLEM IS WHAT A SCALAR EDIT MEANS TO A MATRIX. The revise route accepts title, description, listing_price, quantity and photos. For a variation listing those split cleanly in two: TITLE, DESCRIPTION and PHOTOS are unambiguous — they live on the group AND on every member item, so a revise applies them to both, exactly as publish does. PRICE and QUANTITY are NOT. The publish path creates ONE OFFER PER VARIANT SKU, each with its own price (the per-variant override, else the base) and its own quantity (variant.quantity). A single listing_price in the revise body has no defined meaning against that: does it overwrite every variant's price, or only the ones with no override, or set a new base the overrides continue to shift from? Each answer is defensible and they produce different money on a LIVE listing. Same for quantity against variant.quantity. Guessing here is not a call code should make — it is the same class of decision as the offer-route-vs-return-route split in US-2227, and the wrong guess silently reprices a seller's whole variation matrix. RECOMMENDED SHAPE, if the decision goes the obvious way: implement the group branch for title/description/photos only, and REFUSE price/quantity on a variation listing with a message naming eBay as the place to change them — the same truthful-refusal pattern this story already used in place of the misleading 'republish to enable edits' advice. That ships the majority of the value with no ambiguity, and leaves the pricing question to be decided on its own rather than smuggled in. WHY I DID NOT IMPLEMENT IT THIS PASS, stated plainly rather than dressed up: this is a mutation path against live eBay listings, AC7 already says it cannot be verified without a real multi-variation listing, and I have no way to exercise it end to end from here. A branch that looks right and is wrong is worse than the current honest 409, because the 409 loses an edit and a bad branch loses a listing's pricing. The unambiguous half is genuinely small once the price/quantity decision is recorded; it is the decision that gates it, not the code. AC6 IS COUPLED, NOT INDEPENDENT: tenant-isolation_test.ts already covers 'B cannot revise A's eBay listing' via loadListingOwned (line ~1930), and a VARIATION-specific case needs a seeded variation listing id the fixture does not have (seed-tenant-isolation-fixture.ts) plus a group branch to actually exercise. Adding it before the branch exists would assert the refusal, not the ownership check. VERIFIED UNCHANGED: resolveReviseStrategy (AC2), the composer's isLiveListing fix (AC5) and the truthful 409 all still in place; full edge suite green this session at 6213 passed / 0 failed. | 2026-08-15 AC1, AC3 and AC6 DONE. Only AC7 remains, which is the check against a real multi-variation listing after a deploy. WHY THIS COULD LAND NOW when the previous pass deliberately stopped: the risk it named was breaking the COMMON single-offer revise to fix the rare one, and the branch as built cannot. The group path returns before the offer path is reached, and it only runs for a listing with variations and no platform_offer_id - which is exactly the set that answered 409 until today. The blast radius is the listings that were already broken. AC1: the 409 is now keyed on resolveReviseStrategy returning none rather than on platform_offer_id being absent, which is the offer-first read that caused the bug. The variation-specific refusal is DELETED, and the test that used to pin its presence now pins its absence - it was honest while the branch did not exist and would be a lie now. AC3: new reviseVariationGroup, placed AFTER the shared assembly so the group push uses the same title, description, aspects, photos and condition the offer path builds; a second copy of that assembly is how the two paths would start disagreeing about what a revision contains. Order is items, then group, then per-variant offers, then publish, and a test pins that order by source position: the group references the items, price and category live on the offers rather than on the item, and the publish call applies the lot. Offer ids are found with listOffersForSku, since a group listing has none stored - that absence IS the bug this story is about. TWO DELIBERATE REFUSALS. Quantity is not pushed: quantity on a group is per variant, and one number applied to every variant multiplies the seller's stock silently, so the response says so instead. A variant carrying its own price_cents keeps it through a base-price edit, or a deliberately-differentiated variant would be flattened by an edit to the listing price. THE PART I CANNOT VERIFY, stated in the code as well as here: publish_by_inventory_item_group is how eBay applies pending item and group changes to an already-published group, and if it instead rejects the call as already-published the error surfaces as a 422 with its own message rather than being swallowed. That is the failure mode worth having - the alternative is reporting success on a listing that did not change. AC7 stays open for exactly this. AC6: a tenant-isolation case for the group branch, and it needed a fixture rather than a classification. Before the branch existed the 409 was doing the isolation work by accident; now the route performs real eBay writes, so the ownership check is the only thing between B and A's live listing. The seed script emits TEST_USER_A_VARIATION_LISTING_ID - a plain insert with variations set, a pinned inventory_sku and no offer id, which is what eBay leaves behind after a group publish. The structural guard caught the new gating id immediately and refused to let it skip quietly, which is the guard working. ALSO EXTRACTED: clearReviseDrift, so both paths clear the same sync_drift and publish_error state. A revise that succeeded through the group and left the marker standing would show eBay differs on a listing that no longer does. VERIFIED: full edge suite 6781 passed / 0 failed / 195 ignored, deno check and deno lint clean on the route, the test file and the seed script, listing-variations 18 passed (7 new). Negative-verified twice: removing the publish step reddens the order case, and flattening the per-variant price reddens its own case; both restored. | 2026-08-15 (same day, second pass) A DEFECT IN MY OWN CHANGE, found while doing the vault same-commit review rather than by a test, and fixed with two guards. THE BUG: the group branch sits inside the block gated on hasTitle or hasDesc or syncPhotos or resyncFields, because that is where the shared title/description/aspect/photo assembly happens. A PRICE-ONLY or QUANTITY-ONLY revise satisfies none of those, so it skipped the block entirely, fell through to the offer-side push at the end, and called updateOfferFields with the empty string a group listing resolves to as its offer id. A malformed eBay write against a live listing, reachable from Save-and-resubmit with only the price changed, and invisible until production. Before this story the same request met the 409 and could not get that far, so the branch introduced it. FIXED IN TWO PLACES because one alone leaves it reachable: the gate now includes groupRevise, so a price-only revise runs the group path (the extra item and group PUTs are the same idempotent ones publish sends, and that path re-publishes the group anyway), and the offer-side push is guarded with !groupRevise so a future early-exit that skipped the branch still cannot send an empty offer id. Two new cases pin both, and the first was negative-verified: removing groupRevise from the gate reddens it.
