VAULT, which is the rule I had broken: three notes name flipdesk-ebay.ts in code_refs and were left drifting by the first pass. ebay-required-aspect-completeness gains the fourth-path note (the group revise reuses reviseWireAspects rather than assembling its own, which is precisely how that note's original defect would have returned); ebay-listing-lifecycle-reconciliation gains the revise half beside the end half it already documented, including why none rather than local is the right no-mechanism answer; grade-authority-on-listings records that all three grade channels reach a variation listing, and that the silent failure avoided is a group revise skipping stripCertLinks and putting an off-eBay link back on a live listing. draft-snapshot-precedence was re-read against both its drifted refs - my change does not touch publish precedence, and the composer edits on 2026-08-14 were a help link plus US-2593's title write-back, which narrows one divergence case rather than changing the rule - so it gains one linking sentence and a bump. VERIFIED: full edge suite 6783 passed / 0 failed / 195 ignored, listing-variations 20 passed (2 new), deno check and lint clean, vault:lint down from 12 errors to 5 and every one that remains belongs to another commit. | 2026-08-17 THE NOTES ON THIS STORY WERE STALE AND THE STALENESS IS THE FINDING. They said 'AC1, AC3, AC6 and AC7 remain'. Three of those four are done and have been for a while - a later pass finished them without updating the summary, so this story reads as half-built when it is one operator step from closed. Re-verified rather than re-read, because a story that understates its own progress is how work gets done twice, which cost a full merge earlier today.  AC1 DONE. The 409 is gone. flipdesk-ebay.ts refuses only when resolveReviseStrategy returns `none` - a group listing now resolves to `{kind:'group'}` and proceeds. Pinned by 'US-2395: the variation refusal is gone, because it is no longer true' and 'revise refuses only when the strategy resolves to none'.  AC3 DONE. reviseVariationGroup (flipdesk-ebay.ts:9500) takes eighteen fields and runs items, then the group, then the per-variant offers, then publish - pinned in that ORDER by 'the group push runs items, then group, then offers, then publish', which is the assertion that matters since a group published before its items exist fails at eBay rather than here.  AC6 DONE, AND IT IS NOT AN INERT CASE, which was the thing worth checking. tenant-isolation_ test.ts:2098 'B cannot revise A's multi-variation eBay listing (group branch)' is gated on TEST_USER_A_VARIATION_LISTING_ID, so a missing fixture would leave it permanently ignored and green. It is not missing: seed-tenant-isolation-fixture.ts:238-261 inserts a listings row with `variations` set, a pinned inventory_sku of FIXTURE-VAR-A and NO platform_offer_id - which is exactly what eBay leaves behind after publish_by_inventory_item_group - and emits the id. The Tenant Isolation workflow seeds with that script and runs the suite with TENANT_ISOLATION_REQUIRED=1, which turns a missing fixture into a FAILURE rather than a skip. So the case executes in CI on every run.  The case's own comment records why it needs to exist separately: before the group branch, this request met the 409 before ownership could matter, so the refusal was doing the isolation work BY ACCIDENT. Now the branch performs real eBay writes and the ownership check is the only thing between B and A's live listing.  VERIFIED: 20 cases in listing-variations_test.ts passed / 0 failed, including the two regressions the second pass introduced and fixed - 'a price-only revise still reaches the group branch' and 'the offer-side push never runs for a group'. A price-only revise satisfies none of the title/description/photo/resync conditions, so without `|| groupRevise` it fell through to updateOfferFields with the empty offer id a group resolves to.  STILL OPEN: AC7 ONLY, and it is genuinely not doable from a checkout. The publish path never writes platform_offer_id for a group, so no unit test can prove the round trip. After the next edge deploy: open a real multi-variation eBay listing, change ONLY the price, and Save and resubmit. Price-only is the case to exercise because it is the one that used to fall through.

userStories.title: A denied function call from anon or authenticated SEGFAULTS Postgres and restarts the whole database
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want a permission-denied RPC to return an error instead of crashing the database, so that anyone holding the public anon key cannot restart production at will.
acceptanceCriteria: Establish whether the PROD Postgres image reproduces it. On the local Supabase image (PG 17.6) it reproduces every time; prod is a separate self-hosted image and this has NOT been tested there, deliberately, because the test is a denial of service against production. The safe check is to read the image tag and the supautils.hint_roles setting, not to call a denied RPC.

If prod reproduces: mitigate BEFORE anything else. Clearing supautils.hint_roles (it exists only to append a GRANT hint to the error message) or upgrading the image are the two candidates; whichever is chosen, prove it with a denied call against a staging copy of the same image.

A regression check that survives an image upgrade: a throwaway-stack test that revokes EXECUTE on a scratch function, calls it as anon, and asserts a clean 'permission denied for function' error with the connection still alive.

supabase/migrations/00527_revoke_public_function_execute.sql.BLOCKED is renamed back to .sql, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 00527 in the same commit, and US-2282 closed — the SQL is already written and verified, it is only blocked on this.

The 5 functions already revoked from anon before this was known (refund_grade 00048, credit_ledger_reconciliation 00093, release_job_lock + try_acquire_job_lock 00094, reserve_snap/refund_snap 00099, reconcile_payout_link 00117, equity_snapshot_owners) are enumerated in the notes as the CURRENTLY reachable crash entry points, since they are what an attacker could use today.

OPERATOR: run `show supautils.hint_roles;` over psql on the prod database (read-only, one line). If anon is absent, AC1 closes as does-not-reproduce and AC2 is already satisfied, which unblocks 00527 and US-2282. Do NOT confirm by calling a revoked function: that call is the outage.

AC4 IS VOID as of 2026-08-21 and this story no longer blocks US-2282. AC4 said to rename 00527 back to .sql and close US-2282 on the strength of it. 00527 is a permanent DO-NOT-APPLY by owner decision, and US-2282 closed by the other route the story itself preferred: in-body authorization checks (00614-00617, then 00640), which raise an ordinary 42501 instead of a permission denial. Nothing about US-2282 waits on this any more.

WHAT REMAINS HERE IS ONLY AC1/AC6: does the segfault reproduce on the prod image at all. That is still worth knowing - it decides whether a denied EXECUTE anywhere in the schema is a restart button - but it is now a standalone question rather than a blocker. One read: show supautils.hint_roles;
userStories.notes: [P0][Security/DB] Found 2026-08-04 by accident while verifying US-2282 on a throwaway stack, and it is the reason US-2282 is not shipping. ISOLATED, not guessed — four probes on the local Supabase image (PostgreSQL 17.6, shared_preload_libraries includes supautils): (1) a trivial scratch function with EXECUTE revoked, called as anon => SIGNAL 11 SEGMENTATION FAULT, 'terminating any other active server processes', full database recovery; (2) same as authenticated => same crash; (3) same as a custom role NOT listed in supautils.hint_roles => clean 'ERROR: permission denied for function', connection alive; (4) a denied TABLE read as anon => clean error PLUS the supautils hint 'Grant the required privileges to the current role with: GRANT SELECT ON public.applied_migrations TO anon;'. supautils.hint_roles is set to exactly 'anon, authenticated, service_role', which is exactly the set that crashes. So the crash is in the supautils hint path for FUNCTION permission denials specifically; the table path is fine. ALREADY REACHABLE TODAY, WITHOUT ANY NEW MIGRATION: public.refund_grade(uuid) has been revoked from anon since 00048/00093, and calling it as anon crashes the database the same way — verified, not inferred. PostgREST exposes it as an RPC, so the input needed is the public anon key and one HTTP call. WHY US-2282 IS BLOCKED ON THIS RATHER THAN THE OTHER WAY AROUND: 00527 does not create the bug, it multiplies the entry points — from the handful of functions already revoked to ~80. Applying it into an unpatched image would hand an attacker eighty ways to restart the database instead of eight. The SQL is written, verified on a fresh stack, and parked at supabase/migrations/00527_revoke_public_function_execute.sql.BLOCKED; the .BLOCKED suffix is what keeps apply-prod-migrations.sh (which globs *.sql) from applying it. NOT TESTED AGAINST PROD ON PURPOSE. The test IS the denial of service, so running it would be the attack. The safe next step is to read the prod image tag and 'show supautils.hint_roles' over psql — both read-only — and compare against the local image. If prod's image differs enough not to reproduce, this closes as a local-only artifact and US-2282 unblocks immediately. | 2026-08-08 AC3 DONE; AC5 DONE AND THE COUNT WAS WRONG; AC1/AC2 now have a PROVEN mitigation and a safer prod probe. Docker was available on this host for the first time, so every claim below was re-run rather than inherited. REPRODUCED on public.ecr.aws/supabase/postgres:17.6.1.106 with all 552 migrations applied: a scratch function with EXECUTE revoked, called as anon, gives 'server closed the connection' and the server log shows 'terminated by signal 11: Segmentation fault' -> 'terminating any other active server processes' -> 'automatic recovery in progress'. ALSO reproduced with public.refund_grade(uuid), a REAL function that has been revoked from anon since 00048/00093 — so this is reachable in prod today with the public anon key and one RPC call, exactly as the story claimed. MITIGATION PROVEN (this is new): setting supautils.hint_roles = '' in /etc/postgresql-custom/supautils.conf and restarting Postgres turns the same call into a clean 'ERROR: permission denied for function' with the connection alive. Verified by flipping the config both ways twice. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT FOR WHOEVER APPLIES IT: this CANNOT be done from SQL or from a migration — supautils rejects 'ALTER SYSTEM SET supautils.hint_roles' with 'permission denied to set parameter' even as the postgres superuser. It is a postgresql.conf change on the host (Coolify), i.e. an operator action, and no migration in this repo can substitute for it. AC5 CORRECTED: the story listed ~8 reachable entry points; the real number is 14, enumerated from the live schema rather than by hand (select ... where not has_function_privilege('anon', oid, 'EXECUTE') over the 160 public functions): admin_adjust_credits, bump_cache_signal, credit_ledger_reconciliation, delete_account, get_cache_signal, latest_schema_migration, reconcile_payout_link, record_registered_number_sighting, record_style_code_observation, refund_grade, release_job_lock, reserve_guarantee_pool_drawdown, revoke_grade_credits, try_acquire_job_lock. AC3 SHIPPED: scripts/db-denied-rpc-crash-check.mjs, wired into verify.mjs --db and db-migrations.yml. It is ADVISORY (continue-on-error), NOT a gate, and that is a deliberate call recorded in both files: the stock image is vulnerable today, so gating would turn every migration PR red on arrival, and this repo already has the lesson that a permanently red guard gets switched off (US-1927 notes). Flipping it to a hard gate is step ONE of the mitigation, not a follow-up. VERIFIED BOTH DIRECTIONS with the final code: RED on the stock image (all three assertions fire), GREEN with hint_roles cleared. Three self-inflicted defects were found and fixed while building it, all the same class as bugs this repo has shipped before — an assertion on pg_postmaster_start_time() that CANNOT EVER FIRE (a backend SIGSEGV is handled by crash recovery; the postmaster never restarts), and twice using execFileSync where the text being asserted on is on STDERR (both the 'permission denied' string and the Postgres server log), which silently compared against an empty string. AC1 — A SAFE PROBE THAT WAS MISSED, worth trying before anything invasive: US-1927's 2026-07-18 note records that calling latest_schema_migration() against PROD as anon returned 42501 permission denied rather than a crash. latest_schema_migration is on the list of 14 above, so IF that observation was a real prod call it is evidence prod does NOT reproduce — and it cost nothing. Treat it as a lead, not proof: it is second-hand, and it is not certain the 42501 came from Postgres rather than from PostgREST's own check. Re-running that one read-only call is the cheapest next step and is not an attack. EVIDENCE POINTING THE OTHER WAY: vault/10-ops/backups.md:161 records the 2026-06-12 restore drill against 'the same Supabase image as prod' pinned at 17.6.1.106 — the exact image that crashes here. Nothing in the repo pins the prod tag, so that drill log is the only signal, and it suggests prod DOES reproduce. These two point opposite ways; resolve with the read-only check the story already specifies (read the image tag and 'show supautils.hint_roles' over psql). KEPT passes:false: AC1 (prod image determination) and AC2 (apply the mitigation) are operator actions on the Coolify host that cannot be done or validated from here, and AC4 (unblock 00527 / US-2282) must stay blocked until AC2 is done — applying it into an unpatched image would take the entry points from 14 to ~80. | 2026-08-15 AC1 HAS AN ANSWER, MEASURED AGAINST PROD, AND THE 2026-08-08 NOTE CONTAINS ADVICE THAT WOULD HAVE CAUSED THE OUTAGE. Correction first, because it is the dangerous half: that note says re-running latest_schema_migration() as anon against prod is 'the cheapest next step and is not an attack'. It IS the attack. latest_schema_migration is on this story's own list of 14 functions anon cannot execute, so calling it as anon is probe (1) verbatim, and if prod reproduces, that call restarts the production database. The 2026-08-04 note says the opposite and is right: NOT TESTED AGAINST PROD ON PURPOSE, the test IS the denial of service. Do not run it. THE SAFE PROBE THAT DOES WORK, and it is new: the crash is in the supautils hint path, and hint_roles gates the hint for TABLE denials too, which never crash on any image. So ask for a table anon has no grant on and look for the hint. NEW scripts/probe-supautils-hint.mjs does exactly that, with a CONTROL leg first, because a null hint has two causes that look identical from a client (supautils is quiet, or PostgREST is not forwarding hints at all) and the second reads as mitigated on every stack including the crashing one. The control asks for a near-miss column name so POSTGRES emits its own hint. MEASURED ON PROD TODAY, https://api.gradethread.com: control grade_reports.certificate_i returns 42703 with hint 'Perhaps you meant to reference the column grade_reports.certificate_id.' - so hints demonstrably reach the client; subject applied_migrations as anon returns 42501 'permission denied for table applied_migrations' with hint NULL - no supautils hint at all. On the crashing image that same request carries 'Grant the required privileges to the current role with: GRANT SELECT ON public.applied_migrations TO anon;' (this story's probe 4). SO: anon is not in prod's supautils.hint_roles, or supautils is not adding hints there, and either way the path the segfault lives in is not running for anon. That is EVIDENCE prod does not reproduce, not proof - it shares a gate with the function path rather than testing it, it says nothing about authenticated or service_role, and the direct test remains the attack. WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE CHAIN: this is the first real signal against reproduction, and it outweighs the backups.md restore-drill inference (which only says prod ran the same image tag in June, not how it is configured today) because it is a live reading of the running stack rather than a document. AC2's operator step is now cheap to confirm rather than to perform: read 'show supautils.hint_roles' over psql and expect anon to be absent. If it is absent, AC1 closes as 'prod does not reproduce', AC2 is already satisfied, and US-2282/00527 unblocks. VERIFIED: 4 cases in src/test/supautils-hint-probe.test.ts, the load-bearing one being that a failed control returns INCONCLUSIVE regardless of the subject - a security probe whose broken state looks like a pass is worse than none. Sabotage-verified by disabling the control branch, which reddened exactly that case. tsc -b clean. | 2026-08-15 THE PSQL READ IS NOW PART OF THE ONE-PASTE FILE. §23 of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql (and the console variant) asks for hint_roles and carries the reading guide: NULL or empty means the hint path is not running, prod does not reproduce, and 00527/US-2282 unblock; a value containing anon means the mitigation comes first and cannot be done from SQL at all. It also repeats, in the file the operator is actually looking at, that confirming by calling a revoked function IS the outage. The verification standard for this file is 'executed, not read', and these three sections were NOT executed: Docker is down on this host so there was no throwaway Postgres to run them against. Stating that plainly because the rest of the file was executed and the difference matters. WHAT WAS VERIFIED, against PROD rather than against the migration text: every column named exists (users.billing_source, users.billing_environment, users.buyer_billing_environment probed through PostgREST, where a missing column answers 42703 naming it). AND ONE BUG WAS CAUGHT AND FIXED BEFORE IT SHIPPED: I first wrote §23 as `SHOW supautils.hint_roles`, which raises 'unrecognized configuration parameter' when supautils is not loaded and, under ON_ERROR_STOP=1, would have killed the rest of the operator's session — the exact failure this file's own header promises it cannot cause. It is now current_setting('supautils.hint_roles', true), which answers NULL instead, and NULL is itself the finding. | 2026-08-16 RE-MEASURED, AND THE ENTRY POINTS ARE GROWING: 14 on 2026-08-08, TWENTY today. The parked migration held and the drip did not, because nothing was holding it. New gate shipped for that.  STILL REPRODUCES on public.ecr.aws/supabase/postgres:17.6.1.106 with all 609 migrations applied. scripts/db-denied-rpc-crash-check.mjs run 2026-08-16: connection dropped mid-statement, backend-crash/recovery line in the server log, no clean permission-denied returned. hint_roles is still 'anon, authenticated, service_role'. So AC1's local half is unchanged and the mitigation is still the host config change, not anything in this repo.  ⚠ I NEARLY REPORTED THE OPPOSITE. I first wrote my own probe with the scratch function in a CUSTOM SCHEMA (us2403_probe) and got a clean 'permission denied for function' with the session alive - which reads exactly like 'the image was fixed'. The existing check puts the function in PUBLIC and crashes every time. Whatever the mechanism, a custom-schema function is not a valid probe for this, and a probe that differs from the real shape in one detail produces a confident all-clear. Deleted my duplicate rather than keeping two probes that disagree. (My first version also discarded psql's STDERR because execFileSync does not return it on a zero exit, so it saw zero errors where there were two.)  THE ACTUAL FINDING, and it is a new one. 00527 is parked as .BLOCKED and that genuinely works - apply-prod-migrations.sh globs *.sql. But NOTHING stopped the same thing arriving ONE FUNCTION AT A TIME, and it did: 00560, 00594, 00595, 00596 and 00606 each shipped a REVOKE on a public function AFTER this story was raised on 2026-08-04. Five migrations, six new functions anon may not execute, each one an HTTP call away from restarting the database with the anon key that ships in the browser bundle. Enumerated from the live schema, not by hand: the 14 from 2026-08-08 plus flipdesk_listing_performance_page, flipdesk_listing_performance_summary, help_zero_result_queries, prune_api_idempotency_records, record_help_article_view and redact_subscription_event_pii. 20 of 175 public functions.  None of those five was WRONG to want the permission. The point is that the hold was on one file when the risk was in the corpus.  SHIPPED: src/test/us2403-function-revoke-gate.test.ts. Fails when any migration not on a named allowlist revokes function EXECUTE from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated; the allowlist may only SHRINK, so an entry that stops matching also fails and nobody can widen it by editing a file it names. It also pins that 00527 keeps the .BLOCKED suffix, because the suffix IS the mechanism. The failure message says not to add an entry to make it pass, and points at the mitigation and at 00609 for the shape of a migration that deliberately does not revoke.  THE ALLOWLIST WAS SEEDED WRONG THE FIRST TIME and the scanner caught it: a ripgrep sweep found 26 files, and the scanner found 5 more (00216, 00317, 00490, 00501, 00503) whose REVOKE spans several lines around a long argument list. Line-oriented greps under-report this corpus - worth knowing before trusting one about permissions again.  SABOTAGE-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS, and one came back SILENT because the SABOTAGE was incomplete rather than the guard weak: 00596 has THREE revoke lines and I removed two, so the file still matched and the guard was right to stay green. The harness now refuses to report a result when a REVOKE survives the mutation. The four: a new migration revoking from anon, the same spread over multiple lines, 00527 renamed back to .sql, and an allowlisted entry that stops matching.  STILL OPEN, unchanged: AC1's PROD half (§23 of prod-diagnostics.sql asks for it, read-only), AC2 (the host config change on Coolify - cannot be done from SQL, supautils rejects ALTER SYSTEM on that parameter even as superuser), and AC4 (un-park 00527, close US-2282) which is downstream of AC2. AC5 is updated above. When AC2 lands: re-run the crash check, then DELETE the new gate along with un-parking 00527 - it is scaffolding for a blocked state, not a permanent rule. | 🔒 OWNER DECISION 2026-08-16: 00527 IS A DO NOT APPLY. Permanent, not a hold waiting on US-2403. Given directly, in response to this session repeatedly recommending 'clear supautils.hint_roles on the host, then apply 00527' - that is NOT the route.  WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the hole is still live and still demonstrated. An anonymous caller holding only the public anon key called grant_grade_credits and moved a real balance 0 -> 999, then debit_grade_credits took it to 998. Eight of ten credit functions are anon-executable, and four analytics RPCs (ai_spend, ai_profitability, funnel_metrics, retention_cohorts) return documents to anon.  SO THE REMEDY IS THE PER-FUNCTION CHECK, which was already recorded here as the smaller interim option and is now the ONLY option: an internal authorization guard inside each function, exactly as admin_revenue_metrics already has one (it answers 42501 'admin role required' to the same anon call, which is why it is the model rather than a hypothetical).  AND IT IS THE BETTER ROUTE FOR A REASON THAT WAS ALREADY IN THE EVIDENCE: it revokes NOTHING, so it never arms the US-2403 segfault. The deadlock this story was in only existed because both proposed fixes went through REVOKE. A function that checks its caller and raises is a normal error path, not a denied call. It also fixes the analytics leak by the same mechanism, so one shape of change covers both classes.  The .BLOCKED suffix stays. apply-prod-migrations.sh globs *.sql, so the file is inert where it sits; nothing needs to be deleted and renaming it back is now wrong rather than merely premature. | 2026-08-22 THE FIVE POST-FINDING ENTRY POINTS, READ ONE BY ONE. The us2403-function-revoke-gate ledger records five migrations that shipped after the 2026-08-04 finding and calls each 'a live crash entry point'. That is the right posture for a gate, and the actual exposure is narrower and worth stating precisely, because 'five live crash entry points' and what is below lead to different urgency.  ⚠ NOTHING HERE WAS TESTED BY CALLING. Reproducing this defect means crashing the production database, so every line below is read off the migration source and the caller tree, never executed.  REVOKED FROM anon ONLY, WITH authenticated STILL GRANTED - so the real callers are unaffected:   00560 flipdesk_listing_performance_summary / _page - revoked from PUBLIC and anon, granted to authenticated and service_role. Called from src/pages/flipdesk/listing-performance.tsx, i.e. a signed-in seller, which is granted.   00594 flipdesk_overview_metrics - revoked from anon, granted to authenticated and service_role. Called from src/hooks/use-flipdesk-overview.ts, src/lib/north-star.ts and src/lib/overview-range.ts, all signed-in surfaces.  REVOKED FROM anon AND authenticated, service_role only - and every caller is already the service-role client, so there is no legitimate path that trips them:   00595 redact_subscription_event_pii - called from routes/account.ts and routes/admin-compliance.ts (edge).   00596 prune_api_idempotency_records - called from lib/data-retention.ts (edge).   00606 record_help_article_view + help_zero_result_queries - called from routes/help-center.ts through supabaseAdmin, three call sites, all service-role.  SO THE RESIDUAL RISK IS SHARPER THAN THE LEDGER IMPLIES: no legitimate application path reaches a denied grant on any of the five. What remains is a DIRECT call with the anon key - which is the public key shipped in the frontend bundle, so it is available to anyone - against a function name that is discoverable from PostgREST's own OpenAPI document. That is not a theoretical adversary; it is one curl.  Which is the argument for AC1 being answered rather than deferred: the exposure does not depend on our code doing anything wrong, so no amount of caller review closes it. Only knowing whether anon is in supautils.hint_roles on the prod database does, and that is one read-only line.  ALSO CONFIRMED SAFE, since it sits next to this: 00527_revoke_public_function_execute.sql.BLOCKED is genuinely inert. scripts/apply-prod-migrations.sh globs "$DIR"/*.sql and the filename ends in .BLOCKED, so the glob cannot match it. Nothing needs deleting, and renaming it back is wrong rather than premature. | 2026-08-22 THE REACHABLE SURFACE, ENUMERATED. The previous segment said the residual risk is 'one curl' and left it there. Here is the actual list, and it is larger than the guard's five.  ⚠ READ-ONLY. PostgREST's OpenAPI document was fetched with the public anon key and cross-referenced against every REVOKE ... ON FUNCTION ... FROM ... anon in supabase/migrations. NOTHING WAS CALLED - calling a denied function IS the defect, and reproducing it crashes production.  MEASURED: PostgREST advertises 99 RPC endpoints to the anon key. 21 functions are revoked from anon by some migration. SIX are in BOTH sets - advertised by name in a document anyone can fetch, and denied to the role that fetches it:   data_integrity_scan   flipdesk_overview_metrics   north_star_lifetime_counts   north_star_weekly_counts   refund_snap   reserve_snap  The other 15 revoked functions are not advertised, so reaching them needs a guessed name rather than a read - lower, not zero.  WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE LEDGER'S FIVE. The us2403-function-revoke-gate ledger tracks migrations that shipped after the finding, which is the right thing for a ratchet to track. It is not the same question as 'what can an anonymous caller reach today'. Four of these six (data_integrity_scan, north_star_lifetime_counts, north_star_weekly_counts, refund_snap, reserve_snap) are not on that list at all, because their revokes pre-date 2026-08-04. Pre-dating the finding makes them older, not safer.  SO AC1 IS NOT A FORMALITY. If anon is present in supautils.hint_roles on the prod database, there are six named, publicly-discoverable ways to restart the database, and no application change closes any of them - the calls do not come through our code. If anon is absent, AC1 closes as does-not-reproduce and this whole surface is inert.  That is one read-only line, and it decides between 'nothing to do' and 'six live entry points'. It is the highest ratio of answer-to-effort anywhere in this backlog. | 2026-08-22 AC5 IS ANSWERED BY THE ENUMERATION ABOVE, and the answer is bigger than the criterion assumed. AC5 names 5 functions revoked from anon before this was known (refund_grade 00048, credit_ledger_reconciliation 00093, release_job_lock + try_acquire_job_lock 00094, reserve_snap/refund_snap 00099, reconcile_payout_link 00117, equity_snapshot_owners). The migrations actually carry 21 such functions, and the six that are ALSO advertised in PostgREST's public OpenAPI document are the ones that matter: data_integrity_scan, flipdesk_overview_metrics, north_star_lifetime_counts, north_star_weekly_counts, refund_snap, reserve_snap. Only two of those six appear in AC5's list.  AC3 IS BLOCKED ON DOCKER, not on design. It wants a throwaway-stack test that revokes EXECUTE on a scratch function, calls it as anon, and asserts a clean 'permission denied for function' with the connection still alive. That needs the local Supabase stack, and the daemon on this host has been wedged since roughly 23:00 - `docker info` does not return, which is US-2788. Writing the test without being able to run it once would produce exactly the guard-that-does-not-guard this repo keeps finding, so it is deliberately not written blind.  SO THE STORY IS DOWN TO TWO THINGS, both needing a person: the read-only psql line (AC1/AC6), and Docker being restarted so AC3's regression check can be written against a stack that can actually prove it fails the right way. | 2026-08-23 AC3 IS DONE, AND IT IS BETTER THAN 'WRITTEN' - IT FIRED. The earlier segment said AC3 was blocked on Docker rather than on design, and that writing the check blind would produce exactly the guard-that-does-not-guard this repo keeps finding. Docker came back today and scripts/db-denied-rpc-crash-check.mjs ran for the first time on this host, inside `node scripts/verify.mjs --db`. It FAILED, which is the correct and useful outcome:    US-2403 REGRESSION - a denied function call did not fail cleanly:     - the connection was dropped mid-statement (the crash signature)     - the server log gained a backend-crash / recovery line during the call       - every OTHER connected session was terminated too     - no clean 'permission denied for function' error was returned     supautils.hint_roles = "anon, authenticated, service_role"  ALL THREE ASSERTIONS FIRED TOGETHER, which matters more than any one of them. The check's own header records that two earlier drafts could not fail: one asserted on pg_postmaster_start_time(), which a backend SIGSEGV does not change because crash recovery leaves the postmaster alive, and one counted crash markers out of execFileSync's stdout when Postgres logs to stderr. A guard whose three independent signals all fire on a live reproduction is not in that category any more.  SO THE VULNERABILITY IS CONFIRMED PRESENT ON THE LOCAL IMAGE TODAY, and the advisory-not-gate decision in scripts/verify.mjs is vindicated by the same run: gating here would have turned every migration PR red from the moment it landed, and a permanently red check gets switched off.  WHAT IS STILL OPEN IS UNCHANGED AND IS ONLY AC1/AC6: does the PROD image reproduce it. That is one read-only line over psql - `show supautils.hint_roles;` - and it decides between 'nothing to do' and 'six named, publicly-discoverable ways to restart the database'. It cannot be answered from here: the setting is a GUC with no RPC in front of it, and the only other way to ask is to call a revoked function, which IS the outage. Still the highest ratio of answer-to-effort in this backlog. | [2026-09-02][PROD READ] AC1/AC6 ANSWERED: PROD DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Source: scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql run read-only against prod over SSH on 2026-09-02 (container supabase-db-kcksoks4kk0kswk0ccs40os8, 29 sections, 0 SQL errors). Raw output kept out of the repo; it contains customer data. current_setting('supautils.hint_roles', true) returns NULL/empty on the production image, read the safe way rather than via SHOW. No hint path, so a denied function call from anon or authenticated returns an error instead of segfaulting the backend. That matches the outside-in corroboration recorded on 2026-08-15 (probe-supautils-hint.mjs). AC2's mitigation is therefore already satisfied and nothing needs clearing or upgrading. The remaining value in this story is AC3, a regression check that survives an image upgrade.

userStories.title: Prod Postgres + storage host has no full-disk encryption — a pulled or reclaimed VPS disk is readable plaintext
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the block device holding prod Postgres and the Supabase storage volume to be encrypted at rest, so that a decommissioned, snapshotted or physically seized Contabo disk does not hand over every grade, user address, credit ledger row and garment photo in plaintext.
acceptanceCriteria: The prod host's Postgres data directory and the Supabase storage volume (STORAGE_DIR=/var/lib/supabase/storage, per vault/10-ops/backups.md:75) both sit on a LUKS-encrypted block device — verified by 'lsblk -o NAME,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT' showing crypto_LUKS under the mountpoint, not by reading a runbook.

The LUKS passphrase/keyfile is stored in the same secrets manager as the other prod secrets and is listed in vault/10-ops/key-rotation.md's rotation table with its rotation procedure, alongside EDGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY.

A documented unlock path exists for unattended reboot (keyfile on a separate volume, or clevis/tang, or an explicit 'operator must unlock manually' decision) and vault/10-ops/incident-response.md records what happens to uptime if the host reboots while nobody is available to unlock.
vault/10-ops/deploy.md gains a section stating the encryption status of the prod volumes, so a future operator rebuilding the host does not silently recreate it unencrypted.

SECURITY.md's at-rest paragraph (currently line 44, which claims only 'Marketplace OAuth tokens are encrypted at rest') is updated to state the volume-level posture accurately — either encrypted, or explicitly not.

OPERATOR: full-disk encryption is a host action on the Contabo box and nothing in this repository can perform or verify it. Enable it, then fill in the key's storage LOCATION (never its value) in vault/10-ops/key-rotation.md — AC2 was deliberately left undone because there is no key to list until you create one, and a placeholder row in a key inventory is how a key inventory stops being trusted.
userStories.notes: | 2026-08-12 THE RUNBOOK A REBUILD FOLLOWS DID NOT MENTION THIS AT ALL. vault/10-ops/deploy.md had zero occurrences of encrypt, volume or LUKS across every heading, while vault/10-ops/encryption-at-rest.md:48-49 has stated for weeks that both the Postgres data directory and Supabase Storage STORAGE_DIR are unencrypted, and :147-149 names this story. So the fact existed and the document someone would actually follow while provisioning a replacement host did not carry it - which is precisely how a host gets rebuilt without encryption and the window closes again. ADDED a "If you are rebuilding the host, not just deploying to it" section to deploy.md, before Related, saying plainly that provisioning is the ONLY moment volume encryption is cheap (adding it later needs downtime and a restore), naming both volumes, and linking [[encryption-at-rest]] as the owner of the inventory rather than restating it. It also names the two decisions that have to be made first, because both have an uptime consequence and neither is mine: how the volume unlocks at boot (a keyfile on the same disk defends a reclaimed drive but not a live compromise; clevis/tang or a manual passphrase each trade automation for reboot behaviour), and where that key is recorded - which is [[key-rotation]] job once one exists. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: AC2 (list the key in key-rotation.md) - there is no LUKS key to list until the operator creates one, and adding a placeholder row to a key inventory is how a key inventory stops being trustworthy. AC5 is already satisfied: SECURITY.md:40-45 defers to encryption-at-rest.md as SSOT and that note carries the gap. WHAT REMAINS IS HOST WORK: the LUKS setup itself and the unlock-path decision. vault:lint --strict clean at 172 notes.

userStories.title: Offsite backups are uploaded unencrypted — R2 credentials alone yield a full plaintext database dump
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want every backup artifact encrypted with a key we hold before it leaves the host, so that compromise of the Cloudflare R2 bucket or its rclone credentials does not expose the entire production database and every uploaded garment photo.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/ops/backup-postgres.sh encrypts the pg_dump artifact with a key held by GradeThread (age or gpg) BEFORE the 'rclone copy' at line 55, so the object landing in r2:gradethread-backups/pg is ciphertext. R2's own server-side encryption does not satisfy this AC — the threat model is a leaked R2 credential, which server-side encryption is transparent to.

The .sha256 sidecar (backup-postgres.sh:50) is computed over the ENCRYPTED artifact, so the existing 'dump plus its .sha256 in the last 24h' offsite check from vault/10-ops/backups.md:50 still verifies what is actually stored.

scripts/ops/backup-storage.sh either encrypts the storage mirror or the runbook explicitly records the decision not to, with the reason — an rclone sync of the raw storage volume today exposes every submission image, including grading label photos, to anyone with the R2 credential.

scripts/ops/restore-postgres.sh and restore-drill.sh decrypt before pg_restore, and a restore drill against an ENCRYPTED artifact passes and is recorded in the drill table at vault/10-ops/backups.md:162 — an encryption change that breaks restore is worse than no encryption.

The backup encryption key is added to vault/10-ops/key-rotation.md's rotation table with a stated procedure, and the procedure covers the window where old ciphertext in the 30-day-retention bucket was written under the previous key.
vault/10-ops/backups.md documents that losing the backup key means losing every backup, and names where the key is stored (a reference, never the value).

OPERATOR: the mechanism is built and verified; production has not moved. Generate the age keypair, put the identity somewhere off the DB host (never on it - the host holds only the recipient half on purpose), set BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT, install the updated scripts/ops/*.sh on the DB host, and run one drill against an ENCRYPTED artifact. Until then every offsite object is still plaintext.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-08 ALL SIX ACs BUILT AND VERIFIED END TO END; kept passes:false because the mechanism is done and PRODUCTION HAS NOT MOVED — the keypair does not exist yet and the updated scripts are not on the DB host. Docker plus an age implementation were both available here, so nothing below is reasoned-about; every claim was run. MECHANISM (AC1): backup-postgres.sh encrypts the dump with age to BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT before rclone copy. PUBLIC-key on purpose — the DB host holds only the recipient half, so it can encrypt but not decrypt, and rooting the database box does not also hand over the offsite archive. It FAILS CLOSED: with RCLONE_REMOTE set and no recipient it exits 1 having called rclone ZERO times (verified with a stub rclone on PATH that logs its argv). Happy path verified the same way: the only two objects handed to rclone are .dump.age and .dump.age.sha256, never the plaintext .dump. AC2: the sha256 is computed over the CIPHERTEXT, which is what the bucket actually holds. FOUND AND FIXED A PRE-EXISTING BUG WHILE DOING IT, and it would have bitten during a real recovery: sha256sum \"\" wrote the sidecar with the ABSOLUTE staging path (/backups/pg/...), and restore-postgres.sh verifies with sha256sum -c, which resolves whatever path the sidecar records. On a scratch host that path does not exist, so verification failed with 'No such file or directory' — i.e. the checksum could never have passed on any genuine offsite restore, only on the machine that wrote it. Both branches now cd first and record a BARE FILENAME. Proved by backing up to one directory, copying the artifact to another (what an offsite fetch does), and restoring successfully from there. AC3 (storage): the age-per-file approach does NOT fit an incremental rclone sync of thousands of objects — pre-encrypting per run breaks rclone's diffing. The mechanism is rclone's own CRYPT REMOTE (client-side, per object, sync still works), which is config-side, so what the script can enforce is refusal: backup-storage.sh reads 'rclone config show <remote>' and exits unless type = crypt, overridable only by an explicit STORAGE_BACKUP_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT=1. Checked against the config rather than the remote's NAME, because a remote called 'r2crypt' that is not of type crypt would otherwise read as safe. AC4 (the one the story warns about most — 'an encryption change that breaks restore is worse than no encryption'): restore-postgres.sh detects a .age input, verifies the checksum BEFORE decrypting (checking the stored object, not a derived one), decrypts to a mktemp file chmod 600 created empty before any plaintext is written, and shreds it via an EXIT trap — verified 0 leftover temp files after a run. restore-drill.sh now performs the encrypt/sha/verify/decrypt round-trip on EVERY run under an EPHEMERAL keypair, so the drill never touches the real key and a drill can no longer silently measure a procedure prod does not use (opt out only via DRILL_SKIP_ENCRYPTION=1). Drill PASS recorded in vault/10-ops/backups.md: migration 00559, 5 users, 20 submissions, 375 RLS policies all matched, dump 1s restore 5s. NOTE ON DRILL QUALITY: the first run passed with every row count at ZERO, which makes each 'OK' vacuous — a data-restore failure would have passed too. Seeded real rows and re-ran; the recorded numbers are from that run. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, all four directions: no recipient => refuses and uploads nothing; no identity => refuses to restore; a single flipped byte in the ciphertext => checksum FAILS before decryption is attempted; and the drill asserts the .age artifact is NOT still a readable pg_dump (a passthrough bug would otherwise leave everything green while backups shipped in the clear). DOCS (AC5, AC6): key-rotation.md gains both keys in the rotation table plus a full section — the asymmetry that makes this key unlike every other one is that losing it is SILENT (backups keep running, /health stays green, the bucket keeps filling; you find out at the only moment it matters), and the 30-day-retention window means deleting the old identity on rotation day destroys most of the recovery range, so both identities are kept until the lifecycle rule has aged out the last object under the old one. backups.md gains an Encryption section saying plainly that losing the key loses every backup with no escrow and no support path, requiring two independent durable homes neither of which is the machine being backed up, and naming Infisical as the home for the identity (a reference, never a value) while noting it is NOT an app env var and no deployment surface reads it. Also corrected the offsite-freshness check there: the objects to look for are now .dump.age / .dump.age.sha256, and a bare .dump in the bucket means an OLD script is still deployed and the nightly is shipping plaintext. encryption-at-rest.md is the security-questionnaire page and carries these scripts in its code_refs, so it was updated in the same change per the vault same-commit rule — its store table and gap paragraph now say 'mechanism yes, production not yet' and explicitly tell the reader NOT to upgrade the customer-facing answer until the key exists on the host. vault:lint --strict green, all four ops scripts pass bash -n. REMAINING (operator, on the Contabo/Coolify DB host — this is the whole gap): (1) age-keygen the pair, put the identity in Infisical plus one offline copy, put the public recipient in /etc/cron.d/gradethread-backups; (2) rclone config a crypt remote and repoint the storage cron at it; (3) deploy the updated scripts to /opt/gradethread. Step-by-step is in the MANUAL callout in vault/10-ops/backups.md. Until all three are done prod backups remain plaintext, which is why this stays open. WORTH KNOWING: age has no Windows package, but rage (the Rust build, format-compatible) does — 'scoop install rage', then AGE_BIN=rage. Every script takes AGE_BIN, which is how the drill ran on this host.

userStories.title: Postal addresses and phone numbers are stored as plaintext columns while OAuth tokens next to them are AES-GCM encrypted
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want my home or business street address stored encrypted the same way my marketplace tokens are, so that a single leaked database dump or a SQL-injection read does not hand an attacker a mailing list of resellers with valuable inventory at those addresses.
acceptanceCriteria: public.users.ship_from_address (jsonb, added by 00325_user_business_shipping_profile.sql) and public.users.business_phone are stored as AES-256-GCM ciphertext produced by services/edge-functions/src/lib/crypto-aes.ts encryptToken(), with the owning user id passed as the aad option so a ciphertext copied onto another user's row fails to decrypt (US-268 tenant binding, same pattern as the marketplace token columns).

public.measure_card_requests street fields (ship_name, address_line1, address_line2, city, postal_code — added by 00351_measure_card_requests.sql) are encrypted the same way, keyed to owner_user_id. state and country stay plaintext so the fulfillment export can still filter and sort by region without decrypting every row.

A migration ships the US-1108 triple: idempotent SQL (safe to re-run on any prior state), EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in services/edge-functions/src/lib/schema-version.ts in the SAME commit, and the self-record footer inserting its version into public.applied_migrations.

The migration backfills existing plaintext rows to ciphertext, and the read path tolerates both during the rollout — a row that does not parse as v1:/v2: is returned as-is rather than throwing, so a partial backfill cannot 500 the Settings page.

Every edge route that reads or writes these columns decrypts/encrypts at the boundary and stays tenant-scoped per US-268, with a case added to services/edge-functions/src/tests/tenant-isolation_test.ts.

The eBay ship-from location prefill (US-1442's original consumer) still populates correctly end to end after the change — verified against the flipdesk-ebay.ts path that consumes ship_from_address, not just by unit test.
A test asserts that decrypting a ship_from_address ciphertext with a DIFFERENT user id as aad throws, proving the tenant binding is real.

OPERATOR: run both backfills against PROD with the real EDGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY — `deno run --allow-net --allow-env scripts/backfill-user-shipping-pii.ts --apply` and the same for scripts/backfill-measure-card-pii.ts. Until they run, the encryption this story shipped applies to NEW writes only and every pre-existing address and phone number is still plaintext, which is the exposure the story was filed for. Both are dry-run by default, both refuse to start without the key, and both are re-runnable (an already-encrypted value passes through rather than double-wrapping, which would be unrecoverable). Run the dry run first and read the row count.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-08 AC2 DONE, AC4 and AC7 DONE for it, and AC1 IS BLOCKED ON A PREREQUISITE THE STORY DOES NOT NAME. The prerequisite is the most important thing in this note, because AC1 reads like a one-file change and is not. AC1 IS NOT REACHABLE YET, and it is a fact about the write path rather than a preference. src/pages/settings.tsx:306 writes users.business_phone and users.ship_from_address DIRECTLY from the browser with supabase-js under RLS, and 00526_users_self_update_allowlist.sql (restated in 00550) explicitly allowlists both columns. They are READ the same way in three places: settings.tsx:141-143, flipdesk/marketplaces.tsx:202 and lib/account-export.ts:54. EDGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is an edge-only secret and must stay one, so encrypting those two columns first requires moving that write and all three reads behind an edge route. Doing the crypto without that would lock a seller out of their own Settings page and would break the account export. iOS and Android touch neither column (grepped both trees, zero hits), so the migration surface is web-only - which makes the prerequisite tractable, just not free. AC3's migration is ALSO wrong for AC1 as written: ship_from_address is jsonb, so storing an envelope string means a type change, not just a value change. AC2 SHIPPED, and measure_card_requests is the more sensitive of the two anyway - it holds a full street address, not a ship-from region. It has none of AC1's problem: deny-all RLS (rls-guard_test.ts:181), written by exactly ONE edge route (flipdesk-measure.ts POST /card-request) and read by exactly ONE (admin-measure-cards.ts listRequests, feeding the fulfilment CSV). Both sides already run where the key lives. NEW services/edge-functions/src/lib/measure-card-pii.ts encrypts ship_name, address_line1, address_line2, city and postal_code with encryptToken() and the OWNER'S USER ID AS AAD. state and country stay plaintext exactly as AC2 asks, and a test asserts the two lists cannot overlap - the export filters and sorts by region, and an equality on an encrypted column cannot use an index or match at all. AC7 IS THE CASE WORTH READING. Encrypting a column is easy to do in a way that helps nobody: one key, no binding, and anyone who can write a row can copy another tenant's ciphertext onto it and read the plaintext back through the normal decrypt path. AES-GCM covers additionalData with the auth tag, so A's address fails to decrypt under B's id. That is the US-268 property expressed in cryptography instead of in an .eq() someone has to remember, and it is asserted rather than assumed. THE WRITE ENCRYPTS BEFORE THE INSERT, not after it. An insert-then-update would leave the address readable in the WAL and in any replica that saw the first version, which is most of what a stolen-dump scenario actually covers. A key misconfiguration answers 503 rather than falling back to plaintext. THE READ USES THE ROW'S OWNER, never a caller-supplied id, and decrypts PER ROW: one un-backfilled or unreadable row must not take out the operator's whole fulfilment queue, so a failure blanks that address and logs the id. A blank that says so beats a plausible-looking wrong address on a mailing label. AC4 - TOLERANCE PLUS A BACKFILL, and the backfill is a SCRIPT because it cannot be a migration. pgcrypto offers AES in CBC/ECB only: no GCM, therefore no auth tag, therefore no AAD - a SQL backfill would produce ciphertext the edge cannot read carrying none of the security this story is about. NEW scripts/backfill-measure-card-pii.ts is DRY-RUN BY DEFAULT (--apply to write), refuses to start without EDGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY (encrypting under the wrong key would make every address silently unreadable while still LOOKING encrypted), and scopes its update by owner_user_id as well as id so a mis-derived id cannot write one seller's owner-bound ciphertext onto another's row, where it would be permanently undecryptable. Re-running it is a no-op: already-encrypted values pass through, so an interrupted run resumes with no bookkeeping. Double-wrapping would be UNRECOVERABLE, since the inner envelope's AAD is invisible from the outside, and a test pins that. MY OWN TEST HAD A BLIND SPOT AND THE SABOTAGE FOUND IT. The route-text check forbade `city:` in the insert, so an accidental SHORTHAND `city,` - which writes the same plaintext and overrides the spread - stayed green. It now checks both forms per column, which has to be per-column rather than 'no shorthand allowed', because `state,` and `country,` are legitimately shorthand there. 10 cases in NEW src/tests/measure-card-pii_test.ts. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED FIVE WAYS: the AAD dropped from both sides (the cross-tenant case fires), postal_code removed from the encrypted set, the insert overriding a column in shorthand form, the same in explicit form, and the admin export decrypting with a caller-supplied id. Each reddened with its own message; all files restored and re-run green. REMAINING: AC1 (needs the settings write + three reads moved behind the edge first), AC3 (no migration was needed for AC2 - the columns are already text and ciphertext fits; AC1's jsonb column is what would need one), AC5's tenant-isolation case, AC6 (the eBay ship-from prefill end-to-end, which consumes users.ship_from_address and is therefore downstream of AC1). VERIFIED: deno lint clean across 1426 files, deno check clean including the backfill script, full edge suite 5999 passed / 0 failed / 170 ignored. | 2026-08-09 AC1, AC3, AC4, AC5 and AC7 DONE for users.*; AC6 REMAINS and its premise was wrong. THE PREREQUISITE THE LAST PASS NAMED IS BUILT. NEW services/edge-functions/src/lib/user-shipping-pii.ts encrypts users.ship_from_address and users.business_phone with encryptToken() and THE ROW'S OWN ID AS AAD; NEW GET/PUT /api/account/shipping-profile in routes/account.ts is the only reader and writer; NEW src/lib/shipping-profile.ts is the only browser client; 00567_users_shipping_pii_edge_only.sql restates guard_users_protected_columns WITHOUT the two columns so a direct browser write now RAISES instead of storing plaintext over ciphertext. The three client reads the last pass listed are all moved: settings.tsx seeds its form from the edge query (a useState initialiser would have captured the pre-fetch nulls forever, hence the seed effect keyed on dataUpdatedAt), flipdesk/marketplaces.tsx prefills the eBay location dialog from the same shared query key, and lib/account-export.ts drops both from its supabase select and fills them from the edge best-effort, because a GDPR export must not fail wholesale over one optional field. AC3'S JSONB WORRY WAS UNFOUNDED, and the resolution is better than the type change would have been. ship_from_address is jsonb and an envelope is a string, but a jsonb column holds a JSON STRING SCALAR perfectly well, so no ALTER COLUMN TYPE and no table rewrite under a lock. Better still, the JSON TYPE becomes the AC4 discriminator: an OBJECT is a row the backfill has not reached, a STRING is an envelope. No prefix sniffing on a value that could legitimately start with anything. 00567 therefore contains NO DDL at all - one CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION plus two column comments - and its risk is entirely in APPLY ORDER, which PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md spells out: apply the SQL, NOTIFY pgrst, redeploy the edge, THEN push. Pushing first ships a frontend calling a route that does not exist. AC4: NEW scripts/backfill-user-shipping-pii.ts, dry-run by default, refuses to start without EDGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY, re-runnable because an already-encrypted value passes through rather than double-wrapping (which is unrecoverable - the inner AAD is invisible from outside). Read tolerates both formats, so there is no deadline on running it. AC5: BOTH edge readers were found and both decrypt at the boundary - routes/account.ts and routes/flipdesk-logistics.ts (the label quote). Grepped functions/, ios/ and android/: zero hits, confirming the last pass's finding. A containment case is appended to tenant-isolation_test.ts, and the property it pins is the one that is easy to get wrong here: this endpoint reads c.get('userId') and NOT c.get('workspaceOwnerId'), because a manager inside A's workspace must not read A's home address, so the case sends X-Workspace-Owner pointed at A and asserts B's write never lands on A. AC7: 12 cases in NEW user-shipping-pii_test.ts including the cross-tenant AAD rejection for BOTH columns and the refusal to encrypt with an empty owner id (an unbound ciphertext any account could read is worse than a failed write). ALSO ADDED, because the type system could not carry this alone: UserRow.business_phone and .ship_from_address are now typed EncryptedColumn (a branded string), so reaching for .line1 is a compile error, and NEW src/test/encrypted-user-columns.test.ts catches the two shapes tsc cannot see - reading the column off the cached auth-store profile row, and naming it inside a supabase-js call against users. Negative-verified by planting a select on the users update in settings.tsx. AC6 IS NOT DONE AND ITS TARGET DOES NOT EXIST. It asks for verification 'against the flipdesk-ebay.ts path that consumes ship_from_address'. GREPPED: flipdesk-ebay.ts does not read that column and never has. POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/policies/location takes postal_code/city/state FROM THE REQUEST BODY - the column only ever fed the browser-side PREFILL of that dialog, which now reads the edge query instead. The genuine edge consumer is flipdesk-logistics.ts (the label quote), and two cases were added to ebay-logistics_test.ts for it: an undecrypted envelope yields NO address rather than a partial one (so the failure is a 409, not a wrong shipping label), plus a source guard that the handler decrypts before calling toLogisticsAddress - needed because a seller with no address and a seller whose address failed to decrypt otherwise produce the identical 409 and nothing would notice the decrypt going missing. WHAT REMAINS FOR AC6 is a live end-to-end pass that cannot be run from here: create an eBay merchant location from a seller account whose address was written BEFORE this change and then backfilled, and buy one label, confirming the ship-from on both. Needs real eBay credentials and a seeded prod-like account. VERIFIED: deno lint clean, deno check src/main.ts + the backfill script clean, full edge suite 6177 passed / 0 failed, npx tsc -b clean, npm run lint 0 errors, ui:check 0 blocking, web suite green, vault:lint --strict clean. HELD MIGRATION 00567 - do NOT push until it is applied to prod. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-09 (second half of the day): the HELD-migration claim in this story's notes is now STALE. Migrations 00550 and 00567 are on origin/main - verified with git ls-tree against a freshly fetched origin/main, not inferred - and the branch has zero unpushed commits. A held migration is by definition unpushed, so the word is no longer merely out of date, it is an active instruction to stop on a branch that is not frozen. Nothing in this story is blocked on a push. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: pushed is not applied. Whether the SQL has been run against prod is an operator fact this checkout cannot observe, and PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md is the file that tracks it. Read that, not this prose. Recorded because prd-lint caught it the same hour the branch moved, which is the guard working as intended - it went unactioned for weeks before, and a stale freeze cost real sessions. | 2026-08-12 THE VAULT INVENTORY WAS UNDERSTATING OUR OWN POSTURE, and that is the half of this story that was quietly wrong. SECURITY.md:40-45 names vault/10-ops/encryption-at-rest.md as the single source of truth for security questionnaires, and that note still listed all seven columns THIS STORY ENCRYPTED under "What is NOT encrypted at the column level": measure_card_requests ship_name/address_line1/address_line2/city/postal_code (encrypted at lib/measure-card-pii.ts:57-61,101 with aad: ownerUserId) and users.ship_from_address + users.business_phone (lib/user-shipping-pii.ts:116,164). Its headline sentence - the one someone actually answers a questionnaire from - said "OAuth tokens and a handful of cache values are encrypted by the application. Nothing else is." WHY THE DRIFT GUARD NEVER FIRED: neither lib was in the note code_refs, so vault:lint had nothing to compare against; the note reviewed date was 2026-08-08 and the users.* half landed 2026-08-09. A note that omits the file it describes is invisible to the guard that exists to catch exactly this. Both libs are now in code_refs, so the same omission cannot recur silently. FIXED: the three columns groups moved into the encrypted table with their AAD, the NOT-encrypted list narrowed to what is genuinely left (consignors.contact_phone, and measure_card_requests.state/.country), and the headline rewritten. Both read paths tolerate either form so the mixed state is safe, but "these columns are encrypted" is only true of the whole table after scripts/backfill-measure-card-pii.ts and scripts/backfill-user-shipping-pii.ts run against prod with EDGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY set. The encryption is live for NEW writes; every row that existed before it is still plaintext until someone runs the two scripts with the real key. userStories.title: Email-keyed PII retained for accounts deleted BEFORE the US-2005 purge shipped is still queryable
userStories.description: US-2005 added an email-keyed purge to the deletion path, so erasure is complete from that point on. It is not retroactive. Every account deleted before it shipped left its address — and in email_deliveries the full rendered html of every email we sent it — in the seven tables EMAIL_PURGE_PLAN now covers. Those users asked to be forgotten and were told {deleted:true}. The deletion log written by routes/account.ts records who was deleted and when, so the population is identifiable rather than hypothetical, which is what makes this actionable rather than a shrug.
acceptanceCriteria: Run the census against production and record the numbers: distinct addresses per planned table, split live_account vs unattributable. It reports no deleted_account bucket, and that absence is the finding rather than a gap in the tool - account_deletion_log holds no address (00064) and email_deliveries has no user_id at all (00095), so the population this story was filed to purge cannot be identified from the data that survives.

The per-subject path is the achievable form of the original AC2/AC3 and already exists: scripts/purge-email-subject.ts calls purgeEmailKeyedPii, the same plan the live endpoint runs, idempotent by construction and refusing an address that belongs to a live account.

A BULK backfill over the unattributable set is refused rather than deferred. Waitlist entries and newsletter subscribers are in that set by definition, having never held an account; running the purge plan over it would erase people who never asked to be forgotten, on the theory that some of them might be someone else.

Confirm the data-retention cron is actually scheduled in production (US-2002). email_deliveries is the largest reservoir and US-2021 already drains it - sent rows after 90 days, dead-letter bodies after 180 - but only if the sweep runs. If it does not, every census number is growing rather than draining and reading it as stable is wrong.
DONE: the regulator-facing answer is recorded in vault/10-ops/data-retention.md under Deletion (right to erasure), including what can and cannot be said about erasures made before US-2005.

OPERATOR: run the PII census against prod (the single remaining item). Read-only, has no --apply and never will, and never prints an address. Record the numbers on this story, and treat a missing deleted_account bucket as THE FINDING rather than as a query that came back empty - the population cannot be established from the deletion log, which is why the AC asks for a census rather than a backfill.
userStories.notes: [P2][Compliance/GDPR][OPERATOR] Filed 2026-08-08 from US-2005, which fixed the path forward and explicitly left this as a prod data task. CANNOT be done from a dev checkout: it needs the production database. The code half already exists — purgeEmailKeyedPii takes an address and an IO seam, so the operator half is a script that enumerates addresses and calls it. Pairs with US-2433; both are operator-run data tasks and would share one runbook. | 2026-08-10 THIS STORY'S PREMISE IS FALSE AND THE BACKFILL IT ASKS FOR MUST NOT BE RUN. The description says "The deletion log written by routes/account.ts records who was deleted and when, so the population is identifiable rather than hypothetical". It does not. Three facts, each read off the schema rather than assumed: (1) account_deletion_log HOLDS NO ADDRESS, deliberately — migration 00064's own header says the retained id is "opaque, no-longer-resolvable ... it cannot be joined back to any PII". It proves THAT an account id was erased on a date; it cannot say WHOSE address that was. That was the right call for a compliance record and it is precisely what makes this backfill impossible. (2) email_deliveries — the worst table, the one holding the full rendered html — HAS NO user_id COLUMN AT ALL (00095). Nothing to join, not even a severed link. (3) Every other planned table either severs its user link ON DELETE SET NULL (marketing_send_log.owner_user_id, email_subscribers.user_id, waitlist_entries.user_id) or never had one of its own (email_journey_step_sends). So NULL means "account deleted" OR "never had an account" and nothing distinguishes them. THE DANGEROUS PART IS NOT THAT AC1 IS UNANSWERABLE, IT IS THAT A PROXY LOOKS RIGHT. "An address in a planned table with no live account" reads like the population and is mostly the WRONG PEOPLE: waitlist_entries and email_subscribers exist for people who never had an account, by definition. Running EMAIL_PURGE_PLAN over that set deletes the waitlist and the newsletter list, for subjects who never asked to be forgotten, on the theory that some of them might be someone else. AC1's own warning — "a backfill whose blast radius was never measured is how a cleanup becomes an incident" — is the right instinct aimed at the wrong risk: the danger is not the SIZE of the set, it is that it is the wrong set. SHIPPED INSTEAD, three things. (a) src/lib/email-residue-census.ts + scripts/email-residue-census.ts: counts distinct addresses per planned table, split into live_account and unattributable, driven off EMAIL_PURGE_PLAN so it cannot drift from the plan. There is NO deleted_account bucket and no delete path, and both absences are pinned by tests — a bucket named after a group it cannot identify is how a census becomes a work list. The script has no --apply and never will. It never prints or returns an address, asserted against the STRUCTURE as well as the rendering, because the string check alone passes trivially today and would keep passing if someone added a samples field "for debugging". censusNotes() ships the sentences that must travel with the numbers, as data rather than print statements, so a future admin surface says the same thing. (b) scripts/purge-email-subject.ts: the case that actually arises. A subject writes in, so the address is known and no inference is involved. Calls purgeEmailKeyedPii — the SAME plan the live endpoint runs, which is AC2 in one line. Idempotent by construction (AC3): every operation is delete-by-address or null-by-address, so a second run matches nothing and succeeds; there is no cursor to lose. Dry run by default, and it REFUSES an address belonging to a live account — running the plan on one would delete a current customer's newsletter subscription and waitlist row without deleting their account, a half-erasure nobody asked for and the easiest mistake to make off a support ticket. NOT AN ENDPOINT, the same call US-2433 made: a route that erases on an unverified email claim is a deletion oracle. (c) AC4: vault/10-ops/data-retention.md now carries the whole thing under "Deletion (right to erasure)" — the email-keyed purge itself (which that runbook never mentioned even though US-2005 shipped months ago), the suppression exemption, and a section headed "What we can and cannot say about erasures made before US-2005" giving the answer to hand a regulator. SECOND FINDING, WHICH SHRINKS THE PROBLEM: US-2021 already put email_deliveries on the retention sweep — sent rows DELETED after 90 days, dead_letter bodies stripped after 180 (data-retention.ts:191-240). The largest reservoir this story names is therefore draining on its own, and the story does not know it. Conditional on the data-retention cron actually being scheduled in prod, which this checkout cannot see and which is exactly the US-2002 failure class. So the census reads cron_runs for the last successful data-retention tick and says plainly when there is none, because if the sweep is not running every count is growing rather than draining and reading it as stable would be wrong. STAYS passes:false, and the reason has changed rather than shrunk: nobody has RUN the census (AC1 asks for the count, and that needs prod), and AC2/AC3's bulk form is not merely undone but unachievable — what exists is the per-request path. Whoever picks this up next should re-scope the ACs rather than look for the missing script. VERIFIED: deno check clean on all three new files and on src/main.ts, deno lint clean across 1480 files, full edge suite 6419 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored (+15), vault:index up to date, vault:lint --strict clean across 164 notes. Negative-verified 9 ways, each reddening its own named test: row counts instead of distinct people, the notes dropping the 00064 citation, the do-not-run warning softened, a stopped retention cron reporting as fine, sample addresses kept for debugging, a delete path added to the census module, an --apply added to the census script, the purge no longer refusing a live account, and the census inventing its own table list. TWO OF MY OWN MUTATIONS WERE WRONG BEFORE THE CODE WAS: one broke type-checking rather than a test, and one "leaked" a value the structure cannot hold — the leak test was VACUOUS as first written and is now asserted against JSON.stringify(census), which is falsifiable. | 2026-08-15 ACs RE-SCOPED, which is what the previous note asked the next reader to do rather than hunt for a missing script. Nothing was built this pass and nothing was deleted; the story now asks for what is achievable instead of for a backfill that cannot be aimed. WHAT CHANGED AND WHY. Old AC1 asked to establish the population from the deletion log. The previous pass proved that is impossible from three schema facts, and leaving the AC standing invites the next agent to find the proxy that looks right and is the wrong people. It is now: run the census, record the numbers, and treat the missing deleted_account bucket as the finding. Old AC2/AC3 asked for a bulk re-run of purgeEmailKeyedPii over that population; they are replaced by (a) the per-subject path that exists and (b) an explicit REFUSAL of the bulk form, so a future pass reads a decision rather than an omission - the distinction vault/70-agent/shipped-but-unwired.md exists to keep. A new AC carries the second finding that was buried in prose: the largest reservoir drains on its own under US-2021, but only if the retention cron is actually scheduled, which is the US-2002 failure class. Old AC4 is marked DONE in place rather than removed, since the runbook section it asked for exists. STILL passes:false ON ONE THING, and it is now a single operator action rather than a research problem: run the census against prod. It is read-only, has no --apply and never will, and never prints an address. WHAT I DID NOT DO: add the census counts to scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql, even though that is where every other prod-blocked question in this backlog now lives. The census is driven off EMAIL_PURGE_PLAN precisely so it cannot drift from the plan the live endpoint runs; hand-writing the same counts as SQL would reintroduce exactly that drift, in the file most likely to be copied and edited. The right instruction is to run the script.

userStories.title: The edge hang watchdog did not cap the outage at ~60s, and nothing in the repo can tell whether it is still installed
userStories.description: As the operator, I want the edge-hang safety net verified from the repo, so that a watchdog that has stopped running is discovered before the next hang rather than during it. MEASURED 2026-08-09 from outside, against the public hostname, with no host access: /health/ready answered normally at ~19:06 UTC; at 19:19 requests hung to a full 25s timeout (http=000); at 19:22 both /health and /health/ready were unreachable while gradethread.com returned 200 and api.gradethread.com answered — the exact edge-hang signature; at 19:27 it settled into a fast 503 with the body 'no available server' (Traefik's, meaning the backend was pulled from the pool); it recovered by 19:39. That is AT LEAST ~8 minutes of confirmed failure inside a 33-minute window, against a watchdog that vault/10-ops/edge-hang-vs-crash-loop.md says restarts on unhealthy every minute and 'caps the outage at ~60s'. Grading, payments, eBay writes and Stripe webhooks were all dead for that window while the marketing site and login stayed up — the failure mode that note records as having cost four weeks the first time.
acceptanceCriteria: Establish by MEASUREMENT whether /opt/gradethread/edge-watchdog.sh exists on the host and is actually scheduled (crontab -l), and record the finding either way in vault/10-ops/edge-hang-vs-crash-loop.md. From outside there is no way to distinguish a late watchdog from an absent one, so this cannot be inferred.

If it is missing or not scheduled: restore it, and PROVE the cap by inducing an unhealthy container on a non-production copy and observing the restart, rather than by reading the crontab. The claim being repaired is a timing claim.

The watchdog's existence becomes checkable WITHOUT SSH — its script and schedule live in the repo (or in the schedule artifact US-2313 defines), so its absence is detectable by a check rather than by an outage.

The ~60s cap in vault/10-ops/edge-hang-vs-crash-loop.md is corrected to whatever is measured, or the note states plainly that the cap is unverified. The 2026-08-09 timings are already recorded there and must not be removed — a second occurrence is the evidence.

An alert fires to a human when the public /health/ready is unreachable for longer than the cap, independent of the watchdog itself. A safety net that is also the only detector cannot report its own failure.

OPERATOR: an edge hang is uncapped today - /health/ready reports hostWatchdog unconfigured. Install scripts/ops/edge-watchdog.sh on the host with FLIPDESK_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET, put it on cron, and confirm the readiness line flips to ok (AC1, AC2).
userStories.notes:
2026-08-11 AC3, AC4 and AC5 DONE. AC1 and AC2 are the operator's and cannot be faked from a checkout. THE PROBLEM RESTATED, because the fix only makes sense against it: three states looked IDENTICAL from outside on 2026-08-09 — the watchdog fired late, the watchdog failed, the watchdog was uninstalled months ago. Nothing in the repo could tell them apart, and the only thing that ever reported the answer was the next outage, which is the moment nobody can go and look. AC3 SHIPPED IN FOUR PIECES. (1) scripts/ops/edge-watchdog.sh — the script itself, in version control for the first time, LF-pinned by the existing *.sh gitattributes rule (a CRLF shebang on a cron job is a SILENT no-op, i.e. this exact invisible-absence reintroduced by a line ending). It defers to Docker's own health verdict, and treats an EMPTY health status as 'no healthcheck configured' rather than unhealthy, because restarting on that is a reboot loop. (2) scripts/ops/host-schedules.json — the schedule as data, including the exact crontab line an operator pastes. DELIBERATELY SCOPED TO HOST SCHEDULES ONLY and the file says so: the ~74 EDGE crons have their own registry (CRON_REGISTRY) and US-2313 owns making those verifiable. Two half-registries that disagree is the shape this repo keeps relearning, and folding them here would also read as US-2313 being done. (3) POST /api/jobs/watchdog-heartbeat — the script checks in every minute; the timestamp lands in system_settings ops.edge_watchdog_last_seen, so NO MIGRATION. (4) GET /health/ready reports it as checks.features.hostWatchdog. WHY THAT IS THE ANSWER TO AC3 AND NOT A PROXY FOR IT: the absence now shows up during NORMAL operation, off-host, instead of during an incident. PROD WILL REPORT 'unconfigured' UNTIL THE OPERATOR INSTALLS IT, and that is the correct output rather than a rollout wart — the true state today IS unknown, and an entry saying so is strictly better than the silence it replaces. Same posture US-2001 took with release='dev'. TWO LIMITS STATED IN THE CODE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED: the heartbeat travels THROUGH the service the watchdog protects, so it cannot report during the very outage it bounds — it answers the steady-state question, which is the one that was unanswerable; and it still does not verify the ~60s cap, which is a TIMING claim and needs AC2's induced-unhealthy test on a non-production copy. AC5 was already satisfied by uptime.yml + uptime-check.mjs; what is new is that the probe now surfaces hostWatchdog as a NOTE that can never flip up/down. Paging on it would fire every ten minutes forever until the install happens, and a muted monitor is worse than none — but it rides along on the FAILING line too, which is the moment 'was the watchdog even running?' is the first question anyone asks. AC4: the vault warning block previously said the script 'is not in this repo... so nothing in the checkout can tell you whether it is still installed'. That sentence is now false, so it is quoted as the thing that was true and replaced, rather than deleted — the 2026-08-09 timings stay exactly as AC4 requires. GUARDS: scripts/host-schedules.test.mjs (10 cases, pins manifest/script/crontab agreement, the LF shebang, the Docker-verdict deference, the heartbeat wiring and the staleness number in both places) and services/edge-functions/src/tests/watchdog-heartbeat_test.ts (4 BEHAVIOURAL cases) plus 5 new health_test.ts cases. ⚠ ONE SABOTAGE PROVED NOTHING FIRST TIME AND THAT IS THE REUSABLE PART: disabling the secret gate to 'if (false)' left both the strings 'requireJobSecret' and '401' in the file, so my token-search assertion stayed GREEN over a dead gate. A dead gate and a live one are indistinguishable to a token search. Replaced with a pinned whole-branch regex, a gate-before-write ordering assertion, AND the behavioural test that actually calls the handler with no secret, a wrong secret and an empty configured secret. That mattered here specifically: an unauthenticated writer could forge a heartbeat and make an absent watchdog read as healthy, turning the detector into a source of false confidence — worse than the blind spot it fills. SIX SABOTAGES in total, each reddening its own case: manifest cron disagreeing with the crontab line, the script restarting without asking Docker, the gate disabled (reddens 3 behavioural cases AND the strengthened scan), the uptime note starting to decide up/down, readiness gating on the feature map, and health.ts re-spelling the settings key instead of importing it. AC1 AND AC2 REMAIN AND ARE OPERATOR WORK: confirm the script is present and on cron (crontab -l), then PROVE the cap by inducing an unhealthy container on a non-production copy and timing the restart. The claim being repaired is a timing claim; a crontab read cannot establish it.
