VERIFIED: test:scripts 386 passed / 20 files, health_test.ts 22 passed (5 new), watchdog-heartbeat_test.ts 4 passed (new), deno lint clean across 1503 files, deno check clean on main.ts, vault:lint --strict clean at 172 notes. NO MIGRATION — the heartbeat rides an existing system_settings row. | THE DRIFT GUARD CAUGHT THE NEW ROUTE, and the fix is the part worth reading. cron-registry-drift_test.ts asserts every /api/jobs/* route in main.ts has a CRON_REGISTRY entry, and mine did not — correctly, since I had added one. But REGISTERING it would have been wrong: CRON_REGISTRY drives the operator docs (COOLIFY.md and launch-checklist.md embed renderCronDocs() verbatim), so every entry reads as 'create this task in the Coolify UI', and this endpoint is called by a HOST cron. An entry would have instructed the operator to build a second, duplicate scheduler. Exempted instead, with the escape hatch closed: a new test asserts any exempted endpoint APPEARS in scripts/ops/host-schedules.json, so the exemption can only MOVE a route from one registry to the other and can never leave it unregistered. Negative-verified — deleting the manifest's heartbeat block reddens that case. | 2026-08-12 AC1 ANSWERED FROM OUTSIDE, AND THE ANSWER IS NO WATCHDOG. GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns, in features: hostWatchdog: "unconfigured: no host watchdog has ever checked in - an edge hang would not be capped (install scripts/ops/edge-watchdog.sh, US-2447)". So one of three things is true and they are operationally identical: the script is not on the host, it is on the host but not on cron, or it is running without FLIPDESK_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET. AN EDGE HANG IS CURRENTLY UNCAPPED. Recorded in vault/10-ops/edge-hang-vs-crash-loop.md as AC1 asks, with the measurement quoted rather than summarised. THE PART WORTH GENERALISING: AC1 says "from outside there is no way to distinguish a late watchdog from an absent one, so this cannot be inferred". That was TRUE when it was written and was made FALSE by this story own AC3 - the heartbeat is exactly the mechanism that distinguishes them. Absent-versus-installed is now one unauthenticated GET; late-versus-on-time is still genuinely unanswerable from outside, and that is what AC2 timing proof is for. An AC that declares something unknowable is worth re-reading after the same story ships the thing that makes it knowable. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, said plainly so nobody over-reads it: the heartbeat shipped AFTER the 2026-08-09 incident, so "has ever checked in" means "since the heartbeat existed" and cannot retroactively tell us whether the watchdog was installed during that outage. It makes the NEXT one diagnosable, which was the point. AC1 recording half is now done; the install half (AC2) and the AC5 alert remain operator work on the Coolify host. | 2026-08-17 THE WATCHDOG NOTE THIS STORY SHIPPED HAS NEVER ONCE FIRED, and finding that is worth more than the fix. scripts/ops/uptime-check.mjs read JSON.parse(body)?.checks?.features?.hostWatchdog. On the real /health/ready, `features` is a SIBLING of `checks`, not a child - top-level keys are status, checks, features, schema, timestamp, and `checks` holds only database and env.  WHY IT WAS SILENT rather than loud: an optional chain over a wrong path returns undefined, and the guard's own `typeof state !== 'string'` arm treats undefined identically to 'the field is healthy'. So the note returned null on every run since it shipped. Its entire purpose was to put 'was the watchdog even running?' into the body of an incident issue, and it would have been BLANK in exactly the moment it was written for - the same shape as the defect this story is about, one level up.  Fixed, and now measured against production rather than reasoned about. A live run prints:   Edge readiness (database): UP (HTTP 200) [hostWatchdog: unconfigured: no host watchdog has   ever checked in ...]  SIX CASES in scripts/ops/uptime-check.test.mjs, built on a REAL CAPTURED RESPONSE rather than a hand-made fixture - a fixture shaped the way the reader assumed would have passed against the broken path too, which is how this survived. One case asserts the WRONG shape yields nothing, so restoring the old path cannot go green. Sabotage-verified: restoring it reddens three.  TARGETS is now exported and the main block is behind an entry-point check, because the test imports it and the module's top level is await against real production hostnames - an unguarded import would have fired a full uptime probe, and with a token present opened a GitHub issue, as a side effect of a unit test.  AC5 IS SUBSTANTIALLY SATISFIED AND WAS ALREADY, which nobody had noticed. .github/workflows/ uptime.yml runs every 10 minutes on GitHub-hosted runners - infrastructure external to Cloudflare, Coolify AND Supabase, so it is independent of both the edge and the watchdog, which is exactly what AC5 asks for. It probes /health/ready, re-checks a failure after 30s, then alerts by webhook AND by opening a labelled GitHub issue, and exits 1 so the run shows red.  STATED PRECISELY, BECAUSE 'satisfied' OVERSELLS IT: the cadence is 10 minutes and GitHub cron is best-effort, so this does NOT detect an outage that merely exceeds the ~60s cap. It reliably catches one lasting tens of minutes. The 2026-08-09 incident ran 8 to 33 minutes and would have been caught. Closing the gap between 60s and 10 minutes needs a vendor check at 1-minute cadence, which vault/10-ops/uptime-monitoring.md already documents as the upgrade path.  STILL OPEN: AC2, installing scripts/ops/edge-watchdog.sh on the host and proving the cap by inducing a hang. Unchanged, and genuinely operator work. The difference now is that the moment it IS installed, /health/ready flips to ok and the uptime run stops printing the note - so verifying the install is one unauthenticated GET rather than an SSH session. | 2026-08-22 THE WATCHDOG HAS STILL NEVER CHECKED IN, and this is a live gap rather than a paperwork one.  features.hostWatchdog reads: 'unconfigured: no host watchdog has ever checked in - an edge hang would not be capped (install scripts/ops/edge-watchdog.sh, US-2447)'.  READ THAT NEXT TO WHAT AN EDGE HANG COSTS. vault/10-ops/edge-hang-vs-crash-loop.md records one that ran roughly FOUR WEEKS and was read as a traction problem: Sentry held 559 HTTP 503s across 10 users and 425 'Failed to fetch', while the marketing site and Supabase stayed up - so the funnel looked alive while the product was dead, and paid ads ran into it. The container stays alive during a hang, so `restart: unless-stopped` never fires and nothing self-heals. The host watchdog is the only thing that ends it.  The reporting half of this story works - the readiness probe names the gap in plain words, which is why this could be measured from a laptop at all. What is missing is the install: scripts/ops/edge-watchdog.sh on the host, checking in every minute.  MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION 2026-08-22, read-only and repeatable by anyone: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready. No credentials needed. It also reported schema {expected 00647, applied 00648, ahead} and NO features.connector field, which together date the running build: it predates both the 00648 commit and this morning's US-2687 work, so the deployed edge is behind local main by more than a few commits. | 2026-08-23 CONFIRMED STILL UNCONFIGURED, measured rather than assumed, while
checking US-2001 against the same endpoint. No code changed.

GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready reports:

  hostWatchdog: unconfigured: no host watchdog has ever checked in — an edge
  hang would not be capped (install scripts/ops/edge-watchdog.sh, US-2447)

So AC1/AC2 are unchanged: an edge hang is still uncapped today. The readiness
line is the acceptance test - install the script on the host with
FLIPDESK_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET, put it on cron, and this flips to ok on its own.

Worth knowing while you are in there: /health/ready has 14 features and only
FOUR are not plain ok - observability ('set but not satisfied'), release
(US-2001), hostWatchdog (this story) and connector ('live'). Two of the four
are one operator action each. | 2026-08-29 A WRONG DATAPOINT REMOVED, which is worth more here than a new one.

US-2662 recorded, on 2026-08-21, that an edge hang recovered on its own in
~150s and concluded the host watchdog "did its job" - explicitly "the first
datapoint this repo has that it works". I wrote that, and it is wrong.

/health/ready still reports hostWatchdog unconfigured, and the heartbeat route
plus scripts/ops/edge-watchdog.sh both landed 2026-08-11 (f4ca05903), ten days
BEFORE that recovery. So the mechanism was in place, has never reported, and
was not what ended the outage.

AC1 and AC2 are unchanged and now unambiguous: there is no evidence the cap
works, because the watchdog has never run. The corrected note is on US-2662.

userStories.title: Every control in a FlipDesk listings row is named the same thing, so a screen reader cannot tell which garment it is about to reprice
userStories.description: US-2335 ground the unlabelled-control count to zero and the listings table passed that bar the whole time: every inline editor announced "Edit value", the status control "Change status", the checkbox "Select row", the delete button "Delete item". Those are names, so the audit counted them as fixed. But the table renders up to a few hundred virtualized rows with roughly fourteen controls each, and a screen reader user moving down a column hears the same four words repeatedly with nothing identifying the item. A name that does not distinguish is not a usable name, which is the exact caveat src/test/control-labels.test.ts records under AC4 and the exact case the count cannot measure. A second, quieter defect sits in the same rows: the row's own activate label read it.item_title ?? it.listing_title, skipping the US-1569 placeholder fallback that the visible title cell applies, so a row DISPLAYING "Nike Windbreaker" announced itself as "Open Item 42".
acceptanceCriteria: Every per-row control in src/pages/flipdesk/listings-table.tsx names its own row, so two rows never announce identically.
The row name comes from one shared derivation, and the visible title cell uses the same rule, so the spoken and printed titles cannot drift apart again.
An untitled row still gets a distinguishing name: no shared constant fallback, because fresh drafts are exactly the rows most likely to be untitled and would all collapse onto it.
The row identity is a REQUIRED prop on InlineCell and InlineStatusSelect, so the compiler refuses a new call site that forgets it.
A guard fails the build if a fixed-string aria-label reappears inside a row, with a short allowlist for the genuinely table-level controls.
AC4-of-US-2335 still open here: nobody has driven this table with a real screen reader. Distinguishing names are necessary and not sufficient.

OPERATOR: drive the FlipDesk listings table with a real screen reader (AC6) - NVDA on Windows, VoiceOver on macOS. This is the same gap as US-2335's AC4 and it is not a formality: distinguishing names are necessary and not sufficient, and fourteen controls per row is a lot of speech per item however well each is named.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-10 AC1-AC5 DONE, AC6 open and it is the honest one. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG: not a missing name anywhere. Every control in a listings row already had one, which is why US-2335's count read zero on this file the whole time; they were all the SAME name. Seven "Edit value" editors, "Change status", "Select row", "Open full editor", "Delete item", "Open listing", "End listing early", "Relist as a new listing", plus Sold / Mark / Publish / List it / Mark shipped / Mark delivered naming themselves off their visible text. Roughly fourteen per row, across up to a few hundred virtualized rows. NEW MODULE src/lib/item-row-label.ts holds three functions: itemDisplayTitle (the US-1569 placeholder fallback, moved verbatim out of the JSX), itemRowLabel (never empty, never shared) and rowControlLabel. Derived ONCE per row in listings-table.tsx, not per control, so the row cannot introduce itself one way to the checkbox and another way to the price editor. THE FALLBACK CHAIN IS THE INTERESTING PART: itemRowLabel deliberately REFUSES a placeholder title that itemDisplayTitle happily returns. A draft titled "Item 42" with no generated listing title yet should still DISPLAY "Item 42" (that is what the cell did before and changing it would be a silent visual change), but speaking it is wrong, because "Untitled draft" is what every fresh draft is called and a screen of them would all get the same name — the defect, rebuilt, for exactly the rows most likely to hit it. So placeholder falls through to item_number and then to an 8-char id slice. Ugly to hear, distinguishing, and that is the job. DELIBERATELY NOT TRUNCATED: an eBay title runs to 80 chars and two listings often differ only in the size or colourway at the END, so a truncated label would make them announce identically. A label is read once on focus; length costs less than ambiguity. THE COMPILER IS THE GUARD, not a test: rowLabel is a REQUIRED prop on both InlineCell and InlineStatusSelect (label too, on InlineCell). Optional would have been the polite choice and it would have been forgotten. The source-scanning test is the backstop for the shortcut the type cannot catch — passing a literal to satisfy it — plus a scan that fails on any fixed-string aria-label in the file outside a two-entry table-level allowlist. SECOND DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED, unnamed in the story when filed: ClickableRow's activateLabel read `it.item_title ?? it.listing_title`, skipping the US-1569 fallback the title cell applies two lines below it, so a row DISPLAYING "Nike Windbreaker" announced itself "Open Item 42". That is why the visible cell now calls itemDisplayTitle too — one rule, one place. activateLabel is not an aria-label attribute so the fixed-label scan cannot see it; it has its own assertion. OUT OF SCOPE ON PURPOSE: the "Queue" link in the drafts column. Its target is a publish BATCH shared by many rows, so naming it after one item would be actively wrong, and the batch has no human-readable name to use instead. Left alone rather than given a plausible-sounding label. AC6 IS NOT A FORMALITY: nobody has driven this table with a real screen reader. Distinguishing names are necessary and not sufficient — a correct name can still be announced at the wrong moment, and fourteen controls per row is a lot of speech per item however well each one is named. That is the same gap US-2335 AC4 records, and this story does not close it. VERIFIED: npx tsc -b clean, npm run lint 0 errors / 13 warnings (unchanged), npm run ui:check 0 blocking 0/0 noise, full web suite 320 files 3916 passed 0 failed (+24), npm run build green through the 216-route prerender, prd-lint OK. Negative-verified 8 ways, each reddening its own named test and only its own: a fixed aria-label back in a row, an InlineCell handed a literal instead of its row, the activate label drifting off the helper, the placeholder rule inlined into the JSX again, the id fallback removed, a placeholder accepted as a name, the label truncated, and tagAttrs reverted. | 2026-08-22 THE SAME DEFECT WAS ONE TABLE ALONG THE WHOLE TIME, and this story fixed one file and stopped. AutoLister bulk edit had thirteen controls per row, every one a fixed string: Select row, Title, Price, Condition, Department, Brand, Size, Color, Quantity, Best offer and its two thresholds, Scheduled publish time. Over a virtualized list of up to a few hundred drafts - which is the surface where a seller is MOST likely to be moving straight down one column at speed. Invisible to US-2335's count for the same reason as the first table (every control had a name) and invisible to this story's own guard because the guard read one path.  FOUND BY SWEEPING THE CLASS, not by reading this file. A scan for a literal aria-label or title inside a .map() body reports 129 sites across 47 files. Most are noise - a `title` on a non-interactive element is a tooltip, and many maps are over columns rather than items - but the ones that matter are the ones rendering an interactive control per ITEM. Ranked, the remaining work list is:   autolister.tsx (16)      per-PHOTO controls - Select photo, Delete photo,                            Dismiss proposal - repeated down a photo grid   filter-builder.tsx (6)   Filter field / operator / value, per filter row;                            real but a handful of rows, not hundreds   autolister-drafts (5), admin/ai-models (5), admin/submissions (4) - mostly                            `title` tooltips on icon buttons, lower severity  NO NEW MECHANISM WAS INVENTED: src/lib/item-row-label.ts already had exactly the right three functions and one consumer. The row identity is derived ONCE per row and threaded into all thirteen.  THE PRECEDENCE IS THE PART THAT COULD HAVE BEEN WRONG QUIETLY. In this table the inputs RENDER r.title and use the item's stored title only as a placeholder, which is the opposite of the listings table where the item title leads. So r.title is item_title here. Reversing it would have made a row announce a name it is not displaying - the same class as the activate-label bug this story found the first time - and a test pins it.  SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 3 of 3, green control either side: restoring one fixed label (literally its original state), inverting the show/speak precedence, and giving one control its own identity object.  THE THIRD ONE INITIALLY GOT THROUGH, and closing it is the useful part. `rowControlLabel("Brand", { id: r.id })` leaves the single-derivation count at one and the call count unchanged, so both original assertions passed while that control announced an id fragment and its twelve neighbours announced the title - the row introducing itself two ways, which is the drift the shared derivation exists to prevent. The guard now pins the ARGUMENT, not just the call.  ALSO LEARNED, AND IT COST THE WORK ONCE: the sabotage harness restored with `git checkout -- <file>`, which restores to HEAD. The fix was not committed, so the first restore deleted it and the next two mutations silently failed to apply - reported honestly as "MUTATION DID NOT APPLY, the sabotage proves nothing" rather than as a pass. A sabotage harness must back up the file it is about to mutate, not assume the good state is the committed one.  AC6/AC7 UNCHANGED AND STILL OPEN: nobody has driven either table with a real screen reader, and thirteen or fourteen controls per row is a lot of speech per item however well each one is named.  VERIFIED: 27 cases in item-row-label.test.ts (7 new), tsc -b exit 0, eslint exit 0, ui:check 0 blocking, audit-control-labels still 0. | 2026-08-22 BATCH 2: the AutoLister photo grid and the two AI chips. Four more controls, and a NEW SUB-CLASS the aria-label sweep could not see - recorded below with line numbers, because it is the larger half and it is not done.  FIXED HERE. Every tile in the ungrouped photo grid announced "Select photo (Shift-click selects the range)" and every delete button "Delete photo", down a virtualized grid of a whole shoot. Both now carry the photo's own name.  tileLabel IS A DIFFERENT FALLBACK FROM itemRowLabel AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. An item falls back to its number and then an id fragment; a photo falls back to POSITION. A photo has no title to recover, and position is how a person refers to one - "the third one". An id fragment would distinguish and mean nothing.  THE POSITION IS THE PART THAT COULD HAVE BEEN QUIETLY WRONG. The map slices one grid ROW out of the sorted list, so the obvious `col + 1` restarts at 1 on every row and gives seven photos per screen the same name - the defect rebuilt, and the kind that looks fixed because every label is now dynamic. It is `row.index * gridColumns + col + 1`, and a test pins that exact expression.  THE TWO CHIPS REUSE WHAT IS ALREADY ON SCREEN rather than inventing a second description. The suggestion chip renders suggestionLabel(s, g.id) and now says it; the proposal chip says its photo count and confidence, which is its visible text. Where the visible text would not distinguish two chips, no name could - that is a visual problem, not a labelling one.  SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 4 of 4, green control either side: a delete button restored to its original fixed label, position counted within the row instead of across the grid, select and delete deriving the name separately, and the suggestion chip inventing its own text.  ⚠ STILL OPEN IN THIS FILE, AND IT IS THE BIGGER HALF: ten icon buttons whose accessible name comes from `title` or from visible text rather than from an aria-label, so the aria-label sweep reported them clean and audit-control-labels counts them as labelled. They are the same defect:   ungrouped tile   Undo background removal (3136), Clean background (3147),                    Auto-enhance (3156), Edit photo (3168)   group tile       Set as cover (3500), Remove from group (3513),                    Edit photo (3531)  - these need a per-photo derivation of                    their own, inside g.photos rather than the ungrouped grid   group buttons    Generate (3412), Auto-tag (3422), Ungroup (3435) - named by                    their visible text, so every group announces "Generate" Not done here because they need roughly twelve lines and the file is at its ratchet, so they need their own extraction - which is the ratchet working, not an obstacle to route around.  THE LINE CEILING WENT DOWN, NOT UP. The labels pushed autolister.tsx to 3670 against a ceiling of 3657, so stagedSortName moved into autolister/staged-sort-name.ts - a pure function that had just gained a second caller (the grid SORTS by the filename and now SPEAKS it) and now has six tests of its own. The sourceSig parsing is the part that can be quietly wrong: the signature is `name|size|mtime` and the name may itself contain a pipe, so the two trailing segments are stripped rather than parts[0] taken - otherwise "front|back.jpg" truncates to "front". Ceiling lowered 3657 -> 3655.  VERIFIED: 37 cases in item-row-label.test.ts + 6 new in staged-sort-name.test.ts, tsc -b exit 0, eslint exit 0, ui:check 0 blocking, audit-control-labels 0, check-web-unwired OK. | 2026-08-22 BATCH 3 closes autolister.tsx. The ten controls the previous segment listed are done, and one of them turned out to be a bug that had already shipped.  THE SUB-CLASS: AN ICON BUTTON WITH A `title` AND NO aria-label IS NAMED BY THE TITLE. That is why both sweeps called these clean - an aria-label scan sees no aria-label to object to, and audit-control-labels counts `title` as a resolvable name, which it is. It is just the SAME name on every photo. Clean background, Auto-enhance, Undo background removal, Edit photo, Set as cover, Remove from group. The titles stay as visual tooltips; the aria-label is what is read.  AND THE GROUP BUTTONS ARE NAMED BY THEIR VISIBLE TEXT, which is the third way a control gets a name and the third way to be invisible to a scan. Every card's button announced "Generate", "Auto-tag", "Ungroup".  ⚠ A SHIPPED BUG FOUND WHILE DOING IT, one line from its own fix. The group checkbox read aria-label={`Select group ${g.name}`} with NO fallback, and g.name is empty for a fresh group - so a screen of new groups all announced "Select group " with nothing after it. The name field ONE LINE BELOW already used `g.name || row.index + 1`. Two answers to "what is this group called" in adjacent lines, which is exactly the drift the shared derivation exists to stop, and it was inside the file this story is about. One groupName now, used by the checkbox, the name field, the SKU field and all three buttons.  TWO photoName DERIVATIONS NOW, NOT ONE, and that is correct rather than a regression: there are two independent photo grids - the ungrouped staging grid and the grid inside each group card - and they count position differently, because position within a group is what a seller means there. The test asserts exactly two and says why; a third would mean two controls on the SAME tile deriving separately.  SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 5 of 5, green control either side: an icon button losing its label, the checkbox restored to raw g.name, groupName losing its positional fallback, a group button no longer naming its group, and one tile control deriving the photo name a second time.  ONE SABOTAGE WAS A NO-OP ON THE FIRST RUN and was reported as "MUTATION DID NOT APPLY - proves nothing" rather than as a pass, which is the only reason it was noticed: the mutation guessed an indentation and the line had two spaces fewer. Re-anchored on the label text plus the following newline so it cannot depend on indentation at all.  THE CEILING WENT DOWN AGAIN, 3655 -> 3639, by moving filesFromDataTransfer into autolister/files-from-data-transfer.ts. Its header now records the two things about that function that lose photos silently and that a reader would not guess: readEntries PAGES and must be called until empty (one call reads about the first hundred entries in Chrome, which looks right on a test folder of six and drops the tail of a real shoot), and webkitGetAsEntry must be read BEFORE the first await because the DataTransferItem list is only valid during the drop event.  THE SWEEP ITSELF WAS WRONG AND IS FIXED. It counted every literal `title` inside a repeated element, so autolister.tsx still reported 12 after every control in it had been given a distinguishing name - a title BESIDE an aria-label is a visual tooltip and is correct. Refined to skip those, and the two AutoLister files now drop off the list entirely rather than sitting near the top of it. That matters because this list is what the next batch picks from.  REMAINING, 88 across 45 files on the corrected rule, worst first and with the seller-facing ones called out because the ranking by COUNT buries them:   buyer/alerts.tsx (3)       Open item / Remove from watchlist, per alert -                              buyer-facing and the highest value left   flipdesk/consignment (3)   Pay consignor / Edit consignor, per row, and it                              is money   content/authors, blog-list Delete author / Delete post, per row - a                              destructive action named identically down a list   filter-builder.tsx (6)     Filter field / operator / value, per filter row;                              real but a handful of rows, not hundreds   admin/* (~20)              Edit tier, Delete entry, Re-trigger grading - real                              and lowest traffic  VERIFIED: 39 cases in item-row-label.test.ts, 8 in autolister-split, 6 in staged-sort-name, tsc -b exit 0, eslint exit 0, ui:check 0 blocking, audit-control-labels 0, check-web-unwired OK. | 2026-08-22 BATCH 4, and the sweep becomes a GUARD rather than a list I keep re-running. src/test/repeated-labels.test.ts holds a shrink-only baseline of 77, names the five worst files when it fails so the next batch picks itself, and pins listings-table, autolister and autolister-bulk-edit at zero individually so they cannot drift back under cover of a baseline that happens to have room.  FIXED HERE, the two surfaces that mattered most on the list rather than the two with the highest counts: buyer/alerts.tsx (Delete alert, Open item, Remove from watchlist) and flipdesk/consignment.tsx (Pay, History, Edit - and it is money). Plus the Queue link in listings-table, which is named by its visible text and so announced "Queue" on every row.  ONE CONTROL WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE and it is the more interesting call. The "Alert name" INPUT keeps its fixed label, because a text input announces its label AND its value - it already reads as "Alert name, Nike jackets". The controls that need naming are the ones with no value of their own to announce. The guard counts inputs anyway, which is why the baseline is a number rather than zero: over-reporting is the safe direction for a rule this fiddly.  THE GUARD KNOWS ALL THREE WAYS A CONTROL GETS A NAME, which is the thing four batches taught: an aria-label; a `title` on an icon-only button, where the title IS the name; and visible button text. It counts the first two and says plainly that it cannot see the third - the version that tried flagged every button on every page, and the three real ones found by hand are fixed with no guard behind them.  REFINING THE RULE FOUND A REAL ONE AND REMOVED TWO FALSE ONES. A `title` only becomes an accessible NAME on something focusable; on a Badge or a span it is an explanatory tooltip. Two of the three findings keeping listings-table off the already-fixed list were exactly that, and the third was the Queue link, which was real. Count 84 -> 77 with the tighter rule, and the number is now trustworthy rather than an upper bound.  THE GUARD HAS ITS OWN FIXTURE, because the rule is fiddly enough to have been wrong twice already: it asserts the scan fires on a bare aria-label and a bare title, does NOT fire on a tooltip beside a real label or on an interpolated name, and does not fire outside a map at all.  SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 3 of 3, green control either side: an already-fixed surface regressing one control, a NEW page arriving with a fixed label in a row, and the rule itself being narrowed so it stops recognising a bare title - which fails the fixture, not just the count.  A LINE-ENDING TRAP WORTH RECORDING: consignment.tsx is CRLF while its neighbours are LF, so a multi-line anchor written with \n matched ZERO times. It said so and aborted rather than patching something else, which is the only reason it was noticed. Single-line anchors, and inserted lines use the file's own ending, so the diff is five lines rather than the whole file.  REMAINING: 77 across the rest, and it is now a ratchet rather than a memo. The worst are filter-builder (6), admin/ai-models (5), admin/submissions (4), autolister-drafts (4), admin/condition-index (3) - admin-heavy, which is the same shape US-2335 found: the seller-facing surfaces are in better condition than the raw count suggests.  AC6/AC7 UNCHANGED: nobody has driven any of this with a real screen reader.  VERIFIED: 50 cases across the three label suites, tsc -b exit 0, eslint exit 0, ui:check 0 blocking, audit-control-labels 0. | 2026-08-22 BATCH 5, first one driven by the ratchet rather than by a scan I ran by hand. 77 -> 61 across five files, and the guard named every one of them.  filter-builder (6). Field / Operator / Value / Remove, per rule row. POSITION is the identity, not the field: the selects announce their own value, so "Filter field, Brand" already reads - but two rules both filtering Brand collide, and stacking conditions on related fields is the entire point of a rule builder. "rule 2" is also how a person refers to one.  autolister-drafts (2). The Queue link, named by its visible text, and the inline-edit button, named by its tooltip. The row identity goes through itemRowLabel rather than the file's own titleFor(), because titleFor falls back to "Untitled draft" - correct to PRINT and wrong to speak, since a screen of fresh drafts would all be called that. itemRowLabel refuses that placeholder and falls through to an id fragment.  content/authors (2) and content/blog-list (2). Both files ALREADY had the idiom on the row itself - authors reads `Edit ${a.name}` and the submissions table reads `View submission ${s.title}` - and the action buttons beside them did not follow. So "Delete author" and "Delete post" were identical down a column of destructive buttons. A post can be untitled and the cell prints "(untitled)", so the slug is the fallback: unique by definition, and it is what the row links to anyway.  admin/submissions (4). Two of these act on a real seller's grade - Re-trigger grading and Mark as failed - and both announced identically on every row.  TWO ANCHORING TRAPS, both of which reported themselves rather than patching the wrong thing. A 26-space indent is a SUBSTRING of a 32-space one, so the shorter anchor matched two buttons and the script refused; anchored on the onClick instead. And the failed-submissions table is a second map with an EXPRESSION body, so `const s` is not in scope there at all and the identity is item.submission.title - which the compiler would have caught, but only after a wrong edit had been written.  REMAINING 61, and the ratchet now names the worst five itself: admin/ai-models (5), admin/condition-index (3), admin/config-pricing (3), flipdesk/expenses (3), team (3). The seller-facing surfaces are done; what is left is admin, plus team.tsx which is new to the list because everything above it moved.  VERIFIED: 50 cases across the three label suites, tsc -b exit 0, eslint exit 0, ui:check 0 blocking, audit-control-labels 0. | 2026-08-22 BATCH 6. 61 -> 44, nineteen controls across five files, and the pattern the last three batches keep turning up is now the finding rather than a coincidence.  THE ROW WAS ALREADY NAMED CORRECTLY IN EVERY ONE OF THEM. team.tsx has `Role for ${m.member_name || m.member_email}` on the role select, and the button that REMOVES the person said "Remove member". admin/ai-models has `View ${version.version_name}` on the row and its five buttons said "View", "Test prompt", "Activate", "Deactivate", "Delete". content/authors, content/blog-list and admin/submissions were the same last batch. Six files now.  So this is not a case of nobody knowing the rule. Somebody applied it to the row and did not carry it to the controls INSIDE the row, six separate times. That is what the ratchet is for: it does not depend on anybody remembering.  THE SHARPEST TWO. team.tsx's remove button is the highest-consequence control on that page and it announced identically for every teammate. admin/ai-models' Activate/Deactivate decides which prompt grades live traffic.  flipdesk/expenses gained a helper rather than an inline expression, because an expense has NO name of its own: the description is what the row prints and it is optional, so the fallback is the category and the date - the other two things the row shows. Deliberately not a constant like "this expense", which is the defect rebuilt for a column of delete buttons. Two expenses in one category on one day still sound alike; they also LOOK alike, which makes that a row problem rather than a labelling one.  condition-index's enable/disable toggle is fixed even though the scan does NOT count it - it is already an expression, `s.enabled ? "Disable" : "Enable"`. Two possible values across ten rows is the same ambiguity as one value, and a rule keyed on "is it a literal" cannot see that. Worth knowing the guard has that blind spot rather than assuming a green run means every row is distinguishable.  A JSX TRAP: an inserted `{/* comment */}` before <TableRow> broke the build, because that map's body is a single parenthesised expression and a sibling comment is a second child. Removed - the reasoning belongs in the helper's docblock, which is where it now is.  REMAINING 44, and the shape has changed: nothing is above 2 any more. The worst are ai-budgets-card, item-card-list, admin/brand-knowledge, admin/coupons and api-keys, two each. item-card-list is the one to take next - it is seller-facing and the rest are admin.  VERIFIED: 50 cases across the three label suites, tsc -b exit 0, eslint exit 0, ui:check 0 blocking, audit-control-labels 0. | 2026-08-22 BATCH 7. 44 -> 36, and this finishes the SELLER-FACING surfaces. Everything still on the list is admin or a known false positive.  item-card-list (2). The card prints `it.item_title || "Untitled item"`, so the spoken name goes through itemRowLabel instead: a grid of fresh drafts is exactly where a shared constant lands, and it would make every card say the same thing.  api-keys (2). Rotating or revoking the WRONG key breaks a live integration silently, and both buttons announced identically down the table.  upload-panels (2). t.name is the photo's filename - printed two lines above and the only thing telling one failed upload from another in a list of them.  sources (2). Deleting the wrong source unlinks it from every item that came from it.  ⚠ TWO OF THE REMAINING 36 ARE A KNOWN FALSE POSITIVE and should not be "fixed": autolister-drafts' Save & next and Cancel. They carry a `title` and visible text, they sit inside the row map, and the scan counts them - but only ONE row is in edit mode at a time, so they never repeat. Their accessible name comes from their visible text and is correct. Named here so the next batch does not spend effort making them worse, and left in the count rather than allowlisted because the baseline is deliberately a number and not zero.  WHERE THIS THREAD STOPS. Seven batches took 361 unlabelled controls (US-2335) to zero and then this second defect - a name that does not DISTINGUISH - from every seller-facing surface. What is left is 36 across ~20 admin files at two each, which the ratchet holds from growing and names on every failure. That is a better place to leave it than half-done in the middle of a file.  AC6/AC7 UNCHANGED AND UNCHANGEABLE FROM HERE: nobody has driven any of this with a real screen reader, and no count in this repo can substitute for that.  VERIFIED: 50 cases across the three label suites, tsc -b exit 0, eslint exit 0, ui:check 0 blocking, audit-control-labels 0.

userStories.title: Buyer audit rows are indistinguishable from seller ones, so the reconciler reads a buyer cancellation as a seller cancellation
userStories.description: Found 2026-08-10 by a sweep for remaining buyer/seller asymmetries, and it is partly a regression introduced the same day. flipdesk_subscription_events is the audit table for BOTH products - App Store and Play rows have always been namespaced (appstore., googleplay.) - but the buyer rows added by US-2119/2451/2452/2453 carried the RAW Stripe event type. reconciliation_candidates (migration 00217) is DISTINCT ON (e.user_id) with no product filter, so the newest row wins whichever product it belongs to, and it returns only event_type, to_plan and raw_payload->>status. deriveExpectedState then maps customer.subscription.deleted to {canceled, free} and invoice.payment_failed to {past_due, toPlan} and detectDivergence compares that against the SELLER cached columns. So a seller in good standing who cancels their buyer plan is flagged status_divergence, and a buyer whose card fails puts that seller in the operator dunning queue. The remedy for that flag is a resync that can overwrite flipdesk_subscription_id with the buyer subscription id, after which a plan change would push a FlipDesk price onto their Guard/Connoisseur subscription. A false flag on this queue is not noise, it is a loaded destructive action.
acceptanceCriteria: Every buyer row written to flipdesk_subscription_events is namespaced so it cannot be read as a seller signal, matching the appstore./googleplay. convention already in use.
detectDivergence refuses to compare a buyer event against the seller cached state, and says why rather than deriving something plausible.
A test asserts every buyer write site is namespaced, discovered from the source rather than listed, so a new buyer audit row cannot ship raw.

OPEN / NOT AGENT WORK: buyer subscriptions are not reconciled at all - CachedSubscriptionState has no buyer columns and the 00217 RPC selects none - so a dropped buyer webhook drifts permanently with nothing detecting it. Skipping is strictly better than a wrong flag, but it is a gap and needs its own reconciliation pass.

OPEN / NOT AGENT WORK: the resync remedy (admin-billing pickRelevantSubscription) lists subscriptions by customer with NO product filter, and buyer and seller share one Stripe customer - so it can select the buyer subscription and write its id into flipdesk_subscription_id. That is destructive and predates this story.

OPERATOR: start Docker Desktop, which is the single blocker on AC4 and takes seconds. Confirmed down again 2026-08-16 (docker info cannot open the named pipe), so npm run verify:db and verify:security are SKIPPED on every run - the throwaway-Postgres lane that proves a migration applies to a fresh schema is not running at all. AC4 needs a migration that ALTERS A UNIQUE INDEX on an operator-facing table, and shipping an index change that no Postgres has ever executed is the one thing that lane exists to prevent. With Docker up this is a single focused session rather than a blocked one.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-10 AC1, AC2 and AC3 DONE. AC4 and AC5 stay open and are NOT agent work - they are named on this story so the sweep that found them is not lost. PART OF THIS IS A REGRESSION I INTRODUCED TODAY, and that is the first thing to say. US-2119, US-2451, US-2452 and US-2453 added buyer audit rows to flipdesk_subscription_events carrying the RAW Stripe event type. App Store and Play rows have always been namespaced (appstore., googleplay.); I did not follow the convention because I did not know the table was read by anything other than an operator. IT IS. reconciliation_candidates (migration 00217) is DISTINCT ON (e.user_id) with no product filter, and returns only event_type, to_plan and raw_payload->>status. So the newest row wins whichever product it belongs to, deriveExpectedState maps customer.subscription.deleted to {canceled, free} and invoice.payment_failed to {past_due, toPlan}, and detectDivergence compares that against the SELLER cached columns. Net effect: a seller in good standing who cancelled their BUYER plan would be flagged status_divergence, and a buyer whose card failed would put that seller into the operator dunning queue. WHY THAT IS WORSE THAN NOISE: the operator remedy for such a flag is a resync which - per AC5, pre-existing - lists subscriptions by CUSTOMER with no product filter, and buyer and seller share one Stripe customer. So it can select the buyer subscription and write its id into flipdesk_subscription_id, after which a plan change would push a FlipDesk price onto that person's Guard or Connoisseur subscription. A false flag on this queue is a loaded destructive action, not a stray line. AC1: every buyer write is namespaced through buyerEventType() - the cancellation row, the renewal receipt, the dunning and bank-challenge rows, the advance-notice row (conditionally, since handleInvoiceUpcoming serves both products from one call) and the in-place consent artifact in payments.ts. The consent artifact was BENIGN for divergence (its type is not in deriveExpectedState's vocabulary) and namespaced anyway, because it still DISPLACES the seller's genuine latest event in a distinct-on-user query and silently stops reconciling that seller until their next event. AC2: detectDivergence now refuses a buyer event with the same shape as the existing comp short-circuit, and returns expected {null,null} rather than deriving something plausible - there is no buyer column in CachedSubscriptionState to have compared against, so there is nothing honest to say. SKIPPING RATHER THAN RECONCILING IS THE DELIBERATE CHOICE: it means a buyer drift goes undetected, which is a gap, but a silent gap is strictly better than a confident wrong flag whose remedy is destructive. AC3: the guard derives the buyer write sites from source rather than listing them, so a new buyer audit row cannot ship raw. SIX SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening its own case: the cancellation row un-namespaced, the dunning row un-namespaced, the shared upcoming handler no longer branching, the consent artifact un-namespaced, the detectDivergence skip removed, and the skip widened to swallow SELLER events too - which correctly reddens THREE pre-existing reconciliation tests as well as mine, and that is the half worth having: a skip that ate real seller signals would be a much more expensive fix than the flag it prevented. ⚠ ONE MUTATION PROVED NOTHING FIRST TIME and the harness lesson is now twice-learned. Writing the skip as `if (true)` made the file fail TYPE CHECKING (unreachable code), so deno test never ran, and my parser reported NOTHING FAILED because it only looked for '... FAILED' lines and for 'error: TS'. A malformed sabotage is indistinguishable from a weak guard unless the harness can tell a compile failure from a test pass. Rewritten as a mutation that compiles, and the detector now recognises 'Type checking failed' too. AC4 OPEN - BUYER SUBSCRIPTIONS ARE NOT RECONCILED AT ALL. CachedSubscriptionState has no buyer columns and the 00217 RPC selects none, so a dropped buyer webhook drifts permanently with nothing detecting it. That is the revenue leak US-893 exists to catch, on the product it does not cover. Needs its own reconciliation pass and probably a migration. AC5 OPEN AND PRE-EXISTING - the resync remedy in admin-billing.ts (pickRelevantSubscription) lists by customer with no product filter. Destructive, and it predates every buyer row I wrote; namespacing removes the most likely TRIGGER but not the hazard itself. ALSO SURFACED BY THE SAME SWEEP, recorded here rather than lost: no admin route reads buyer_plan / buyer_subscription_status at all, so support cannot see, cancel, change or comp a buyer subscription, and buyer past-due accounts never enter the operator dunning queue. Buyer refunds DO work, because charges are listed customer-wide. Account export and deletion are correctly covered (buyer columns via select *, buyer tables via BUYER_PII_TABLES, subscription cancelled by the customer delete). The trial-expiry and journey crons are correctly seller-only because no buyer trial exists. VERIFIED: deno check clean on webhooks.ts, payments.ts and billing-reconciliation.ts; deno lint clean across 1493 files; buyer-audit-namespace_test.ts 5 passed (new); full edge suite 6496 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored (up 5). | 2026-08-10 AC5 DONE. I called this 'not agent work' in the previous pass and that was wrong - the fix is a product filter, which is code. Correcting it here rather than leaving the misjudgement standing. THE DEFECT, and it is pre-existing rather than mine: the resync fallback listed the customer's subscriptions with NO product filter, and buyer and seller subscriptions ride the SAME Stripe customer. So for a buyer-only account - or a seller whose own subscription had lapsed - pickRelevantSubscription returned the BUYER subscription and the resync wrote its id into flipdesk_subscription_id, its status into subscription_status, and mapSubscriptionToFlipdeskPlan(buyerSub) ?? 'free' into flipdesk_plan. The row then claims an ACTIVE subscription on a FREE plan, pointing at the other product's. THE SECOND-ORDER DAMAGE IS WHAT MAKES IT URGENT. POST /users/:id/change-plan acts on flipdesk_subscription_id. So support changing that person's FlipDesk plan afterwards would push a FlipDesk PRICE onto their Guard or Connoisseur subscription - a real charge, on the wrong product, initiated by someone trying to help. That is the chain the previous pass described and did not close. FIXED IN TWO PLACES, because one alone leaves the corruption alive. (1) pickRelevantSubscription filters buyer subscriptions out BEFORE the live/newest pick, and returns null when every candidate is a buyer one - null is the correct answer, since the caller then records 'no seller subscription', which is true; borrowing the other product's is what created the defect. (2) THE REPAIR HALF: if the STORED flipdesk_subscription_id already points at a buyer subscription - which an earlier unfiltered resync could have written - the retrieve path now discards it and falls through to the (now filtered) customer lookup, so the run CORRECTS the row instead of resyncing the seller columns from the buyer's state forever. Without that, the retrieve short-circuits the lookup and the corruption is permanent. THE TESTS PIN THE FILTER'S COMPLETENESS, not its presence: a filter applied to the candidate list while `live` is still picked from the unfiltered one would return a buyer subscription about half the time and read as fixed. Every subsequent read must be off the filtered list, and two assertions fail if `subs.find(` or `[...subs]` survives anywhere in the function. A fourth case pins the blast radius - the seller resync must write no buyer_* column, because buyer state is owned by customer.subscription.updated and this route has no buyer reconciliation behind it. SIX SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening its own case: the filter removed, the live pick reading the unfiltered list, the newest-fallback reading the unfiltered list, the all-buyer case falling back instead of returning null, the stored-buyer-id guard removed, and the resync starting to write buyer columns. AC4 REMAINS THE ONLY OPEN ONE and it genuinely is not a filter: buyer subscriptions are not reconciled at all, because CachedSubscriptionState has no buyer columns and the 00217 RPC selects none. A dropped buyer webhook still drifts permanently with nothing detecting it. That needs its own reconciliation pass and probably a migration to widen the RPC. VERIFIED: deno check clean on admin-billing.ts; deno lint clean across 1494 files; resync-product-filter_test.ts 4 passed (new); full edge suite 6500 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored (up 4). | 2026-08-10 THE OTHER END OF THE SAME FALSE FLAG, which AC5 alone did not close. jobs-billing-reconciliation.ts fetchStripeSubscriptions builds a map of every live Stripe subscription KEYED BY CUSTOMER, and detectStripeDivergence compares it against the SELLER cached columns. Buyer and seller subscriptions share one customer, and the map was unfiltered - so an account holding an active Guard plan and a canceled FlipDesk one produced a stripe_divergence flag claiming Stripe thinks they are active. THE TWO DEFECTS FED EACH OTHER: this manufactured the flag, and the resync fixed in the previous pass was the remedy that flag points at - the one that adopted the buyer subscription into flipdesk_subscription_id. Fixing only the resync would have left the queue generating the cases; fixing only the sweep would have left the button loaded. Both halves are now filtered by the same predicate. THE FILTER IS NOT A TIDY-UP, and a second test says so: `status: "all"` stays, because 'Stripe says canceled while we say active' is the most expensive divergence there is - a customer served a paid plan for free - and narrowing the list is exactly what would hide it. The prefer-live-over-canceled rule is pinned too. ⚠ THE SHARED SOURCE-SCAN HELPER HAD A SECOND BUG, found by these tests failing against CORRECT code. fnBody took the first `{` after the parameter list - but a RETURN TYPE can contain one: fetchStripeSubscriptions is declared `): Promise<Map<string, { id: string; status: string | null }> | null> {`. So the 'body' was the return type annotation and two true assertions failed as though the code were missing. This is the SECOND instance of the same class in that helper (the first was an inline object PARAMETER type), and both look identical from the test - which makes the tempting response 'weaken the assertion' rather than 'fix the slicer'. fnBody now tracks angle-bracket depth and takes the first brace outside it. Two new fixtures in source-scan_test.ts cover the return type and a generic parameter list. That is exactly why US-2454 gave the helper its own tests an hour ago: the primitive is used by nine guards now, and a slicing bug in it silently weakens all of them at once. FOUR SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening its own case: the sweep no longer filtering, the filter moved AFTER the map write, `status: "all"` removed, and fnBody reverted to the naive brace search - which correctly reddens the two sweep tests AND its own new fixture, because that is what a broken primitive does. ⚠ ONE MUTATION PROVED NOTHING FIRST TIME, third occurrence today: my 'filter after write' edit put the set AFTER the filter anyway, so it tested nothing. Re-anchored so the write genuinely precedes the filter. A sabotage that does not create the condition it names is a green run that means nothing. AC4 REMAINS OPEN and is now the only one. Buyer subscriptions are still not reconciled at all - CachedSubscriptionState has no buyer columns, the 00217 RPC selects none, and billing_reconciliation_flags is keyed one-open-flag-per-user with no product dimension, so a buyer flag and a seller flag cannot coexist. That last point is why AC4 genuinely needs a migration rather than another filter, and it is the reason I am not starting it in the same breath as two held prod changes. VERIFIED: deno check clean on jobs-billing-reconciliation.ts; deno lint clean across 1494 files; resync-product-filter_test.ts 6 passed (2 new) and source-scan_test.ts 12 passed (2 new); full edge suite 6504 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored (up 4). | 2026-08-10 THE PATTERN IS NOW WRITTEN DOWN. Ten defects in one session shared one sentence, and nothing recorded it — so instance eleven was going to be written by whoever touches the seller subscription next. NEW vault/70-agent/buyer-is-a-second-tenant.md. All ten in a table with what a buyer actually got, plus the two one level up (buyer audit rows read as seller signals; no admin surface reading a buyer column). THE PART WORTH THE NOTE IS WHY IT KEEPS HAPPENING, because it is not carelessness. The early return is USUALLY CORRECT: `if (invoiceIsBuyer(invoice)) return;` genuinely guards the seller cycle resets, the dunning transition and the plan columns. The bug is never the return - it is that something which was NOT seller-specific had been written inside the region the return protects. So a reviewer sees a guard with a good reason, and the reason is true. AND THE COMMENTS MADE IT WORSE, twice. One skip read 'so a buyer doesn't get a seller-shaped email' - an honest statement of intent whose consequence, silence, nobody re-read. Another said the buyer path 'is carried by subscription.updated', which is true of the STATUS and false of the EMAIL three lines below it. Both read as decisions. THE THIRD REASON IS THE ONE I WOULD NOT HAVE GUESSED: half a feature working hides the other half. Buyer CHARGES show in the admin tools, because charges are listed customer-wide - so the money half of a support call worked while the state half was blank. A gap that breaks half a workflow is a gap nobody reports, because the half that works is the half people phone about. SIX-POINT CHECKLIST for anyone touching the seller subscription, each earned from a specific defect: does the buyer equivalent EXIST (name the file); what sits BELOW an early return that is not seller-specific; split the send out rather than widening the skip (threading isBuyer past every write is how a buyer's renewal resets a seller's quota); product is a PARAMETER, never inferred; is the SENTENCE true of the buyer product; and does the guard name a route or find them. PLUS THE ENUM TRAP, which caught me four separate times: from_plan/to_plan are typed public.flipdesk_plan (00037) and buyer tiers are public.buyer_plan (00402), so writing 'guard' raises 22P02 - and every one of those inserts is best-effort by design, so the row silently never appears while the charge goes through. ALSO CLEARED THE VAULT WARNING I had been leaving deliberately. vault/50-business/ios-in-app-purchases.md drifted against appstore.ts and I had refused to bump 'reviewed' without a genuine re-read, since doing that to silence a warning is the one failure no automation catches. Re-read it properly and found a sentence that HAD gone stale: 'a user who subscribes on both web and iOS is currently only caught by hand'. US-2456 closed that at purchase time on every path. Corrected the sentence, added precedence.ts to its code_refs, and bumped the date on the strength of an actual read rather than to clear a line. VERIFIED: vault:lint --strict clean at 169 notes, zero warnings for the first time today. | 2026-08-10 AC4 SCOPED IN FULL AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT. The reasoning matters more than the plan, so it is first. WHY NOT NOW: there is already ONE migration in the queue (00586) that has never been executed against a Postgres, because Docker is down and verify:db cannot boot the throwaway stack. AC4 needs a SECOND migration - larger, and it alters a UNIQUE INDEX on an operator-facing table. Adding an untested index change on top of an untested function replacement is compounding, and it gates the push on two prod applies instead of one. This is the same call US-2118 made about the proration figures: when the verification that would catch a mistake is unavailable, shipping the mistake-prone half is worse than waiting. Re-check `docker info`; if it is up, this is a single focused session. THE BLOCKER IS MEASURED, not assumed. billing_reconciliation_flags (00217) carries a partial UNIQUE INDEX billing_reconciliation_flags_open_subject_key ON (subject_user_id) WHERE status = 'open'. ONE open flag per person, with no column saying which product it is about. So a buyer flag and a seller flag cannot coexist for the same customer, and the job would silently overwrite one with the other - which is worse than not reconciling buyers at all, because it would start LOSING seller flags. That index is why this cannot be done with a filter. THE PLAN, in the order it has to happen: (1) MIGRATION. ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS product text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'flipdesk' (the default is what makes it safe on a table with live rows - every existing flag IS a seller flag). DROP the partial unique index and recreate it on (subject_user_id, product) WHERE status='open'. Then CREATE OR REPLACE reconciliation_candidates to return buyer_status, buyer_plan and buyer_subscription_id alongside the seller columns, and to stop filtering the event scan to seller rows only - it must return the latest SELLER event and the latest BUYER event per user, which with the US-2457 namespacing is now a clean split on event_type LIKE 'buyer.%'. US-1108 triple: idempotent, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in the same commit, self-record footer, manifest regenerated. (2) lib/billing-reconciliation.ts. CachedSubscriptionState gains a buyer variant rather than being widened - the same argument the precedence helpers settled in US-2456, and for the same reason: a type that accepts either row family is how a comparison ends up reading the wrong one. detectDivergence's buyer short-circuit (added today) is REPLACED by a real buyer comparison, and that is the line to be careful about - until the migration lands, the skip is what stops false flags. (3) THE JOB. fetchStripeSubscriptions currently filters buyer subscriptions OUT and keys by customer. For the buyer half it needs the opposite selection, keyed the same way - which means the map must become two maps, or one keyed by (customer, product). Do NOT reuse the seller map; it is the shape that caused this story. (4) SIX CONSUMERS to update, enumerated so none is missed: admin-billing.ts at 1470, 1481, 1667 and 1755, lib/agent-tools.ts at 455, and lib/finance-agent.ts. Each currently assumes a flag is about the seller subscription. The two admin panels also need the product on screen - a flag an operator cannot attribute to a product is a flag they cannot act on, and the resync they would reach for is seller-only (AC5). (5) THE RESYNC REMEDY needs a buyer equivalent, or the buyer flags have no fix button. AC5 fixed the seller one so it can no longer ADOPT the buyer subscription; it still cannot RESYNC one. WHAT I WOULD GET WRONG WITHOUT A DATABASE: the index swap. DROP INDEX then CREATE UNIQUE INDEX on a table with existing rows fails if any two open flags for one subject would now collide - they cannot today, since every row is implicitly seller, but that is exactly the assumption a throwaway-stack run exists to prove rather than reason about. STATUS: AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC5 are done and committed. AC4 is the only one left and it is one focused session behind a working Docker.

userStories.title: Support cannot see a buyer subscription at all — no admin route reads buyer_plan or buyer_subscription_status
userStories.description: Found 2026-08-10 by a sweep for buyer/seller asymmetries. Not one admin route reads buyer_plan, buyer_subscription_status or buyer_subscription_id. admin-growth exposes an aggregate buyer rollup and nothing per-account. Concretely: GET /users/:id/payments (admin-billing.ts) selects only flipdesk_subscription_id, so an agent opening a Guard or Connoisseur subscriber sees subscription: null and has no way to tell whether they are subscribed, on what, or when it renews. POST /users/:id/change-plan acts solely on flipdesk_subscription_id, so there is no admin path to cancel, downgrade or change a buyer subscription. admin-users POST /:id/plan writes flipdesk_plan and subscription_status, so a buyer comp or goodwill grant is impossible. And the operator dunning queue filters users.subscription_status, so a buyer whose card is failing never appears in it. Buyer REFUNDS do work, because charges are listed customer-wide and both subscriptions ride one Stripe customer — which makes the gap easy to miss, since the money half of a support conversation succeeds while the state half shows nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /users/:id/payments returns the buyer subscription alongside the seller one, each labelled with its product, so an agent can see what the customer actually holds.

The response shape is additive: the existing `subscription` field keeps its exact meaning (the seller subscription) so the admin UI and any consumer are unchanged, and the buyer state arrives beside it rather than replacing it.
A test asserts the two are never conflated — a buyer-only account must not report its buyer subscription in the seller field, which is the same mistake the reconciliation resync made (US-2457 AC5).

OPEN / NEEDS A DECISION: whether support should be able to CANCEL or CHANGE a buyer subscription, and whether a buyer comp is a product we want. Both are writes against a customer's money and neither is a read-only fix; the comp path also needs a buyer equivalent of subscription_status='comp', which today is a seller-only enum value.

OPEN / NEEDS A MIGRATION: buyer past-due accounts in the operator dunning queue. The panel filters users.subscription_status, and there is no buyer_past_due_since column, so the US-395 grace clock has no buyer equivalent to sort by.

OPERATOR: decide two things, both writes against a customer's money, which is why neither was built speculatively. (1) Should support be able to CANCEL or CHANGE a buyer subscription from the admin surface, or should that stay with the customer via the portal? (2) Is a buyer comp a product we want at all? This is AC4 and it is now the ONLY item left - AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC5 are all done and verified 2026-08-22 (8 tests green, and the buyer_past_due_since column confirmed present in production via PostgREST's OpenAPI document). No code can start until the answers exist.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-10 AC1, AC2 and AC3 DONE. AC4 and AC5 stay open by design - one needs a product decision, the other a migration - and they are named here so the sweep that found them is not lost. GET /users/:id/payments now returns buyerSubscription beside subscription. Before this, an agent opening a Guard or Connoisseur subscriber saw subscription: null and had no way to tell whether they were subscribed, to what, or when it renewed. WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED, and it is the interesting part: the CHARGES were fine. They are listed customer-wide and both products ride one Stripe customer, so the money half of a support conversation worked - an agent could see the payments and refund them - while the state half was blank. A gap that only breaks half of a workflow is a gap nobody reports, because the half that works is the half people call about. AC2 IS ADDITIVE ON PURPOSE. `subscription` keeps its exact meaning, the SELLER subscription, so the admin UI and every other consumer are untouched. Repurposing it to 'whichever they have' would have been fewer lines and would have repeated the exact conflation US-2457 spent two commits undoing. The no-customer early return carries buyerSubscription: null too, so a caller never gets undefined on one path and null on the other - a test pins that, because it is the kind of asymmetry that shows up as a crash six months later. AC3: each subscription is retrieved by its OWN stored id. Listing the customer and choosing is precisely what let the reconciliation resync adopt the buyer subscription into the seller columns; the two ids are recorded separately so nobody has to guess, and a test fails if this route ever calls subscriptions.list. BOTH SUMMARIES GO THROUGH ONE SHARED SHAPE, extracted rather than copied. The agent is comparing one against the other, and two hand-written shapes drift - the drift shows up as a field present for sellers and missing for buyers, which reads as 'the buyer has no renewal date' rather than as a bug. SIX SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening its own case: the buyer field dropped from the response, buyer_subscription_id dropped from the SELECT, the seller field repurposed, the early return forgetting the new field, the buyer sub picked off the customer list, and the shared summary losing the renewal date. ONE ASSERTION WAS TOO LOOSE AND SABOTAGE CAUGHT IT - the fourth time today for this exact shape. I checked that buyer_subscription_id appears in the ROUTE; it also appears in the retrieve below, so dropping it from the SELECT stayed green. An unselected column is undefined, the retrieve is skipped, and the agent sees the same blank as before with no error anywhere. Now scoped to the select list itself. AC4 OPEN - a product decision, not a build. Whether support may CANCEL or CHANGE a buyer subscription is a write against a customer's money, and a buyer comp additionally needs a buyer equivalent of subscription_status='comp', which today is a seller-only enum value. AC5 OPEN - needs a migration. Buyer past-due accounts cannot enter the operator dunning queue: the panel filters users.subscription_status, and there is no buyer_past_due_since column, so the US-395 grace clock has no buyer equivalent to sort by. VERIFIED: deno check clean on admin-billing.ts; deno lint clean across 1495 files; admin-buyer-visibility_test.ts 4 passed (new); full edge suite 6508 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored (up 4). | 2026-08-10 (second pass) I SHIPPED THE API FIELD AND NOTHING RENDERED IT. Correcting my own instance of the exact failure this session keeps finding in other people's work. The previous commit added buyerSubscription to GET /users/:id/payments and stopped. src/components/admin/billing-actions-card.tsx - the only consumer - typed and rendered `subscription` alone, so support still saw nothing for a buyer subscriber. A field with no surface is invisible to tsc, to lint, and to every test that exercises the route directly, which is precisely how US-2145's contest endpoint sat unreachable behind a missing button and how confirm-signup corroborated a row that was never written. FIXED: both subscriptions now render, each through one shared SubscriptionSummary block and each LABELLED by product. The label is a required prop rather than defaulted - two subscriptions can be on screen at once and the agent is about to act on whichever they believe they are looking at, so an unlabelled one is worse than none. A test asserts the render, the label, and that both go through the shared block, so a field cannot appear for the seller and not the buyer. ⚠ AND A GENUINELY SURPRISING SIDE EFFECT, worth recording because nothing warns you about it. Extracting the shared mapper as a top-level `function` in admin-billing.ts made THREE UNRELATED ROUTES fail the US-2355 audit-policy guard - /pending-refunds/:id/resolve, /webhook-dead-letters/:id/resolve and the reconciliation resync all reported as writing no audit row. They audit fine. scripts/audit-admin-mutations.mjs classifies a route by appending the body of any TOP-LEVEL DECLARATION it references, and declarations() slices each declaration's body from itself to THE NEXT DECLARATION IN THE FILE. Adding one anywhere moves those boundaries, so a purely presentational helper silently changed the audit classification of routes it has nothing to do with. RESOLVED BY MOVING THE MAPPER TO lib/admin-subscription-summary.ts, with the reason in its header so nobody moves it back for tidiness. That is the right home anyway - it is a pure Stripe-to-view mapper with no route concerns - but the forcing reason is the classifier, and a future reader would never guess it. I DID NOT WEAKEN THE CLASSIFIER, which was the tempting alternative: its slicing model is genuinely fragile, but loosening a guard that decides 'is this admin action audited' to unblock a cosmetic refactor is the worst possible trade. Recorded here instead; if it bites again it deserves its own story rather than an exemption. THREE SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening the render guard: the buyer block never rendered (the state I shipped an hour ago), the labels dropped so an agent cannot tell the two apart, and the buyer block hand-written instead of sharing the seller's. VERIFIED: npx tsc -b clean; eslint 0 errors / 13 warnings; ui:check 0 blocking; deno lint clean across 1496 files; admin-buyer-visibility_test.ts 5 passed (1 new); admin-audit-policy.test.ts 6 passed (restored); full edge suite 6509 passed / 0 failed; full web suite 3937 passed / 0 failed across 322 files. | 2026-08-12 AC5 DONE (bd7a2b9d). Migration 00591 adds users.buyer_past_due_since - one nullable timestamptz mirroring 00091, its seller twin - and the reconciliation route gains a SEPARATE buyerPastDue list beside the existing pastDue one. Before this a buyer in dunning appeared in NO operator surface: the panel filters users.subscription_status, which is the seller column. SEPARATE, NOT MERGED, and that is the story's own thesis. AC2 kept `subscription` meaning exactly the seller subscription; AC3 exists because conflating the two is the mistake the resync already made once (US-2457 AC5) - it adopted a buyer subscription into flipdesk_subscription_id, and the remedy an operator reaches for next could push a FlipDesk price onto someone's Guard plan. A merged list would put that ambiguity back on screen, so a test asserts the seller query still reads no buyer_ column. THE COLUMN DOES NOT GATE ENTITLEMENT, deliberately. past_due_since additionally drives effectivePlanFor() dropping paid caps after the grace window; this one is operator visibility only. Dropping a buyer's caps on a dunning clock is a pricing decision and it belongs with AC4 - doing it silently inside a column addition would be smuggling it in. The clock is stamped in the customer.subscription.updated handler beside the status it anchors, reusing the already product-agnostic nextPastDueSince so it survives retries and can elapse. NOT from an invoice handler: that file's own comment records that writing buyer status from an invoice event makes the stored state depend on Stripe's delivery order. Four cases, three sabotages each watched failing. ONE OF MY OWN ASSERTIONS FAILED AGAINST CORRECT CODE FIRST - it sliced the seller block on the '(a)' / '(a2)' section COMMENTS, and the shared code() helper strips comments before any of it runs, so the slice matched nothing. Re-anchored on the query's own .in() filter. AC4 REMAINS AND IS YOURS: may support CANCEL or CHANGE a buyer subscription, and is a buyer comp a product you want? A comp additionally needs a buyer equivalent of subscription_status='comp', which is seller-only today. HELD: 00591, and order matters more than usual - SQL before the edge, or the webhook's write 42703s and buyer subscription state stops updating entirely. | 2026-08-15 THE HELD-MIGRATION WORDING ABOVE IS HISTORICAL, RESOLVED. The owner applied every outstanding migration and pushed main; origin/main and local are the same commit, PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md lists no HELD section, and the session-context hook reports none. So nothing in this story is waiting on a prod apply and the branch is not frozen on its account. Recorded as an appended correction rather than by editing the sentence, because these notes are append-only and prd-lint resolves by segment order. WHY THIS GETS ITS OWN NOTE INSTEAD OF BEING LEFT TO ROT: HELD is not a status, it is an instruction to stop, and a stale one tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not. That has cost real sessions in this repo (US-2286's 2026-08-09 note says so explicitly). VERIFY IT RATHER THAN TRUST THIS: curl -fsS https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready | jq .schema — US-2603 added a missing[] listing versions this build ships that the database never recorded, which is the check a bare status:match cannot do. | 2026-08-15 STATUS CORRECTION, formal: no migration named in this story is held. Every outstanding migration is applied to prod and main is pushed (origin/main == local). The previous segment said this in words prd-lint does not recognise, so the guard kept warning; this one uses the token it reads. | 2026-08-22 AC5 IS DONE, AND ITS PREMISE HAD GONE STALE. The criterion still reads 'OPEN / NEEDS A MIGRATION: ... The panel filters users.subscription_status, and there is no buyer_past_due_since column'. There is one, it is populated, and the panel no longer filters the seller column.  MEASURED, not read. Migration 00591_users_buyer_past_due_since.sql created it. PostgREST's OpenAPI document for production lists users with 108 columns including buyer_plan, buyer_subscription_status, buyer_past_due_since, buyer_period_end and past_due_since - all five present, read with the public anon key, so the column exists on the live database rather than only in the repo.  IT IS ALSO WIRED END TO END, which is the half a schema check cannot answer. routes/admin-billing.ts runs a dedicated buyer past-due query - select on buyer_* columns, .in("buyer_subscription_status", ["past_due"]), ordered by buyer_past_due_since - as a SEPARATE list rather than merged into the seller one, and its own comment says why: merging would put on screen the same ambiguity the reconciliation resync already shipped once (US-2457 AC5), where a buyer subscription was adopted into flipdesk_subscription_id and the next operator remedy would have pushed a FlipDesk price onto a person's Guard plan. routes/webhooks.ts writes the column through nextPastDueSince.  AC1, AC2 and AC3 were already done and are re-confirmed: GET /users/:id/payments returns buyerSubscription alongside subscription, the seller field keeps its exact meaning, and src/tests/admin-buyer-visibility_test.ts holds the never-conflated property. 8 passed / 0 failed, including two cases named for AC5 - 'the two products are separate lists, never merged' and 'the buyer dunning clock is stamped where status is'.  SO THE ONLY THING LEFT IS AC4, AND IT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN CODE: whether support may CANCEL or CHANGE a buyer subscription, and whether a buyer comp is a product worth having. Both are writes against a customer's money, which is why they were never built speculatively. Now declared as an OPERATOR criterion so the queue counts it.  WORTH RECORDING: this story was picked up because it read as 'no admin route exists', which is what its title says. Four of its five criteria were finished. An acceptance criterion that describes the world at filing time and is never re-read becomes a false report of the work remaining - the same shape as US-2772, where a shipped story sat open, and the same expensive direction: it costs a reader's time before anyone notices.

userStories.title: Grading + AI prompts name photo roles instead of numbered slots
userStories.description: As the grading pipeline, we want the prompt hints and macro-quality floors to speak in roles, so the model is told what a photo shows rather than which numbered slot it landed in.
acceptanceCriteria: PREREQUISITE, found 2026-08-11: the role has to REACH the grader first. submission_images.image_type is a Postgres ENUM (00001, grown by 00103), so a role cannot be encoded into it and the epic deliberately stopped growing that enum - this needs a submission_images.image_role column plus mapPhotoTypeForGrading taking the (type, role) pair. Load the `migrations` skill; it is a US-1108 triple
ai-grading.ts, ai-authenticity.ts and ai-extract.ts prompt hints name roles (fabric, hem, hardware, brand, size, care) instead of detail_2 / detail_3 / detail_4 / tag_2
macro-photo-quality.ts resolution and sharpness floors move from per-numbered-slot to per-role, keeping today's numbers for the equivalent role
ai-extract is told WHICH tag photo carries the brand and which carries the size, instead of guessing between tag and tag_2
No change to the fabric-close-up confidence cap logic, which already moved to roles in US-2467
OPERATOR: run the golden-set eval with GRADING_PHOTO_ROLES on, then take it through a canary slice before flipping it in prod (AC2). Needs real vision calls, so neither CI nor an agent can do it.
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Photos] Category-aware photo tags epic (US-2461). SPLIT OUT OF US-2467 on 2026-08-10. 2026-08-11 IN PROGRESS - AC1/AC3/AC4 done, AC2 built but gated, AC5 verified untouched. AC1 (the prereq) is DONE: migration 00589 adds submission_images.image_role (US-1108 triple; HELD - see PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md, do NOT push before Dj applies it), and mapPhotoTypeForGrading now takes the (type, role) pair and returns {imageType, imageRole}. THAT FIXED A LIVE REGRESSION nobody had reported: 00587 rewrote measurement_chest into (measurement, chest), a bare measurement is the MeasureCard calibration frame that 00346 excludes from grading on purpose, and the function read the type alone - so from 00587 onward EVERY tape-measure photo resolved to null and silently stopped reaching the grader. Two cases in grading-readiness-parity_test.ts pin it, and it is written into vault/20-domain/listing-photos.md, which already carried the identical warning for LISTABILITY and had never had it applied to grading. AC3 DONE: macro-photo-quality.ts keys every floor on (type, role) via baseSlot(); the retired numbered slots collapse onto their base pair so an older cached bundle still resolves; the guidance copy names the role (fill the frame with the fabric close-up). The numbers did NOT move - MACRO_MIN_LONG_EDGE_BY_ROLE ships deliberately EMPTY, because raising detail:fabric is an accuracy change that belongs behind an eval, not inside a refactor whose whole claim is that nothing moved. Also closed a latent gap: RETIRED_PHOTO_TYPES is the FlipDesk vocabulary only, so the grading spelling label_2 needed its own collapse or the both-spellings test would have gone red. AC4 DONE and LIVE: ai-extract is an unversioned prompt, so it ships without a gate. ExtractPhoto carries a role, photoSlotLabel() announces Photo 3 (tag: size tag) instead of Photo 3 (tag), the guidance line names which role holds brand / size / care / made-in, and flipdesk-ai.ts selects photo_role. AC2 BUILT BUT NOT LIVE, and that is the correct state: a grading prompt only changes through shadow to eval gate to canary. IMAGE_ROLE_CONTEXT covers 15 (image_type, role) pairs; buildUserPrompt and analyzeImage take imageRole as a LAST positional param; grading-pipeline selects image_role and passes it; PerImageAnalysis carries image_role; the composite stamps a +roles suffix (appended after +cat2) only when a role actually SELECTED a sentence. All of it behind GRADING_PHOTO_ROLES, default off and fail-closed, with photo-role-prompts_test.ts pinning byte-identity when off. Same shape and same reasoning as GRADING_CATEGORY_CRITERIA_V2 (US-2222). ai-authenticity turned out to have NO numbered-slot prompt hints at all - its only slot-number references are AUTHENTICITY_IMAGE_PRIORITY.
