It behaved exactly as designed - dry run, refused, exit 1, wrote nothing - so this is the script working, not failing. source rows: 8 existing help articles: 83 REFUSING: 1 slug(s) already exist in help_articles: reading-your-grade-report IT WILL HAPPEN IN PROD, and that is the point of finding it now. Both sides arrive there by construction: the KB row is seeded by MIGRATION 00189, which is applied in prod; the help article is content/help/180-reading-your-grade-report.md, which lands the moment US-2618's seed runs. So whoever runs this migration will meet the same stop, and the script will refuse until it is resolved by hand - which is correct, and is why it refuses rather than merging or skipping. THE RESOLUTION IS NOT A CLOSE CALL, though it is a content decision rather than mine to make. Same slug, same category (grading), same audience/visibility (public). The difference is length: the KB row is 941 characters, the hand-written help article is 4787. The KB version is a stub from the assistant launch seed; the help version is the written article. RECOMMEND: keep the help article, drop the KB row from the migration set. Confirm before running. THE OTHER SEVEN ROWS ARE UNBLOCKED by that one decision - the script reports one collision, not eight, so nothing else in the KB corpus contends with the written help articles. ORDERING NOTE THAT NOW HAS A CONSEQUENCE: the script's header says it must run BEFORE retrieval is repointed, and the previous note says the flag flip must come after rows land in prod. Both are still right, but there is a third constraint the collision exposes: this migration cannot be run until AFTER the help seed (US-2618 AC1), because the collision only exists once the 83 articles are there - and running it BEFORE the seed would migrate a KB stub into the slug the written article is about to claim, turning a clean refusal into a silent conflict at seed time. So the order is: seed help (US-2618), resolve this one slug, run this migration, then flip HELP_CORPUS_UNIFIED. | 2026-08-16 (same session) AC2's MECHANISM IS NOW PROVEN, not just built. The colliding help article was deleted on the LOCAL stack only and the migration was run with --apply. All 8 rows moved and every mapping is correct: account -> account subscriber -> members billing -> billing subscriber -> members flipdesk -> flipdesk public -> public grading -> grading public -> public disputes -> troubleshooting (judgement call #1) photos -> grading (judgement call #2) plans -> billing (a third remap, not flagged as one) All 8 land status=published with a NON-EMPTY, actually-rendered body_html (765-1369 chars, all containing markup) - so the markdownToHtml reuse the script's header argues for does work, and the migrated articles will render like the hand-written ones rather than nearly like them. RETRIEVAL ROUND-TRIPS, with a query chosen so the cap cannot explain the result: 'proration' matches 2 published articles total, one members-visible. public -> 1 [plans-and-credits]; subscriber -> 2 [+ upgrading-and-downgrading]. The widening and the narrowing both hold on real rows. ⚠ I FELL FOR THE CAP TRAP AGAIN FIRST. My initial retrieval probe searched 'access' and 'invoice', saw zero migrated hits for subscriber, and would have read as 'migrated rows are not searchable' - which would have been a serious false alarm. Both queries return 5 rows against KB_MAX_RESULTS=5. Checked in SQL instead: the migrated rows DO have a populated generated search_tsv and DO match those terms; they simply rank below five others. Second time today the same cap produced a plausible non-finding. ONE REAL, MODEST FINDING: every migrated row gets summary = '' because support_kb_articles has no summary column and help_articles.summary is NOT NULL. It degrades correctly rather than breaking - the SSR uses `article.summary || HELP_HUB_DESCRIPTION` and the list omits the paragraph entirely on a falsy value, so there is no empty meta description and no stray empty

. But 8 public articles would then SHARE the generic hub description, which is a duplicate-description signal across 8 pages. Worth either deriving a summary from the first paragraph in the script, or writing 8 by hand after the move. Not a blocker; recorded so it is a decision rather than a surprise. STATE OF THE LOCAL STACK, for whoever uses it next: it now has the migration APPLIED and reading-your-grade-report deleted, so it no longer matches a clean seed. Re-run `npm run help:seed` after a `supabase db reset` to get back to the 83-article baseline. | 2026-08-16 (same session) THE EMPTY-SUMMARY FINDING IS FIXED rather than just recorded. deriveSummary() builds one from the first real PARAGRAPH of the body, and toHelpArticle uses it. SIZED AGAINST THE CORPUS rather than guessed: the 83 hand-written summaries run 93-200 characters averaging 133, so the cap is 200 and the target is a whole sentence. Re-ran the migration against the local stack and all 8 landed between 80 and 152 characters, in range and readable. DELIBERATELY CONSERVATIVE ABOUT WHAT COUNTS AS PROSE - headings, list items, blockquotes, tables and fenced code blocks are skipped, and link/emphasis markup is stripped from what survives. A summary that opened with a fence marker or a bullet would be worse than the empty string it replaces, and this text is customer-facing on a public page. Where there is no prose at all it returns empty, which the SSR already handles. TRUNCATION PREFERS A SENTENCE, falls back to a word boundary, and never cuts mid-word. 9 cases in the new scripts/migrate-support-kb-to-help.test.mjs, which also pin the two judgement-call category maps and the audience-to-visibility map so they cannot drift from the convergence note. Sabotage-verified four ways: reverting to the empty string, a naive slice, letting list items through, and letting link markup survive. ⚠ WORTH KNOWING FOR THE PROD RUN: these summaries are DERIVED, not authored. A reasonable default that removes the duplicate-description problem; not a substitute for 8 written ones if these articles matter for search. | 2026-08-22 ONE MORE THING RIDES ON THE PROD MIGRATION, and it is in another story that does not name this one. US-2619 AC5 is 'recheck /og/help/ once real content exists'. Measured today: the live sitemap advertises 558 URLs and ZERO are /help/ pages, so /og/help has nothing to render and returns the branded fallback (exactly 133,915 bytes, byte-identical to /og-image.png). Its sibling /og/verified/pearson returns 124,359 bytes - a real render - which proves the renderer works and the help path is simply starved of input. So the row migration here is what unblocks that criterion. Worth knowing before the prod run, because it means the run has a second beneficiary and a second way to check it worked: after the rows land and the pages are in the sitemap, /og/help/ should stop returning 133,915 bytes.

userStories.title: The verify-email step is unmeasured, and a link opened on a second device dead-ends
userStories.description: As a person who just signed up, I want to finish verifying my email wherever I opened it, so that I actually reach the product. Signup emits four analytics events and verification emitted none, so a drop-off between the two can be asserted and not located. Two mechanisms sit behind it: whether GoTrue sends the branded hook email (a token_hash link plus a 6-digit code, both device-independent) or its own template (a PKCE code that only exchanges in the browser that started the signup), and whether SES delivers the mail at all.
acceptanceCriteria: The verify funnel is measurable end to end: an event for the check-your-email screen, for a resend, for a verification success, and for each distinct failure reason.

A confirmation link opened on a second device stops dead-ending. The client detects that it holds no PKCE verifier and offers the 6-digit code path instead of a fifteen-second spinner and advice that cannot work.
Whether the branded auth-email hook is configured is visible from outside in one unauthenticated GET, and the health line states the CONSEQUENCE rather than only the missing variable.
OPERATOR: confirm AUTH_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET on the edge and GOTRUE_HOOK_SEND_EMAIL_* on the auth container, then re-measure /health/ready features.auth_email_hook.
OPERATOR: confirm SES is out of sandbox and confirmation mail is actually delivered. No client event can tell an unopened email from an undelivered one.
Once the funnel has data, state the real drop-off number and decide whether anything further is worth building.
userStories.notes:
AC1-AC3 DONE 2026-08-15; AC4-AC6 are operator work and the story stays open on them. ⚠ THIS STORY WAS FILED AFTER THE WORK, and the reason belongs in the record: the pass began from a backlog row I read as 'GT-001 Fix the verify-email drop-off, priority high'. No such story exists - not in prd.json, not in prd.archive.json, not in git history, and the string 'verify-email drop-off' appears nowhere in the repo. It was a misread on my part, caught by prd.json refusing to contain the id I tried to edit. The engineering below is real and verified; only its provenance was wrong, and it is filed here rather than attached to a phantom. AC1: four events in src/lib/analytics-events.ts - signup.confirm_sent (the check-your-email screen, i.e. the denominator), signup.confirm_resend (at: signup|confirm), signup.email_verified (via: link|code), signup.verify_failed (reason: cross_device_pkce|link_expired|code_expired|code_rejected|callback_timeout). Emitted from signup.tsx, auth-confirm.tsx and auth-callback.tsx. Before this, signup emitted trial.started and signup.buyer and verification emitted nothing, so the funnel ended immediately before the part in question. AC2 IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT, and it is a real dead end rather than a UX nicety. The client runs PKCE (supabase.ts flowType). GoTrue's built-in confirmation template links at emailRedirectTo, which arrives carrying ?code=, and supabase-js can only exchange that code with the verifier it stored in the SIGNING-UP browser's localStorage. Open the mail on a phone and the exchange cannot succeed on any timescale - but auth-callback.tsx waited the full 15s and then said 'Sign-in is taking longer than expected. Please try signing in again.', which is advice that produces the same nothing every time. NEW src/lib/auth-pkce.ts (hasPkceVerifier / isCrossDeviceConfirmation) scans storage for a *-code-verifier key - by SUFFIX deliberately, because the key embeds the project ref, which on a self-hosted domain is the first host label (api), and a key rebuilt wrongly would route every user to recovery. Read ONCE on mount, because a successful exchange DELETES the verifier and a later read would call a completed sign-in a failure. Cross-device gets a 4s wait (long enough for an exchange that finished before mount to surface as a session) and then a card that says the link completes in the other browser, offers /auth/confirm for the 6-digit code, and states that nothing is wrong with the account. AC3: new auth_email_hook feature group in env-validation.ts, production-only, plus a new optional FeatureGroup.whenMissing that appends the CONSEQUENCE to the readiness line - 'missing: AUTH_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET' names a variable and not the fact that cross-device verification is broken meanwhile, which is exactly the shape that let release=dev sit in prod for three weeks (US-2001). MEASURED, not assumed: GET /health/ready today returns no auth_email_hook key at all, so whether prod sends branded device-independent mail or GoTrue defaults was invisible from every endpoint we serve. ALSO MEASURED IN THE SAME CALL: schema reports {expected:00603, applied:00606, status:ahead} - prod has 00604-00606 applied while the running edge image expects 00603, so the edge is behind the database, not the other way round. VERIFIED: env-validation_test.ts 26 passed (4 new), health + ops-health + env-debug 41 passed, auth-pkce.test.ts 9 passed (new), src/lib/__tests__ + auth-pages-have-seo 1074 passed across 81 files, tsc -b clean, eslint clean, ui:check 0 blocking 0/0 noise, deno lint + deno check clean on env-validation.ts. Negative-verified twice: dropping the whenMissing append reddened its own case, and the smtp case pins that it never fires on a satisfied group. DOCS: vault/40-growth/analytics-event-registry.md gains the funnel table and the note that these events see only people who reach the app (an undelivered email and an ignored one have the same client-side shape); vault/10-ops/env-reference.md gains the one-line curl that answers whether the hook is on. | 2026-08-15 HALF OF THIS IS ALREADY DONE AND THE LIST DID NOT KNOW. /health/ready now reports features.auth_email_hook = ok, so AUTH_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET IS set on the edge. Found by an inverse check - re-reading the live health surface against the declared operator queue, because telling someone to do a finished task is how a list stops being trusted. BUT ok OVERSTATED IT, and that is the real finding. The check reads ONE variable, AUTH_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET, on THIS service. It cannot see GOTRUE_HOOK_SEND_EMAIL_ENABLED / _URI / _SECRET on the auth container, and with those unset GoTrue quietly falls back to its built-in templates - so the cross-device signup stays broken while the health line says ok. A readiness line that overstates is worse than one that admits an edge, because the operator stops looking. FIXED, and it generalises to the story next door: new alsoUnverifiable field on a feature group, appended EVEN WHEN SATISFIED. whenMissing disappears the moment a variable is set, which is exactly the wrong moment for a two-sided feature - pages_origin_bypass spelled out the same value must also be set on the Cloudflare Pages project, and that sentence would have vanished the instant someone set the edge half, leaving a bare ok. Both groups now carry the caveat, and the Pages one names the redeploy too. TWO EXISTING TESTS ASSERTED THE OPPOSITE, deliberately, and I read their reasoning before overriding: whenMissing must never trail a satisfied group, or the page tells an operator to fix a working feature. That rule is UNCHANGED and still pinned - the smtp case proves a one-sided group is still a bare ok. This is a different field whose whole purpose is to trail a satisfied one, and each new assertion also refuses the alarm text. A MISTAKE WORTH KEEPING: my first negative assertion checked the satisfied line does not contain different device, and it failed against my own text - the satisfied line legitimately ends with the same advice, because signing up and opening the mail elsewhere is how you check the half it cannot see. Anchored to falling back instead, which only the missing branch says. A negative assertion has to name something only the WRONG branch says. STILL OPEN FOR THE OPERATOR: the GoTrue container half, and SES delivery. Neither is visible from here - but the readiness line now says so instead of implying otherwise. | 2026-08-15 (second) THE SMTP HALF IS NOT DONE EITHER, AND I NEARLY RECORDED THAT IT WAS. /health/ready reports smtp: ok, and my own memory note said SMTP/SES was misconfigured in prod - so the obvious read was that the note had gone stale. It has not. That check tests whether FOUR VARIABLES ARE PRESENT: SMTP_HOST, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL. An SES account still in sandbox ACCEPTS the connection and drops anything addressed to an unverified recipient, and the outbox retry swallows that gracefully by design - so every variable can be correct, the health line can read ok, and no customer receives anything. Same overstatement as auth_email_hook an hour earlier, on a group nobody would have questioned. smtp now carries alsoUnverifiable saying the variables are set and delivery is unproven, and pointing at the outbox and the sandbox question. THE CONTROL TEST HAD TO MOVE, and that is worth knowing before someone deletes it: one case exists purely to prove a bare ok is still REACHABLE - that whenMissing never leaks onto a satisfied group. It used smtp as its subject, and smtp has just stopped qualifying. Moved to ebay, which is genuinely one-sided (four credentials present IS the whole condition), with a note to move it again rather than delete it if that ever changes. A guard that proves the negative case needs a subject that stays negative. ALSO CORRECTED THE MEMORY rather than deleting it: memory is injected every session and silently outranks a note, so a memory that says the opposite of a health line is worse than none. It now says delivery is UNPROVEN, names US-2597 as the owner, and records that smtp: ok does not contradict it and why. WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT FOR THE OPERATOR ON THIS STORY: the GoTrue container half (GOTRUE_HOOK_SEND_EMAIL_*), and SES out of sandbox with one real delivery confirmed. Neither is visible from here - the difference now is that the readiness line says so instead of implying otherwise. VERIFIED: edge suite 6864 passed / 0 failed, deno check + lint clean, 29 cases in env-validation_test.ts. | 2026-08-29 MEASURED IN POSTHOG, which this session can reach. AC6 cannot be
answered yet, and the reason is not the one anyone would guess. No code changed.

POSTHOG IS CONNECTED AND RECEIVING. Project 'GradeThread' (464669), org Pearson
Media LLC. Unlike Sentry - where the connected account gets a 403 on the
project the app reports to - this one is live and queryable.

WEB TRAFFIC, $pageview by week over 30 days:
  2026-07-26   50
  2026-08-02   64
  2026-08-09   78
  2026-08-16   92
  2026-08-23   99 (partial)

That is roughly 380 pageviews in a month, rising steadily but from almost
nothing. AC6 says 'once the funnel has data, state the real drop-off number'.
The funnel does not have data because the SITE does not have traffic, which is
a different problem from the instrumentation being wrong and wants a different
fix.

NONE OF THE 89 EVENTS IN src/lib/analytics-events.ts APPEARS IN POSTHOG'S
TAXONOMY - not as active, not as stale. ⚠ AND THAT IS NOT EVIDENCE OF A BROKEN
PIPELINE, which is what I first took it for. Three things have to be held
together before drawing a conclusion:
  1. Browser autocapture DOES arrive: $pageview, $web_vitals, $rageclick.
  2. A separate MOBILE vocabulary arrives fine and is NOT in that registry -
     onboarding_started, paywall_opened, ai_extract_used, photo_upload_ok,

  3. track() in src/lib/analytics.ts is `window.posthog?.capture?.(...)` - a

At 380 pageviews a month, spread across certificates, calculators, checkers,
passports and the paywall, and gated behind a consent banner, zero custom
events is what you would expect. It is consistent with low volume; it is not
proof of a fault.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, for whoever picks this up: one deliberate visit that
accepts the consent banner and hits a page with a known track() call site
(cert_view and calculator_view each have exactly one), then look for that event.
That separates 'nobody has triggered it' from 'it cannot fire' in a single
action, which no amount of querying can.

THIS ALSO RE-FRAMES THREE OTHER THINGS. The calculator funnel's four saved

userStories.title: Every push to main restarts the production edge, including doc-only commits
userStories.description: Coolify auto-deploys the edge service on any push to main, with no path filter, so a commit that touches only PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md or prd.json rebuilds the image and rolls the container. Each roll is a short window where Traefik has no healthy backend and the public API answers 'no available server' - observed directly on 2026-08-15: two consecutive probes of /health returned 503 and the third returned 200, with /health/ready clean on five reads immediately after. Nothing was wrong; that IS the rollover. The cost is small per push and this repo pushes often - six times in one afternoon during a backlog loop, which is six avoidable 503 windows on the seller-facing API plus six image builds. WHY IT ALSO MATTERS FOR DIAGNOSIS, which is the sharper half: 'no available server' is the documented signature of an edge event-loop HANG (vault/10-ops/edge-hang-vs-crash-loop.md). A routine doc push producing the same string as a real incident trains whoever sees it to shrug, and the one time it is not a rollover is the time that costs an outage.
acceptanceCriteria: The edge redeploys only when something that ships inside its image changed: services/edge-functions/** and the files its build reads.
A commit touching only markdown, prd.json or src/ does not roll the edge container.
The mechanism is recorded in vault/10-ops/deploy.md next to the auto-deploy line, so the next person does not rediscover it from a 503.
The frontend half is checked at the same time: Cloudflare Pages rebuilds on every push too, which is cheaper but not free.

OPERATOR: this is a Coolify setting, not a repo change. In the edge resource, set the build/watch path filter to services/edge-functions (Coolify calls it Watch Paths). Nothing in this repository can do it, and nothing here can verify it either except by pushing a doc-only commit and watching whether the container rolls.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-15 FILED FROM A LIVE OBSERVATION, not from reading config. During a backlog loop, curl https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returned the bare string 'no available server'. Two consecutive /health probes then returned 503 and the third 200, with five clean /health/ready reads immediately after - so it was a Coolify rollover from the push a minute earlier, not an incident. THE DIAGNOSTIC COST IS THE REAL POINT: 'no available server' is the documented signature of an edge event-loop HANG (vault/10-ops/edge-hang-vs-crash-loop.md, and a memory note says the same). A routine doc-only push producing the identical string as a genuine incident teaches whoever sees it to shrug, and the one time it is not a rollover is the time that costs an outage. Six pushes in one afternoon meant six of these windows on the seller-facing API, every one of them for a commit that changed markdown or prd.json and nothing that ships inside the edge image. The fix is a Coolify Watch Paths setting on the edge resource; nothing in this repo can make it or verify it. | 2026-08-17 AC3 AND AC4 DONE. AC1/AC2 are the Coolify setting and stay with the owner, as AC5 says.  AC3: vault/10-ops/deploy.md section 2 now carries the mechanism next to the auto-deploy line, with the observation that produced it and the exact setting to change - Watch Paths on the edge resource, set to services/edge-functions/**. The part worth having in the runbook is not the seconds of downtime, it is that a doc-only push emits the bare string "no available server", which edge-hang-vs-crash-loop.md documents as the signature of an event-loop HANG. Someone reading a real hang and a routine deploy sees the same string, and the runbook now says so on the page where they will be looking.  AC4 CHECKED, AND THE TWO HALVES ARE NOT THE SAME SHAPE, which is the useful finding. Cloudflare Pages does rebuild on every push, so the story is right that it is not free - but a Pages rebuild costs build minutes and nothing else. Pages keeps serving the previous deployment until the new one is ready and swaps atomically, so there is no window with no backend and no 503. The edge rolls its only container; Pages does not. That asymmetry is why the edge setting is worth doing and the frontend one is optional.  AND THE FRONTEND HALF HAS A FAILURE DIRECTION THE EDGE HALF DOES NOT, recorded rather than left for whoever tries it: Pages calls the setting Build watch paths, and the include set has to cover everything `npm run build` reads - src/**, public/**, functions/** (the Pages Functions are deployed from there), index.html, package.json, package-lock.json, vite.config.ts, the tsconfig*.json files and scripts/prerender.mjs, since build is `tsc -b && vite build && node scripts/prerender.mjs`. Get that list wrong in the TIGHTENING direction and a real change silently does not deploy, which is worse than a wasted build. So the runbook says do the edge one and treat the frontend one as optional.  NOTHING HERE CAN VERIFY EITHER, unchanged and stated in the runbook: the only test is a doc-only push followed by watching whether the container rolls.  VERIFIED: vault:index regenerated, vault:lint --strict clean (187 notes, 0 errors). deploy.md reviewed bumped to 2026-08-17.  STILL OPEN: AC1, AC2 and AC5 - one setting in the Coolify UI. | 2026-08-17 (second pass) THE FACT REACHED THE OPERATOR-FACING COPY, which is where it was always going to matter most.  The first pass put the rollover in vault/10-ops/deploy.md. The vault lane then failed - runbook-sync flagged the SHIPPED distillation in src/lib/admin/runbooks.ts as stale against it. That guard is doing exactly its job: the vault note is what an engineer reads, and the shipped copy is what an operator reads IN THE ADMIN CONSOLE DURING AN INCIDENT. This story fact only pays off in the second place.  The deploy-order runbook now carries it as a callout: `no available server` is what a routine deploy produces AND the documented signature of an edge event-loop hang, two 503s then a 200 during a deploy is the rollover, re-check /health/ready a few seconds later before escalating, and if it stays down past a minute it is not the rollover. Someone who has not been told that either escalates a rollover or - worse - shrugs at a real hang.  ALSO CARRIED ACROSS, from US-2665: docker-compose.coolify.yml is not the deployed configuration, with the /health/metrics measurement. That one stops an operator chasing a setting the repo declares and the running container does not have.  WORTH NOTING ABOUT THE GUARD ITSELF: this is the FIRST of four consecutive checks on that copy to produce an actual edit. The previous three cost a date bump and nothing else, because the copy names no counts and points at CRON_REGISTRY instead. That is the phrasing working rather than the check being noisy - and it means a bump is cheap enough that nobody should be tempted to skip the re-read.  VERIFIED: node scripts/verify.mjs --vault, all 5 checks pass; npx tsc -b clean; runbook + ci-parity tests 13 passed; ui:check 0 blocking.

userStories.title: A garment with no readable tag cannot be graded at all, and that is a real garment, not an edge case
userStories.description: image-quality.ts REQUIRED_IMAGE_TYPES is ['front','back','label'] at severity 'block', applied at grading-pipeline Step 4b BEFORE any confidence scoring, so a submission with no label photo abstains to needs_photos and is never graded. US-2304 confirmed that requirement on purpose (owner, 2026-08-03) and it is the right call for the common case - a FlipDesk item without a tag used to be charged, burn one vision call per image, abstain, and be refunded, which cost the seller a round trip and cost us the AI spend. But the note that recorded the decision also recorded what it left open, and nothing carries it: SOME GARMENTS GENUINELY HAVE NO READABLE TAG. Lululemon and several athletic brands print a cut size on a heat-transfer label that wears off entirely; resale-grade basics are often tagless by design; vintage tags are frequently cut out by the original owner. Those sellers are not photographing badly, they are photographing what exists, and today the product tells them to add a photo they cannot take. The pipeline is not wrong to want provenance evidence - the question is what stands in for a tag when there is no tag, and whether a grade without it is capped rather than refused.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide what a seller with a genuinely tagless garment is asked to photograph instead: a size/wash print inside the collar, a hem or seam construction shot, or nothing at all with the grade capped.

If a substitute is accepted, the abstention becomes a CAP rather than a refusal, composed through composeConfidenceCap like every other cap, lowering both the confidence and the reported ceiling (US-2299).
The seller is told this up front, in the client validator, not after paying and round-tripping.
The grading prompt is told the tag is absent rather than left to infer it from a missing image, so it does not read the absence as evidence about the garment.
Measure first: how many submissions abstain on a missing label specifically, versus the other two required types. If it is rare, the honest answer may be a clearer refusal message and nothing more.

OPERATOR: run section 27 of scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql (AC5), which decides whether this story gets built at all. It counts submissions stuck in needs_photos by which required photo is missing. READ IT WITH ITS LIMIT: quality_feedback is nulled the moment a grade is produced, so this measures who is STUCK NOW, not how often it has happened - it undercounts by every seller who added the photo and succeeded. If 'label' is far ahead of front and back, the tagless case is real and worth building; if the three are level, it is ordinary incomplete uploads and the fix is upload-time guidance rather than a grading change.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-15 FILED FROM US-2304's OWN LEFT-OPEN NOTE, which had no story carrying it. That note said, verbatim, that the old comment's concern is real and that tagless garments are a product question 'r...' - the segment was truncated mid-sentence and nothing downstream picked it up. VERIFIED THE MECHANISM before filing rather than trusting the note: services/edge-functions/src/lib/image-quality.ts:80 is REQUIRED_IMAGE_TYPES = ['front','back','label'], line 83 puts all three in CORE_TYPES, and lines 129-136 raise a 'missing' issue at severity BLOCK for any absent one. So the refusal is real and it is unconditional. AC5 IS DELIBERATELY FIRST IN INTENT EVEN THOUGH IT IS LAST IN ORDER: this may be rare enough that the honest answer is a clearer refusal message and nothing else, and building a substitute-photo path before measuring picks a fix blind - the same mistake US-2288's notes describe. The measurement is narrow: of submissions that abstain, how many abstain on 'label' specifically rather than on front or back. NOT A DUPLICATE OF US-2397, which made a missing fabric CLOSE-UP a cap instead of an abstention. That story's reasoning is the precedent this one would follow, and its rule is the constraint: a cap must lower the confidence AND the reported ceiling (US-2299), or the next provenance boost lifts the stored number straight back over it. | 2026-08-15 AC5's MEASUREMENT IS NOW ONE PASTE, and writing it surfaced a limit worth knowing before anyone reads the number. §27 of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql counts submissions currently in needs_photos, grouped by which required image_type raised a blocking 'missing' issue. THE LIMIT: quality_feedback is set to NULL the moment a grade is produced (00069), so every seller who added the photo and succeeded has already erased their own row. §27 therefore measures who is STUCK, not how often this has happened. That is arguably the more actionable set - it is the people the product is failing right now - but it is a different question from the one AC5 asks, and reading it as a history would undercount by exactly the recoveries. Said in the section itself, not just here. ONE PIECE OF DEFENSIVE SQL THAT IS NOT DRESSING: jsonb_array_elements RAISES on a non-array, and a single malformed quality_feedback row would end the operator's session before every section after it. The CASE guard yields an empty array instead. Same class as the SHOW bug caught in §23 an hour earlier, which is twice now that the failure mode of this file is 'kills the session' rather than 'returns the wrong answer'. READING GUIDE: label far ahead of front/back is the tagless case and this story is worth building; roughly level across the three is ordinary incomplete uploads and the fix is upload-time guidance, not a grading change. | [2026-09-02][PROD READ] AC5 ANSWERED: it is the DETAIL photo, not the label. Source: scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql run read-only against prod over SSH on 2026-09-02 (container supabase-db-kcksoks4kk0kswk0ccs40os8, 29 sections, 0 SQL errors). Raw output kept out of the repo; it contains customer data. Submissions stuck on a missing required photo: detail 6, label 1. So the garment that cannot be graded is overwhelmingly one missing a detail shot rather than one with no readable tag, which is a different fix from the one the story's title assumes. Worth re-reading the premise against this before building.

userStories.title: Wire the remaining unmonitored crons into the ledger, starting with the eBay token refresh
userStories.description: US-2616 made the cron fleet monitor name the eight registry entries it never examines. This closes them. ebay-token-refresh is done: its handler already gated on requireJobSecret, so it was reachable as a cron all along and only the recordEbayCron mount was missing. The rest split into three shapes, and only one is a mount. THREE ARE UNREACHABLE, not merely unrecorded: ebay-orders-sync, photo-archive and reconciliation-sweep sit behind authMiddleware with no requireJobSecret branch, so they 401 before the handler runs - pinned in cron-registry-drift_test.ts KNOWN_UNREACHABLE_CRONS since US-2310. They can neither run nor be seen not running, and each needs a job-secret branch plus a server-side tenant loop. TWO USE A DIFFERENT SECRET: content-tick and content-digest authenticate with CONTENT_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET while recordEbayCron keys on the X-Internal-Job-Secret header, so recording them means teaching the recorder a second header rather than adding a mount. TWO ARE ONE-OFFS: passport-backfill and cert-integrity-backfill have no cadence to miss, which is correct and permanent.
acceptanceCriteria: ebay-token-refresh records to cron_runs and is examined by cron-fleet-health.
content-tick and content-digest record, via a recorder that recognises CONTENT_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET, or the reason they cannot is written at the registry entry.
The three unreachable crons get a requireJobSecret branch and a server-side tenant loop, so they can actually be invoked by a scheduler - and then recorded.
The shrink-only list in cron-fleet-governance_test.ts loses a name for each one closed; the one-offs stay and are labelled permanent.

OPERATOR: after the next edge deploy, expect cron-fleet-health to report ebay-token-refresh as STALLED if its Coolify task does not exist. That is the finding, not a false positive - the detector computes expected slots from the schedule rather than from prior runs, so this is the question is-this-task-installed answering itself for the first time.

OPERATOR: delete the Coolify scheduled task named ebay-orders-sync. Its registry entry is gone (ebay-order-backstop was already the same half-hourly sweep, working), so the task now hits a seller route that answers 401 and nothing in the repo can see it - the drift check catches a MISSING task, never an extra one.

OPERATOR: change the photo-archive Coolify task URL to /api/jobs/photo-archive. It has pointed at /api/flipdesk/images/archive, a seller route, so the nightly sweep has answered 401 every night since it was created. The old URL still works for a signed-in seller and is deliberately left alone.

OPERATOR: change the reconciliation-sweep Coolify task URL to /api/jobs/reconciliation-sweep. Same fault as photo-archive - it pointed at a seller route and has answered 401 every night. /api/flipdesk/reconciliation/run stays as the seller Auto-match button.
userStories.notes: PARTIAL 2026-08-15 — AC1 DONE, and it was two lines once the premise was checked rather than trusted. The registry said 'served under /api/flipdesk/* - not in the ledger', which states WHERE the job lives, not a reason it cannot be seen; flipdesk-ebay.ts:633 shows the handler gating on requireJobSecret, so it has always been invocable as a cron. main.ts mounts recordEbayCron by path and simply did not cover this one. Mounted it and flipped recorded to true; COOLIFY.md and vault/10-ops/launch-checklist.md regenerated from CRON_REGISTRY (the drift guard caught the stale table, correctly). WHY THIS ONE FIRST: if the hourly refresh stops, seller eBay tokens expire and their listings stop syncing - a failure with no symptom until a seller notices, which is exactly what the fleet alert exists to catch. EXPECT AN ALERT, and it is not a false positive: detectMissedTicks computes expected slots from the SCHEDULE rather than from prior runs, so a job whose Coolify task does not exist reads as stalled from the first elapsed hour. That is the question 'is this task actually installed?' answering itself for the first time in the ledger - recorded as an OPERATOR criterion so nobody silences it as noise. THE SHRINK-ONLY GUARD DID ITS JOB: US-2616's case asserted ebay-token-refresh BY NAME as part of the blind spot, so fixing the job reddened the test instead of letting it keep passing on a quietly smaller set. The list now carries a reason beside each remaining name. VERIFIED: 28 cases across cron-registry-drift_test.ts and cron-fleet-governance_test.ts pass, deno check + deno lint clean, tsc -b clean, vault:lint strict clean. | 2026-08-15 (second pass) AC2 DONE, AND THE PREMISE IN THE STORY WAS WRONG. This story said content-tick and content-digest could not be recorded because they authenticate with CONTENT_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET while the recorder keys on X-Internal-Job-Secret. Reading content-scheduler.ts:74 shows that is a confusion between the HEADER and the SECRET: both schedulers read the same X-Internal-Job-Secret header and merely validate it against a different env var. recordEbayCron only asks which header ARRIVED - the handler still decides whether the value is valid - so it needed a mount, not a second header. Both are now recorded, and the blind spot is 8 -> 5 (three unreachable + two one-offs). ONE REAL WIDENING WHILE THERE: the recorder now treats X-Internal-Job-Signature as a cron call too. The content, newsletter and drip schedulers all accept the signed variant (HMAC + freshness + single-use), so keying only on the static header would have recorded a caller using the WEAKER path and silently skipped the same job on the stronger one - a ledger gap that appears exactly when someone improves the caller. NEW GUARD, and it caught a false positive on its first run, which is the part worth keeping: 'every recorded cron outside /api/jobs/* has a recorder mounted' immediately flagged drip-tick and newsletter-kickoff. Both were fine - they call recordCronRun DIRECTLY inside their handlers, with per-branch statuses the middleware could not produce (the drip tick records a 404 no-such-campaign as its own error row). So the guard was too narrow, not the code, and it now accepts either mechanism. Had I trusted it, the next reader would have been sent to fix two things that were already right. WHY THIS GUARD MATTERS AT ALL: recorded:true is a CLAIM, and nothing checked it. Flipping it without a recorder is worse than leaving it alone - cron-fleet-health starts expecting ledger rows that can never arrive, so the job reads as permanently stalled and the alert is about the wiring rather than the job, which is how an on-call learns to ignore the channel. VERIFIED: 13 cases in cron-registry-drift_test.ts and 17 in cron-fleet-governance_test.ts, all green; sabotage-verified by deleting the content-tick mount, which reddened the new guard naming that exact endpoint. COOLIFY.md and vault/10-ops/launch-checklist.md regenerated. deno check + lint clean, tsc -b clean. | 2026-08-15 (third pass) THE FULL EDGE SUITE CAUGHT THREE FAILURES FROM THIS WORK, and one was a pre-existing bug two steps from anything I edited. Running the whole suite rather than only the touched files is what found it: 6852 passed, 3 failed. (1) cert-public-allowlist_test.ts — display_title (US-2613) is route-added like 'title' itself, so it belongs in ROUTE_ADDED; recorded there with a pointer to why it has no counterpart in the public_grade_reports view. (2) cron-runs_test.ts — the case used /api/flipdesk/ebay/oauth/refresh as its example of an UNRECORDED path, which this story just made recorded. Swapped to ebay-orders-sync, the honest example now (US-2310: it 401s on every fire, so there is genuinely nothing to record), plus a new case asserting the three newly-recorded paths resolve. (3) ops-jobs_test.ts — THE IMPORTANT ONE. isRunnableJob is built from the recorded flag, and its comment claimed that meant 'served at /api/jobs/*'. That was a PROXY, and it decides which jobs get a Run-now button in the admin console. Following it found the real defect: admin-ops.ts sent FLIPDESK_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET to every job, while FOUR recorded jobs authenticate against their own env var — drip-tick, newsletter-kickoff, content-tick, content-digest. So Run-now on those has always answered 401, and an operator reading a red result concludes the JOB is broken when the CALLER was. drip-tick and newsletter-kickoff have been in that state for a long time; this story added two more of the same shape and made the pattern visible. FIXED: new jobSecretEnvFor() resolves secretEnv ?? DEFAULT_JOB_SECRET_ENV, admin-ops uses it, and a missing secret now NAMES the variable rather than saying 'Job runner secret not configured' — which sent whoever read it to check the one they already had set. The registry has carried secretEnv since US-1561 for exactly this and nothing consumed it. GUARD-THE-GUARD: one case pins the four by name, another DERIVES the expectation from CRON_REGISTRY for every recorded job, so a new job with its own secret cannot be silently sent the default. | 2026-08-15 (fourth pass) AC3 IS ONE THIRD DONE, AND THE FIX WAS A DELETE. I had the /jobs/orders-sync route written - requireJobSecret, an acquireJobLock, a stalest-first owner scan over marketplace_connections, triggerEbaySyncForUser per owner, bounded fan-out - before checking whether that job already existed. IT DID. ebay-order-backstop (US-1965, routes/jobs-ebay-order-backstop.ts) is the same */30 fleet sweep through the same triggerEbaySyncForUser, plus a 15-minute freshness window and a PURE unit-tested selector (selectBackstopOwners) my version did not have. So the scheduled eBay orders sync has been running correctly this whole time, and the ebay-orders-sync registry entry described a second, permanently-401ing copy of it. Shipping my route would have put two fleet sweeps on one eBay rate-limit bucket on the same cadence. Reverted it and deleted the entry instead. WHAT MADE IT LOOK LIKE MISSING WORK: the entry pointed at /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/pull, a SELLER route that reads workspaceOwnerId ?? userId, so it 401d on every fire; recorded:false meant no ledger row; and US-2310 had already classified it as needing 'a job-secret branch plus a server-side tenant loop'. Every signal pointed at build-the-loop and none of them pointed at look-for-the-existing-job. The tell I should have caught earlier is that the tenant-isolation suite already had a case titled 'eBay order-backstop job rejects a user JWT' describing a sweep over EVERY active tenant's connection. SCOREBOARD: KNOWN_UNREACHABLE_CRONS 3 -> 2 (photo-archive, reconciliation-sweep remain, and both should be checked for an existing equivalent before either gets a loop written). The fleet monitor's blind spot 5 -> 4. CRON_REGISTRY 78 -> 77, which reddened the deploy.md count guard correctly and was fixed there. NEW GUARD, and it is a guard against RE-ADDING rather than a shrink-only list: a case asserts ebay-orders-sync is absent from CRON_REGISTRY and that ebay-order-backstop is present, so if the backstop is ever deleted the assertion fails instead of quietly protecting nothing. Sabotage-verified by re-adding the entry, which reddened exactly that case. OPERATOR, and it is new work rather than a re-statement: DELETE the Coolify scheduled task named ebay-orders-sync. It has never succeeded and the drift check cannot see an EXTRA task, only a missing one - so nothing in the repo will ever tell you it is still there. VERIFIED: edge suite 6862 passed / 0 failed, deno check + deno lint clean, tsc -b clean, vault:lint --strict clean, runbook-sync clean. COOLIFY.md, CRON_SETUP.md and vault/10-ops/launch-checklist.md regenerated from the registry; vault/10-ops/cron-schedule-governance.md records the look-for-the-existing-job lesson under 'what is still manual', which is where the extra-task risk was already written down. | 2026-08-15 (fifth pass) AC3 IS TWO THIRDS DONE — photo-archive now has the /jobs/ route and fleet loop, and this time building it was the RIGHT call, which is only knowable because I ran the check the last pass told me to run. Grepped for an existing photo-archival job: there is none, and /api/flipdesk/images/archive is the only implementation. The opposite of ebay-orders-sync, and the two together are the rule: LOOK FOR THE EXISTING JOB FIRST, THEN WRITE THE LOOP. The search costs a grep; the wrong answer costs a duplicate sweep. WHAT SHIPPED. flipdesk-images.ts:/archive was a 130-line inline handler; it is now three pieces. loadArchivablePhotos(ownerId|null, limit) holds the eligibility predicate ONCE - the ownerId and the fleet read share it deliberately, because the predicate carries the US-979 PII refusal (tag/tag_2/certificate close-ups live in the PRIVATE bucket and archival rewrites photo_url to an UNAUTHENTICATED public R2 URL), and a second copy of that filter written for the cron is exactly how a private tag gets published. archiveOwnerPhotos(ownerId) is the per-owner work, returning {ok,result}|{ok:false,error} so the route can still failSafe and the cron can count. listOwnersWithArchivablePhotos(limit) is the fleet read, named so it cannot be mistaken for a seller-facing one at a call site - the null branch is NOT exported. NEW routes/jobs-photo-archive.ts at /api/jobs/photo-archive: requireJobSecret, a 900s lock (this job does the work rather than dispatching it, unlike the sync crons), owners resolved from the photo ROWS and never from the request, bounded at 25 owners per nightly tick with a scan limit 20x that - a scan capped at 25 ROWS could resolve one owner and report the fleet done. eligible_owners reports the whole eligible fleet so a cap that stopped keeping up is readable rather than inferable. R2 unconfigured returns skipped rather than 500, because a nightly 500 for an optional integration is how an on-call learns to ignore the ledger. TENANT ISOLATION: two cases in tenant-isolation_test.ts (user JWT -> 401, bogus secret -> 401). The route publishes to public URLs across every tenant, so the job secret is the only thing between a signed-in user and a fleet-wide publish. THE GUARD I ACTUALLY CAME AWAY WITH, and it is bigger than this story. cron-registry-drift's US-2310 check SKIPS /api/jobs/* with the comment 'every handler there gates on the secret'. That was an assumption nobody had checked, and it is the MORE dangerous half: a cron behind authMiddleware with no secret branch merely 401s forever, while an /api/jobs/* route with no secret branch is callable by anyone on the internet, and several of them sweep every tenant. New case asserts it from source for all 40 routes. IT TOOK THREE CORRECTIONS AND EVERY ONE WAS THE GUARD, NOT THE CODE. (1) Scanning only routes/ reported seven safe handlers as ungated - email-retry lives in lib/email-retry.ts, sync-reaper in lib/sync-run-lock.ts. (2) Non-recursive lib/ missed two more in lib/appstore/ and lib/google-play/. (3) Anchoring handler names on a 'handle' prefix missed watchdogHeartbeatHandler, which puts the word at the other end; it matches any identifier called with (c) now. Each time I read the named handler before touching it, and each time it was already correct. A guard that names a safe route is worse than no guard, because whoever checks the first name deletes the rest. AND ONE SABOTAGE THAT PASSED WHEN IT SHOULD NOT HAVE, which is the part worth keeping: the first version took a fixed 700-character window after each app.post, which SPILLED into the following routes - so a neighbour's handler name satisfied this route's check. Deleting the photo-archive gate left the guard green. The window now ends at the next top-level app.* declaration. An over-wide window is the failure mode that makes a guard look like it works. SCOREBOARD: KNOWN_UNREACHABLE_CRONS 2 -> 1 (reconciliation-sweep alone), blind spot 4 -> 3, CRON_REGISTRY 77 (photo-archive changed endpoint, it was not added or removed). Neither touches a payout row. THE ALLOWLIST IS KEPT AT ZERO RATHER THAN DELETED, and the assertion is === 0 rather than <= 3: a guard whose budget has slack is a guard that permits one more. KNOWN_UNREACHABLE_CRONS 3 -> 0. userStories.title: The Help Center is live and empty: 83 articles are written and none are in the database
userStories.description: Measured against production on 2026-08-15. https://gradethread.com/help returns 200 and renders its header, search box and support CTA with ZERO article links. help_categories has all 14 seeded rows readable by anon, so the schema and the seed migration landed. help_articles returns [] to anon. Meanwhile content/help/ holds 83 written markdown articles and scripts/seed-help-articles.mjs exists to load them - it reads SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY from the environment and POSTs to /rest/v1/help_articles. It is wired to NOTHING: no npm script, no workflow, no cron, no deploy step. So an epic's worth of content sits in the repo while the page that exists to show it renders an empty state to customers and to Google. The indexability angle sharpens it: /help is in the sitemap, and a live thin-content hub is worse than no page at all on a domain that already has an unresolved indexing problem (US-2095).
acceptanceCriteria: The 83 articles in content/help/ are loaded into help_articles in production, and /help lists them.
Seeding is repeatable and idempotent rather than a one-off paste: re-running must update rather than duplicate, keyed on slug, which the script's existing slug read suggests it already intends.
Loading is wired to something - an npm script at minimum, ideally a step that runs on deploy - so the next 83 articles do not need someone to remember a command.
A check fails, or at least reports, when the Help Center hub renders zero articles. A page that serves 200 with no content is the failure mode nothing currently notices.

OPERATOR: run SUPABASE_URL=... SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=... node scripts/seed-help-articles.mjs against production, then re-check https://gradethread.com/help. The script needs the service-role key, which is why it cannot be automated from here.
userStories.notes: PARTIAL 2026-08-15 — AC3 and AC4 DONE; AC1, AC2 and the OPERATOR criterion remain. HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the method generalises: verifying US-2572's schema against production rather than against the migration file. help_categories returns all 14 seeded rows to anon, so 00602 landed; help_articles returns []. Then GET /help — 200, 15689 bytes, and ZERO href="/help/..." links. The page renders its header, search box and support CTA over nothing. AC3: `npm run help:seed` now exists. The loader (scripts/seed-help-articles.mjs) was written and wired to NOTHING — no npm script, no workflow, no deploy step — which is how 83 finished articles ended up invisible with every check green. AC4: the production route probe (US-2611) grew a `mustLink` check for /help and /blog. A status code cannot see this failure: both are INDEXES whose whole job is to link to what they index, and an empty one still answers 200 with a full page of chrome. THE EXCEPTION IS DELIBERATE AND SHAPED LIKE THE REST OF THIS REPO'S: /help is in a KNOWN_EMPTY_INDEXES map, reported rather than failed, because the condition is TRUE TODAY and a check that is red on the day it ships gets ignored before it earns any authority — the reason db-denied-rpc-crash-check.mjs is advisory and what US-1927's notes record. The entry names the work that removes it and the list is shrink-only, so seeding the articles and deleting the line turns it into a real gate. Known gaps print BEFORE the verdict, so they are visible on a green run too. AC1/AC2 need the service-role key against production, which is the OPERATOR criterion. AC2 looks already satisfied by the script (it reads existing slugs first and skips them, with --force upserting via merge-duplicates) but that is unverified against a real database, so it is not being claimed. VERIFIED: 9 cases in src/test/public-routes-probe.test.ts; the probe exits 0 with the exception present and 1 without it, checked directly rather than through a pipe. eslint + tsc -b clean. ONE SELF-INFLICTED LOSS WORTH RECORDING: after sabotage-verifying, I restored the file with git checkout -- , which reverted to the last COMMIT and destroyed every uncommitted edit in it. Redone from a /tmp copy. Restore from a copy, not from git, when the work is not yet committed. | 2026-08-15 THE COMMAND IS PROVEN BEFORE YOU RUN IT, which is the point of this pass - an operator step that fails halfway through is worse than one nobody has started. Ran scripts/seed-help-articles.mjs --dry-run: all 83 files in content/help/ parse cleanly, every one has frontmatter, a category, a visibility and 2 FAQ entries, and word counts land between 604 and 826. CHECKED THE THREE THINGS THAT WOULD MAKE IT FAIL PART-WAY. (1) CATEGORIES: the articles use 13 distinct category keys and all 13 are among the 14 seeded live in help_categories (confirmed against production earlier today by an anon read that returned all 14). Only account is unused, so no insert can fail on the foreign key. (2) VISIBILITY: the files use public, members and internal, which are exactly the three values the 00602 enum defines - and 00602 is applied in production (health/ready reports only 00594 missing). (3) THE SIX ops-* ARTICLES ARE internal, and that is correct rather than an oversight: US-2594 established that NOBODY reaches internal through the support assistant, not a subscriber and not an admin, so seeding operator runbooks alongside customer articles does not expose them. WHAT THE DRY RUN CANNOT PROVE: that the write succeeds. It never opens a connection. But a parse failure, an unknown category or a bad enum value are the three ways this would break mid-run, and none of them is present. NOTHING ELSE CHANGED. This is a de-risking pass on an operator step, not a code change. | 2026-08-16 THE OPERATOR COMMAND WAS DE-RISKED BY RUNNING WHAT COULD BE RUN, and one branch of it could never have worked. The story stays open on AC1 (the seed actually reaching prod) and AC4.  --force COULD NOT WORK, and would have failed in exactly the situation it exists for. It POSTed with Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates, and this table cannot be upserted through PostgREST at all. PROVEN against a real Postgres, not argued, inside a rolled-back transaction:   - inserting an existing slug raises 23505 unique_violation;   - ON CONFLICT (slug), which is what ?on_conflict=slug compiles to, raises     42P10 'there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT     specification'. The reason is that 00602 makes the slug unique with an EXPRESSION index - create unique index idx_help_articles_slug on public.help_articles (lower(slug)) - and Postgres can only target that with ON CONFLICT (lower(slug)), which PostgREST has no syntax for. So --force would have reported FAIL on every already-live article and exited 1. FIXED: --force now PATCHes ?slug=eq.<slug>, which is what 'overwrite' honestly means here. Exact match, never ilike - _ and % are SQL wildcards and both are legal in a slug, the same trap the erasure runbook records for email addresses.  THE PAYLOAD FITS, which was the other unknown. All 83 parsed articles were INSERTED into the live schema on a stack built from the whole migration corpus, inside a transaction that was rolled back: every column exists, every category_key resolves against the FK, no slug collides. So the operator's run will not fail on a schema mismatch.  WHAT IS STILL UNEXERCISED, stated because the rest was executed and the difference matters: the HTTP half. The local stack in this repo runs Postgres WITHOUT PostgREST (supabase start reports kong/rest/studio stopped under this config.toml), so nothing has round-tripped a real REST call. The SQL the calls reduce to has been proven; the transport has not.  NOT A PROBLEM, CHECKED: the existing-slug read has no explicit limit, which would matter if PostgREST clipped it - a truncated set means re-inserting live articles and 23505 on each. vault/10-ops/postgrest-row-cap.md settles it: db-max-rows is UNSET in prod, measured twice including from the server side. No guard added, because inventing one would imply a cap that does not exist.  AC2 IS ALREADY SATISFIED BUT NOT THE WAY IT IS WORDED, and the wording should not be followed literally. It asks that 're-running must update rather than duplicate'. The script deliberately SKIPS an existing slug and says why: once an article is live the admin editor owns it, and a re-run that overwrote would clobber UI edits with a stale file. Repeatable and idempotent: yes. Update by default: no, on purpose. --force is the opt-in, and it now works.  AC3 IS DONE: package.json already carries help:seed. AC4 - a check that fails or reports when the hub renders zero articles - remains, and is genuinely open.  NEW GUARD scripts/seed-help-articles.test.mjs, 6 cases, in the suite that runs in verify.mjs:208 and ci.yml:140. It pins the PATCH, refuses the merge-duplicates spelling and ilike, asserts the expression-index PREMISE still holds (so a later migration adding a plain unique(slug) reddens rather than silently invalidating the reasoning), reads the NOT NULL columns out of the migration rather than hand-listing them, and refuses two articles sharing a slug.  THE GUARD'S FIRST VERSION FAILED ON THE CORRECTED FILE: it searched the raw source for 'resolution=merge-duplicates', and the fix's own comment names the string while explaining the bug. Comments are stripped now. THIRD time this shape has appeared here, and it is not coincidence - it is what happens when the guard and the explanation live in the same file.  SABOTAGE-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS, each reverted green: restoring the upsert, ilike on the slug, a plain unique(slug) appearing in the migration, and two article files sharing a slug. 436 tests across 27 script suites passing. | 2026-08-16 AC4 DONE. The uptime probe gains a help_hub target, so a Help Center that serves 200 with nothing on it stops being invisible.  WHY NOTHING NOTICED, traced rather than assumed: renderCategoryGrid (functions/_shared/help-render.ts:264) returns an EMPTY STRING when every category is empty. So the hub renders its breadcrumbs, its heading, its description and its search box, and then stops. No 404, no error, no empty state - the page looks finished. That is the live state today, and a status-only check reports it healthy because it IS 200.  The new target asserts on the BODY: the absence of class="related-grid" is the signal. Its presence says nothing about HOW MANY articles, which is fine - zero is the number worth naming.  A NOTE, NOT A FAILURE, and that is the decision rather than a weaker version of one. The hub is empty RIGHT NOW, so a hard check would open an incident issue on the first run and keep the monitor red until someone runs the seed. A monitor red for a known reason is one nobody reads during a real outage. The probe already records exactly this reasoning for hostWatchdog (US-2447) and this follows it. AC4 asks for a check that 'fails, or at least reports'; a note surfaces in every run log AND in the body of any incident issue, which is the moment 'the help centre is also empty' is worth knowing. A test asserts it is NOT bodyOk, so promoting it later is a deliberate act rather than a tidy-up.  IT SELF-CLEARS. Once the seed lands the grid renders and the note stops appearing, with nothing to remember to turn off - which is the property a 'revisit later' comment does not have.  NEW CASES in scripts/uptime-check.test.mjs (8 total). One of them EXTRACTS the predicate and RUNS it against an empty hub and a populated one, rather than only asserting the string 'related-grid' appears in the file - a regex check would pass on a function that ignores its argument, which is sabotage 3 below.  SABOTAGE-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS, each reverted green: deleting the target, dropping bodyNote so it becomes status-only, a predicate that always returns null, and promoting it to bodyOk.  STILL OPEN: AC1 ONLY, and it is the operator command - run npm run help:seed with the prod URL and service-role key, then re-check /help. AC2 and AC3 were already satisfied (see the previous note for why AC2's wording should not be followed literally), and the --force branch it depends on was fixed in the same session after being proven unable to work.  VERIFIED: 440 tests across 27 script suites passing, eslint clean. | 2026-08-16 THE HTTP HALF IS NOW EXERCISED TOO, so the previous note's caveat is closed and --force is proven working rather than proven broken.  POSTGREST CAN RUN LOCALLY - the earlier note said it could not, and that was wrong in the useful direction. `supabase db start` boots Postgres only, and `supabase start` afterwards STOPS kong/rest/studio rather than adding them, so the stack reads as DB-only. But the CLI leaves those containers STOPPED, NOT REMOVED: `docker start supabase_rest_gradethread supabase_kong_gradethread` brings the API up in about a second against the same 609-migration schema. Recorded in CLAUDE.md, because 'cannot be verified locally' has been written about REST-shaped work more than once in this backlog.  ALL THREE PATHS EXECUTED END TO END against real PostgREST:   RUN 1 (fresh):   83 written, 0 skipped   RUN 2 (re-run):  0 written, 83 skipped - idempotent, AC2's real behaviour   RUN 3 (--force): 83 UPDATED, and the table still holds 83 rows with 83                    distinct lower(slug) - so it patched in place rather than                    duplicating, which is exactly what the old                    resolution=merge-duplicates spelling could not do.  That last line is the one worth keeping: before the fix this branch raised 23505 on every already-live article. It has now been run, not reasoned about.  68 of the 83 land as status=published + visibility=public, so the hub's category shelf renders and the new uptime note (AC4) goes quiet - which also confirms the note fires on the right condition rather than on any 200.  STILL OPEN: AC1 ONLY, unchanged, and it is the operator command against PROD. Everything about the mechanism is now executed rather than inferred: the payload fits the schema, the three paths behave, and the failure branch that would have met an operator mid-incident is fixed. | 2026-08-16 THE NEW HUB CHECK WAS RUN AGAINST PRODUCTION and it works, which also re-measures this story premise rather than inheriting it. Full uptime probe, no GitHub token so no issue channel, read-only GETs:    Help Center hub: UP (HTTP 200, 822ms) [help hub renders NO category shelf —   the Help Center is empty (US-2618: run npm run help:seed)]  So as of today /help is LIVE, answers 200 in under a second, and has nothing on it. That is AC1 still open, confirmed from outside rather than from the database, and it is the first time the emptiness has been detected by something other than a person looking.  THE NOTE BEHAVED AS DESIGNED: the run ended All targets healthy and exited 0. It reports without failing, which is the call recorded when it was added - the hub is empty for a known reason, and a monitor held red on a known reason is one nobody reads during a real outage. It will go quiet on its own the moment the seed lands, with nothing to remember to switch off.  ALSO MEASURED, since the probe covers them: the other five targets are all UP. SPA 200, deep-link routing 200 (the /_redirects regression guard), edge /health 200, edge /health/ready 200 - so the database dependency is live - and Supabase Auth 401 through Kong, which is the expected answer without an anon key. Production is healthy. | 2026-08-17 STILL EMPTY, confirmed from outside on a live uptime run rather than assumed: 'Help Center hub: UP (HTTP 200) [help hub renders NO category shelf - the Help Center is empty (US-2618: run npm run help:seed)]'.  That note works and always has - it is a regex over the HTML, not a JSON path, so it escaped the bug that silenced the hostWatchdog note beside it in the same file. Worth recording together: two notes, same file, same purpose, and only the one that had to PARSE something was broken. The parsing is where the assumption hides.  So the seed remains the whole of the remaining work, and its absence is now provably visible in every ten-minute monitor run rather than only to someone who opens the page. | 2026-08-22 RE-MEASURED, SEVEN DAYS ON, AND NOTHING HAS CHANGED. GET /help returns 200 with 15659 bytes and ZERO href="/help/..." links - the header, the search box and the support CTA rendered over nothing, exactly as on 2026-08-15. /help/getting-started answers 200 and is likewise empty. The public sitemap carries exactly ONE /help entry, the index itself, so not one article is indexed either.  EVERYTHING ON THIS SIDE IS READY, which is what makes the gap worth restating rather than just leaving the AC open. 83 files in content/help/. `npm run help:seed` is wired. The script is idempotent by design - an existing slug is skipped and reported, and --force UPDATES keyed on slug rather than upserting, because this table cannot be upserted through PostgREST. All three paths (insert, skip-on-rerun, --force) have been executed against a local stack built from the full migration corpus, so AC2 is proven rather than intended.  IT NOW BLOCKS A SECOND STORY, which it did not when it was filed. US-2619 AC5 asks for /og/help/<slug> to be re-checked once real content exists. Measured today, /og/help returns 133915 bytes - byte-identical to the branded fallback - and that is NOT evidence of a render fault, it is the not-found branch, because there is no article to render. That AC cannot be answered either way until this one is done. Same for /og/verified.  So the single command in AC5 clears AC1 and AC2 here AND unblocks the last open AC on US-2619. Nothing else in either story is waiting on code.

userStories.title: Two OG image endpoints return 200 with an EMPTY body, so blog posts and social cards preview blank
userStories.description: Measured against production 2026-08-15. GET /og/social/card (every ratio: landscape, square, story, pin) and GET /og/blog/<a real published slug> both return HTTP 200, Content-Type image/png, and ZERO bytes. A zero-byte PNG is a blank link preview everywhere it is used - and content-social-publish.ts auto-fills a /og/social/card URL whenever a post has no asset_image_url, while src/test/pinterest-rich-pins.test.ts pins media at https://gradethread.com/og/social/card?ratio=pin. So every auto-filled social image and every Pinterest pin is currently blank. THE MECHANISM, which explains why nothing caught it: card.ts wraps the render in try/catch and falls back to the branded card on a throw, but workers-og's ImageResponse STREAMS - the raster happens lazily as the body is consumed, after the Response object has been constructed and returned. A failure during streaming is therefore invisible to that try/catch, the catch never fires, brandedFallbackResponse never runs, and the client gets a well-formed 200 with nothing in it. This is the same class of problem that moved the certificate card off in-Function rendering: functions/og/cert/[id].ts's header records that workers-og inside a Pages Function exceeded the Free-plan Worker CPU limit and that streaming bytes from the edge is pure I/O by comparison. NOT EVERY OG ENDPOINT IS BROKEN, and the distinction matters: /og/grade-check renders 134022 bytes in-Function and is fine. /og/cert/:id serves 112844 bytes by proxying the edge. WHAT LOOKED FINE AND WAS NOT: /og/help/<slug> and /og/verified/<handle> both returned 133915 bytes, which is byte-for-byte /og-image.png - the static branded FALLBACK. They were serving the fallback because there is no such handle and help_articles is empty (US-2618), so their real-render path is untested and may share the same fault.
acceptanceCriteria: /og/social/card returns a real PNG for every ratio, and /og/blog/<slug> does for a published post.
A streaming failure reaches the fallback. The current try/catch cannot see one, so the fix is either to buffer the render before responding or to move it to the edge the way the certificate card was.

A check distinguishes a REAL render from the branded fallback. Both are 200 image/png, and the fallback is a fixed byte length, so 'it returned an image' is not evidence the renderer works - that is exactly how /og/help and /og/verified read as healthy.
Zero-byte responses are impossible to serve: any og endpoint returning 200 with no body should fail loudly rather than silently.
/og/help and /og/verified are re-checked once real content exists, since their render path has never actually been exercised.

OPERATOR: open the Cloudflare Pages real-time log and search for [og/social/card] render failed. Every failure now logs the actual exception with the endpoint named, and that one line is the cheapest path to the root cause by a wide margin - four hypotheses have been eliminated from the outside and the fifth cannot be tested without the Workers runtime.

Migrate the four in-Function renderers (og/social/card, og/blog, og/verified, og/help) to the PROXY shape og/cert already uses: a Deno-edge endpoint renders the PNG and the Pages Function streams the bytes. The remedy is already deployed and working for og/cert, slab/cert and badge/cert, adopted for this same symptom, so it does not depend on naming the exception first.

The edge already has the engine: lib/cert-image-render.ts renderPng(markup, w, h) is a generic HTML-to-PNG with Inter and the resvg WASM bundled. It is currently private; exporting it (or a thin wrapper) is the whole plumbing job.

DECIDE AND RECORD what happens to the Pages-side template. The three already-migrated cards left buildCertOgHtml, buildCertSlabHtml and buildCertBadgeHtml DEAD in functions/_shared/og-template.ts - zero importers outside their own tests - while their layouts were re-authored on the edge. Repeating that silently gives seven dead builders and a test suite pinning templates nobody renders. Either delete the Pages copy as part of each migration, or state why it is kept.

A guard so a builder cannot go dead unnoticed: every exported build*Html in functions/_shared/og-template.ts is either imported by a Pages Function or listed with a reason. scripts/check-unwired-modules.mjs does not cover this - it flags whole edge modules nothing imports, and og-template.ts IS imported; only three of its exports are dead.

DEPENDS ON US-2612 BEING FINISHED, and this changes the order rather than being a footnote. The proxy fix has the Pages Function call the edge server-to-server, and the only trust mechanism between them is the x-pages-origin header carrying CF_PAGES_ORIGIN_SECRET. That secret is set on the EDGE and not yet on the Cloudflare Pages project, so a route built today could not be called successfully in production - the Pages worker would send no header and the edge would refuse it. Finish US-2612 (Pages value + redeploy) before building this, or the first deploy of the fix looks like the fix not working.

CORRECTION 2026-08-22: the four ratios are landscape, square, PORTRAIT and pin (SocialCardRatio in functions/_shared/og-template.ts:163). AC1 and the description say "story", which is a SLAB format on the unrelated /slab/cert endpoint. ?ratio=story falls back to landscape, correctly, and nothing in the repo requests it.
userStories.notes:
2026-08-15 AC3 and AC4 DONE (detection); AC1, AC2 and AC5 are the fix and stay open. The production route probe now checks OG images two ways, because a status code sees neither. AC4: a 200 under OG_MIN_BYTES is a failure — /og/social/card returns 200, image/png, and ZERO bytes on every ratio. AC3 IS THE SHARPER ONE and it is why this was nearly missed entirely: /og/help/<slug> and /og/verified/<handle> both returned 133915 bytes and read as perfectly healthy. 133915 is byte-for-byte /og-image.png — the static branded FALLBACK. They were serving it because there is no such handle and help_articles is empty (US-2618), so their real render path has never executed and may share the same fault. userStories.title: The privacy page says security logs are purged at 90 days; the audit log is append-only by design
userStories.description: Found 2026-08-16 while checking the sibling retention promises after fixing US-2642. privacy.tsx retention table says "Server & security logs - Up to 90 days, then purged or aggregated." HAND-CHECKED, not inferred: admin_audit_log, ops_events and user_events have NO delete anywhere in the edge tree, and admin_audit_log is append-only ON PURPOSE - audit-append-only_test.ts fails if any RLS policy on it grants UPDATE, DELETE or ALL, because a deletable audit log is not an audit log. So there is real tension between two correct positions: security wants the record immutable, and the privacy page promises it is purged. WHICH IS RIGHT DEPENDS ON WHAT THE ROW MEANS, and that is an owner decision, not a code fix. "Server & security logs" most naturally reads as infrastructure - Coolify, Cloudflare, Sentry - whose retention is configured outside this repo and may well be 90 days. If it also covers the application audit tables then either they need a sweep or the row needs rewriting, and rewriting a legal page retention claim is not something to do unilaterally. FILED RATHER THAN FIXED for that reason. Also filed with a warning: the automated sweep I wrote to inventory this is unreliable - it reported radar_scan_events as never purged when radar-aggregate-engine.ts does delete them, through a helper the pattern could not see - so a proper inventory has to come before any conclusion about the other 23 tables.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide which tables the privacy row "Server & security logs" actually covers: infrastructure logs (Coolify, Cloudflare, Sentry) only, or application audit/event tables too. Record the decision.

If it covers application tables, either they are purged or aggregated at 90 days, or the row is rewritten to say what is true. admin_audit_log is DELIBERATELY append-only (audit-append-only_test.ts pins that no UPDATE/DELETE RLS policy exists), so it needs an explicit carve-out either way.

Build a trustworthy inventory first. My scan is NOT that - it reported radar_scan_events as never purged when radar-aggregate-engine.ts deletes them through a helper, so its NONE results are unreliable and only the three hand-checked tables below are evidence.
