userStories.title: The storage mirror has no restore path, and its key lives on the host it protects against losing
userStories.description: Found 2026-08-16 while running the Postgres restore drill, which passes. The storage half has no equivalent and nothing has ever read the photo mirror back.  TWO HALVES, AND THE SECOND IS THE SERIOUS ONE.  (1) NO RESTORE PATH AT ALL. scripts/ops/ carries backup-postgres.sh, restore-postgres.sh AND restore-drill.sh. For storage it carries backup-storage.sh and nothing else - no restore-storage.sh, no drill, and no procedure in vault/10-ops/backups.md, whose 'Restore procedure (VERIFIED 2026-06-12)' section and whose entire drill log are Postgres-only. The nearest thing to a read-back instruction anywhere is one clause in key-rotation.md's re-seed advice: 'verify a sample decrypts'. That mirror is every listing photo, every grading photo including LABEL shots, and every certificate asset.  (2) THE DECRYPTION SECRET LIVES ON THE MACHINE THE BACKUP EXISTS TO SURVIVE. vault/10-ops/key-rotation.md:48 records the rclone crypt password + salt as held in 'DB host rclone config'. backup-storage.sh reads it from there (rclone config show, line 56) and refuses a non-crypt remote, which is correct. But if the Contabo host is lost - the disaster an offsite mirror is FOR - the crypt config goes with it and every object in R2 is unreadable ciphertext. The R2 credential alone yields nothing, which is the point of the crypt remote and is also the trap.  THIS IS THE EXACT MISTAKE THE AGE KEY PROCEDURE WAS WRITTEN TO AVOID, made on the other artifact. US-2416 AC7 says of the Postgres identity: 'put the identity somewhere off the DB host (never on it - the host holds...)', and backups.md:121 requires 'a second copy somewhere offline and durable that does not depend on Infisical or the Contabo host'. The storage secret has no such instruction, no Infisical entry, and no offline copy named anywhere.  NOT COVERED BY AN EXISTING STORY, checked rather than assumed: US-2002 is the Postgres cron and a Postgres restore against a real offsite dump; US-2416 is encryption, and its AC3 asks only whether backup-storage.sh encrypts, which it now does. Neither asks whether the photos can be recovered.
acceptanceCriteria: A scripts/ops/restore-storage.sh counterpart to restore-postgres.sh: point it at the crypt remote and a target directory, pull objects back, and verify a sample against a checksum rather than reporting rclone's exit code as success.

A storage restore DRILL, the way restore-drill.sh does it for Postgres: sync a known set of files to a scratch crypt remote, pull them back into a fresh directory, and compare counts and content hashes. It must run without touching the production remote.

The rclone crypt password and salt get the same treatment as the age identity: stored off the DB host, with a second offline copy, and the LOCATION recorded in vault/10-ops/key-rotation.md - never the value. Losing the host must not lose the photos.
vault/10-ops/backups.md gains a storage restore procedure next to the Postgres one, and the drill log gains a storage row. Today both are Postgres-only and read as though the whole system is covered.

Decide and record what a PARTIAL restore looks like: a single deleted object recovered from a dated storage-deleted/ prefix is a different operation from a full-volume rebuild, and only the second is a disaster-recovery drill. Both should be written down; today neither is.

OPERATOR: move the rclone crypt password and salt off the DB host and take a second offline copy, then record where (never the value) in vault/10-ops/key-rotation.md. Nothing in this repository can do it, and until it is done the offsite photo mirror does not survive the loss of the host it is backing up.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-16 AC1, AC2, AC4 AND AC5 DONE AND EXECUTED. The mirror has been read back. AC3 and AC6 are the operator half and are untouched - they are also the serious half, and the drill now says so out loud on every PASS rather than leaving it to this note.  AC1: NEW scripts/ops/restore-storage.sh. It does three things a bare rclone copy does not, each because of a specific way this can look like it worked when it did not. It REFUSES A ZERO-FILE RESTORE, because rclone exits 0 on a copy that produced nothing, so a wrong prefix or an empty bucket reads as success. It RE-CHECKS A SAMPLE BYTE-FOR-BYTE with rclone check --download, which is the check that actually proves the crypt password: a wrong password does NOT error on listing, it yields names that decrypt to garbage, so only comparing content catches it. And it refuses a non-empty target unless told otherwise, so two generations of the mirror cannot be mixed by accident. It also mirrors the backup script's crypt-type check, which here tells you early that you are pointed at the wrong remote before a long pull.  AC2: NEW scripts/ops/restore-storage-drill.sh, AND IT RUNS ON A WINDOWS DEV BOX WITH NO CLOUD CREDENTIAL - no Docker, no network, no R2. It defines an EPHEMERAL rclone crypt remote over a local directory in a THROWAWAY config, so the real config is never read or written. Six steps: build a fake volume, sync it with the real backup-storage.sh, assert there is NO PLAINTEXT in the remote directory (the claim backups.md makes), restore with the real restore-storage.sh, compare count and every SHA-256, then delete an object, re-sync, and recover the original bytes from storage-deleted/<ts>/. It calls both real scripts rather than reimplementing them, which is what makes it a drill rather than a self-test.  FIRST RUN: PASS. 8/8 files byte-identical through the crypt remote, no plaintext on the remote side, deleted object recovered intact from storage-deleted/20260817T034102Z. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS, each reddening and each restored: the remote made a plain alias instead of crypt (caught by the type check AND would have been caught by the plaintext scan), backup-storage.sh losing --backup-dir so single-object recovery becomes impossible, the restore pulling a prefix that does not exist (the zero-file guard), and restored bytes altered after the copy (counts still match, hashes do not).  AC4 DONE, AND WRITING IT FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN THE EXISTING RUNBOOK. backups.md's 'Restore procedure (VERIFIED 2026-06-12)' step 5 read: rclone sync r2:gradethread-backups/storage/ /var/lib/supabase/storage/. That is wrong three ways and the worst one is destructive: SYNC (not copy) DELETES local files absent from the backup, so running it partway through a recovery destroys what you just salvaged. It also names the PLAINTEXT remote rather than the crypt remote backup-storage.sh actually writes to, and it treats rclone's exit code as success. Replaced with the script, and the old line is KEPT and labelled so nobody reinstates it. New 'Storage restore procedure' section, the drill log gains a storage row, and the frontmatter summary no longer says the storage mirror has no restore path.  AC5 DECIDED AND RECORDED as a table in that section: FULL REBUILD is prefix `storage`, an empty real STORAGE_DIR, and is the disaster-recovery case the drill exercises; SINGLE-OBJECT RECOVERY is prefix `storage-deleted/<ts>`, a SCRATCH directory, and one manual copy. The runbook says outright never to point the full-rebuild form at the live volume to recover one file, because it pulls the whole prefix and would drag every other object back to its backed-up state.  ⚠ WHAT NONE OF THIS PROVES, and it is AC3/AC6: the drill uses an EPHEMERAL password, so it proves the round trip. It says nothing about whether the REAL crypt password and salt exist anywhere other than the DB host - which is the exact machine an offsite mirror exists to survive losing. Until that is answered, a total host loss still means every object in R2 is unreadable ciphertext and restore-storage.sh cannot help. The drill prints this on every PASS, and the runbook carries it as a warning callout, because a green drill is precisely when someone stops asking.  TOOLING NOTE: rclone was not on this box and is now (scoop install rclone, v1.75.0), which is what made the drill executable rather than another unrun operator script.

userStories.title: Stopping impersonation calls a GoTrue route that does not exist, so nothing is revoked
userStories.description: Found 2026-08-16 while measuring the impersonation token lifetime for US-2351 AC7. US-2351 AC2 - 'Stopping impersonation revokes the target's sessions' - is recorded as DONE, and the code is there: POST /stop calls revokeUserSessions() (lib/impersonation-session.ts:163), which POSTs to {SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/admin/users/{id}/logout with scope 'global', and its comment correctly says that global scope is 'the only scope that reaches a token already copied out of the browser'.  THAT ROUTE DOES NOT EXIST IN GoTrue v2.195.0. Measured against a running container, with the control that makes the result mean something:    GET    /auth/v1/admin/users/{id}          -> 200   (auth, routing, id all fine)   POST   /auth/v1/admin/users/{id}/logout   -> 404   DELETE /auth/v1/admin/users/{id}/sessions -> 404  and auth.sessions for that user stayed at 2 rows across the attempt. The same 404 comes back when the call is made DIRECTLY to the container on :9999 with a service-role bearer, so it is not the API gateway. POST /logout (the user's-own-token route) answers 403 rather than 404, which is how you can tell the admin variant is genuinely absent rather than merely unauthorised.  SO STOPPING IMPERSONATION DOES NOT REVOKE ANYTHING on this version. Every call returns 404, revokeUserSessions() takes its !res.ok branch, captures the exception and returns false, and /stop answers sessions_revoked: false. The admin's copy of the target's refresh token stays live for its full lifetime.  IT FAILS LOUDLY, WHICH IS THE ONE PIECE OF GOOD NEWS and also the way to check prod without touching it: captureException fires with route 'impersonation.revoke' and the message 'GoTrue logout returned 404'. If prod runs a GoTrue where the route exists, there will be no such events; if it does not, they are already there.  NOT ASSUMED ABOUT PROD. The local stack is public.ecr.aws/supabase/gotrue v2.195.0. The self-hosted prod auth container's version is unknown from here and is the first thing to establish.
acceptanceCriteria: Establish which GoTrue version production runs, and whether POST /admin/users/{id}/logout exists on it. GET /auth/v1/health returns the version and is unauthenticated.

If the route is absent in prod too: revoke by a mechanism that exists. The service-role client already reaches the database, and deleting the user's rows from auth.sessions and auth.refresh_tokens is under our own control rather than a bet on an upstream route — but confirm a deleted session actually rejects a refresh before relying on it.

A test that FAILS when revocation does not happen, rather than one that asserts the call was made. The current shape is exactly why this shipped: the code is correct, the endpoint is not, and nothing exercised the pair.
POST /stop's response already carries sessions_revoked; surface it to the admin UI so a failed revocation is visible at the moment it matters instead of only in Sentry.
Re-check US-2351 AC2, which is marked done on the strength of this code path and is not currently true on GoTrue v2.195.0.

OPERATOR: read the GoTrue version on the prod auth container (curl -fsS https://api.gradethread.com/auth/v1/health, unauthenticated, returns it), and search Sentry for 'GoTrue logout returned' with route impersonation.revoke. Those two answers together settle whether this is live in production or a local-version artifact, and neither requires impersonating anyone.

AC1, FIRST HALF ANSWERED 2026-08-21: production GoTrue is v2.174.0 (GET /auth/v1/health with the anon key; the endpoint is NOT unauthenticated through Kong, contrary to AC6 - it 401s without a key). Note the direction: prod is OLDER than the v2.195.0 the local finding came from, so the local result does not transfer either way and the second half of AC1 still stands.

AC1, SECOND HALF UNRESOLVED, and the obvious probe is a trap worth recording. Probing POST /auth/v1/admin/users/<nil>/logout with the anon key returns 401 - but so does a deliberately nonexistent control route, because KONG rejects before GoTrue routes at all. Any 404-vs-401 reading taken from outside without a control is therefore meaningless, and it would have read as 'the route exists'. Settling it needs a service-role call against a nil UUID (which matches no user, so nothing is revoked) where the response BODY separates 'no such route' from 'no such user'. No service-role key is on the dev box, so this needs the operator or a shell on the host.

AC6 SECOND HALF ATTEMPTED 2026-08-21 AND THE PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD FROM HERE. The Sentry account reachable from this machine has exactly ONE project, `react-native`, and ZERO issues of any kind in the last 90 days - not zero matching 'GoTrue logout returned', zero full stop, on `is:unresolved` with no other filter.

SO A ZERO READING IS NOT EVIDENCE, which is the whole point of the check. The story's reasoning is 'if the route is absent, the events are already there' - that only follows if the edge reports to the Sentry being searched. An org with one mobile project and no issues at all is far more consistent with the edge's SENTRY_DSN pointing somewhere this account cannot see than with a healthy edge that has never raised anything.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is cheaper than the original AC6: confirm which Sentry project the edge's prod SENTRY_DSN actually targets, then search THAT. Until then AC6 cannot be answered by searching, and nobody should read an empty result as 'the defect was never live'. The edge only ships to Sentry when SENTRY_DSN is set at all (observability.ts:240), so 'not configured' is also a live possibility and would make every past search equally void.

UNCHANGED BY THIS: the fix itself. 00612's admin_revoke_user_sessions is applied in production and the edge falls back to it, so stopping an impersonation has a mechanism that exists whichever way AC6 lands.
userStories.notes:
2026-08-16 (same session) THE REPLACEMENT MECHANISM IS PROVEN, AND THE OBVIOUS WAY TO CALL IT IS PROVEN NOT TO WORK. Both measured, so the next person does not spend the hour I did.  (1) DELETING auth.sessions DOES REVOKE. Against GoTrue v2.195.0, with the control first so the result means something:     refresh with a live session   -> 200 accepted     delete auth.sessions for user -> 5 rows     refresh with the same token   -> 400 refresh_token_not_found Refresh tokens hang off sessions, so removing the rows invalidates them. That is the mechanism we own, and it does what the missing admin route was for.  (2) BUT THE EDGE CANNOT REACH IT. I wrote the fallback as supabaseAdmin.schema('auth').from('sessions').delete(), it type-checked and linted clean, and it CANNOT WORK: PostgREST only exposes the schemas in its config, which is schemas = ['public','storage'] (supabase/config.toml:5). A DELETE on auth.sessions through the REST client answers 406. Reverted rather than shipped - a fallback that also does nothing would be strictly worse than the 404 it replaces, because it would look handled.  SO THE FIX NEEDS A MIGRATION, and that is the shape to plan for rather than a code-only change: a SECURITY DEFINER function in `public` that deletes from auth.sessions for a given user id, called with .rpc(). Same pattern as the other privileged operations in this schema. NOT written here, because a commit containing a migration is held under the standing rule and because the prod GoTrue version (AC1) decides whether any of this is needed at all - if prod has the admin route, the current code is correct and a migration would be churn.  ORDER, THEREFORE: answer AC1 first (GET /auth/v1/health on prod returns the version, unauthenticated), and only build the RPC if the route is absent there too. AC1 stays open and is one operator curl. AC2: 00612 adds public.admin_revoke_user_sessions(uuid), SECURITY DEFINER, which deletes the user's auth.refresh_tokens and auth.sessions rows and returns the session count. The previous segment had proven the mechanism and proven that the obvious way to call it does not work; this is the RPC that shape needs. Guard is in the BODY, not a REVOKE, per US-2666: a denied call from anon or authenticated segfaults this image (US-2403), and revoking from anon alone is a no-op anyway. It decides whether the fallback is doing all the work or none of it; the fix is correct either way, which is why it did not block this. | 2026-08-17 STATUS CORRECTION for the 2026-08-16 segment above, which says the migration was not written because a commit containing one is held under the standing rule. That rule is superseded by the pre-production practice: migrations are pushed to origin/main AND recorded in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md for the operator to apply separately. 00610, 00611 and 00612 are all in that file under PUSHED, NOT YET APPLIED. Nothing here is waiting on a frozen branch. | 2026-08-17 THE FIX IS BUILT AND MEASURED. AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC5 are done; the story stays open on the held migration and one operator lookup.  AC2 THE MECHANISM. public.revoke_user_sessions(uuid) in 00614 deletes the user's auth.sessions rows and returns the count. Refresh tokens go with them: refresh_tokens_session_id_fkey is ON DELETE CASCADE, read from pg_constraint rather than assumed, which is why the function does not touch auth.refresh_tokens itself. Service-role only, using the positive allowlist from vault/20-domain/security-definer-caller-allowlist.md.  It had to be a function: PostgREST serves only public and storage, so the direct delete this story already recorded as impossible stays impossible. The edge now calls it by name and the dead GoTrue route is GONE rather than kept as a fallback - a second thing that looks handled and does nothing is the defect, not a hedge against it.  AC3 A TEST THAT CAN FAIL. scripts/check-session-revocation.mjs seeds a user, two sessions and a refresh token, calls the function, and fails if the rows survive. Wired into the db verify lane and db-migrations.yml. CHECKED BY SABOTAGE, twice: a body returning 0 without deleting went red on three counts, and a body with the guard removed went red on the anon refusal. The old assertion in impersonation-bounds_test.ts is kept but relabelled WIRING ONLY, with the reason written above it, so nobody reads it as proof again.  AC4 THE ADMIN FINDS OUT. /stop returns revoked, sessions_revoked and revoke_error. The exit hard-reloads, so a toast raised at the moment of failure would be destroyed before it rendered - the notice is parked in sessionStorage and flushed by RootLayout on the next boot, the same shape flushPendingAffiliateClick uses. Worded as an instruction (reset their password) because there IS something the admin can do.  WHAT I ADDED THAT THE STORY DID NOT ASK FOR, because it is the honest limit: revocation stops the holder REFRESHING and cannot touch an access token already issued. A Supabase access token is a JWT verified by signature with nothing to look up, so it stays valid until jwt_expiry - an hour. The GoTrue route would have had exactly the same limit; this is a property of stateless tokens, not of the replacement. The 30-minute cap and the server-side marker are what bound that window. Written into the code comment and the vault note rather than left for someone to discover.  AC1 IS ANSWERED AS FAR AS IT CAN BE WITHOUT TOUCHING PROD, and the earlier note has the measurement: production is GoTrue v2.174.0, older than the v2.195.0 where the route is proven absent. Stated as inference and it stays inference.  STILL OPEN, both outside this repo:   - 00614 is HELD under the standing rule. Packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md with the     NOTIFY pgrst reload it needs (a NEW RPC, so PostgREST must be told) and the warning that     the frontend reads the new response fields the moment it deploys.   - AC6's second half: search Sentry for 'GoTrue logout returned' under route     impersonation.revoke. That settles whether the defect was live in production rather than     a local-version artifact. It does not change the fix, which is right either way.  vault/10-ops/impersonation-session-revocation.md carries the whole finding. | 2026-08-17 THE EARLIER SEGMENT HERE IS SUPERSEDED, and I wrote it, so this is a correction rather than a hand-off. It says '00614 is HELD under the standing rule' and describes a revoke_user_sessions function. Neither is true now.  A SECOND AGENT SHIPPED THIS STORY IN PARALLEL and landed on origin first, as 00612_admin_ revoke_user_sessions.sql plus commit 47af152c. My 00614 created public.revoke_user_sessions doing the same job, so it was DELETED in the reconciliation - two functions for one purpose is the same silent-winner problem as two migrations replacing one function: neither errors, whichever runs last wins, and the code you read is not necessarily the code that runs.  THEIRS IS THE BETTER SHAPE ON ONE POINT and it is worth naming rather than glossing. I removed the GoTrue call outright on the grounds that a dead fallback is worse than none. Theirs keeps it and falls back to the RPC, reporting an incident only when BOTH fail. That means the day a GoTrue upgrade restores POST /admin/users/{id}/logout, the supported path resumes with no code change - which my version would not have done.  ONE PIECE OF MINE SURVIVED, because it answers a question theirs does not. scripts/check-session-revocation.mjs seeds a user, two sessions and a refresh token, calls the function and fails if the rows survive. Their impersonation-revoke_test.ts drives the fallback through injected seams and proves the DECISION LOGIC; nothing stubbed can prove the SQL actually deletes. Repointed at admin_revoke_user_sessions and still green: 2 sessions and 1 cascaded refresh token removed, anon refused 42501. It runs in the db verify lane and in db-migrations.yml, and it was sabotage-checked both ways.  NOTHING ON THIS STORY IS HELD. 00612 is on origin/main and listed in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md as PUSHED, NOT YET APPLIED. The convention changed: migration commits go to origin AND get an entry there; the operator applies on their own schedule.  vault/10-ops/impersonation-session-revocation.md was rewritten to describe the implementation that actually shipped - the GoTrue-then-RPC fallback, the varchar cast on auth.refresh_tokens.user_id, and the two guards and what each proves.  STILL OPEN, unchanged: AC6's Sentry search, which settles whether the defect was live in production rather than a local-version artifact. It does not change the fix. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-17: STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM in the earlier segments above. Every migration named on this story is on origin/main and listed in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md as PUSHED, NOT YET APPLIED. Nothing here is holding the branch.  The convention changed and the old segments predate it: migration commits now go to origin AND get an entry in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md, and the operator applies the SQL on their own schedule. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md says so at the top. Read a 🟠 entry as 'on origin, not in the database', not as 'unpushed'.  The migration on this story is 00612_admin_revoke_user_sessions.sql, which the parallel agent authored. My 00614 was deleted as a duplicate, so it holds nothing because it no longer exists. | 2026-08-17 admin_revoke_user_sessions IS LIVE IN PRODUCTION. The PostgREST OpenAPI document (pure read, anon key) lists /rpc/admin_revoke_user_sessions with p_user_id, so 00612 applied and the schema cache has it - which is the half a NOTIFY pgrst could have silently missed. /health/ready reports applied 00617, so the migration landed rather than merely being pushed.  WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THIS STORY: stopping an impersonation now has a mechanism that exists, in production, for the first time since the feature shipped. The edge tries GoTrue first and falls back to this, so the fallback is reachable.  NOT YET PROVEN: that a real stop revokes a real session in prod. That needs an actual impersonation, which is AC6's territory and not something to exercise against a live user to satisfy a checkbox. The SQL itself is proven by scripts/check-session-revocation.mjs on the local stack and runs in the db lane on every push.

2026-08-21, NOTED IN PASSING WHILE PROBING PROD FOR AC6: functions.gradethread.com returned 503 'no available server' on four consecutive probes at 12:15 UTC, with gradethread.com at 200 and api.gradethread.com routing normally - the exact edge-hang signature in vault/10-ops/edge-hang-vs-crash-loop.md, where Traefik has dropped an alive-but-unhealthy container. It RECOVERED on its own: 200 on six probes from t+25s to t+150s. So the host watchdog did its job this time, which is the first datapoint this repo has that it works - the vault note flags the ~60s cap as UNVERIFIED and records a previous instance that ran four weeks. Not an incident to action; recorded because the hang recurring at all is the thing that note asks to be tracked. | ⚠ CORRECTION 2026-08-29 to this story's own last segment, which I wrote.

That segment recorded the 2026-08-21 edge hang recovering on its own (503 on
four probes at 12:15 UTC, then 200 from t+25s to t+150s) and concluded: "the
host watchdog did its job this time, which is the first datapoint this repo has
that it works".

THAT INFERENCE IS WRONG, and it matters because it is recorded as positive
evidence for a safety net that is not installed.

Measured today, unauthenticated: /health/ready reports

The obvious objection is that the heartbeat route might postdate the recovery,
which would make "never checked in" say nothing about 2026-08-21. It does not:
both scripts/ops/edge-watchdog.sh and the heartbeat route landed in f4ca05903 on
2026-08-11, TEN DAYS BEFORE. The mechanism existed and has still never reported.

So the watchdog was not running on 2026-08-21, and whatever ended that outage -
Traefik re-resolving, a Coolify restart, the hang clearing itself - it was not
the cap. The repo still has ZERO datapoints that the watchdog works, which is
what US-2447 AC1/AC2 say and what its readiness line has been saying all along.

Nothing else in this story changes. The impersonation fix is unaffected. | [2026-09-02][PROD READ] The prod half is answerable now and the answer is that there is no evidence either way. Source: scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql run read-only against prod over SSH on 2026-09-02 (container supabase-db-kcksoks4kk0kswk0ccs40os8, 29 sections, 0 SQL errors). Raw output kept out of the repo; it contains customer data. impersonation sessions with an end_reason: 0 rows. distinct_targets_affected 0. open_past_expiry 0. So no impersonation has ever been STOPPED in production, which means the broken GoTrue logout route has never actually been exercised against a real session and Sentry would have nothing to show regardless of which project the edge DSN points at. That retires AC6's premise (searching Sentry cannot answer this) without retiring the fix, which AC12 already records as applied via 00612's admin_revoke_user_sessions.

userStories.title: docker-compose.coolify.yml is not what deploys the edge, so nine settings it declares are unset in production
userStories.description: Established 2026-08-16 by the owner, from two independent signals rather than by inspection. (1) The edge served release:"unknown" for weeks while docker-compose.coolify.yml:33-34 has declared `args: { GIT_SHA: ${SOURCE_COMMIT:-dev} }` the whole time - a compose deploy would have stamped it. (2) EDGE_ENV had to be set BY HAND in the Coolify UI today (US-2660), and the same compose file sets `EDGE_ENV: production` at line 69. Both are explained by one fact: the Coolify resource is a DOCKERFILE deployment, so the compose file is repo decoration.  WHAT IS THEREFORE UNSET unless someone typed it into the UI: PORT=8787, EDGE_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB=2048 (what /health/metrics computes headroom against - wrong or absent means the load-test gate is measuring against nothing), EDGE_TRACE_SAMPLE_RATE=0.1, GRADING_MAX_CONCURRENT_PIPELINES=6, the SOURCE_COMMIT/COMMIT_SHA passthroughs, the json-file log rotation (max-size 10m x max-file 5 = the ONLY thing bounding on-host log disk, so without it container logs grow until the volume fills), the healthcheck block, and the deploy memory limit.  THE SHAPE THAT MATTERS beyond this list: several stories have been closed on the strength of a setting being present in that compose file. compose-release-arg_test.ts asserts the build arg is DECLARED and passes green today. A test that pins a file nothing reads is a test that proves the repo's intent, not production's state, and it read as the latter.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm the resource type in Coolify (Dockerfile vs Docker Compose) and RECORD it in vault/10-ops/deploy.md, because every later question about edge configuration depends on the answer.

Decide: switch the resource to the compose file, or accept the Dockerfile deploy and move every setting the compose declares into the Coolify UI. Do not leave a compose file in the repo that nothing runs.
If the Dockerfile deploy stays, the compose file must say so at the top, in the first ten lines, or the next reader repeats this.

Log rotation specifically: an unbounded json-file driver fills the host volume, and the edge and Postgres share it. Verify what the running container actually has (docker inspect) rather than assuming the daemon default.

compose-release-arg_test.ts and any sibling that asserts a compose-file value must state in its own header that it pins repo intent, not deployed state - or be re-pointed at something production actually reads (/health, /health/ready).

OPERATOR: paste the output of `docker inspect <edge-container> --format '{{json .HostConfig.LogConfig}}{{json .HostConfig.Memory}}'` on the Coolify host. That one line settles the log-rotation and memory questions together, and neither can be answered from this repo.
userStories.notes: [P1][Ops/Deploy] Filed 2026-08-16 while answering how to set SOURCE_COMMIT. NOT a duplicate of US-2001 (which fixed the release-identity precedence bug in code and is correct) or US-2660 (blank EDGE_ENV, fixed in code). Those were both real. This is the reason neither fix changed anything in production: the file carrying the operator half is not the file being deployed. The immediate SOURCE_COMMIT remedy is separate and already given to the owner - add GIT_SHA=${SOURCE_COMMIT} as a BUILD variable in the Coolify UI, since ARG is read at build time and a runtime env var cannot reach it. | 2026-08-17 AC3 AND AC5 DONE, and AC1 is half MEASURED rather than half assumed. The story was filed from two inferences; one of them is now a reading off production, taken from a public endpoint that needs no credentials.  THE MEASUREMENT. GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/metrics answers memory.limit_mb: null, headroom_pct: null, pressure: "unknown". limit_mb is read straight from EDGE_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB (routes/health.ts), and docker-compose.coolify.yml sets it to 2048. So that file is NOT the deployed configuration - this is no longer an inference from EDGE_ENV having been set by hand, it is the setting being absent in the running process. The load-test gate has been measuring headroom against nothing.  AND ONE VALUE DISAGREES RATHER THAN BEING ABSENT, which is worse and was not in the filing. The same probe answers grading.buffer_pipeline_cap: 10. The code default is 6 (DEFAULT_MAX_BUFFERING_PIPELINES, grading-capacity.ts:25) and the compose file declares 6, so 10 can only come from GRADING_MAX_CONCURRENT_PIPELINES being set to 10 somewhere outside this repo. vault/10-ops/capacity.md chose 6 to hold peak base64 residency near 600 MB under a 2 GiB limit; ten pipelines is roughly a gigabyte of peak residency, against a limit nothing is checking because of the paragraph above. Those two findings compound.  WHAT IS STILL OPEN ON AC1, stated so the next reader does not think it is closed: proving coolify.yml is not deployed does not prove WHAT is. Two candidates remain - a Dockerfile build pack, or a compose build pack pointed at the sibling docker-compose.yml, whose own first line calls itself "Production compose used by Coolify". THE EVIDENCE POINTS BOTH WAYS AND BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE REAL. For compose-of-some-kind: commit 407fb9f5 (2026-08-10) fixed an outage where EVERY edge deploy died at the build step on "non-string key in services.edge-functions.environment: 0" - a message that can only be produced by Coolify parsing and re-serialising a compose file of ours, since a Dockerfile build pack never reads an environment block. Against either compose file driving the BUILD: both declare the GIT_SHA build arg and /health still answers release:"unknown". Note that 407fb9f5 changed all three compose files at once, so it never discriminated between them, and the header comment claiming "Coolify reads docker-compose.yml" is an inference by that commit rather than a measurement.  AC3: docker-compose.coolify.yml now opens with the finding, the /health/metrics numbers that prove it, the instruction to treat everything below as intent, and the rule that a setting added there is not shipped. The old "In Coolify: New Resource -> Docker Compose -> point at this file" steps are kept but retitled "To make this file the deployed one", since they are a procedure for a state that does not hold.  AC5: both siblings now say what they pin. compose-release-arg_test.ts gets a warning block naming the three public endpoints that DO report deployed state (/health, /health/ready, /health/metrics) and the fact that it was green on 2026-08-17 while release read "unknown". scripts/compose-env-shape.test.mjs records that the outage proves Coolify parsed A compose file but that the fix touched all three, so it never identified which.  AC1 also recorded in vault/10-ops/deploy.md as the runbook asks - the bullet there SAID "compose is docker-compose.coolify.yml", which is the claim just disproved, so it was replaced rather than appended to. The two disagreeing live values are recorded there too, linked to capacity.  VERIFIED: compose-env-shape 7 passed, compose-release-arg + edge-env-blank 15 passed, deno lint clean, vault:index + vault:lint run (the one remaining lint error is pre-existing drift on subscription-copy-review-register.md from commit 35b3e175 and is unrelated).  STILL OPEN: AC1 second half and AC2 (the Coolify UI answer, and the decision), AC4 (docker inspect for the log driver) and AC6 (the same). Add to AC2 when it is decided: GRADING_MAX_CONCURRENT_PIPELINES is currently 10 in production against a documented sizing of 6, so the decision is not only where settings live but which value is right. | 2026-08-17 (second pass) THE TWO MEASUREMENTS FROM THE FIRST PASS ARE NOW A REPEATABLE CHECK, not a one-off in a note.  scripts/probe-prod-readonly.mjs gains two US-2665 entries against /health/metrics, and running it today reports:    is EDGE_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB actually set on the running container     -> unset - rss 231.7MB, headroom unknowable     -> ANSWERED - so docker-compose.coolify.yml (which declares 2048) is NOT the deployed config   does the live grading pipeline cap match the repo sizing     -> buffer_pipeline_cap 10 (repo default and compose both say 6)     -> LOOK - set outside the repo  WHY THIS IS WORTH MORE THAN THE NOTE IT REPLACES: the first pass proved the compose file is not deployed by measuring it once. A setting that is wrong today can be right tomorrow and wrong again after a redeploy, and a number in a story note cannot tell anyone which. The probe is run before deciding a question needs a session, so this now re-answers itself every time anyone checks anything.  The verdict wording is deliberately LOOK rather than ANSWERED for the pipeline cap: 10 is not necessarily wrong, it is unexplained, and the owner has been asked whether it was deliberate. If the answer is yes, capacity.md gets the new sizing and this line flips to a match on 10.

userStories.title: Four scheduled jobs fail on every single run: trial-expiry 500 (cause proven) and three 502s
userStories.description: Measured on the server 2026-08-17 from the cron ledger, as a FAILURE RATE rather than a count, which is what makes it a different story from the deploy-window transients: trial-expiry 7/7 500, ads-sync 7/7 502, content-refresh 7/7 502, keyword-research 1/1 502. These are daily crons, so 7 in 7 days is EVERY run, not once a day. They have fired this way for nine days and are unrelated to any container event. TRIAL-EXPIRY'S CAUSE IS PROVEN, not suspected. jobs-trial-expiry.ts:177-189 issued `.update(...).select("id").limit(BATCH_LIMIT)` with no ordering. PostgREST refuses a limit on a MUTATION unless an explicit order accompanies it. Reproduced against PostgREST 12 on the real 617-migration schema, with both controls: the exact PATCH supabase-js builds answers PGRST109 / HTTP 400 'A limit was applied without an explicit order'; the same PATCH WITHOUT limit answers 200; the same PATCH with limit AND order=id answers 200. So the qualifier is the whole cause, the handler's error branch returned 500 on every run, and NO EXPIRED TRIAL HAS EVER BEEN DOWNGRADED by this job. The three 502s are not diagnosed. A 502 is the proxy reporting that the app did not answer, which points at duration or a crash rather than a handled error, and the agent-eval finding beside it (200 after 6.5-8.5 minutes, with Coolify timing out waiting on curl) is the same shape. They need the same treatment trial-expiry just had: reproduce the call, read the actual answer.
acceptanceCriteria: trial-expiry: the UPDATE carries an explicit .order() before .limit(), and a source guard prevents the class returning. DONE 2026-08-17 - the fix plus src/tests/mutation-qualifier-guard_test.ts, which also holds the sibling .or()-on-mutation rule from US-1552 because it is the same blind spot.

The three 502s are NOT proxy timeouts and AC3 as originally written is void. Each handler RETURNS 502 deliberately, meaning its own upstream failed: jobs-ads-sync.ts:34 passes through httpStatus 502 for a classified GoogleAdsError, jobs-keyword-research.ts:30 maps result.status==="error" to 502, and jobs-content-refresh.ts:237 returns 502 when refreshBlogArticle throws. No duration is involved. Read the recorded reason rather than timing anything.

Every one of the three already PERSISTS its own error message, so the diagnosis is three queries and not a code hunt: select error from ads_sync_runs where status='failed' order by finished_at desc limit 5; select error, status, trigger from keyword_research_runs where status='error' order by started_at desc limit 5; select error, outcome, ran_at from content_scheduler_runs where outcome='error' order by ran_at desc limit 5. Fix what those say, not what the status code suggests.

A regression check that fails when a scheduled job's failure RATE is 100% over its own cadence. The count-based reading of this data ('7 failures in 7 days, about once a day') is what made four deterministic app bugs look like a container restart pattern, and it cost a session.

Re-read the cron ledger after the fixes: trial-expiry should return 200 with a downgraded count, and the first non-zero count is the backlog of trials that expired while it was broken. Expect it to be larger than a normal day's.

OPERATOR: after deploy, confirm trial-expiry answers 200 and report the first `downgraded` value. It is the size of the backlog, and it tells us how many accounts held Pro entitlements past their trial end.
userStories.notes:
[P0][Jobs/Billing] Filed 2026-08-17 from the server readout. NOT the same story as the deploy-window failures: those are `curl (7) connect to localhost:8787` plus 'No containers running', share one container, and resolve themselves. These four return an HTTP status from a running app. WHY THIS WAS INVISIBLE. It type-checks, it lints, supabase-js builds the request happily, and only the server objects - at runtime, on a cron nobody watches, in a job whose success is silent. CLAUDE.md already documents the sibling of this exact trap for `.or()` on a mutation ('the self-hosted prod PostgREST rejects logical operators on mutations while the newer local-stack PostgREST accepts them, so CI can't catch it'). Same family, second instance, and the repo had no source-level guard for either until now. ⚠ IT CONNECTS TO US-2288, which should be re-read rather than trusted. That story measured 16 trials and 0 conversions and concluded the free-trial hole was 'real and unexploited'. If trial-expiry has never downgraded anybody, then no trial has ever ENDED, so no trial account was ever put to a conversion decision. A 0% conversion rate on trials that never expire is not evidence about pricing or about abuse; it may be evidence about this bug. The trial-cap work from US-2288 stands on its own, but that conversion number should not be reasoned from until this has run. | 2026-08-17 THE 502 HALF IS DIAGNOSED TO THE SEAM, and the timeout hypothesis this story was filed on is WRONG. A 502 here is not a proxy giving up. The cron curls localhost:8787 from inside the container, so there is no proxy in the path at all, and each of the three handlers RETURNS 502 itself as its documented way of saying 'my upstream failed'. That also disposes of the agent-eval parallel: agent-eval is a genuine timeout, these are not the same shape. TWO OF THE THREE ARE ONE ROOT CAUSE. ads-sync and keyword-research both depend on GOOGLE ADS - the sync pulls structure and daily metrics, keyword-research pulls the keyword planner. Both are written to no-op cleanly with a 200 'skipped' when the Ads env is absent (google-ads-sync-job.ts:38-40 says so explicitly), so a 502 proves the OPPOSITE of unconfigured: the seven GOOGLE_ADS_* variables are set and the API is rejecting us. google-ads-sync-job.ts:114 only returns 502 for a classified GoogleAdsError - a bad token or an unapproved developer token - and 500 for anything else, so the 502 is itself the classification. The likely answers are an expired or revoked refresh token, or a developer token still limited to test accounts. THE THIRD IS UNRELATED: content-refresh 502s when refreshBlogArticle throws, which is AI generation, and it records 'generation failed: <msg>'. ALL THREE ALREADY WROTE DOWN THE ANSWER, which is the useful part: ads_sync_runs.error, keyword_research_runs.error and content_scheduler_runs.error each hold the real message for every failed run. Nine days of them. Nobody has read the column. That is why this needed no timing work and why AC2/AC3 have been rewritten. WHAT THAT MEANS FOR OWNERSHIP: if the Ads messages say token, this is operator credential work rather than a code fix, and the code is behaving correctly by surfacing a 502 instead of failing silently. content-refresh may still be a real bug. Read the three columns first. | 2026-08-17 AC4 DONE. The fleet report now reads failure RATE, and the 100% case is its own critical incident.  WHAT WAS ALREADY THERE AND WHY IT WAS NOT ENOUGH. cron.fleet_failing has fired at warning since US-2312 for any job with failed_runs > 0, so all four of these WERE inside it for nine days. The alert was not missing; the reading was. Its title and payload carried counts, and a count is what turned "failed every one of its 7 runs" into "7 failures in 7 days, about once a day". So the fix is not another alert on the same fact - it is the rate, stated where the count used to be.  JobScorecard gains hard_failed_runs, failure_rate, hard_failure_rate and always_failing; CronFleetReport gains an always_failing[] bucket. The bucket is a SUBSET of failing rather than a fifth verdict, deliberately: a new verdict would have REMOVED these jobs from report.failing, so the warning that already covers them would have stopped seeing them, and every existing reader of `failing` would have quietly lost a job.  THE ONE REAL JUDGEMENT: always_failing reads http_status >= 400, not status === "error". cronRunStatusFor merges two different incidents into that one string - a 5xx, where the whole run failed, and a 2xx that reported failed units in its own body. Basing a CRITICAL alert on the merged value would page someone every six hours forever for affiliate-payouts answering 200 with {failed:1} while one Connect account stays broken, which is a real problem and is already covered at warning. That false alarm has its own test case. A run with no recorded http_status cannot satisfy it either, so the signal fails toward silence.  Route: a third ops-event type, cron.fleet_always_failing at critical, with its own suppression memory - folding it into cron.fleet_failing would let one intermittently-failing job mute the job that has never once succeeded, the same reason US-2312 split failing off from stalled. The payload carries runs and hard_failed_runs, so the rate cannot be reassembled as a count. New metric cron_fleet.always_failing; the response gains the name list.  BOTH runsByJob BUILDERS had to carry http_status - the route AND the agent read-tool in agent-tools.ts, which share one data path on purpose. Dropping it from either compiles, lints, and turns nothing red while always_failing silently reports false for every job. That seam is pinned by a source-scan case (comments stripped, so a header describing a field that is no longer passed cannot satisfy it).  VERIFIED: 6 new governance cases + 2 new alert cases, 38 green across the three cron-fleet files, full edge suite 7085 passed / 0 failed / 199 ignored, deno lint clean over 1558 files, deno check src/main.ts clean. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS - basing always_failing on failedRuns instead of hardFailedRuns (reddened the sweep false-alarm case AND the no-http_status regression case), dropping the summary clause, dropping http_status from the route mapping, and downgrading the event severity to warning. Each reddened, each restored.  STILL OPEN, unchanged: AC3 (read ads_sync_runs.error, keyword_research_runs.error and content_scheduler_runs.error - nine days of messages nobody has read, and they decide whether the three 502s are operator credential work or a real bug), AC5 (re-read the ledger after deploy) and AC6 (the operator confirmation of the first downgraded count trial-expiry reports). | 2026-08-17 (second pass) THE AC1 GUARD PUT main RED, AND NOT FOR THE REASON ANYONE WOULD GUESS.  src/tests/mutation-qualifier-guard_test.ts shipped with AC1 and is correct. But it documents the sibling US-1552 rule, so its own header necessarily WRITES `.update(`, `.delete(` and `.or()` as prose. src/lib/__tests__/no-or-on-mutations.test.ts finds mutation chains with a raw regex over the whole file, started a chain inside that comment, walked forward to an unrelated `.or(` further down, and reported a hit. One guard failed another guard on its documentation.  IT HAD BEEN RED SINCE THAT COMMIT, on main, unnoticed - and the reason nobody saw it is worth more than the fix: no-or-on-mutations.test.ts lives in src/lib/__tests__/, so `npx vitest run src/test/` never runs it. Twenty commits of mine reported a green "web suite" that was a SUBSET. Only `npm run verify --web`, which runs the full include and the coverage floor, found it. Run the lane, not a directory.  THE FIX: commentRanges(src) computes the comment spans string-awarely, and findHits refuses to START a chain inside one. Deliberately not "blank the comments out of the source" - that shifts every index and would break the line numbers the report prints, which is the same constraint the tagAttrs fix in US-2335 worked under.  BOTH DIRECTIONS PROVEN BY EXPERIMENT, not by reading: a temporary file containing a REAL `.update(...).or(...)` is still caught, and the same text inside a comment is not. Three permanent cases pin it, including one asserting real code is still a hit - because a guard that stops firing is worse than no guard, which is this file own stated failure mode.  ALSO FIXED IN THE SAME RUN, and also mine: scripts/check-unwired-modules.mjs still listed size-systems.ts as deliberately dead. US-2215 wired it this afternoon, so the allowlist entry stopped being true and the shrink-only rule failed the lane exactly as designed. Removed, with the reason left as a comment rather than deleted silently - the same treatment grading-reliability.ts got.  VERIFIED: node scripts/verify.mjs --web, all 14 checks pass - including vitest + coverage (5303 tests) and the unwired-module gate, both of which were failing before this pass. | 2026-08-23 AC4 WAS SABOTAGED RATHER THAN RE-READ, AND TWO MUTATIONS SURVIVED. Commit ce033ae62. The detector itself is correct and unchanged; what was missing was any test at the two shapes that matter most.  THE ONE THAT MATTERS: narrowing the hard-failure threshold from http_status >= 400 to >= 500 left the whole file green, because every case in it uses 500. Trial-expiry - the job whose cause THIS STORY proved, reproduced against a real 617-migration schema - answered PGRST109 / HTTP 400. So the guard written for that incident carried no test at the status the incident actually produced, and a 4xx-only outage would have gone straight back to being invisible. That is the story's own failure mode surviving inside the fix for it.  THE SECOND: replacing hardFailedRuns === runs.length with hardFailedRuns > runs.length / 2 also stayed green, because the file tests 1-of-6 and 6-of-6 and nothing between. Running backwards, that is the same misreading - four failures in six is a partial outage, and escalating it as a deterministic bug is how a 100% signal stops meaning anything.  TWO CASES ADDED. The 4xx one pins the boundary in both directions (400 counts as a hard failure, 399 does not). The majority one pins 4-of-6 and 5-of-6 as failing-but-not-always, and asserts they stay inside `failing` so the existing warning still covers them - the subset rule the file already had.  VERIFIED: five mutations against cron-fleet-governance.ts, each confirmed applied and each RED, with a green control either side - vacuous-truth on an empty ledger, majority-instead-of-every, the signal removed entirely, body-reported failures re-counted as hard failures, and the 5xx threshold slip. Edge suite 8362 passed / 0 failed / 262 ignored; deno lint clean.  UNCHANGED: AC1 (the .order() fix plus the mutation-qualifier guard) and the rest of AC4's detector. AC2 and AC3 are prod reads of the three 502 handlers' own persisted error columns, and AC5/AC6 are the post-deploy cron-ledger check. All still operator. | 2026-08-29 THE THREE 502s ARE TWO CAUSES, NOT THREE, traced from the code
rather than from prod - which is what AC3 assumed would need three queries.

ads-sync AND keyword-research SHARE ONE CREDENTIAL SET. keyword-research reads
GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN / CLIENT_ID / CLIENT_SECRET / REFRESH_TOKEN /

AND THE 502 ITSELF PROVES THE VARIABLES ARE SET. performGoogleAdsSync returns

There was none - the endpoint reports ebay, shopify, google_photos,

VERIFIED: 4 new cases (35 in env-validation_test.ts, was 31), including the one
that separates this group from its neighbours - the shared GOOGLE_CLIENT_* pair

Full edge suite 9095 passed / 0 failed; deno lint and check clean.

STILL OPEN: AC2/AC3's actual VALUES - the three handlers' persisted error
columns still have to be read on prod, and this only narrows what to expect.
AC5/AC6 remain the post-deploy ledger check. | 2026-08-29 (later) THE google_ads HEALTH GROUP SHIPPED THIS MORNING NOW ANSWERS
