userStories.title: The disputes RLS insert policy never checks who owns the grade report
userStories.description: Found 2026-08-17 while checking US-2016 claim that iOS has no dispute flow (it has one, and the claim is stale). Both INSERT policies on public.disputes gate on the user_id COLUMN and nothing else: 00001 "Users can create disputes" WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id), and 00042 "Workspace members can create disputes" WITH CHECK is_workspace_member_with_role(user_id, 'member'). Neither looks at grade_report_id. So an authenticated caller who sets user_id to their OWN id can file a dispute against ANY grade report id that exists, including another seller. grade_report_id is a plain FK, and RLS on grade_reports governs SELECT, not an insert into a different table that merely references it. The edge route is what actually enforces ownership - routes/grade.ts loads the submission .eq("user_id", ownerId) before filing - so every client that goes through the route is safe and the policy has been carrying no weight. iOS was inserting directly and is fixed in the same pass (see notes); this story is the defence-in-depth half, so the database stops depending on every client remembering.
acceptanceCriteria: A migration tightens the disputes INSERT policies so grade_report_id must belong to the caller (or to the workspace owner the caller is acting for), not merely user_id matching.
The workspace policy keeps working: a member filing for the owner must still succeed, which is why the check is on the OWNER of the report rather than on auth.uid() directly.
A test proves a foreign grade_report_id is refused - the tenant-isolation suite is the right home, since this is exactly a foreign-id-must-be-rejected case.
Check whether any dispute already in production has a grade_report_id whose report belongs to a different user. That decides whether this was ever exploited or is only ever a latent hole.

OPERATOR: apply the migration, then re-run AC4 query against prod. The count is expected to be zero - every client except iOS has always gone through the edge route, and iOS filed with its own user_id against reports it was displaying, so the realistic exposure is a crafted API call rather than anything a normal app produced.
userStories.notes: [P1][Security/Disputes] Filed 2026-08-17 from the US-2016 re-verification. NOT a duplicate of US-2153, which moved the filing WINDOW server-side; this is the ownership check, which was never anywhere but the route. The reason it stayed invisible: the route does the right thing, so the policy has never been the thing standing between a caller and another seller report - and a policy that is never the last line of defence is a policy nobody re-reads. Migration is deliberately not written here: it is push-held until the operator applies it, and the client-side hole that made this reachable is already closed, so shipping the client fix first is the right order. | 2026-08-17 THE OBVIOUS FOLLOW-UP SWEEP WAS RUN AND CAME BACK CLEAN, recorded so nobody repeats it.  The question worth asking after this one: if iOS wrote to `disputes` directly, what ELSE does it write directly, and does any of it go around a rule the table cannot express? Every direct write from ios/GradeThread was enumerated: inventory_items (21), listings (14), item_photos (9), users (7), sources (3), marketplace_connections (3), flipdesk_reconcile_sessions (2), flipdesk_ebay_listings (2), consignors (2), workspace_members, workspace_invitations, flipdesk_expenses.  MOST OF THAT IS THE INTENDED ARCHITECTURE, not a finding. The offline-first SwiftData sync writes the seller own rows and RLS scopes them by user_id - which is the whole design, and a blanket "clients must not write tables" rule would be wrong. `disputes` was the outlier for a specific reason: it is the only one whose insert references ANOTHER table row (grade_report_id) that the policy does not check.  THE TWO HIGH-STAKES ONES WERE CHECKED INDIVIDUALLY AND ARE FINE. marketplace_connections: iOS writes only `label` and `is_primary` (EbayConnectionService) - selection and cosmetics, never token columns. users: only preference fields (full_name, use_case, radar_contribute, ai_enrichment_enabled, ai_action_limit, dismissed_ebay_publish_disclaimer), and migration 00526 defines exactly that self-update allowlist.  ONE THAT LOOKED LIKE A METERING BYPASS AND IS NOT, worth writing down because the next reader will have the same suspicion: users.ai_action_limit is client-writable, so a seller can set their own AI action limit. effectiveAiCap (plan-gate.ts:449) returns Math.min(planLimit, userLimit), and where the plan is unlimited (-1) it returns the user value - so the self-cap can only ever LOWER the ceiling, never raise it. It is a user-set budget, not a limit override. | 2026-08-19 AC1/AC2/AC3 SHIPPED as migration 00624_disputes_insert_checks_report_owner.sql. Both disputes INSERT policies now AND in public.grade_report_belongs_to(grade_report_id, user_id). The check is on the ROW's user_id rather than auth.uid(), which is what keeps AC2 true: a member filing for the workspace owner passes because the row keys the owner and the report must belong to that same owner. WHY A SECURITY DEFINER HELPER AND NOT AN INLINE EXISTS: a subquery inside a policy is evaluated with the referenced table's RLS applied for the CALLING role, so an inline join through submissions would have made the check depend on the caller also holding a SELECT policy there. is_workspace_member_with_role (00042) solves the same problem the same way. NO REVOKE, DELIBERATELY: the helper is an RLS predicate, so it runs as the querying role and has to stay executable by anon and authenticated. Revoking it would break RLS AND arm the US-2403 segfault. The explicit GRANT states the CREATE FUNCTION default rather than widening anything, and it is what the US-2282 AC4 guard requires. AC3 IS A REAL TEST RATHER THAN A SKIPPED ONE, which took a second change: the case goes DIRECTLY at PostgREST as user B with A's grade_report_id, because routes/grade.ts has always scoped the submission to the owner, so the route was never the hole and testing through it would prove nothing. That needed a grade report owned by A, which the fixture did not seed, so seed-tenant-isolation-fixture.ts now emits TEST_USER_A_GRADE_REPORT_ID. Without it the case would have skipped on every run while the suite reported green. STILL OPEN: AC4 and AC5. The migration is PENDING (not yet applied); the entry in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md carries the read-only census that joins disputes to grade_reports to submissions and lists any row whose filer differs from the report owner. Zero rows closes this story. ⚠ NUMBERING NOTE: this migration was first written as 00619 in a local session working on a main that was 69 commits behind origin. Origin had already used 00619 through 00623, so it was renumbered to 00624 before pushing. Nothing was applied under the old number.

userStories.title: listing_gen_v2 carries the verified eBay policy rules and has never gone live
userStories.description: As a FlipDesk seller, I want the listing prompt that encodes eBays title policy and AI-summary description rules to be the one generating my drafts, so that my listings never carry search-manipulation phrasing or a keyword-dump description.
acceptanceCriteria: runListingEval (services/edge-functions/src/lib/listing-eval.ts) runs against listing_gen_v2 and its ai_prompt_versions row shows eval_passed = true before any activation attempt.
Activation goes through activatePromptVersion (lib/grading-eval.ts). No code path changes the LISTING_GEN_PROMPT_VERSION default to hot-swap the champion.
A canary window is recorded: listing_prompt_acceptance rows exist for both listing_gen_v1 and listing_gen_v2 before v2 can become champion.
summarizeListingPromptPerformance (lib/listing-acceptance.ts) reports v2 field keep-rate at or above v1 over at least 30 drafts, or the activation is rolled back.
A unit test asserts resolvePromptText returns LISTING_GEN_SYSTEM_PROMPT_V2 when the active ai_prompt_versions row has version_name listing_gen_v2 and empty prompt_text.
vault/30-platform/ebay-ranking-playbook.md gap 10 is struck in the same commit that activates v2.

OPERATOR: run the eval and the canary. AC1, AC3, AC4 and AC6 all need production, and none of them is a code change. (1) Run runListingEval against listing_gen_v2 so its ai_prompt_versions row shows eval_passed = true - this costs real vision calls, which is why it has never been done casually. (2) Activate through activatePromptVersion, never by editing the LISTING_GEN_PROMPT_VERSION default; that door is now guarded by prompt-activation-single-door_test.ts. (3) Let a canary window accumulate listing_prompt_acceptance rows for BOTH listing_gen_v1 and listing_gen_v2. (4) Check summarizeListingPromptPerformance reports v2 field keep-rate at or above v1 over at least 30 drafts, and roll back if not. (5) Strike gap 10 in vault/30-platform/ebay-ranking-playbook.md in the same commit that activates v2. The code side is finished and verified: AC2's two guards and AC5's resolvePromptText case pass, 16 tests green across listing-gen-prompt-v2_test.ts and prompt-activation-single-door_test.ts.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-19 AC5 DONE, AC2 GUARDED; THE ACTIVATION ITSELF IS UNCHANGED AND IS WHY THIS STAYS OPEN. Re-read the machinery before touching it: everything this story needs already exists and is wired. runListingEval (listing-eval.ts) is reachable from grading-eval.ts:284, activatePromptVersion is grading-eval.ts:814, the A/B challenger slot is loadListingPromptBundle (ai-listing.ts) reading in_trial + eval_passed + NOT is_active, summarizeListingPromptPerformance is listing-acceptance.ts:238, and jobs-listing-prompt-promote.ts already runs the promote-or-end-trial decision on a cron. Migration 00446 seeded the listing_gen_v2 row INACTIVE with empty prompt_text. So the gap is not missing code -- it is that v2 has never been put through the lifecycle.  WHAT SHIPPED. AC5's assertion did not exist and is the one that mattered most, because the failure it catches is invisible from every surface. The v2 row carries EMPTY prompt_text by design (text lives in code and is reviewed as code), so serving v2 depends entirely on one lookup: version_name -> code constant, in CODE_PROMPT_TEXT via resolvePromptText. Break that mapping and ai_prompt_versions still says listing_gen_v2, every eval result and acceptance row is still STAMPED listing_gen_v2, and the model is being sent v1 -- so the canary compares v1 against v1, correctly finds no regression, and promotes a champion that never changed. Nothing reads red anywhere. resolvePromptText is now exported (it was module-private) and asserted directly rather than through the bundle, since going through the bundle needs a database and would have made the most important assertion the one that gets skipped.  Eight cases added to listing-gen-prompt-v2_test.ts, 14/14 green: empty-text v2 resolves to V2; NULL text resolves the same way (the column is nullable even though 00446 writes ''); whitespace is not prompt text; a DB-authored prompt_text still wins over the registry; an unknown version_name falls back to v1 rather than serving empty or throwing; empty-text v1 still resolves to v1.  The v1-versus-v2 case earns its own line. tsc narrows both constants to their exact string literal types and REJECTED the comparison as provably never-equal -- a stronger guarantee than the test, but a compiler error is not a test and it evaporates the moment either side stops being a literal, so it is compared through String() and LISTING_GEN_SYSTEM_PROMPT is now exported for it. Without this case the other seven pass while both names point at one constant and the whole rollout measures nothing.  AC2 has a behavioural guard now, deliberately NOT a source scan: a case pins LISTING_GEN_PROMPT_VERSION to listing_gen_v1, so editing the code default to hot-swap the champion past the eval gate reddens the suite. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED rather than assumed, per the standing rule that a guard is not a guard until it has failed once: pointing CODE_PROMPT_TEXT's v2 entry at the v1 constant turns the AC5 case FAILED, and restoring it returns 14/14.  STILL OPEN, AND NONE OF IT IS CODE: AC1 (runListingEval against listing_gen_v2 until its row shows eval_passed = true) needs real vision calls against the golden set. AC3 (listing_prompt_acceptance rows for BOTH versions before v2 can be champion) and AC4 (v2 field keep-rate at or above v1 over at least 30 drafts) need a canary window on live seller traffic, which cannot be manufactured here. AC6 (strike gap 10 in vault/30-platform/ebay-ranking-playbook.md) is explicitly bound to the commit that ACTIVATES v2, so striking it now would be the drift the acceptance criterion exists to prevent -- it is left standing. The operator sequence is: run the listing eval, confirm eval_passed, flip in_trial on the v2 row, let jobs-listing-prompt-promote.ts gather 30 drafts, then let it promote or end the trial. | 2026-08-19 (second pass) AC2 GETS THE TWO GUARDS THE FIRST PASS DID NOT REACH. The earlier note closed AC2 with a behavioural pin on LISTING_GEN_PROMPT_VERSION, which stops the code DEFAULT being edited to hot-swap the champion. That is one door. AC2's claim is that activation goes through activatePromptVersion, which is a claim about EVERY door, and the remaining ones are absences rather than behaviours. NEW services/edge-functions/src/tests/prompt-activation-single-door_test.ts, 2 cases: (1) nothing outside grading-eval.ts writes is_active TRUE on ai_prompt_versions, which is what would bypass the eval gate and the US-2307 model stamp; (2) the admin PATCH cannot smuggle is_active into its payload, which guard (1) cannot see because that payload is a variable rather than a literal. MY FIRST VERSION OF GUARD 1 WAS WRONG AND FAILING IT IS WHY THIS IS TRUSTWORTHY. It forbade any .update() on ai_prompt_versions and named four files. All four are legitimate: accuracy-tracking writes accuracy_score, listing-eval writes its own eval_passed/qualified_model verdict, listing-acceptance only reads and promotes through the proper door, admin-grading creates drafts with is_active FALSE. A guard that broad forbids the eval recording its own result. Narrowed to the property AC2 actually states: a second way to turn a prompt ON. Sabotage-verified both ways - adding is_active:true to listing-eval's write and assigning patch.is_active in admin-grading each reddened its own case. AC1/AC3/AC4/AC6 unchanged and still runtime, exactly as the earlier note describes.

userStories.title: Every paid plan is denied the Claude connector, including the two sold with it
userStories.description: Measured against a real database on 2026-08-19, not inferred: `select key, gate_flags ? 'connectorAccess' from public.pricing_plans` returns false for all four tiers. pricing_plans.gate_flags is CANONICAL once the row exists (pricing-config.ts load() overwrites the hardcoded FALLBACK_MATRIX with the DB row), and the read is `gateFlags[k] = flags[k] === true`, so an absent key is a hard false on every plan. US-9124 added connectorAccess to GATE_FLAG_KEYS and to FALLBACK_MATRIX with no migration. A Business seller calling the connector gets 'The GradeThread connector is not included in this plan ... see pricing to upgrade' - an upgrade prompt shown to the customer already on the top tier. Nothing errors and no unit test goes red, because every test that never touches the database reads the fallback and sees the flag set. The only visible symptom is the Tenant Isolation workflow, which has failed on every commit since 2026-08-19 12:47 on a case that reads like an authorization test: 'MCP: A's own key CAN read A's item - the tool is reachable, not blanket-denied'.
acceptanceCriteria: A migration sets connectorAccess on all four pricing_plans rows to match FALLBACK_MATRIX (free false, starter false, pro true, business true), and only where the key is ABSENT so an operator override survives a directory re-run.

A guard fails when a gate flag the code reads appears in NO migration. That is the defect shape, and it will recur the next time a flag is added - the fallback matrix makes it invisible to every test that does not use a database.
A guard fails when FALLBACK_MATRIX and the 00166 seed disagree on a flag both define. Two definitions of one table, one read by CI and the other by production.
The Tenant Isolation workflow goes green on main. It has been red since 2026-08-19 12:47 and the failing case is about the plan gate, not about tenancy.

OPERATOR: apply 00625 to production and confirm with `select key, gate_flags->>'connectorAccess' from public.pricing_plans`. Until it is applied, every Pro and Business seller is still refused the connector. No NOTIFY needed - no table, column or RPC changed, only row data.

OPERATOR: decide whether anyone was actually turned away. The connector is dark in production behind MCP_ENABLED, so the likely answer is nobody - but that is worth confirming rather than assuming, and the mcp audit rows record a `plan_required` denial reason.
userStories.notes: Filed 2026-08-19 while diagnosing a red Tenant Isolation lane on main. VERIFIED END TO END on the local stack, which is what makes this a measurement rather than a reading: before the migration all four rows lack the key; after it, free/starter false and pro/business true; a second run reports UPDATE 0 / UPDATE 0 / INSERT 0; and a pro row deliberately set to false by hand SURVIVES a re-run. Migration 00625, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 00625 in the same commit, manifest regenerated. HELD pending the owner's prod apply. | 2026-08-20 STATUS CORRECTION, formal: 00625 is APPLIED to production and is NOT held. The owner applied it on 2026-08-19 and the confirmation query returned the expected shape - business true, free false, pro true, starter false - so Pro and Business sellers reach the connector for the first time since US-9124 shipped the gate that had nothing to read. The earlier segment says HELD because it genuinely was when it was written. HELD is not a status, it is an instruction to stop, and a stale one tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not - which has cost real sessions in this repo (US-2286 records one). VERIFY RATHER THAN TRUST THIS: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready reports applied 00629, status match, no missing key. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md now carries a banner saying the same, because that file records intent while only the database records state. | 2026-08-21 AC4 IS CONFIRMED GREEN, and AC6 was probed and stays operator. That leaves AC6 as the only open item.  AC4: the Tenant Isolation workflow has been SUCCESS on main for the last six runs (gh run list --workflow="Tenant Isolation" --branch main), the most recent 2026-08-22T04:35Z. The case that read like an authorization test - "MCP: A's own key CAN read A's item" - passes, which is the plan gate being fed a connectorAccess value for the first time. Red since 2026-08-19 12:47, green now.  AC6 PROBED AND THE PROBE IS INCONCLUSIVE, recorded so nobody repeats it. The story assumes the connector is dark behind MCP_ENABLED and reasons from that to "nobody was turned away". I tried to measure it: mcp-transport_test.ts asserts MCP_ENABLED=false hides the endpoint entirely with a 404 rather than a 503, so a 404 from https://functions.gradethread.com/mcp would settle it. Production answers 401 to both GET and POST. THAT IS NOT AN ANSWER: main.ts mounts mcpAuthMiddleware at :1273-1274 BEFORE app.route("/mcp", mcpRoutes) at :1304, and the killswitch 404 lives inside the route handler (routes/mcp.ts:186, reached through isConnectorLive). So the 401 is emitted before the killswitch is ever consulted and the two states are indistinguishable from outside. AC6 needs the deploy env or the mcp audit rows, both of which are operator reads.  AC1/AC2/AC3 shipped (migration 00625 plus src/test/plan-gate-flags-seeded.test.ts, which holds all three shapes: no flag known only to the code, every flag set on all four plans, and the 00166 seed agreeing with FALLBACK_MATRIX). AC5 was confirmed applied on 2026-08-20. | 2026-08-22 AC6 IS STILL OPERATOR, but the reason it could not be answered is now fixed. Commit 1812b2d15.  The earlier probe was recorded as inconclusive because production answers 401 to an unauthenticated GET of /mcp whether the connector is live or dark: mcpAuthMiddleware is mounted before app.route("/mcp"), and the killswitch 404 lives inside the route handler. I took that as the finding rather than the obstacle. A stop button whose state nobody can observe is a bad stop button - during an incident you flip claude_connector and the only way to confirm it took effect is to hold credentials for the surface you are trying to stop.  /health/ready now carries a `connector` entry beside `release` and `hostWatchdog`, following the same rules those two do: informational, best-effort, and structurally unable to fail the probe. It reports which of the two switches is off - the MCP_ENABLED deploy default or the claude_connector runtime flag - and they read differently on purpose, because an operator seeing "off" needs to know which one to flip.  THREE STATES, NOT TWO, and this is the part that would have been easy to get wrong. isFeatureEnabled fails OPEN: a missing row and an unreachable flag store BOTH return the caller's default, so a single read cannot tell either of them from a rule that genuinely says on. Reporting that as "live" would have rebuilt this story's exact blind spot one layer down. Reading the flag twice with opposite defaults settles it - agreement means a real rule was read - and since both reads hit the same flag cache it stays one query. When there is no readable rule the report says live AND says the killswitch currently cannot stop anything, which is the true and more useful sentence.  isMcpEnabled is now exported rather than copied into health.ts. Two readings of one env var is how a report and the thing it reports drift apart.  VERIFIED: 10 cases in services/edge-functions/src/tests/connector-readiness_test.ts, six sabotages all red with a green control either side (always-live, flag checked before env, unreadable collapsed to live, the two off states sharing one message, the double read collapsed to a single read, flag state inverted). The four flag-state cases drive the EXPORTED connectorFlagState through the feature-flags __testing seam rather than a copy of it - the first draft had its own re-implementation, which is precisely the failure US-2789 spent itself measuring, so it was removed. Full edge suite 8311 passed / 0 failed / 261 ignored, exit 0. deno lint and deno check src/main.ts clean.  ONE THING THE GUARD CAUGHT AND I DID NOT: the first version of the test omitted `import "./_env.ts"` and passed standalone while failing inside the suite, because health.ts reaches lib/supabase.ts through its static imports. test-env-isolation_test.ts (US-2379) named the file and the reason. Worth recording that the standalone green was the misleading signal.  WHAT REMAINS OPERATOR, unchanged: the mcp audit rows are the only record of who was actually denied with reason plan_required, and no anon-key read reaches them. What changed is that the next question of this shape is answerable with curl instead of with credentials. | 2026-08-23 AC6'S PREMISE IS FALSE, MEASURED. The story says 'The connector is dark in production behind MCP_ENABLED, so the likely answer is nobody' and reasons from that to 'nobody was turned away'. Production says otherwise: GET /health/ready reports features.connector = "live", the BARE value. READ WHAT THAT EXACT STRING MEANS, because connectorReadiness (health.ts:296) deliberately returns four different ones. Bare "live" is the only branch that requires BOTH that MCP_ENABLED is on for this deploy AND that the claude_connector flag was read twice with opposite defaults and AGREED, which is how that function distinguishes a real rule row from the fail-open default. So this is not 'we could not tell' and not 'it is serving on a default' - the connector is deliberately on, with a real flag row saying so. THE IRONY WORTH RECORDING: this field was built BY this story, precisely because the previous AC6 probe could not distinguish live from dark through the 401. It has been answerable by one unauthenticated curl ever since, and the answer was never read. A probe built and not run is the same as no probe. WHAT IT CHANGES. Between US-9124 shipping the gate with nothing to read and 00625 being applied on 2026-08-19, every Pro and Business seller who called the connector was told their plan does not include it and shown an upgrade prompt for a tier they were already on. AC6 can no longer be closed with 'the connector was dark'. The open question is narrower and real: was anyone using it during that window. WHAT AN AGENT CANNOT SETTLE. The connector requires an API key through mcpAuthMiddleware, so the answer is a count of connector calls or keys in that window, and both live in tables no unauthenticated read reaches. AC6 stays OPERATOR, but it is now a question with a real chance of a non-zero answer rather than a formality. AC1-AC5 all remain satisfied and AC5 was re-confirmed today by the same probe: prod pricing_plans gate_flags read free false, starter false, pro true, business true.

userStories.title: Filing a grade dispute from iOS fails every time, and the customer is shown a property name
userStories.description: Found 2026-08-19 by reading the encoder, not from a report. DisputeSheet.submit() declared its request struct inline with a plain `gradeReportId` property. Every EdgeAPI request is encoded by JSONEncoder.iso8601, which sets .convertToSnakeCase, so the phone sent `grade_report_id`. routes/grade.ts reads `body.gradeReportId` and has no snake_case fallback, so it answered 400 'gradeReportId is required' - and the sheet renders error.localizedDescription, which carries the server's own string, so the customer was shown a property name. Web (submission-detail.tsx) and Android (kotlinx, no naming strategy) both hand-build camelCase and were never affected. It started on 2026-08-17 when US-2670 correctly moved iOS filing off a direct table insert and onto the route; the insert path had no such key. A dispute is how a seller challenges a grade they paid for inside a 7-day window (DISPUTE_WINDOW_DAYS), so on iOS that window has been shut since.
acceptanceCriteria: The request type carries explicit CodingKeys so .convertToSnakeCase cannot rewrite the one spelling the route accepts, and it lives outside the view so a test can encode it.
A test asserts the encoded BYTES contain "gradeReportId" and not "grade_report_id". Asserting the property name is what passed while this was broken.
A test pins that the shared encoder DOES still transform an unprotected key, so the explicit CodingKeys read as load-bearing rather than redundant and nobody tidies them away.
A guard fails if the ROUTE is ever changed to read a snake_case key, which would silently invert the fix and leave the Swift pinned to the wrong spelling.

Evidence photos: the sheet sends `images` (up to MAX_DISPUTE_EVIDENCE = 8, downscaled on device). Web and Android have sent these since US-1437; on a CONDITION dispute the photograph is the argument, and the client built around a camera was the one that could not attach one.

OPERATOR: check whether any iOS dispute was lost. The filings 400ed so nothing was written - a seller who tried saw an error and may have given up inside the 7-day window. Sentry carries the failures if the sheet reported them.
userStories.notes: Filed 2026-08-19 while scoping US-2016's evidence-photo gap. ⚠ THE SWEEP FOR SIBLINGS WAS RUN AND FOUND NONE, and the first pass of it was WRONG in a way worth recording. I initially reported three broken routes - dispute, ebay aspects/write-back and category/derive-aspects - by matching the request struct against the route's body key. That is the wrong test: EbayAspectsService builds its OWN plain JSONEncoder and so was never affected. The app has at least two transports with opposite key behaviour (28 files construct a plain JSONEncoder; the rest use EdgeAPI's snake-casing one), which means neither the struct nor the route tells you whether a call is correct - only the transport does. Re-run keyed on transport: 13 iOS files send a multi-word body through the SHARED encoder, and every one of their routes reads snake_case except this one. platform-fields reads body.item_id, appstore/verify reads body.jws, autolister/batch reads body.item_ids. So the defect is a single route reading camelCase where the rest of the edge reads snake_case, and iOS is the only client whose transport rewrites keys. | 2026-08-23 THE FIX SHIPPED ON 2026-08-19 AND NOTHING WAS EVER RECORDED HERE, so this story has been reading as untouched for four days while five of its six criteria were already met. Two commits did it: f663e2e67 (iOS) and 6b278bc91 (the route). Checked against the code, per AC: AC1 MET, BUT NOT BY THE MECHANISM IT PRESCRIBES, and the difference is the most useful thing on this story. AC1 says the request type carries explicit CodingKeys so convertToSnakeCase cannot rewrite the key. THAT DOES NOT WORK. Swift applies the strategy to the CodingKey's stringValue, so `case gradeReportId = "gradeReportId"` still goes out as grade_report_id. It was tried and iOS CI caught it, which is the byte-level tests earning their place. DisputeRequest now carries NO CodingKeys, deliberately, with a comment saying they would read as protection and provide none. What AC1 actually wanted - the route receives a spelling it accepts - is met server-side. AC2 MET. DisputeFilingTests asserts the encoded BYTES, and asserts grade_report_id rather than gradeReportId, because that is what the phone genuinely sends. Asserting the property name is what passed while this was broken, which the criterion itself warned about. AC3 MET. testTheEncoderTransformsEveryCamelCaseKey pins that the shared encoder still rewrites an unprotected key, so nobody reads the absence of CodingKeys as an oversight. AC4 DONE TODAY, commit below, and PINNED IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION TO THE ONE WRITTEN. The criterion assumed a client-side fix and therefore guards against the route becoming snake_case. The real fix made the route accept BOTH, so the dangerous edit is now someone TIDYING it back to one spelling - the camelCase branch looks canonical and the ?? reads like clutter. Removing the snake_case branch breaks every iOS filing again with no error anywhere but the customer's screen. src/tests/dispute-key-spelling_test.ts holds both branches, scoped to the dispute handler's body and with comments stripped first - the route's own comment block names both spellings, so a raw scan passes against a deleted body. Five mutations, each applied, each RED, green controls either side. AC5 MET. The sheet sends `images` (evidence.map(dataURL)), capped at MAX_DISPUTE_EVIDENCE, and testEvidenceIsSentUnderTheKeyTheRouteReads plus testEvidenceCapMatchesTheEdge pin it. STILL OPEN: AC6 ONLY, and it is OPERATOR. Check whether any iOS dispute was lost. The filings 400ed so nothing was written and there is no queue to drain - the loss, if any, is sellers who saw a raw property name, gave up, and ran out the seven-day window. Sentry carries the failures if the sheet reported them. That is a customer-contact question rather than a code one.

userStories.title: EPIC: extension sold-sync — two-way truth for the no-API marketplaces
userStories.description: As a FlipDesk seller, I want GradeThread to learn when one of my Poshmark, Mercari, Grailed or Vinted listings sells, so that the sibling delist planner that already protects my eBay and Shopify listings finally protects these channels too and I stop overselling the same garment.
acceptanceCriteria: Umbrella only: this story closes when every child passes. Children are filed immediately after it and named in the closing AC below
Design of record is docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-extension-sold-sync-design.md; a child that departs from it updates the document in the same commit

Standing constraint, inherited from the ADR at vault/60-decisions/adr-no-server-side-marketplace-automation.md and the US-715 decision: every marketplace read happens in the seller's own browser on pages of their own account. No GradeThread server holds a marketplace cookie, password or session token, and no server fetches a marketplace page
The extension observes and the server decides: no extension code concludes that an item sold or triggers a delist. A child that puts a confidence decision in extension-unified/ fails review

At close, a sale on Poshmark or Mercari detected by the extension produces a sales row and a sibling delist plan through the existing services/edge-functions/src/lib/cross-listings.ts path, with no manual step by the seller
No child ships a seller-visible automation whose only disclosure is in a README (US-2472 AC5)
Children: US-2697, US-2698, US-2699, US-2700, US-2701, US-2702. This epic closes when all six pass

OPERATOR: the remaining work is one sitting, carried by three children that already declare it: US-2698 (Poshmark), US-2700 (Mercari), US-2702 (Grailed and Vinted). Each needs the same thing and none of it is code — a person with a logged-in account running the popup's Check selectors probe against their own sold pages, saving a scrubbed fixture into extension-unified/test/fixtures/, setting lastVerified, bumping the version off -draft and flipping enabled in sync/selectors.js. This criterion exists so the epic appears in `npm run prd:operator` rather than reading as buildable.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-23 THE PRIVACY GUARD THIS EPIC RESTS ON WAS HALF DECORATIVE. Commit 3e3044b56. No child changes; the epic's standing constraints are unaffected in intent, and one of them is now actually enforced.  sync-payload-guard_test.ts opens by stating it has two halves that fail differently: the guard stops PII arriving, and the column allowlist 'stops a future migration adding somewhere to put it'. The second half did not do that. It read 00632 alone and parsed only its CREATE TABLE block, so `ALTER TABLE public.marketplace_sync_observations ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS buyer_name text` in any later migration was invisible to it. Three probes - buyer_name, shipping_address, and a generic raw_payload jsonb - each left the suite green.  WHY IT MATTERS TO THIS EPIC SPECIFICALLY. A Poshmark order page prints the buyer's name and their shipping address. The argument for letting the extension read those pages is that the schema has nowhere to put either, and the column allowlist WAS the evidence for that claim. US-2698, US-2700 and US-2702 are the children that will actually start reading sold pages, so the guard needed to be real before they ship rather than after.  FIXED: both assertions now read the tables as they exist today - created columns plus anything a later migration added, across the whole migration corpus. The existing allowlists were correct (nothing has been added to those three tables since 00632), so no expectation changed; only what the check can see did.  VERIFIED: eight mutations, each applied and each RED with a green control either side - the buyer key removed from the forbidden list, the walk stopped from descending into objects and into arrays separately, the depth bound tightened to 1, matching made case-sensitive, and the three ALTER TABLE probes. Edge suite 8362 passed / 0 failed. The probes are a throwaway migration file created and deleted rather than an edit to a committed one, so a crashed run cannot leave the tree wrong.  ALSO CHECKED AND FOUND SOLID, since it is the other thing every child depends on: rls-guard_test.ts caught all five probes thrown at it - a user_id table with no RLS at all, an RLS table with USING (true), one gated on bare `authenticated`, a zero-policy table not declared service-role-only, and the subtle one, a table with a correct SELECT policy and an INSERT policy of WITH CHECK (true). Nothing to fix there.  UNCHANGED: US-2697, US-2699 and US-2701 are done. US-2698, US-2700 and US-2702 all need the same thing and it is not code - a person with a logged-in Poshmark, Mercari, Grailed or Vinted account running the popup's Check selectors probe against their own sold pages, saving a scrubbed fixture, and flipping the selectors off -draft.

userStories.title: Poshmark sold-sync observer: passive harvest, no automated traffic
userStories.description: As a FlipDesk seller, I want the extension to read my own Poshmark Sold page and closet whenever I happen to be on them, so that GradeThread learns about my sales without sending a single automated request to Poshmark.
acceptanceCriteria: extension-unified/sync/observe.js is pure: no chrome namespace, no document, no fetch. A source guard in extension-unified/test/ fails the build if any of the three appears

extension-unified/sync/selectors.js carries version and lastVerified per platform, and scripts/verify-lister-selectors.mjs is extended to cover it rather than a second gate being written. The gate refuses enabled true with a null lastVerified or a draft version, as it already does for the lister
A content script runs only on the seller's own Poshmark closet and Sold or Orders pages. It never runs on another seller's listing page, and a manifest-hosts test asserts the match patterns
Every closet observation carries a coverage field naming which pages were enumerated and whether the last page was reached
The observer never extracts a buyer name, buyer handle or shipping address from an order row. A node guard asserts the exact extracted field set, so adding a field is a deliberate change to the guard
A login wall produces a not-signed-in result and zero rows. A human check stops the read and hands the tab back, matching the rule in lister/engagement.js
GT_SYNC_OBSERVE is handled in extension-unified/background.js and posts the batch to POST /api/flipdesk/sync/observations with the extension token
Passive only: no code added by this story calls tabs.create or navigates a tab. A source guard asserts it

Node guards under extension-unified/test/ run via scripts/test-extensions.mjs against saved HTML fixtures. Fixtures are scrubbed of buyer details before entering the repo, and a test asserts no fixture contains a street address pattern

The popup's Check selectors probe (extension-unified/lister/selector-probe.js) is extended to cover the sync selectors, so a human with a logged-in account can verify against the live page in one click

OPERATOR: one sitting with a logged-in Poshmark account. Open the popup's Check selectors probe on your closet and on the Sold page, save the scrubbed HTML into extension-unified/test/fixtures/ (the fixture guard checks it on that commit), then set lastVerified, bump the version off -draft and flip enabled in sync/selectors.js. Nothing else in this story needs code - all 40 extension test files pass and the fixture guard was sabotage-checked 6 of 6.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-22 AC9's GUARD IS BUILT AND ARMED. The fixtures themselves still need a logged-in Poshmark account, which is the same human step `enabled: false` is waiting on.  WHAT WAS ALREADY DONE, checked rather than assumed: all 40 extension test files pass, and the sold-sync scaffolding covers most of this story. sync/observe.js is pure and guarded, sync-manifest.test.cjs holds 'reach is narrow, sync/ is passive, unverified adapters do not read' (AC1/AC3/AC8), sync-observe.test.cjs already pins the extracted field set as an ALLOWLIST that cannot quietly grow a PII field (AC5), sync-content.test.cjs covers the three refusals and the human check (AC6), GT_SYNC_OBSERVE is handled in background.js (AC7), and selector-probe covers the sold-sync flows 'without carrying buyer identity' (AC10). The Poshmark selectors exist in sync/selectors.js as version 2026.08.1-draft with enabled:false and lastVerified:null, which is the CORRECT state - that file's own rule is that enabling claims a human loaded the page.  THE GAP WAS AC9, and only half of it is buildable from here. It asks for node guards driven by saved HTML fixtures of the seller's own pages, scrubbed of buyer details, plus a test asserting no fixture carries a street address. An authentic Sold page needs a logged-in account, so the fixtures cannot be written here. THE GUARD CAN BE, AND THE ORDERING IS THE WHOLE POINT: a scrubbing rule written AFTER the first fixture lands is a rule that never inspected the thing it exists for. It is now armed and empty, so the first fixture to arrive is checked on the commit that adds it.  IT PASSES ON AN EMPTY DIRECTORY DELIBERATELY, and the reason is in the test. An absent fixture is a gap in COVERAGE - recorded here, and the reason enabled is still false - not a leak. Failing on empty would only pressure someone into adding a fixture to make a test go green, which is precisely the wrong incentive for a file that may contain a stranger's address.  FIVE PATTERNS, matched on SHAPE rather than on a name, because 'Jane Doe' is unguessable and '1 Main St' is not: US street address, US ZIP, UK postcode, email, phone. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED 6 OF 6 - each of the five leaks reddens the suite and a clean fixture (price plus a listing link) stays green, with a green control either side.  ⚠ AND THE GUARD WAS SILENTLY BLIND ON THE FIRST WRITE, which is the finding worth keeping. It passed against a fixture reading 'Jane Doe, 1 Main Street, Springfield'. The regexes had been written through a Python heredoc, and ` ` was interpreted as a literal BACKSPACE (0x08) rather than the two characters a word boundary needs. So the pattern was /<0x08>d{1,6}.../ and could never match. IT RENDERED CORRECTLY IN EVERY TOOL I CHECKED WITH: grep showed the regex without the boundary and looked plausible, sed the same, and String(regex) at runtime printed a well-formed pattern. The same regex typed by hand into `node -e` matched the leak; the one in the file did not. Only od -c showed the truth - one byte where two characters should be. This is the CLAUDE.md invisible-character rule arriving as a real defect rather than a style note, and it is the guards-that-do-not-guard failure in its purest form: a guard that looks right in every rendering and is broken by a byte nobody can see. Fixed by rewriting the bytes through node rather than through another escaping layer; Python re-introduced the same character on the repair attempt.  VERIFIED: all 40 extension test files pass, and the fixture guard sabotage-checked 6 of 6.  STILL OPEN, and it is one human sitting: log in to Poshmark, open the popup's Check selectors probe on the closet and the Sold page (AC10 already covers the sold-sync flows), save the scrubbed HTML into extension-unified/test/fixtures/ - the guard will check it on that commit - then set lastVerified, bump the version off -draft and flip enabled in sync/selectors.js. Nothing else in this story needs code.

userStories.title: Mercari sold-sync observer
userStories.description: As a FlipDesk seller cross-listing to Mercari, I want the same sold detection I get on Poshmark, so that a Mercari sale pulls my other listings before someone buys the same garment twice.
acceptanceCriteria: A Mercari adapter is added to extension-unified/sync/selectors.js with its own version and lastVerified, verified against a live logged-in account and recorded in the same way the lister flows are
Mercari's pagination shape is handled and reports coverage honestly: a partial read reports partial coverage rather than claiming the end was reached
The content script runs only on the seller's own Mercari listings and sold pages, asserted by a manifest-hosts test
Node guards cover the Mercari fixture with the same scrubbing rule as Poshmark
No new code path is added to the server: this story is selectors plus extraction only, proving the intake from the previous story is platform-agnostic

OPERATOR: sign in to a real Mercari account with at least one sold item and confirm the sold-sync observer harvests it. This is AC1 and it is the only item left - AC2 through AC5 are satisfied, three of them by construction. AC5 is the story's own thesis and it measured true: no Mercari-specific code path was added to the server, so the intake built in the previous story really is platform-agnostic.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-22 AC2-AC5 ARE ALREADY SATISFIED, three of them by construction rather than by Mercari-specific code. AC1 is the only thing left and it needs a live logged-in account.  AC5 IS THE INTERESTING ONE because it is the story's own thesis: 'no new code path is added to the server, proving the intake from the previous story is platform-agnostic'. Measured: grep for mercari across the sync route and lib returns nothing, and sync-manifest.test.cjs section 4b ASSERTS the agnosticism from the other side - it fails if sync/content.js names ANY platform as a string literal, iterating Object.keys(SEL) so a new adapter is covered the moment it is added. The concrete failure it records is content.js having pinned PLATFORM to 'poshmark'. So the thesis is not just true, it is guarded.  AC3 IS COVERED BY THE SAME ITERATION. sync-manifest.test.cjs walks every platform in sync/selectors.js and asserts each declared host is reachable by a manifest match pattern - so Mercari is covered automatically, and grepping the test for 'mercari' returning nothing is the correct answer rather than a gap.  AC2 COVERAGE HONESTY IS IN THE SHAPE OF THE CODE. observe.js buildClosetObservation writes `reachedEnd: cov.reachedEnd === true`, so an absent or undefined value reads as NOT reached. A partial read cannot claim the end by omission, which is the failure the AC is about; the file calls reachedEnd 'the single most consequential field'. The Mercari adapter's own comment addresses its numbered pager specifically and notes it is the one place its shape differs from Poshmark.  AC4 IS SATISFIED BY THE US-2698 GUARD, which is platform-blind by design: it scans every .html under extension-unified/test/fixtures/ for street addresses, ZIPs, UK postcodes, emails and phone numbers, whichever marketplace they came from. Sabotage-verified 6 of 6 there. So the Mercari fixture is covered before it exists.  STILL OPEN: AC1 ONLY. The Mercari adapter is present as version 2026.08.1-draft with enabled:false and lastVerified:null, which is the CORRECT state - the file's rule is that enabling claims a human loaded the page. One sitting: log in, run the popup's Check selectors probe on /mypage/listings/sold, save a scrubbed fixture, set lastVerified, bump off -draft, flip enabled.

userStories.title: Grailed and Vinted sold-sync observers
userStories.description: As a FlipDesk seller on Grailed, I want to be told the moment a Grailed listing sells, because Grailed can never be delisted automatically and I am the only one who can end my other listings.
acceptanceCriteria: Grailed and Vinted adapters are added to extension-unified/sync/selectors.js, each with its own version and lastVerified verified against a live logged-in account

A detected Grailed sale produces an explicit seller instruction rather than a silent delist, because Grailed delete is confirmed by a native browser dialog nothing in a page can answer (recorded in extension-unified/README.md). The notification names Grailed as needing a manual end
Vinted's locale domains are handled the way the lister handles them: an uncovered locale reports that it cannot read rather than guessing at the page
Both channels report coverage honestly on paginated closets
Node guards cover both fixtures with the same scrubbing rule

OPERATOR: the first step needs a human with logged-in Grailed and Vinted accounts, running the popup's Check selectors probe against their own sold pages. AC5 is the only criterion already met; everything else waits on those selectors being read off real pages rather than guessed.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-22 NOT BUILT, DELIBERATELY, and one AC is now easier than when it was written.  WHY NOT BUILT. The Grailed and Vinted adapters are genuinely absent from sync/selectors.js (only poshmark and mercari exist). Drafting them from here would mean guessing selectors for pages I have never loaded, and this repo has a recorded history of exactly that failing: US-2739's notes say the deep probe 'is the same two-step that produced every correct Poshmark selector and that every guess made before it failed', and US-2743 says the same. A draft adapter full of guessed selectors is worse than an absent one, because absent is honest and a draft invites someone to flip enabled.  AC3 HAS A STRUCTURAL PROBLEM WORTH NAMING BEFORE ANYONE STARTS, and it is not about selectors. The sync layer resolves ONE pollUrl per platform: poll-plan.js pollUrlFor reads sold.pollUrl, requires https, requires the host to be one the adapter itself declares, and requires the URL to match the sold flow's urlPattern. Vinted has 22 country domains. One pollUrl cannot serve them, and nothing in sync/ has any notion of a locale - grep for 'locale' across sync/*.js returns two comments and no code.  WHAT CHANGED TODAY: THE MISSING INPUT NOW EXISTS. US-2777 shipped flipdesk_settings.lister_locales, a per-seller platform -> country-domain map ({"vinted": "vinted.fr"}), with the edge stamping it onto queued extension work and the web reading it for direct sends. When US-2702 was written there was no source of truth for which Vinted a seller uses; there is one now. So AC3's 'handled the way the lister handles them' has a concrete answer rather than an open design question: the poll needs the seller's locale key the same way a lister job does, and pollUrlFor needs a locale-aware sibling that still takes its URL from the bundled config. THAT IS A DESIGN NOTE, NOT A BUILT THING. It is recorded so whoever picks this up does not rediscover that the sync layer has no locale concept, and does not conclude the answer has to be invented.  AC5 IS ALREADY DONE by the US-2698 fixture guard, which is platform-blind: it scans every .html under extension-unified/test/fixtures/ for street addresses, ZIPs, UK postcodes, emails and phone numbers regardless of which marketplace produced them. Sabotage-verified 6 of 6. Both channels' fixtures are covered before either exists.  AC2 IS A PRODUCT DECISION SOMEONE SHOULD MAKE BEFORE THE ADAPTER, not after: a detected Grailed sale must produce an explicit seller INSTRUCTION rather than a silent delist, because Grailed's delete is confirmed by a native browser dialog no page script can drive. That constraint shapes what the observer is allowed to conclude, so it belongs in the design rather than in a later correction.  STILL OPEN: all of it, and the first step is a human with logged-in Grailed and Vinted accounts running the popup's Check selectors probe against their own sold pages. AC5 is the only criterion already met.

userStories.title: EPIC: grade as dispute evidence — turn the grade report into an eBay INAD defense
userStories.description: As a FlipDesk seller facing an item-not-as-described case, I want GradeThread to assemble my dated, signed grade report and the disclosure my listing actually carried into one-click eBay evidence with a drafted argument, so that I stop losing INAD cases I should win with a screenshot and a defensive paragraph.
acceptanceCriteria: Umbrella only: this story closes when every child passes. Children are filed immediately after it and named in the closing AC below
Design of record is docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-grade-as-dispute-evidence-design.md; a child that departs from it updates the document in the same commit

Standing honesty constraint: no surface in this epic claims that submitting evidence wins a case. eBay decides. The claim is one-click dated signed specific evidence, and copy asserting an outcome fails review

Standing safety constraint: no draft may cite a defect that is not present in the item's grade report. The AI matcher proposes and a pure deterministic layer decides what survives, mirroring the split in lib/grading-pipeline.ts

Standing safety constraint: when the grade report documents a flaw that the listing did not disclose, the pack refuses to auto-assemble and tells the seller to consider refunding. Handing eBay proof against our own user under our signature is the failure this epic must not ship
At close, an eBay INAD return on an item graded and published through FlipDesk produces a drafted response and an attachable evidence pack from the post-sale surface with no manual file assembly
Children: US-2704, US-2705, US-2706, US-2707. This epic closes when all four pass

OPERATOR: drive one real eBay INAD return end to end and confirm AC6. All four children (US-2704..US-2707) pass; this is the only thing left and no child carries it. On the next INAD return for an item graded and published through FlipDesk, open it on the post-sale page, press Evidence, paste the buyer's words, READ THE VERDICT BEFORE SENDING, and confirm a drafted response and an attachable pack come out with no manual file assembly. If the verdict says the report agrees with the buyer and refuses to assemble, that is AC5 working and the story still closes. Why it cannot be done here: the Post-Order file contract (UploadFileRequest then SubmitFileRequest, activation by filePurpose) was verified from eBay's reference and never exercised, and there is no sandbox INAD case to drive. Closing on the children alone would assert an end-to-end result nobody has seen.
userStories.notes:
ALL FOUR CHILDREN PASS as of 2026-08-21: US-2704 (publication snapshots), US-2705 (matcher, plan, three verdicts), US-2706 (return evidence + the review surface), US-2707 (payment-dispute parity). AC7's condition is met.

THE EPIC STAYS OPEN ON AC6, which is not a coding task. AC6 asks that a real eBay INAD return on a real graded, published item produce a drafted response and an attachable pack from the post-sale surface. Nothing here has been driven against a live eBay case: the Post-Order file contract (upload then submit, UploadFileRequest / SubmitFileRequest, activation by filePurpose) was verified from eBay's own reference, not exercised. Closing this epic on the children alone would assert an end-to-end result nobody has seen.

THE STANDING CONSTRAINTS HELD, and each is enforced by a test rather than by intent:
  AC3 (no outcome claims) - the panel is scanned for win/guarantee/proves your case/eBay will side, and every line of the sheet copy is scanned separately.
  AC4 (the model proposes, code decides) - matches are filtered against the real defect list BEFORE the verdict logic, and an out-of-range index is dropped rather than clamped. Driven with a snapshot whose text would have supported the fabrication.
  AC5 (refuse when the report agrees with the buyer) - refused server-side on BOTH case types, with a parity guard that walks each handler body, and refused on the surface too, where the Send button is not rendered at all.

AC2's same-commit rule: the design document needed no change. The one place the implementation departed from it is recorded on US-2704 - the wire-level funnel cannot record a FIRST publish, because the listings row does not carry inventory_sku or platform_offer_id until step 5 while the inventory item is PUT at step 2, so the publish route records it after persist.

WHAT TO DO WHEN A REAL CASE ARRIVES: open the return or dispute on the post-sale page, press Evidence (or Grade pack), paste the buyer's words, and read the verdict before sending. If it says the report agrees with the buyer, that is the feature working.

userStories.title: EPIC: market condition index — aggregate the claimed-vs-actual gap the extension already measures and throws away
userStories.description: As the GradeThread team, we want the condition reads our extension already performs to accumulate into a de-identified market-wide measurement of how far seller claims sit from objective condition, so that the extension gets better for everyone as more people use it and we own a dataset no competitor can construct.
acceptanceCriteria: Umbrella only: this story closes when every child passes. Children are filed immediately after it and named in the closing AC below

The asset this epic creates: how far claimed condition sits from objective condition, aggregated by marketplace, brand, category and price band. Today lib/listing-ingest.ts scores that gap per read, persists it on ingested_listings (00535), and the row is pruned, so the measurement is discarded after serving one buyer

Standing constraint from US-2148: a seller-adverse score is never published from unconfirmed model reads. The recorded asymmetry holds — penalise only what a human confirmed, credit on either — so this epic publishes categorical aggregates and may credit a seller, and no child ships a per-seller deficit derived from extension reads

Standing constraint from the anti-crawl contract in lib/listing-ingest.ts and vault/20-domain/buyer-platform.md: one buyer-initiated listing per request, marketplace hosts only, page HTML never fetched. No child extends retention of an identifying listing row to make aggregation easier; the statistic is extracted at read time and the row prunes on the schedule it already has

Every published rate follows the honesty rule already used by lib/resale-condition.ts: a minimum sample before a rate is stated, and null with a not-enough-data message rather than a misleading number
At close, a buyer read on a supported marketplace can be stated in market context rather than in isolation, and the aggregate is published on a public route
Children: US-2709, US-2710, US-2711, US-2712, US-2713. This epic closes when all five pass

OPERATOR: nothing in this epic can start until US-2709's question to counsel is answered. All five children (US-2709..US-2713) sit behind it: US-2709 carries the question itself, and US-2710 through US-2713 each depend on it for the fields they are allowed to retain. The spike's AC1-AC5 are done and the decision contract is written at vault/20-domain/market-condition-index-contract.md; what is missing is a per-marketplace go or no-go on whether aggregating buyer-initiated listing reads is consistent with each marketplace's terms. One question, six marketplaces, because the clause is the same shape everywhere. This criterion exists so the epic appears in `npm run prd:operator` rather than reading as buildable — its children are correctly blocked via dependsOn, and the umbrella was not.

userStories.title: Decision spike: what may be aggregated from buyer condition reads, and under what contract
userStories.description: As the founder, I need a written decision on what the market condition index may retain and publish before any of it is built, because the source rows sit under an anti-crawl contract and a deliberate prune, and getting this wrong is a legal problem rather than a bug.
acceptanceCriteria: A vault note is written under vault/20-domain/ recording the contract, linked from the index, and passing npm run vault:lint --strict as a type: contract note

The note states exactly which fields may be extracted from an ingested_listings row at read time, and asserts that no identifying field (listing_url, thumb_url, title, seller handle) survives into the aggregate store
The note states the retention decision: the aggregate row's lifetime, and confirmation that the source row's existing prune schedule is unchanged
The note states the k-anonymity floor per aggregation bucket, and the reasoning for the number, following the precedent set by RESALE_MIN_SAMPLE in lib/resale-condition.ts
The note applies US-2148's asymmetry explicitly to this dataset and records that a per-seller deficit from unconfirmed reads is out of scope, with the condition under which that could be revisited

The note records whether aggregating buyer-initiated reads is consistent with each marketplace's terms, per marketplace, with the reasoning written down rather than assumed. A marketplace that cannot be cleared is excluded from the index rather than included quietly
NO-CODE story: the deliverable is the note plus a go or no-go per marketplace. A no-go on a marketplace removes it from the children below

OPERATOR: one question to counsel, covering all six marketplaces at once - the terms clause governing automated processing of listing data by a browser extension acting for a logged-in shopper. That is AC6 and AC7, the only two left, and it is deliberately ONE action rather than six because the clause is the same shape everywhere. The decision contract is already written up at vault/20-domain/market-condition-index-contract.md with the k-anonymity floor, the price-banding rule and the user_id decision settled; the per-marketplace go/no-go is the part that needs a lawyer. US-2710 through US-2713 are all blocked behind this answer.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-22 THE NOTE IS WRITTEN. AC1-AC5 are done. AC6/AC7 need one decision from you and it is a legal reading, not a measurement.  DELIVERABLE: vault/20-domain/market-condition-index-contract.md, type: contract, source_of_truth: code with three code_refs, passing npm run vault:lint --strict (198 notes, links resolve, no orphans). Linked from the index, which the no-orphans check proves rather than the file claiming it.  AC2 THE EXTRACTION RULE. Seven fields may be extracted (marketplace, brand, category, BANDED price, claimed_grade, overall_score, discrepancy magnitude) and seven must not survive (listing_url, thumb_url, title, user_id, id, matched_search_ids, raw price_cents). TWO CHOICES THERE THAT ARE NOT OBVIOUS AND ARE ARGUED IN THE NOTE. (a) Price is BANDED, not carried: a price is not identifying alone and is close to it in combination, because marketplace + brand + category + an exact price to the cent is very often exactly one listing. Banding is what makes the row an aggregate rather than a re-identifiable record wearing an aggregate's shape. (b) user_id is ABSENT, not hashed: a per-buyer hash still permits counting how many checks a person ran and on what, which is the browsing history the published 90-day promise exists to delete. The aggregate has no buyer column at all.  AC3 RETENTION. Extraction happens AT READ TIME in the request that already scored the listing; the source row keeps INGEST_RETENTION_DAYS = 90 unchanged, with both prunes (the inline write-path one and the fleet-wide backstop in data-retention.ts) untouched. Stated as a rule for the children: if the aggregate needs a longer window it takes it in the AGGREGATE, never in the identifying row.  AC4 THE FLOOR IS 25, ADOPTED FROM RESALE_MIN_SAMPLE RATHER THAN RE-DERIVED, and the adoption IS the argument: the site already tells buyers 'not enough data yet' at 25 in the resale bands, and two different floors on two public honesty statements is a difference a reader would have to discover. Below the floor the field is null with a message, never a number with a caveat. Recorded as a floor and not a ceiling on caution - a bucket narrow enough to be one seller's inventory should be widened before publication, which is a design constraint on US-2710 written down now rather than discovered later.  AC5 THE ASYMMETRY, APPLIED. No per-seller deficit from extension reads, because an extension read is an unconfirmed model verdict and that is exactly the evidence US-2148 refuses for a seller-adverse score. Crediting stays allowed. THE REVISIT CONDITION IS NAMED so nobody has to guess it: a per-seller figure becomes arguable only if the reads behind it are HUMAN-CONFIRMED - a buyer's own confirmation, or a completed guarantee claim with a reviewer verdict - which is a different dataset with a different story, not a threshold change on this one.  AC6/AC7 ARE YOURS, AND THE NOTE SAYS SO IN A WARNING CALLOUT RATHER THAN BURYING IT. The eleven allowlisted hosts collapse to six marketplaces. eBay is recommended GO - we are an API partner with a commercial relationship, the reads are buyer-initiated on pages the buyer opened, and the aggregate carries no listing content. The other five (Poshmark, Mercari, Grailed, Depop, Vinted) are recorded as OWNER CALL: the same mechanical argument applies to all six, and 'applies' is not 'cleared by counsel'. The note explicitly says not to read the eBay row as settled either - it is the strongest case, not a legal opinion.  WHY I DID NOT JUST DECIDE THEM. AC6 asks for a determination per marketplace with reasoning written down rather than assumed. I can write the reasoning; the determination turns on how each marketplace's terms treat automated processing of listing data by an extension acting for a logged-in shopper, and nothing in this repo answers that. Filing a guess as a determination would be the assumption AC6 exists to prevent. AC7's own rule already handles the unanswered state: a marketplace that cannot be cleared is EXCLUDED rather than included quietly, so the safe default costs nothing while the question is open.  WHAT WOULD ANSWER IT, so this is one action and not six: a single question to counsel covering all six marketplaces - the terms clause governing automated processing of listing data by a browser extension acting for a logged-in shopper. The note records that framing.  STILL OPEN: AC6 and AC7 only. Nothing else in this story needs code or another session.

userStories.title: Extract the gap at read time: the de-identified aggregate store
userStories.description: As the GradeThread team, we want each buyer condition read to contribute a de-identified row to an aggregate store as it happens, so that the measurement survives the prune without retaining anything that identifies a listing, a seller or a buyer.
acceptanceCriteria: A new aggregate table holds only the bucketed dimensions cleared by the spike (marketplace, brand, category, price band, period) plus the claimed-vs-actual gap and a count. No listing_url, no thumb_url, no title, no seller identifier, no user_id. A CHECK constraint or a column-level test pins the absence of identifying columns
The write happens inside the existing read path in services/edge-functions/src/lib/listing-ingest.ts, at the point the gap is already scored, so no second pass over listing data is introduced
The source row's prune schedule is unchanged by this story; a test asserts retention was not extended
The aggregate write is best-effort and never fails a buyer's read, following the pattern in lib/closet-grade-link.ts
A pure module computes the bucketing and is unit-tested with no DB, so bucket boundaries are reviewable in one place
Rows are written with the service-role client and the table is RLS deny-all, registered in the rls-guard test the way other platform-level tables are (see vault/20-domain/service-role-tables.md)

The table carries the US-1108 triple: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in the same commit, and a self-record footer. Added to PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md and not pushed until the owner has applied it
userStories.notes: 2026-08-22 NOT STARTED - still blocked by US-2709 AC6/AC7, which need a lawyer's reading of six marketplaces' terms and are marked OPERATOR. AC1 here depends on 'the bucketed dimensions cleared by the spike', and the spike is cleared only as far as AC1-AC5.  BUT AC2 NAMES THE WRONG FILE, and that is worth fixing now rather than being discovered by whoever picks this up. Verified today by grepping call sites, not by reading the story.  AC2 says the write goes 'inside the existing read path in services/edge-functions/src/lib/listing-ingest.ts, at the point the gap is already scored'. THE GAP IS NEVER SCORED IN THAT FILE. listing-ingest.ts captures claimedCondition as verbatim text (line 121) and its own comment on that field says 'scored later'. scoreDiscrepancy is not imported there.  The gap is scored in routes/public-grading.ts, at TWO call sites, and the second one is the reason this matters:   - line 1124, inside POST /grade-from-url (route opens at 1038)   - line 1791, inside POST /ingest-listing (route opens at 1659) Both are buyer condition reads. A write bolted onto one of them silently aggregates half the traffic, and the resulting index would be biased by which entry point a buyer happened to use rather than by the market - a failure that looks like data, not like a bug.  So AC2 should read: the aggregate write happens where scoreDiscrepancy is called, and it must cover BOTH sites - preferably by extracting the score-then-record step into one helper both routes call, so a third read path added later cannot forget it.  AC5's pure bucketing module and AC4's best-effort rule are unaffected by this correction. AC7's migration triple and the standing held-migration rule still apply whenever this is built.

That is now stale. Fetched https://gradethread.com/assets/lister-extension-o8De6_t5.js (found by scanning the entry chunks named in index.html for the chunk name, since the lister chunk is lazy and not in the HTML):   listerExtensionId()  -> function D(){return"apinefjjagmigmobdlbiilhbjebmjkdh"}   isListerAvailable()  -> function tt(){return(p()||typeof M()?.sendMessage=="function")&&!0} The `import.meta.env.VITE_LISTER_EXTENSION !== "true"` early return has been CONSTANT-FOLDED AWAY ENTIRELY, and `!!listerExtensionId()` folded to `!0`. On 2026-08-20 the same function was `return!1` and the id function was `return""`. Both Pages variables are set and the Send-to-extension button renders. `return""` now occurs zero times in the whole chunk.  AC2 CONFIRMED NOT DONE, and the probe is calibrated so the absence is a real answer rather than a quiet endpoint. OPTIONS preflight to https://functions.gradethread.com/api/flipdesk/extension-queue/claim:   Origin: chrome-extension://apinefjjagmigmobdlbiilhbjebmjkdh -> 204, NO access-control-allow-origin   Origin: https://gradethread.com                             -> 204, access-control-allow-origin: https://gradethread.com   Origin: https://evil.example                                -> 204, NO access-control-allow-origin So EXTENSION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is empty on the live edge. THAT WHOLE CLASS OF QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERABLE FROM A LAPTOP: 'did the operator set the edge CORS variable' is one read-only curl, the same way the PostgREST OpenAPI read answers 'did anyone send NOTIFY pgrst'. It needs the negative control to be worth anything - without the evil.example line an endpoint that never emits the header would look identical.
