userStories.title: listings.listed_at is NOT NULL but the code writes null for a draft, so the extension writeback INSERT has never succeeded
userStories.description: As a seller cross-posting to Poshmark, I want the draft row the extension writeback creates to actually insert, so that a filled marketplace form is recorded in FlipDesk instead of lost.
acceptanceCriteria: CAUSE, captured live 2026-08-20: '[flipdesk.extension-writeback.insert] 23502 | null value in column listed_at of relation listings violates not-null constraint'. Confirmed NOT a production drift - the local stack carrying all 633 migrations reports listings.listed_at is_nullable = NO as well, so this INSERT path has failed on every environment since US-1877.

US-1877 is right and stays: a prefilled row is a DRAFT and must not carry a listed_at, because a date there is what made phantom rows look like real dateable cross-listings. The database is the piece that was never updated - listed_at has been NOT NULL DEFAULT now() since 00002 and no migration ever changed it.

The rest of the codebase already treats the column as nullable: lib/api-listings.ts and lib/api-items.ts type it 'listed_at: string | null' and openapi-spec.ts declares nullable true. The published API contract and the schema disagreed, and the schema was wrong.

Migration 00634 drops the NOT NULL and carries the US-1108 triple: idempotent (ALTER COLUMN DROP NOT NULL is a no-op when already nullable, verified by applying it twice locally), EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 00634 in the same commit, self-record footer, and the manifest regenerated.

The DEFAULT now() is deliberately KEPT. Dropping NOT NULL is what allows an explicit null; removing the default would change behaviour for every other writer that omits the column, which is a separate decision.

Proven end to end on the migrated local schema: the exact writeback INSERT (poshmark, gradethread origin, draft, is_active false, listed_at null, draft_id null) now returns a row with listed_at null and listing_status draft.
OPERATOR: apply 00634 to prod, then NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema', then retry one Send to extension and confirm a 200.

AC7, FIRST TWO THIRDS CONFIRMED 2026-08-21: 00634 is applied and listings.listed_at is NULLABLE in production - it is absent from the `required` array of the listings definition, where 30 other columns appear. Read from PostgREST's own OpenAPI document (GET /rest/v1/ with Accept: application/openapi+json and the public anon key). It lists every exposed table's columns and every column's nullability via the `required` array, plus every exposed RPC - so a whole class of 'go and run this in psql' operator steps can be answered from a laptop, read-only, with no credentials beyond the key that ships in the frontend bundle.
The remaining third is a human with a Poshmark tab: retry one Send to extension and confirm a 200. The schema can no longer be what blocks it.
userStories.notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-20, from the migration-triple check. The PENDING_MIGRATIONS entry claimed 'Client-side read risk: NONE - the rest of the codebase already treats the column as nullable'. That was true of the EDGE and false of the FRONTEND: src/types/database.ts typed the row as non-null listed_at: string and the Insert as listed_at?: string, which would have rejected the explicit null in TypeScript and described a shape the database can no longer guarantee. Fixed in the same change - Row is string | null, Insert accepts null - and correcting the type is what surfaced two unguarded parses, src/lib/price-suggestions.ts getDaysListed and src/components/analytics/listing-suggestions.tsx getDaysListed, both doing new Date(listing.listed_at). Neither was a LIVE NaN: both are reached behind an is_active filter and the writeback writes listed_at null together with is_active false. But that is an argument from the caller rather than from the type, so both now return 0 for a draft. Nothing else in src/ reads the column. The note has been rewritten to say LOW rather than NONE and to state what was wrong. Two further points from the same check are recorded in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md: the edge change in this commit makes a missing draft_id fail EARLIER (a hard WRITEBACK_GROUP_LOAD 500) rather than limping to the INSERT, so the apply order matters more than the note first implied; and the 00134 draft_id repair leaves no durable record - it is SQL in a markdown file, apply-prod-migrations.sh will never run it, and no applied_migrations row will mark it done, so a future audit cannot distinguish a repaired prod from a broken one.

userStories.title: Every platform variant is priced from the eBay draft alone, so an item priced on the item generates a kit with no price at all
userStories.description: As a seller cross-posting to Poshmark, I want the price I set to reach the marketplace form, so that the one field deciding what I get paid is not blank.
acceptanceCriteria: PROVEN 2026-08-20 by elimination, not inference: after the selectors were fixed the deep probe reported price and originalPrice both 'ok', and the Listing price row in the Poshmark kit tab was EMPTY. The selectors were never the problem.

CAUSE: generatePlatformVariants builds its base with priceCents from the eBay DRAFT row only - Math.round((d.listing_price ?? 0) * 100) - and platform-variants.ts derives every variant's price from it. inventory_items.target_price was not even in the item SELECT. An item priced on the item therefore produced price 0 for every channel.

That 0 then travels: normalize() in listing-kit.tsx keeps it as 0, buildListerPayload turns 0 into the empty string, and GT.fill refuses an empty value before it ever looks at the page - so the extension told the seller 'the price was NOT filled in' on every single cross-post while doing nothing wrong.

Fixed with the draft-then-target precedence the extension writeback already uses (routes/flipdesk-listings.ts), so the kit and the recorded listings row cannot disagree about what an item costs. target_price added to the item SELECT and its type.
An unpriced draft still resolves to 0 rather than inventing a number, and a negative price never becomes a listing price. 4 cases in platform-variants_test.ts pin the rule; 11 pass.
OPERATOR: the fix only affects newly generated variants. Existing drafts carry the stored 0 - press Regenerate on the Listing Kit to pick up the price.
userStories.notes: RENDER-TIME FALLBACK ADDED 2026-08-20, after the server fix alone did not clear it. The server fix is correct but only affects NEWLY generated variants: a variant's price is written once, at generation, so every draft made before it carries the stored 0 and stays broken until someone thinks to press Regenerate. That is the wrong dependency for a field this important. listing-kit.tsx now resolves the price at RENDER: it reads the eBay draft's listing_price alongside platform_fields and the item's target_price, applying the same draft-then-target precedence the generator and the extension writeback use, so all three agree about what an item costs. The resolved variant is used in THREE places deliberately - the displayed row, the live validation that decides Ready to list, and buildListerPayload - because patching only the render would show the seller a filled-in price while still handing the extension an empty string, which is exactly the failure this whole thread has been about. It never invents a price: fallbackPrice 0 leaves the variant exactly as stored. 3 guards in src/test/cross-post-setup.test.ts; 34 pass. This fixes every existing draft with no regeneration and no deploy ordering to get right. | THIRD SOURCE 2026-08-20, and it was the one that mattered. After both earlier fixes were confirmed LIVE in the deployed bundle (priceStep, target_price and fallbackPrice all present in composer-COhLjvXk.js) the Listing price row was still blank - so the fallback was resolving to 0, which meant the price was in neither place I had checked. It was in the third: inventory_items.list_price. The composer has always read all three, [listing.listing_price, item.target_price, item.list_price] with the FIRST POSITIVE winning (composer.tsx), and my fallback implemented two thirds of that rule while its own comment claimed the surfaces agreed. Now copied whole into all three places that resolve a price - listing-kit.tsx, ai-listing.ts and the extension writeback - so the claim is true rather than aspirational. First-positive rather than first-non-null is the load-bearing half: a stale 0 on a draft row must not shadow a real price further down, which is exactly the shape of row this item had. Guards: 4 more cases in platform-variants_test.ts (13 pass) and the kit guard now asserts all three sources by name plus the positive test (38 pass). | REGRESSION I CAUSED, AND FIXED, 2026-08-20. The 'third source' change added list_price to three inventory_items SELECTs. inventory_items HAS NO SUCH COLUMN - list_price is a column on the items_full VIEW, where it aliases a listing's own listing_price. Production proved it: '42703: column i.list_price does not exist'. Consequences were worse than the blank price it was meant to fix: PostgREST fails the WHOLE query, so the kit lost target_price too; the edge generator's item select throws 'Item not found for this workspace', which would have broken platform-field generation outright; and the extension writeback would have 500'd on every call. All three reverted. The kit now reads the equivalent third source from a table that actually has it - any of the item's listings rows carrying a positive listing_price - and the two edge paths are deliberately TWO-source with a comment saying why, rather than pretending to agree. The edge test that asserted the three-source rule now asserts the two-source one and records the 42703 as the reason. LESSON WORTH KEEPING: I read item.list_price in composer.tsx and assumed the column was on the table the composer's item object came from. It came from a view. A column name seen in application code is not evidence that a table has it.

userStories.title: Photos are reported as attached when the page never took them, because the file list was shadowed rather than assigned
userStories.description: As a seller cross-posting to Poshmark, I want the photos to actually arrive, and to be told the truth when they do not, so that I never publish a listing believing images are on it.
acceptanceCriteria: OBSERVED 2026-08-20: no photos reached Poshmark, and the toast carried NO photo message at all - which by photoNote's own logic means total was above zero and failed was zero. The extension believed it had attached every photo. That is the worst failure shape available: a silent false success on the one thing a buyer sees.

CAUSE: attachPhotos used Object.defineProperty to hang a files value off the input. That shadows the prototype getter, so anything reading el.files sees the list, but the input's REAL state never changes - el.value stays empty and no internal file selection exists, so an uploader that checks value, or reads the selection at submit time rather than from the event, sees an empty input.
NOT a CORS or fetch problem, checked before changing anything: the public bucket returns access-control-allow-origin * to a poshmark.com origin, so a content-script fetch is allowed.

Chrome accepts a direct assignment from a DataTransfer, which sets the real selection and populates value with a fake path. The fill now assigns, and treats a non-empty value as the BROWSER confirming it took - a witness we did not write ourselves. defineProperty stays as a fallback for any host that refuses the assignment.

A refused list now reports every photo as FAILED rather than attached, so photosAttached goes false and the seller is told to drag them in. Verified against three cases: accepted 8/0, refused 0/8, partial 6/2.
Both input and change are dispatched, in the order a real selection fires them - some uploaders listen for one, some for the other.

STILL UNPROVEN until tested live: whether Poshmark's uploader accepts the assignment at all. If it does not, the honest report is now the deliverable and the next step is a different mechanism, not a louder claim.

OPERATOR: open a live Poshmark listing form, run the extension's photo attach, and report whether the images actually land. This is AC7 and it is the only thing keeping the story open. It also DECIDES US-2775: if Poshmark accepts the direct assignment, US-2775 is a latent gap on other hosts; if it refuses and the defineProperty fallback runs, US-2775 IS the live bug and this story is not fixed. The honest-failure reporting is already in place, so a refusal now shows the seller 0/8 attached rather than a silent success.
userStories.notes:
AC5 IS NOW HELD BY A TEST, 2026-08-21. It said 'Verified against three cases: accepted 8/0, refused 0/8, partial 6/2' and nothing ran that verification again. extension-unified/test/attach-photos-accepted.test.cjs does, plus AC6's event order, and it opens by proving its own refusing stub can actually refuse - otherwise the whole file would pass against the original broken code.

SABOTAGE-CHECKED, control-first, 6 of 7 caught: restoring the original defineProperty-and-assume-success, dropping the refusal-to-failed conversion, dispatching only `change`, dispatching in the wrong order, and removing the fallback.

THE SEVENTH IS A REAL GAP AND IS NOW US-2775. Removing the `input.value !== ""` witness changed no outcome, because the fallback beneath it decides acceptance with `input.files.length === dt.files.length` immediately after defineProperty WROTE input.files. It reads back what it just set and cannot fail. So on a host that swallows the direct assignment but permits defineProperty, the original silent false success is still reachable - through the fallback added to make the report honest.

NOT FIXED HERE ON PURPOSE: reporting the fallback as failed would raise a false alarm on hosts where the shadow works, across seven platforms. That is a decision, not a typo. The test pins current behaviour with a comment saying so.

AC7 STILL BLOCKS CLOSURE and is unchanged: nobody has put this in front of a live Poshmark form. If Poshmark accepts the direct assignment, US-2775 is latent; if it does not, US-2775 IS the live bug and this story is not actually fixed.

userStories.title: Poshmark takes whole dollars and we send cents, so the price we type is a value the field cannot hold
userStories.description: As a seller cross-posting to Poshmark, I want the price sent in the units Poshmark accepts, so that the field takes it instead of rejecting it.
acceptanceCriteria: CONFIRMED by the founder against the live form 2026-08-20: Poshmark prices in WHOLE DOLLARS. Its listing-price input is inputmode=numeric pattern=[0-9]* — digits only, no decimal point — so '32.49' is not a value that field can hold. Sending one is not a rounding nicety; it is handing the marketplace something it rejects.

MarketplaceSpec gains priceStep, and poshmark declares priceStep 1. It lives in marketplace-specs.ts rather than the extension's selector config because it is a fact about the MARKETPLACE, not about a selector, and the kit has to show the seller the same number it is about to send. Omitted everywhere else, so eBay and Shopify keep their cents.

Applied in listing-kit.tsx where the resolved variant is already built, so the displayed row, the validation that decides Ready to list, and the extension payload all carry the same stepped number. Rounding only in the payload would show one price and send another.
Rounded to NEAREST, not floored: flooring quietly costs the seller money on every cross-post, and the adjusted number is visible in the row before they send it.
Never below one step and never invented: 0.40 becomes 1, a zero price stays 0, and a platform with no priceStep keeps its cents. Six cases pinned in src/test/cross-post-setup.test.ts; 37 pass.

STILL UNCONFIRMED: whether this was the ONLY thing stopping the price. The render-time fallback (US-2736) had not reached production when the last attempt was made, so an empty payload is still a live candidate — the Listing price row in the Poshmark kit tab is what distinguishes them.

AC5's 'six cases pinned' WAS NOT COVERAGE, found 2026-08-21 by sabotage. The case list re-implemented the stepping expression inside cross-post-setup.test.ts and asserted against that copy; listing-kit.tsx was never called. Changing it to Math.floor - the exact thing AC4 exists to prevent, because flooring quietly costs the seller money on every cross-post - left all six cases green.

FIXED: stepPrice is exported from listing-kit.tsx and src/test/step-price.test.ts calls it. 7 tests. The mirror is deleted; the source scans that pin the CALL SITE stay, because where the stepping is applied is a real property worth holding, and they now point at the behavioural file.

MEASURED, with a green control asserted before the first sabotage: new test 4 of 4 caught, old source scan 4 of 4 MISSED. Sabotages were flooring instead of rounding, dropping the never-below-one-step floor, stepping every platform rather than only those declaring a step, and dropping the non-finite guard.

A REAL DEFECT CAME OUT OF WRITING THE TEST: an Infinity step produced NaN, because Math.round(price / Infinity) is 0 and 0 * Infinity is NaN - so a nonsense step turned a real price into NaN and put it on the row. stepPrice now returns the price untouched for any non-finite step or price.
AC6 REMAINS THE ONLY OPEN ITEM and it needs a live Poshmark form: whether the units were the ONLY thing stopping the price. Nothing in the code can answer that.

OPERATOR: publish one Poshmark listing through the extension and report whether the price lands. This is AC6/AC11 and it is the only item left. The units bug is fixed (whole dollars, rounded to nearest, never below one step) and so is the reason nobody saw the real failure: the deep probe skipped priceDialog entirely, because its walker only pushed STRING values off the flow config and priceDialog is an OBJECT - so every report saying the Poshmark list flow probes clean was true of nine selectors and blind to three, including the one selectors.js openly records as inferred rather than read off the page. What is unproven is whether the units were the ONLY thing stopping the price. If it still fails, the banner text distinguishes the cases: 'could not set the price' means the dialog never opened, and that is a selector, not a number.
userStories.notes:
2026-08-21, FROM A LIVE REPORT: the founder cross-posted one item to Poshmark on 2026-08-20 and THE PRICE WAS STILL EMPTY. So the whole-dollar units were not what was stopping it, and AC6 is answered in the unhelpful direction. Both price fixes ARE in the build that ran: 7d68e9ede (fill the dialog, not the form field) and 3677e2b1a (open the dialog before the photos) are both ancestors of the v0.10.0 release commit 92290ef9d.

READING THE PATH AGAIN FOUND TWO WAYS THE RUN CAN REPORT THE PRICE FILLED WHILE THE FIELD IS EMPTY. Neither is proven to be what happened - nothing here can see that page - but both are reachable, and a silent wrong success is the worst of the outcomes: the seller is told the price is set, looks at a blank Listing price, and has no reason to connect the two.

(1) THE ALREADY-OPEN CHECK COULD MATCH THE CREATE FORM. fillPriceDialog starts with querySelector(cfg.price) to avoid clicking an opener while a dialog is up - correct, and the backdrop hazard it guards is real. But Poshmark's cfg.price is '#listing-price-modal-listing-price-input, input[aria-label="Listing Price"]', and that second clause is unscoped. A create-form control carrying the same aria-label answers it with NO dialog open anywhere, so the check concludes 'already open', the modal is never opened, setValue writes into the opener - which does not hold the price - and the function returns true. FIXED: new GT.inPriceDialog gates the already-open match. The modal's own inputs are id-anchored and answer for themselves; anything else has to prove it by sitting inside [role=dialog] / [aria-modal=true] / .modal. When neither holds we fall through and click the opener, which is exactly what the function did before the already-open check existed, so the fix cannot make a run worse.

(2) setValue SETTING A VALUE IS NOT THE INPUT KEEPING IT. GT.setValue returns true unconditionally after dispatching input+change. A React-controlled input can reject the assignment and re-render its old contents. FIXED: the value is read back and compared, so a rejected write now reports unfilled and the seller gets the loud 'could NOT set the price' banner instead of a success line.

TESTS: two cases added to extension-unified/test/price-dialog.test.cjs (7 and 8), driving the REAL fillPriceDialog through a harness whose create-form control answers the aria-label clause, and through an input that rejects writes. Sabotage-checked 2 of 2 with a green control either side: reverting only the readback fails case 8, and making inPriceDialog accept any element fails case 7 with the price landing in the opener. The existing six cases still pass and all 40 extension test files pass.

STILL OPEN: which of the two it was, or whether it was neither. The distinguishing observation is the BANNER on the Poshmark page - 'including the price' means one of these two silent successes, 'could NOT set the price' means the dialog never opened and the cause is elsewhere.

ALSO FOUND, unrelated and now fixed: extension-unified/test/sync-poll.test.cjs failed on every Windows checkout. Its comment stripper split on '\n' and then ran //.*$ per line, and in JS a '.' never matches '\r' - so on CRLF the strip removed nothing and the guard failed on poll-plan.js's own header, which contains the words 'with no chrome.*'. sync-manifest and sync-observe already normalised CRLF first and carry a comment about the day the line endings changed; this copy was the one that missed it. Green on Linux CI, red on this box. | 2026-08-21, SECOND FINDING, and this one is measured rather than inferred. The founder confirmed the banner said 'could NOT set the price'. That is the honest branch: fillPriceDialog returned false, so the two silent successes fixed earlier today were NOT what happened, and - usefully - it also proves the WEB half is fine, because that banner only renders when payload.price is truthy. The price reached the extension. The dialog never opened.

THE PRICE DIALOG HAS NEVER BEEN PROBED, ON ANY RUN. selector-probe.js's list-flow walker pushed only STRING values off the flow config, and priceDialog is an OBJECT, so its three selectors were skipped in silence. Every deep report saying 'the Poshmark list flow probes clean' was true of nine selectors and blind to three - including priceDialog.open, which the selectors.js comment openly records as 'the one piece INFERRED rather than read off the page'. The single unmeasured selector in the flow is the one nothing was measuring, and it is the one the live run failed on.

FIXED: the list branch now walks a declared allowlist of nested groups (LIST_GROUPS = ['priceDialog']) and reports them under dotted keys, so a miss names its group. An allowlist rather than 'every object-valued key' on purpose - the platform config also carries delist and engage, which are their own flows on their own pages, and walking them into the create-page report buries it under thirteen expected misses. POST_INTERACTION gains priceDialog.price and priceDialog.originalPrice: those live inside the modal and cannot resolve until it opens, so scoring them as failures would hide the one line that matters. priceDialog.open is deliberately NOT excused - it is a create-page control, and excusing it would excuse the exact miss this exists to catch.

TESTS: a block in selector-probe.test.cjs pins all four properties. Sabotage-checked 4 of 4 with a green control either side: not walking groups at all, marking the opener post-interaction, un-marking the two modal inputs, and walking every object-valued key (which pulls in all thirteen delist/engage selectors). All 40 extension test files pass.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not fix the selector. It makes the selector ANSWERABLE. The next step is a deep probe run on the Poshmark sell page, which will now report priceDialog.open as found or missed and, on a miss, offer candidate controls - the same two-step that produced every correct Poshmark selector and that every guess made before it failed. Guessing a replacement from here would repeat the mistake the story's own notes record.

userStories.title: Predict the shipped parcel from the measurements we already took - the bulk margin floor prices postage at zero
userStories.description: As a reseller bulk-pricing drafts, I want the margin floor to account for postage, so that flooring 40 drafts at 30% margin does not silently set a loss on every heavy garment.
acceptanceCriteria: One pure, dependency-free module src/lib/parcel-estimate.ts turns an inventory item into a predicted parcel, mirrored BYTE-IDENTICAL to services/edge-functions/src/lib/parcel-estimate.ts because the edge cannot import from src/, with a guard test that fails the build if the copies drift. Copy the existing pattern exactly: src/lib/ebay-fees.ts and its test.

THE DEFECT THIS FIXES, and it is the reason to do it: autolister-bulk-edit.tsx:467 passes NO shipping to priceForMargin, so 'floor at 30% margin' across 40 drafts prices every one as if postage were free. On a wool coat that floor is a loss, applied in bulk, silently. The drafts list repeats it at :260 and :578, and the composer passes a hand-typed field that is usually null.

Three consumers read the predicted parcel: listing-profit.ts, the eBay publish path (which has never sent packageWeightAndSize), and the logistics rates route (where parseParcel reads a weight the seller retypes on every sale).

A jsonb column on sales records WHAT WAS PREDICTED, so it can be compared against what eBay actually charged. eBay's payout sync already writes the real cost to sales.shipping_cost, which is what makes the predicted-vs-actual loop cheap rather than a new pipeline.
PREDICT ONLY. Label buying already exists for eBay (US-2160); this story does not touch it.
Mirrored modules stay dependency-free - pure constants and pure functions only, so the file type-checks under both tsconfig and Deno. ASCII only in code.
The migration follows the US-1108 triple: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in the SAME commit, self-record footer, manifest regenerated. It is HELD from push until the owner applies it.

OPERATOR: read eBay's packageWeightAndSize field shape from a browser, or point at a vendored SDK type. That is the ONLY thing left. services/edge-functions/src/lib/ebay-client.ts InventoryItemPayload has no such field, so adding it means writing eBay's exact field names, nesting and unit enums - and developer.ebay.com has timed out six times across three sessions on five distinct URLs plus the edp.ebay.com mirror, while pe.usps.com answered four times in a single session. It is eBay's documentation specifically, not the network. Writing that shape from memory is what this story's own carrier-number discipline forbids, and a wrong eBay field name fails at PUBLISH rather than at compile - the expensive place, because the offer is already created by then. Everything else shipped: the estimator and its edge mirror, the pack model, USPS dimensional weight at the published 139 divisor (the design draft said 166, which is UPS/FedEx), the sourced rate table with both provenance guards, the shared margin rule, the bulk grid (the original defect), the logistics rates route, migrations 00649 and 00650 both applied, the prediction writer, and the per-item profit figure.
userStories.notes: FILED 2026-08-22 from work that already existed and was invisible.  The design spec was committed on 2026-08-21 (d23592dec, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-shipping-truth-design.md). A 55-task implementation plan was written alongside it and left UNTRACKED at docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-shipping-truth.md, with 0 of 55 tasks done. There was no story for any of it in prd.json or prd.archive.json, and src/lib/parcel-estimate.ts does not exist.  So a fully specified, fully planned piece of work sat in three states at once: spec in git, plan on disk only, story nowhere. A clean checkout would have kept the spec and lost the plan, and nothing in the backlog would have said the work was intended at all.  The plan file is committed in the same change as this story, so the two now travel together.  SCOPE NOTE: filed at the size the spec describes, not smaller. The plan's own global constraints are carried into the acceptance criteria because they are the parts most likely to be dropped - the byte-identical edge mirror with its drift guard, dependency-free mirrored modules, and ASCII-only code. | 2026-08-22 CHECKED THE OTHER FOUR SPECS, and this was the only orphan - recorded so nobody re-audits. docs/superpowers/specs/ holds five design documents. Four have story coverage: extension-sold-sync is US-2696 and its three observer children; grade-as-dispute-evidence is US-2703; autolister-visual-verification is covered across the US-1532 accuracy epic and the US-2778..2781 visual-pass work; style-code-discovery is covered from US-544 and US-1526 through the recent brand-first discovery crawl. Only shipping-truth had none, and it is also the only one whose PLAN was left untracked. Those two facts are probably the same event rather than two: the story and the plan were both the step after writing the spec, and the session ended between them. ⚠ THE FIRST SEARCH SAID THREE SPECS WERE ORPHANED. It matched the filename slug with hyphens turned to spaces, so 'extension sold sync' never matched a title reading 'extension sold-sync'. A crude matcher over-reporting orphans would have sent someone to file three duplicate stories, which is the more expensive direction of that error. | 2026-08-22 TASKS 1 AND 2 SHIPPED; TASK 3 IS SOURCED BUT NOT WRITTEN, deliberately.  Landed: src/lib/parcel-estimate.ts with its byte-identical edge mirror and drift guard, the weight model, pack selection, and USPS dimensional weight. 26 cases, ten sabotages all red with a green control either side, tsc/eslint/deno check/deno lint clean on both copies.  TWO CARRIER NUMBERS IN THE DESIGN WERE WRONG AND THE SOURCING STEP CAUGHT BOTH. The draft had DIM_DIVISOR = 166; USPS publishes 139 for both Priority (DMM 123) and Ground Advantage (DMM 283). 166 is the UPS/FedEx retail divisor. And the published rule rounds to whole POUNDS, rounded UP, which the draft omitted entirely - rounding in ounces under-reports by up to 15 oz. Both errors run in the direction that under-prices postage, which is the failure this story exists to fix.  ⚠ DIMENSIONAL WEIGHT NEVER ENGAGES AT THE CURRENT PACK SIZES, and this is pinned by a test rather than left to be discovered. box_medium is 16x12x8 = 1,536 cubic inches, under the 1,728 threshold, so every pack bills on actual weight. That is CORRECT for those sizes and it means the bulky-and-light case the spec names as where sellers lose the most is not yet covered. Closing it needs a pack size measured off a real box; inventing a bigger one to make the case fire would be fabricating a number in a directory whose whole rule is that numbers come from sources.  TASK 3 (the rate table) IS SOURCED, NOT CODED. docs/shipping/usps-rates-CONFIRMED.csv carries Ground Advantage retail bands read from USPS Notice 123, with the real effective date printed on the notice (July 12, 2026) - so RATE_EFFECTIVE_FROM will be a read date rather than an invented one. The CSV has a `confidence` column because the page is a dense multi-service table read through a summarising fetch: three cells were asked for twice in differently worded requests and agreed (Zone 4 at 1 lb and 2 lb, Zone 1&2 at 1 lb), the rest were read once. Bands above 5 lb, Priority Mail, and every other zone are UNREAD and absent rather than guessed.  Writing the rate table from single-read rows would put a plausible wrong number into pricing, which is precisely the failure src/lib/ebay-fee-schedule.ts already had once and the reason the sourcing rule exists. So the numbers are recorded and the code waits.  NEXT: cross-check the remaining bands, then Task 3's table, then the three consumers (listing-profit.ts, the eBay publish path, the logistics rates route) and the sales jsonb column. The migration is HELD from push per the standing rule. | 2026-08-22 THE DEFECT IS FIXED. Commit 97c8ee32d: the bulk margin floor reads a predicted parcel through the sourced USPS table instead of pricing postage at zero.  SHIPPED SO FAR: lib/parcel-estimate.ts (weight model, pack selection, USPS dimensional weight) with its byte-identical edge mirror; lib/shipping-rates.ts (eight Ground Advantage zone-4 bands, real effective date, band-edge nudge) with its mirror; lib/margin-floor.ts as the shared rule; and the bulk grid calling it. docs/shipping/ carries both CONFIRMED CSVs with URLs, dates and a per-row confidence column.  TWO GUARDS SHAPED THE FIX AND BOTH WERE RIGHT. The US-2520 shrink-only ratchet refused the inline version at 2038 lines against a 2010 ceiling, and its message says to extract rather than raise the number - correct twice, because three surfaces need this same figure and three copies of a pricing rule end up disagreeing. So margin-floor.ts exists and the item-attrs query moved to autolister/use-item-attrs.ts, leaving the page at 1970, below where it started. The US-2527 subprocessor guard flagged pe.usps.com; nothing calls it at runtime, so it is a stated exception with that reason.  THE REMAINING CONSUMERS, and what each actually needs:  1. item-card-list.tsx calls estimateListingProfit with price and costBasis and no shipping, so the profit shown per card omits postage. NOT WIRED, deliberately: ItemFullRow carries `measurements` but neither `garment_category` nor `material`, so the estimate would rest on a default base weight and one input. The spec's own words are that a precise-looking number derived from one input is a lie with a decimal point in it. This needs the row type and its query extended first, which is a change to whatever populates ItemFullRow rather than to this component.  2. The eBay publish path has never sent packageWeightAndSize. Edge-side, and the natural next one - the mirror already exists there.  3. The logistics rates route, where parseParcel reads a weight the seller retypes on every sale.  4. The sales jsonb column recording what was predicted, so it can be compared against what eBay actually charged. That is the migration, and it is HELD from push per the standing rule.  VERIFIED THIS PASS: 3898 web tests / 0 failures, tsc -b and eslint clean, deno check and deno lint clean on both mirrors. Sabotages: 10 on the estimator, 9 on the rate table (including both provenance guards - a CSV row demoted to single_read, and the CSV disagreeing with the table), all red with a green control either side. | 2026-08-22 CONSUMER 2 (the eBay publish path) IS BLOCKED ON THE SAME THING US-1980 IS. services/edge-functions/src/lib/ebay-client.ts InventoryItemPayload has no packageWeightAndSize field at all, so adding it means writing eBay's exact field names, nesting and unit enums. MEASURED 2026-08-22: developer.ebay.com timed out again at 60s (the sixth failure across three sessions and five distinct URLs plus the edp.ebay.com mirror). What is NEW is the control: pe.usps.com was fetched successfully FOUR times in the same session, including a dense multi-service rate table. So this is not a slow network or a blocked environment - it is eBay's developer documentation specifically. That narrows the conclusion from 'docs are unreliable here' to 'eBay's are unreachable and other carriers' are not', which is worth knowing before anyone spends another attempt. Writing that shape from memory is precisely what this story's own carrier-number discipline forbids, and an eBay payload that is wrong in a field name fails at publish rather than at compile - which is the expensive place. So it is not written. The unblock is one page read by a human, or the generated SDK type if one is already vendored. | 2026-08-22 CONSUMER 3 SHIPPED (commit f3ff38afe: the logistics rates route predicts the weight the seller was retyping). CONSUMER 1 IS BLOCKED ON A MIGRATION, and the reason is sharper than the earlier note guessed.  The earlier segment said item-card-list.tsx could not be wired because ItemFullRow carries neither garment_category nor material. That is true and it is not the whole reason. ItemFullRow is not a table row - it is the shape of the `items_full` VIEW, fetched with select("*"), and the view does not expose either column. 00506_items_full_quality_score.sql selects garment_category only INSIDE `coalesce(i.item_category::text, i.garment_category::text) as category`, and material not at all.  So adding the two fields to the TypeScript type would produce a type that LIES: declared present, undefined at runtime, on a shape six composer components already consume. Exposing them means changing the view, which is a migration - HELD from push per the standing rule, and holding one right now would block 86 verified commits behind it.  ⚠ AND A TRAP FOR WHOEVER WIRES IT: ItemFullRow.category is that coalesce, so it is item_category when one is set and garment_category otherwise. It is NOT the garment enum the estimator takes. Feeding it in would pass values like a merchandising category where a garment type is expected, and estimateParcel would fall through to the `other` base weight while reporting basis: ["category"] - a confident-looking number from a wrong input, which is the exact failure mode the spec names.  REMAINING ON THIS STORY, both needing a migration: expose garment_category and material on items_full so the card list can show honest per-item profit, and add the sales jsonb column recording what was predicted so it can be compared against what eBay actually charged. Consumer 2 (the eBay publish path) is blocked separately, on eBay's docs being unreachable.  WHAT IS DONE: the estimator, the pack model, USPS dimensional weight, the sourced rate table with both provenance guards, the shared margin rule, the bulk grid (the original defect), and the logistics route. 3898 web tests and 33 edge logistics cases green; sabotages 10 + 9 + 4 + 6 across the four commits, every one red with a green control either side. | ⚠ CORRECTION 2026-08-22, and prd-lint caught it rather than a reader: the previous segment put the word HELD in the same breath as migration 00506, and the guard reads that as claiming 00506 is held. IT IS NOT. 00506_items_full_quality_score.sql is applied and on origin/main; it is cited only as the file that DEFINES the items_full view and shows the view does not expose garment_category or material.  WHAT IS ACTUALLY HELD: nothing. The migration that would expose those columns has not been written. When it is, it will be held from push until the owner applies it - that is the standing rule, stated about a FUTURE file rather than about 00506.  Worth recording plainly: this is the same defect class this session spent the day finding - a stale HELD claim telling the next reader a branch is frozen when it is not - and I created one while documenting why they are expensive. The guard caught it in the same commit. That is the guard working exactly as designed, and it is a better outcome than my being careful would have been. | THE WARNING ABOVE IS A KNOWN FALSE POSITIVE ON THIS STORY, recorded so nobody chases it. prd-lint flags a story whose notes contain the uppercase marker near a migration that is already on origin/main. Both are true here for an innocent reason: 00506 is cited as the file that DEFINES the items_full view, and the marker appears in the sentences explaining that a FUTURE, unwritten migration would be held.  The check is keyed on PUSHED rather than on a version number precisely so an annotation explaining a fix cannot re-trigger it - the comment in scripts/prd-lint.mjs says so. That reasoning holds for a note naming a PENDING migration and does not cover one naming a pushed migration for an unrelated reason, which is this case. Its own history has the same shape: it once fired on the phrase SERVER-held facts, about trust boundaries.  NOT worth changing the guard for. It is a warning rather than an error, prd-lint exits OK, and loosening it to allow a pushed version number near the marker would take away the thing it is actually for. The cheap habit that avoids it: cite a migration by what it does rather than by number when the marker is anywhere nearby. | 2026-08-22 PROGRESS: five of the six pieces are in, and 00649 is APPLIED while 00650 is HELD.  SHIPPED AND PUSHED: lib/parcel-estimate.ts + its edge mirror (weight model, pack selection, USPS dimensional weight at the published 139 divisor, not the draft's 166); lib/shipping-rates.ts (eight cross-checked Ground Advantage bands, real effective date, both provenance guards); lib/margin-floor.ts; the bulk grid, which was the original defect; the logistics rates route, which no longer makes a seller retype a weight the system measured; and migration 00649 with the writer that records what was predicted beside what the carrier charges.  HELD, AWAITING THE OWNER: 00650_items_full_parcel_inputs.sql exposes garment_category and material on the items_full view. The type change and the item-card-list consumer land AFTER it applies, deliberately, so no client reads a column production does not have.  BLOCKED, NOT FORGOTTEN: the eBay publish path still never sends packageWeightAndSize. InventoryItemPayload has no such field and adding one means writing eBay's exact names, nesting and unit enums - developer.ebay.com has timed out six times across three sessions while pe.usps.com answered four times in one, so it is eBay specifically. Writing that shape from memory is what this story's own sourcing discipline forbids, and a wrong eBay field name fails at PUBLISH rather than at compile.  ⚠ ONE EXPORT IS BUILT WITH NO CONSUMER, recorded rather than wired: rateBreakWarning(billableOz) tells a seller they are a few ounces over a band edge and what trimming would save. The PLAN specifies it and tests it and never names a surface for it, so wiring it anywhere would be me making a product decision the design did not make. The bulk grid's existing toast is a batch-level signal and this is a per-row one, which is why it does not obviously belong there. It is covered by 6 cases and costs nothing to leave; whoever picks the surface should also decide whether it fires per row or as a summary.  VERIFIED THIS PASS: 37 edge logistics cases, 46 across the two lib suites, 3898 web tests at the last full run, deno check/lint and tsc -b clean, migrations-lint green at 646 migrations, and the held-migration gate correctly BLOCKING on 00650. | 2026-08-22 THE LIST PROJECTION CAUGHT A REAL BUG, recorded because the shape generalises to any future column on this view.  items_full is never read with select(*) on the list path - src/lib/item-list-columns.ts holds an explicit ITEM_LIST_COLUMNS, and use-items-full.test.ts asserts every ItemFullRow field appears either there or in ITEM_DETAIL_ONLY_COLUMNS. I added garment_category and material to the TYPE and to the VIEW and not to the projection.  THE CONSEQUENCE WOULD HAVE BEEN WORSE THAN A MISSING NUMBER. item-card-list.tsx is fed by the LIST read, so both fields would have arrived undefined on EVERY row. estimateParcel treats undefined like null, falls back to the `other` base weight, and STILL reports basis ["category"] - so every card would have shown a confident wrong figure rather than an absent one. That is the exact failure this story names about the coalesced `category` column, reached by a different route.  Both belong in the list rather than detail-only: the card list needs them, garment_category is an enum and material is a short text.  ⚠ THE METHOD FAILURE IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. My targeted run covered src/test, src/lib and src/components - the directories I thought I had touched. The guard lives in src/hooks. A full run caught it; a targeted one structurally could not. Same miss as the edge marketplace-specs mirror earlier today, and the same rule applies: for a change that touches a SHARED TYPE, the targeted run is the wrong instrument, because the consumers you have not thought of are exactly the ones at risk.  Full verify after the fix: 32 of 33 green with only this lane red before it, now 6,069 web tests passing. db skipped on the wedged Docker daemon (US-2788). | 2026-08-22 THE 'HELD' LANGUAGE IN THIS STORY IS STALE. RESOLVED. prd-lint has been warning about it on every run: a held migration is by definition unpushed, so the word tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not. Checked rather than assumed, and it is stale on BOTH counts. PUSHED: every migration this story names is on origin/main — verified with git cat-file against the remote ref, not inferred from a local log. APPLIED: PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md opens with 'HELD: none' and records everything through 00644 as applied, 00646 and 00647 applied and verified 2026-08-21, and 00650 applied and VERIFIED 2026-08-22 against the database itself — items_full reporting 63 columns in PostgREST's OpenAPI document with garment_category and material both present. THE TWO ARE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS AND THIS NOTE ANSWERS BOTH ON PURPOSE. 'Pushed is not applied' is the trap the migration process warns about, and a note that cleared only the first half would swap one wrong impression for another. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md remains the file that tracks applied state; this note is not a substitute for reading it. Nothing in this story is blocked on a push or an apply. | 2026-08-22 STATUS CORRECTION: every migration named in this story is on origin/main and applied to production. Nothing here is frozen. PUSHED: verified with git cat-file against the remote ref rather than inferred from a local log. APPLIED: PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md opens with a 'none outstanding' banner and records everything through 00644 as done, 00646 and 00647 verified 2026-08-21, and 00650 verified 2026-08-22 against the database itself — items_full reporting 63 columns in PostgREST's OpenAPI document with garment_category and material both present. BOTH QUESTIONS ANSWERED ON PURPOSE. Pushed is not applied, and a correction clearing only the first half would swap one wrong impression for another. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md stays the file that tracks applied state; this is not a substitute for reading it. ⚠ THE SEGMENT I APPENDED JUST BEFORE THIS ONE MADE THE WARNING WORSE, and the reason is worth more than the fix. It said the same thing in my own words, so it matched none of prd-lint's three correction phrases while itself containing the trigger word beside a list of migration numbers — the guard read it as a fresh claim and the warning grew. A correction has to speak the detector's vocabulary, and reading the detector first would have cost thirty seconds. | 2026-08-22 AC8 IS ANSWERED. The field shape is sourced, from two independent generations of eBay's own OpenAPI contract, and written down here so nobody spends an eighth attempt on developer.ebay.com.  EBAY'S DOCS FAILED AGAIN - seventh timeout at 60s, consistent with the five recorded before it. AC8 offers an alternative in its own words ('or point at a vendored SDK type'), and the repo has no vendored eBay SDK: grepped the whole tree for packageWeightAndSize and the only hits are our own spec, our own plan and prd.json. src/lib/ebay-aspect-registry.json is aspects, not payload types. So the shape came from generated clients instead.  THE SHAPE, wire names as they appear in the JSON body:   packageWeightAndSize: {     dimensions?: { height: number, length: number, width: number, unit: string },     weight?:     { value: number, unit: string },     packageType?: string,        // PackageTypeEnum     shippingIrregular?: boolean, // will not go through a stamping machine   }   dimension unit: INCH or FEET (English), CENTIMETER or METER (metric)   weight unit:    POUND or OUNCE (English), KILOGRAM or GRAM (metric)   Both unit AND value are required whenever the weight container is present;   same for dimensions. A partial container is an error, not a default.  PROVENANCE, because a shape this specific is worthless without it:   1. zVPS/ebay-sell-inventory-php-client docs/Model/{PackageWeightAndSize,      Dimension,Weight}.md - OpenAPI-Generator output from eBay's spec. Gave the      three containers, the sub-model fields, and the unit enums.   2. api-evangelist/ebay json-schema/ebay-packageweightandsize-schema.json - an      independent JSON Schema rendering. Confirmed the wire names are camelCase      and ADDED shippingIrregular, which source 1 does not list.   The two agree on dimensions/weight/packageType. That agreement is the reason   to trust this over anything written from memory, which is what the earlier   segment warned against.  TWO CAVEATS, stated rather than smoothed over:   - Source 1 is a PHP client, so its property names are snake_cased by the     generator (package_type). The WIRE names are camelCase; source 2 is what     settles that, and every field this repo already sends on this payload     (shipToLocationAvailability, conditionDescription) is camelCase too.   - eBay's own prose has a copy-paste error that survives into both     generations: the DIMENSION unit description says 'the applicable values for     WEIGHT units are METER and CENTIMETER'. Those are dimension units. Recorded     so the next reader does not take it as a sign the source is unreliable.  STILL NOT IMPLEMENTED, deliberately. This unblocks AC3's consumer 2 (the eBay publish path) rather than shipping it. ebay-client.ts InventoryItemPayload still has no packageWeightAndSize field. Adding it writes to the LIVE publish body, where a wrong shape turns into a publish failure on a seller's listing, and the shape - however well cross-checked - comes from generated clients rather than from eBay. Worth one verification against a real sandbox PUT before it goes out, which is a smaller and much more decisive operator task than reading the docs.  Everything else in this story is shipped and applied; see the segments above.

userStories.title: US-826 closed with AC1 unmet: the attribute confirm chips exist and no screen presents them
userStories.description: As a seller running AI extract on my phone, I want to confirm department, size type, vintage and condition tier in one tap, so that the eBay aspects the AI can only infer are right before they reach a listing.
acceptanceCriteria: AIExtractView (or whichever screen owns the post-extract step) presents AIAttributeConfirmView. Today ios/GradeThread/AIExtract/AIAttributeConfirmView.swift is mentioned exactly once in the whole repo - its own declaration - so nothing constructs it and no seller has ever seen it.

All four fields are offered pre-selected, which is what US-826 AC1 asked for and is NOT what ships today. AIFillReviewSheet.swift:401-402 does route attribute-bound fields through AIAttributeConfirm.Result, but only for entries the AI returned as LOW CONFIDENCE conflicts. A confident wrong department is never shown to anyone.

The view's own doc comment describes the wiring that is missing - 'Confirming hands the user's choices back to AIExtractView which persists them to inventory_items.attributes with ai_field_sources provenance'. Either make that sentence true or delete the file; it must not stay as a description of code that does not exist.

AIExtractView carries a .confirmationDialog today and no .sheet. Check ios/Scripts/check-chained-sheets.py before adding one - two sheet modifiers on one view is a known trap in this repo and the loser opens and closes in the same frame.

scripts/check-ios-orphans.mjs stops listing AIAttributeConfirmView, and its ALLOWED entry is deleted in the same commit. That check fails on a stale entry precisely so a fix cannot leave the reason behind.

OPERATOR: needs a macOS toolchain to compile and a device or simulator to judge. This is a screen, and a screen written blind is where an agent ships something that compiles and looks wrong. The iOS CI lane is the compile gate, not the design gate.

userStories.title: Live Capture and Verified 360 cannot be earned: no client sends the opt-in
userStories.description:
MEASURED 2026-08-22, not inferred. routes/grade.ts is the ONLY writer of submissions.live_capture_opt_in, verified_360_opt_in and capture_360, and it reads all three off the multipart form. Nothing on web, iOS, Android or the extension appends any of them. A repo-wide search for liveCapture / live_capture / LiveVerified returns 13 files and NONE is a .swift or .kt.

THE CONTRAST IS THE PROOF, and it sits on adjacent lines of the same insert. verified_capture_opt_in (grade.ts:839) IS fed — new-submission.tsx holds it in state and posts it. The three lines below it (840-842) are fed by nothing.

evaluateLiveCapture (verified-capture.ts:330) opens with a hard gate: if the opt-in is false it returns immediately with reasons ['not opted into Live Capture']. So EVERY submission takes that branch and the `live_verified` badge — described in the pipeline as "the strongest provenance tier" — has never been issued. Its confidence boost has never applied.

There is a SECOND gate behind the first, also unfed: the badge additionally requires every image's capture_source to be the in-app value, which grade.ts reads from the `capture_sources` form field (grade.ts:472). Nothing sends that either.

certificate.tsx renders the badge on both branches (:1220 earned, :1240 not earned), so the display half was built and only ever shows the second one.

⚠ NOT THE SAME AS THE VIDEO TIER, which works. video_live_capture_verified (certificate.tsx:1200) belongs to the US-1762 walk-around clip, and video-walkaround.tsx really does set IN_APP_VIDEO_CAPTURE_SOURCE. The PHOTO live-capture tier is the unreachable one; naming them apart matters because the working one makes the broken one look wired.

US-1283 (archived, passes:true) is the story that owns this. Its AC1 asks for "a capture mode that accepts ONLY in-app camera images" and its AC4 for "clear UX explaining the value". Neither exists. Its note carries no evidence trail — it is the text from the day it was FILED, so nothing records what was checked at close.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide the scope first: this is a capture MODE with fraud claims attached, not a checkbox. Confirm which client ships it (the web camera dialog exists; iOS and Android have no live-capture concept at all) and whether device attestation is in scope or the in-app capture_source is the claim.
The chosen client posts live_capture_opt_in AND a capture_sources value per image, since the badge needs both and either alone earns nothing.
The same decision is made for verified_360_opt_in and capture_360, which are unfed in exactly the same way and were found in the same sweep.
A submission that does not opt in behaves byte-identically to today, which it already does — the point is that this stays true.
US-1283's closure is corrected: either its remaining ACs move here, or a note records what was actually shipped versus what its ACs asked for.
The guard added alongside this (scripts/check-unfed-form-fields.mjs) drops these fields from its allowlist when they are genuinely fed.
userStories.notes:
2026-08-22 RE-VERIFIED BY A SECOND METHOD, because the original finding rested on a text search and a filed story should not. iOS has a CANONICAL FIELD LIST for a photo grade submission — PhotoGradeFields in Grading/PhotoGradeUploader.swift, enumerated in one place and consumed by the multipart writer in PhotoGradeSubmit.swift, which interpolates whatever that list yields. It is exactly ten fields: authenticity_addon, brand, closet_item_id, description, garment_category, garment_type, inventory_item_id, tier, title, verified_capture_opt_in. That is a structural answer rather than a search result: there is no other way for iOS to add a form field to this request. Per-field count of CLIENT files naming each as a quoted form-field string, across src/ ios/ android/, tests excluded: live_capture_opt_in 0 verified_360_opt_in 0 capture_360 0 capture_sources 0 style_attributes 0 verified_capture_opt_in 4 The last row is the control and it is what makes the other five meaningful: the same search, the same corpus, the sibling field on the adjacent line of the same insert, and it finds four files. Web posts it at new-submission.tsx:876 and iOS carries it in the list above. ⚠ ONE CORRECTION TO MY OWN EVIDENCE. An earlier pass extracted the web's field list by matching `.append(` on a single line and concluded the web does not send verified_capture_opt_in. That was wrong: the call spans two lines with the name on its own. The extraction was incomplete, not the code, and the story text was right for a reason I had not actually established at the time. | 2026-08-22 SCOPE DECIDED BY THE OWNER, WEB HALF SHIPPED. Commit 51fb04af1. AC1 asked which client ships this; the owner's answer is all three (web, iOS, Android). Web is done and verified; the two native halves remain and this story stays open for them.  WHAT SHIPPED. src/lib/photo-capture-contract.ts is the written-down handshake, modelled on video-grading-contract.ts and for a sharper reason: that one had ONE client speaking it inline, this one had ZERO, so all three clients would otherwise have reverse-engineered the same strings out of grade.ts. PhotoUploadItem gains a required captureSource; the camera dialog call site in photo-upload.tsx is the ONLY place that may claim in-app capture and every other path (picker, drag-drop, US-952 seeding) defaults to library. new-submission.tsx sends both the opt-in and the per-image array, satisfying AC2 - the badge needs both and either alone earns nothing.  AC2's opt-in is DERIVED, not a checkbox, which is a deliberate reading of the AC rather than a shortcut. 'Every photo was taken live in the app' is a fact about how the seller shot them. Deriving it also makes it impossible to send the one combination grade.ts:546 rejects (opted in with a library photo), so no seller meets a submit-time error for a box they were invited to tick. AC4 holds: a submission that does not qualify sends neither field and is byte-identical to today.  TWO DEFECTS FOUND WHILE WIRING IT. Either would have shipped a tier that still could not be earned, which is why they are recorded rather than just fixed.   1. A camera capture is a canvas.toBlob JPEG with NO EXIF. provenanceAvailable      demands device+timestamp metadata on EVERY photo, so a seller who shot      everything in-app failed it and got the Verified Capture control      DISABLED, while a seller uploading library files with intact metadata got      it enabled. The stronger evidence was treated as the weaker one. Worse,      the disabled-state copy already promised 'available when photos are taken      in-app'. Gate is now provenanceAvailable OR all-in-app.   2. Declaring the 360 constants in the contract module DISARMED      check-unfed-form-fields.mjs on those two fields: it decides a field is fed      by finding its bare name under src/ outside tests, quotes not required,      and its own header admits it cannot tell a mention from an append. Prose      that merely spelled the names did it too. Both mistakes were made here      before the comment warning about them was written. This is mode 7 of the      guards-that-do-not-guard family, twice in one file.  AC6 PARTLY DONE: the allowlist is down from 6 entries to 4. The two wired fields dropped out, which is the shrink-only list working.  AC3 HAS A REAL ANSWER FOR WEB AND IT IS 'CANNOT': verified-360.ts scores photogrammetric/LiDAR coverage metrics that a BROWSER has no sensor for. Web has nothing honest to send, so those two stay unfed and keep their allowlist entries with that reason recorded. They are the iOS/Android half's to answer.  OWNER CAVEAT, FLAGGED NOT BURIED. The removed on-page copy carried a real prior decision from US-1283: web should not offer Live Capture because a browser 'cannot truly attest'. That is right about hardware attestation - getUserMedia has no Secure Enclave or Play Integrity signature, and a virtual camera device can feed it. It is app-OBSERVED capture, not device-attested: genuinely stronger than a file upload, since the seller cannot substitute a stored image through that path, but weaker than what a native client will provide. The server has ONE badge and one in-app source value, so web capture currently earns the same live_verified as a native capture will. If the owner wants those distinguished, that is a server-side policy change (a second capture-source value, or a tier on the badge) and should be decided before the native halves land rather than after.  ALSO WORTH KNOWING: the copy this replaced told sellers to 'grade in the GradeThread app with Live Capture'. The app had not built it either, so the promise was false twice over - the page advertised a tier no surface could earn and pointed at a surface that did not implement it.  VERIFIED: 6157 web tests pass / 0 failed across 503 files, 12 of them new. Eight sabotage mutations, each confirmed applied and each red, with a green control before and after - camera site un-claimed, both provenance defaults flipped to fail OPEN, source string drifted from the server's, empty photo set made vacuously live, every->some, capture_sources dropped, opt-in gate narrowed back to EXIF-only. tsc -b clean, eslint clean (one pre-existing react-refresh warning on assignSlotKeys), ui:check 0 blocking.  STILL OPEN: the iOS half (PhotoGradeFields in Grading/PhotoGradeUploader.swift is the canonical ten-field list and is where the two new fields go), the Android half, AC3's 360 answer on both, and AC5's correction of US-1283's closure. | 2026-08-22 THE NATIVE HALF IS BLOCKED, and not on effort - there is no native surface to add Live Capture TO. Traced before writing any Swift, which is the useful part: the obvious move was to append two fields to PhotoGradeFields and call it the iOS half, and that would have been unreachable code on top of unreachable code.  WHAT LIVE CAPTURE NEEDS is a client that posts image BYTES to POST /api/grade/submit, because capture_sources is a multipart field read by routes/grade.ts and capture_source is a column on submission_images (migration 00314). NEITHER PHONE HAS SUCH A CLIENT IN USE.  iOS has one and nothing mounts it. ios/GradeThread/Grading/ holds a complete consumer photo-grade client - PhotoGradeUploader (multipart writer, PhotoGradeImage, the ten-field PhotoGradeFields list, seller-facing error copy), PhotoGradeSubmit posting to /api/grade/submit, PhotoGradeStatus, ConsumerGradeFlow orchestrating submit -> pay -> poll. All 12 references to ConsumerGradeFlow in the repo are in ConsumerGradeFlowTests.swift, and PhotoGradeImage is only ever constructed by tests. No view calls start(images:request:).  Android has nothing of the kind: grading/GradingService.kt knows only the three /api/flipdesk/grading paths.  WHAT IS ACTUALLY WIRED on both phones is the FlipDesk route. CertifiedGradeSection -> GradeRequestSheet -> GradeRequestStore -> GradingService posts JSON to /api/flipdesk/grading/submit against an inventory item whose photos are already uploaded. It sends no image bytes, and flipdesk-grading.ts has no capture-provenance concept at all - grepped for capture_source, live_capture and verified_capture, zero hits. item_photos also has no capture_source column; only submission_images does.  SO THE OWNER'S 'all three clients' ANSWER STANDS but costs more than it looked like, and splits into a choice that is US-2815's to make:   (a) Mount the orphaned iOS flow and build the Android equivalent, then this       story's native half is the small wiring job it was assumed to be.   (b) Keep native grading on the FlipDesk route and carry provenance there       instead. That needs a capture_source column on item_photos (a MIGRATION,       so it is owner-gated and PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md applies) plus       flipdesk-grading passing it into the grading pipeline the way       routes/grade.ts does. Recommend deciding US-2815 first. Doing (b) blind would add a column to a table on the guess that native grading stays where it is.  AC3's 360 half is blocked behind the same wall for the same reason, on top of needing sensors.  The WEB half remains shipped and verified (see the previous segment, commit 51fb04af1). Nothing here changes it. | 2026-08-23 THE ANDROID HALF IS SHIPPED. Commit 97797cd63. The block recorded in the previous segment is gone: US-2815 chose option (a), both phones now have a client that posts image BYTES to POST /api/grade/submit, and Live Capture had something to attach to.  WHAT SHIPPED ON ANDROID. PhotoGradeContract gains IN_APP_CAPTURE_SOURCE, LIBRARY_CAPTURE_SOURCE, the two field names and qualifiesForLiveCapture. PhotoGradeImage carries a captureSource and the uploader appends capture_sources in the same interleaved loop as images and image_types, so the three arrays stay positionally aligned. GradeCameraSheet is the in-app camera; ConsumerGradeScreen offers Take and Library per slot and says which side of the line the submission is on.  THE OPT-IN IS DERIVED, matching the web half deliberately rather than by copying: it is a fact about how the photos were shot, and deriving it makes the one combination grade.ts:546 rejects unsendable. Three defaults fail closed - an unrecorded origin reads as library, an empty set is not live (Collection.all is vacuously true on one), and a library pick overwrites an earlier camera source for that slot.  TWO OF NINE MUTATIONS SURVIVED THE FIRST SABOTAGE RUN and the serious one is worth carrying to the iOS half. Changing IN_APP_CAPTURE_SOURCE to the video tier's string left every Kotlin test green, because they all referenced the constant symbolically and followed the drift. The server compares against its own literal, so the whole tier would have earned nothing with no error anywhere - the exact failure this story is about, reintroduced by the fix for it. Now pinned in src/test/native-photo-grade-contract-parity.test.ts, which reads the value out of verified-capture.ts. The second was the file-scoped-assertion shape this session has hit five times: the addShot check was satisfied by submit()'s own LIBRARY_CAPTURE_SOURCE fallback further down.  ALSO FIXED WHILE THERE: the camera path left both the raw CameraX file and the PhotoProcessor output in filesDir forever. The draft holds the bytes, nothing else visits that directory, so every retake cost two full-size JPEGs of storage the person never gets back.  VERIFIED: spotless, detekt and unit tests green; 12 mutations across the contract, uploader, view model and camera sheet, each confirmed applied and each red with a green control either side; the full web suite 2708 passed.  STILL OPEN: the iOS camera path (ConsumerGradeView has the library picker only), AC3's 360 answer on both phones, AC5's correction of US-1283's closure, and AC6's remaining allowlist entries. | 2026-08-23 THE IOS HALF IS SHIPPED AND AC5 IS DONE. Commit dcb2a1e8f. Live Capture is now earnable on all three surfaces the owner named: web 51fb04af1, Android 97797cd63, iOS dcb2a1e8f. AC2 and AC4 hold on every one of them.  iOS carries the same three fail-closed defaults as Android, and one of them needed a Swift-specific fix worth recording: PhotoGradeImage.captureSource is written as an explicit init rather than an inline default, because a `let` property with an inline default is OMITTED from Swift's synthesised memberwise initializer entirely - callers could not have set it at all, and every existing test would have kept compiling.  ONE SHEET SLOT, NOT TWO. ConsumerGradeView already had a .sheet for the library picker, so the camera shares it through .sheet(item:) switching on how the slot was opened. Two .sheet modifiers on one view compete and the loser opens and closes in the same frame; check-chained-sheets.py exists because twelve views in this app were doing that.  CameraPicker was reused rather than hand-rolled - UIImagePickerController, already used by three other screens, with isSourceTypeAvailable(.camera) guarded at the call site as its own header asks. US-2815's lesson was that an API with no sibling in this codebase is unverifiable without a toolchain, and there is none here.  AC5 IS DONE: US-1283's closure is corrected in prd.archive.json rather than left. That story was marked passes:true while its badge had never been issued once, and its notes were still the text from the day it was filed. The correction records what was actually true at close, what US-2802 shipped against each of its ACs, and the two that are still not met - it asked for DEVICE-ATTESTED and timestamped capture, and what ships is app-OBSERVED capture with no attestation and no capture time.  THAT GAP IS NOW US-2831, filed rather than absorbed. Web, iOS and Android all earn the SAME live_verified badge from one in-app source value, and a browser cannot attest while a phone can. This story's own earlier note said that decision should be made BEFORE the native halves landed; they have landed, so it is due.  VERIFIED: eleven iOS/Android source guards pass including the one-sheet and no-raw-jpeg gates; unfed-form-fields 4 accounted for; tsc -b clean; 2710 web tests pass. Three mutations on the Swift pins, each applied and each red with a green control either side. SWIFT IS NOT COMPILED HERE - every symbol was checked against its declaration, and two that would not have compiled were caught that way: a key path to a tuple element (\.0 is not addressable) and a two-element zip splatting into two closure parameters. iOS CI is the real check.  STILL OPEN: AC3 ONLY. verified_360_opt_in and capture_360 remain unfed on both phones. Web has a real answer and it is 'cannot' - verified-360.ts scores photogrammetric and LiDAR coverage a browser has no sensor for - and the native answer is a genuine feature (ARCore / LiDAR depth capture) rather than the wiring job Live Capture turned out to be. AC6's allowlist is correspondingly still at 4 entries. | 2026-08-23 AC3's DECISION IS RECORDED AND NOW ENFORCED. Commit 5b4ceb55d. AC3 still
does not close, and the reason is a feature investment rather than a missing
answer.

AC3 asks that 'the same decision is made' for verified_360_opt_in and
capture_360. Half of it was already made and written down in the right place:
scripts/check-unfed-form-fields.mjs's allowlist says web CANNOT feed these -
verified-360.ts scores photogrammetric and LiDAR coverage a browser has no
sensor to measure, so there is nothing honest for it to send. That is a real
decision, not a deferral.

The half that is NOT decided is whether to BUILD the native side (ARCore depth /
LiDAR capture). That is a feature investment and it is yours, not something an
agent should settle in a note. Nothing is blocked by it: no submission earns the
badge, and no surface claims one.

WHAT I CHECKED BEFORE CONCLUDING THAT, because 'nobody can earn it' and
'somebody is promised it' are very different problems:
  - src/pages/certificate.tsx:1172 renders verified_360_badge CONDITIONALLY.
  - functions/cert/[id].ts:260 does the same in the edge-SSR'd certificate.
  - No marketing page, no SEO copy and no seller-facing page mentions 360 at
    all. Grepped src/pages/marketing, src/lib/seo and new-submission.tsx.
So the product is honest today. NOTHING HELD IT THAT WAY, which is what this
commit fixes.

SHIPPED: src/test/badge-claims-match-capability.test.ts, four cases. The rule
writes itself because the capability is already recorded precisely - a field on
the unfed allowlist has never arrived in production - so: advertise the badge,
or leave the field unfed, but not both. It holds BOTH directions, which is what
makes it a coupling rather than a ban: Verified 360 unfed and therefore
unadvertised, Live Capture fed and therefore fairly advertised, with the
disappearance of the seller copy treated as a regression too.

Scoped to surfaces that PROMISE - the marketing tree, the SEO registry, and the
pre-capture seller copy where the choice is made. A certificate rendering the

THE ALLOWLIST MOVED to scripts/lib/unfed-form-fields.mjs. Importing the guard
script killed the test outright: its top level walks five source trees and ends
in process.exit, so vitest died with 'process.exit unexpectedly called with 0'
before an assertion ran. Restructuring a working guard to suit an importer is
the wrong trade, so the data moved instead.

SABOTAGE FOUND THE GUARD READING A FUNCTION NAME AS A PROMISE. Deleting the
actual seller copy left it GREEN, because the live pattern was
/live[\s-]?verified|live[\s-]?capture/ and the second alternative matches the
IDENTIFIER qualifiesForLiveCapture - imported on line 54 of new-submission.tsx
and called on line 933. A promise is something a person can read; an identifier
is not, and matching it meant the check could never tell copy from plumbing. The
patterns are badge NAMES now.

VERIFIED: 6445 web tests pass, tsc -b + eslint clean, unfed-fields 4 accounted
for. Six mutations, each confirmed applied, each red, green controls either
side. One green ON PURPOSE and asserted as such: a COMMENT saying Verified 360
is unbuilt must not count as advertising it. Three mutations did not apply on

STILL OPEN: AC3, on whether to build native depth capture. AC6's allowlist stays
at 4 entries, correctly. | 2026-08-23 STATUS CORRECTION. No migration on US-2802 is held. Migration 00314
is long since on origin/main, and prd-lint paired it with the uppercase word
HELD in my previous segment - which was the phrase 'NOTHING HELD IT THAT WAY',
about the badge claim being unguarded, not about a migration. The check is right
