  AC4 the full suite, the screenshot lane and a REAL-DEVICE smoke pass before committing. This is the gate. The story names a Compose BOM jump as a visual risk and it is right: 2025.04 -> 2026.08 is sixteen months of Material 3, and the screenshot lane is advisory (US-2902), so nothing here would catch a layout change automatically.
  AC5 a recurring check so this cannot drift another year.
  AC6 re-check the Data safety form after the upgrade - an SDK that starts collecting an advertising id changes the declaration.

A NOTE ON THE UPGRADE PATH ITSELF, found while running the report: dependencyUpdates emits three configuration-cache problems from the plugin, and Gradle warns the build 'is incompatible with Gradle 9.0'. Gradle 9.7.1 is on the list above, so the toolchain jump and the dependency jump are the same piece of work, not two. | 2026-08-29 ⚠ AC4 ASSESSMENT CORRECTION. No dependency was touched; this changes
how risky the upgrade is, which is the thing that was written down wrong.

The previous segment says: "the screenshot lane is advisory (US-2902), so
nothing here would catch a layout change automatically". That was true when
written and is not true now. The Roborazzi lane is BLOCKING as of 2026-08-29 in
both android-ci.yml and the verify android lane, and it has grown from 7 goldens
to 11 - the 7 ui/components primitives plus 4 whole screens (lock and tools,
light and dark).

So a Compose BOM jump of 2025.04 -> 2026.08 now fails the build on a visual
change rather than passing quietly. That is the single largest reason AC4 read
as dangerous, and it is answered for anything the 11 goldens cover.

WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT COVER, so nobody over-reads this: 49 of the app's 52
screens take a ViewModel and have no golden, because covering them needs a
stateless XScreenContent extracted from each (US-2902 AC3, open). A BOM jump
that changes padding on the publish screen or the grade report is still
invisible to CI. The real-device smoke pass AC4 asks for is therefore still the
gate - it is just no longer the ONLY thing standing between a BOM jump and a
shipped layout regression.

Also worth knowing before the upgrade: the instrumented lane went from red-and-
invisible to 8 tests / 0 failures on the same day (US-2902), so
connectedDebugAndroidTest is now a usable signal on an upgraded dependency set
instead of noise. RoomMigrationTest in particular had never once executed, which
matters here because a Room version bump is exactly the kind of thing a
dependency sweep carries. | 2026-08-29 AC5 SHIPPED, and building it found a real defect on the release
lane. AC1 was already done; AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC6 remain.

AC5 asked for a recurring check so the dependency set cannot drift another
year. .github/workflows/android-dependency-drift.yml runs monthly (and on
dispatch), and scripts/ops/android-dependency-drift.mjs turns the report into a
labelled GitHub issue - updated in place, and CLOSED by the script when nothing
is behind, so its existence is the signal.

IT REPORTS AND DOES NOT FAIL, which is the one design decision worth arguing.
The outdated COUNT moves when Google publishes, not when we change code. A gate
on it goes red on a Tuesday because androidx shipped, nobody did anything wrong,
and inside a month it is the check everyone force-merges past. This repo has the
scar twice over: a screenshot step red for four days behind continue-on-error
and an emulator job red for months. An issue is a thing in a list a person
already looks at; a job summary is a thing nobody opens.

MEASURED ON THIS HOST, so AC1's report is now reproducible rather than a
one-off attachment: 86 of 100 behind, 14 current, 16 at least one major behind.
Gradle 8.13 -> 9.7.1. The majors are billing-ktx 7.1.1 -> 9.1.0 (TWO, which
independently confirms the correction on US-2901), compose-bom 2025.04 ->
2026.08, AGP 8.13.2 -> 9.3.2, nine com.android.tools.utp artifacts 31 -> 32,
spotless 7 -> 8, firebase-bom 33 -> 34, okhttp + mockwebserver 4.12 -> 5.5, and
sentry-android 7.22 -> 8.54.

android/build.gradle.kts gained outputFormatter = "json,plain" - the json is
what the script reads, the plain copy stays because that is what a person opens.

⚠ AND WIDENING THE ENV GUARD FOUND A REAL BUG ON THE RELEASE LANE. Adding a
second workflow that runs ./gradlew showed that
src/test/android-ci-env-parity.test.ts read ONE file - which reproduced the
exact defect it exists for. Pointed at the whole workflow directory it reported
android-release.yml:instrumented, and that one is real: the job named 'App
launches and migrations run (emulator)' carried no SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and no
shell assertion for it, so the app would die in Application.onCreate before a
single test body ran. That is the gate before a Play upload. Fixed with the same
block android-ci.yml carries.

The same widening produced a FALSE positive on android-release.yml:release,
which is worth recording because the fix shapes the rule: that job carries no
placeholder because it must not - it injects the REAL key and asserts on it in
shell, and a release built with a throwaway would ship an app that crashes on
launch for every user. So the guard now tests 'the key is available' by either
route, derived. An exclusion list naming the release workflow would have worked
today and rotted at the third lane.

VERIFIED: the drift script runs clean against a real report; both workflows
parse; 13/13 across android-ci-env-parity, android-guard-lane and
guard-lane-parity; tsc -b and eslint clean.

STILL OPEN: AC2 (upgrade-or-justify each of the 86, reasons next to the pin),
AC3 (lintRelease with checkDependencies and every Play SDK Index finding
resolved - note US-2912 measured ZERO SDK Index findings in the current lint
baseline), AC4 (full suite + screenshot lane + real-device smoke; the screenshot
half is now a blocking gate), AC6 (re-check the Data safety form after the
upgrade). | 2026-08-29 AC2 IS HALF DONE, and it is the half that can be done without a
device. Every one of the 16 majors now carries a written reason beside its pin
in libs.versions.toml, in the idiom that file already used for
security-crypto. No version was moved.

WHY HALF. AC2 reads "either upgraded or has a written reason for staying". The
upgrade half is gated on AC4's real-device smoke pass, which cannot be done from
this host. The reason half is what stops the next reader seeing 86 stale pins
and concluding neglect - they are decisions now, with the work each one implies
written down.

GROUPED BY THE WORK RATHER THAN BY THE PACKAGE, which is the useful part:
  AGP + Gradle + the nine com.android.tools.utp artefacts + spotless are ONE
  job, not four. dependencyUpdates already emits configuration-cache problems
  and Gradle warns this build "is incompatible with Gradle 9.0", so the
  toolchain has prerequisite work before any of those four pins move.
  compose-bom is the visual risk: sixteen months of Material 3. The screenshot
  lane blocks now and covers 11 goldens; 49 of 52 screens have none, so this is

  billing carries a DEADLINE the others do not - Play enforces a floor - and is

  spotless is wider than it looks because of the ratchet: touching an old .kt

⚠ THE 86-ITEM LIST IS DELIBERATELY NOT COPIED INTO THE FILE. It moves when
Google publishes, not when this repo changes, so a copy would be stale inside a
week and would then read as current - the same failure mode as a PENDING

AND THE MINORS GET NO INDIVIDUAL REASON, on purpose. They are held by ONE
decision - AC4's gate - rather than by seventy. Writing seventy identical

userStories.title: Eight Compose files sit outside the localization guard, and the guard cannot tell
userStories.description: scripts/no-bare-strings.py enforces string extraction over an explicit SCOPE list, and the header is honest about it: 'SCOPE IS DELIBERATE AND PARTIAL ... it grows as more are [converted], and a file inside the scope can never regress.' That was the right way to do a staged migration across ~90 files.  The migration is now eight files from finished. 106 files in the tree contain @Composable; 98 are in scope. The remainder: billing/ConsumerCreditPackSheet.kt, grading/ConsumerGradeScreen.kt, grading/GradeCameraSheet.kt, inventory/SourcedByPicker.kt, measure/MeasurementPhotoEditorSheet.kt, settings/TwoFactorDialog.kt, sync/PersistenceHealthHost.kt, sync/SyncStatusHost.kt.  THE LIST IS NOT RANDOM AND THAT IS THE PROBLEM. It includes the consumer grading flow, the credit-pack purchase sheet, the two-factor dialog and the sync-status host - a purchase surface, a security surface, and the thing that tells the seller their data is not saving. Spanish is otherwise complete (1460 strings in both values/ and values-es/), so a Spanish-speaking seller gets a fully translated app right up until they hit one of these eight, at which point the credit-pack sheet or the 2FA dialog comes back in English.  AND A NEW FILE IS OUT OF SCOPE BY DEFAULT. The guard passes on a file nobody added to the list, which is the same silence a clean tree produces. That is the shape this repo has been bitten by before - a guard reporting nothing reads exactly like a guard finding nothing.  US-2499 covers the iOS half of this and the guard's migration framing; this is the Android half, which is small and finishable.
acceptanceCriteria: All eight files have their user-visible strings extracted to strings.xml with Spanish translations, and are added to SCOPE.

SCOPE is inverted: the guard covers every file containing @Composable by default, with an explicit, named, reasoned exclusion list instead of an explicit inclusion list - so a new screen is covered the day it is written.
The self-test proves the inversion works: add a temporary Composable file with a bare string and confirm the guard reddens without anyone editing a list.
check-string-formats.py still passes across both locales after the new strings land.
The pseudo-locale build (en-XA / en-XB, already enabled on debug) is used to check the eight converted screens for clipping and RTL, which is what those locales were turned on for.
The 'migration under way' framing in the guard header is replaced, since after this there is no migration - matching what US-2499 asks for on the iOS side.
userStories.notes:
STATUS 2026-08-26, read from the code rather than done here. AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC6 are ALREADY DONE and were never recorded - this story had empty notes, so the next reader would have re-derived all of it. android/scripts/no-bare-strings.py is inverted: its header says 'SCOPE IS EVERY COMPOSE FILE. There is no migration any more (US-2908)', EXCLUDED is empty with a comment saying an entry is a claim a human checked the file, and composable_files() WALKS the tree for @Composable instead of reading a list. AC3 is satisfied better than it asked: _self_test_discovery() writes a probe Composable with a bare string INSIDE the source tree on every invocation (not behind a flag, because a guard whose own test is opt-in is back where it started), and fails if the walk does not reach it or does not flag it. There is also a staleness check on EXCLUDED and an empty-scope check, since discovery finding nothing looks identical to a clean tree. Verified by running it here: 'self-test OK (24 cases + discovery)' then 'OK (106 Compose files)' - 106 is the full count the story named, so the eight stragglers are in scope. Spot-checked four of the eight named files: ConsumerCreditPackSheet, ConsumerGradeScreen and TwoFactorDialog carry 2, 27 and 19 stringResource calls and zero bare Text literals; SyncStatusHost has no user-visible text at all. AC4 green: check-string-formats OK across 1565 resources in en and es. STILL OPEN: AC5 alone, the pseudo-locale (en-XA / en-XB) pass over the eight converted screens for clipping and RTL. That is a look-at-it criterion on a device or emulator, and this host has neither an Android SDK nor a way to install one (dl.google.com is blocked by the network policy). Filing rather than faking. | 2026-08-30 AC7 CORRECTION, filed by US-2976. This story's own note said the
guard was inverted and "There is no migration any more", and both the note and
the guard header meant COMPOSE files. Read as a statement about the app, which
is how the next person read it, it was wrong twice over.

WHAT WAS TRUE: no-bare-strings.py walks every file containing @Composable, 106
of them, and its self-test writes a probe into the tree on every run. That part
is done and stands.

WHAT IT DID NOT SAY: 356 Kotlin files contain no @Composable and were outside
that walk entirely. The Android bottom bar's five labels - Home, Inventory, Add,
Money, Marketplaces - lived in an enum in ui/shell/Sections.kt and were
hardcoded English underneath a fully translated top bar. Nothing in the repo
could see them.

AND WIDENING THE WALK WOULD NOT HAVE HELPED, which is the useful half.
no-unlocalized-copy.py already scanned every non-Compose Kotlin file from
2026-08-28, with a ratcheting baseline. So the gap was never which files are
scanned. It was WHAT COUNTS AS COPY: is_copy() is a sentence detector, and
measured against the app's own strings it caught 5 of 5 sentences and 3 of 41
UI labels. Title Case and single words are invisible to it by construction.

FIXED under US-2976 AC9 (commit 6893659a3): a positional LABEL rule in
android/scripts/label_rule.py, wired into no-unlocalized-copy.py. It surfaced
211 previously invisible strings across 9 more files - 567 in 152 files becomes
778 in 161.

Nothing about this story's other criteria changed. The correction is only to the
scope its note claimed.

userStories.title: The widget shows up in the picker as a grey box with no preview
userStories.description: res/xml/seller_snapshot_widget_info.xml declares description, initialLayout, sizes, resizeMode, updatePeriodMillis and widgetCategory. It declares neither android:previewImage nor android:previewLayout.  Without one of those the system has nothing to draw in the widget picker, so it falls back to the app icon on a plain background. The seller browsing widgets sees every other app's widget rendered as itself and GradeThread's rendered as a launcher icon, which is the difference between 'this shows me today's takings' and 'I don't know what this is'. It is the only place the widget is ever advertised.  previewLayout is the modern answer (Android 12+) and it renders the real layout with sample values; previewImage is the pre-12 fallback and minSdk here is 26, so both are wanted. Glance has a supported way to produce the preview from the same composable the widget uses, which avoids the usual failure of a hand-drawn PNG drifting from the widget it depicts.  SECOND, SMALLER THING IN THE SAME FILE: resizeMode is 'horizontal' only, and targetCellWidth/Height are 2x1. A seller who wants the snapshot taller cannot have it. Worth a decision rather than an accident - if 2x1 is the deliberate shape, the comment in that file (which explains updatePeriodMillis at length) should say so.
acceptanceCriteria: previewLayout renders the real snapshot layout with plausible sample numbers - no zeroes, no lorem, no real seller data.
previewImage is supplied for pre-Android-12 devices, generated from the same composable rather than drawn by hand.
The picker is checked on an Android 12+ device and on an older one, and the widget is confirmed to be recognisable in both.
resizeMode and the target cell size are decided deliberately and the reasoning added to the file, alongside the existing updatePeriodMillis note.
The signed-out state is checked in the picker and on the home screen, since WidgetPublisher.publishSignedOut is what a fresh install renders.
The widget is included in a screenshot for the listing, per the PLAY_STORE_SUBMISSION.md section 2 storyline, which names it as shot 7.
userStories.notes:
SCOPED 2026-08-28, not started. AC2 is not achievable on the current Glance pin, and that changes the shape of the whole story.

CONFIRMED FIRST, by reading the file: res/xml/seller_snapshot_widget_info.xml declares description, initialLayout, minWidth/minHeight, targetCellWidth/Height 2x1, resizeMode horizontal, updatePeriodMillis 0 and widgetCategory - and neither previewImage nor previewLayout. The premise is exactly right.

THE BLOCKER. AC2 asks for previewImage 'generated from the same composable rather than drawn by hand', and AC1 for a previewLayout that 'renders the real snapshot layout'. The supported Glance mechanism for both is GlanceAppWidget.providePreview(), which arrives in Glance 1.2.0. android/gradle/libs.versions.toml pins glance = "1.1.1" (line 69). On 1.1.1 the only options are a hand-written XML previewLayout or a hand-drawn previewImage - which is precisely the drift the story's own description says to avoid ('avoids the usual failure of a hand-drawn PNG drifting from the widget it depicts').

So this story depends on androidx.glance 1.1.1 -> 1.2.0. That is a MINOR bump and not one of the 17 major-version jumps in US-2906's report, so it is a much smaller ask than the rest of that story and is worth pulling out on its own rather than waiting for the whole dependency sweep - which is itself gated on a real-device smoke pass (US-2906 AC4).

WHAT IS READY WHEN THE PIN MOVES. SellerSnapshotWidget.Content(snapshot, nowMs) takes both inputs as parameters and wraps everything in GlanceTheme, so a preview can call the real composable directly with no refactor. WidgetSnapshot is a plain data class with defaults, so the sample is a one-line construction - no fixture plumbing. SignedOut() already exists as its own composable, so AC5's signed-out case has something real to render rather than needing a state invented for the picker.

ONE THING THE SAMPLE MUST GET RIGHT: WidgetSnapshot.generatedAt drives a 'Updated 5m ago' stamp via WidgetCopy.updatedAgo(generatedAt, nowMs). A preview with a default generatedAt of 0 would advertise the widget as years stale in the picker, which is worse than no preview. nowMs has to sit close to generatedAt in the sample.

AC4 IS DOABLE NOW AND INDEPENDENTLY, and is the half worth not losing: resizeMode is 'horizontal' only against a 2x1 target, so a seller cannot make the snapshot taller. The file explains updatePeriodMillis at length and says nothing about this, which is what makes it read as an accident. Decide it and write the reason next to the existing note - that needs no Glance upgrade and no device.

STILL DEVICE-GATED regardless of the pin: AC3 (the picker checked on an Android 12+ device AND an older one), AC5 (the signed-out state on a home screen), AC6 (the widget as shot 7 of the listing storyline, which is US-2894's blocker too).

userStories.title: Error and empty states are handled in three screens out of fifty-three
userStories.description: The app has ErrorStateView in ui/components and three screens use it. It has two pull-to-refresh implementations. It has 53 screens.  That is not an assertion that the other fifty handle failure badly - most of them surface something - but it is a strong signal that failure UX was built per screen rather than as a pattern, and the count is the kind of thing that is true of an app right before the first bad review about a blank page.  WHAT MAKES IT WORTH A STORY HERE RATHER THAN LATER. This app is offline-tolerant by design: there is a mutation queue, a watermark-based sync, a connectivity monitor, realtime, and a SyncStatusHost. All of that machinery exists so a seller can work in a dead spot in a thrift store, which is the actual usage the product is built around. The failure states are therefore not an edge case, they are the primary environment - and a screen that renders an empty list when the pull failed is indistinguishable, to the seller, from a screen that correctly says they have no items.  PULL-TO-REFRESH IS THE OTHER HALF. Two uses across fifty-three screens. On Android a list that cannot be pulled reads as broken, and it is the gesture a seller reaches for the moment they suspect the app is stale - which, given the sync model, is a reasonable suspicion they should be able to act on.
acceptanceCriteria: Every screen that loads from the network is audited and the finding tabulated: what it shows while loading, when the load fails, and when it succeeds with nothing.
The three states are distinguishable on every one of them - a failed load never renders as an empty list.
Every list backed by a sync pull supports pull-to-refresh, and the gesture is wired to the real pull rather than to a local re-read.
Error copy tells the seller what to do, in strings.xml with Spanish, and never shows a raw exception or an HTTP status.
The offline case is exercised deliberately with the device in airplane mode across the main flows, and what the seller sees is confirmed rather than assumed.
Screenshot goldens cover the error and empty state of at least the inventory, money and marketplaces lists, so this cannot silently regress.
userStories.notes:
AC1 MEASURED 2026-08-28, nothing built yet. The headline number is wrong in a way that matters, and the real finding is sharper than the one the story names.

⚠ 'THREE SCREENS OUT OF FIFTY-THREE' COUNTS ErrorStateView IMPORTS, NOT BEHAVIOUR. Three files import it (AiExtractScreen, GradeReportScreen, and the component itself). Measuring what screens actually DO: of 51 screens that load state, 36 distinguish an error somehow - an isError flag, an `error != null` branch, an errorMessage field - and 27 render an empty state. Anyone starting from the headline would rewrite screens that already work.

The story's own DESCRIPTION is right where its title is not: 'failure UX was built per screen rather than as a pattern'. That is exactly what the numbers say. 36 of 51 handle it, 36 of 51 handle it differently.

THE SHARP FINDING, and it is AC3: PULL-TO-REFRESH IS 1 OF 51. InventoryListScreen only. For an app whose whole architecture - mutation queue, watermark sync, connectivity monitor, SyncStatusHost - exists so a seller can work in a dead spot, a seller who comes back into signal has one screen that lets them ask for the data again. Every other list waits for a trigger they cannot see. That is a bigger hole than the error copy and it is a smaller job.

NINE SCREENS HAVE NEITHER AN ERROR BRANCH NOR AN EMPTY STATE: CommunityInsights, BarcodeScan, BulkGrade, GradeRequest, Home, Import, GlobalSearch, Lock, Settings. Home is the one to start with - it is the first screen after launch and the one most likely to be looked at while signal is bad.

SIX MORE HAVE NO ERROR BRANCH but do render an empty state, which is precisely the failure mode AC2 names - a failed load rendering as 'you have no items': ConsumerGrade, GradesList, InventoryList, Sales, RadarNearby, RadarVenueDetail. InventoryList and Sales are the two where an empty list reads as a dead business rather than as a network problem.

HOW MUCH TO TRUST THIS. It is a pattern scan over the four idioms this codebase uses for failure, so a screen handling it another way reads as a gap and is not one, and a screen that catches an exception and renders nothing reads as handled and is not. A WORKLIST, NOT A VERDICT: every line needs the file opened. The counts are still worth having because they replace an impression with a number, which is what AC1 asked for.

The script is in the session scratchpad rather than committed - it is a one-off measurement, not a gate, and a committed scan that nothing runs is the shape this repo has been retiring.

NOT STARTED, and the sequencing suggestion: AC3 (pull-to-refresh on every sync-backed list) is the highest value per unit of work and needs no device. AC2 on the six empty-state-without-error screens is next. AC4's copy needs Spanish, so it lands with the localization work. AC5 needs a phone in airplane mode and AC6 needs the screenshot lane, which is still advisory (US-2902).

userStories.title: Predictive back is off, and in-app updates were never wired
userStories.description: Two platform integrations that are each a small amount of work and are each what separates an app that feels current from one that feels ported.  PREDICTIVE BACK. AndroidManifest.xml does not set android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback, and nothing in the tree uses the predictive-back APIs. So the back gesture gets no preview animation anywhere in the app: no peek at the screen behind, no shared-element transition out of a detail screen, and every dismissible surface - the sheets, the dialogs, the item detail - snaps rather than animates. On Android 14+ this is the default experience of every well-maintained app, and it is the kind of thing a reviewer registers as 'this feels old' without being able to name why. Moving to API 36 makes this more pressing, not less, since the platform defaults shift again there.  IN-APP UPDATES. PLAY_STORE_SUBMISSION.md notes, under 'the things to leave alone at first release', that in-app updates are not wired and the Play Core library is not a dependency. That is the correct call for the first submission and the wrong steady state: this app talks to a server whose API moves, and the only way to get a seller off a broken client version today is to hope they update. A flexible update prompt for ordinary releases and an immediate one for a version the server can no longer support is the mechanism, and the second half of that needs a server-side minimum-version signal that does not exist yet.  Neither blocks submission. Both are cheap now and awkward later, and the second one is only useful if it ships BEFORE the version it needs to rescue people from.
acceptanceCriteria: android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback is set and the back gesture previews correctly across the shell, the detail screens, the bottom sheets and the dialogs.
Anything that intercepted back predictively-unaware (a sheet, a multi-step flow, the capture screen) is migrated to the predictive-back APIs rather than left on a plain back handler.
The gesture is checked on a device running the current Android release, in both gesture and three-button navigation.
The Play in-app update API is wired: a flexible prompt for an ordinary new version, and an immediate one for a version below a server-declared minimum.
The server exposes that minimum supported client version, and the client asks for it - the immediate path is worthless without a signal to trigger it.
PLAY_STORE_SUBMISSION.md section 4.4's 'not wired' line is updated once it is.
userStories.notes:
AC5 DONE 2026-08-28, AC1 already half-done, the rest is device work. Shipped in the commit above.

AC1 IS PARTLY DONE ALREADY, by a different story. android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true" is set in AndroidManifest.xml (line 69), and US-2891 set it EXPLICITLY rather than taking the platform default - it was safe to do because the app had no legacy back handling to break: zero onBackPressed overrides, zero KEYCODE_BACK reads and zero BackHandler calls across 688 Kotlin files, so back is entirely Navigation-Compose's and androidx.activity already bridges it. What remains of AC1 is the half a compiler cannot answer: whether the gesture PREVIEWS correctly across the shell, the detail screens, the sheets and the dialogs. That needs a device.

AC2 follows from the same finding and is probably empty: with no BackHandler calls anywhere, there is nothing left on a plain back callback to migrate. Worth confirming with a fresh grep when someone picks this up rather than trusting this line - the codebase has moved since US-2891 measured it.

AC5 DONE, and it is the one that unblocks AC4. GET /api/client-version/minimum returns client.android_min_version_code and client.ios_min_build_number from system_settings. Separate keys because a versionCode and a CFBundleVersion are different numbers on different scales; one key for both would be a silent cross-platform floor.

PUBLIC AND UNAUTHENTICATED, deliberately - an app below the floor may be failing auth for the very reason it needs replacing, so a signal behind a session could never reach it. A test asserts no middleware is mounted on the path, because that regression is silent: the endpoint keeps working for everyone who does not need it.

IT FAILS OPEN, and that is the opposite of the consent regime shipped the same day (US-2914) for a reason worth stating. A version floor is a kill switch pointed at your own users: wrong in the strict direction locks every seller out of an app that works, with no way for them to fix it and no way to reach them except another deploy. Wrong in the permissive direction costs nothing, because Play still offers the update through the flexible prompt. So absent, junk, negative and zero all mean no floor; a fraction floors rather than rounding up (rounding up would put the floor above a version that exists); and a client that cannot report its own version is never blocked.

NO MIGRATION was needed and none was written: getSetting returns its fallback for a key with no row, and that fallback is no-floor. Registering the two keys in the settings registry is worth doing for the admin editor and is a FOLLOW-UP - a story that holds a migration to ship a read ships later for no gain. 8 tests, deno check and lint clean, route-shadowing guard passes, no tenant table touched.

OUTSTANDING:
  AC1 the gesture checked on a device, in both gesture and three-button navigation.
  AC2 confirm nothing intercepts back predictively-unaware (likely already true).
  AC3 a device running the current Android release.
  AC4 the Play in-app update API itself. Nothing exists yet - no app-update dependency in libs.versions.toml, no AppUpdateManager anywhere. It now has a signal to trigger the immediate path, which is what it was missing. Testing a flexible vs immediate prompt needs a device and a Play track.
  AC6 the PLAY_STORE_SUBMISSION.md 4.4 line, once AC4 lands.

userStories.title: Play Console setup and the reviewer demo account: the five operator blockers
userStories.description: PLAY_STORE_SUBMISSION.md section 0 lists seven things that block submission. Two are marked Fixed (in-app account deletion, the data-deletion URL). Five are unticked and every one needs a human with credentials - no amount of code closes them, and each one fails LATE and expensively if skipped.  3. UPLOAD KEY. ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 plus its password and alias, and PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON, in Infisical prod /. Without them the release lane fails at its first step - which is the good outcome, since that step was added specifically so a missing keystore does not surface as an unsigned AAB rejected twenty minutes later.  4. TEN IN-APP PRODUCTS. Six subscriptions and four consumable credit packs, with ids matching ANDROID_CATALOG exactly. The server fails closed on an unknown id, so a typo in the Console is a real charge with no entitlement, and a test pins the client catalog to the server one but nothing pins the Console. Each subscription also needs a base plan AND an offer - the paywall reads offerToken and renders a row as unpurchasable without one, so a base plan with no offer ships as a price tag with a dead button.  5. REVIEWER DEMO ACCOUNT. The app is login-gated from the first screen. Without credentials in App access, review returns 'we could not access the app' and the clock restarts. The review-notes block is already written in section 3.2, including that the eBay connection must be SANDBOX so a reviewer cannot touch the live marketplace.  7. SERVER ENV FOR PLAY BILLING. GOOGLE_PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON, GOOGLE_PLAY_PACKAGE_NAME and GOOGLE_RTDN_WEBHOOK_SECRET in Coolify, plus the RTDN Pub/Sub topic pointed at the webhook. Missing, every purchase verifies as an error: the buyer is charged and gets nothing.  And one decision, not on that list: the public support email. Section 4.2 says pick one and use it everywhere; the checklist assumes support@gradethread.com. It is shown publicly on the listing and it has to be an address someone reads.
acceptanceCriteria: The upload keystore is generated once, base64'd into Infisical prod / with its password and alias, the local file deleted, and PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON stored with release-manager rights.

All ten in-app products exist in Play Console with ids matching ANDROID_CATALOG exactly, each subscription carrying a base plan AND at least one offer, and grace period / account hold / resubscribe set per section 5.1.
The three server vars are set in Coolify and the RTDN Pub/Sub topic pushes to https://functions.gradethread.com/api/webhooks/google-play with the shared secret.
License testers are added and the five-step round trip in section 5.5 is run and passes: buy a subscription, buy credits, re-verify the same token grants nothing more, cancel, expire.

A seeded demo account exists with sample inventory, photos, a completed grade with certificate, listings, sales, payouts and a credit balance, its eBay connection on SANDBOX, and its credentials plus the section 3.2 review-notes block are in App access.
The public support email is chosen, monitored by a human, and used identically in the Console, the listing copy and the app.
Every box in the section 7 pre-submission checklist is ticked from something that was actually observed, not from an intention.

userStories.title: EPIC: Size check against brand size charts
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want the Composer to tell me when an item's measurements disagree with the size on the label, so that I stop publishing a Large that measures like an XS.
acceptanceCriteria: Children US-2916..US-2922 are filed and linked. The epic closes only when all seven pass.

The motivating case works end to end: a Lululemon top with chest 17.5 in (35 in around) and size Large raises a discrepancy in the web Composer, and the note names the size the measurements actually point to.
No new chart store is introduced. The check reuses the existing corpus in services/edge-functions/src/lib/sizing-charts.ts (about 160 brands) and public.brand_size_charts (migration 00389).

Founder decisions recorded here so they are not re-litigated: (1) the checker ships before the top-100 chart curation; (2) the warning offers a one-click size fix and NEVER blocks publish; (3) it fires in Composer, Prep and the AutoLister review; (4) tolerance is one size step on a verified brand chart and two steps on a generic fallback chart.

The architecture is the band-table split, chosen over a per-keystroke verdict endpoint and over bundling the charts into each client: the edge resolves brand, department, garment and ease and returns a small precomputed table of expected FLAT ranges per size; each client only does the lookup, so the check is instant while typing and the judgement lives in one place.

The honesty limit is stated in the UI copy and is accepted: garment ease varies by cut, so the check catches gross errors (an XS labelled Large) and deliberately stays quiet on subtle ones (an oversized tee labelled Small).
userStories.notes: Status 2026-08-26. SIX of seven children pass: US-2916 (the math), US-2917 (the endpoint + migration 00674), US-2918 (Composer and Prep), US-2919 (AutoLister queue), US-2920 (iOS), US-2921 (Android). US-2922 is PARTIAL - its guard, its admin field and its coverage script are done, but the top-100 ranking needs prod inventory and each chart needs a human check before verified flips true. The epic stays open on that one child, per AC1. The motivating case works end to end in code and is pinned by a fixture that all four implementations run: a Lululemon men's top measuring 17.5 in flat but labelled Large raises a discrepancy naming 'smaller than XS', and an ordinary 22 in tee labelled L stays silent because a generic Large is exactly 22 to 26.5 in flat. All four founder decisions are implemented as written: the checker shipped before the curation; the note offers a one-click fix and never blocks publish; it fires in Composer, Prep and the AutoLister review; tolerance is one size step on a verified or brand chart and two on a generic one. The band-table split held up - the edge resolves brand, department, garment and ease once and returns a table, and each client does a pure lookup, so the check runs on every keystroke with no request. The honesty limit is in the UI copy: a generic chart says 'Estimate only - no <brand> chart on file'. TWO THINGS THE BUILD ADDED that the epic did not anticipate, both worth keeping. (1) The fix button is ABSENT when the measurements land off the end of a chart. 'smaller than XS' is not a size the brand makes, so there is nothing to change to and writing it into the size column would be worse than saying nothing. (2) findSizingCharts and the pack assembler both fall back to the WHOLE chart pool when a category narrows to nothing - right for the grading prompt, wrong here. The first draft of the endpoint returned a men's TOPS chart for garment=wristwatch. It now requires a real category match and returns tier 'none' otherwise. BLOCKING THE MERGE: migration 00674 is HELD in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md and must be applied to prod first. | CONFIRMED APPLIED 2026-08-26: migration 00674 is on prod. The evidence is a row for '00674' in public.applied_migrations, read with services/edge-functions/scripts/check-prod-migration.ts - not the column showing up in the schema, which would only prove the file got that far. The self-record insert is the LAST statement in the migration, so the row means the ADD COLUMN, the CHECK constraint and the comment all ran. Prod records every migration that is meant to be applied; the only gap is 00527, which is the owner's permanent do-not-apply. Anything above in these notes calling 00674 HELD or BLOCKING is superseded. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md now reads APPLIED and held-migration-gate.mjs passes. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-26. Migration 00674 is applied to production, and 00527 is the owner's permanent do-not-apply. Every earlier segment of these notes that describes either one as still awaiting the operator is superseded and should not be acted on. Evidence is a row in public.applied_migrations, read with services/edge-functions/scripts/check-prod-migration.ts, whose sweep reports that prod records every migration meant to be applied. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md reads APPLIED and scripts/held-migration-gate.mjs passes.

userStories.title: Top 100 brand size charts: verified, sourced and department-complete
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want the size check to be right on the brands I actually sell, so that the warning is trustworthy instead of a polite estimate.
acceptanceCriteria: The 100 brands are chosen from real data, not intuition: the top 100 by inventory_items.brand row count across the platform, and the ranked list is written into this story's notes so the target is falsifiable.
Each of the 100 has at least one public.brand_size_charts row per department it actually sells (Men, Women, Kids as applicable), covering tops and bottoms at minimum.
Every seeded row carries source_url pointing at the brand's OWN published size guide (not a reseller blog), confidence, and verified = true only after a human has compared the row against that URL.
Rows whose source publishes garment-flat specs instead of body measurements are stored with measurement_basis = 'flat', so the band builder does not add ease on top of ease.

services/edge-functions/src/tests/sizing-chart-parity_test.ts is extended: every verified DB chart either has a code-seed counterpart or is listed explicitly as DB-only, so the in-code fallback can never contradict the DB.
The admin UI src/pages/admin/brand-knowledge.tsx can set verified, source_url and measurement_basis on a chart row, and doing so changes the tier the composer shows with no deploy.
A coverage script prints how many of the top 100 have a verified chart per department, and the closing number is recorded in this story's notes.
Migrations seeding the charts satisfy the US-1108 triple: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in the same commit, self-record footer.
OPERATOR: apply the seed migrations to prod and re-run the coverage script against prod, recording the result in the notes.
userStories.notes: PARTIAL 2026-08-26. The checkable half is done; the curation itself is BLOCKED and needs the owner. DONE: (AC5) new services/edge-functions/src/tests/verified-chart-parity_test.ts parses every brand_size_charts INSERT across all 674 migrations (a hand-rolled VALUES splitter, because the rows carry ARRAY[], $json$ and prose full of commas) and fails when a chart marked verified has no sizing-charts.ts counterpart and is not classified DB-only. It found SEVEN on its first run - New Era x2, Stetson, Kangol, Goorin Bros, golf shoe widths, western boot widths - all real and all correctly DB-only: headwear circumference and shoe-width letter axes have no ease and no band, so compiling them into the edge would add rows nothing reads. They are now classified with that reason, plus a guards-the-guard case (the parser must find >100 charts, since a broken parse reads exactly like a clean corpus) and a case that a verified chart carries a source_url, since verified without a URL is a row nobody could have checked. (AC6) measurement_basis added to the admin allow-list on BOTH sides - src/pages/admin/brand-knowledge.tsx EDITABLE and the edge KB_TABLES in admin-brand-knowledge.ts, which is the one that actually enforces it. (AC7) new services/edge-functions/scripts/size-chart-coverage.ts ranks brands by real inventory_items.brand row count, reads the department each brand actually sells from the items rather than guessing, and prints coverage per brand+department: any chart / verified chart / tops AND bottoms / source_url, plus the flat-basis count. Read-only, deno lint and deno check clean. BLOCKED, and why: (AC1) the top-100 ranking is a fact about PROD inventory. There is no prod access from this sandbox and Docker will not start here, so the script has never been executed and the ranked list cannot be written into these notes. (AC2/AC3/AC4/AC8) seeding 100 brands' charts requires that ranking first, and every row needs a human to compare it against the brand's own published guide before verified flips true - that is the whole point of the tier and it is not something to fabricate. (AC9) is an OPERATOR step by its own wording. NEXT STEP FOR THE OWNER: run 'deno run --allow-net --allow-env services/edge-functions/scripts/size-chart-coverage.ts --top 100 --json' against prod with SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY set, and paste the ranking here. The seeding work can then be scoped against real numbers instead of intuition. | AC1/AC7 UNBLOCKED 2026-08-26: the script ran against prod. 711 items scanned, 321 charts in the DB, 100 brands ranked, 119 brand+department pairs. HEADLINE: 38 of 119 pairs have any chart, 13 cover tops AND bottoms, and only FOUR have a verified chart - Lululemon Men and Women, Athleta Women, Nike Men. Weighted by items rather than by brand: 49.3% of paired items have some chart, 19.7% have a verified one. flat-basis charts: 0 (every one of the 321 is 'body', as 00674's comment predicted).  THE RANKING CHANGES THE STORY'S SCOPE, and this is the reason the AC insisted it come from data. The platform holds 711 items, not the tens of thousands the phrase 'top 100 brands' implies. Rank 1 (Lululemon) has 63 items; rank 10 has 8; rank 50 has 3; rank 100 has 2. The top 100 brands are 63.9% of all items, so ranking deeper buys almost nothing, and the bottom half of the 100 is a two-item tail that a human would be checking a size guide for on spec.  Real work remaining, by unit: 115 of the 119 pairs lack a verified chart, but they collapse into 87 BRANDS, and a brand's own size page usually serves both departments in one visit. 34 of the 115 pairs ALREADY have a chart and only need a human to compare it to its source_url (all 38 charted pairs carry one). 81 need a chart built from scratch.  RECOMMENDED SCOPE: verify 20 brands, not 100. The first 20 brands by item count cover 132 of the 269 uncovered items (49%); going to 87 brands to reach 100% is 4x the work for 2x the coverage. In order: Vuori(15), Peter Millar(12), prAna(8), GANT(7), Bonobos(7), Vineyard Vines(7), Polo Ralph Lauren(7), Carhartt(7), Patagonia(7), Ermenegildo Zegna(6), Lauren Ralph Lauren(6), Vince(6), Banana Republic(6), Quince(5), Free Fly(5), L'AGENCE(5), Beyond Yoga(4), Christian Dior(4), St. John(4), Mizzen+Main(4). Six of those twenty (Vuori, Peter Millar, Bonobos, Vineyard Vines, Vince, Banana Republic) are CHECK-not-build, so they are the cheapest wins and should go first.  Kids is negligible and should be dropped from AC2: 4 pairs, 7 items total, zero charts, spread across Carhartt, Polo Ralph Lauren and Patagonia.  TWO SCRIPT DEFECTS FOUND BY RUNNING IT, both fixed before the numbers above were trusted. (1) It selected brand_size_charts.measurement_basis, and against a database without 00674 PostgREST fails the WHOLE select with 42703, so readCharts() returned an empty list and every brand printed NONE - a fabricated zero that reads exactly like the real answer to the question the script exists to ask. The column is optional now and the flat count reports 'unknown' rather than 0. (2) The first prod attempt captured one character of the pasted service-role key; Deno rejected the Authorization header, supabase-js surfaced it per query, and the script wrote a complete report of zeros. It now trims both env values and refuses to start on a key that is not header-safe and JWT-shaped. Both paths were verified against the local stack, whose brand_size_charts is the same pre-00674 shape.  ALSO: migration 00674 IS ALREADY APPLIED TO PROD, though PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md still lists it as HELD and BLOCKING. measurement_basis appears in prod's PostgREST OpenAPI definition for brand_size_charts, and all 321 rows read back with a basis value. Confirm applied_migrations holds '00674' and then clear the hold; the session-start hook is warning about a migration that has shipped. | CONFIRMED APPLIED 2026-08-26: migration 00674 is on prod. The evidence is a row for '00674' in public.applied_migrations, read with services/edge-functions/scripts/check-prod-migration.ts - not the column showing up in the schema, which would only prove the file got that far. The self-record insert is the LAST statement in the migration, so the row means the ADD COLUMN, the CHECK constraint and the comment all ran. Prod records every migration that is meant to be applied; the only gap is 00527, which is the owner's permanent do-not-apply. Anything above in these notes calling 00674 HELD or BLOCKING is superseded. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md now reads APPLIED and held-migration-gate.mjs passes. Prod's 321 charts are all measurement_basis='body', so AC4's flat path has no production data behind it yet. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-26. Migration 00674 is applied to production, and 00527 is the owner's permanent do-not-apply. Every earlier segment of these notes that describes either one as still awaiting the operator is superseded and should not be acted on. Evidence is a row in public.applied_migrations, read with services/edge-functions/scripts/check-prod-migration.ts, whose sweep reports that prod records every migration meant to be applied. userStories.title: iOS and Android: description block editor parity
userStories.description: As a reseller listing from my phone, I want the same description block list as the web composer, so that a listing I edit on mobile keeps its structure.
acceptanceCriteria: The iOS composer shows the block list with toggles, reorder and in-place edit, backed by the same four /api/flipdesk/description/ routes, and renders no description text locally.
The Android drafts surface under android/app/src/main/java/com/gradethread/app/autolister/ gets the same block list.

The description-rendering half of ios/GradeThread/Marketplaces/Publish/ListingDescriptionTemplate.swift (measurementsBlock, ensureGradeLine, ensureSellerCredentials, splitSellerCredentials) is DELETED; the measure-card value formatter stays.
A listing edited on iOS and then opened on web shows the same block array and the same preview string.
npm run verify:android passes and iOS CI passes.
userStories.notes: HELD 2026-08-28, not started: needs a machine with Xcode and the Android SDK. This container cannot compile either client (Swift is macOS-only; dl.google.com is blocked by the network policy, so the Android SDK cannot be installed and npm run verify:android cannot run), and AC5 requires that lane to pass. Everything it depends on is done and on the branch: US-2960 (composer block list), US-2961 (snippets + apply-to-drafts), US-2962 (bulk toggles), US-2963 (credentials cron re-renders). IMPLEMENTATION PLAN, so the session on a capable machine is short. (1) iOS service: new ios/GradeThread/Marketplaces/Publish/DescriptionBlocksService.swift wrapping the four routes already live at /api/flipdesk/description/ - GET :id/blocks (returns blocks + preview + converted, adopt the preview VERBATIM, never re-request it, that is what makes convert-on-open byte-exact), POST /preview (debounce 400ms, sequence number so a stale response cannot overwrite a newer one - see src/lib/description-preview.ts for the contract), POST :id/save, POST :id/regenerate. Mirror the block shape from src/types/database.ts DescriptionBlock (key/on/src/text/fields/unit/ref/sep) - sep is load-bearing, do not drop it. (2) iOS view: a block list inside ItemCanvasView with per-row toggle, drag reorder, in-place TextEditor for intro/features/condition/snippet/text, and go-to-field for the derived rows; facts and credentials pinned (no drag handle) for the US-2682 reason. Render NOTHING locally - the preview string always comes from the server. (3) iOS deletion (AC3): remove measurementsBlock, ensureGradeLine, ensureSellerCredentials and splitSellerCredentials from ListingDescriptionTemplate.swift (444 lines; the measure-card value formatter STAYS), fix the three call sites - ListingRewriteService.swift:125, ItemCanvasView.swift:2382 and :2408-2411 - and drop the eight now-dead cases in ios/GradeThreadTests/ListingDescriptionTemplateTests.swift. The web equivalent of those call sites is applyWholeText in src/lib/description-blocks.ts, which strips the markers and folds the string into the intro block; copy that behaviour rather than inventing one. (4) Android: the same list under android/app/src/main/java/com/gradethread/app/autolister/ (DraftsLibraryScreen.kt and DraftsService.kt are the surfaces to extend). (5) AC4 check: edit a listing on iOS, open it on web, confirm the same block array and the same preview string - both clients read the same GET, so a difference means one of them rendered locally. Estimated ~1300 lines across the two clients. | 2026-08-28 (from US-2967): iOS has the same boilerplate bug the web just lost. ListingDraftService.swift:668 appends template.descriptionTemplate onto the description STRING. That is correct today because iOS has no block editor yet, and it becomes the web's old bug the moment this story gives it one — the append lands outside description_blocks and the first save renders it away. Port the edge's withTemplateBlock / the web's appendTextBlock (both added in US-2967) rather than the string concat: the footer is its own text block, spliced in front of the credentials and facts rows.

userStories.title: The Android bottom bar is hardcoded English, and the localization guard cannot see it
userStories.description:
MEASURED 2026-08-28, found while walking US-2891's remaining AC. The Android
bottom bar's five labels - Home, Inventory, Add, Money, Marketplaces - are
hardcoded English string literals in the ShellSection enum
(ui/shell/Sections.kt:17-24). A Spanish seller gets Herramientas and Ajustes in
the top bar, from shell_tools and shell_settings in values-es, and English in
the bottom bar directly beneath them.

THE GUARD CANNOT SEE THEM, AND THAT IS THE STORY. US-2908 inverted
android/scripts/no-bare-strings.py so its scope is every file containing
@Composable, and its header now says 'There is no migration any more'. Sections.kt
contains no @Composable - it is an enum consumed by AppShell - so the walk never
reaches it. 106 Compose files are covered; 356 Kotlin files are not.

SCOPE, MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED: of those 356, 28 declare a display-ish
String property (label/title/displayName/caption/heading) and assign it an
English literal, carrying 142 distinct strings. The largest are
capture/PhotoSlotType.kt (23: Front, Back, Tag, Detail, Chest / Bust...),
capture/DetailsIntakeState.kt (12), importer/ImportField.kt (12),
capture/PhotoProfile.kt (10), inventory/InventoryStage.kt (7). Also in the set:
grading/GradeFactor.kt (the five grading factor names), grading/Disputes.kt (the
dispute reasons a seller picks from), sync/BackgroundRefresh.kt ('You made a
sale', 'Grade ready' - PUSH NOTIFICATION text), and billing/SubscriptionCatalog.kt.

NOT ALL 142 ARE DEFECTS and the story must not treat them as such. Some are WIRE
values that happen to look like prose - marketplaces/publish/EbayCondition.kt
carries 'New with tags' as eBay's own condition name, and translating it would
break the listing. Others are brand names (plan tiers). The count is the size of
the QUESTION, not the size of the bug.

SEPARATELY, AND VISIBLE ON A DEVICE: 'Marketplaces' is 12 characters in a
five-item NavigationBar and wraps onto two lines on a compact phone, leaving a
lone 's' under the label on every screen. Observed on the API 36 emulator during
US-2891's shell walk and recorded in that story's notes with nothing to carry it.
acceptanceCriteria: The five ShellSection labels move to strings.xml with Spanish translations, and the bottom bar and rail both read them. The enum cannot call stringResource (it is not a Composable), so the label becomes a @StringRes Int the two call sites resolve - which is also what makes the guard able to see a regression.

The bottom-bar label that wraps is fixed and the fix is CHECKED at compact width, not assumed: either a shorter label for the bar (the section is 'Marketplaces' everywhere else in the app, so a different bar label is a deliberate choice that must be recorded) or the bar allowed to size for it. A screenshot test at compact width pins it.

no-bare-strings.py's scope stops being '@Composable files' and becomes every Kotlin file under app/src/main/java, with the 27 not-yet-converted files in EXCLUDED, each named with its reason and a pointer to this story. A NEW file is then covered the day it is written, which is what US-2908's inversion was for and what this gap shows it did not achieve.

The guard's self-test proves the WIDER scope: a temporary non-Composable Kotlin file carrying a bare display string is discovered and flagged without anyone editing a list. US-2908's existing discovery self-test writes a probe with @Composable in it and would keep passing against this bug.

Each of the 28 files is classified DISPLAY or WIRE before any conversion, and the WIRE ones stay in EXCLUDED permanently with the reason on the entry - EbayCondition.kt is the worked example, since translating eBay's own condition names would break publishing. A file moved to EXCLUDED without a reason is the failure mode this replaces.

check-string-formats.py passes across both locales after the new strings land, and the pseudo-locale build is used on the bottom bar specifically, since that is the surface a longer translation breaks first.
US-2908's note is corrected: its 'There is no migration any more' and its 106-file count were true of Compose files and read as true of the app.

AC3 IS NOT ENOUGH ON ITS OWN, MEASURED 2026-08-28. Widening the walk to every Kotlin file would NOT have caught this bug. no-bare-strings.py detects a literal at a Compose SINK - Text(, contentDescription =, label = { Text( - and the ShellSection literals are at a DECLARATION site, inside an enum constructor call, where no sink appears. Proven rather than reasoned: a probe file carrying both @Composable (so it is unambiguously in scope) and `enum class ZzProbe(val route: String, val label: String) { ONE("one", "Marketplaces") }` was written into the source tree and the guard reported OK across 108 Compose files. So AC3 needs a SECOND detector alongside the wider walk: a String property in a display-ish role (label/title/displayName/caption/heading) assigned a quoted literal. Without it, inverting the scope adds 250 files to the walk and finds nothing new, which is the most expensive way to stay exactly as blind.

AC3 IS SUPERSEDED BY A MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-29. A guard that scans every non-Compose Kotlin file ALREADY EXISTS - android/scripts/no-unlocalized-copy.py, added 2026-08-28 in 2997a9341, with a 153-file / 570-string ratcheting baseline. So the gap was never 'which files are scanned'. The gap is WHAT COUNTS AS COPY. Its is_copy() requires length >= 12, a space, a leading capital, AND at least two all-lowercase words - a SENTENCE detector. Measured by importing the real function and feeding it the app's actual labels: 5 of 5 sentences caught, and 3 of 41 UI labels (7%). The 38 it misses are the ones that matter here: Home / Inventory / Add / Money / Marketplaces, the five grading factor names (Fabric Condition ... Odor & Cleanliness), the photo slots (Front, Back, Tag, Detail, Chest / Bust), the inventory stages and sort options, and the plan names. Title Case and single words are invisible to it by construction. So the work is a LABEL detector alongside the sentence one, not a wider walk and not a second copy of no-bare-strings.py. The obvious shape: a String property in a display-ish role (label/title/displayName/caption/heading) assigned a quoted literal - which is how all 28 files carry theirs, as ENUM_ENTRY("wire_value", "Display Label"). Whichever guard grows the rule, it must ratchet against a baseline the way no-unlocalized-copy.py does, because turning it on at zero would fail the build on ~142 strings on day one and a guard switched off protects nothing - that is the lesson US-2908's own header records.
userStories.notes:
2026-08-28 AC1 AND AC2 SHIPPED. AC5's classification is done and CORRECTS this
story's own description. AC3, AC4, AC6 and AC7 remain.

AC1: the five ShellSection labels are @StringRes ids resolved at the two call
sites, with shell_home / shell_inventory / shell_add / shell_money /
shell_marketplaces in both locales. An enum cannot call stringResource, so the
id travels and AppShell resolves it - which is also what puts these strings
inside a guard's reach at all.

AC2 IS TWO FIXES, NOT ONE, and the second is the one that lasts. The bar gets a
separate shorter label (shell_marketplaces_short, 'Markets'; the rail keeps the
full word because it has the room), AND the bar label is now maxLines = 1 with
an ellipsis. A shorter English string fixes English. A label that ellipsizes
fixes every locale, and an ellipsis is a legible failure where a lone trailing
's' is not - which matters here because 'Inventario' is ten characters and would
have been the next one to wrap.

SectionsTest's labels_areNonEmpty is replaced. It could never have failed on
this bug: a hardcoded English string is not blank. The replacements assert the
ids resolve, and that EXACTLY ONE section shortens its bar label - a section
called one thing and shown as another is a deliberate decision, and a second one
appearing silently is the drift worth catching.

AC3 WAS WRONG AS WRITTEN AND THE NEW CRITERION RECORDS WHY. Widening the walk
to every Kotlin file would not have caught this. The guard detects a literal at
a Compose SINK - Text(, contentDescription =, label = { Text( - and these
literals sit at a DECLARATION site inside an enum constructor, where no sink
appears. Proven, not reasoned: a probe file carrying @Composable AND an enum
with a String label was written into the source tree and the guard reported OK
across 108 files. A second detector is needed, not just a wider walk.

AC5 CLASSIFICATION DONE, AND IT CONTRADICTS THIS STORY'S DESCRIPTION. I wrote
that EbayCondition.kt's 'New with tags' is a WIRE value whose translation would
break publishing. It is not. The shape across all 28 files is the same:
ENUM_ENTRY("wire_value", "Display Label") - eBay's wire value is the FIRST
argument ("NEW", "NEW_OTHER", "FOR_PARTS_OR_NOT_WORKING") and the second is our
own prose in a picker. It should be translated like everything else.

So the split I expected does not exist: essentially all ~142 are display labels.
That makes the story BIGGER and simpler at once - there is no wire/display
judgement call to make per string, and EXCLUDED does not need permanent
entries. What it does need is the second detector, or inverting the scope adds
250 files to the walk and finds nothing, which is the most expensive way to stay
exactly as blind.

The set includes: capture/PhotoSlotType.kt (23 - Front, Back, Tag, Detail, the
measurement slots), importer/ImportField.kt (12), capture/DetailsIntakeState.kt
(12), capture/PhotoProfile.kt (10), inventory/InventoryStage.kt and SortOption.kt,
grading/GradeFactor.kt (the five factor names), grading/Disputes.kt (the reasons
a seller picks from), grading/GradeTier.kt, home/ActivationState.kt,
billing/SubscriptionCatalog.kt, marketplaces/negotiation/NegotiationTypes.kt
(Accept / Counter / Decline) and analytics/CommunityBenchmarks.kt.

VERIFIED SO FAR: no-bare-strings self-test 24 cases + discovery, OK across 107
Compose files; check-string-formats OK across 1602 resources in en and es. The
Gradle build and unit suite are NOT yet run - a full verify was holding the box
- so AC1/AC2 are not closed until spotless, detekt, lint and testDebugUnitTest
have passed. | 2026-08-30 AC3/AC4/AC7/AC9 DONE. AC5 done with a corrected reason. AC6 verified.
What is left is AC5's remaining classification and AC6's pseudo-locale pass on a
device.

AC9 SHIPPED: android/scripts/label_rule.py, wired into no-unlocalized-copy.py
(commit 6893659a3). The rule is POSITIONAL, not textual, because the strings it
has to find are written like constants: find a constructor parameter whose name
says a person reads it (label/title/displayName/caption/heading/shortLabel/
subtitle), then take the argument at that index out of every entry. Nothing
about the string itself is consulted - "Front" is indistinguishable from a wire
value by inspection and entirely distinguishable by where it sits.

MEASURED RESULT: 211 strings in 9 more files were invisible to every guard in
the repo. Baseline 567 in 152 files -> 778 in 161. Ratcheted rather than failed
at zero, exactly as AC9 required.

TWO BUGS IN MY OWN FIRST CUT, both found by reading the OUTPUT rather than the
code, and both of the silent kind:
  Display indexes are merged across every class in a file, so an unrelated call
  putting a wire value at the same index was read as a label. ItemDraft.kt
  reported `acquired_price`, `sku` and `sold`; MeasureGeometry.kt reported
  `inseam`. NOT_COPY now filters the candidates and both files are clean. A
  baseline full of column names is the place things go to be forgotten.
  A default argument containing a bracket shifted every position after it. That
  reports the WRONG strings rather than none, which reads as a working rule.
  The bracket matcher is string-aware and there is a case for it.

AC3 IS SUPERSEDED AND SHOULD NOT BE BUILT. AC9 already recorded why: widening
no-bare-strings.py to every Kotlin file adds ~250 files to a walk that looks for
a literal at a Compose SINK, and a declaration site has none. Confirmed again
here: the probe file below is flagged by no-unlocalized-copy.py and reported
CLEAN by no-bare-strings.py on the same run.

AC4 PROVEN, not argued. label_discovery_test() writes this into the source tree
on EVERY invocation and fails if the scan does not find it:
    enum class ZzLabelProbe(val route: String, val label: String) {
        ONE("one", "Marketplaces"),
    }
Not behind a flag, because a guard whose own test is opt-in is back where it
started. Also sabotage-verified: breaking DISPLAY_ROLE makes the guard exit 1
with LABEL RULE SELF-TEST FAILED rather than reporting a clean tree.

AC5, WITH A CORRECTION TO THE STORY. EbayCondition.kt is in LABEL_VOCABULARY,
and the reason this AC gives is wrong about the mechanism: [wire] carries the
API value ("NEW_WITH_DEFECTS"), so translating [label] ("New with defects")
would NOT break publishing. The real argument is that a seller picking a
condition is choosing an eBay grade whose meaning eBay defines, and a Spanish
gloss of "Pre-owned - Excellent" would be our word for their category. Right
answer, wrong reason, and the entry says so - a reason nobody can check is worse
than none. LABEL_VOCABULARY is staleness-checked: an entry naming a file the
rule finds nothing in fails.

AC6: check-string-formats.py OK (1643 resources, en, es). No new resources
landed this pass, so nothing could drift. The pseudo-locale check on the bottom
bar still needs a device or emulator.

AC7: US-2908's note is corrected in its own notes, this date.

WHAT IS LEFT. The 211 strings are now COUNTED and frozen, not translated. Each
one still needs classifying DISPLAY or WIRE and moving to strings.xml with a
Spanish counterpart. That is the remaining half of AC5 and it is a big one -
28 files - but it can now be worked file by file with the baseline shrinking,
which is what it could not be before. | 2026-08-30 (later) FIRST TWO FILES TRANSLATED, and a THIRD CLASS OF STRING
FOUND that neither detector can see.

Eleven strings, en and es. Baseline 778 in 161 files down to 768 in 159.

⚠ THE THIRD CLASS: CONCATENATED FRAGMENTS, and sync/BackgroundRefresh.kt is the
worked example. It is a PUSH NOTIFICATION builder, so its copy is the text a
Spanish seller reads on their lock screen. The label rule found three strings
there - "You made a sale", "Grade ready", "While you were away" - and those are
the only three it CAN find. The rest of the notification is assembled:

    body = buildString {
        append(item.title.ifBlank { "Your item" })
        append(" graded ")
    }
    add("$it ${if (it == 1) "sale" else "sales"}")
    body = parts.joinToString(" and ") + " landed."

"Your item", " graded ", "sale"/"sales", " and ", " landed." are fragments. Not
a sentence, so is_copy misses them; not at a display position, so the label rule
misses them; not at a Compose sink, so no-bare-strings misses them. Three guards,
none of which can see the text on the lock screen.

AND A FRAGMENT CANNOT BE FIXED BY EXTRACTION ALONE. "3 sales and 2 grades
landed." is not a translatable unit - Spanish needs a different word order and a
different plural rule, so this needs plurals resources and one format string per
sentence, not five string moves. That is a different job from the other 26 files
and should be its own story rather than being folded into AC5's count.
