proof it is. | 2026-08-30 (seventeenth pass) FINISHED THE FILES THE NEW RULE REOPENED.

SHIPPED (commit 437dd2ba5). Baseline 736 in 148 files down to 721 in 145.

grading/Disputes.kt was marked done two passes ago and was not: the four dispute
STATUS labels and the accessibility line sit in a `when` inside a display-named
function, the shape nothing could see until the previous pass. Now translated.

TWO MORE BUILT SENTENCES BROKEN UP, and this is the recurring shape:
  accessibilityLabel returned "Grade dispute: Under review" - two strings joined
  with a colon a translator cannot move.
  VerifiedBadge.sinceLabel returned "Verified since 2026-03-04" - "since" goes
  in a different place in Spanish.
Both return the pieces now and the caller formats. That is the same lesson as
BulkPricing.Summary and ActivationChecklist.Progress: A FUNCTION WITH NO CONTEXT
CANNOT BUILD A SENTENCE, it can only hand back the parts.

THE TWO-OWNERS STRINGS STOP BEING COUNTED AS REMAINING WORK. A value list in
LABEL_VOCABULARY now filters BOTH rules, so DisputeReason.record and
Feedback.Category.triage - deliberately English, for the reviewer and for
support - are excluded with their reason instead of sitting in the number
forever.

⚠ AND THE STALENESS CHECK FOUND ITS OWN BUG. It asked only the label rule
whether an entry still matched; the two-owners strings are sentences, so only
is_copy sees them, and it reported a live entry as stale. It reads both rules
now. A guard whose own bookkeeping is wrong in the safe direction is still
wrong - this one would have made me delete a correct exclusion.

⚠ ALSO, FOR THE NEXT PERSON ON THIS MACHINE: the Kotlin daemon poisoned its
incremental cache mid-pass ("Could not close incremental caches ...
class-attributes.tab"). `gradlew --stop` plus `rm -rf app/build/kotlin` did NOT
clear it; only `rm -rf app/build` did, at the cost of a 7.5-minute cold build.
Same family as the poisoned-build-cache note in CLAUDE.md, different directory.

Verified: 2525 tests 0 failures, check-string-formats OK (1839 resources, en,
es), verified and grades-list goldens unchanged 17 of 17. | 2026-08-30 (eighteenth pass) THE HOME-SCREEN WIDGET, and a behaviour change I
made while "just" moving strings.

SHIPPED (commit a5163e74d): widget/WidgetCopy.kt. Baseline 721 in 145 files down
to 709 in 144.

The whole widget was English on a Spanish seller's home screen, TalkBack
sentence included - and that sentence is the only version of the widget a blind
seller ever gets.

WidgetCopy was PURE BY DESIGN, and the KDoc said why: a Glance composable cannot
be asserted in a JVM test, so the copy was pulled out to be checkable. Every
function takes a Context now, and the tests MOVED to a Robolectric
WidgetCopyTest rather than going away. Same assertions, same sentences, one more
parameter. Worth stating because "the code was pure so it could be tested" is a
real reason and the conversion had to preserve it, not trade it away.

The sentences stop being concatenated. "3 sales today, $412.00" was five appends
in a row; each is a format string with its arguments now and the counts are
plurals. Fourth instance of the same lesson in this story.

⚠ THE TEST CAUGHT A REGRESSION I INTRODUCED. updatedAgo had an explicit
`minutes < 0L -> null` branch with a comment: a clock that moved backwards
(timezone change, NTP correction) is not a reason to claim the future. I
rewrote it as `.coerceAtLeast(0L)` while shuffling the code around the resource
lookups, which turns "say nothing" into "Updated just now" - a widget claiming
numbers are fresh when it has no idea. The branch is restored with a note.

THE LESSON, and it applies to every remaining file: MOVING COPY IS NOT A NO-OP
REFACTOR WHEN THE COPY LIVES INSIDE THE LOGIC. Every one of these conversions
rewrites a `when` or a `buildString`, and a `when` is where the behaviour is.
The goldens catch layout and the unit tests catch this; a file with neither is a
file to be careful in.

Also: widget_sold_today already existed as "Sold today". check-string-formats
caught the duplicate name, which aapt2 would have rejected later and with a line
number 600 lines from the real one.

Verified: 2525 tests 0 failures, check-string-formats OK (1854 resources, en,
es), no-bare-strings OK. | 2026-08-30 (nineteenth pass) REFERRALS, including the message a seller sends
OUT of the app.

SHIPPED (commit d7130b2b4): referrals/ReferralTypes.kt, seventeen strings.
Baseline 709 in 144 files down to 692 in 143.

The share text is the one worth naming: a seller sends it to a friend by
WhatsApp or wherever, so it has to be in the seller's language, and it was
English. shareText returned a finished sentence built around the code and the
link; it returns the two PARTS now and the screen formats
R.string.referral_share_text. Fifth instance of the same lesson.

creditsSummary became creditsPerReferral returning an Int, with the singular
and plural in a plurals resource - which Spanish needs regardless, since the
noun changes and a Kotlin `if (n == 1)` cannot express that for every language.

redeemError is a UiMessage. Third user of that type after the mileage log and
bulk pricing, and it is the shape EdgeApiError will need at scale - this is the
third small proof before the 69-call-site one.

THE TESTS KEPT THEIR CLAIMS, and two of them were real claims:
  "every rejection says something specific" existed because a generic "that
  code isn't valid" in front of someone who typed their OWN code is a dead end.
  "pending and qualified are different kinds of not-yet" existed because one is
  waiting on the friend and the other on us.
Converting each to assertEquals(R.string.x, ...) asserts the plumbing and drops
both claims. They now check the ids AND that the set of distinct ids is as large
as the set of states. invalid_code and not_found deliberately share one sentence,
and the test says that out loud rather than pretending they differ.

That is the sixth file where the mechanical conversion would have silently
weakened a test. It is not an occasional hazard; it is what happens by default,
and it is worth stating as the rule: IF A TEST ASSERTS WORDS, IT IS ASSERTING A
PRODUCT DECISION - move the assertion, do not delete it.

Verified: 2525 tests 0 failures, check-string-formats OK (1868 resources, en,
es), referrals goldens unchanged 9 of 9. | 2026-08-30 (twentieth pass) EdgeApiError SPLIT OUT AS US-3025, and pushes
stopped at the user's request.

⚠ WORKFLOW CHANGE, mid-session and standing: the user asked me to HOLD COMMITS
LOCALLY and stop pushing. Their words: "Your consistent pushes are making my
CRON fail because every few minutes the edge container goes down to start the
new [deploy]". Every push to main triggers a Coolify redeploy and kills any cron
mid-flight - and it does that for ANDROID-ONLY commits too, because the deploy
is triggered by the push, not by the paths in it. Everything up to c4fbf0ff0 is
on origin; work after that is local until asked for. This supersedes the "good
to push, push regular" instruction from earlier the same day.

US-3025 FILED for platform/net/EdgeApiError.kt. It is the highest-value
untranslated file left - every error a seller reads, and the guard's own header
names error toasts as the reason it exists - and it is the third file this story
has deferred with a reason rather than half-doing.

SIZED PROPERLY RATHER THAN GUESSED: 20 strings, called from 43 files, roughly
two lines each. The cost is VOLUME, not difficulty, and the reason it wants its
own story is that a half-converted error path is worse than either end: the half
still returning String compiles, renders, and looks correct.

The pattern is already proven three times, each added deliberately as a smaller
rehearsal: the mileage log (UiMessage's original use), BulkPricing.rowErrors,
and ReferralsViewModel.redeemError. The story carries the plan, the six branches
that have no server detail, the two that must NOT leak their reason (Decoding
prints the raw reason; Network hides its OkHttp text on purpose because it names
the edge host), and a warning to check for tests asserting words before
converting them.

REMAINING AFTER THIS: 692 strings in 143 files. The photo/measurement vocabulary
cluster (128, needs the server-versus-local decision), EdgeApiError (20, now
US-3025), BackgroundRefresh's push fragments, and about ten mid-size mechanical
files. 111 files hold four strings or fewer. | 2026-08-30 (twenty-first pass) SCOUT AND PROSPECT, and a guard that stops the
worst error message in this whole story.

SHIPPED (commit 2fcfce888, LOCAL - not pushed, see the workflow note above).
Baseline 692 in 143 files down to 680 in 140.

UiMessage GAINS AN ARGS LIST, and the Scout plan wall is why. Its sentence is
ours and translates; the PLAN NAME inside it comes from the server. A server
NOUN to substitute is not the same thing as a server SENTENCE to prefer, and
`detail` was only ever the latter. That distinction now has a place to live, and
it is the shape US-3025 will need too.

The three error sources got one helper with the precedence written down rather
than repeated in two ViewModels: a plan wall wins (specific, and ours to
translate); otherwise the server's sentence (not ours, not localizable, usually
the only thing that says what happened); our fallback only if both are absent.

⚠ THE PLAN-WALL GOLDENS CHANGED AND THE OLD ONES WERE WRONG. Their fixtures said
"Scout is on Pro and above." - a sentence this app has never produced. The new
ones show what the wall actually says. That is the FOURTH over-claiming golden
this story has found, after the seven in US-2902, the Money viewport and the
onboarding gap. The pattern: a fixture written from memory of what a screen
probably says.

⚠ AND A GUARD FOR THE ERROR THAT COST THE MOST TIME. An unescaped `'` in a
string value makes aapt2 fail with "Can not extract resource from
com.android.aaptcompiler.ParsedResource@3f054c72" and a line number from the
MERGED values.xml - thousands of lines from the file anyone edits. It bit me on
2026-08-30 twice, hours apart, and the second time I did not recognise it either.
check-string-formats.py now names the file, the line, and the fix.
Sabotage-verified.

The root cause of BOTH occurrences was mine and is worth naming: a `\'` written
inside a bash heredoc loses its backslash. That is the same backslash-eating
trap CLAUDE.md already records for regexes in shell arguments, and it applies to
generated XML too. Write the script with a file, not a heredoc.

userStories.title: EPIC: Books and Taxes — bookkeeping a reseller can hand to an accountant, and a QuickBooks connection for the ones who already have one
userStories.description: Money today answers 'did that flip make money'. It does not answer 'what do I owe' or 'what do I give my accountant in March'. The gap is structural, not cosmetic. There is no chart of accounts, so the eight expense_category enum values map to no IRS line. There is no ledger, so every report re-derives its own totals from sales + inventory_items + flipdesk_expenses and two screens can legitimately disagree. There is no ending-inventory number, which Schedule C Part III line 41 requires and which nothing in the schema can compute. Marketplace facilitator sales tax sits in sales.tax and is never excluded from income. A 1099-K arrives reporting gross including shipping and sales tax, and nothing in the app bridges that number to the seller's actual profit. Mileage is an expense_category with no odometer, no purpose and no date-by-date log, which is not a record the IRS accepts. And there is no accounting integration of any kind: a grep for quickbooks, qbo or xero across src/, services/edge-functions/src/ and supabase/migrations/ returns zero hits. This epic is the umbrella. It closes when the child stories close.
acceptanceCriteria: Every child story in this epic is closed, or is explicitly deferred with the reason recorded here.
A seller can answer four questions from inside the app without a spreadsheet: what did I make, what do I owe, what can I deduct, and what do I hand my accountant.
One number is one number: the P&L, the tax packet, the Money overview and the QuickBooks push all read the same ledger, and a test proves they agree.
Nothing in this epic gives tax advice. Every computed figure names the form line it feeds and carries the not-tax-advice framing already used in the content module.

userStories.title: Mileage and receipts on the phone, where they actually happen
userStories.description: Both of these are captured at a thrift store, not at a desk. A mileage log filled in on a laptop three weeks later is the reconstructed record the IRS specifically discounts, and a receipt photographed on a phone and then uploaded from a computer is a step most people skip. iOS and Android already have the camera and the upload path from the photo work. This is the parity story, and it is deliberately last: the web surfaces have to settle first or this ports a moving target.
acceptanceCriteria: iOS and Android can both log a trip and photograph a receipt, offline-tolerant, syncing when the connection returns.
Receipt capture uses the same edge extraction as the web so there is one prompt and one set of results, not a second implementation that drifts.
The known dated-value sync bug is not repeated: US-2339 has Android expense dates walking back one day per edit cycle, which is a timezone defect, and a trip date is exactly the same shape of field.
Trip entry is two taps from the sourcing screen, because a feature that takes longer than the trip is a feature nobody uses.
Parity is verified with the parity-auditor rather than asserted.

notes.body:
ANDROID IS COMPLETE. Three commits: the data layer (Room table, version-9
migration, offline queue wiring, repository), the trip UI reachable in two
taps from Scout, and receipt capture through the shared edge extraction.
Verified on the Windows box: compileDebugKotlin clean, spotless and detekt
clean, 159 of 160 money unit tests passing. The one failure is
TabletLayoutScreenshotTest, which needs Java 21 for Robolectric and fails
identically on a pristine checkout.

AC3 is met and then some: the date rule now lives in ONE place
(CalendarDateField) with ExpenseDraft delegating to it, so trip_date cannot
repeat US-2339. CalendarDateFieldTest drives three round trips through six
zones either side of Greenwich and asserts the defect itself so the fix is
not a coincidence. It also caught a live residual: the add-expense button
seeded System.currentTimeMillis(), so an 8pm entry in Chicago pre-filled
tomorrow. Fixed.

AC5 was met with the parity-auditor rather than asserted, and the audit is
what produced US-3014.

iOS IS NOT STARTED and is now US-3014. It has NEITHER feature - audited,
not assumed. Swift cannot be compiled on this machine, so writing it here
would put code on main that nobody has ever seen build, and this repo does
not push, so CI would not catch it either.

A split was proposed to the owner four times across five loop iterations
with no answer. Filing US-3014 rather than closing this story: declaring
US-3000 done while iOS has nothing would be false, and narrowing its scope
is the owner call. This story stays open and points at US-3014.

userStories.title: Three clients, three grade ladders: the web has no Steel Navy band and Android's red matches no spec
userStories.description: As a seller who checks a grade on my phone and again on the laptop, I want the same garment to be the same colour, so that I do not think two different things were graded.
acceptanceCriteria: FOUND 2026-08-29 while fixing Android's failing-grade red (the fix shipped in the same commit as this filing). vault/20-domain/brand-design-system.md section 3B defines FOUR grade bands: Pristine/NWT 9.5-10.0 Emerald Mint #10B981, Excellent/NWOT 7.0-9.0 Steel Navy #0F3460, Good/Fair 5.0-6.5 Amber Gold #F59E0B, Poor/Damaged 1.0-4.5 Crimson Red #F03D5F.

THE WEB HAS NO STEEL NAVY BAND. src/lib/constants.ts getScoreColor is three bands: >7 emerald, >=5 amber, <5 red. Its own comment cites section 3B and paraphrases it as 'Emerald Mint (>7), Amber Gold (5-7), AA-safe brand red (<5)' - a three-band reading of a four-band spec that drops Steel Navy silently. getTierBadgeClasses is the same three bands with a fourth red (rose). So the web agrees with itself and with nothing else.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE COMMON CASE, NOT AN EDGE. Every grade from 7.0 to 9.4 renders GREEN on the web and NAVY on both mobile clients. GradeColor.kt calls 7.0-9.4 'the ordinary band - most resale garments land there'. A seller sees a different colour for the same garment depending on the device.

IT WAS NEVER DECIDED. US-605 CONSOLIDATED the ladder from code 'copy-pasted in 6+ files' and its note records the target as 'the media-kit emerald/amber/brand-red palette' - three colours, no navy. So the three-band shape was inherited from the copies, not chosen. Nothing in vault/ mentions getScoreColor at all.

AND A TEST PINS THE WRONG LADDER, which is what would make this look like a regression to fix: src/lib/__tests__/status-score-tokens.test.ts asserts getScoreColor(7.5) === 'text-emerald-500'. 7.5 is squarely inside the spec's Steel Navy band. Anyone correcting the ladder hits a red test that reads as though they broke something.

DECIDE WHICH IS AUTHORITATIVE before changing code. Either the web gains a Steel Navy band (matching the spec and both phones) or section 3B is amended to three bands (and iOS + Android change instead). This is a brand decision, not a bug fix - which is why it is filed rather than patched.

SEPARATELY, THE RED IS THREE DIFFERENT VALUES. Spec says #F03D5F. iOS uses exactly that. The web uses #cc1f3d. Android used #E94560, which matches nothing - now fixed to MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error (#CC1F3D light / #FB5E78 dark), deliberately aligning Android with the WEB rather than the spec, because #F03D5F is 3.79:1 on white and US-439 deepened it to #cc1f3d precisely because the vibrant red fails AA as text. constants.ts:1045 states the rule: never the surface red as a text colour on a light surface.

SO iOS DRAWS GRADE TEXT AT 3.79:1 in light mode, since it follows the spec value. It mitigates in two ways Android has neither of: GradeScale.tierSymbol (US-1281, Differentiate Without Color) gives each band its own SF Symbol, and the asset catalogue carries contrast:high variants (#C81E45 for red) that honour Increase Contrast. Whether that is sufficient is part of the same decision.

ALSO MEASURED, and it argues AGAINST a blanket restyle: on the DARK surface the literals are fine - emerald 6.72:1, amber 7.94:1, red 4.46:1 against Night. On WHITE they are not - emerald 2.54:1, amber 2.15:1, both far worse than the red that prompted this. That is true on web, iOS and Android alike, and nothing guards it: src/lib/a11y/__tests__/contrast.test.ts covers the red CTA and muted-foreground only, never getScoreColor.

ANDROID IS MISSING DARK AND HIGH-CONTRAST VARIANTS for the three non-navy bands. iOS defines four variants per colour (light, light high-contrast, dark, dark high-contrast); BrandPalette has a single fixed value for Emerald and Amber. Navy already resolves per theme via colorScheme.primary and red now via colorScheme.error, so only emerald and amber remain fixed.
userStories.notes:
2026-08-30 AC10 IS DONE. Android now has the four emerald and amber variants iOS has always had: BrandPalette gains EmeraldDark/EmeraldHighContrast/EmeraldDarkHighContrast and the three Amber equivalents, all ported byte-for-byte from ios/GradeThread/Assets.xcassets/Brand{Emerald,Amber}.colorset. New StatusColor.kt exposes statusEmerald() and statusAmber(), which resolve the four-way choice; gradeColor() calls them. Commit 1905da7ae.  THE LIGHT VALUES DELIBERATELY DO NOT MOVE, which is what keeps this separate from AC6. Picking Android's own numbers would BE the brand decision AC6 is waiting on; porting the ones iOS already ships is not a decision at all. Nothing anyone is looking at today changes. AC9's contrast problem is untouched and still real - emerald 2.54:1 and amber 2.15:1 on white - and the high-contrast variants only appear when the reader has Increase Contrast on.  MECHANISM: two CompositionLocals provided by GradeThreadTheme, LocalIsDarkTheme and LocalHighContrast. LocalIsDarkTheme is NOT isSystemInDarkTheme() and that is load-bearing: GradeThreadTheme takes darkTheme as a PARAMETER and every screenshot test passes it explicitly while Robolectric's system setting stays light, so a system read would return a light colour inside a golden captured as dark. LocalHighContrast samples Settings.Secure 'high_text_contrast_enabled' once at first composition, failing closed to false; the constant is @hide but the key string is not. Both are allowlisted with the reason in config/detekt/detekt.yml AND a new app/lint.xml - detekt and the Slack compose-lints Android lint check both ban new CompositionLocals, and the two allowlists must agree.  WHAT IS EXPLICITLY NOT DONE, counted rather than hand-waved: SEVENTEEN other sites still paint a status emerald or amber from a fixed token or a raw hex, and EIGHT of those use the raw hex (AiFillReviewSheet, GradeReportScreen x2, GradesListScreen x3, SalesScreen, DisclosureGeometry). A raw hex duplicating a token is the same shape US-3009 fixed for navy and red; these sit below that scan's threshold because the value is semantic rather than brand. BrandLiteralTest's header now says so and carries the count. statusEmerald/statusAmber are public precisely so the next pass has somewhere to land.  VERIFIED: 6 new cases in StatusColorTest (all four combinations asserted as hex, all four proven distinct, and gradeColor proven to follow the theme), sabotage-checked by collapsing the dark high-contrast branch - 2 cases red, restored. Four dark goldens re-recorded: screen-grades-bands-dark, screen-grades-refresherror-dark, screen-gradereport-pristine-dark, screen-gradereport-amber-dark. Those diffs ARE the fix. detekt, lint and the full 2241-test Roborazzi verify green apart from three pre-existing Money failures unrelated to this (see below).  ONE THING FOUND WHILE VERIFYING, not caused here: MoneyScreenshotTest equityLoaded_light / equityUnavailable_light and TabletLayoutScreenshotTest moneyOnATabletWidth_light fail on CLEAN HEAD - confirmed by reverting every file in this change and re-running. Stale goldens from recent Money work, left for whoever owns it. | 2026-09-04 THE ADOPTION PASS AC10 LEFT FOR "the next pass" IS DONE. The story stays OPEN on AC6, which is the owner's decision and not mine to take.

SEVEN CALL SITES NOW RESOLVE THROUGH statusEmerald()/statusAmber(): AiFillReviewSheet (confidence bands), GradeReportScreen (certificate integrity tone), GradesListScreen (pending badge + dispute tone), SalesScreen (pending chip), InfoCard (Success/Warning, which is the wide one - 23 screens use it), SyncStatusBar (pending background + foreground) and RadarNearbyScreen (WARM hotness). Light values are unchanged by construction, so nothing moves in the default theme; the diff is entirely dark and high-contrast.

THREE SITES DELIBERATELY DO NOT, and two of them MUST NOT. This is the part that matters, because "finish the migration" is the obvious next instruction and on two of these it would be a regression:
  - DisclosureGeometry.SeverityColor is painted into a BITMAP that is exported and shown to buyers. It must match the web's SEVERITY_COLOR, not the reader's theme - the same annotation has to be the same colour wherever the image is opened.
  - MeasurementPhotoEditorSheet draws over the seller's PHOTOGRAPH behind a white halo. A dark-theme variant solves for a background that is never there.
  - StatusStyle.tone is pure and unit-tested by seven assertions that read it directly. Making it @Composable costs that purity and needs the colour hoisted to every caller. Worth doing, worth doing deliberately - it is the one of the three that SHOULD eventually move.

THE COUNT IS NOW AN ASSERTION INSTEAD OF PROSE. BrandLiteralTest's header said "SEVENTEEN OTHER SITES DO NOT YET, and eight of those hold the raw hex" and nothing checked it, so it could only be right on the day it was typed - it was already stale before this pass started. NEW StatusColorAdoptionTest (3 cases) asserts the set both ways: any unlisted site fails, and any listed site that stops matching also fails, so the allowlist can only shrink. A third case pins the two must-not-move entries by name. SABOTAGE-VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: reverting RadarNearbyScreen to BrandPalette.Amber reddens the first case; making DisclosureGeometry stop carrying a status colour reddens the other two. Both restored.

THIRTEEN GOLDENS RE-RECORDED, ALL DARK, and each diff was checked rather than assumed. Pixel analysis of screen-radar-dark: 1895 pixels, 245,158,11 -> 255,184,60, which is Amber -> AmberDark exactly. screen-fulfillment-shipped-dark: 2921 pixels, 16,185,129 -> 52,211,153, Emerald -> EmeraldDark. No structural change in either. The gradereport and grades compare images were reviewed by eye: the only thing that moves is the "Pending review" badge and the "Certificate verified" callout.

⚠ TWENTY MORE GOLDENS CAME BACK IN THE SAME GIT STATUS AND ARE NOT MINE. Drafts (8) and Prospect (12) re-record differently on a tree with NO source changes at all, so they were already stale in the repo. Telling them apart took six clean-tree recording runs. Full detail is on US-3030; the reason it is recorded there and not here is that it is a property of those two classes, not of this change. They were reverted, so this commit carries thirteen goldens and no others.

WHAT WAS VERIFIED, and what was not. Green: compileDebugKotlin, spotlessCheck, detekt, the three new cases, StatusStyleTest, BrandLiteralTest, and verifyRoborazziDebug for GradeReportScreenshotTest + GradesListScreenshotTest (6 of the 13 goldens). Full unit suite: 2550 tests, 6 failures, five of which were proven pre-existing by re-running them against a stashed clean tree (ProspectRolesTest x4, ProcessedPathsOnlyTest) and one of which is FLAKY (TwoFactorPolicyTest failed once in a full run and passed on a targeted re-run of the same tree).

NOT verified: the remaining 7 goldens were never put through verifyRoborazziDebug. Eight attempts were killed by the environment - five as background tasks that died with no output, and one that I invalidated myself by running gradlew --stop underneath it, which returned exit code 0 while the log said "Gradle build daemon has been stopped". That exit code nearly went into these notes as a pass. What stands in for verify on those 7: each of their classes was proven stable on a clean tree, so the diff is attributable to this change alone, and two of the seven were pixel-analysed as exact colour substitutions.

AND THE LINT LANE CANNOT PASS FOR ANYONE RIGHT NOW: :app:lintDebug fails on main at Autolister.kt:69 with a ResourceType error that has nothing to do with this work. Filed as US-3115.

STILL OPEN AND STILL THE OWNER'S CALL - AC6. The web renders every grade from 7.0 to 9.4 GREEN while both phones render it NAVY, and that is the ordinary band most resale garments land in. Either the web gains a Steel Navy band to match the spec and both phones, or vault section 3B is amended to three bands and both phones change instead. Nothing in this pass touches it, because picking one would be answering a brand question with a code change.

userStories.title: Buying an eBay shipping label is a Pro capability, and postage is passed through at cost
userStories.description: As a Pro seller, I want buying an eBay shipping label to be part of my plan, so the ship step stays in the app and the postage lands in my books without me typing it. US-2160 already built the whole eBay Sell Logistics slice - rate shopping, buy, reprint, void, the real cost written to sales.shipping_cost, and src/lib/ledger-math.ts:175 posting it to the shipping_postage account. Two things were missing. It was ungated, so it would have been free on every tier the moment eBay grants the scope (US-2380). And nothing said what it costs. This closes both: a shippingLabels gate flag at Pro and up, enforced on the two routes that spend money, with postage passed through at eBay's own rate and no markup. Markup was considered and rejected: eBay's built-in label flow and Pirate Ship are both free at the same commercial rates, so a margin would be found by any seller comparing receipts, and this is a product whose whole pitch is being the honest party.
acceptanceCriteria: A shippingLabels flag exists in GateFlags (services/edge-functions/src/lib/pricing-config.ts) and FlipdeskGateFlags (src/lib/constants.ts): false on free and starter, true on pro and business, in both the type and FALLBACK_MATRIX/FLIPDESK_PLANS.

Migration 00696 merges the key into public.pricing_plans.gate_flags for all four plans, only where absent, because the DB row is canonical and a missing key resolves to a hard false on every tier (the US-2687 / connectorAccess failure).
src/test/plan-gate-flags-seeded.test.ts passes, and fails when 00696 is removed - proving the guard is not vacuous.

logisticsCapability() takes a third planAllows argument and returns a plan_locked code; the order is deployment scope, then plan, then reconnect, so a seller on a deployment eBay has not licensed is never sold an upgrade that would buy them nothing.
planAllows defaults to true so logisticsFailure()'s existing two-argument call still reports a scope 403 as reconnect_required rather than as an upsell.

POST /rates and POST /label are gated and return 402 with code plan_locked when the plan excludes it; GET /label (reprint) and POST /label/void are NOT gated, so a seller who downgrades can still print a label they bought and still claim its refund.
The plan is resolved on workspaceOwnerId, so a team seat inherits the workspace plan rather than their own.
The ship dialog shows an upgrade prompt for plan_locked only, and keeps hiding the buy path for feature_unavailable and reconnect_required, since neither is fixed by paying us.
GATE_FEATURE_COPY in src/lib/plan-gates.ts has a plain-English sentence for shippingLabels, and the Pro and Business feature bullets say postage is at eBay's rate with no markup.
EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION is bumped to 00696 in the same commit and the migration self-records its version (US-1108 triple); the migration contains no REVOKE.
No code path adds a percentage or per-label fee on top of the carrier rate.
userStories.notes:
Rescoped 2026-08-29, same sitting it was filed. The first draft added EasyPost as a second label provider, a prepaid postage wallet and carrier-adjustment chargebacks. Owner chose eBay-direct instead, and that is the cheaper shape by a lot: eBay bills the SELLER's own eBay account for the postage and for any reweigh adjustment, so we never hold seller money, never float postage, and never have to reconcile a carrier bill that lands three weeks later. The wallet, the Stripe top-up and the adjustment ledger all disappeared with that one decision. What it costs is coverage - eBay Logistics only covers eBay orders, so a Shopify sale or an extension-listed Poshmark sale still has no in-app label path. File that as its own story if sellers ask for it.

STILL DARK. None of this can run until eBay grants sell.logistics on the prod keyset (US-2380), and the capability check puts the deployment scope AHEAD of the plan check deliberately, so today every seller on every plan still gets feature_unavailable. That ordering is tested, not incidental: showing a Starter seller an upgrade prompt for a capability no plan can currently reach would be selling something that does not exist yet.

userStories.title: iOS: a mileage log and receipt capture, neither of which exists today
userStories.description: The iOS half of US-3000, split out because it could not be verified on the Windows dev box and was blocking that story from closing. Android shipped complete over three commits (data layer, trip UI reachable in two taps from Scout, receipt capture through the shared edge extraction). iOS has NEITHER feature and the absence was audited rather than assumed: rg -i mileage ios/ returns three files and all three are the expense CATEGORY enum; TripDraft/MileageView/MileageStore/VehicleUse return zero; mileage_trips/mileage_rates/vehicle_use_years/mileage_summary appear in no Swift file. For receipts, every -i receipt hit in ios/ is a different meaning (the App Store receipt in DiagnosticsSection.swift, a comment about the internal photo slot, and plain English in AutoListerView); flipdesk/expenses appears in no Swift file; VNDocumentCamera and VisionKit are absent. ExpenseFormSheet.swift has no photo, camera or image control at all. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS TO BUILD ON: the offline mutation queue Android was ported FROM (ios/GradeThread/Persistence/OfflineMutationQueue.swift, PendingMutationActor.swift, SyncEngine.swift), and ExpenseStore.swift already returns .savedOffline. Persistence is SwiftData, so a trip needs a new @Model plus a schema-version entry - and note the duplicate-checksum launch crash trap in this repo memory. Swift cannot be compiled on the Windows box; iOS CI on macOS runners is the only safety net, and this repo does not push, so nothing verifies until the owner does.
acceptanceCriteria: A trip log on iOS: date, miles, purpose, optional from/to, round trip. Offline-tolerant through the existing OfflineMutationQueue, returning the same three-way saved / queued / failed the expense store already returns.

The date rule is NOT reimplemented. trip_date is a DATE column and US-1494 already settled this on iOS with ExpenseStore.bucketingCalendar, a UTC calendar. Parsing, formatting and bucketing happen in one zone, in one named place, exactly as Android now does in CalendarDateField.

Receipt capture on iOS calls the SAME edge extraction (POST /api/flipdesk/expenses/extract, then /adopt-staged). One prompt and one set of results, never a second implementation that drifts. Android does this in ReceiptScanService.kt and is the model to copy.
The model proposes and the seller confirms: the scan opens the ordinary expense form pre-filled and never writes a row.
Save then attach, and the attach is best effort. An expense with no receipt is a correct expense; a receipt with no expense is a file nobody finds.

Trip entry is two taps from a screen the seller is already on when they arrive at a shop. Android put it on Scout; iOS has SourcesView, ScoutView and ProspectView, and which one is a design call to make rather than to assume.
Parity is verified with the parity-auditor against the shipped Android surface, not asserted.
It compiles. Nothing here can be verified on the Windows dev box, so the owner runs iOS CI before this closes.

userStories.title: EasyPost as the second label provider, on seller-billed sub-accounts so we never touch the postage money
userStories.description: As a seller whose sale did not come from eBay - or whose platform eBay never granted the logistics scope to - I want to buy a shipping label in FlipDesk anyway, so the ship step does not depend on one marketplace's approval. US-3011 shipped the Pro gate and US-2160 shipped the eBay path, and the eBay path is dark pending US-2380. This adds EasyPost behind the same route surface as the fallback and as the answer for Shopify and extension-listed sales. THE BILLING MODEL IS THE WHOLE DESIGN: EasyPost referral customers on EasyPost-Managed Billing, where the seller enters their own card with EasyPost through Stripe and EasyPost charges THEM for postage. We never front postage, never hold a float, and carry no liability for a carrier reweigh that lands three weeks later. The prepaid wallet, the Stripe top-up and the adjustment-chargeback ledger that the first draft of US-3011 called for all disappear with that one choice, and they were most of the work.
acceptanceCriteria: A services/edge-functions/src/lib/easypost.ts wraps rate shopping, label buy, refund/void and shipment read-back, mirroring the exported shape of lib/ebay-logistics.ts so one route surface serves both providers.

Sellers are onboarded as EasyPost ReferralCustomers under our partner account, on EasyPost-Managed Billing: the seller's own card is charged by EasyPost for postage, and no GradeThread-held balance, wallet or float exists anywhere in the code.

A seller with no EasyPost sub-account or no payment method on it gets a clean onboarding prompt, never a failed purchase - the same contract as the eBay capability gate, checked before the buy button renders.

routes/flipdesk-logistics.ts picks the provider per sale: an eBay order on a connection holding the sell.logistics grant uses eBay; every other sale, and every sale when the deployment has no logistics scope, uses EasyPost. The rates response names the provider it used.

logisticsCapability() generalizes past its eBay shape: the feature_unavailable state must stop meaning 'this deployment has no eBay scope' once a second provider can serve the same seller, or an eBay rejection leaves the fallback unreachable behind a check about eBay.
The existing Pro gate (shippingLabels, US-3011) covers the EasyPost path unchanged - rates and buy gated, reprint and void open - with no second flag and no plan-matrix migration.
An EasyPost purchase writes the same sales columns the eBay path writes: shipping_cost, tracking_number, carrier, label_purchased_at, and never overwrites a real cost with 0.
For an eBay-sourced sale whose label was bought through EasyPost, the tracking number still reaches eBay through the existing createShippingFulfillment call rather than a second implementation.
Label cost continues to post to the shipping_postage account through src/lib/ledger-math.ts with no provider-specific branch, so the P&L is right whichever provider bought the label.
A label purchase is never automatically retried: EasyPost buy is idempotent only on its own terms, so an unclear 5xx is settled by reading the shipment back, never by re-posting.
Every new route is tenant-scoped per US-268 and has a case in tenant-isolation_test.ts; the seller-to-EasyPost-sub-account mapping is owner-scoped and never read from a request body.

EASYPOST_API_KEY (partner account) is documented in vault/10-ops/env-reference.md and services/edge-functions/.env.example. With the key absent, the EasyPost path reports unavailable rather than throwing a 500.
Postage is passed through at cost on this path too: no percentage, no per-label fee, nothing added to the carrier rate.

userStories.title: eBay drops every descriptive aspect value the AI produces, because nothing maps Taupe onto Beige
userStories.description:
The AI capture pass describes a garment the way a seller would, and eBay's SELECTION_ONLY aspects accept only their own coarse list. Nothing bridged the two, so the descriptive value was dropped and the seller saw an empty field on a listing whose photos plainly answer it.

Color came back Taupe or Sage Green; eBay wants Beige and Green. Dress Length came back Mini or Maxi; eBay wants Short, Knee Length, Midi, Long, Hi-Low, Asymmetric. Same for Neckline, Pattern, Sleeve Length, Rise, shaft height and hardware colour.

The values were already there to check against: every category a seller opens in the composer caches its verbatim getItemAspectsForCategory response in public.ebay_category_aspects. What was missing was the mapping. aspect-normalize.ts only knew spelling EQUIVALENCES (M = Medium, Poly = Polyester, Grey = Gray), which run in either direction and therefore cannot narrow anything.

Adds directional family tables to that file as step 6 of the cascade: a specific value names the coarse buckets it belongs to, in preference order, and the first bucket the category actually allows wins. It runs LAST, so a category offering Navy or Olive outright still keeps them. When no bucket is allowed the value is still refused, so the old "wrong is worse than empty" rule holds; a COARSER value is not wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: aspect-normalize.ts gains directional family tables for colour, hem length, sleeve, neckline, pattern, fit, rise, closure, occasion, season, heel, toe, shaft and strap, applied as step 6 AFTER every existing exact/equivalence path so an exactly-offered value is never coarsened
A compound value with no table entry resolves by reading its tokens right to left (Sage Green -> Green, Dark Olive Green -> Green, Heather Charcoal -> Gray)
The file stays a single-file verbatim mirror at src/lib/aspect-normalize.ts; both test suites cover the new step

scripts/aspect-value-coverage.ts reads ebay_category_aspects back and reports, per aspect, which values still resolve to null against the real allowed lists; --reference prints the harvested allowed-value union
OPERATOR: run scripts/aspect-value-coverage.ts against prod once the cache is warm, and fold any reported misses into the family tables
userStories.notes:
2026-08-30. AC1-AC4 done; AC5 is the operator run and is why this stays open.

Family tables landed in services/edge-functions/src/lib/aspect-normalize.ts as step 6 of normalizeAspectValue, mirrored verbatim to src/lib/aspect-normalize.ts. Fourteen kinds, picked by the aspect display name with the specific test first, so "Hardware Color" reaches colour and "Sleeve Length" reaches sleeve rather than hem.

MEASURED, not asserted. 87 descriptive values (the ones the ai-extract prompt hints actually tell the model to produce) run against eBay's real apparel lists: 83/87 resolved on the first pass, and the four misses were real table gaps, not test noise. Knee-Length had no bucket in a Mini/Midi/Maxi skirt list, Henley listed Round Neck but not Crew Neck, Tie-Dye and Houndstooth listed only their own spellings. Adding the fallback buckets took it to 87/87. Edge suite 20 passed / 0 failed, web mirror 11 passed / 0 failed, tsc -b clean, deno lint + check clean.

ORDERING CARRIES THE JUDGEMENT, and that is the part to read before editing the tables. Coral is shelved under Pink before Orange and Teal under Blue before Green because those are the buckets eBay buyers filter on. A value that belongs to neither bucket more than the other is deliberately absent from the table, so it falls through to null and a human fills it.

WHAT WAS ALREADY THERE, so nobody rebuilds it: eBay's real allowed values per category have been cached in public.ebay_category_aspects since 00030 (30-day TTL, shared across all users, read-through in lib/ebay-client.ts getCategoryAspects), and the aspect REFINE pass already builds a JSON-schema enum from them (ai-extract.ts buildAspectTool). Neither was the gap. The gap was the five column-owned attributes (Brand/Size/Color/Material/Style) plus the wider canonical set, which the capture pass writes as free text on purpose, and which then had only spelling equivalences to get them onto eBay's list.

AC5, for whoever runs it: deno run --allow-net --allow-env scripts/aspect-value-coverage.ts against prod. It is read-only on one cache table. --reference prints the harvested allowed-value union per aspect, which is the "one big reference" without anyone researching eBay by hand. It could not be run here; no prod service-role key is on this box (.env.example only). | 2026-08-30, second pass. The first cut fixed the wrong half, and running AC5 against prod is what showed it.

WHAT THE PROD CACHE SAID. 121 cached categories. Color is FREE_TEXT in 107 of them and still ships 25 allowed values. Pattern FREE_TEXT in 82 with 222 values, Neckline FREE_TEXT in 26 with 16, Sleeve Length FREE_TEXT in 38, Fit in 52, Closure in 67, Rise in 10, Toe Shape in 9, Dress Length in 1. Almost nothing the seller complained about is SELECTION_ONLY.

FREE_TEXT on eBay means "we will accept a value we did not list", not "we listed none", and its buyer filters are built from the list it did publish. normalizeAspectValue returned raw on line 3 for anything that was not SELECTION_ONLY, so every family table added in the first pass never ran for Color, Pattern, Neckline, Sleeve Length, Fit, Closure, Rise, Toe Shape or Dress Length. Taupe was never dropped. It published fine and then sat outside every Beige search, which is exactly what the seller reported and not what the first pass assumed.

The early return is gone. An open list now tries to land on a listed value and falls back to the seller's words; a closed list still refuses. Nothing that shipped before stops shipping. Step 5 (whole-word containment) is now closed-list only: prod ships Brand as FREE_TEXT with 27,421 values, Model 17,374, Character 13,713, and a lone containment hit at that size is coincidence more often than intent.

THREE THINGS PROD CORRECTED that no amount of reading would have. Rise and Heel Height are stated as measured RANGES ("High (Greater than 12 in)", "Mid (2-2.9 in)"), so matchFamily now also compares a bucket against the label before the parenthesis, and only when exactly one allowed value carries it, so "Low" cannot reach "Ultra Low (Less than 8 in)". Heel Height and Heel Style are separate aspects taking different answers (a range versus Block/Cone/Cuban/Flat/Kitten/Spool/Stiletto/Wedge) and one table answering both put a wrong value in one of them every time. Leg shape is its own aspect: prod's Fit list is Athletic/Classic/Extra-Slim/Regular/Relaxed/Slim, so Bootcut and Wide Leg could never land there.

MEASURED AGAIN against the verbatim prod lists: 121/135 land on a listed value, up from effectively zero for the FREE_TEXT fields. Of the 14 remaining, four are deliberate refusals (Wedge and Platform and Block are shapes, not heights; Bootcut is a leg shape, not a fit width), one is a value eBay has no bucket for (Neckline has no hood), one is real (Season has no "All Seasons"), and five are Pattern values I could not confirm because the sample printed only 14 of its 222 values.

Edge suite 27 passed / 0 failed, web mirror 14 passed / 0 failed, tsc -b clean, deno lint and check clean, mirrors byte-identical.

THE SCRIPT HAD ITS OWN BUG, worth recording because its output read exactly like a catastrophic failure. It matched an aspect name to a vocabulary in BOTH directions, so the aspect "Type" picked up the "Strap Type" word list and a shoe category that allows only "Flat" was reported 0/160. A vocabulary aimed at the wrong aspect is indistinguishable from broken code in the output. Now matched by exact name plus an explicit alias table. Its Strap Type vocabulary was also wrong on the facts: prod says that aspect belongs to activewear tops (Halter, Racerback, Spaghetti, Strapless, Wide Strap), and bag straps live under Handle Style.

STILL OPEN: Pattern and Occasion need their full value lists before the last gaps can be judged. Run scripts/aspect-value-coverage.ts --reference --aspect Pattern and the same for Occasion. | 2026-08-30, third pass. Read the full Pattern and Occasion lists back rather than the 14-value sample the audit prints.

FOUR OF THE FIVE PATTERN "MISSES" WERE THE SAMPLE, NOT THE CODE. Pattern carries 222 distinct values and the audit prints the first 14 of one category, so Solid, Striped, Polka Dot and Tie Dye all read as dropped when every one of them is on the real list. The lesson is in the audit output, not the mapping: a truncated fixture and a genuine gap are indistinguishable on the page, and I acted on the truncation twice before checking.

THE ACCENT BUG IS THE ONE WORTH REMEMBERING. loose() reduces to a whitelist of a-z0-9, which DELETES an accented letter rather than folding it. eBay ships "Ombré". That reduced to "ombr" while our own "Ombre" reduced to "ombre", so the two never matched, on a pair of strings that look identical in any report. loose() now runs NFD and strips combining marks first. This was never about Pattern; every accented value in the taxonomy had the same silent miss.

TWO REAL MAPPING GAPS, both invisible from the sample. Prod names the animal (Leopard Print, Zebra Print, Snakeskin Print, Cow Print, Tiger Print, Giraffe Print, Dalmation Print) as well as carrying the Animal Print umbrella, so the specific print is now preferred and the umbrella is the fallback for the short lists. And prod has no Heathered and no Marled at all; the cloth they describe is Flecked.

OCCASION IS 25 VALUES, and about a third of the 80 categories carry a workwear-shaped subset with no Formal and no Wedding on it, which is what the first audit was reporting as 20-22/59 misses. Every dressy value now has a Special Occasion fallback, Work reaches Business or Workwear or Wear to Work, Beach reaches Summer/Beach, Club reaches Clubwear. A list with genuinely no dressy bucket still leaves Formal alone, which is right: there is nothing on it that means Formal.

MEASURED: 42/47 against the verbatim lists. All five remaining are correct refusals -- two Pattern values on a 14-value list with no graphic or tie-dye bucket, three Occasion values on a list with no dressy half. Edge suite 31 passed / 0 failed, web mirror 17 passed / 0 failed, tsc -b clean, deno lint and check clean, mirrors byte-identical.

ONE TEST EXPECTATION WAS MINE, NOT THE CODE'S: prod carries Cocktail outright, so step 1 returns Cocktail rather than coarsening to Party/Cocktail. The test now asserts both, with a list that lacks the bare value for the compound case.

AC5 IS SATISFIED FOR THE AUDIT ITSELF -- it has been run against prod three times and each run corrected something. What remains before this closes is a rerun after these changes to confirm the numbers, and that rerun is the last thing the story is waiting on. | 2026-08-30, fourth pass. Reran the audit against all 121 categories after the third-pass changes.

THE NUMBER. Open lists went from 1641/5914 landing to 5707/6028 (321 off-list, down from 4273). Colour, Rise, Dress Length, Skirt Length, Exterior Color and Hardware Color now report "every value lands on a listed value in every category". SELECTION_ONLY moved 660/822 to 666/822.

THE LARGEST REMAINING CAUSE WAS OURS, NOT THE MAPPING. 70 of the 156 SELECTION_ONLY empties are the single value "All Seasons", which the CANONICAL_ATTRIBUTES hint in ai-extract.ts asked the model to produce and which eBay does not carry in ANY of the 70 categories that have a Season aspect. The mapping could never have fixed that; the hint was wrong. It now asks for exactly Spring/Summer/Fall/Winter and says to omit a year-round garment. That is the shape worth remembering: an audit that only measures the mapping will keep reporting a prompt defect as a coverage gap.

TWO SMALL REAL FIXES: crossbody now reaches "Crossbody Strap" (prod's actual Handle Style value) before falling back to Shoulder Strap, and the audit's own Strap Type vocabulary dropped "Adjustable", which is not one of that aspect's five values.

EVERYTHING ELSE LEFT IS A CORRECT REFUSAL, checked one by one. Fit/Bootcut 52/52 and Leg Style/Cargo and Cropped 13/13 are values those lists genuinely do not carry (prod's Leg Style is Bootcut/Flared/Skinny/Straight/Tapered/Wide-Leg, so cargo is a pocket and cropped is a length). Neckline/Hooded 26/26: eBay's Neckline has no hood. Heel Style/Platform 4/4: its list is Block/Cone/Cuban/Flat/Kitten/Spool/Stiletto/Wedge. Occasion still ships empty in about 20 of 59 SELECTION_ONLY categories that carry a workwear-shaped list with no dressy value at all. The remaining Pattern counts (Plaid 4/82, Houndstooth 3/82, Striped 1/82) are odd non-apparel categories with two- or three-value lists.

A STALE FIXTURE FAILED AS A REGRESSION, which is the second time this story has produced that shape. src/lib/__tests__/ebay-prefill.test.ts had a case built on "Chartreuse" precisely BECAUSE it was unmappable; the family tables now resolve it to Green, so the column value became expressible and the projection overwrote a manual value exactly as it is designed to. The behaviour is right and the fixture was the thing that aged. It now uses "Iridescent", with a second case asserting the overwrite explicitly so the design is pinned rather than resting on a value's accidental unmappability.

VERIFIED: web 1540 passed / 0 failed across 106 files, edge aspect+ebay+publish suites 329 passed / 0 failed, edge extract suites 75 passed / 0 failed, tsc -b clean, deno lint and check clean, mirrors byte-identical. Note the edge suites need -A (or at least --allow-read): several read source files off disk to assert cross-client parity, and without it they fail as NotCapable, which reads like eight broken tests. | 2026-08-30, fifth pass. Different question from the first four: not "is the value we send usable" but "does the field get filled at all", which is the one that decides whether a listing is findable. Added a --coverage mode to scripts/aspect-value-coverage.ts and ran it against the 121 cached categories.

TWO OF THE THREE SUSPECTED RISKS WERE NOT REAL. The categories average 27 aspects and 0 of 121 exceed MAX_AI_ASPECTS (45), so nothing is being cut by that cap and raising it would buy nothing. I had guessed 40-60 out loud beforehand and was wrong; the measurement is the only reason that guess did not turn into a change.

THE VALUE CAP WAS REAL AND IT WAS HURTING EVERY LISTING. Exactly three SELECTION_ONLY aspects run past MAX_ALLOWED_VALUES_PER_ASPECT (150): Country of Origin at 244 values in ALL 121 categories, Year Manufactured at 159 in one, Silhouette at 7,286 in two. eBay returns countries in its own order, so a 150-value cut removed most of the late alphabet -- Vietnam, Thailand, Turkey, Taiwan, Sri Lanka, Portugal, Philippines, Pakistan, Romania, Tunisia, United States -- which between them are most of what a resale seller holds. The model was asked where a garment was made and handed a menu with the answer missing. Raised to 300, which clears the first two outright. Silhouette stays capped and always will.

THE TYPE GAP, WHICH IS THE ONE WORTH UNDERSTANDING. eBay's Type aspect is REQUIRED in 36 of the 121 cached categories and no registry entry could fill it in 33 of them. The cause is not an oversight: the style COLUMN lists ["Style", "Type"] and ownedAspectName deliberately binds each entry to exactly ONE aspect, because one column writing two aspects is the bug that made Type uneditable on Women's Tops. So wherever both names exist, Style wins and Type is left for the AI -- on a REQUIRED field, where empty blocks the publish.

Nothing we captured answered it either. `style` is the marketing style name (Sheath, Trucker), `product_line` is the family (501, Dri-FIT); neither is a Blouse. Added CANONICAL_ATTRIBUTES key `product_type` -- what KIND of item this is in eBay's Type vocabulary -- and an attribute-sourced registry entry mapping it to ["Type"]. Attribute-sourced ON PURPOSE: garment_category is a real Postgres ENUM column, and a column entry would flow into reverseColumnAspects, so a seller typing "Cardigan" into the Type specific would write an out-of-enum value and 500 the save.

Four behaviours pinned in aspect-registry_test.ts: it fills Type when the style column owns Style; a lowercase capture ("t-shirt") takes eBay's casing on a SELECTION_ONLY Type; it STANDS DOWN in the ~3 categories where the style column owns Type, since columnAspectProjection re-asserts the column authoritatively there anyway; and it never overwrites a user-set Type.

THE COUNT GUARD DID EXACTLY WHAT IT WAS WRITTEN FOR. canonical-attributes_test.ts pins the attribute count and its comment says to bump it only after checking the truncation canary. The canary was run first and passes, so 41 -> 42 is deliberate rather than a red test made green. Both halves of the reason are now in that comment.

STILL NOT MEASURED, and it is the honest limit of all of this: everything above measures what CAN fill deterministically, not what actually IS filled on live listings. The remaining six unowned required aspects (Outer Shell Material 6 categories, Insect Repellent Treated 3, Inseam 2, Exterior Color 1, Exterior Material 1, Game 1) are all reachable by the AI refine pass, which is asked about every required aspect, so "AI only" is not the same as "empty". A query over inventory_items.ebay_aspects for real fill rate per aspect is the measurement that would settle it.

VERIFIED: web tsc -b clean and 1540 passed / 0 failed across 106 files; registry, drift, canonical-attribute, priority, normalize, parity and prompt-candidate suites 126+ passed / 0 failed; deno lint clean on all six changed files; vendored src/lib/ebay-aspect-registry.json regenerated via scripts/sync-aspect-registry.mjs and the drift guard is green.

userStories.title: EdgeApiError returns a String, so every error a seller sees is English
userStories.description: platform/net/EdgeApiError.kt's userMessage() returns a built String, and it is the single highest-value untranslated file left on Android: it is EVERY error a seller reads. no-unlocalized-copy.py's own header names error toasts as the reason that guard exists. Measured 2026-08-30: 20 strings in the file, called from 43 files. THE SHAPE IS WHY IT WAS NOT DONE INSIDE US-2976. Most branches are 'detail ?: fallback', where detail is the SERVER's sentence. Translating the fallback alone gives a Spanish seller Spanish only in the cases where the server said nothing, which is the least useful half. The answer already exists in this repo and has been proven three times: com.gradethread.app.ui.UiMessage, a @StringRes id plus a nullable server detail, with the renderer showing detail when there is one. Its three users so far are the mileage log (US-2891), BulkPricing.rowErrors and ReferralsViewModel.redeemError, each added deliberately as a smaller rehearsal for this one. THE COST IS VOLUME, NOT DIFFICULTY. userMessage(): String becomes userMessage(): UiMessage; each ViewModel's errorMessage: String? becomes UiMessage?; each render site becomes 'it.detail ?: stringResource(it.res)'. 43 files, roughly two lines each. A HALF-CONVERTED ERROR PATH IS WORSE THAN EITHER END, because the half that still returns String looks fine, so this wants to land as one change rather than a file at a time.
acceptanceCriteria: userMessage() returns a UiMessage. Every branch that is currently 'detail ?: literal' becomes UiMessage(R.string.x, detail), so the server's sentence still wins when there is one and ours is translated when there is not.
All 43 calling files are converted in the same change. A half-converted error path is the failure mode: the half still returning String compiles, renders and looks correct.
The branches with no server detail at all - Unauthorized, WorkspaceMfaRequired, WorkspaceAccessRevoked, OfferNotOpen, SubscriptionConflict, PurchaseNotOwned - are plain resources with no detail.

Decoding and Network keep their reason OUT of the user-facing text. Decoding currently renders 'Unexpected response from server: $reason' and Network deliberately hides its reason already, with a comment explaining that OkHttp names the edge host in it. Do not let the conversion leak either.
check-string-formats passes across en and es, and no-unlocalized-copy's baseline for platform/net/EdgeApiError.kt reaches 0.

Any test asserting the WORDS of an error moves its assertion to values/strings.xml rather than becoming assertEquals(R.string.x, ...). Six files in US-2976 would have silently lost a product claim to that conversion; check for it here before assuming there is none.
userStories.notes: Blocked-on discovery 2026-08-31: platform/net/PlanGate.kt is entangled and must land in the SAME change. PlanGateError.title and .recommendation are composed by EdgeApiError.kt:225 as "${gate.title}. ${gate.recommendation}" — so converting either to a UiMessage breaks userMessage(), and EdgeApiError is a plain error type with no Context to render one. PlanGate's own shape is worth doing properly when it lands: title splices capLabel(cap) into "You've reached your X limit", which wants a whole sentence per cap (activeListings, aiActions, includedGrades, marketplaces, teamSeats, plus the fallback) rather than a fragment glued in, and PlanGatePresentation.kt:85 splices the same capLabel into a second sentence. prettyPlan() should stay untranslated for the same reason billing/SubscriptionCatalog.kt is in LABEL_VOCABULARY: plan names are product names. 5 strings in PlanGate.kt, still in the no-unlocalized-copy baseline.

userStories.title: Android /prospect sends no imageRoles, so it can never reach visual search
userStories.description: MEASURED 2026-08-30 while doing US-3026. ScoutService.kt:95 builds ProspectRequest(images, costCents) and the data class has no imageRoles field at all. The server decides who identifies a prospect purely from the roles (planProspectIdentification, US-2759), and an absent or unrecognised role is deliberately NOT permission - so every Android scan takes the no-usable-role branch, reads the tag, and can never reach eBay visual search however good a garment shot the seller took. It also means the identification prompt captions Android photos 'Photo 0' / 'Photo 1' rather than 'Close-up of the brand/size tag', which US-3026 added precisely because a model that knows which photo is a care label stops trying to read a silhouette out of it. THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIELD ADD. iOS earns its roles from named capture slots (US-2923): the seller states what each photo shows, because guessing the role from a photo's POSITION is the tempting shortcut and the wrong one - a seller who photographs only the care label would have it labelled 'front', and US-2758 measured a care label returning a midi dress, joggers and a mini skirt with no expressed doubt. Android's ProspectScreen has a generic strip of up to two photos with no slot identity, so the capture UI is the actual work.
acceptanceCriteria: ProspectScreen captures into two NAMED slots (item photo, brand tag) the way ProspectView does, rather than a generic strip. Do not infer the role from list position.
ProspectRequest carries imageRoles parallel to images, and a photo that fails to encode drops its ROLE with it rather than shifting the remaining roles up.

userStories.title: Play billing copy is English, and Conflict.message is the head of the chain
userStories.description: PlayPurchaseRules.Conflict.message returns a String, and it is the head of a chain that US-2976 could not convert file-by-file. Converting it to @StringRes was attempted on 2026-08-31 and REVERTED in the same session, on purpose: BillingRepository has no Context, so the Int cannot be resolved there, which forces PurchaseOutcome.Failed.message to become a UiMessage, which forces FIVE separate 'errorMessage: String?' state classes to follow - ConsumerCreditTopUpViewModel, CreditTopUpViewModel, PaywallViewModel, PlanStepHost and SubscriptionService - plus CreditTopUpFlow.State.Failed and the screens rendering each. Same family as US-3025 and the same reason for landing whole: the half still returning String compiles, renders, and looks correct. The four sentences are the ones that matter most to get right, because each names a way OUT of a dead end - manage the Stripe subscription on the web, manage the App Store one on an iPhone, sign in with the other account - and a buyer reading the generic 'something went wrong' instead will tap it forever. Two other literals in BillingRepository.kt are in the same chain: 'This purchase is still pending with Google Play.' and 'That purchase did not name a product we sell.' NOT IN SCOPE: the literal 'Google Play billing is not configured' inside PlayPurchaseRules.conflict is a WIRE MARKER matched against a plain-text response body, sent by the server; it must stay English and needs a LABEL_VOCABULARY entry rather than a resource.

userStories.title: A full-suite verifyRoborazziDebug fails 120 goldens that pass per-class
userStories.description: Measured 2026-08-31. Running 'gradlew verifyRoborazziDebug' with NO --tests filter reports 120 golden failures across roughly 30 screenshot classes. Running the same classes with a --tests filter, minutes apart on the same working tree and the same goldens, reports them GREEN. ReconciliationScreenshotTest and SnapScreenshotTest were verified green in a filtered run and then failed in the unfiltered one; PayoutReconciliationScreenshotTest was re-recorded to green and also appears in the 120. So this is not copy drift and the goldens are not stale - something about running every screenshot class in one JVM renders differently. THE DANGEROUS RESPONSE IS TO RE-RECORD. 120 goldens re-recorded from the full-suite run would bake the wrong baseline in permanently and every future filtered run would then be the thing that looks broken. Only 11 of the 120 are the known spinner-frame nondeterminism (loading/submitting/processing/running/saving), so that explains under a tenth of it. Suspects worth checking in order: font loading or fallback differing once many classes have run in one process; a Robolectric qualifier or Looper state leaking between classes; and memory pressure changing text rendering, since the same JVM OOMs on a full recordRoborazziDebug and needs per-class --tests to record at all (already a known constraint). WHAT THIS MEANS FOR CI: if CI runs the unfiltered task, its screenshot signal is currently noise, and a real regression would be invisible inside 120 failures. Check what the Android CI workflow actually invokes before treating any of this as urgent.
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce: run verifyRoborazziDebug unfiltered, then run one failing class with --tests, on an unchanged tree. Record both results.

Identify the shared state that differs - font/typeface loading, Robolectric qualifiers, Looper or resource cache leaking across classes, or memory pressure - and name it with evidence rather than a guess.
Do NOT bulk re-record. Any golden that is genuinely stale must be shown stale by a FILTERED run of its own class before it is re-recorded.
Confirm which task the Android CI workflow invokes. If it is the unfiltered one, either fix the shared state or make CI run per-class, so that a red screenshot lane means something again.
The 11 spinner-frame failures (loading/submitting/processing/running/saving) are a separate known class - freeze the frame or exclude them deliberately, with a comment saying which.
userStories.notes:
2026-09-04 TWENTY GOLDENS IN THE REPO DO NOT MATCH WHAT THE CODE RENDERS, measured rather than inferred, and found while doing unrelated colour work in US-3010.

HOW IT WAS MEASURED, which matters because this story is about a full-suite-versus-per-class difference and this is neither. On a tree with NO source changes at all (git stash push -u -- android/, confirmed by git status returning zero modified files), running :app:recordRoborazziDebug re-wrote twenty goldens:

  DraftsLibraryScreenshotTest   8  screen-drafts-{banner,batch-failed,batch,selected,stalled,light}-light,
                                   screen-drafts-{dark,error-dark}
  ProspectScreenshotTest       12  screen-prospect-{bought,camera-denied,checking,idle,light,nocost,
                                   thin,slots,tag-only}-light, screen-prospect-{dark,error-dark,planwall-dark}

Recording writes exactly what the current code produces, so a golden that changes under a no-op tree is a golden that was already wrong. These are not flaky and not full-suite-only: they were recorded one class at a time.

THE DIFFERENCE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A TOLERANCE. screen-drafts-light.png differs in 298,174 pixels of a 1080x2340 frame, spanning rows 576 to 2141, with the first differing row going from a flat surface colour to text-weight darks. That is a layout or content change, not anti-aliasing drift.

CONTRAST WITH THE ELEVEN THAT WERE NOT STALE. The same clean-tree probe was run against AnalyticsScreenshotTest, ConsignmentReportScreenshotTest, FulfillmentScreenshotTest, RadarNearbyScreenshotTest, ListingPerformanceScreenshotTest and PaywallScreenshotTest, and every one of them recorded ZERO changes. So this is confined to two classes rather than being a property of the harness, which is what makes it a defect in those two rather than the tolerance question this story was filed about.

PROSPECT HAS A CORROBORATING SIGNAL and Drafts does not. ProspectRolesTest fails four cases on the same clean tree (noPhotoReadableIsAnErrorRatherThanARolelessScan, anUnreadablePhotoDropsItsRoleWithIt, aTagOnlyScanSendsOnePhotoWhoseRoleIsTag, aGarmentOnlyScanSendsTheFrontRoleThatVisualSearchNeeds), so the Prospect screen has code changes its tests AND its goldens were never updated for. US-3027 is the open story on that surface. Drafts has no failing unit test, so its eight stale goldens are silent - nothing in the suite says anything is wrong until someone records.

ALSO SEEN, AND NOT THE SAME THING: ProcessedPathsOnlyTest fails on the clean tree too (US-2658's guard), and TwoFactorPolicyTest is FLAKY - it failed once in a full run and passed on a targeted re-run of the same tree.

WHY THIS COST SOMETHING TODAY, which is the argument for fixing it rather than noting it. Doing a legitimate colour change meant re-recording goldens, and twenty stale ones came back in the same git status as the thirteen real ones. Telling them apart took six separate clean-tree recording runs. Anyone who skips that step commits twenty unrelated golden changes under a colour commit, and the next reader has no way to know which diffs the commit was actually about.

userStories.title: [GATE] Measure real coverage before a single public measurement page is written
userStories.description: Fifth story of the Fit & Measurement Index (design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-fit-measurement-index-design.md), and it is a gate rather than a build. The design names three things that would kill this feature, and two of them are only answerable once the aggregate has run over real data. Answer them here, before any page exists, because a public surface built on thin coverage is expensive to remove and embarrassing to leave up. Question one: how many brand-style-size cohorts actually clear 5 samples and 3 contributors. If the answer is fewer than a few dozen, the public pages (the two stories after the disclosure work) should NOT ship yet, and this story says so in its close. If the resolved share is low, US-2216 stops being a neighbour and becomes a prerequisite, and this story raises that. Report the numbers. Do not estimate them.
acceptanceCriteria: Run the aggregate job against real data and report the actual count of cohorts with sufficient=true, broken down by measurement_group.
Report the share of garment_measurements rows that resolved to a non-empty style_key, and the share that fell back to brand level.
Report the top brands by cohort count, so the first public pages can be chosen on evidence rather than on which brand came to mind.

userStories.title: The public measurement pages: hub, brand, and the style page that holds the whole size run
userStories.description: Eighth story of the Fit & Measurement Index (design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-fit-measurement-index-design.md). Three page tiers, deliberately NOT four. /measurements is the hub explaining what a flat measurement is and how to read the table. /measurements/:brand lists every published style. /measurements/:brand/:style is the money page and holds the full size run in one table. Per-size pages are excluded on purpose. vault/40-growth/seo-indexability.md records that about 79 percent of the static surface is already templated and that a large templated footprint on this domain invites suppression. A style page holding the whole size run is one strong page instead of twelve thin ones, and it matches how the query is actually typed: 'levis 550 measurements', not 'levis 550 w34 measurements'. Copy is seller-first. The 2026-08-18 finding is that 99 percent of this keyword universe's volume carries seller intent and buyer traffic has no monetization path attached yet. The page answers what measurements to put in the listing, the CTA is FlipDesk autofill, and a buyer-facing fit line sits below it linking to the existing /tools/fit-checker. Rendered at the edge because the data grows nightly and static prerender would need a deploy per change.

userStories.title: eBay Application Growth Check: close the compliance gaps before applying
userStories.description: Audit of the eBay integration against the Application Growth Check found three blockers and four fix-firsts. (1) The buyer extension read eBay listing pages in the DOM and posted the photos, title, condition and price to our servers for grading, appraisal and alert-matching. eBay's API License Agreement is explicit that eBay content comes through the API, and a shopper's browser is not the API; this is the finding most likely to end the review and to put the existing production keyset at risk. (2) The MARKETPLACE_ACCOUNT_DELETION handler only deactivated the seller's marketplace_connections row and nulled its tokens. Most deletion notifications name BUYERS, whose usernames we hold across sales, flipdesk_ebay_orphan_sales, marketplace_post_sale_cases and marketplace_offers, three of which also keep eBay's raw order/case/offer payload naming the person. For those the handler matched nothing and acknowledged anyway. (3) No eBay API call was counted anywhere, so the call volume the application form asks for had no answer and eBay rejects applications with no measured usage. Fix-firsts: no retention limit on eBay-derived data beyond the 30-day category-aspect TTL; no eBay attribution on the surfaces that display eBay data; Marketplace Insights shipping written-but-dormant needs to be declared rather than discovered; and Logistics should be asked for separately from sold data so a weak ask does not sink a strong one.
acceptanceCriteria: The extension sends only an eBay item id (grade) or the listing URL (ingest, appraise) on eBay hosts. The server resolves photos, title, brand, price and condition through Browse getItemByLegacyId and REPLACES rather than merges any client-supplied values. Other marketplaces are unchanged.

A source-level guard (extension-unified/test/ebay-no-scrape.test.cjs) fails the build if any DOM extractor is called on the eBay path in the content script, or if any scraped field reappears in the eBay request bodies in background.js.

The account-deletion handler erases the eBay user across every table holding eBay buyer identity, nulling the identity columns and redacting the raw eBay payloads, while keeping the sale rows themselves. An erasure error blocks the 204 and releases the idempotency claim so eBay retries.
A coverage test reads the migrations, finds every table declaring buyer_username, and fails if one is not in BUYER_ERASURE_TARGETS.

Every eBay HTTP call is counted through one choke point into a daily rollup (ebay_api_call_daily), with endpoints templated so cardinality stays bounded, 429 split out from 4xx, and no-response failures distinguished from eBay rejections.
An hourly cron records eBay's own getRateLimits response to ebay_rate_limit_snapshots so our count and eBay's can be compared.

A daily retention cron applies a published policy to eBay-derived data, and a test fails the build if a rule is not described on the privacy page or the privacy page promises a deletion no rule performs.
eBay attribution plus the non-endorsement notice appears on every surface that displays eBay data, not only on the trademarks page.
