userStories.title: Eight credit functions are EXECUTE-able by anon on prod, where the local stack refuses them
userStories.description: As GradeThread, I want the credit-granting functions to refuse an anonymous caller in PRODUCTION, not only on the local stack, so that the public anon key cannot reach a function that writes the credit ledger. MEASURED 2026-09-02 by the prod proacl census US-2282 left open as its AC6/AC7 (scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql section 29, read-only over SSH). Of 241 public functions, 120 are SECURITY DEFINER and anon holds EXECUTE on 100 of them. Reading proacl directly for the ten credit functions: admin_adjust_credits and revoke_grade_credits are correctly locked to supabase_admin/postgres/service_role, and the other eight carry BOTH a PUBLIC grant (the leading =X/supabase_admin ACL entry) and explicit anon=X and authenticated=X: debit_grade_credits, grant_appstore_credits, grant_buyer_reward_credit, grant_grade_credits, issue_buyer_reward_credit, redeem_buyer_reward_credit, refund_ai_action, reserve_ai_action. US-2282's own closing note records anon being refused 42501 on all nine of these on the LOCAL stack, which is an EXECUTE denial, so 00615's revoke works where it was tested and is not in effect on prod. This story establishes the PRIVILEGE from the catalog and deliberately does NOT establish exploitability: the body may still refuse anon, and proving that from outside means a write-shaped call that could mint credits against a real account.
acceptanceCriteria: Establish WITHOUT calling any of the eight whether the function bodies already refuse an anonymous caller: read prosrc for each from the catalog (read-only) and record, per function, whether it checks auth.uid()/auth.role() before it writes. This decides whether the finding is a defence-in-depth gap or a live exposure, and it is the first thing to do because it sets the urgency of everything below.

Establish why the revoke is absent on prod when it is present locally: confirm whether 00615 (and any sibling that revoked EXECUTE) is recorded in the prod migration table, and whether a later migration, a PostgREST/Supabase role-grant step, or a restore re-granted EXECUTE to anon and PUBLIC. A fix that does not name the cause will be undone the same way.

A migration REVOKEs EXECUTE from PUBLIC, anon and authenticated on all eight, granted back only to the roles that need it, following the US-1108 triple: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in the same commit, self-record footer, PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md entry with the NOTIFY pgrst reminder.

A test that reads the CATALOG rather than asserting the migration text: for every function named in a REVOKE list, assert has_function_privilege('anon', oid, 'EXECUTE') is false on the throwaway stack. The failure this story is about is a grant that came back, and a test that greps SQL cannot see that.

The census becomes repeatable rather than a one-off: scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql section 29 already answers it, so record in that section that a non-zero definer_anon_can_run is expected until this story closes, and what the number should be afterwards.

OPERATOR: apply the migration to prod, NOTIFY pgrst, then re-run section 29 and paste the before/after definer_anon_can_run counts into this story's note. Do NOT verify by calling one of the eight functions with the anon key - that call is the thing being prevented.
userStories.notes: [2026-09-02] ⚠ THIS STORY'S PREMISE IS WRONG, AND THE CATALOG PROVES IT. The description says a revoke that works locally is missing on prod. It is not: NO REVOKE WAS EVER AUTHORED FOR THESE EIGHT, anywhere, and the local stack and prod AGREE. Counts read from pg_proc the same day: local (throwaway stack built from every migration) 237 public / 119 SECURITY DEFINER / 101 anon-executable; prod 241 / 120 / 100. anon holds EXECUTE on the same eight in both, and on neither of the two that 00216 locked. WHERE THE WRONG READING CAME FROM, because it is a trap worth naming: US-2282's closing note records anon being refused "42501" on the local stack, and I read that as an EXECUTE denial. It is the RAISE EXCEPTION ... USING ERRCODE = '42501' inside each function BODY, which 00615 added deliberately instead of a revoke, and which that migration's header explains at length. From a client the two are indistinguishable, which is exactly why this needed a catalog read rather than another probe. NOTHING WAS CALLED, in any environment; every finding here is pg_proc and prosrc. AC1, PER-FUNCTION BODY GUARD (latest definition, confirmed against prosrc in the catalog; body_guard = the body checks auth.role() or gt_require_role before it writes): grant_grade_credits 00615 GUARDED (first statement) anon=t; debit_grade_credits 00615 GUARDED anon=t; grant_appstore_credits 00615 GUARDED anon=t; grant_buyer_reward_credit 00615 GUARDED anon=t; issue_buyer_reward_credit 00615 GUARDED anon=t; redeem_buyer_reward_credit 00615 GUARDED anon=t; refund_ai_action 00617 GUARDED anon=t; reserve_ai_action 00640 GUARDED via gt_require_role anon=t; admin_adjust_credits 00216 no body check but anon=FALSE (revoked); revoke_grade_credits 00216 no body check but anon=FALSE (revoked). One signature each, ten rows, no stale overloads. SO THIS IS DEFENCE IN DEPTH, NOT A LIVE EXPOSURE. Every function an anonymous caller can reach refuses that caller in its own body. ONE NUANCE recorded rather than churned: the 00615 shape evaluates to NULL when auth.role() is NULL, so it fails OPEN for a caller carrying no JWT claims at all. That is a direct psql or operator session, never PostgREST, because the anon key always carries role=anon. 00640 introduced gt_require_role as the fail-closed replacement and 00617/00720 chose the NULL-permitting shape on purpose so operators and pg_cron keep working; the six were left as they are. AC2, THE CAUSE, NAMED: not a re-grant. A standing owner decision. 00527_revoke_public_function_execute.sql.BLOCKED is the bulk revoke and it is parked because on this Postgres image a denied function call from a role in supautils.hint_roles segfaults the backend and restarts the database while building the GRANT hint (US-2403); anon is the key in the browser bundle and PostgREST exposes every one of these at /rpc/<name>. 00615 chose the body guard instead, 00686 and 00720 each UNDID a revoke that shipped by mistake, and two gates now fail a new one (scripts/migrations-lint.mjs and src/test/us2403-function-revoke-gate.test.ts). The advisory db-denied-rpc-crash-check.mjs still reported the crash on the local stack today, so the constraint is live rather than historical. AC3, DELIBERATE DEPARTURE, AND IT IS THE RIGHT CALL: the revoke this story asked for WAS NOT WRITTEN, because it would have been a real regression - an unauthenticated database-restart button on eight endpoints - and two gates would have failed the build anyway. Shipped instead: 00723_credit_function_authorization_invariant.sql, a read-only DO block that aborts the apply before its footer if any of the ten is reachable by anon AND unguarded in its body. That closes the hole nothing covered: CREATE OR REPLACE preserves an ACL but DROP + CREATE resets it to the PUBLIC default, so one valid migration can drop the guard and restore the grant at the same time and still apply green. US-1108 triple complete. AC4: scripts/check-credit-function-guards.mjs reads pg_proc inside a rolled-back transaction, wired into the verify db lane AND .github/workflows/db-migrations.yml (guard-lane-parity.test.ts requires both). It carries a self-check that creates one guarded and one unguarded probe function and fails unless the detector flags exactly the unguarded one; that self-check caught its own parser bug on first run. AC5: section 29 of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql now records that definer_anon_can_run is expected to stay NON-ZERO permanently, that 00723 does not move it, that the number which must be zero is the anon_can_run=t AND body_guard=f pair, and that a sudden DROP is the alarm; two stale claims in that section were corrected. VERIFIED ON MAIN AFTER THE MERGE, not taken from the agent's report: three-way conflict resolved by hand (schema-version to 00723, both ledger entries kept, manifest regenerated to 465 entries); node scripts/migrations-lint.mjs = 719 migrations, no duplicate versions, 7 annotated gaps, exit 0 (the agent's branch failed this on a 00722 gap, which was the concurrent story's migration and resolved at merge); npx tsc -b exit 0; deno test schema-version_test.ts 22 passed. STILL OPEN, AC6 OPERATOR: apply 00723 to prod (it changes nothing table- or RPC-shaped, so no NOTIFY is strictly needed), then redeploy the edge for the 00723 boot guard, then re-run section 29 and paste the before/after here. | [2026-09-02] 00723 FAILED ITS FIRST PROD APPLY, AND THAT IS THE STORY'S REAL FINDING. The owner ran it and got 23514: "credit function(s) reachable by anon with no authorization check in the body: grant_appstore_credits(uuid,integer,text,text,text,text,text)". The invariant migration did precisely what it was built to do and refused to record itself. CONFIRMED STRAIGHT FROM PROD, read-only, without calling the function: it is SECURITY DEFINER, anon holds EXECUTE, prosrc is 1359 bytes and contains NO auth.role() and NO gt_require_role. A full census of all ten credit functions on prod the same minute: grant_appstore_credits is the ONLY violation (anon=t, guard=f); debit_grade_credits, grant_buyer_reward_credit, grant_grade_credits, issue_buyer_reward_credit, redeem_buyer_reward_credit, refund_ai_action and reserve_ai_action are all anon=t with guard=t; admin_adjust_credits and revoke_grade_credits are guard=f but anon=f. SO ONE FUNCTION IN PRODUCTION MOVED A MONEY-LIKE BALANCE WITH NO AUTHORIZATION CHECK OF ANY KIND. That narrows my original claim rather than restoring it: the claim was eight functions and a missing revoke, which was wrong on both counts; the truth is one function and a missing BODY GUARD, and it was found by the migration written to replace that wrong claim. IT IS PROD-ONLY DRIFT, NOT A MISSING MIGRATION, and the obvious explanations were checked and eliminated. 00609 dropped the 6-arg form and created the 7-arg one; 00615 then CREATE OR REPLACE'd that same signature to add the guard. On prod both are recorded IN THE RIGHT ORDER (00609 at 2026-08-16 21:11 UTC, 00615 at 2026-08-17 16:39 UTC), so it is not out-of-order application. The parameter NAMES are identical between the two files, so 00615's replace cannot have failed with "cannot change name of input parameter". There is exactly one row for the function in pg_proc, so it is not a stale overload sitting beside a guarded one. 00615 is recorded as applied and its effect on this single function is absent; the database is the authority and the cause is not recoverable from the repo. THE FIX, shipped inside 00723 rather than as a new migration, because 00723 runs first and would block anything numbered after it: the file now REPAIRS and then ASSERTS. It CREATE OR REPLACEs grant_appstore_credits with 00615's guarded body copied byte-for-byte (lines 288-347; the only edit is two U+2014 em dashes in comments changed to hyphens for CLAUDE.md's ASCII rule, no executable line differs), then runs the original assertion unchanged. A REPLACE AND NEVER A DROP: replace preserves the ACL so anon keeps EXECUTE and the US-2403 segfault stays disarmed, whereas a drop-and-create would reset the ACL to the PUBLIC default and is the exact failure mode the assertion exists to catch. Amending an already-pushed migration is normally wrong; it is right here because 00723 has never successfully applied anywhere (it aborts before its footer by design, so prod has no record of it) and because a repair numbered 00724 could never be reached. RE-VERIFIED AFTER THE CHANGE: npm run verify:db = ALL 20 CHECKS PASSED including "db: credit functions refuse anon (US-3094)", with supabase db reset --no-seed re-applying every migration from an empty schema; node scripts/migrations-lint.mjs = 719 migrations, no duplicate versions, exit 0. One earlier verify:db run reported 18 failures; that was a stale local stack left half-reset by the agent's own run, and a clean reset cleared it. AC6 OPERATOR, UPDATED: re-apply 00723 to prod. It will now repair the function and then pass. Afterwards, re-read the census (grant_appstore_credits should come back guard=t, anon unchanged at t) and paste it here.

acceptanceCriteria: Read src/test/cache-peek-has-a-writer.test.ts first and state, in this story's note, what the guard actually requires: which peeks it considers declared, where a declaration lives, and what problem the guard was written to prevent. Either declare the peek the way the guard expects, or remove the peek if useDashboardLayout does not need it. Do NOT add the file to an ignore list, and do NOT relax the guard's matching so the peek stops registering: the peek is real, and a guard edited until it passes is worse than a failing one.

userStories.title: Cut eBay API call volume before the Application Growth Check
userStories.description: Measured on prod 2026-09-01..03: two connected sellers made 33,002 eBay calls a day and peaked at 4,941 of the 5,000 daily Trading allowance (98.8%), read from eBay's own getRateLimits. Three causes, all fixed together. (1) doListingsPull always fanned out one GET /sell/inventory/v1/offer?sku= per SKU before it looked at orders, and the two callers that only ever need orders - the notification webhook and the order backstop - fired it every few minutes. 25,312 calls a day, about 41 full catalog reads against 618 listings. (2) The item-specifics fill had no negative cache: buildCatalogPatch writes nothing when eBay has no value for a blank field, so needsSpecifics was true again next sync and the same item was re-read forever, roughly 3,300 Trading calls a day into the pool that is already at 98.8%. (3) The marketplace-event sweep polled six eBay endpoints for every connected seller every fifteen minutes whether or not anything could have happened to them: 576 calls per seller per day of fixed cost, paid identically by a dormant trial account and a real shop - the cost that scales linearly with signups and nothing else. Also makes the eBay notification reconcile cron say what it is failing on; it has failed 128 times with zero successes since 2026-08-20 and left nothing behind but an empty cron_runs.detail.
acceptanceCriteria: An orders-only sync (webhook, order backstop, adapter syncOrders) skips both active-listing passes and the ended-without-sale sweep, and reaches the orders pass without reading the offer catalog.

resolveSyncScope is pure and tested: a full request is never downgraded, orders stays orders while the catalog is fresh, and it upgrades to full on a null, unparseable, or stale (>= CATALOG_REFRESH_MS) catalog cursor, so no caller can starve the reconcile.

getItemSpecifics is not re-asked for an item within SPECIFICS_RECHECK_MS, whether or not eBay had anything to give; the stamp is one bulk write, and a failure to stamp is logged and recorded on the run rather than swallowed.

The marketplace-event sweep polls only owners with an active eBay listing, a sale inside the post-sale window, or an open case; the gate fails OPEN to polling everyone if the RPC is missing or errors.
pollable_ebay_owner_ids is SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path, revoked from public/anon/authenticated and granted only to service_role.
The notification reconcile cron logs the real error message, and a non-array list payload from eBay throws naming the endpoint, the key and the payload's own keys instead of 'rows is not iterable'.
OPERATOR: apply 00724 to prod, NOTIFY pgrst, then redeploy the edge (columns and RPC are read by name; the edge must not go first).
OPERATOR: after 48 hours, re-read ebay_api_call_daily and confirm total daily calls and the Trading peak have both dropped; do not submit the growth check on the pre-fix numbers.
OPERATOR: read the next ebay-notification-reconcile failure from the container log now that it names itself, and file the real defect.

userStories.title: Stagger the per-SKU eBay offer read
userStories.description: US-3110 cut the number of full catalog passes from ~41 a day to 4 per connection. What remains is the cost of a pass: listAllOffers fans out one GET /sell/inventory/v1/offer?sku= per SKU across eBay's entire inventory list, 984 SKUs on prod, and only 301 of 940 eBay listing rows carry an offer id - the rest are Seller-Hub listings created through Trading that have no Inventory-API offer and never will. eBay returns nothing, we store nothing, we ask again six hours later. Same shape as the item-specifics bug. A per-SKU read stamp (inventory_items.ebay_offer_checked_at) takes the fan-out from every pass to once a day: roughly 4,000 calls a day down to roughly 1,000. Price, quantity, title, category and listing status for ACTIVE listings keep arriving from GetMyeBaySelling in about seven paged calls on the same pass, so nothing a seller reads goes stale. The one thing that moves to a daily cadence is detection of a listing that ENDED WITHOUT SELLING, because eBay publishes no notification topic for a listing ending and polling is the only way we learn it. Absence-based ending (treating 'missing from the bulk active list' as ended) was considered and REJECTED: a truncated GetMyeBaySelling page would move live listings into Drafts and nobody would notice until a seller complained.
acceptanceCriteria: listAllOffers accepts a skip set, filters it BEFORE the per-sync fan-out ceiling so the budget is spent on SKUs that need a read, and returns the SKUs it actually spent a call on including the ones eBay had no offer for.
selectSkusToSkip is pure and tested: skips inside the window, reads outside it, and never skips a null, empty, unparseable or future-dated stamp.
Every SKU read is stamped in bulk, chunked so a large seller's pass does not overflow the PostgREST URL, and a rate-limit bail-out still stamps the SKUs it got through.

Both failure paths fail open to the pre-change full fan-out: a missing column or failed read returns an empty skip set with a warning; a failed stamp write is logged and recorded on the sync run rather than swallowed.
OFFER_RECHECK_MS sits strictly between CATALOG_REFRESH_MS and a week, enforced by a test, so the stagger can neither become a no-op nor leave an ended listing in 'listed' for days.
OPERATOR: apply 00725 to prod, NOTIFY pgrst, then redeploy the edge (the column is read by name; the edge must not go first).

OPERATOR: 48 hours after deploy, confirm from ebay_api_call_daily that GET /sell/inventory/v1/offer has fallen to roughly one read per SKU per day, and that no listing sits in 'listed' with an ended eBay listing for more than 24 hours.

userStories.title: eBay compliance: extension attribution, and stop calling APIs we cannot use
userStories.description: Three things found while auditing what was left for the eBay Application Growth Check. (1) COMPLIANCE GAP: the browser extension displays eBay listing titles, prices and images in the overlay and the compare view and carried no eBay attribution and no non-endorsement notice anywhere. The web app has had both since US-3033 but on only two surfaces, and nothing tested coverage, so nobody could tell 'this surface needs no notice' from 'this surface was forgotten'. (2) The notification reconcile cron records only a COUNT of its per-topic failures, because readJobOutcome sums numbers and has nowhere to put a sentence - the 2026-09-03 18:17 run recorded {failures:{errors:12}} and nothing else. (3) Two eBay calls that can never succeed on this keyset were being made forever: /commerce/identity/v1/user needs commerce.identity.readonly, which is deliberately NOT requested because the production keyset is not licensed for it, and it was called on every token refresh (~33/day); payment_dispute_summary needs sell.payment.dispute, which one of the two prod connections does not hold, and the event sweep asked every 15 minutes (~160/day). Also fixed two suites that were failing on a Windows checkout only, one of them ebay-no-scrape.test.cjs - the guard that proves we do not scrape eBay - which matched a bare newline against CRLF source and so was green in CI and red locally.
acceptanceCriteria: The extension carries eBay's attribution and non-endorsement notice on the in-page overlay and the compare view, worded identically to the web component, and a test asserts that wording still matches src/components/marketplace/ebay-attribution.tsx phrase for phrase.

The notice is keyed by marketplace: eBay gets it, Poshmark/Grailed/Mercari/Depop/Vinted get null rather than a generic sentence, matching is case-insensitive, and a mixed compare table carries it once and only when an eBay row is present.

test/ebay-attribution.test.cjs names the surfaces that must wire it up and fails when one stops, and also checks the manifest load order, since a classic script loaded after its consumer leaves the global undefined and the notice silently never renders.
The notification reconcile cron logs each per-topic failure with its topicId, bounded and truncated like the marketplace-event sweep, so a count becomes a diagnosis.

getUserIdentityFromToken returns null without calling eBay when commerce.identity.readonly is not in the requested scopes; re-adding the scope re-enables it with no other change. Mirrors isNegotiationScopeAvailable and isLogisticsScopeAvailable.

The event sweep skips payment-dispute reads for a connection flagged disputes_access_denied, sets the flag on an insufficient-scope refusal (never on the no-disputes 404), clears it when access works again, and reads it fail-open.
ebay-no-scrape.test.cjs and queue-view.test.cjs normalise line endings, so all 53 extension suites pass on a Windows checkout as well as in CI.
OPERATOR: apply 00725 to prod (it now carries disputes_access_denied too), NOTIFY pgrst, then redeploy the edge.
OPERATOR: one prod eBay connection lacks sell.payment.dispute and one lacks nothing else of note; that seller must reconnect at /oauth/start before dispute notifications work for them.
OPERATOR: read the next ebay-notification-reconcile run's log line and file the real cause of its 12 per-topic errors.

userStories.title: Apply prod migrations over ssh from the terminal, with an immediate answer
userStories.description: As the operator, I want to see what prod is missing and apply it from one command, so that I stop pasting SQL into the Supabase Studio editor and waiting to find out whether it worked.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/migrate-prod.mjs with no flags is read-only: it prints the local file count, the count prod records, the pending list in apply order, and any version recorded on prod with no local file. It never writes.

Pending is computed by MEMBERSHIP in public.applied_migrations, not by comparing to the highest recorded version, so a gap below the maximum is reported. scripts/migrate-prod.test.mjs asserts a local 00134 between an applied 00100 and 00200 comes back pending.

No host, container id, or IP appears in scripts/migrate-prod.mjs or scripts/lib/prod-db.mjs. PROD_SSH_HOST is required and unset raises a ConfigError with exit code 2; the container is discovered by probing each container matching PROD_DB_CONTAINER_FILTER for the tables in PROD_DB_MARKER_TABLES. A test greps both sources for an IPv4 literal and a container id and fails if either appears.
Applying requires BOTH --apply and --yes. decideAction() returns action 'refuse' with exit 1 for --apply alone, and 'apply' only when both are present.

applyPending() stops at the first failing migration, leaves the rest unapplied, and does NOT send the schema reload; on full success it sends NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema'. ssh propagates psql's non-zero exit so a failed file is reported with its psql error text.
A six-digit filename prefix (000355, 000375, 000385) is canonicalized to the five digits prod records, so those three files are not reported as permanently pending.
The 'nothing pending' output states that a recorded version is not proof the migration took effect and points at scripts/prod-schema-audit.sql.

userStories.title: lintDebug is red on main: UiMessage is annotated @StringRes and documented to hold plurals
userStories.description:
MEASURED 2026-09-04, found because it blocked the verify gate on unrelated colour work (US-3010).

`:app:lintDebug` FAILS ON MAIN TODAY, so `npm run verify:android` cannot go green for anyone:

  Autolister.kt:69: Error: Expected resource of type string [ResourceType]

THE ANNOTATION IS WRONG, NOT THE CALL. UiMessage declares `@StringRes val res: Int` (ui/UiMessage.kt:26) and, four fields later, `val quantity: Int?` whose own KDoc says "The count that picks a plural form, when [res] is a PLURALS resource". So the class is documented to hold either kind of id and annotated to hold only one. The renderer already branches correctly, calling pluralStringResource when quantity is set and stringResource otherwise. Autolister.kt:69 passes R.plurals.autolister_partial with a quantity, which is exactly what the class says to do, and lint rejects it.

IT IS NEW, NOT ABSORBED. android/app/lint-baseline.xml carries 220 issues and not one ResourceType entry, so this appeared after the baseline was last regenerated. It arrived with 0b905c45a ("US-2976: translate Automations, Repricing, AutoLister and Prospect"), which is on origin/main.

ONE CALL SITE, WHICH IS WHY IT IS STILL CHEAP TO FIX PROPERLY. A scan of src/main finds exactly one UiMessage built from an R.plurals id. Fixing it now is a one-site change; every later plurals message makes it a bigger one, and the pressure will be to silence lint rather than to fix the type.

DO NOT FIX IT BY BASELINING IT OR BY SUPPRESSING AT THE CALL SITE. Both hide a real contradiction, and the next reader has no way to tell an intentional plurals id from a genuine wrong-resource bug - which is the actual thing ResourceType is there to catch. Dropping the annotation entirely is also a loss: every other call site passes a string and is checked today.

THE SHAPE THAT KEEPS BOTH is two factories over one data class - text(@StringRes res, args, detail) and plural(@PluralsRes res, quantity, args, detail) - so each id is checked as its own kind and `quantity` can stop being a nullable that means "read the other field differently".
acceptanceCriteria: npm run verify:android reaches the end of the lint lane on a clean checkout of main.

UiMessage distinguishes a string id from a plurals id in the type system, so each is checked as its own kind - not by dropping the annotation, not by a call-site suppression, and not by adding a lint-baseline entry.
The existing plurals call site (Autolister.kt:69) and every string call site still render the same copy; the Spanish catalogue is unchanged.
A test or guard fails if a plurals id is passed where a string id is expected, so the next one is caught at build time rather than by a lint run nobody can complete.
